decline_pages.title: Roots, Rational Powers, and Classical Inequalities: Examples and Counterexamples

items.title: Rational powers of rational bases computed from the definition
items.statement: In $\mathbb{R}$, with the rational powers of [[def-rational-power]]: $(4/9)^{1/2} = 2/3$; $(8/27)^{1/3} = 2/3$; $(4/9)^{3/2} = 8/27$; $(27/8)^{-2/3} = 4/9$; and $8^{2/6} = 8^{1/3} = 2$, one value produced from either representative of the rational $1/3 = 2/6$. Every base occurring is a positive rational and every exponent a rational with numerator an integer and denominator a natural $\ge 1$, so the definition applies in each case; the last display is the instance of [[lem-rational-power-well-defined]] that [[def-rational-power]] records in its `justified_by`. The item also checks the negative-exponent and non-coprime-representative cases, the two places where the definition is most easily misread.

items.title: Odd powers are bijections of $\mathbb{R}$: $x^{3} = -8$ has the unique solution $x = -2$
items.statement: Let $n \ge 1$ be odd. Then $x \mapsto x^{n}$ is a bijection of $\mathbb{R}$ onto $\mathbb{R}$: every real number has exactly one real $n$-th root. Explicitly, $x^{3} = -8$ has the unique solution $x = -2$, and $x^{5} = -32$ has the unique solution $x = -2$. For a negative right-hand side this is a statement about the solution of $x^{n} = a$; it does not extend the symbol $a^{1/n}$, since [[thm-nth-roots-exist]] produces that symbol only for $a \ge 0$ and [[def-rational-power]] does not define rational powers of negative bases (its separate zero-base clause concerns nonnegative bases only). This is the claim the A-page prose records when it says that odd roots of negatives do exist while [[fs-negative-has-square-root]] shows that even ones do not.

items.title: The two-term AM-GM inequality, its equality case, and $x + x^{-1} \ge 2$
items.statement: (a) For all $a, b \ge 0$, $\dfrac{a+b}{2} \ge \sqrt{ab}$, equivalently $ab \le \Big(\dfrac{a+b}{2}\Big)^{2}$, with equality in either form exactly when $a = b$. (b) Consequently, for every $x > 0$, $x + x^{-1} \ge 2$, with equality exactly when $x = 1$.

items.title: Comparing rational powers: $2^{1/3} < 2^{1/2} < 3^{1/3}$
items.statement: (i) $2^{1/2} > 2^{1/3}$; (ii) $3^{1/2} > 2^{1/2}$; (iii) $2^{1/2} < 3^{1/3}$; hence $2^{1/3} < 2^{1/2} < 3^{1/3}$. All bases are positive and all exponents rational, so [[def-rational-power]] applies. Clauses (i) and (ii) are instances of the two monotonicity statements of [[lem-rational-power-monotone]], but (iii) is not: it compares bases $2 < 3$ against exponents in the opposite order $1/2 > 1/3$, and neither monotonicity clause decides it.

items.title: A weighted AM-GM computation: $8^{2/3}\,1^{1/3} \le \frac{2}{3}\cdot 8 + \frac{1}{3}\cdot 1$
items.statement: Take $n := 2$, $x_0 := 8$, $x_1 := 1$ and the rational weights $w_0 := 2/3$, $w_1 := 1/3$, so that $\iota(w_0) + \iota(w_1) = 1$ in $\mathbb{R}$. Then [[thm-weighted-am-gm-rational]] gives $$8^{2/3}\cdot 1^{1/3} \;\le\; \tfrac{2}{3}\cdot 8 + \tfrac{1}{3}\cdot 1,$$ where the left-hand side is $4$ and the right-hand side is $17/3$; so $4 < 17/3$ and the inequality is strict here. With $x_0 := x_1 := 8$ instead, both sides equal $8$, so the bound is attained by a constant list.

items.title: Young's inequality at $p = q = 2$ and at $p = 3$, $q = 3/2$
items.statement: (i) At the conjugate pair $p = q = 2$, [[thm-young-inequality]] reads $ab \le \frac{a^{2}}{2} + \frac{b^{2}}{2}$ for all $a, b \ge 0$, with equality exactly when $a = b$; the instance $a := 4$, $b := 9$ gives $36 \le 97/2$. (ii) At $p := 3$ and $q := 3/2$, conjugate since $\frac13 + \frac23 = 1$, it reads $ab \le \frac{a^{3}}{3} + \frac{2}{3}\,b^{3/2}$; the instance $a := 2$, $b := 4$ gives $8$ on both sides.

items.title: The two-term Lagrange identity and Cauchy-Schwarz
items.statement: For all reals $a_0, a_1, b_0, b_1$, $$(a_0^{2} + a_1^{2})(b_0^{2} + b_1^{2}) - (a_0b_0 + a_1b_1)^{2} = (a_0b_1 - a_1b_0)^{2};$$ consequently $(a_0b_0 + a_1b_1)^{2} \le (a_0^{2} + a_1^{2})(b_0^{2} + b_1^{2})$, with equality exactly when $a_0b_1 = a_1b_0$ — the two-entry form of the proportionality clause of [[thm-cauchy-schwarz-finite]]. The instance $a_0 := 1$, $a_1 := 2$, $b_0 := 3$, $b_1 := 4$ reads $5\cdot 25 - 121 = 4 = (-2)^{2}$.

items.title: Hölder at the conjugate pair $p = 3$, $q = 3/2$: an exact equality instance and a strict instance
items.statement: $p := 3$ and $q := 3/2$ are conjugate rationals, $\frac13 + \frac23 = 1$. For the two-entry lists $a_0 = a_1 = b_0 = b_1 = 1$, [[thm-holder-finite]] reads $$\sum_{k<2}|a_kb_k| = 2 \;\le\; \Big(\sum_{k<2}|a_k|^{3}\Big)^{1/3}\Big(\sum_{k<2}|b_k|^{3/2}\Big)^{2/3} = 2^{1/3}\,2^{2/3} = 2,$$ so both sides are equal here. For $a = (2,0)$ and $b = (0,3)$ the inequality is strict: the left-hand side is $0$ and the right-hand side is $2\cdot 3 = 6$.

items.title: Minkowski for two-entry vectors: equality and strict cases
items.statement: For all reals $x_0, x_1, y_0, y_1$, $$\big((x_0+y_0)^{2} + (x_1+y_1)^{2}\big)^{1/2} \;\le\; \big(x_0^{2} + x_1^{2}\big)^{1/2} + \big(y_0^{2} + y_1^{2}\big)^{1/2},$$ and equality holds exactly when $x_0y_1 = x_1y_0$ and $x_0y_0 + x_1y_1 \ge 0$. Two instances: for $x = (3,4)$ and $y = (6,8)$ both sides are $15$; for $x = (3,4)$ and $y = (4,-3)$ the left-hand side is $\sqrt{50} = 5\sqrt{2}$ and the right-hand side is $10$, so the inequality is strict.

items.title: AM-GM fails for negative entries: $(-1,-4)$ has geometric mean $2$ and arithmetic mean $-5/2$
items.statement: **Refuted claim:** the conclusion $\sqrt{ab} \le \dfrac{a+b}{2}$ of the two-term arithmetic-geometric mean inequality holds for arbitrary real $a, b$. Witness: $a := -1$, $b := -4$. The product is $ab = 4$, so the geometric mean is $4^{1/2} = 2$, while the arithmetic mean is $(-1-4)/2 = -5/2$; thus $G = 2 > -5/2 = A$ and the inequality fails. The failure is not an accident of the witness: for any two negative entries $a, b < 0$ the product is positive, so $G > 0$, while $A < 0$, giving $G > A$. A second failure mode is non-existence: for $a := -1$, $b := 1$ the product is $-1$, which has no real square root ([[fs-negative-has-square-root]]), so $G$ is not defined at all. By contrast the equivalent squared form $ab \le A^{2}$ of [[thm-am-gm]] survives for all real $a, b$, since $A^{2} - ab = (a-b)^{2}/4 \ge 0$; the hypothesis $a, b \ge 0$ is spent exactly on passing from that squared form to the geometric-mean form, which needs a nonnegative arithmetic mean and a real geometric mean.

items.title: Weighted AM-GM needs nonnegative weights summing to $1$
items.statement: **Refuted claim:** the inequality $\prod_{k<n} x_k^{w_k} \le \sum_{k<n} w_k x_k$ of [[thm-weighted-am-gm-rational]] holds for all positive $x_k$ and all rational weights $w_k$ of sum $1$, or for all rational weights whatsoever. Two witnesses. (i) For $x_0 := x_1 := 4$ and $w_0 := w_1 := 1$, whose sum is $2 \ne 1$: the left-hand side is $4^{1}\cdot 4^{1} = 16$ and the right-hand side is $1\cdot 4 + 1\cdot 4 = 8$, so $16 > 8$. (ii) For $x_0 := 4$, $x_1 := 1/4$, $w_0 := 2$ and $w_1 := -1$, whose sum is $1$ but which contains a negative weight: the left-hand side is $4^{2}\cdot(1/4)^{-1} = 16\cdot 4 = 64$ and the right-hand side is $2\cdot 4 + (-1)\cdot(1/4) = 8 - 1/4 = 31/4$, so $64 > 31/4$. Both hypotheses on the weights — nonnegativity and total mass $1$ — are therefore load-bearing.

items.title: Minkowski fails for $p = 1/2$: the hypothesis $p \ge 1$ is load-bearing
items.statement: **Refuted claim:** the inequality of [[thm-minkowski-finite]] holds for every positive rational $p$. Witness: $p := 1/2$, with the two-entry lists $x_0 := 1$, $x_1 := 0$ and $y_0 := 0$, $y_1 := 1$. The left-hand side $\big(\sum_{k<2}|x_k+y_k|^{1/2}\big)^{1/(1/2)} = \big(\sum_{k<2}|x_k+y_k|^{1/2}\big)^{2}$ is $(1+1)^{2} = 4$, while the right-hand side $\big(\sum_{k<2}|x_k|^{1/2}\big)^{2} + \big(\sum_{k<2}|y_k|^{1/2}\big)^{2}$ is $1 + 1 = 2$; so the inequality fails. Every expression is defined: $1/2$ is a positive rational, $|z|^{1/2} = \sqrt{|z|}$ is the rational power of [[def-rational-power]] with its supplementary clause $0^{1/2} = 0$, and the outer exponent $1/p = 2$ is an integer power.

items.title: Bernoulli fails for $x < -1$: $x = -4$, $n = 3$
items.statement: **Refuted claim:** $(1+x)^{n} \ge 1 + nx$ holds for every real $x$ and every natural $n$. Witness: $x := -4$, $n := 3$. Then $(1+x)^{3} = (-3)^{3} = -27$ while $1 + 3x = -11$, so $(1+x)^{3} < 1 + 3x$ and the inequality fails. Two boundary remarks sharpen the failure: at $n = 1$ the two sides agree for every $x$, so the failure needs $n \ge 2$; and at $x = -3$, $n = 3$ the two sides happen to agree ($-8 = -8$), so a witness must be chosen rather than assumed. The hypothesis $x \ge -1$ of [[lem-bernoulli-inequality]] is therefore load-bearing.

items.title: The iterated rational-power law fails without a positive base: $\big((-3)^{2}\big)^{1/2} = 3 \ne -3$
items.statement: **Refuted claim:** the identity $(a^{r})^{s} = a^{rs}$ of [[lem-rational-power-laws]] holds for every real $a$ and all rationals $r, s$ for which both sides are defined. Witness: $a := -3$, $r := 2$, $s := 1/2$. Here $a^{r}$ is the integer power $(-3)^{2} = 9$, so $(a^{r})^{s} = 9^{1/2} = 3$ by [[thm-nth-roots-exist]], while $a^{rs} = (-3)^{1} = -3$ is again an integer power; the two sides differ. Both displayed expressions are defined by the library's definitions — only the rational-power step, on the positive base $9$, uses [[def-rational-power]] — so the positivity hypothesis $a > 0$ in [[lem-rational-power-laws]] cannot be dropped. The correct general statement in this case is that $\big(a^{2}\big)^{1/2} = |a|$ for every real $a$.

items.title: Five finite proofs of Bernoulli, with rational exponents and the quadratic refinement
items.statement: Five proof routes verify the same integer statement: for $x\ge-1$ and a natural $n$, $(1+x)^n\ge1+nx$, with equality exactly when $n\le1$ or $x=0$. The routes are ordinary induction, geometric-sum comparison, an exact nonnegative supporting-line remainder, AM-GM, and a finite binomial/positive-weight expansion. They cover $-1\le x<0$ as well as $x\ge0$; $0^0=1$ is the integer-power convention. In addition, with rational $r$ and $x\ge-1$ (requiring $x>-1$ when $r<0$), $(1+x)^r\ge1+rx$ for $r\ge1$ or $r\le0$, and $(1+x)^r\le1+rx$ for $0\le r\le1$. Equality is exactly $x=0$ or $r\in\{0,1\}$. For rational $r\ge2$, the promised quadratic refinement follows in the stronger form $(1+x)^r\ge1+rx+(r/2)x^2$; hence it holds with any natural coefficient $m$ satisfying $2m\le r$, including the coefficient customarily written $\lfloor r/2\rfloor$. For $1\le r<2$ that floor coefficient is zero and the ordinary bound applies. The stronger refinement has equality exactly when $x=0$ or $r=2$. At $x=-1$, the supplementary clause of [[def-rational-power]] supplies $0^r=0$ for rational $r>0$, and [[def-integer-power]] supplies $0^0=1$; negative powers of zero remain undefined. No irrational exponent or exponential/general convexity theorem is asserted.

items.title: Five finite AM-GM proofs, with the same sharp equality case
items.statement: For a natural $n\ge1$ and nonnegative reals $a_0,\ldots,a_{n-1}$, put $A=(\sum_{k<n}a_k)/n$ and $G=(\prod_{k<n}a_k)^{1/n}$, using the unique nonnegative root. Five finite routes verify $\prod_{k<n}a_k\le A^n$, equivalently $G\le A$, with equality exactly when every entry is the same. They are Cauchy's forward-backward induction, ordinary induction by sum-preserving replacement, ordinary induction by product-preserving replacement, ordinary induction from the independently proved integer Bernoulli inequality, and binary averaging with geometric-mean padding. The last route stops after one padding argument, rather than the backward descent used by the first. No route invokes a derivative, logarithm, exponential, convergence or an unproved optimization theorem.

items.title: The PBW (monomial) basis theorem for KLR algebras
items.statement:
Let $Q$ be a KLR datum as in [[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]] and fix a reduced-expression system: for each $w\in S_n$ one reduced word $w=s_{i_1}\cdots s_{i_r}$, and for $
u\in I^n$ put $	au_w:=	au_{i_1}\cdots	au_{i_r}\in R_n(Q)$. Then the monomials $	au_wx_1^{a_1}\cdots x_n^{a_n}e(
u)$, over all $w\in S_n$, $a_1,\dots,a_n\ge0$ and $
u\in I^n$, form a $k$-basis of $R_n(Q)$; equivalently $R_n(Q)$ is a free $k$-module on these monomials, and $R( eta)$ has the corresponding basis. Moreover each $R( eta)$ has finite-dimensional homogeneous components, and the graded dimension of the summand $e(
u)R_n(Q)e(
u')$ is the formal Laurent Hilbert series counting the monomials (bounded below, equivalently the finite sum of the corresponding rational geometric series), so the graded ranks are independent of the parameters $Q$: for each fixed $ eta$, $\dim_kR( eta)_m<\infty$ for all $m$ and $R( eta)_m=0$ for $m\ll0$; if $I$ is finite the same holds for $R_n(Q)$. In particular $R( eta)$ is a locally finite graded algebra ; its degree-zero part need not be one-dimensional (already $x_1	au_1\in R(2\alpha_i)_0$ is a nontrivial idempotent).

items.title: Induction and restriction bimodules for KLR algebras
items.statement:
Let $Q$ be a KLR datum as in [[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]]. For $ eta,\gamma\in Q_+$ put $e( eta,\gamma):=\sum_{
u\in I^{ eta},
u'\in I^{\gamma}}e(
u\ast
u')\in R( eta+\gamma)$, where $
u\ast
u'$ is concatenation; this is an idempotent. The block inclusions $R( eta)\hookrightarrow R( eta+\gamma)$, $r\mapsto r\otimes1$ and $R(\gamma)\hookrightarrow R( eta+\gamma)$, $s\mapsto1\otimes s$ combine into an injective $k$-algebra map $R( eta)\otimes_kR(\gamma)	o R( eta+\gamma)$ whose image is the separated-block subalgebra of the corner $e( eta,\gamma)R( eta+\gamma)e( eta,\gamma)$; the inclusion generally is proper; in the diagram calculus it is horizontal concatenation of diagrams. **Induction** and **restriction** are the functors on graded left modules
$$\mathrm{Ind}_{ eta,\gamma}(M oxtimes N):=R( eta+\gamma)e( eta,\gamma)\otimes_{R( eta)\otimes_kR(\gamma)}(M\otimes_kN),\qquad \mathrm{Res}_{ eta,\gamma}L:=e( eta,\gamma)L,$$
where $\otimes_{R( eta)\otimes_kR(\gamma)}$ is the graded balanced tensor product of [[def-graded-balanced-tensor-product-and-homogeneous-hom]] (total-degree grading) and $M\otimes_kN$ carries the graded tensor product structure. Both functors are additive and degree-zero on degree-zero maps and extend to the direct sums over weights; the $R( eta+\gamma)e( eta,\gamma)$-side is a graded $(R( eta+\gamma),R( eta)\otimes_kR(\gamma))$-bimodule and $e( eta,\gamma)R( eta+\gamma)$ is its right-module counterpart, so the two tensor functors are of the two HA-18 sidedness types. Shifts satisfy $\mathrm{Ind}_{ eta,\gamma}(M\{r\} oxtimes N\{s\})\cong\mathrm{Ind}_{ eta,\gamma}(M oxtimes N)\{r+s\}$ and $\mathrm{Res}_{ eta,\gamma}(L\{r\})\cong(\mathrm{Res}_{ eta,\gamma}L)\{r\}$ ([[lem-graded-balanced-tensor-and-shift-isomorphisms]]). For a partial flag $ eta= eta_1+\cdots+ eta_r$ the iterated functors are defined by iteration, and the parenthesization-independent identification is the one consumed below.

items.title: Nil-Hecke idempotents and divided-power KLR projectives
items.statement:
Let $Q$ be a KLR datum as in [[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]]. For $i\in I$ and $n\ge1$ the subalgebra $R(n\alpha_i)$ is generated by the polynomial subalgebra $k[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ and the crossings $\tau_1,\dots,\tau_{n-1}$ with $\tau_a^2=0$ (because $Q_{ii}=0$), the braid and far commutation relations, and the nil-Hecke dot moves, i.e. it is the nil Hecke algebra of rank $n$; its PBW basis is $\{x_1^{a_1}\cdots x_n^{a_n}\tau_w\}_{a\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}^n,w\in S_n}$. Fix a reduced expression $w_0=s_{i_1}\cdots s_{i_{\binom n2}}$ of the longest element and put $\partial_{w_0}:=\tau_{i_1}\cdots\tau_{i_{\binom n2}}$ (independent of the reduced expression). The **divided-power idempotent** is
$$e_{i,n}:=x_1^{n-1}x_2^{n-2}\cdots x_{n-1}\,\partial_{w_0}\in R(n\alpha_i),$$
and its horizontal reflection is $\psi(e_{i,n}):=\partial_{w_0}x_1^{n-1}\cdots x_{n-1}$. Both are nonzero idempotents of degree $0$, and $e_{i,n}\ne0$ because the PBW basis separates the monomials involved. The **divided-power projective** is
$$P_{i,n}:=R(n\alpha_i)\,\psi(e_{i,n})\{-d_i\tbinom n2\},$$
where the shift is the one fixed by the source normalization: as a graded left module $R(n\alpha_i)\psi(e_{i,n})$ is the polynomial representation, it is indecomposable projective, and with this shift one has $R(n\alpha_i)\cong P_{i,n}^{\oplus[n]_{q_i}!}$ with $[n]_{q_i}!=\prod_{a=1}^n\frac{q_i^a-q_i^{-a}}{q_i-q_i^{-1}}$, so $P_{i,n}$ is the unique indecomposable projective summand up to shift and $\mathrm{End}_{R(n\alpha_i)}(P_{i,n})_0=k$. For a divided-power sequence $\theta=i_1^{(n_1)}\cdots i_r^{(n_r)}$ put $\beta=\sum_an_a\alpha_{i_a}$ and $P_\theta:=\mathrm{Ind}(P_{i_1,n_1}\boxtimes\cdots\boxtimes P_{i_r,n_r})$ along the ordered concatenation of the blocks; then $[P_\theta]$ represents the ordered product of these divided powers; one may reorder only by the proved commuting/Serre relations, and adjacent colours need not commute, and for a single colour $\theta=i^{(n)}$ one has the indecomposability above.

items.title: Graded Krull-Schmidt and shift-orbit bases for finitely generated KLR modules
items.statement:
Let $Q$ be a KLR datum as in [[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]] and $\beta\in Q_+$.
(i) Every finitely generated graded left $R(\beta)$-module has a decomposition into finitely many indecomposable graded modules, unique as a finite multiset of degree-zero graded isomorphism classes, including the actual shifts of their summands; in particular the category $\mathrm{GrMod}_0R(\beta)$ of finitely generated graded modules has the Krull-Schmidt property.
(ii) Every simple graded $R(\beta)$-module is finite-dimensional, killed by the augmentation ideal $\mathrm{Sym}^+(\beta)$ of the CENTRAL color-symmetric polynomial subalgebra C_beta; up to isomorphism and shift there are finitely many, and each has a projective cover which is finitely generated.
(iii) The split Grothendieck group $K_0(R(\beta))$ of finite graded projective modules is a free $\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$-module: the classes of the indecomposable finitely generated graded projectives, modulo grading shifts, form a basis with the shift action $q[P]=[P\{1\}]$; equivalently the classes of all finitely generated indecomposable graded projectives form a shift-orbit basis. Similarly $G_0(R(\beta))$ is free on the shift orbits of simple modules, and the Hom pairing of projective covers and simples has diagonal entries dim_k End^0(S_b), with the selected cover/simple shifts, under the Hom convention of [[def-projective-simple-hom-pairing-on-grothendieck-groups]].

items.title: Generic KLR induction and restriction adjunctions preserve projectives
items.statement:
Let Q be the KLR datum above and beta,gamma in Q_+. Put A=R(beta+gamma), B=R(beta) tensor_k R(gamma), e=e(beta,gamma), and c=(beta|gamma). The bimodules eA and Ae are ungraded free respectively as left and right B-modules, of rank binomial(|beta|+|gamma|,|beta|). As GRADED modules they are finite projective direct sums of the appropriate principal idempotent B-modules with labelled shuffle shifts: for each concatenated word xi=nu*eta the right-module summand e(xi)B has shift delta_R(w,xi)=deg(tau_w e(xi)); the left-module summand B e(xi) has shift delta_L(w,xi)=deg(e(xi)tau_w)=delta_R(w,w^-1 xi), using respectively the corresponding right/left minimal shuffle representatives. These degrees depend on the labels; no common shift for an entire B copy is asserted. Ind=Ae tensor_B - and Res=e(-) are exact, commute with internal shifts, and preserve finitely generated graded projectives. Ind is left adjoint to Res. The right adjoint of Res is Coind=HOM_B(eA,-), with (a f)(t)=f(ta), and the exact generic second-adjunction formula is
Coind_(beta,gamma)(M boxtimes N) ~= Ind_(gamma,beta)(N boxtimes M){c}.
Thus the second adjunction reverses the two blocks and has the displayed shift; same-ordered unshifted biadjunction is not asserted. The formula is an isomorphism of functors and holds on arbitrary graded B-modules after interpreting the right side with the block-flip equivalence. This is distinct from the cyclotomic E_i/F_i biadjunction theorem. Moreover, e_(beta,gamma) R(beta+gamma) e_(beta',gamma') has a finite Mackey filtration indexed by nonnegative four-block weight matrices ((a,b),(c,d)) with row sums beta,gamma and column sums beta',gamma'. Its subquotient is the corresponding composite four-block restriction, flip of the middle blocks and induction bimodule, shifted by -(b|c). The same statement holds for arbitrary numbers of blocks.

items.title: The KLR Cartan (graded Hom) pairing on the projective Grothendieck group
items.statement:
Let $Q$ be a KLR datum as in [[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]] and let $\psi$ be the horizontal-reflection anti-involution of $R(\beta)$ (reflection of diagrams about a horizontal axis, which reverses the order of crossings); for a finite graded left module $P$ let $P^{\psi}$ be the right module with $p\cdot r:=\psi(r)p$. For $\beta\in Q_+$ define the **Cartan pairing**
$$(\ [P],[Q]\ )_\beta:=\mathrm{gdim}_k\bigl(P^{\psi}\otimes_{R(\beta)}Q\bigr)\in\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]\cdot(\beta)_q,\qquad (\beta)_q:=\prod_i\prod_{a=1}^{\beta_i}\frac1{1-q^{2d_i a}},$$
for finite graded projective modules $P,Q$, where $\mathrm{gdim}_kM=\sum_{m\in\mathbb Z}q^m\dim_kM_m$; the tensor is over the graded algebra with the total-degree grading ([[def-graded-balanced-tensor-product-and-homogeneous-hom]]). Equivalently define the **hom pairing** $([P],[Q])'_\beta:=\mathrm{gdim}_k\operatorname{HOM}_{R(\beta)}(P,Q)$ ([[thm-projective-hom-pairing-is-additive-and-graded-sesquilinear]]); then $([P],[Q])'_\beta=([P^\#],[Q])_\beta$ for the graded left projective $P^\#:=\operatorname{HOM}_{R(\beta)}(P,R(\beta))^\psi$. Thus the tensor form is symmetric and bilinear; the Hom form is conjugate-linear in its first variable and linear in its second. For the tensor form $([P],q[Q])=q([P],[Q])$ and $(q[P],[Q])=q([P],[Q])$, while the Hom form obeys $h(q^r[P],q^s[Q])=q^{s-r}h([P],[Q])$. Both are additive, vanish on different-weight components, and descend to $K_0(R)=\bigoplus_\beta K_0(R(\beta))$: the tensor form is A-bilinear and the Hom form is A-sesquilinear (first variable conjugate-linear), with values in $\mathbb Q(q)$, more precisely the localization adjoining all $(1-q_i^{2a})^{-1}$; the values lie in $\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]\cdot(\beta)_q$ because $P^\psi\otimes_{R(\beta)}Q$ is a finite free graded module over the central color-symmetric polynomial subalgebra C_beta. Normalization: $([P_i],[P_i])=(1-q^{2d_i})^{-1}=(1-q_i^2)^{-1}$ and $([P_i],[P_j])=0$ for $i\ne j$.

items.title: Maximal KLR tails give a unique induction head and absolute simple modules
items.statement: Let R be any graded KLR datum in this page over any field k. For a finite-dimensional graded module M of weight beta set epsilon_i(M)=max{r:e(beta-r alpha_i,r alpha_i)M!=0}. If S is simple and r=epsilon_i(S)>0, there is a simple graded R(beta-r alpha_i)-module N with epsilon_i(N)=0 such that Delta_i^r S=N boxtimes L(i^r), where L(i^r) is the unique nil-Hecke simple up to shift. Conversely, for any such N, Ind(N boxtimes L(i^r)) has a unique simple graded head S, appearing once as a composition factor, with epsilon_i(S)=r and Delta_i^r S=N boxtimes L(i^r). Every other composition factor has smaller i-tail. The graded simples of every R(beta) remain simple without grading and are absolutely simple; all ordinary endomorphisms are k and nonzero homogeneous endomorphisms have degree0. The classes of normalized simples and their projective covers are therefore unscaled dual shift-orbit bases for the projective/simple Hom pairing. For each beta there is a finite family of ordered divided-power words Y_b whose normalized projective classes pair triangularly with the simple classes, with diagonal entries1 after choosing the simple grading shifts. Thus the selected [P(Y_b)] form an A-basis of K_0(R(beta)); arbitrary divided words span, but need not be a basis. The identical statements hold for maximal FIRST-color blocks, with epsilon_i^L(M)=max{r:e(r alpha_i,beta-r alpha_i)M!=0}, restriction Delta_i^(L,r), and induction Ind(L(i^r) boxtimes N).

items.title: The KLR Grothendieck ring satisfies the divided-power quantum Serre relations
items.statement:
Let $Q$ be a KLR datum as in [[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]] and let $K_0(R):=\bigoplus_{\beta\in Q_+}K_0(R(\beta))$ be the split Grothendieck group of finite graded projective modules with the shift action $q[P]=[P\{1\}]$ ([[def-split-grothendieck-group-of-an-additive-category]], [[def-graded-grothendieck-group-shift-module-and-cartan-map]], [[lem-klr-module-categories-are-krull-schmidt-with-shift-orbit-bases]]).
(i) The induction product $[P][P']:=[\mathrm{Ind}_{\beta,\gamma}(P\boxtimes P')]$ for $P\in K_0(R(\beta)),P'\in K_0(R(\gamma))$ makes $K_0(R)$ a unital associative $\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$-algebra, and $[\mathrm{Res}]$ makes it a coassociative counital $\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$-coalgebra; with the twisted multiplication on $K_0(R)\otimes K_0(R)$ defined by $(x_1\otimes x_2)(x_1'\otimes x_2')=q^{-(|x_2|\mid|x_1'|)}x_1x_1'\otimes x_2x_2'$ on homogeneous elements, $[\mathrm{Res}]$ is an algebra homomorphism ([[thm-klr-induction-and-restriction-are-biadjoint-and-preserve-projectives]], KL I Propositions 3.1-3.2).
(ii) With the divided-power projectives $P_{i,n}$ of [[def-divided-power-klr-idempotents-and-projectives]], the classes $[P_{i,n}]$ satisfy, for all $i\ne j$, the divided-power quantum Serre relation
$$\sum_{a+b=-a_{ij}+1}(-1)^a[P_{i,a}]\,[P_{j,1}]\,[P_{i,b}]=0\qquad\text{in }K_0(R),$$
with the convention $[P_{i,0}]=1=[P_{j,0}]$, and satisfy $[P_{i,1}][P_{j,1}]=[P_{j,1}][P_{i,1}]$ when $a_{ij}=0$; these are the defining relations of the negative half.
(iii) Consequently the assignment $\theta_i\mapsto[P_{i,1}]$ extends uniquely to an algebra homomorphism $\gamma:A f\to K_0(R)$ of the divided-power form of the negative half, with $\gamma(\theta_i^{(n)})=[P_{i,n}]$ and $\gamma(\theta_{i_1}^{(n_1)}\cdots\theta_{i_r}^{(n_r)})=[\mathrm{Ind}(P_{i_1,n_1}\boxtimes\cdots\boxtimes P_{i_r,n_r})]$; $\gamma$ is compatible with the coproducts ($r$ on $A f$ and $[\mathrm{Res}]$ on $K_0(R)$) and with the bar involutions, and it is $\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$-linear.

items.title: The KLR Cartan pairing is the Lusztig-normalized half form
items.statement:
Let $Q$ be a KLR datum as in [[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]], let $B_K$ be the normalized Lusztig-Kashiwara form on the negative half of [[def-the-lusztig-kashiwara-bilinear-form-on-the-negative-quantum-half]] and put $B_L:=C_
u B_K$ on the weight component $
u$, $C_
u=\prod_i(1-q_i^2)^{-
u_i}$, the Lusztig-normalized form of [[lem-lusztig-and-kashiwara-normalizations-match-by-root-color]]. Then for homogeneous $x,y\in A f_
u$ the Cartan pairing of [[def-the-klr-cartan-pairing]] satisfies
$$(\gamma(x),\gamma(y))_{KLR}=B_L(x,y)=C_
u\,B_K(x,y),$$
where $\gamma:A f	o K_0(R)$ is the algebra homomorphism of [[thm-klr-projective-grothendieck-group-satisfies-the-negative-quantum-serre-relations]]. Equivalently, the two bilinear forms are equal under the identification of divided-power classes; in particular the KLR pairing is $\mathbb Q(q)$-nondegenerate on each finite weight component $A f_
u\otimes_A\mathbb Q(q)$ after extending scalars, and $(\gamma(x),\gamma(y))'_{KLR}=B_L(\overline{x},y)$, where bar acts on the first input, not on the scalar value for the hom pairing. On generators: $([P_i],[P_j])=\delta_{ij}(1-q_i^2)^{-1}=B_L(	heta_i,	heta_j)$ and $([P_{i,n}],[P_{i,n}])=B_L(	heta_i^{(n)},	heta_i^{(n)})=\prod_{a=1}^n(1-q_i^{2a})^{-1}$.

items.title: The KLR category categorifies the negative quantum half
items.statement:
Let $Q$ be a KLR datum as in [[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]] over any field $k$. Then the homomorphism $\gamma:A f\to K_0(R)$ of [[thm-klr-projective-grothendieck-group-satisfies-the-negative-quantum-serre-relations]] is an isomorphism of $\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$-algebras and of $\mathbb N[I]$-graded twisted bialgebras:
(i) **Surjectivity.** Every class in $K_0(R(\beta))$ is a $\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$-linear combination of classes of divided-power projectives $[P_\theta]$, $\theta$ a sequence of divided powers of weight $\beta$; hence $\gamma$ is onto.
(ii) **Injectivity.** $\gamma$ is injective, because it preserves the forms by [[thm-klr-cartan-pairing-agrees-with-lusztigs-bilinear-form]] and the source form $B_L$ (equivalently $B_K$) is nondegenerate on each finite weight component.
(iii) **Compatibility.** $\gamma$ intertwines the multiplications ($[\mathrm{Ind}]$ against the product in $A f$), the comultiplications ($[\mathrm{Res}]$ against $r$), the bar involutions and the forms; the free A-rank of $K_0(R(\beta))$ equals the free A-rank of $A f_\beta$; no rank or dimension comparison of the infinite-dimensional algebra $R(\beta)$ itself with $f_\beta$ is asserted.
Equivalently, $K_0(R)$ is a free $A$-module with the classes of the indecomposable graded projective $R$-modules as a shift-orbit basis ([[lem-klr-module-categories-are-krull-schmidt-with-shift-orbit-bases]]), and the divided-power classes span; the triangularly selected classes $[P(Y_b)]$ form an A-basis, whereas the family of all divided-power words is generally redundant.

items.title: Self-dual KLR projectives have positive first-block divided-string leading terms
items.statement:
For any graded KLR datum in this page and any field k, each finite-dimensional graded simple shift orbit has a unique representative S_b self-dual for D(M)_d=Hom_k(M_-d,k), with action (a f)(m)=f(psi(a)m). Its projective cover P_b, normalized by Hom^0(P_b,S_b)=k, satisfies P_b#=P_b for P#=HOM_R(P,R)^psi. These are unique normalizations. Induction of two self-dual finite projectives is self-dual. If epsilon_i^L(S_b)=r>0 and Delta_i^(L,r) S_b=L(i^r) boxtimes S_a with epsilon_i^L(S_a)=0, normalized as above, then
[P_(i,r)][P_a]=[P_b]+sum_(epsilon_i^L(S_c)>r) m_c(q)[P_c],
with m_c in N[q,q^-1], each invariant under q->q^-1. Under gamma the integral LEFT divided-string ideal I_(i,>=n)=sum_(r>=n) F_i^(r) U_A^- is the A-span of [P_b] with epsilon_i^L(S_b)>=n. Consequently, if the normalized projective classes are known to be a SIGNED lower-global set, this leading coefficient1 identifies them with the POSITIVE lower-global set using the general adapted right-string recursion; no finite-ADE canonical-comparison theorem is needed. For the conclusions compared with the quantum half and the conditional lower-global/LEFT-string recursion, carry the inherited Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) of those quantum suppliers; the generic finite module duality/parity/Frobenius arguments themselves are choice-free.

items.title: Self-dual indecomposable KLR projectives give the lower global basis (symmetric type)
items.statement: Assume the Cartan datum of [[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]] has symmetric Cartan matrix $a_{ij}=a_{ji}$ and uses the quiver normalization $d_i=1$ for every $i$, the field $k$ has characteristic $0$, and the KLR parameters are the quiver-geometric ones (the specialization attached to a finite quiver without loops, with arbitrary arrow multiplicities $h_{ij}$ and $a_{ij}=-(h_{ij}+h_{ji})$: $Q_{ij}(u,v)=(-1)^{h_{ij}}(u-v)^{h_{ij}+h_{ji}}$ for $i\ne j$, in the fixed native crossing-sign convention; arbitrary parameter changes, including a global replacement by $u+v$, require their own proved gauge equivalence). Then, normalizing each indecomposable finitely generated graded projective $R(\beta)$-module to be self-dual for the contravariant graded projective duality $P^\#=\operatorname{HOM}_{R(\beta)}(P,R(\beta))^\psi$ ($P\cong P^\#$ after the unique normalizing shift), the map $b\mapsto[P_b]$ is a bijection between the lower global basis $B(\infty)$ of the negative half ([[def-lower-global-basis-of-a-quantum-highest-weight-module]], [[thm-existence-bar-invariance-and-uniqueness-of-the-lower-global-basis]]) and the shift-orbit basis of $K_0(R)$ by self-dual indecomposable projectives; under the isomorphism $\gamma$ of [[thm-klr-categorification-of-the-negative-quantum-half]] one has $\gamma(G(b))=[P_b]$ for the lower global lift $G(b)$, and the identification is compatible with the based quotient of [[thm-global-basis-projection-from-the-negative-half-to-a-highest-weight-module]]. No extension to arbitrary KLR parameters or to non-symmetric Cartan data is asserted here; any such extension requires its own parameter-change invariance theorem.

decline_pages.title: Cyclotomic KLR Algebras and Highest-Weight Categorification

items.title: The cyclotomic KLR quotient at a dominant integral weight
The minimal-parabolic KLR diagram proof category
items.statement:
Fix a symmetrizable Cartan datum with real simple roots, a field $k$ placed in degree zero, and admissible weighted-homogeneous KLR polynomials $Q_{jk}$ as in [[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]]. Write $b_{jk}=d_j a_{jk}=b_{kj}$ and fix a color $i$. The **minimal-parabolic KLR diagram proof category** $\mathcal P_i$ is the additive graded $k$-linear category of weighted oriented diagrams with objects weights, downward generators $G_j:\mu\to\mu-\alpha_j$ for every $j$, and the single upward generator $H_i:\mu\to\mu+\alpha_i$. Horizontal composition reads chronological negative words from the vacuum outward. Take additive sums and grading shifts; use idempotent completion when speaking of word projectives. The generator $H_i$ denotes normalized projective restriction: in the polynomial flag realization at input weight $h$, it is basic reversed flag restriction shifted by $-d_i(1+h)$; it is distinct from unshifted basic restriction.

Dots have degree $2d_j$ and downward crossings have degree $-b_{jk}$. The native crossing is $\tau$, with native equal-color divided difference $(f-sf)/(x_1-x_2)$; for expressing the source diagram equations put $\kappa=-\tau$ for **every** color pair, retaining dots, idempotents and $Q$. Thus the native cubic braid numerator is globally opposite to the source numerator, while the quadratic $Q$ is unchanged. Impose the full downward KLR relations of the cited Definition.

At input $i$-weight $h=\langle h_i,\mu\rangle$, the first unit $1\to H_iG_i$ and second counit $H_iG_i\to1$ have degree $d_i(1-h)$; the first counit $G_iH_i\to1$ and second unit $1\to G_iH_i$ have degree $d_i(1+h)$. Impose both adjunction triangles with their adjacent input-weight shifts and cyclicity of the dot. For $h\ge0$ prescribe the degree-zero rank-one matrix $H_iG_i\cong G_iH_i\oplus\bigoplus_{r=0}^{h-1}1\{d_i(1-h+2r)\}$; for $h<0$ prescribe $G_iH_i\cong H_iG_i\oplus\bigoplus_{r=0}^{-h-1}1\{d_i(1+h+2r)\}$. The off-diagonal crossing component is the cup--source-crossing--cap transfer, and the identity columns/rows are the indicated dotted units/counits. Adjoin its actual inverse blocks, requiring both matrix inverse equations; the dotted dual rows/columns are the finite triangular coefficient convolution determined by bubble inversion, and the crossing block satisfies the local cross-and-cap equations. In particular, at $h<0$, if $r_h:G_iH_i\to H_iG_i\oplus D_{-h}$ is this matrix, $r_h^{-1}j_H$ and $p_Hr_h$ are the specified natural inclusion/projection with product $1_{H_iG_i}$.

The normalized far-left bubble series $A_\mu(t),\mathsf H_\mu(t)$ have constant coefficient1 and satisfy $A_\mu(t)\mathsf H_\mu(t)=1$. Genuine negative-degree bubbles vanish. The $A$ coefficient with index $m$ is the clockwise bubble with $-h-1+m$ dots when this count is nonnegative, extended by formal inverse coefficients otherwise; its degree is $2d_i m$. The other family has dot count $h-1+\ell$ and degree $2d_i\ell$. Impose the finite-coefficient slides verified on the monic flag model: adjoining an $i$ root $z$ divides $A$ by $(1-zt)^2$ and multiplies $\mathsf H$ by that factor; adjoining a spectator root $y$ of color $j\ne i$ multiplies $A$ by $q_{ij}^{\rm rev}(y,t)=t^{-a_{ij}}Q_{ij}(t^{-1},y)/t_{ij}$, where $t_{ij}$ is the nonzero extremal coefficient, and divides $\mathsf H$ by it. Every reciprocal coefficient is defined by the finite recursion with constant coefficient1.

Impose the rank-one cross-and-cap equations: the two oppositely oriented single-crossing curls are the signed sums of a dotted uncrossed cap and an opposite bubble over indices $a+b=-1$; the two opposite-crossing cancellations are the straight pair plus the dotted cup--bubble--cap sums over $a+b+c=-1$, with the corresponding opposite-orientation signs. A negative dot count on an open strand is zero. These are the four source $\kappa$ equations, converted globally by $\kappa=-\tau$. For $j\ne i$, the two sideways crossings, defined as the two adjunction mates of the downward crossing, cancel in the two orders with the nonzero scalars $t_{ij}$ and $t_{ji}$; scale the reverse mate by the corresponding inverse to obtain the mixed isomorphism $H_iG_j\cong G_jH_i$, commuting with the $j$ dot. These are relations of this proof-tool category. Their consistency and homogeneous realization are established by the polynomial flag model, rather than assumed for the actual cyclotomic induction/restriction action.

items.title: Mixed relations, local nilpotence and weights give the integrable quantum action
items.statement: Let $V=\bigoplus_{\mu\in P}V_\mu$ be a label-weight-graded $\mathbb Q(q)$-vector space with its toral operators, and operators $E_i,F_i$ of weights $\alpha_i,-\alpha_i$. Assume the toral conjugation and mixed relations, and local nilpotence of each $E_i,F_i$; vectors have finite label support. Then these operators uniquely define an integrable type-one $U_q(\mathfrak g)$-module for EVERY real symmetrizable datum. Every vector has a finite rank-one $U_i$ orbit and the admissible Kashiwara $i$-string decomposition applies. Finite weight spaces do not imply finite-dimensional full-$\mathfrak g$ orbits; no such conclusion is asserted.

items.title: Cyclotomic KLR induction and restriction functors
items.statement: Use the standard graded quotient of [[def-cyclotomic-klr-quotient-at-a-dominant-weight]]. Put $A=R^\Lambda(\beta)$, $B=R^\Lambda(\beta+\alpha_i)$ and $e=e(\beta,i)$. Right append defines a graded CORNER homomorphism $\iota_i:A\to eBe$, sending $1_A$ to $e$, $e(\nu)$ to $e(\nu i)$, and the old dots/crossings to their positions in the first $|\beta|$ strands. It is not asserted injective and $e$ may be zero. Define $F_i^{\rm basic}(M)=Be\otimes_A M$ and $E_i^{\rm basic}(N)=eN$. These additive functors preserve shifts and satisfy $F_i^{\rm basic}\dashv E_i^{\rm basic}$ by degree-zero tensor-Hom evaluation. $F_i$ increases ROOT degree by $\alpha_i$ and decreases module weight $\Lambda-\beta$ by $\alpha_i$; restriction does the reverse. Both composites are endofunctors at a fixed root degree. The same underlying definitions apply ungraded to monic deformations. Exactness/projective preservation and the shifted second adjunction are theorems below.

items.title: Cyclotomic dot annihilators, finite-dimensional blocks, and finite root strings
items.statement: Let $k$ be any field and let $Q$ satisfy (Q1)–(Q4) for a real symmetrizable Cartan datum with finite color set. For monic $a_j(u)\in k[u]$ of degree $\lambda_j\ge0$, impose $a_{\nu_1}(x_1)e(\nu)=0$ and write $R^a(\beta)$ for the resulting ordinary quotient. Every dot has a scalar-coefficient monic annihilator in each fixed block, every $R^a(\beta)$ is finite dimensional over $k$, and, for fixed $\beta,i$, $R^a(\beta+m\alpha_i)=0$ for all sufficiently large $m$. Thus right-append induction has finite $i$-strings. In the standard homogeneous specialization $a_j(u)=u^{\lambda_j}$, every dot is nilpotent and these are statements about the induced graded algebra and graded functors. For an inhomogeneous monic specialization the assertions are ungraded; no graded highest-weight Grothendieck identification is included.

items.title: Generic KLR induction and restriction: mixed relations and the opposite-end exact sequence
The minimal-parabolic polynomial flag model realizes the graded diagram relations
items.statement:
Fix a color $i$ and the formal proof category of [[def-minimal-parabolic-klr-diagram-proof-category]], on a symmetrizable real Cartan datum with finite index set and arbitrary field $k$. Use the native KLR parameters of [[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]], degrees of [[def-klr-grading-and-diagrammatic-composition]], PBW convention of [[thm-klr-pbw-basis-theorem]], and nil-Hecke matrix/idempotent convention of [[def-divided-power-klr-idempotents-and-projectives]]. Then the following polynomial flag construction realizes all the defining graded diagram relations of that formal category, including its rank-one cross/cap, bubble-slide/inversion and mixed-color cup/cap relations; it asserts a representation of the formal proof category, not faithfulness or a cyclotomic quotient identification.

Choose a color order with $i$ last. For spectator alphabets $Y_j$ of sizes $m_j$ ($j\ne i$), put $C=\bigotimes_{j\ne i}k[Y_j]^{S_{m_j}}$, $r=m_i$, $A_{ij}=-a_{ij}$, $t_{ij}=[u^{A_{ij}}]Q_{ij}(u,v)\in k^\times$, $q_{ij}=Q_{ij}/t_{ij}$, and choose a monic framing polynomial $a_i(u)$ of degree $\lambda_i$. Initially its coefficients have their universal homogeneous degrees, so all formulas are graded; the standard specialization is $a_i(u)=u^{\lambda_i}$. Set
$$p_m(u)=a_i(u)\prod_{j\ne i}\prod_{y\in Y_j}q_{ij}(u,y),\qquad N=\lambda_i+\sum_{j\ne i}A_{ij}m_j,\qquad h_m=N-2r.$$
Let $c_r(u)=u^r-e_1u^{r-1}+\cdots+(-1)^re_r$. The vertex ring $L_m$ is the monic factor ring for $p_m=c_rb_{N-r}$: equivalently it is $C[e_1,\ldots,e_r]$ modulo all coefficients beyond degree $N-r$ of the monic expansion $p_m/c_r$. It is finite free over $C$, of rank $\binom Nr$, and is zero for $r>N$. Its $i$ flag is $B_m=L_m[z]/b_{N-r}(z)$, free of rank $N-r$ over $L_m$ and rank $r+1$ over $L_{m+i}$, with target root alphabet obtained by adjoining $z$. The underlying spectator flag is $C_m^j=L_m[y]$; its target action appends $y$ to $Y_j$ and replaces $p_m$ by $p_mq_{ij}(u,y)$.

Every downward generator carries the ordered shift
$$s_j(m)=-2d_jm_j+\sum_{\ell>j}(-b_{j\ell})m_\ell.$$
Thus $G_i=F_i^{\mathrm{basic}}$ is the $B_m\{-2d_ir\}$ tensor functor; $G_j$ for $j\ne i$ is the $C_m^j\{s_j(m)\}$ tensor functor. The basic reversed $i$ flag is $E_i^{\mathrm{basic}}=B_m\otimes_{L_{m+i}}-$ without a shift, whereas the formal upward generator at INPUT vertex $m$ is
$$H_i(m)=E_i^{\mathrm{basic}}(m)\{-d_i(1+h_m)\}.$$
These are distinct conventions. The basic flags have degree-zero $F_i^{\mathrm{basic}}\dashv E_i^{\mathrm{basic}}$ and $E_i^{\mathrm{basic}}\{t_i(m)\}\dashv F_i^{\mathrm{basic}}$, where $t_i(m)=-2d_i(h_m-1)$. At vertex $m$ the formal first unit and second cap have degree $d_i(1-h_m)$, and the formal first cap and second unit have degree $d_i(1+h_m)$.

All four maps are explicit dual-basis maps of the two monic coefficient forms on $B_m$: $\tau_{\mathrm{old}}:B_m\to L_m$ extracts $z^{N-r-1}$ and has degree $-2d_i(N-r-1)$; $\tau_{\mathrm{new}}:B_m\to L_{m+i}$ extracts $z^r$ and has degree $-2d_ir$. The first cap is $b_1\otimes b_2\mapsto\tau_{\mathrm{new}}(b_1b_2)$ and first cup is its dual-power-basis Casimir; the second cap/cup use $\tau_{\mathrm{old}}$. For a monic polynomial $f$ their Casimir is the polynomial kernel $K_f(X,Y)=(f(X)-f(Y))/(X-Y)$ in the two-root quotient.

Source crossings are $\kappa=-\tau_{\mathrm{native}}$ for EVERY color pair. Source equal-color operators are $(s-1)/(X-Y)$; source unequal operators are the switch/quotient in the increasing-color direction and switch times $Q$ in the reverse direction. Thus native operators are their negatives, and both actual crossing degrees are $-b_{jk}$ with the ordered shifts above. On the $i,j$ pair the successive underlying rings are $D_1=L_m[y,z]/(b(z)q_{ij}(z,y))$ and $D_0=L_m[y,z]/b(z)$, with source maps $\pi:D_1\to D_0$ and $f\mapsto Q_{ij}(z,y)f:D_0\to D_1$. Their normalized opposite-sideways composites have scalars $t_{ij}$ and $t_{ji}$; in the NE/SW-$i$, NW/SE-$j$ source orientation the double-mate ratio is $t_{ji}/t_{ij}$. Native minus signs leave the two-crossing scalars and ratio unchanged. Basic $E_iG_j\cong(G_jE_i)\{-b_{ij}\}$; normalized formal $H_iG_j\cong G_jH_i$ is unshifted.

The canonical rank-one $\rho$ and its inverse, the same-color cross/cap equations, the bubble series $\Phi_i(u)=p_m(u)/c_r(u)^2$ and its reciprocal, and the finite coefficient bubble-slide identities are realized by the stated polynomial maps. In particular the normalized positive $h$ identity columns have degrees $d_i(1-h+2k)$ for $0\le k<h$, and the negative branch uses the inverse crossing plus the dot/cap rows. All polynomial pairings and relations persist after arbitrary monic coefficient specialization as UNGRADED identities. Such a specialization does not assert nilpotence, a homogeneous trace degree, or a highest-weight $K_0$ claim. No geometry, characteristic restriction, or one-dimensional-Hom hypothesis is imposed.

items.title: One-step simple restriction and induction, and the first-dot index
items.statement: Let k be any field and R(Q) the graded KLR algebra for a real symmetrizable Cartan datum and any homogeneous Q satisfying the standing symmetry and nonzero extremal-coefficient conditions. Graded simple modules are compared up to internal shift. For a simple S of root weight beta and r=epsilon_i(S)>0, its ordinary one-step last-i restriction has a single simple graded socle and a single simple graded head, each once and of the same shift orbit, with epsilon_i=r-1; its maximum-epsilon composition part has coefficient a grading shift of [r]_i. The last-dot nilpotence index on that restriction is exactly r. The first-end statements hold with epsilon_i^L and the first dot. For every n>=1, Ind(S boxtimes L(i^n)) has a unique simple graded head f_i^n S, occurring once in its whole composition series, with epsilon_i=r+n (also when r=0); all other constituents have smaller epsilon_i. One-step simple socle and simple induction head are partial inverses. A simple S survives the first-strand cyclotomic quotient with exponents lambda_i exactly when epsilon_i^L(S)<=lambda_i for all i. Right restriction preserves surviving simples, while projected right induction has the same simple head when that generic head survives and is zero otherwise. These are shift-orbit assertions and do not assert factorial socle multiplicity.

items.title: PBW and bubble normal form in the minimal-parabolic diagram category
items.statement: Fix a color $i$. In the formal graded minimal-parabolic proof category of [[def-minimal-parabolic-klr-diagram-proof-category]], the reduced perfect-matching diagrams, dot monomials on their open components, and monomials in the independent far-left normalized $i$-bubble coefficients form a basis of every morphism space. In particular, at all-downward boundaries of weight difference $\beta$, the morphism space is the corresponding KLR PBW corner tensored with the polynomial ring in one positive bubble family; the opposite/fake family is its coefficientwise reciprocal. The graded polynomial flag models of [[lem-minimal-parabolic-polynomial-flag-model-realizes-the-graded-diagram-relations]], with universal monic framing and arbitrarily large auxiliary framing at each fixed physical source weight, are jointly faithful. The assertion is about this formal proof category before cyclotomic quotient transfer.

items.title: Cyclotomic induction is projective on the right
The cyclotomic cap-off quotient has no extra downward relations
items.statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be dominant, $\lambda_j=\langle h_j,\Lambda\rangle$, and let $\mathcal P_i$ be [[def-minimal-parabolic-klr-diagram-proof-category]], with its homogeneous polynomial realization and PBW/bubble normal form. Fix monic $a_j(u)=u^{\lambda_j}+\sum_{r<\lambda_j}c_{j,r}u^r$. For the standard graded cyclotomic quotient take $a_j(u)=u^{\lambda_j}$ as in [[def-cyclotomic-klr-quotient-at-a-dominant-weight]]. More generally first take universal graded coefficients of degree $2d_j(\lambda_j-r)$; arbitrary monic specializations over the field are interpreted as ungraded.

In the representable category $\mathcal P_i(\Lambda)$, let $J$ be the ideal generated by $1_{H_iv_\Lambda}$ and $a_j(x)1_{G_jv_\Lambda}$ for every $j$, closed under arbitrary vertical pre/postcomposition and horizontal whiskering by the allowed 1-morphisms. For downward words $\mu,\nu$ of the same weight $\beta$, include their ordinary KLR corner by the PBW/bubble normal form. Then
$$J\cap e(\nu)R(\beta)e(\mu)=e(\nu)I_a(\beta)e(\mu),\qquad I_a(\beta)=\sum_j R(\beta)a_j(x_1)e(j,\beta-\alpha_j)R(\beta).$$
The vacuum bubble specialization is forced by these generators: $A_\Lambda(t)=1+c_{i,\lambda_i-1}t+\cdots+c_{i,0}t^{\lambda_i}$ and $\mathsf H_\Lambda=A_\Lambda^{-1}$. Consequently the map from the ordinary monic cyclotomic corner to the downward-word Hom corner of $\mathcal P_i(\Lambda)/J$ is an isomorphism, with composition corresponding to multiplication. This holds over every degree-zero field for the entire admissible homogeneous $Q$ family, without finite-type or characteristic-zero restrictions. Inhomogeneous monic specializations assert the ungraded corner equality, not a graded quantum-action conclusion.

items.title: The two-colour jump formula and strict elementary embeddings
items.statement: Let k be any field and R(Q) the graded KLR algebra for a real symmetrizable Cartan datum and any homogeneous Q satisfying the standing symmetry and nonzero extremal-coefficient conditions. Graded simple modules are compared up to internal shift. Set c_i(S)=epsilon_i^L(S) and J_i(S)=max{n>=0:c_i(f_i^n S)=c_i(S)}. This maximum is finite and J_i(S)=epsilon_i(S)+c_i(S)-<h_i,beta>. For i!=j one has c_i(f_j S)=c_i(S); for j=i it stays constant or increases by1, and increase is equivalent to f_i S=f_i^L S and to simplicity of Ind(S,L(i)). Once it increases, it increases at every later right-i step. Put wt(S)=-beta and phi_i=epsilon_i+<h_i,wt>. The maps Psi_i(S)=(e_i^L)^c_i(S) S tensor b_i(-c_i(S)) are strict injective elementary-crystal maps, and every nonvacuum simple has positive extraction at some i. The simple graph is lowering-generated with every generic f_i nonzero. In any first-strand cyclotomic quotient containing S the actual surviving lowering length is lambda_i+epsilon_i(S)-<h_i,beta>. All containing-weight arguments take place in the auxiliary primitive-coroot finite-support datum, leaving R,A,D,Q unchanged, so no positive-dominant-label assumption on the original P is added. Linear divided restriction/G_0 operators satisfy the quantum Serre relation; the simple-socle crystal operators are not asserted to satisfy a linear Serre identity.

items.title: The categorical $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ commutator for cyclotomic KLR functors
items.statement:
Let $R^\Lambda$ be the cyclotomic KLR algebra of [[def-cyclotomic-klr-quotient-at-a-dominant-weight]], let $E^\Lambda_i,F^\Lambda_i$ be the functors of [[def-cyclotomic-klr-induction-and-restriction-functors]], and read the composites $E^\Lambda_iF^\Lambda_i$ and $F^\Lambda_iE^\Lambda_i$ as endofunctors of $\mathrm{Mod}(R^\Lambda(\beta))$ via the weight bookkeeping fixed there. Put $\lambda:=\Lambda-\beta$ and $q_i:=q^{d_i}$ ([[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]).
(a) If $\langle h_i,\lambda\rangle\ge0$, there is a natural isomorphism of endofunctors of $\mathrm{Mod}(R^\Lambda(\beta))$
$$q_i^{-2}F^\Lambda_iE^\Lambda_i\oplus\bigoplus_{k=0}^{\langle h_i,\lambda\rangle-1}q_i^{2k}\,\mathrm{Id}\;\cong\;E^\Lambda_iF^\Lambda_i.$$
(b) If $\langle h_i,\lambda\rangle\le0$, there is a natural isomorphism of endofunctors of $\mathrm{Mod}(R^\Lambda(\beta))$
$$q_i^{-2}F^\Lambda_iE^\Lambda_i\;\cong\;E^\Lambda_iF^\Lambda_i\oplus\bigoplus_{k=0}^{-\langle h_i,\lambda\rangle-1}q_i^{-2k-2}\,\mathrm{Id}.$$
Applied to the object $R^\Lambda(\beta)$ the same computation gives an isomorphism of graded $R^\Lambda(\beta)$-bimodules obtained from $F^\Lambda_iE^\Lambda_iR^\Lambda(\beta)$ and $E^\Lambda_iF^\Lambda_iR^\Lambda(\beta)$ by the displayed summands ([[def-graded-ring-module-bimodule-and-internal-shift]] for the shift conventions).

items.title: Coherent graded biadjunction and the crossing mates
items.statement:
For the standard homogeneous first-strand cyclotomic quotient over any field and every homogeneous Q1–Q4 datum, use basic right-append induction $F_i$ from $ eta$ to $ eta+\alpha_i$ and basic restriction $E_i$ in the reverse direction. Put $h=\langle h_i,\Lambda- etaangle$ and $t_i( eta)=2d_i(1-h)=(\alpha_i|\alpha_i)-2(\Lambda- eta|\alpha_i)$. There are explicit homogeneous bimodule units and counits with both triangle identities giving $E_i\{t_i( eta)\}\dashv F_i\dashv E_i$ on all graded module categories. They preserve the standard dot-cyclic and same-color crossing-mate identities and the coherent different-color double-mate identity: for $p_
u=	au_r e(
u)$ with bottom adjacent colors $(i,j)$, $i
e j$, its double right mate is $(t_{ji}/t_{ij})p_
u$, where $t_{ij}$ is the coefficient of $u^{-a_{ij}}$ in $Q_{ij}(u,v)$ and the strand of color $i$ runs SW to NE. Equivalently the associated right closure satisfies $\operatorname{cl}(p_
u a)=(t_{ji}/t_{ij})\operatorname{cl}(a p_
u)$ for $a\in e(
u)R^\Lambda( eta)e(s_r
u)$; dots, idempotents and equal-color crossings have ratio $1$. The corresponding arbitrary monic field quotients have the same underlying ungraded biadjunction and ordered crossing-mate identities after forgetting internal shifts. No Frobenius, integral Grothendieck-module or crystal theorem is a premise.

items.title: Normalized cyclotomic functors give an integrable quantum action
items.statement: For the standard graded quotient over arbitrary $k$ and graded admissible $Q$, let $h=\langle h_i,\Lambda-\beta\rangle$. On projective $K_0$ take $F_i=F_i^{\rm basic}$ and $E_i=q_i^{1-h}E_i^{\rm basic}$ on input $\beta+i$ to output $\beta$. On module $G_0$ take the KK action $E_i=E_i^{\rm basic}$ and $F_i=q_i^{1-h}F_i^{\rm basic}$ on input $\beta$; also the canonical action with the SAME shifts as projectives. The torus acts on root component $\beta$ by $K_a=q^{\langle a,\Lambda-\beta\rangle}$. Each action satisfies all mixed relations, and $E_i,F_i$ are locally nilpotent. After scalar extension to $\mathbb Q(q)$ these are integrable type-one $U_q(\mathfrak g)$-modules. This does not assert a decomposition into finite-dimensional full-$\mathfrak g$ submodules and does not cover ungraded monic deformations.

items.title: The word-mirror involution of a KLR algebra and the quantum star
Cyclotomic KLR algebras are finite-dimensional graded symmetric algebras
items.statement: For the STANDARD graded cyclotomic quotient over any degree-zero field and admissible graded real symmetrizable KLR datum, every block $B=R^\Lambda(\beta)$ is finite-dimensional, all dots are nilpotent, and $R^\Lambda(\beta+n\alpha_i)=0$ for large $n$. Put $\operatorname{def}_\Lambda(\beta)=(\Lambda,\beta)-(\beta,\beta)/2$. A nonzero block has a perfect symmetric homogeneous functional $\operatorname{tr}_\beta:B\to k$ of degree $t_\beta=-2\operatorname{def}_\Lambda(\beta)$; on a zero block perfectness is vacuous and the functional is zero. Thus $DB\cong B\{t_\beta\}$ as graded bimodules. For finite projective $P$, with $P^\#=\operatorname{HOM}_B(P,B)^\psi$, one has $D_\psi P\cong P^\#\{t_\beta\}$, so vector duality preserves projectives. This does not assert $P^\#=P$ for every shifted projective, nor self-duality of every indecomposable finite module. For arbitrary monic deformation polynomials the separate conclusion is finite-dimensional and symmetric UNGRADED, with finite root strings and monic dot annihilators; nilpotence and homogeneous trace degree are not asserted. In rank one the standard trace is the top coefficient on $k[x]/x^{\lambda_i}$ and has degree $-2d_i(\lambda_i-1)$.

items.title: Canonical elementary crystal extraction and highest-weight survivors
items.statement: For every real symmetrizable Cartan datum, the canonical negative-half crystal has strict elementary embeddings Psi_i(b)=bar b tensor b_i(-c_i(b)), where c_i(b)=epsilon_i(star b), bar b=(e_i^star)^c_i(b)b, c_i(bar b)=0, and every nonvacuum vertex has positive extraction for some i. The negative-half reversal star permutes B(infinity) without signs; this unsigned conclusion is proved from the existing signed lattice theorem and positive highest-weight tensor residues, not assumed. The survivors of pi_lambda are exactly c_i(b)<=lambda_i for all i; with weight lambda+wt(b), inherited raising and surviving lowering, and epsilon/phi, they are B(lambda). Any two lowering-generated, everywhere-lowerable negative crystals with strict nonpositive elementary extractions and positive extraction at every nonvacuum vertex are uniquely isomorphic by their lowering words; the proof uses finite color cycles and terminates after a height bound. Consequently for any field and any general homogeneous nondegenerate Q of the first two lemmas, the shift-orbit simple-module crystal is canonically B(infinity), its first-strand cyclotomic simple graph is B(lambda), and the graph labeled by indecomposable projective COVERS P(S) is the same graph under the unscaled cover–simple pairing. Projective crystal operators here mean operators transported on cover labels; no arbitrary #-dual-of-simple identification, generic global-basis theorem, or independent linear Kashiwara action on the projective class basis is asserted.

items.title: Cyclotomic projective covers and dualities descend through the quotient
items.statement: Let $A=R(\beta)$ and $B=A/J$ be the standard homogeneous cyclotomic quotient. For an indecomposable finite graded projective generic cover $P(S)$, $B\otimes_A P(S)$ is its same-head indecomposable $B$-cover if $JS=0$, and is zero otherwise. Every graded simple/indecomposable projective $B$-orbit arises this way, and distinct surviving heads do not merge. Finite projective Hom duality commutes with this basechange, and finite vector duality commutes with inflation. Thus generic normalized $\#$-self-dual covers and $D_\psi$-self-dual simples supply unique normalized $B$-covers/simples. For these labels $h(P,S)=\operatorname{gdim}\operatorname{HOM}_B(P,S)$ and $T(P,S)=\operatorname{gdim}(P^\psi\otimes_B S)$ are both $\delta_{P,S}$; $T$ is bilinear and $h$ first-bar sesquilinear. Extension induces a surjection on projective $K_0$. No Frobenius, geometric basis or cyclotomic crystal premise is used.

items.title: Cyclotomic diagram duality and graded module duals
items.statement: For the standard graded quotient $B=R^\Lambda(\beta)$, $\psi$ is the descended anti-involution fixing $e(\nu),x_a,\tau_a$. For a finite module $M$ define $D_\psi M=\operatorname{HOM}_k(M,k)^\psi$, with $(af)(m)=f(\psi(a)m)$. For a finite graded PROJECTIVE $P$ define instead $P^\#=\operatorname{HOM}_B(P,B)^\psi$. Both reverse internal shifts and are involutive on their respective domains. They are DIFFERENT dualities; Hom duality is not applied to a nonprojective simple to produce its cover. By [[lem-cyclotomic-projective-covers-and-dualities-descend-through-the-quotient]], each simple orbit has a unique $D_\psi$-self-dual representative $S$, and its unique normalized cover $P$ with $\operatorname{Hom}^0(P,S)=k$ is $\#$-self-dual. These are the normalizations in the based statements. No self-dual shift is asserted for every indecomposable finite module. The symmetric theorem additionally gives $D_\psi P\cong P^\#\{-2\operatorname{def}_\Lambda(\beta)\}$; it does not change the canonical projective normalization.

items.title: The vacuum projective is a highest-weight generator
Cyclotomic KLR functors define an integrable quantum action on $K_0$ and $G_0$
items.statement:
For the STANDARD graded cyclotomic quotient over any field and any real symmetrizable Cartan datum with admissible graded KLR parameters, put $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$, $h_i(\beta)=\langle h_i,\Lambda-\beta\rangle$, and $q_i=q^{d_i}$. On projective $K_0$ use $F_i=F_i^{\rm basic}$ and $E_i|_\beta=q_i^{-1-h_i(\beta)}E_i^{\rm basic}$; on module $G_0$ use either the SAME canonical normalization, or the Kang--Kashiwara normalization $E_i^{\rm KK}=E_i^{\rm basic}$, $F_i^{\rm KK}|_\beta=q_i^{1-h_i(\beta)}F_i^{\rm basic}$. In all cases $K_i|_\beta=q_i^{h_i(\beta)}$. These operators satisfy the full quantum mixed and Serre relations and are locally nilpotent; their scalar extensions to $\mathbb Q(q)$ are integrable weight modules. No decomposition into finite-dimensional full-$\mathfrak g$ submodules is asserted in affine or indefinite type.
The tensor pairing $T_\beta(P,M)=\mathrm{gdim}(P^\psi\otimes_{R^\Lambda(\beta)}M)$ is $A$-BILINEAR and weightwise perfect in normalized projective-cover/simple bases. The Hom pairing $h(P,M)=\mathrm{gdim}\operatorname{HOM}(P,M)$ instead satisfies $h(P,M)=T(P^\#,M)$ and is first-bar-sesquilinear. For $T$, projective $E_i$ is adjoint to module $F_i^{\rm KK}$ and projective $F_i$ to module $E_i^{\rm KK}$. The two module actions are conjugate by the weight rescaling $q^{\operatorname{def}_\Lambda(\beta)}$, where $\operatorname{def}_\Lambda(\beta)=(\Lambda,\beta)-(\beta,\beta)/2$.

items.title: The cyclotomic projective $K_0$ is the integral highest-weight module
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice [[def-axiom-of-choice]]. For the standard homogeneous graded quotient over any field, with arbitrary real symmetrizable Cartan datum and admissible graded KLR parameters, there is a unique $U_A$-module isomorphism $\phi:K_0(\mathrm{Proj}\,R^\Lambda)\to V_A(\Lambda)$ sending $1_\Lambda$ to $v_\Lambda$ and intertwining all normalized $E_i,F_i,K_i$ and divided powers. In particular $K_0$ is free over $A$. On the NEGATIVE half the vacuum map has exact kernel
$$\ker(U_A^-\to K_0(R^\Lambda))=\sum_{i\in I}\sum_{s>\lambda_i}U_A^-F_i^{(s)}.$$
This is the integral negative-half presentation; neither a full-$U_A$ quotient by only $F_i^{(\lambda_i+1)}$ nor invertibility of divided-power factorials is asserted.
For projectives, the tensor form $T(P,Q)=\mathrm{gdim}(P^\psi\otimes Q)$ transports to the highest-weight contravariant form normalized by $(v_\Lambda,v_\Lambda)=1$ and $\sigma(F_i)=q_i^{-1}K_iE_i$, $\sigma(E_i)=q_iF_iK_i^{-1}$, $\sigma(K_i)=K_i$. It is not the generic negative-half Lusztig form with a newly alleged radical.

items.title: The cyclotomic module $G_0$ is the restricted dual integral highest-weight module
items.statement:
For the same standard homogeneous general-field/general-Cartan parameters as the integral projective theorem, the tensor pairing $T(P,M)=\mathrm{gdim}(P^\psi\otimes M)$ is weightwise perfect and $A$-bilinear, with normalized cover/simple dual bases. Its associated map
$$\Psi_{\rm can}:G_0(R^\Lambda)\longrightarrow V_A(\Lambda)^\vee=\bigoplus_\beta\operatorname{Hom}_A(V_A(\Lambda)_{\Lambda-\beta},A),\qquad \Psi_{\rm can}(M)(\phi(P))=T(P,M)$$
is an isomorphism to the RESTRICTED weight dual, identified inside $V(\Lambda)$ using the highest-weight contravariant form. It intertwines the CANONICAL module action having the same normalization as projective $K_0$, and sends normalized simple classes to the form-dual projective basis. The KK module action is also sound, but its intertwiner is $\Psi_{\rm KK}|_\beta=q^{\operatorname{def}_\Lambda(\beta)}\Psi_{\rm can}|_\beta$. Thus an unrescaled KK identification is not asserted to send simples to the upper global basis. The Hom pairing is instead first-bar-sesquilinear, $h(P,M)=T(P^\#,M)$; this does not alter the bilinear tensor-dual identification.

items.title: Simple and indecomposable-projective crystals agree with $B(\Lambda)$
items.statement: For the standard homogeneous cyclotomic quotient over any field with the general real symmetrizable datum and graded KLR parameters, let $\mathcal B_\Lambda$ be the normalized $D_\psi$-self-dual simple classes. Set $\mathrm{wt}(S)=\Lambda-\beta$, $\varepsilon_i(S)=\max\{r:(E_i^{\rm basic})^rS\ne0\}$ and $\varphi_i(S)=\varepsilon_i(S)+\langle h_i,\mathrm{wt}(S)\rangle$. For $\varepsilon_i>0$, define $\widetilde e_iS$ by the unique simple isomorphism type in the socle of one-step right restriction, with its unique self-dual normalization; define $\widetilde f_iS$ by the simple head of right induction when nonzero, otherwise zero. The one-step socle/head is one shifted copy, not a quantum-factorial multiplicity. These data form a crystal canonically isomorphic to $B(\Lambda)$, with vacuum sent to $u_\Lambda$. The normalized indecomposable projectives carry the same crystal by their normalized simple heads and covers. The projective graph here is explicitly transported from these labels, rather than obtained by applying linear Kashiwara operators to an unspecified projective basis. The highest-weight quotient has simple survivors exactly when $\varepsilon_i^{\rm LEFT}(S)\le\lambda_i$ for every $i$.

items.title: Cyclotomic extension of scalars respects the based quotient
items.statement:
Assume the full symmetric normalized-$d_i=1$, characteristic-zero,
loopless-quiver geometric-parameter scope of the generic global theorem, and
the STANDARD homogeneous first-strand cyclotomic quotient with RIGHT append.
Let $\gamma:U_A^-\to K_0(R)$ be the approved generic categorification and
$\phi:K_0(R^\Lambda)\to V_A(\Lambda)$ the vacuum-normalized integral
isomorphism. Then the raw extension $q_\Lambda(P)=R^\Lambda\otimes_RP$
satisfies
$$\phi[q_\Lambda(P)]=\pi_\Lambda\bigl(*(\gamma^{-1}[P])\bigr).$$
Composing extension with the generic mirror twist gives $\pi_\Lambda$ without
star. For $b\in B(\infty)$ and the generic normalized indecomposable projective
$P_b$ with $\gamma^{-1}[P_b]=G^-(b)$, raw extension is zero or a SINGLE
normalized indecomposable cyclotomic projective; its image is
$\pi_\Lambda G^-(b^*)$, which is zero or $G^-_\Lambda(\pi_\Lambda b^*)$. The
surviving cover orbits do not merge, and every normalized cyclotomic cover is
obtained. In RIGHT-simple labels $c$, the generic FIRST-recursion theorem gives
$\gamma^{-1}[P(S_c)]=G^-(c^*)$, so raw extension sends it to
$G^-_\Lambda(\pi_\Lambda c)$; these are exactly the crystal-compatible
survivor labels of the preceding theorem. The claim is for indecomposable
projectives, not every finite projective quotient.

items.title: Self-dual indecomposable cyclotomic projectives give the lower global basis
items.statement:
For a symmetric Cartan datum normalized by $d_i=1$, over any
characteristic-zero field, and the SAME finite loopless quiver with arbitrary
edge multiplicities and $Q_{ij}=(-1)^{h_{ij}}(u-v)^{h_{ij}+h_{ji}}$ as the
generic global theorem, use the STANDARD homogeneous first-strand quotient and
RIGHT append. The vacuum-normalized isomorphism
$\phi:K_0(\mathrm{Proj}\,R^\Lambda)\to V_A(\Lambda)$ maps the classes of
normalized $\#$-self-dual indecomposable cyclotomic projectives bijectively
onto the lower global basis. The normalization is by projective HOM duality and
normalized simple heads, not by finite vector duality or a half-trace shift.
The projective with RIGHT crystal label $c\in B(\Lambda)$ maps to
$G^-_\Lambda(c)$. Every such projective is the surviving extension of a
generic normalized cover, with the raw map $\pi_\Lambda\circ*$ and the
FIRST/RIGHT label cancellation proved in the based-quotient lemma. The
uniqueness is at the level of normalized indecomposable projective isomorphism
classes; this is not an assertion that its generic lift is unique. No
arbitrary-parameter based extension is asserted.

items.title: Self-dual simple cyclotomic modules give the upper global basis
items.statement:
In exactly the symmetric normalized-$d_i=1$, characteristic-zero, loopless
arbitrary-multiedge geometric-parameter regime of the lower projective theorem,
the CANONICAL restricted-dual identification
$\Psi_{\mathrm{can}}:G_0(R^\Lambda)\to V_A(\Lambda)^\vee$ maps normalized
$D_\psi$-self-dual simple classes bijectively to the upper global basis,
form-dual to the lower projective basis under the actual highest-weight
contravariant form. A simple and its normalized projective COVER have the same
$B(\Lambda)$ label; this is the cover/simple correspondence, not projective Hom
duality applied to a simple. Canonical $G_0$ operators have the same projective
normalization. The alternative KK module action remains valid, but its
intertwiner is
$\Psi_{\mathrm{KK}}=q^{\operatorname{def}_\Lambda(\beta)}
\Psi_{\mathrm{can}}$ on root $\beta$ and sends a simple to that defect-rescaled
upper vector. The unrescaled upper-basis claim is made only for
$\Psi_{\mathrm{can}}$.

decline_pages.title: Cyclotomic KLR Algebras and Highest-Weight Categorification — Examples

items.title: Cyclotomic KLR quotients in ranks zero, one and two
items.statement:
Work over any field $k$ with a real symmetrizable Cartan datum, arbitrary symmetrizers $d_i$, dominant $\Lambda$ and the STANDARD homogeneous polynomials $a_i=u^{\lambda_i}$.
(a) $R^\Lambda(0)=k$ has one normalized simple and projective, the vacuum.
(b) For every color $i$, $R^\Lambda(\alpha_i)=k[x]/x^{\lambda_i}$ with $\deg x=2d_i$ and graded dimension $\sum_{r=0}^{\lambda_i-1}q^{2d_ir}$ when $\lambda_i\ge1$. Its unique normalized simple is $k$, its normalized projective HOM-self-dual cover is the regular module, and the coefficient-of-$x^{\lambda_i-1}$ Frobenius FUNCTIONAL has degree $-2d_i(\lambda_i-1)$. If $\lambda_i=0$ the block is zero and has NO simple; if $\lambda_i=1$ it is $k$.
(c) In rank one $I=\{i\}$, at EVERY $n\ge0$ the algebra is the cyclotomic nil-Hecke quotient $NH_n/(x_1^{\lambda_i})$. It is nonzero precisely for $0\le n\le\lambda_i$. At each such root it has exactly one normalized self-dual simple, and zero blocks have none; hence there are $\lambda_i+1$ normalized simple classes in total, matching the rank-one highest-weight module. For $1\le n\le\lambda_i$ its symmetric corner is $k[e_1,\ldots,e_n]/(h_{\lambda_i-n+1},\ldots,h_{\lambda_i})$, the graded Grassmannian coinvariant ring, and the algebra is the associated graded polynomial-column matrix algebra. The normalized simple column has graded dimension $[n]_{q_i}!$, where $q_i=q^{d_i}$.
(d) Explicitly at $\lambda_i=2,n=2$, the block is $\operatorname{End}_k(C\{-d_i\})$ with $C=k[x_1,x_2]/(x_1+x_2,x_1x_2)$, its basis $1,x_1$ in degrees $0,2d_i$. Its unique self-dual simple $S_2=C\{-d_i\}$ has graded dimension $q_i^{-1}+q_i$ and is also the normalized indecomposable projective $P_2$. It is NOT a one-dimensional module with both dots zero. The regular class is $[R^\Lambda(2\alpha_i)]=[2]_{q_i}[P_2]$ in $K_0$ and $[2]_{q_i}[S_2]$ in $G_0$.
(e) Arbitrary monic $a_i$ gives the ungraded deformation: $\lambda_i=2$, $a_i=u(u-1)$ gives $k\oplus k$ at root $\alpha_i$. Ordinary finiteness/symmetry remain true, but this is not the standard graded $V(2)$ identification.

items.title: Self-dual shift normalization for a cyclotomic projective
items.statement:
For rank one $d_i=1$ and $\lambda\ge1$, let $B=k[x]/x^\lambda$ and $P=B$. The PROJECTIVE Hom dual satisfies $P^\#\cong P$, so the canonical normalized projective is $P$ with no shift. Its finite vector dual is different:
$$D_\psi P\cong P\{-2(\lambda-1)\}.$$
The unique vector-dual-centered shift of this regular module is $P\{-(\lambda-1)\}$. For $\lambda=1$ both centers agree; for $\lambda=2$, projective Hom-self-duality centers $P$ at $0$ while vector-self-duality centers it at $-1$. If $\lambda=0$ the block is zero and there is no indecomposable projective here. For any normalized cyclotomic projective the general relation is $D_\psi P\cong P^\#\{-2\operatorname{def}_\Lambda(\beta)\}$; it does not redefine the lower-basis projective normalization.

items.title: The categorical $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ commutator in a small cyclotomic weight
items.statement:
Take $I=\{i\}$ with $(\alpha_i\mid\alpha_i)=2$, $d_i=1$, $q_i=q$, and
$\Lambda=2\Lambda_1$, so that $\langle h_i,\Lambda\rangle=2$ and the standard
cyclotomic quotient has relations $x_1^2e(\nu)=0$. Then:

(a) $R^\Lambda(0)=k$, $R^\Lambda(\alpha_i)=k[x_1]/(x_1^2)$ with graded
dimension $1+q^2$, and $R^\Lambda(n\alpha_i)=0$ for $n\ge3$, so the functors
on the nonzero weights are $F^\Lambda_ik=R^\Lambda(\alpha_i)$ and
$F^\Lambda_iE^\Lambda_ik=0$;

(b) the categorical $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ relation of
[[thm-cyclotomic-klr-sl-two-categorical-commutator]] at $\beta=0$,
$\lambda=\Lambda$ (case $\langle h_i,\lambda\rangle=2\ge0$) reads
$q^{-2}F^\Lambda_iE^\Lambda_i\oplus\mathrm{Id}\oplus q^2\mathrm{Id}\cong
E^\Lambda_iF^\Lambda_i$; on the vacuum it says
$E^\Lambda_iF^\Lambda_ik\cong k\oplus k\{2\}$, which is exactly
$R^\Lambda(\alpha_i)\cong k\oplus k\{2\}$;

(c) consequently, with the normalized operators of
[[thm-cyclotomic-klr-functors-define-an-integrable-quantum-action-on-k-zero-and-g-zero]],
on $[\mathrm{Proj}(R^\Lambda(0))]$: $E_iF_i[1_\Lambda]=(q+q^{-1})[1_\Lambda]$
and $F_iE_i[1_\Lambda]=0$, so
$[E_i,F_i][1_\Lambda]=(q+q^{-1})[1_\Lambda]
=(K_i-K_i^{-1})/(q_i-q_i^{-1})[1_\Lambda]$ with
$K_i[1_\Lambda]=q^2[1_\Lambda]$; on $[\mathrm{Rep}(R^\Lambda(0))]$ the same
commutator identity holds: $F_i[k]=q^{-1}[k\oplus k\{2\}]$, $E_i$ lowers back,
$F_iE_i[k]=0$, and $E_iF_i[k]=(q+q^{-1})[k]$. This is the mixed relation of
[[thm-cyclotomic-klr-functors-define-an-integrable-quantum-action-on-k-zero-and-g-zero]]
verified at the first nontrivial weight.

items.title: $K_0$ categorification alone does not identify the global basis
items.statement:
**Statement refuted:** once the isomorphism $[\mathrm{Proj}(R^\Lambda)]\cong V_A(\Lambda)$ of [[thm-cyclotomic-klr-projective-k-zero-is-the-integral-highest-weight-module]] is known, the classes of the word projectives $R^\Lambda(\beta)e(\nu)$ are automatically lower global basis vectors; in particular the K_0-level categorification alone identifies the global basis.
**Counterexample (rank two, $\Lambda=2\Lambda_1$).** Let $I=\{i\}$, $(\alpha_i\mid\alpha_i)=2$, and $\Lambda=2\Lambda_1$. In weight $2\alpha_i$ the word projective is $R^\Lambda(2\alpha_i)=NH_2/(x_1^2)$, which is not indecomposable: by the rank-one case of [[def-divided-power-klr-idempotents-and-projectives]] it is a direct sum of $[2]_{q_i}!=(q+q^{-1})$ copies of the self-dual divided-power projective $P_{i,2}$, so its class is
$$[R^\Lambda(2\alpha_i)]=(q+q^{-1})\,[P_{i,2}].$$
Under $[\mathrm{Proj}(R^\Lambda)]\cong V_A(2\Lambda_1)$ the class $[R^\Lambda(2\alpha_i)]$ is the ordinary product $F_i^2v_{2\Lambda_1}$, while the lower global basis vector in weight $2\alpha_i$ is the divided power $F_i^{(2)}v_{2\Lambda_1}=F_i^2v_{2\Lambda_1}/[2]_{q_i}$; the two differ by the scalar $q+q^{-1}\notin\{\pm q^n\}$, so no K_0-level statement that only names the module $R^\Lambda(2\alpha_i)$ and its class can decide between them. The lower global basis is picked out only by the additional structure: the self-dual shift normalization of [[def-cyclotomic-klr-diagram-duality-and-graded-module-duals]], bar invariance, and the positivity of the divided-power coefficients, none of which is part of the bare $K_0\cong V_A(\Lambda)$ statement. The example also shows the true positive claim: the lower global class in weight $2\alpha_i$ is the class of the *indecomposable* projective $P_{i,2}$, not of the word projective.

items.title: The projective-simple Cartan pairing in a small cyclotomic block
items.statement:
For rank one $d_i=1$, $\lambda=2$, let $B_r=R^\Lambda(r\alpha_i)$. The
normalized simples are $S_0=k$, $S_1=k$ with $x=0$, and
$S_2=C\{-1\}$ of graded dimension $q^{-1}+q$, where
$C=k[x_1,x_2]/(x_1+x_2,x_1x_2)$. Their normalized projective covers are
$P_0=k$, $P_1=k[x]/x^2$, $P_2=S_2$. Then $T(P_r,S_s)=\delta_{rs}$, with
distinct roots paired by zero. Under the integral projective identification
$P_0,P_1,P_2$ map to $v,Fv,F^{(2)}v$, respectively, while
$[B_2]=(q+q^{-1})[P_2]$ maps to $F^2v$. In $G_0$ the correct regular classes
are $[B_1]=(1+q^2)[S_1]$ and $[B_2]=(q+q^{-1})[S_2]$. The canonical
restricted-dual map sends $S_r$ to the form-dual of the corresponding divided
lower vector; it does not identify $B_1$ with $S_1$.
