decline_pages.title: Soergel Intersection Forms and Hodge Theory

items.title: The real type-A Soergel category by scalar extension
items.statement: Extend Q→R and set S=R[x_1,...,x_n] with deg x_i=2, with the place-permuting S_n action. The Hodge page uses the coordinate/length normalization of the published reflection realization: alpha_i here means beta_i=x_i-x_{i+1}, and alpha_i^vee means beta_i^vee, so adjacent Cartan entries are -1. The published alternating balanced roots eps_i beta_i are used for diagrammatic presentations, not for positivity on this page. Both choices have identical reflections, invariant rings and underlying bimodules. Define B_i^R=S⊗_{S^{s_i}}S(1) and the real Soergel category as the idempotent completion of their finite additive graded tensor closure, with the same shifts as the rational category. Its unit is the graded ring S (as an object in cohomological degree zero), not a polynomial ring concentrated in internal degree zero. For a rational bimodule M write M^R=M⊗_Q R; the generator and Bott-Samelson constructions extend in this way. Standard graph supports, Delta/nabla flags and characters use the formulas of the rational page over R; the Hecke algebra remains the same integral normalized algebra. The dominant chamber is Theta={rho=Σ c_j x_j: c_i>c_{i+1} for all i}. It is nonempty, for example c_j=(n+1)/2-j.

items.title: The Hecke trace form, its values on the Kazhdan-Lusztig basis, and the standard pairing
items.statement: Let H = H_v(n) be the normalized type-A Hecke algebra over A = Z[v^{\pm1}] and let a be the A-linear anti-involution with a(v) = v, a(H_x) = H_{x^{-1}} (the reversal anti-involution of the Hecke page). Define the trace eps: H -> A by eps(H_w) = delta_{e,w} on the standard basis, and the bilinear form (-,-): H x H -> A by (h,h') := eps(a(h)h'). Then: (1) eps and (-,-) are well defined (the H_w are an A-basis); (2) (ph, qh') = pq(h,h') for p,q in A; (3) (hH_s, h') = (h, h'H_s) and (H_sh, h') = (h, H_sh') for all h,h' and all simple reflections s; (4) the standard basis is orthonormal, (H_x,H_y) = delta_{xy}; (5) on the Kazhdan-Lusztig basis, (H_x,H_y) in vZ[v] for x != y and (H_x,H_x) in 1 + vZ[v]; (6) the same form is the standard pairing <H_x,H_y> = delta_{xy} used in the type-A Soergel Hom formula, transported through the identification of the normalized standard bases. All statements are integral and use no choice.

items.title: The reduced Soergel module and the dominant Lefschetz operator
items.statement: Work over S as in the real scalar-extension definition and let k := S/S_+ = R be the residue field of the right action, with quotient map S -> R. For a graded (S,S)-bimodule M which is finite free as a right S-module put Mbar := M \otimes_S R = M/(M S_+), a finite dimensional graded R-vector space; dimensions are written dim_R(Mbar)^i and the graded dimension is dim(Mbar) = sum_i dim_R(Mbar)^i v^{-i}. For a morphism f: M -> M' of bimodules write fbar for its reduction, so that fbar is R-linear. Fix rho \in S_2 with rho(alpha_i^\vee) > 0 for every i (a strictly dominant degree-two element, which exists by the scalar-extension definition) and denote by rho.(-) the left multiplication operator; since M S_+ is stable under left multiplication, rho.(-) descends to a degree-two R-linear endomorphism of Mbar, called the dominant Lefschetz operator on Mbar. For x in S_n and s in S_n a simple reflection the same construction applies to B_x^R B_s^R = (B_x B_s)^R, and the operator L_0 := rho.(-) on the reduced tensor product is the case zeta = 0 of the deformed operator defined later. Also record the descent-detection property: (w rho)(alpha_s^\vee) > 0 if and only if s w > w, for every w in S_n and simple s (so this formula detects left descents; its instance w=x^{-1} detects right descents of x).

items.title: Indecomposable labels, characters and filtration ranks agree after real scalar extension
items.statement: Let B_w be the rational indecomposable type-A Soergel bimodule and let B_w^R be its real scalar extension. (1) B_w^R is indecomposable; its finite-dimensional degree-zero endomorphism algebra is local with residue field R. If S(w) holds, its degree-zero endomorphism algebra is R, but no rank-one assertion for the full graded endomorphism module is made. (2) Real extension preserves the labels and shifts of all finite Krull-Schmidt decompositions of rational Soergel bimodules, and every real indecomposable is a unique B_w^R(d). (3) Delta/nabla support-filtration multiplicities, characters, reduction by positive-degree right polynomials, and Hom spaces commute with scalar extension; thus character identities over R descend to Q. (4) If xs>x and S(y) holds for all y<xs, then B_xB_s = B_xs ⊕ ⊕_{y<xs} B_y^{a_y} with a_y nonnegative integers and no grading shifts; the top summand occurs once. If xs<x and S(x) holds, then B_xB_s = B_x(1) ⊕ B_x(-1). All assertions concern the normalized self-dual indecomposables.

items.title: The trace, the invariant intersection form on Bott-Samelson bimodules and its reduction
items.statement: For a finite word x = s_1...s_m let BS(x) = B_{s_1}...B_{s_m} be the real Bott-Samelson bimodule, with its right (and left) S-basis of subexpression elements c_epsil on and the top element c_top := c_{s_1}...c_{s_m}; recall BS(x)(-m) is a commutative ring under termwise multiplication. Define the trace Tr: BS(x) -> S to be the coefficient of c_top when an element is written in the basis {c_epsil on} as a right S-module, and define the intersection form by <b,b'> := Tr(b b'), the product taken in the commutative ring BS(x)(-m). Then: (1) <,> is a graded symmetric form, S-bilinear for the right action, invariant in the sense <rb,b'> = <b,rb'> and <br,b'> = <b,b'r>; (2) if B is a direct summand of a finite direct sum of shifts of Bott-Samelson bimodules, then an invariant form on B is obtained by restriction and is unique up to the choices of the ambient forms; (3) for a self-dual bimodule B the induced form on BB_s is characterised by the three formulas for alpha(b) = b c_id and beta(b) = b c_s: <alpha b, alpha b'> = partial_s(<b,b'>), <alpha b, beta b'> = <b,b'> = <beta b, alpha b'>, <beta b, beta b'> = <b,b'> alpha_s; (4) the intersection form on a Bott-Samelson bimodule is non-degenerate as an S-valued form, and for any summand B of a Bott-Samelson bimodule the restricted form is non-degenerate whenever the summand has finite free right S-rank and the corresponding reduced form is non-degenerate (graded Nakayama); (5) the reduction to Mbar is a graded symmetric R-valued form <,>bar, and non-degeneracy of the S-valued form is equivalent to graded non-degeneracy of the R-valued form; (6) Bott-Samelson bimodules and the indecomposable B_w^R are self-dual, so dim(B_w^R bar)^{-i} = dim(B_w^R bar)^{i} for all i (symmetric Betti numbers). Additionally record the left/right asymmetry: the form is bilinear for the right action and satisfies <rb,b'> = <b,rb'>.

items.title: Primitive subspaces, hard Lefschetz and the Hodge-Riemann signs: the dictionary of hypotheses S, hL and HR
items.statement: Let H be a finite-dimensional graded real space with a graded nondegenerate symmetric form, and let L have degree two and be symmetric for the form. Hard Lefschetz (hL) means L^i:H^{-i}→H^i is an isomorphism for every i≥0. Define P_L^{-i}=ker(L^{i+1}|_{H^{-i}}) for i≥0 and the Lefschetz form (a,b)_L^{-i}=<a,L^i b>. Under hL the primitive decomposition is H=⊕_{i≥0}⊕_{j=0}^i L^j P_L^{-i}, proved in the primitive-decomposition lemma. Assume H is concentrated in one parity and its lowest nonzero degree is -d. HR with standard sign means hL and (-1)^{(d-i)/2}-definiteness on P_L^{-i} for every i≥0; the bottom primitive form is positive. A sign with odd exponent numerator means the primitive space is zero. HR with either global sign allows a common factor epsilon∈{±1}. For B_xbar use d=ell(x), L=left rho. S(x) means ch(B_x)=underline H_x. Under S(x), HR(x) uses the positively normalized intrinsic invariant form; HRbar(x) requires HR for every reduced-word summand embedding, and the invariant-form lemma proves their equivalence. The strong embedded-form HRbar(x) makes sense without S(x). For xs>x the analogous package on B_xB_s has bottom degree -ell(x)-1 and primitive sign (-1)^{(ell(x)+1-i)/2}; HR(x,s) refers to a fixed reduced-word induced form and HRbar(x,s) to all such choices. Their deformed versions use L_zeta from its Definition. S^±(y,x,s) uses the local-intersection-form Definition. For an orthogonal L-stable direct sum, HR is equivalent to HR on the summands with the same ambient degree-dependent signs, which need not be each summand's own standard sign if their bottom degrees differ.

items.title: Minimal complexes and the perverse truncations in the real type-A Soergel category
items.statement: Let B be the real graded type-A Soergel category with degree-zero morphisms. Its categorical radical consists of f:M→N for which 1_M-gf is invertible for every g:N→M; write q:B→B^ss=B/rad B. A bounded complex is minimal when all differentials become zero after q. A Soergel bimodule is perverse when its character is a nonnegative integer combination of the Kazhdan-Lusztig basis elements (not the standard basis); it is p-split when its indecomposable summands are shifts of perverse ones. For a p-split decomposition M=⊕ B_x(k)^{m_{x,k}}, with the normalized B_x perverse, set tau_{≤j}M=⊕_{k≥-j}B_x(k)^{m_{x,k}}, tau_{<j}=tau_{≤j-1}, tau_{≥j}=M/tau_{<j}, and H^j(M)=(tau_{≤j}M/tau_{<j}M)(j). Define pK^b_{≥0} (respectively pK^b_{≤0}) by complexes isomorphic in the homotopy category to complexes whose terms are p-split and satisfy tau_{<-i}(^iF)=0 (respectively ^iF=tau_{≤-i}(^iF)) in each cohomological degree i. Thus their indecomposable shifts k obey k≤i (respectively k≥i). Internal shift (1) changes module degrees; homological shift [1] changes complex degrees. The structural lemma supplies semisimplicity, minimal-model existence/uniqueness, the functoriality of these cuts, and triangle closure.

items.title: The Lefschetz operator factors through deleted Bott-Samelson subwords, with positive rescalings
items.statement: Let x = s_1...s_m be an expression, BS(x) its Bott-Samelson bimodule, Br_i = chi_i o phi_i the Demazure operation at the i-th letter, and Tr, <,> the trace and intersection form. (1) As endomorphisms of BS(x) one has rho.(-) = \Sigma_{i=1}^m (s_{i-1}...s_1 rho)(alpha_{s_i}^\vee) chi_i phi_i + (-).x^{-1}rho (Lemma 3.4). (2) With the rescaled forms <,>'_i := (s_{i-1}...s_1rho)(alpha_{s_i}^\vee) <,>_i on BS(x-hat-i) and <,>' the direct sum, one has <b,rho b'>_{overline{BS(x)}} = <phi(b),phi(b')>' for all b,b' in the reduced module overline{BS(x)}, where phi = \Sigma_i phi_i: BS(x) -> \bigoplus_i BS(x-hat-i)(1) (Lemmas 6.14 and 6.15). (3) If x is reduced then every scaling factor gamma_i := (s_{i-1}...s_1 rho)(alpha_{s_i}^\vee) is strictly positive, so the rescalings change no signs in the HR statements; the un-scattered term (-).x^{-1}rho vanishes after reduction to the Soergel module. (4) Consequently left multiplication by rho on overline{BS(x)} factors, up to positive rescalings, as the composite BS(x) -> \bigoplus_i BS(x-hat-i)(1) -> BS(x)(2), and this composite is the first differential of the Rouquier complex F_{s_1}...F_{s_m} followed by its dual map, up to the same positive rescalings.

items.title: Invariant forms on an indecomposable Soergel bimodule are unique up to scalar, non-degenerate, and agree with the restricted Bott-Samelson form
items.statement: Assume S(x), i.e. ch(B_x^R) = H_x. Then: (1) the space of invariant forms on B_x^R is one dimensional over R, and every non-zero invariant form is non-degenerate; (2) if B_x^R is embedded as a direct summand of a Bott-Samelson bimodule BS(x) for a reduced expression of x, the restriction of the intersection form is a positive multiple of the intersection form on B_x^R; (3) consequently HR(x) holds for the intrinsic intersection form if and only if HRbar(x) holds for every (equivalently: some) embedding, and the two normalizations differ by a positive scalar, so no sign changes; (4) if B = \oplus_z B_z^{R,m_z} with S(z) for all z, then nondegenerate symmetric invariant forms on B are direct sums of the forms on the isotypic components tensored with nonsingular real symmetric multiplicity-space pairings, and an orthogonal decomposition into isotypic components can always be chosen.

items.title: Hard Lefschetz gives the primitive decomposition, orthogonality and the signature formula
items.statement: Let H have a graded nondegenerate symmetric form and a symmetric degree-two operator L. If hL holds then H=⊕_{i≥0}⊕_{j=0}^i L^jP_L^{-i}. In each degree -i≥-d, the decomposition H^{-i}=⊕_{k≥0}L^kP_L^{-(i+2k)} is orthogonal for the Lefschetz form <a,L^i b>. All Lefschetz forms on H^{-i} are nondegenerate exactly when hL holds. If H has one parity and lowest degree -d, standard HR is equivalent to hL and, for every i≥0, sig(<-,L^i ->|_{H^{-i}})=Σ_{k≥0}(-1)^{(d-i-2k)/2}dim P_L^{-(i+2k)} (zero spaces omitted). An L-stable graded subspace V with symmetric dimensions inherits hL; if H satisfies HR, its restricted form is nondegenerate and it inherits the ambient primitive signs. Its standard global sign agrees with that of H when their lowest degrees coincide.

items.title: The deformed Lefschetz operator L_zeta on B_x B_s
items.statement: Fix x in S_n, a simple reflection s and a strictly dominant rho. For zeta≥0 define L_zeta=(rho·(-))⊗id_{B_s}+id_{B_x}⊗(zeta rho·(-)) on B_xB_s. The second term is multiplication at the middle tensor position, equivalently right rho multiplication on B_x, and is well-defined on the balanced tensor product. These commuting degree-two operators descend to the reduced module and are symmetric for the induced invariant form. Write hL(x,s)_zeta, HR(x,s)_zeta and HRbar(x,s)_zeta for the centered hard Lefschetz, Hodge-Riemann and strong embedded-form statements with this operator. L_0 is left multiplication by rho, so the zero-parameter statements equal hL(x,s), HR(x,s), HRbar(x,s). The family is polynomial in zeta. A bimodule summand is automatically stable under L_0; stability under a middle-position operator must be checked separately. The undeformed summand implications used in the induction are supplied by the local restriction lemma, after deforming back to zeta=0.

items.title: Radical quotients, minimal complexes and perverse filtrations in the Soergel category
items.statement: The radical quotient B^ss is semisimple with simple classes B_x(k) and their endomorphism rings R; q reflects isomorphisms. Every bounded complex has a minimal direct summand whose inclusion is a homotopy equivalence, and any two minimal models are isomorphic as complexes. Every direct summand of a perverse (respectively p-split) bimodule is perverse (respectively p-split). For perverse M,N, Hom(M,N(-i))=0 for i>0. The perverse cuts on p-split bimodules are independent of their decompositions and preserved by every morphism. The definitions of pK^b_{≥0} and pK^b_{≤0} can equivalently be tested on the minimal model, and both classes are closed under extensions in distinguished triangles.

items.title: Positive Rouquier complexes are Delta-split
items.statement: Let x be a reduced expression for x in S_n and let F_x be the Rouquier complex F_{s_1}...F_{s_m} in K^b(SBim_n^R) (or its minimal subcomplex). Then for every y in S_n there is an isomorphism in the homotopy category of graded bimodules Gamma_{>=y/>y}(F_x) = Delta_x if y = x, and 0 otherwise. Equivalently: the Bruhat support subquotient of a positive Rouquier complex is contractible except in the top layer Delta_x = R_x(-\ell(x)); F_x is Delta-split in the sense that each of its support subquotients is a direct sum of standard bimodules, and the top layer is a single Delta_x. No positivity of characters and no assumption S is used; the statement is unconditional for every Coxeter group and every reflection faithful realization.

items.title: Signature constancy in a Lefschetz family, the L-stable subspace lemma and the weak-Lefschetz substitute
items.statement: Let H be a finite dimensional graded real vector space with a graded non-degenerate symmetric form. (1) Family lemma: if L_t, t in [a,b], is a continuous family of symmetric degree-two operators each satisfying hL, and L_{t_0} satisfies HR with the standard sign for one t_0, then every L_t satisfies hL and the same HR signs; in the application the family is L_zeta for zeta>=0, which is polynomial (hence continuous) in zeta. (2) Weak-Lefschetz substitute: let phi: V -> W(1) be a map of graded R[L]-modules with (a) phi injective in degrees <= -1, (b) graded forms <,>_V, <,>_W with <phi(a),phi(b)>_W = <a,Lb>_V, and (c) W satisfies HR with the standard sign; then L^i: V^{-i} -> V^i is injective for all i >= 0, and if dim V^i = dim V^{-i} for all i then L satisfies hL on V. (3) Sign bookkeeping: if in (2) the lowest degree of W is -l and of V is -(l+1), then the Lefschetz form on V^{-(l+1)} is +/- definite with the same sign as on W^{-l}, so if V satisfies HR with the standard sign then V has the standard sign if and only if W does. (4) Degenerate shifted case: if L^i: H^{-d-i} -> H^{-d+i} is an isomorphism for all i >= 0 with d > 0 (so hL fails in the centered sense) and the form is not assumed non-degenerate, then the Lefschetz form (h,h')^{-i}_L = <h,L^i h'> on H^{-i} is identically zero for i >= 0 (Lemma 2.5). (5) Stable-subspace lemma: if (H,L,<,>) satisfies hL and HR and V⊂H is an L-stable graded subspace with dim V^{-i}=dim V^i for all i, then the restricted operator and form satisfy hL and HR on V, with the ambient degree-by-degree signs. The restricted form is nondegenerate; its standard global sign agrees with the ambient standard sign if the lowest nonzero degrees agree.

items.title: The local intersection form on Hom(B_y, B_x B_s)
items.statement: Fix xs>x and y<xs, and assume S(z) for all z<xs. Choose reduced-word embeddings B_y→BS(y) and B_x→BS(x), their positively normalized nondegenerate invariant forms, and the induced form on M=B_xB_s. On the finite-dimensional real space E_y=Hom^0(B_y,M), define (f,g)^{x,s}_y by the scalar endomorphism g* f∈End^0(B_y)=R, where g* is the adjoint. The adjoint identifies Hom^0(B_y,M) with Hom^0(M,B_y). The form is symmetric and changes only by a positive scalar when the chosen normalized forms/embeddings change. Define S^±(y,x,s) to mean (-1)^{(ell(x)+1-ell(y))/2}-definiteness, with the parity convention of the primitive-space definition. The degree-zero Hom dimension and the equivalence of nondegeneracy with actual summand multiplicities are proved in the detection theorem; no statement identifies the full graded Hom rank with a KL coefficient.

items.title: Tensoring a direct sum of Hodge-Riemann bimodules with B_s preserves the signs
items.statement: Fix zeta >= 0 and a self-dual Soergel bimodule B = \bigoplus_z B_z^{R,m_z} such that m_z != 0 implies S(z) and HR(z,s)_zeta; if zeta = 0 assume in addition that m_z = 0 whenever zs < z. Assume B is even or odd, carries an invariant non-degenerate form and satisfies HR with the standard sign with respect to left multiplication by rho. Then BB_s satisfies HR with the standard sign with respect to L_zeta and the induced form. More precisely, if the lowest degree of B is -d, then the restriction of its form to a B_z summand is (-1)^{(d-ell(z))/2} times a positive multiple of the normalized form on B_z. Tensoring gives the primitive sign (-1)^{(d+1-i)/2} on degree -i of BB_s, whose lowest degree is -d-1.

items.title: Right-descent Soergel bimodules descend to simple invariants under the character hypothesis
items.statement: Let M=B_x over R and let s be a right descent, xs<x. Assume S(x). There is a graded (R,R^s)-bimodule N and an isomorphism M=N⊗_{R^s}R. Consequently M B_s=M(1)⊕M(-1); choosing the decomposition R=R^s⊕(alpha_s/2)R^s in the middle tensor factor, the reduced operator L_zeta has matrix [[rho,0],[zeta rho(alpha_s^vee),rho]], where the scalar off-diagonal entry is a degree-two map from M(1) to M(-1). The construction requires no singular-category classification or character conjecture beyond S(x). If hL(x) also holds and zeta>0 this matrix satisfies centered hard Lefschetz. At zeta=0 it fails centered hard Lefschetz.

items.title: Minimal positive Rouquier complexes are linear under the lower Soergel induction
items.statement: Assume S(y) for all y <= x (ch(B_y^R) = H_y) and let F_x be a minimal Rouquier complex of a reduced expression of x. Then: (1) ^0F_x = B_x; (2) for every i >= 1, ^iF_x is isomorphic to a direct sum of shifts B_z(i)^{m_{z,i}} with z < x and m_{z,i} in Z_{>=0}; in particular F_x lies in pK^b_{<=0} \cap pK^b_{>=0} and is linear (each summand in homological degree i carries the internal shift exactly i); (3) the multiplicities satisfy the parity vanishing m_{z,i} = 0 unless i and \ell(x)-\ell(z) have the same parity, and consequently, writing the standard basis element H_x = \Sigma_z g_{z,x} underline H_z in the Kazhdan-Lusztig basis (inverse Kazhdan-Lusztig coefficients), one has g_{x,x} = 1, g_{z,x} = \Sigma_i(-1)^im_{z,i}v^i, and (-1)^{\ell(x)-\ell(z)}g_{z,x} has non-negative coefficients. Note that the statement is conditional exactly on S(y) for y <= x and does NOT use S(x') for x' > x nor the final Soergel theorem; it is the induction step of the simultaneous induction.

items.title: Undeformed Lefschetz and Hodge-Riemann restrict to the next Soergel summand
items.statement: Let xs>x. The normalized indecomposable B_xs occurs as a bimodule summand of B_xB_s. If hL(x,s)_0 holds, then hL(xs) holds. If S(<xs) and hL(y) for every y<xs hold, then hL(x,s)_0 is equivalent to hL(xs). If HRbar(x,s)_0 holds, then the restriction to the chosen B_xs summand satisfies the Hodge-Riemann relations for its induced form; once S(xs) has been established, positive comparison of invariant forms gives HR(xs) and HRbar(xs) with the standard sign. More generally an L-stable graded subspace with symmetric Betti numbers inherits HR with the ambient signs, and an L-stable graded direct summand inherits hL. These conclusions apply to a positive deformation only if the chosen subspace and, for the direct-sum argument, its complement are preserved by that operator; they make no identification of the restricted positive operator with left rho.

items.title: Non-degeneracy of the local intersection forms detects Soergel's conjecture one step higher
items.statement: Fix xs>x and assume S(y) for every y<xs. Put M=B_xB_s and write the KL multiplication formula H_x H_s=H_xs+Σ_{y<xs} μ_y H_y, where μ_y are integer constants (zero when absent). For each y<xs, let E_y=Hom^0(B_y,M), and equip E_y with the local intersection form using adjoints of the nondegenerate invariant forms. Then dim_R E_y=μ_y, while the full graded Hom module has graded rank (H_y,H_x H_s), generally not μ_y. The following are equivalent: S(xs); nondegeneracy of every local intersection form on E_y; perfection of every degree-zero composition pairing Hom^0(B_y,M)×Hom^0(M,B_y)→End^0(B_y)=R; and equality of the actual multiplicity a_y of B_y in M with μ_y for every y<xs. The unconditional top summand is B_xs with multiplicity one, and under S(<xs) all remaining summands are unshifted B_y, as supplied by the comparison/classification lemma. No positivity of KL polynomials or conjecture at xs is assumed.

items.title: Embedding theorem: local intersection forms are isometric to primitive Lefschetz forms
items.statement: Fix x, s with xs > x and assume S(y) and HR(y) for all y < xs; fix embeddings and the induced forms, a reduced expression x of x and a generator c_bot of the one-dimensional space B_y^{-\ell(y)}. Then (1) the evaluation map iota: Hom(B_y,B_xB_s) -> (B_xB_s)^{-\ell(y)}, f -> f(c_bot), is injective with image contained in the primitive subspace P^{-\ell(y)}_rho = ker(rho^{\ell(y)+1}); (2) iota is an isometry up to the positive factor N = <rho^{\ell(y)}c_bot, c_bot>_{B_y} > 0: N (f,g)^{x,s}_y = (iota(f),iota(g))^{-\ell(y)}_rho for all f,g, where the right hand form is the Lefschetz form of B_xB_s with respect to the embedding into BS(xs); (3) consequently HR(x,s) implies S(xs) (Corollary 4.3: a definite form restricted to a subspace stays non-degenerate, so the local forms are non-degenerate and the detection theorem applies). The positivity of N uses HR(y) and the normalization <rho^{\ell(y)}c_bot,c_bot> = N > 0.

items.title: Hodge-Riemann relations hold for large positive deformation, and the deformation principle
items.statement: Let B be a Soergel bimodule satisfying hL and HR with the standard sign. Then for zeta >> 0 the induced operator L_zeta on BB_s satisfies hL and HR with the standard sign (Theorem 5.1). The proof contains the following signature comparison (Lemma 5.2): if V, W are finite dimensional graded spaces with graded non-degenerate forms and Lefschetz operators satisfying hL, W is even or odd, dim V = (v+v^{-1}) dim W, and W satisfies HR with the standard sign, then V satisfies HR with the standard sign if and only if for all i >= 0 the signature of the Lefschetz form on the primitive subspace P_W^{-i+1} equals the signature of the Lefschetz form on all of V^{-i}. Consequently (Corollary 5.3): if HR(x) holds and hL(x,s)_zeta holds for every zeta >= 0, then HR(x,s)_zeta holds for every zeta >= 0; and more generally the deformation principle: if hL(x,s)_zeta holds for all zeta >= 0 and HR(x,s)_zeta holds for a single zeta_0 >= 0, then HR(x,s)_zeta holds for all zeta >= 0 (signature constancy). In the signature comparison use the convention P_W^1=0; no positive-degree primitive space is introduced.

items.title: Minimal positive Rouquier complexes carry the induced Hodge-Riemann signs
items.statement: Assume S(<=x) and HR(y,s) for all y < x and simple s with ys > y. Fix a reduced expression x of x. Then F_x satisfies the Hodge-Riemann bilinear relations: there exists an embedding F_x \subseteq F_{s_1}...F_{s_m} such that for every tuple lambda = (lambda_{x'}) of strictly positive real numbers, each jF_x(-j) embedded in \bigoplus_{x' in pi(x,j)} BS(x') carries HR with respect to the rescaled form <,>_lambda and the Lefschetz operator given by left multiplication by rho, with the global sign fixed so that the Lefschetz form is positive definite on primitive subspaces in degrees congruent to -m+j modulo 4. Here pi(x,j) is the set of subexpressions of x obtained by deleting j letters and jF_x(-j) \subseteq \bigoplus_{x' in pi(x,j)}BS(x') is the canonical summand inclusion coming from F_x \subseteq F_{s_1}...F_{s_m}.

items.title: The minimal Rouquier differential supplies the injectivity input of the weak-Lefschetz substitute
items.statement: Let x be reduced and F_x a minimal positive Rouquier complex. As a complex of graded right polynomial modules F_x is homotopy equivalent to the right module R(-ell(x)) in cohomological degree zero. Consequently its right reduction has H^j(overline{F_x})=R(-ell(x)) for j=0 and zero otherwise; the surviving generator has internal degree ell(x). This does not assert that the bimodule cohomology is the untwisted unit. If xs>x and S(≤x), the first differential of F_xF_s has source B_xB_s and target ^1F_xB_s⊕B_x(1); F_xF_s need not itself be minimal. Its reduced first differential is injective in internal degrees ≤ell(x), since reduced degree-zero cohomology is supported only in internal degree ell(xs)=ell(x)+1. Injectivity remains true after splitting off contractible summands that have zero degree-zero source. The form compatibility and commutation with the deformed operators used in the hard-Lefschetz proof are additional inputs from the factorization and HR suppliers; for zeta=0 descent pieces require the kernel-of-d_3 argument of that theorem.

items.title: Hard Lefschetz for the deformed operator on B_x B_s, in the three cases
items.statement: The hard Lefschetz theorem for L_zeta on B_xB_s holds in the following three cases. (1) zeta > 0 and xs < x: under S(x), if hL(x) holds then hL(x,s)_zeta holds. The hL(x)-only descent implication, with the same matrix and no assumed S(x), is retained as an after-induction consequence in the character theorem, where S(x) has already been proved. (2) zeta > 0 and xs > x: if S(<=x), HR(z,t) for all z < x and simple t with zt > z, HRbar(<x,s)_zeta and HR(x) hold, then hL(x,s)_zeta holds. (3) zeta = 0 and xs > x: if S(<=x), HR(z,t) for all z < x and t with zt > z, HR(x) and hL(z) for all z < xs hold, then hL(x,s) holds. In the remaining case zeta=0 and xs<x, centered hard Lefschetz fails: in the decomposition B_x(1)⊕B_x(-1), L_0 is diagonal, but the first summand's bottom vector lies in degree -ell(x)-1 and its (ell(x)+1)-st rho power is zero. The opposite total degree is nonzero by self-duality. The two copies individually have Lefschetz strings centered at -1 and +1, rather than at zero. In case (1) the explicit form of L_zeta on B_xB_s = B_x(1) \oplus B_x(-1) is the matrix [[rho.(-), 0],[zeta rho(alpha_s^\vee), rho.(-)]], which after rescaling describes the action of a nilpotent element e of sl_2 on B_x \otimes V_2, whence hL. In case (2), the weak-Lefschetz substitute uses the HR target W=(^1F_x)(-1)B_s⊕B_x with a degree-one map into W(1). In case (3), first cancel the contractible shifted-descent piece, then use hL on the remaining descent component and the weak-Lefschetz substitute on the kernel of that component; the entire descent target need not satisfy centered HR.

items.title: Simultaneous induction: Soergel's conjecture, hard Lefschetz and the Hodge-Riemann relations hold for all elements
items.statement: Let X \subseteq S_n be a finite Bruhat ideal (closed under passage to lower elements). Assume: (1) HR(z,t)_zeta holds for all zeta >= 0, all z < zt with zt in X and all simple t; (2) HR(z,t)_zeta holds for all zeta > 0, all zt < z with z in X and all simple t. Then for every x in X the three statements S(x), hL(x), HR(x) hold. Since (1) and (2) hold for the initial ideal X_0 = {w : \ell(w) <= 2} by direct inspection of the rank-one and rank-two cases, and since the induction step preserves them when passing from X to X \cup {x'} with x' minimal in the complement and x' = xs, x in X, the theorem gives: for every w in S_n, S(w) (Soergel's conjecture for w), hL(w) and HR(w) hold; and for every x,s with xs > x the strong forms HRbar(x,s)_zeta hold for all zeta >= 0. The induction step: given (1),(2) for X, pick x' = xs minimal outside X; the hard Lefschetz theorems of the previous item give hL(x,s)_zeta for all zeta >= 0; combined with HR(x) and the large-deformation theorem this gives HR(x,s)_zeta for all zeta >= 0 (the deformation principle); the local intersection forms are then definite by the embedding theorem, hence non-degenerate, and the detection theorem gives S(x'); after evaluating at zeta=0, the undeformed restriction lemma gives HR(x') and hL(x') from HRbar(x,s)_0 and hL(x,s)_0; finally (2) for X \cup {x'} follows from the hL(z') case zeta > 0 and the large-deformation theorem applied at x'.

items.title: Soergel's character conjecture for type A
items.statement: For every w in S_n the character of the indecomposable type-A Soergel bimodule B_w^R equals the Kazhdan-Lusztig basis element: ch(B_w^R) = H_w (the underbar H_w of the type-A Hecke page). Equivalently, the class [B_w^R] in the split Grothendieck group corresponds to H_w under the Hecke algebra isomorphism, and the extension of scalars of the rational B_w categorifies the Kazhdan-Lusztig basis. Moreover the hard Lefschetz property hL(w) and the Hodge-Riemann relations HR(w) hold for every w, with the signs of Theorem 1.4; and the same identities hold for the rational category by the base-change comparison. This is the main theorem of the pair: it proves Soergel's conjecture for type A, replacing the citation recorded on the Kazhdan-Lusztig basis page by a local proof. Finally, for every right descent xs<x, the matrix of L_zeta on B_xB_s=B_x(1)⊕B_x(-1) is [[rho,0],[zeta rho(alpha_s^vee),rho]]. For zeta>0, hL(x) implies hL(x,s)_zeta without an additional character hypothesis, since S(x) is now established for all x; at zeta=0 centered hL fails. This retains the unconditional descent claim as a downstream consequence of the induction rather than an imported prerequisite.

items.title: Positivity of Kazhdan-Lusztig polynomials, mu-coefficients and structure constants
items.statement: Write H_w = \Sigma_{y<=w}h_{y,w}H_y for the expansion of the Kazhdan-Lusztig basis element in the standard basis and H_xH_y = \Sigma_z mu^z_{x,y}H_z for the product of two Kazhdan-Lusztig basis elements in the Kazhdan-Lusztig basis. Then: (1) h_{y,w} in Z_{>=0}[v] for all y <= w; equivalently the Kazhdan-Lusztig polynomials P_{y,w}(q) = v^{-(\ell(w)-\ell(y))}h_{y,w}(v) with q = v^{-2} have non-negative integer coefficients, and in particular the mu-coefficients mu(y,w) = [v]h_{y,w} are non-negative; (2) mu^z_{x,y} in Z_{>=0}[v^{\pm1}], the structure constants of the Kazhdan-Lusztig basis are non-negative; more precisely mu^z_{x,y} is the character of the multiplicity space of B_z in the tensor product B_x^R \otimes B_y^R, and equals the graded multiplicity of the indecomposable B_z in the decomposition; (3) also the expansion of the product ch(B_x)ch(B_y) in the standard basis has non-negative coefficients (the Delta-multiplicities of B_xB_y). No sentence of the published Kazhdan-Lusztig basis item proving positivity by citation is used; this corollary is the local proof of the positivity clause, based on the character theorem.

decline_pages.title: Soergel Intersection Forms and Hodge Theory — Examples

items.title: Hard Lefschetz fails for a non-dominant degree-two element: the rank-one case
items.statement: In the rank-one case n = 2 the element rho' := x_1 + x_2 is a degree-two element of S with rho'(alpha_s^\vee) = 0, so it is not strictly dominant. Its action on the reduced rank-one Soergel module is zero: rho' = e_1 = x_1+x_2 is s-invariant and positive-degree, and x_1+x_2 = 1 \cdot e_1 acts on the right basis element c_id bar as the right action by an element of S_+, hence rho'.c_id bar = 0; a fortiori rho' cannot map (B_s bar)^{-1} = R c_id bar isomorphically to (B_s bar)^{1}. Therefore for rho' the hard Lefschetz property fails (the map on the -1 degree is the zero map), even though rho' is a symmetric degree-two endomorphism of the reduced module; the same failure occurs for every degree-two element with rho'(alpha_s^\vee) = 0. Consequently the strict dominance hypothesis on rho cannot be dropped from the hard Lefschetz and Hodge-Riemann theorems, and the constant term of the deformation L_zeta (the zeta = 0 case) is genuinely the delicate one.

items.title: The rank-one Soergel bimodule: trace form, reduced module and hard Lefschetz
items.statement: Take n = 2, so S_n = {e,s} and B_s = S \otimes_{S^s} S(1) with the right S-basis {c_id, c_s} of degrees -1 and +1 and the relations c_id c_id = c_id, c_id c_s = c_s, c_s c_s = c_s alpha_s. The trace is Tr(a c_id + b c_s) = b for a,b in S and the intersection form has the Gram matrix [[<c_id,c_id>, <c_id,c_s>],[<c_s,c_id>,<c_s,c_s>]] = [[0,1],[1,alpha_s]] in the basis (c_id,c_s); its determinant is -1, so the form is non-degenerate, and the induced form on the reduced module is non-degenerate too. The reduced module has the real basis (c_id bar, c_s bar) with degrees -1 and +1, so dim(B_s bar)^{-1} = dim(B_s bar)^{1} = 1, and for rho = (x_1-x_2)/2 = alpha_s/2 (which is strictly dominant: rho(alpha_s^\vee) = 1) one computes rho.c_id = c_s bar and rho.c_s bar = 0; hence rho: (B_s bar)^{-1} -> (B_s bar)^{1} is an isomorphism, hard Lefschetz holds, the primitive subspace in degree -1 is the whole (B_s bar)^{-1}, and the Lefschetz form (a,b) = <a, rho b> is positive on it: <c_id bar, c_s bar> = 1 > 0, matching the Hodge-Riemann sign (-1)^{(-\ell(s)+1)/2} = +1. Finally ch(B_s) = H_s + v = H_s (the Kazhdan-Lusztig basis element of the simple reflection), which is Soergel's conjecture at s, and the rational version over Q gives the same numbers.

items.title: The coinvariant algebra of S_3 as the Soergel bimodule of the longest element
items.statement: Take n = 3 and let w_0 = s_1s_2s_1 be the longest element of S_3. Then B_{w_0} = S \otimes_{S^{S_3}} S(3), and its reduced module is the coinvariant algebra C = S/(S^{S_3}_+) with the external shift removed: C has the Poincare polynomial 1 + 2t^2 + 2t^4 + t^6, so dim C = 6 and in the centered grading dim(B_{w_0} bar)^{-3} = dim(B_{w_0} bar)^3 = 1 and dim(B_{w_0} bar)^{-1} = dim(B_{w_0} bar)^1 = 2. The standard-basis expansion of the Kazhdan-Lusztig basis element is H_{w_0} = H_{w_0} + v(H_{s_1s_2}+H_{s_2s_1}) + v^2(H_{s_1}+H_{s_2}) + v^3, obtained by solving the bar-invariance and triangularity conditions with coefficients in v^dZ[v^{-2}]; its coefficients are non-negative and its value at v = 1 sums to 6 = dim C, and it agrees with the rank-one and rank-two Kazhdan-Lusztig polynomial data P_{e,w_0} = P_{s_i,w_0} = P_{w,w_0} = 1 for \ell(w) = 2. Hence ch(B_{w_0}) = H_{w_0}: Soergel's conjecture holds for the longest element of S_3, and the Delta-multiplicities of the coinvariant bimodule are the six coefficients just displayed, one for each element of S_3.

items.title: The rank-two Bott-Samelson bimodule B_sB_t: character, decomposition and the braid relation
items.statement: Take n = 3 and the two simple reflections s = s_1, t = s_2. The rank-two Bott-Samelson bimodule B_sB_t has character ch(B_sB_t) = ch(B_s)ch(B_t) = (H_s+v)(H_t+v) = H_{st}+vH_s+vH_t+v^2 in the standard basis, so its Delta-multiplicities are 1 at H_{st}, 1 at H_s and at H_t with shift v, and 1 at the identity with shift v^2; in particular all multiplicities are non-negative and the reduced module has dim(B_sB_t bar) = 1+1+1+1 = 4. In S_3 the product st has length 2, and the indecomposable B_{st} has the same character H_{st} = H_{st}+vH_s+vH_t+v^2, so B_sB_t = B_{st} is already indecomposable; equivalently the only summand is the top one B_{st} and all multiplicities m_y for y < st vanish. Similarly B_sB_tB_s = B_{sts} \oplus B_s with characters H_{sts}+H_s, and the rank-two type-A braid relation holds; the example also verifies the rank-two values of the Kazhdan-Lusztig polynomials P_{e,st} = P_{s,st} = P_{t,st} = 1 used on the companion page.

items.title: Hard Lefschetz and the Hodge-Riemann signs for the coinvariant algebra of S_3
items.statement: For n=3 identify the centered reduced longest-element module with C(3), where C=R[x_1,x_2,x_3]/(e_1,e_2,e_3) has dimensions 1,2,2,1 in degrees 0,2,4,6. Thus the centered degrees are -3,-1,1,3. For every strictly dominant rho, hL is rho^3:C(3)^{-3}→C(3)^3 and rho:C(3)^{-1}→C(3)^1, both isomorphisms. The primitive spaces used in HR are P^{-3}=C(3)^{-3}, dimension one, and P^{-1}=ker(rho^2:C(3)^{-1}→C(3)^3), dimension one. Their Lefschetz forms are respectively positive and negative definite. The primitive decomposition consists of one length-four rho string and one length-two string. For an explicit strictly dominant choice let x=x_1, y=x_2, x_3=-x-y, rho=x_1-x_3=2x+y and normalize Tr(x^2y)=1. Then C=R[x,y]/(x^2+xy+y^2,x^3), with basis 1; x,y; x^2,xy; x^2y. The rho map from degree 2 to degree 4 has matrix [[2,-1],[1,1]], rho^3=6x^2y, P^{-1}=R y, and Tr(y rho y)=-2. These computations verify hL and the primitive signs directly in rank two.

items.title: The coinvariant algebra of a finite Weyl group
items.statement: Let $\mathfrak g$ be a finite-dimensional complex semisimple Lie algebra with Cartan subalgebra $\mathfrak h$ and Weyl group $W$ acting on $\mathfrak h$ by reflections, hence on the symmetric algebra $S=S(\mathfrak h)$ by graded algebra automorphisms. Write $S^W_+$ for the ideal of positive-degree invariants and $I:=S\,S^W_+$ for the ideal of $S$ it generates, so that $I$ is the specialization to the Weyl group of the homogeneous ideal of [[def-finite-linear-invariant-and-coinvariant-polynomial-algebras]]. The **coinvariant algebra** is $$C=C(\mathfrak h,W):=S/I.$$ It is a commutative graded $\mathbb C$-algebra with $C_0=\mathbb C$, a canonical surjection $\rho:S\to C$, and an induced action of $W$ by graded algebra automorphisms; $C$ is finite dimensional because $W$ is generated by reflections. The page fixes the degree normalization $\deg\mathfrak h=2$ used throughout the type-A Soergel material, so that the auxiliary permutation-coordinate model is $S_{\mathrm{perm}}=\mathbb k[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ with the place-permuting $S_n$-action and $C\cong\mathbb k[x_1,\dots,x_n]/(e_1,\dots,e_n)$ for the elementary symmetric polynomials $e_1,\dots,e_n$. Elements of $C$ are written as classes $\rho(f)$; no choice principle is used.

items.title: The regular integral block and its antidominant weight
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice, inherited from the published block theory. Work in category $\mathcal O$ of a finite-dimensional complex semisimple Lie algebra $\mathfrak g$ with the conventions of [[def-bgg-category-o]]: Cartan $\mathfrak h$, positive system with simple roots $\alpha_i$, Weyl group $W$, Weyl vector $ho$ and dot action $w\cdot\lambda=w(\lambda+ho)-ho$. Fix the **dominant regular integral representative** $\lambda$ of the block, i.e. $\langle\lambda+ho,\alpha^\veeangle
otin\{0\}$ for every root $\alpha$ and $\lambda$ integral in the sense of [[def-integral-weyl-group-of-a-weight]]; then the integral Weyl group of $\lambda$ is all of $W$, and the linkage class $C=W\cdot\lambda$ has exactly $|W|$ elements. Write $\mathcal O_\lambda:=\mathcal O_C$ for the corresponding block of [[thm-central-character-summands-split-into-linkage-blocks]]; it is a highest-weight category whose simple objects $L(w\cdot\lambda)$, standard objects $\Delta(w\cdot\lambda)=M(w\cdot\lambda)$, costandard objects $
abla(w\cdot\lambda)$ and projective covers $P(w\cdot\lambda)$ are indexed by $w\in W$, with $\Delta(w_0\cdot\lambda)=L(w_0\cdot\lambda)$ the unique simple standard object and the published triangularity $[\Delta(w\cdot\lambda):L(w\cdot\lambda)]=1$ and $[\Delta(w\cdot\lambda):L(v\cdot\lambda)]
eq0\Rightarrow v\cdot\lambda\le w\cdot\lambda$ in the dominance order on the dot orbit ([[thm-bgg-reciprocity]], [[cor-projective-standard-labels-lie-above-the-head]]). The **antidominant** weight in the block is $w_0\cdot\lambda$, where $w_0$ is the longest element; $P(w_0\cdot\lambda)$ is the antidominant projective. The Grothendieck group $K_0(\mathcal O_\lambda)$ has the classes of the standards and of the simples as bases, as on [[def-grothendieck-group-and-character-of-category-o]].

items.title: The sum of basic Weyl invariant degrees minus one counts positive roots
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice inherited from invariant theory. For a finite Weyl reflection group on its rank-r Cartan and basic invariant polynomial degrees d_1,...,d_r (ordinary degree one for Cartan generators), $$\sum_i(d_i-1)=|\Phi^+|.$$ With page degree two, the coinvariant top degree is twice this number.

items.title: Adjoint isotypic modules have the zero-weight rank
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. For complex semisimple g and any finite-dimensional g-module E, the modules Hom_g(E,S(g)) over S(g)^g and Hom_g(E,U(g)) over Z(U(g)) are free of rank dim E_0. Under a g-equivariant harmonic decomposition S(g)=S(g)^g tensor H and its filtered PBW lift U(g)=Z tensor H, every central reduction has adjoint E-multiplicity dim E_0, compatibly with the natural quotient map.

items.title: Projective functors on a regular integral block
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice, inherited from the published block theory. For a finite-dimensional $\mathfrak h$-semisimple $\mathfrak g$-module $E$ and a block $\mathcal O_\lambda$ as in [[def-regular-integral-category-o-block-and-its-antidominant-weight]], let $\operatorname{pr}_\lambda:\mathcal O\to\mathcal O_\lambda$ be the exact block projection of [[def-translation-functor-between-o-blocks]] and let $$F_E:=\operatorname{pr}_\lambda\circ(E\otimes-)\circ\operatorname{incl}_\lambda:\mathcal O_\lambda\longrightarrow\mathcal O_\lambda .$$ By [[prop-tensoring-with-a-finite-dimensional-module-preserves-category-o]] and [[lem-block-projection-preserves-projectives]] the functor $F_E$ is exact, and by [[lem-tensoring-a-projective-with-a-finite-dimensional-module-is-projective]] it sends projectives to projectives. A **projective functor** on $\mathcal O_\lambda$ is an endofunctor of $\mathcal O_\lambda$ isomorphic to a direct summand of some $F_E$; the full additive subcategory of all such functors (with arbitrary natural transformations as morphisms) is written $\mathcal F_\lambda$. It is closed under finite direct sums, composition, direct summands and passage to adjoints: composition corresponds to $F_E F_{E'}\cong F_{E\otimes E'}$, and $F_{E^*}$ is both a left and a right adjoint of $F_E$, by the published biadjunction for tensoring with duals. Every projective functor is exact and preserves projective objects. This is the definition of [BGe] and [Soe90, Section 1.2]; unlike the functors $T_\lambda^\mu$ of [[def-translation-functor-between-o-blocks]], projective functors are not required to come from a single finite-dimensional tensor functor, only from a summand of one.

items.title: The coinvariant algebra is a complete intersection with one-dimensional socle
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice, inherited from the published invariant-theory items. Let $w_1,\dots,w_r$ be homogeneous basic invariants of the finite Weyl group $W$ acting on $\mathfrak h$, of page degrees $2d_1,\dots,2d_r$ so that $d_1,\dots,d_r$ are the classical basic degrees (the degrees with $\deg\mathfrak h=1$; in the type-A model $d_1,\dots,d_r=1,\dots,n$), $S(\mathfrak h)^W=\mathbb C[w_1,\dots,w_r]$, and $\rho$ is the quotient by the ideal $I=(w_1,\dots,w_r)$. Put $N:=\sum_{i=1}^r(d_i-1)$; the top degree of the coinvariant algebra $C$ of [[def-the-coinvariant-algebra-of-a-finite-weyl-group]] is then $2N$. Then: (1) $w_1,\dots,w_r$ is a homogeneous regular sequence in $S$ and $C$ is a complete intersection: $C=S/(w_1,\dots,w_r)$ with $\operatorname{Hilb}(C,t)=\prod_i(1-t^{2d_i})/(1-t^2)^r$, $\dim C_{2N}=1$, $C_j=0$ for $j>2N$; (2) the multiplication pairing $C_i\times C_{2N-i}\to C_{2N}\cong\mathbb C$ is nondegenerate for every $i$, and consequently the socle $\operatorname{soc}(C)=\{c\in C: C_+c=0\}$ equals $C_{2N}$ and is one dimensional; (3) equivalently, $C$ is a graded Gorenstein algebra whose socle sits in the top degree $2N$.

items.title: The harmonic complement of the coinvariant algebra
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice, inherited from the published invariant-theory items. Let $W$ act on $\mathfrak h$ by reflections and on $S=S(\mathfrak h)$ by graded algebra automorphisms, with coinvariant algebra $C=S/I$ as in [[def-the-coinvariant-algebra-of-a-finite-weyl-group]]. Then there is a $W$-stable graded subspace $\mathcal H\subseteq S$ such that the multiplication map $$S^W\otimes_{\mathbb C}\mathcal H\longrightarrow S,\qquad p\otimes h\mapsto ph,$$ is an isomorphism of graded $S^W$-modules and $W$-modules, and the restriction of the quotient map $\rho:S\to C$ to $\mathcal H$ is an isomorphism of graded $W$-modules $\mathcal H\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }C$. One may take $\mathcal H=\{f\in S:\partial_p f=0\text{ for all }p\in S^W_+\}$ for the $W$-equivariant Laplacian attached to a $W$-invariant positive definite form on $\mathfrak h_{\mathbb R}$, or any $W$-stable graded complement of $I$; in particular $\dim\mathcal H_d=\dim C_d$ for all $d$, $\dim\mathcal H=|W|$.

items.title: The deformed category O family over the Cartan symmetric algebra
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $S=S(\mathfrak h)$ be the symmetric algebra of the Cartan subalgebra, graded by $\deg\mathfrak h=2$, and let $\mathfrak b=\mathfrak h\oplus\mathfrak n^+$ act on $S\otimes\mathbb C_\lambda$ by $x\cdot(s\otimes1)=xs\otimes1+\lambda(x)s\otimes1$ for $x\in\mathfrak h$ and $x\cdot(s\otimes1)=xs\otimes1$ for $x\in\mathfrak n^+$, where $xs$ denotes the action of $\mathfrak b	o\mathfrak h$ on $S$ by weight. Put $M_S(\lambda):=U(\mathfrak g)\otimes_{U(\mathfrak b)}(S\otimes\mathbb C_\lambda)\in \mathfrak g\otimes S$-mod, with the right $S$-module structure by multiplication on the last factor, so that $M_S(\lambda)\otimes_S\mathbb C_\epsilon\cong M(\lambda+\epsilon)$ for every $\epsilon\in\mathfrak h^*$. For a localization $T$ of $S$ put $M_T(\lambda):=M_S(\lambda)\otimes_S T$ and let $\mathcal D_T(\lambda)$ be the full subcategory of $\mathfrak g\otimes T$-modules that are direct summands of a finite direct sum of modules $E\otimes M_T(\lambda)$ for finite-dimensional $\mathfrak g$-modules $E$; write $\mathcal D_R(\lambda)$ for the localization $R=S_{(0)}$ at the origin of $\operatorname{Spec} S$. The **deformed family** is the assignment $T\mapsto\mathcal D_T(\lambda)$ together with the specialization functors $-\otimes_T\mathbb C_\epsilon$ at the closed points $\epsilon$ of $\operatorname{Spec} T$; the specializations have Verma constituents with highest weights $\lambda+
u+\epsilon$, where $
u$ runs through the finite-dimensional tensor weights, and can meet several central-character blocks; a generic parameter is generally nonintegral, and the Verma constituents generically have distinct central characters except for repeated identical labels. For a regular dominant integral source $\lambda$ and any dot-dominant integral target $
u$ (so $
u+ho$ is in the closed positive chamber), denote by $\mathcal D_R^{[
u]}(\lambda)$ the component of $\mathcal D_R(\lambda)$ whose closed fiber lies in the selected target block $\mathcal O_
u$; finite Verma flags and pairwise-unit resultants of their central-character polynomials define this component by actual central idempotents over $R$. Other central-character components remain part of the full tensor family. Modules in $\mathcal D_T(\lambda)$ carry an $\mathfrak h$-weight decomposition with locally free finite-rank weight spaces. The conventions are those of [Soe90, Section 2.1].

items.title: The nilpotent central fiber is reduced and integral
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let p_1,...,p_r be homogeneous basic generators of S(g)^g for complex semisimple g, corresponding by Chevalley restriction to basic Weyl invariants. Then $$A=S(g)/(p_1,\ldots,p_r)$$ is a reduced integral domain of dimension dim g-r=2|Phi^+|, with Hilbert series product_i(1-t^{d_i})/(1-t)^{dim g}. For every central character chi, the PBW associated graded of U(g)/U(g)ker chi is canonically A.

items.title: The wall-crossing functor and its unit and counit
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Fix the dominant regular integral block representative $\lambda$ and an integral highest weight $\mu$ such that $\lambda+\rho$ is regular dominant and $\mu+\rho$ is dominant with dot stabilizer exactly $\{1,s\}$. This is the dominant-chamber version of single-wall data; the published datum uses antidominant representatives. Take the finite-dimensional simple $E$ with extremal weight $\mu-\lambda$, and define onto-wall translation $T_{\mathrm{on}}=\operatorname{pr}_{\chi_\mu}(E\otimes-)$ and out-of-wall translation $T_{\mathrm{out}}=\operatorname{pr}_{\chi_\lambda}(E^*\otimes-)$. The wall-crossing functor is $\theta_s=T_{\mathrm{out}}T_{\mathrm{on}}$. It is an exact projective functor, a natural direct summand of tensoring by $E^*\otimes E$ followed by regular block projection. The two tensor-block adjunctions give $\eta:\operatorname{id}\to\theta_s$ and $\varepsilon:\theta_s\to\operatorname{id}$; each belongs to its corresponding adjunction pair and satisfies the triangle identities with the companion unit or counit on the wall category. Up to natural equivalence the functor depends only on the wall and the block; the chosen biadjunction maps remain part of the data.

items.title: The coinvariant algebra is the graded regular representation of W
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice, inherited from the published invariant-theory items. Let $W$ be a finite Weyl group with reflection representation $\mathfrak h$, coinvariant algebra $C=S(\mathfrak h)/S(\mathfrak h)S^W_+$ and basic degrees $d_1,\dots,d_r$ as in [[def-the-coinvariant-algebra-of-a-finite-weyl-group]]. Then: (1) $C\cong\mathbb C W$ as a $W$-module: $C$ is isomorphic to the regular representation of $W$; (2) the graded $W$-character of $C$ is $$\operatorname{HTr}(C,t)(w):=\sum_{i\ge0}t^{i}\operatorname{tr}(w\mid C_i)=\prod_{i=1}^r(1-t^{2d_i})\cdot\det(1-t^2w\mid\mathfrak h^*)^{-1}\qquad(w\in W),$$ where $d_1,\dots,d_r$ are the classical basic degrees of [[lem-the-coinvariant-algebra-is-a-gorenstein-algebra-with-one-dimensional-socle]], an identity of rational functions whose value at $t=1$ is $|W|$ for $w=1$ and $0$ for $w\neq1$; (3) equivalently, $C$ is the graded lift of the regular representation: writing $\operatorname{mult}_E(C,t)$ for the graded multiplicity of the irreducible $W$-module $E$, the identity $\sum_E\operatorname{mult}_E(C,t)\,\chi_E(w)=\operatorname{HTr}(C,t)(w)$ determines the graded multiplicities uniquely, with $\operatorname{mult}_E(C,1)=\dim E$ the multiplicity of $E$ in the regular representation. The Hilbert-series specialization of (2) at $w=1$ is $\prod_i(1+t^2+\dots+t^{2(d_i-1)})$, the published formula in the page's $\deg\mathfrak h=2$ normalization.

items.title: The antidominant projective and the Soergel functor
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice, inherited from the published items. In the regular integral block $\mathcal O_\lambda$ of [[def-regular-integral-category-o-block-and-its-antidominant-weight]] fix the antidominant weight $w_0\cdot\lambda$ and let $P:=P(w_0\cdot\lambda)$ be a projective cover of $L(w_0\cdot\lambda)$; it is unique up to isomorphism and indecomposable by [[prop-projective-covers-in-o-are-indecomposable-and-unique]], and it is an injective object of $\mathcal O_\lambda$. The **Soergel functor** is $$V:=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O}(P,-)\colon\mathcal O_\lambda\longrightarrow \operatorname{End}_{\mathcal O}(P)^{\mathrm{op}}\text{-mod},\qquad M\longmapsto \operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O}(P,M),$$ with the action of $\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal O}(P)$ induced by composition of endomorphisms of $P$. Its values on the standard objects and on the indecomposable projectives are written $V\Delta(w\cdot\lambda):=V(\Delta(w\cdot\lambda))$ and $VP(w\cdot\lambda):=V(P(w\cdot\lambda))$; the choice of projective cover changes $V$ by a natural equivalence only. The functor is exact, and hence left exact, and $VP\cong\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal O}(P)$ with the regular module structure.

items.title: Duflo–Joseph g-finite endomorphisms of every Verma module
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. For every highest weight mu of a finite-dimensional complex semisimple Lie algebra, the action induces an algebra isomorphism $$U(g)/U(g)\ker\chi_\mu\ \xrightarrow{\sim}\ (\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}M(\mu))^{\mathrm{ad}\,g\text{-finite}}.$$ In particular Ann M(mu)=U(g)ker chi_mu. For every finite-dimensional E, dim Hom_g(M(mu),E tensor M(mu))=dim E_0, and the action identifies each finite adjoint isotypic multiplicity with that dimension.

items.title: Wall-crossing acts on standard modules by a two-step extension
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice, inherited from the published items. Let $\theta_s$ be the wall-crossing functor of [[def-wall-crossing-functor-and-unit-counit]] attached to the simple reflection $s$ in the regular integral block $\mathcal O_\lambda$. For every $w\in W$ the object $\theta_s\Delta(w\cdot\lambda)$ has a finite Verma flag with exactly two factors, namely $\Delta(w\cdot\lambda)$ and $\Delta(ws\cdot\lambda)$, each with multiplicity one; in the Grothendieck group $$[\theta_s\Delta(w\cdot\lambda)]=[\Delta(w\cdot\lambda)]+[\Delta(ws\cdot\lambda)].$$ Moreover the functor is exact and preserves Verma-filtered objects and finite Verma flags: if $X$ has a finite Verma flag with multiplicities $(X:\Delta(v\cdot\lambda))$, then $\theta_s X$ has one with multiplicity $(\theta_s X:\Delta(u\cdot\lambda))=(X:\Delta(u\cdot\lambda))+(X:\Delta(us\cdot\lambda))$, and the same formula holds for the images in the Grothendieck group. This is the wall-crossing computation of [Soe90, Section 2.1] in the form supplied by the published wall-translation theorem; the resulting flag is not in general split, but splitting is not asserted or used here.

items.title: Base change, freeness and specialization in the deformed family
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. In the deformed family of [[def-the-deformed-category-o-family-and-its-specializations]] with $T$ a localization of $S=S(\mathfrak h)$ and $M,N\in\mathcal D_T(\lambda)$: (1) the canonical map $$U(\mathfrak g)\otimes_Z T\longrightarrow \big(\operatorname{End}_T(M_T(\lambda))\big)^{\mathfrak g\text{-finite}},\qquad u\otimes t\longmapsto\big(m\mapsto u\cdot m\cdot t\big),$$ is an isomorphism of $T$-algebras, the superscript denoting the $\mathfrak g$-finite part for the adjoint action $X\cdot f=X\circ f-f\circ X$, and $Z=Z(U(\mathfrak g))$ acting on $T$ through the published shifted Harish-Chandra isomorphism $\operatorname{HC}_\rho$ followed by evaluation at $\lambda+\rho+\epsilon$ on the universal parameter $\epsilon$; (2) $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g\otimes T}(E\otimes M_T(\lambda),F\otimes M_T(\lambda))$ is a free $T$-module of rank $\dim(E\otimes F^*)_0$ for finite-dimensional $E,F$, where the subscript denotes the zero weight space, and the natural base-change map $$\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g\otimes T}(M,N)\otimes_T\kappa(\epsilon)\longrightarrow \operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g\otimes\kappa(\epsilon)}(M\otimes_T\kappa(\epsilon),N\otimes_T\kappa(\epsilon))$$ is an isomorphism for every $\epsilon\in\operatorname{Spec} T$, with residue field $\kappa(\epsilon)$; (3) $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g\otimes T}(M,N)$ is locally free of finite rank over $T$; (4) if a $\mathfrak g\otimes R$-linear map of objects of $\mathcal D_R(\lambda)$ is an isomorphism on the special fiber at $0$, it is an isomorphism (Nakayama).

items.title: The wall-crossing action on the Grothendieck group is multiplication by 1+s
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice, inherited from the published items. In the regular integral block $\mathcal O_\lambda$ of [[def-regular-integral-category-o-block-and-its-antidominant-weight]] the assignment $$c\colon K_0(\mathcal O_\lambda)\longrightarrow\mathbb Z[W],\qquad [\Delta(w\cdot\lambda)]\longmapsto w,$$ is an isomorphism of abelian groups, and for every simple reflection $s$ the wall-crossing functor $\theta_s$ of [[def-wall-crossing-functor-and-unit-counit]] satisfies $$c\,[\theta_s X]=c\,[X]\cdot(1+s)\qquad\text{for all }X\in\mathcal O_\lambda,$$ i.e. right multiplication by $1+s$ in the integral group ring $\mathbb Z[W]$. Consequently $c$ intertwines the wall-crossing action with the right regular action of $\mathbb Z[W]$ generated by the elements $1+s$; in particular for a reduced word $w=s_1\cdots s_k$, one has $c[\theta_{s_k}\cdots\theta_{s_1}\Delta(\lambda)]=(1+s_1)\cdots(1+s_k)$, the sum of all subexpression products with their actual multiplicities; its top Bruhat term is $w$ once and all other terms have smaller labels. With the displayed composition $\theta_{s_1}\cdots\theta_{s_k}$ instead, the factors are multiplied in the reverse order.

items.title: Wall-crossing compositions produce the projective with the top standard label
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. For a dominant regular integral representative $\lambda$ and reduced word $w=s_1\cdots s_k$, set $\theta_{\underline w}=\theta_{s_k}\cdots\theta_{s_1}$, so the standards follow right multiplication in word order. Then $$\theta_{\underline w}\Delta(\lambda)\cong P(w\cdot\lambda)\oplus\bigoplus_{x<w}P(x\cdot\lambda)^{m_x},\qquad m_x\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}.$$ Its class is $(1+s_1)\cdots(1+s_k)$ under the standard class map, with actual subexpression multiplicities. The BGG matrix satisfies $(P(x\cdot\lambda):\Delta(y\cdot\lambda))=[\Delta(y\cdot\lambda):L(x\cdot\lambda)]$, vanishes unless $y\le x$ in Bruhat order, and has diagonal entries one. Hence the top summand $P(w\cdot\lambda)$ occurs once and is the only summand whose flag contains $\Delta(w\cdot\lambda)$; the remaining multiplicities are determined by this triangular matrix and the product class. Consequently every indecomposable projective is a summand of a word of wall crossings applied to $\Delta(\lambda)$.

items.title: Lifting of indecomposable projectives to the deformed family
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\lambda$ be dominant regular integral, $R=S(\mathfrak h)_{(0)}$, and use the selected component $\mathcal D_R^{[\lambda]}(\lambda)$ of the tensor-generated deformed family. For every $x\in W$ there is a projective $P_R(x,\lambda)$ in the deformed $\lambda$ block whose residue fiber is $P(x\cdot\lambda)$. It is unique up to isomorphism; every indecomposable of this selected tensor component is one of these lifts. Each lift has a finite deformed Verma flag with the same multiplicities as its closed fiber. More generally, a finite projective in this block is a direct summand of a finite sum of the truncated induced projectives representing relative weight spaces; for every map of deformation algebras $R	o R'$ its base change is projective in the corresponding truncated category, and $$\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_R}(P,N)\otimes_R R'\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_{R'}}(P\otimes_R R',N\otimes_R R').$$ For a finite Verma-filtered target $N$, this Hom module is finite free over local $R$. A g⊗R-linear map between such finite projective/Verma-filtered objects whose residue fiber is an isomorphism is itself an isomorphism, weight by weight. For a dot-dominant integral target $
u$, including singular $
u$, the same local projective construction gives all lifts in its deformed block, with labels the distinct cosets $W/W_
u$. These lifts belong to the target component $\mathcal D_R^{[
u]}(\lambda)$ of a regular-source tensor family; it is not necessary or asserted that the singular Verma itself generates every target projective. The full tensor family, including other central components, is not claimed to have only these indecomposables.

items.title: Indecomposable projective functors are indexed by the Weyl group
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. In a regular integral block with dominant representative $\lambda$: (1) projective functors form a Krull-Schmidt category; (2) their indecomposables are indexed by $W$, with $\Theta_w$ characterized by $\Theta_w\Delta(\lambda)\cong P(w\cdot\lambda)$. For any reduced word $w=s_1\cdots s_k$, $\Theta_w$ is a multiplicity-one summand of $\theta_{s_k}\cdots\theta_{s_1}$ and every other indecomposable summand has a label $x<w$. In particular every indecomposable projective functor is generated as a summand by wall crossings. (3) Two projective functors are naturally equivalent exactly when their induced operators on the Grothendieck group agree. The characterization concerns evaluation on the dominant projective Verma.

items.title: The central action on the deformed antidominant projective
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\lambda$ be dominant regular integral, $S=S(\mathfrak h)$, $R=S_{(0)}$, and $P_R=P_R(w_0,\lambda)$ the deformed antidominant projective. Write $\operatorname{HC}_ho\colon Z(U(\mathfrak g))	o S^W$ for the published shifted Harish-Chandra isomorphism, $\sigma_\lambda(f)(\epsilon)=f(\lambda+ho+\epsilon)$, and define $$a_\lambda\colon Z\otimes_{\mathbb C}R\longrightarrow R\otimes_{R^W}R,\qquad z\otimes r\longmapsto\sigma_\lambda(\operatorname{HC}_ho(z))\otimes r.$$ Then $a_\lambda$ and the action map $Z\otimes R	o\operatorname{End}_{\mathfrak g\otimes R}(P_R)$ are surjective and have the same kernel, inducing a canonical $R$-algebra isomorphism $$\operatorname{End}_{\mathfrak g\otimes R}(P_R)\cong R\otimes_{R^W}R.$$ On a generic Verma constituent of highest weight $x\cdot\lambda+\epsilon$, $z$ acts by the scalar $\operatorname{HC}_ho(z)(x(\lambda+ho)+\epsilon)=\sigma_\lambda(\operatorname{HC}_ho(z))(x^{-1}\epsilon)$; these scalars vary with $x$, and the center need not act by a single scalar on $P_R$. After tensoring the right $R$ factor with the residue field at $0$, the endomorphism algebra becomes $C=S/(S^W_+S)$. More generally, for dot-dominant integral $
u$ (meaning $
u+ho$ lies in the closed positive chamber) the corresponding algebra is $R^{W_
u}\otimes_{R^W}R$, where $W_
u$ is the dot stabilizer. Translation out of that facet identifies the singular antidominant projective with the regular one; under these shifted Harish-Chandra identifications, its induced endomorphism map is the inclusion $R^{W_
u}\otimes_{R^W}R\hookrightarrow R\otimes_{R^W}R$.

items.title: The endomorphisms of the antidominant projective form the coinvariant algebra
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\mathfrak g$ be finite-dimensional complex semisimple, $\lambda$ the dominant regular integral representative of a block and $\mathcal O_\lambda$ its block with antidominant weight $w_0\cdot\lambda$. Let $C$ be the coinvariant algebra of [[def-the-coinvariant-algebra-of-a-finite-weyl-group]] for the Cartan reflection representation, with its grading fixed there. Then: (1) the natural maps $Z(U(\mathfrak g))\to C$ (Harish-Chandra isomorphism, shifted by $\lambda+\rho$ in the published $\operatorname{HC}_\rho$ convention, followed by the quotient map $\rho$) and $Z(U(\mathfrak g))\to\operatorname{End}_{\mathfrak g}P(w_0\cdot\lambda)$ (multiplication) are surjective with the same kernel; (2) consequently the multiplication map induces a canonical algebra isomorphism $$\operatorname{End}_{\mathfrak g}P(w_0\cdot\lambda)\ \cong\ C,$$ identifying $C$ with the endomorphism ring of the antidominant projective, canonically and independently of the choice of projective cover inside its isomorphism class; (3) the grading on the right-hand side is the internal grading of the coinvariant algebra; no graded lift of category $\mathcal O$ is asserted or used. This is Soergel's Endomorphismensatz [Soe90, Theorem 7], in the regular integral case; the companion general form for singular blocks replaces $C$ by the invariants $C^{W_\lambda}$.

items.title: Soergel's Struktursatz: the functor V is fully faithful on projectives
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\mathcal O_\lambda$ be a regular integral block with antidominant projective $P=P(w_0\cdot\lambda)$ and Soergel functor $V=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O}(P,-)$, and let $C$ be the coinvariant algebra, identified with $\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal O}(P)$ by [[thm-endomorphisms-of-the-antidominant-projective-are-the-coinvariant-algebra]], so that $V$ takes values in $C$-modules. Then for every $M\in\mathcal O_\lambda$ and every projective $Q\in\mathcal O_\lambda$ the canonical map $$V\colon \operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_\lambda}(M,Q)\longrightarrow \operatorname{Hom}_{C\text{-mod}}(VM,VQ)$$ is an isomorphism. In particular $V$ is fully faithful on the full subcategory of projective objects of the block, and it is faithful on all of $\mathcal O_\lambda$ after passing to the quotient by the Serre subcategory of objects killed by $V$.

items.title: Wall-crossing under the Soergel functor is tensoring with the coinvariant bimodule
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. For a regular integral block and simple reflection $s$, with $C=\operatorname{End}(P(w_0\cdot\lambda))$, there is a natural isomorphism of functors to left $C$-modules $$V\theta_s\cong C\otimes_{C^s}V.$$ Equivalently the functor is tensoring by the $(C,C)$-bimodule $C\otimes_{C^s}C$, with left action on the first factor and right action on the second. In type A over $\mathbb C$, its polynomial lift is tensoring on the left by $B_s=S\otimes_{S^s}S(1)$; for a right-reduced polynomial bimodule $\bar M=M\otimes_S\mathbb C$, one has $\overline{B_s\otimes_SM}\cong B_s\otimes_S\bar M\cong(C\otimes_{C^s}C)(1)\otimes_C\bar M$. Forgetting the grading gives the displayed category-$\mathcal O$ formula. The normalized self-dual rank-one reduction has generator degrees $-1,1$; shifting it to degrees $0,2$ is an alternative uncentered normalization. No grading on arbitrary category-$\mathcal O$ objects is asserted. In particular $B_s\otimes_S\mathbb C$ itself is not the bimodule $C\otimes_{C^s}C$: the former has vector-space dimension two, whereas the latter has dimension $2|W|$.

items.title: Indecomposable projectives correspond to indecomposable Soergel modules
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice and work in a regular integral type-A block over $\mathbb C$. With the page's right wall-crossing convention and left $C$-module values of $V$, there is an equivalence $$V\colon\operatorname{Proj}(\mathcal O_\lambda)\xrightarrow{\sim}\{\text{ungraded Soergel modules }B\otimes_S\mathbb C\},\qquad P(w\cdot\lambda)\longmapsto\bar B_{w^{-1}}.$$ The target is the additive category of direct summands of the right reductions of polynomial Bott-Samelson bimodules, or equivalently of iterated $C\otimes_{C^s}(-)$ applied to the trivial module $\mathbb C$, not to the regular module $C$. For $w=s_1\cdots s_k$, the projective is the unique new top-label summand of $\theta_{s_k}\cdots\theta_{s_1}\Delta(\lambda)$; applying $V$ gives the new summand of $\overline{B_{s_k}\cdots B_{s_1}}$, thus the inverse label. These normalized indecomposable polynomial lifts supply self-dual auxiliary gradings; in rank one the centered degrees are $-1,1$, with degrees $0,2$ after an uncentered shift. Forgetting grading recovers the projective dictionary. More generally the ungraded equivalence with Weyl-group Soergel modules holds for every complex semisimple regular integral block; the type-A diagrammatic label comparison applies only in type A.

items.title: Verma-flag multiplicities are standard-filtration ranks under V
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. For a projective $P$ in a regular integral type-A block, choose its polynomial Soergel lift $\mathsf B(P)$ determined by the preceding projective dictionary: if $P=\bigoplus_wP(w\cdot\lambda)^{m_w}$, take $\mathsf B(P)=\bigoplus_w B_{w^{-1}}^{m_w}$, so that its right reduction is $V(P)$ after forgetting auxiliary grading. Write $r_{x,d}(\mathsf B(P))$ for the graded multiplicity of the polynomial standard graph module supported at $x$ in its standard support filtration, with the standard-generator normalization of the polynomial Soergel category. Then $$ (P:\Delta(y\cdot\lambda))=\sum_d r_{y^{-1},d}(\mathsf B(P)). $$ Equivalently the polynomial Soergel character of this lift, evaluated at $v=1$ and with inverse labels, recovers the ordinary Verma-flag character of $P$. These are ranks before reduction; no separated Bruhat-support filtration intrinsic to the finite-dimensional module $V(P)$ is asserted, since the graph supports coalesce at the origin. The same ungraded multiplicity comparison holds with the corresponding Weyl-group polynomial/deformed lifts in other complex semisimple types.

decline_pages.title: Projective Functors and the Soergel Functor in Category O — Examples

items.title: The coinvariant algebra of S_2 and S_3 as graded regular representations
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice, inherited from the published items used. For $W=S_2$ acting on $\mathfrak h$ of dimension one: $C=\mathbb k[x]/(x^2)$, of Hilbert series $1+t^2$ in the page normalization $\deg x=2$ (equivalently $1+t$ for $\deg x=1$), with $C_0$ the trivial and $C_2$ the sign representation, so $C$ is the regular representation of $S_2$ with graded multiplicities one and one. For $W=S_3$ acting on the two-dimensional reflection representation: $C=\mathbb k[x_1,x_2,x_3]/(e_1,e_2,e_3)$ has Hilbert series $(1+t^2)(1+t^2+t^4)=1+2t^2+2t^4+t^6$ in the same normalization (equivalently $(1+t)(1+t+t^2)$ for $\deg x_i=1$) and decomposes as $C_0=$ trivial, $C_2=$ standard, $C_4=$ standard$\otimes$sign, $C_6=$ sign, the graded lift of the regular representation with graded multiplicities $1$ for the trivial module, $t^6$ for the sign module and $t^2+t^4$ for the two-dimensional standard module. In both cases the graded character identity of [[thm-the-weyl-coinvariant-algebra-is-the-graded-regular-representation]] evaluates to the regular representation's character and the sum of the graded multiplicities times dimensions recovers $|W|$.

items.title: The wall-crossing functor on Verma modules in rank one
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. In $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ let $\lambda=0$, $\rho=1$, regular standards $\Delta_1=M(0)$, $\Delta_s=M(-2)$, and singular wall weight $\mu=-1$, whose shifted weight $\mu+\rho=0$. The translating finite-dimensional simple has highest weight1 and dimension2. Translation onto the wall sends both regular standards to $M(-1)$; translation out gives the projective $P(-2)$. Thus both $\theta_s\Delta_1$ and $\theta_s\Delta_s$ have the same nonsplit standard extension $$0\to M(0)\to P(-2)\to M(-2)\to0,$$ and their classes are $[\Delta_1]+[\Delta_s]$. The wall is -1 in highest-weight coordinates, or0 in shifted coordinates.

items.title: The class map and the wall-crossing action in rank two
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice, inherited from the published items used. In type $A_2$ with simple reflections $s,t$ of order three, the classes of the standards in the regular integral block are $[\Delta_1],[\Delta_s],[\Delta_t],[\Delta_{st}],[\Delta_{ts}],[\Delta_{sts}]$, and the class map sends them to the elements of $W=S_3$; the wall-crossing functors act by right multiplication by $1+s$ and $1+t$, so that $$[\theta_s\theta_t\Delta_1]=[\Delta_1]+[\Delta_t]+[\Delta_s]+[\Delta_{ts}]$$ while $$[\theta_t\theta_s\Delta_1]=[\Delta_1]+[\Delta_s]+[\Delta_t]+[\Delta_{st}],$$ exhibiting the non-commutativity of the wall-crossing action and matching the multiplication of the corresponding standard generators in the Hecke algebra of $S_3$. The example also computes the standard multiplicities of the projective $\theta_s\theta_t\Delta_1$: by the unitriangularity of BGG reciprocity the indecomposable summand $P(ts\cdot\lambda)$ occurs with multiplicity one and the remaining summands have smaller labels.

items.title: Wall-crossing functors do not commute
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice, inherited from the published items used. In type $A_2$ with distinct simple reflections $s,t$, the projective functors $\theta_s\theta_t$ and $\theta_t\theta_s$ on the regular integral block are not naturally equivalent: on the standard object $\Delta(\lambda)$ their classes are $[\Delta(\lambda)]+[\Delta(t\cdot\lambda)]+[\Delta(s\cdot\lambda)]+[\Delta(ts\cdot\lambda)]$ and $[\Delta(\lambda)]+[\Delta(s\cdot\lambda)]+[\Delta(t\cdot\lambda)]+[\Delta(st\cdot\lambda)]$, which differ because $st\neq ts$ and the Verma classes are linearly independent. So the wall-crossing functors do not define a representation of $W$; they categorify the Hecke algebra of $W$, in which $H_sH_t\neq H_tH_s$ for $m_{st}=3$, rather than the group algebra. The counterexample is the functor-level sharpening of the rank-two class computation and shows that 'generated by wall-crossing' cannot be read as 'representation of $W$'.

items.title: Wall-crossing on the projectives in the sl_2 block
items.statement: Assume the inherited Axiom of Choice. In the regular integral sl_2 block with lambda=0, rho=1, s dot 0=-2 and singular wall weight mu=-1, the indecomposable projectives are P_e=M(0) and P_s=P(-2). The wall-crossing functor theta_s satisfies theta_s(P_e)≅P_s and theta_s(P_s)≅P_s⊕P_s. In ordered projective bases (P_e,P_s), its matrix, with columns as inputs, is ((0,0),(1,2)). On the Soergel side C=k[x]/(x²), C^s=k and V(P_e)=k, V(P_s)=C; hence V theta_s(P_e)=C⊗_k k≅C and V theta_s(P_s)=C⊗_k C≅C⊕C as left C-modules. The latter tensor is the four-dimensional coinvariant bimodule (left C acts on the first factor), while the right-reduced polynomial B_s is only two dimensional. The result computes wall-crossing on projective objects, in addition to the preserved existing computation on Verma modules.

items.title: The Soergel functor on the small regular sl_2 block
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice inherited from the category-O suppliers. Work over k=C in the dominant regular integral sl_2 block at lambda=0, with rho=1 and W={e,s}, so s dot 0=-2. Put Delta_e=M(0), Delta_s=M(-2)=L(-2), P_e=P(0)=Delta_e and P_s=P(-2). There are nonsplit sequences 0→L(-2)→Delta_e→L(0)→0 and 0→Delta_e→P_s→Delta_s→0. With C=k[x]/(x²), deg x=2, and V=Hom(P_s,-), the left C-module values are V(P_e)=k=C/(x), V(P_s)=C, V(Delta_e)=V(Delta_s)=k, V(L(0))=0 and V(L(-2))=k. The projective Hom table, with rows as sources P_e,P_s and columns as targets P_e,P_s, is ((k,k),(k,C)); thus the four dimensions are ((1,1),(1,2)). Choose i:k→C, i(1)=x, and p:C→k, p(a+bx)=a. Under the Struktursatz these are the nonzero mixed projective maps, with p i=0 and i p=m_x, multiplication by x. This explicitly computes End(P_s)=C and the projective full-faithfulness comparison, rather than claiming full faithfulness on the whole block. For S=k[a], s(a)=-a, the polynomial lifts B_e=S and B_s=S⊗_{k[a²]}S(1) reduce on the right to k and C(1); their labels are e^{-1}=e and s^{-1}=s. The centered auxiliary degrees on C(1) are -1,1. Before reduction the standard graph ranks (e,s) are (1,0) for B_e and (1,1) for B_s, agreeing with the Verma-flag multiplicities of P_e and P_s at v=1. These ranks are taken before graph supports coalesce at the origin; no grading on arbitrary O objects or intrinsic separated-support filtration on V(P) is asserted.

items.title: The Soergel functor is not fully faithful on all category-O objects
items.statement: Assume the inherited Axiom of Choice. The assertion that V=Hom(P(-2),-) is fully faithful on every object of the regular integral sl_2 block at lambda=0 is false. Let L_0=L(0) be the nonzero one-dimensional simple. Then V(L_0)=0 and the nonzero identity in Hom_O(L_0,L_0)=k maps to zero in Hom_C(0,0)=0: V is not faithful. It also fails fullness on Hom_O(M(0),L(-2)): that Hom space is zero, whereas V(M(0))=V(L(-2))=k=C/(x) and Hom_C(k,k)=k. Both counterexamples have a nonprojective target, so they do not contradict the Struktursatz, which requires its target Q to be projective (and allows an arbitrary source). Passing to the quotient by the V-killed Serre subcategory is a separate assertion and is not refuted.
