decline_pages.title: The Kazhdan–Lusztig Character and Multiplicity Theorem

items.title: The regular integral dot-orbit labelling convention
items.statement:
Fix a finite-dimensional complex semisimple Lie algebra $\mathfrak g$ of type $A_{n-1}$ with Cartan $\mathfrak h$, positive system $\Phi^+$, Weyl vector $ho$, Weyl group $W$ (identified with $S_n$) and dot action $w\cdot\lambda=w(\lambda+ho)-ho$. Fix a dominant regular integral weight $\lambda$, i.e. $\langle\lambda+ho,\alpha^\veeangle
eq0$ for every root and $\lambda$ integral, and let $\mathcal O_\lambda$ be the corresponding regular integral block in the conventions of [[def-regular-integral-category-o-block-and-its-antidominant-weight]]: standard objects $\Delta(w\cdot\lambda)=M(w\cdot\lambda)$, simples $L(w\cdot\lambda)$, indecomposable projectives $P(w\cdot\lambda)$ for $w\in W$, with $\lambda=e\cdot\lambda$ the unique dominant and $w_0\cdot\lambda$ the unique antidominant element and $\Delta(w_0\cdot\lambda)=L(w_0\cdot\lambda)$. The page freezes the following conventions, each inherited from the cited suppliers and used verbatim below. (i) Multiplicity conventions: $(P(w\cdot\lambda):\Delta(y\cdot\lambda))$ is the Verma-flag multiplicity of [[def-verma-flag-and-its-multiplicities]] and $[M(y\cdot\lambda):L(w\cdot\lambda)]$ the composition multiplicity, and $(P(w\cdot\lambda):\Delta(y\cdot\lambda))=[M(y\cdot\lambda):L(w\cdot\lambda)]$ by BGG reciprocity. (ii) Bruhat reversal convention: along the bijection $W
i w\mapsto w\cdot\lambda$ the Bruhat order runs opposite to the dominance order, in the two exact senses used on this page: $y\le w$ implies $w\cdot\lambda\le y\cdot\lambda$ in the dominance order, and every nonzero multiplicity forces the index direction, i.e. $[M(y\cdot\lambda):L(w\cdot\lambda)]
eq0$ implies $y\le w$ in the Bruhat order. The full statement that the two orders are isomorphic as posets is not needed here and is not asserted. (iii) Hecke and Kazhdan-Lusztig normalization: the KL basis $\underline H_w=\sum_{y\le w}p_{y,w}H_y$ of the normalized type-$A$ Hecke algebra, with $p_{y,w}=v^{\ell(w)-\ell(y)}P_{y,w}(v^{-2})$ in the classical $q=v^{-2}$ normalization, support $p_{y,w}=0$ unless $y\le w$, and simultaneous inversion symmetry $p_{y^{-1},w^{-1}}=p_{y,w}$. (iv) Soergel label and character dictionary: R_x denotes the polynomial standard graph bimodule and B_x the normalized indecomposable polynomial Soergel bimodule. The projective dictionary is V(P(w dot lambda))=bar B_{w^-1}, using left coinvariant modules and right polynomial reduction; graph x corresponds to Delta(x^-1 dot lambda). Individual graph ranks are taken before reduction only. In the published standard-generator normalization Delta_x(d)=R_x(d-ell(x)), put m_x(B;v)=sum_d r_{x,d}(B)v^d. The standard character is h_Delta(B)=sum_x m_x(B;v) tilde T_x, with tilde T_x=v^ell(x)T_x equal to the normalized STANDARD H_x of clause(iii). The published split-K0 simple KL generator H_i=v(T_i+1)=H_{s_i}+v is distinct from that standard element. The standard-character lemma identifies h_Delta with the split-K0 isomorphism. Products of simple Soergel classes compute Bott-Samelson classes and need not equal an indecomposable [B_x]; the character theorem is needed to identify h_Delta(B_x) with underline H_x. Gradings here are auxiliary polynomial gradings; forgetting them recovers the ordinary projective dictionary.

items.title: Projective Verma multiplicities equal Soergel standard ranks
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\mathcal O_\lambda$ be a regular integral type-$A$ block with $W=S_n$, and for $w\in W$ let $B_{w^{-1}}$ be the polynomial Soergel lift of $V(P(w\cdot\lambda))$, so that $V(P(w\cdot\lambda))=\bar B_{w^{-1}}$ is its right reduction. Write $r_{x,d}(B)$ for the graded multiplicity of the polynomial standard graph module supported at $x$ in the standard support filtration of a polynomial Soergel bimodule $B$, in the standard-generator normalization of the polynomial Soergel category. Then for all $y,w\in W$ $$(P(w\cdot\lambda):\Delta(y\cdot\lambda))=\sum_d r_{y^{-1},d}(B_{w^{-1}}).$$ These are ranks before reduction: the right side sums the graded standard support multiplicities of the polynomial lift, not multiplicities in any separated filtration of the finite-dimensional module $V(P(w\cdot\lambda))$.

items.title: Projective Verma multiplicities are Kazhdan–Lusztig values at one
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. In a regular integral type-$A$ block $\mathcal O_\lambda$, for all $y,w\in W$ $$(P(w\cdot\lambda):\Delta(y\cdot\lambda))=P_{y,w}(1),$$ the value at $q=1$ of the classical Kazhdan-Lusztig polynomial of the pair $y\le w$; the multiplicity is the total value at one, not an individual coefficient of $P_{y,w}$, and it vanishes unless $y\le w$ in the Bruhat order.

items.title: Simple Verma composition multiplicities are Kazhdan–Lusztig values
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. In a regular integral type-$A$ block $\mathcal O_\lambda$, for all $y,w\in W$ $$[M(y\cdot\lambda):L(w\cdot\lambda)]=(P(w\cdot\lambda):\Delta(y\cdot\lambda))=P_{y,w}(1),$$ with the pair ordered so that the multiplicity vanishes unless $y\le w$ in the Bruhat order; in particular the Kazhdan-Lusztig conjecture's multiplicity statement holds for every dominant regular integral weight, with the same combinatorial answer.

items.title: The Kazhdan–Lusztig character formula in regular integral category O
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. In a regular integral type-$A$ block $\mathcal O_\lambda$, for every $w\in W$ the class of $L(w\cdot\lambda)$ in the Grothendieck group, equivalently its formal character, is $$[L(w\cdot\lambda)]=\sum_{x\in W}q'_{w,x}(1)\,[M(x\cdot\lambda)],\qquad\text{i.e.}\qquad \mathrm{ch}\,L(w\cdot\lambda)=\sum_{x\in W}q'_{w,x}(1)\,\mathrm{ch}\,M(x\cdot\lambda),$$ where $q'_{x,w}$ are the inverse Kazhdan-Lusztig coefficients of [[def-inverse-kazhdan-lusztig-polynomials]] ($Q'=P^{-1}$, $q'_{x,w}\in v\mathbb Z[v]$ for $x<w$, $q'_{w,w}=1$) and the sum is supported on $x\ge w$. Equivalently, in the signed normalization $q_{x,w}=\mathrm{sgn}(x)\mathrm{sgn}(w)q'_{x,w}$ the formula is the signed inverse-Kazhdan-Lusztig sum $$\mathrm{ch}\,L(w\cdot\lambda)=\sum_{x\ge w}(-1)^{\ell(w)-\ell(x)}q_{w,x}(1)\,\mathrm{ch}\,M(x\cdot\lambda).$$ The coefficients $q'_{w,x}(1)$ are the weighted incidence-algebra inverse of $(P_{y,z}(1))$, given by the finite signed chain sum of products of $P_{y,z}(1)$; they are integers that may be negative. They specialize to ordinary Bruhat Mobius values on intervals where every comparable-pair KL value is $1$, but not in general. Only the value at $q=1$ occurs.

items.title: Translation identifies the regular integral blocks
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\lambda,\mu$ be dominant regular integral weights for the same complex type-$A$ semisimple Lie algebra and fixed positive system. Let $\nu$ be the unique dominant member of $W(\mu-\lambda)$ and $E=L(\nu)$ the finite-dimensional simple. The actual translation functors $$F=T_\lambda^\mu=\operatorname{pr}_{\chi_\mu}(E\otimes-)\operatorname{incl}_{\chi_\lambda},\qquad G=T_\mu^\lambda=\operatorname{pr}_{\chi_\lambda}(E^*\otimes-)\operatorname{incl}_{\chi_\mu}$$ are exact mutually inverse equivalences, with natural adjunction isomorphisms $\operatorname{Id}\cong GF$ and $FG\cong\operatorname{Id}$. They preserve the dot-orbit labels: for every $w\in W$, $$F\Delta(w\cdot\lambda)\cong\Delta(w\cdot\mu),\quad FL(w\cdot\lambda)\cong L(w\cdot\mu),\quad FP(w\cdot\lambda)\cong P(w\cdot\mu),$$ and conversely for $G$. Consequently the two blocks have identical Verma-flag and composition multiplicities, both equal to $P_{y,w}(1)$, and $F$ transports the inverse-KL character identity as a Grothendieck-group identity with the same signed weighted-inverse coefficients $q'_{w,x}(1)$ and the same support $x\ge w$. Formal characters in the two blocks use their respective weights $x\cdot\lambda$ and $x\cdot\mu$; they need not be equal as weight series. The dominant/antidominant, Bruhat, left/right and inverse-Soergel-label conventions are preserved. This is an ungraded categorical transport and supplies no Ext or Koszul grading.

items.title: The full Ext version requires the Koszul grading of category O
items.statement: Scope warning. The grading used on this page is the auxiliary grading of the polynomial Soergel lifts: it is what makes the character theorem read off graded standard-support ranks, and it is forgotten by the Soergel functor, which is an ungraded equivalence on projectives. Consequently the results proved here are the ordinary (ungraded) Verma-flag, composition and character statements, together with the exact shift-to-$q=1$ conversion; they do NOT construct a grading on category $\mathcal O$, and in particular they assert nothing about graded multiplicities, about the $\mathrm{Ext}$-algebra of $\mathcal O$, or about Koszul duality. Individual coefficients of the Kazhdan-Lusztig polynomials are not category-$\mathcal O$ multiplicities: only their value at $q=1$ is. The graded version (a Koszul grading, graded BGG reciprocity and the $\mathrm{Ext}$ form of the multiplicity theorem, in the sense of the Beilinson-Ginzburg-Soergel programme) remains reserved for the separate Koszul-duality frontier of this library and is deliberately not smuggled into this page.

decline_pages.title: Singular and Parabolic Kazhdan–Lusztig Theory

items.title: The parabolic Hecke module and the antispherical standard basis
items.statement: Work with the normalized type-$A$ Hecke algebra $H_v(n)$ over $A=\mathbb Z[v^{\pm1}]$ of [[def-normalized-type-a-hecke-algebra-and-its-bar-involution]]: generators $H_s$ with $H_s^2=1+(v^{-1}-v)H_s$, standard basis $\{H_w:w\in S_n\}$, bar involution $\overline{H_s}=H_s^{-1}=H_s-(v^{-1}-v)$ and Kazhdan-Lusztig basis $\{\underline H_w\}$ of [[thm-existence-and-uniqueness-of-the-kazhdan-lusztig-basis]] (so that $\underline H_s=H_s+v$). Fix $J\subseteq S=\{s_1,\dots,s_{n-1}\}$, let $W_J=\langle s:s\in J\rangle\subseteq S_n$ be the standard parabolic subgroup and let $\Phi_J=\Phi\cap\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb R}\{\alpha_s:s\in J\}$ be its standard type-A root subsystem, all in the conventions of [[def-cg-parabolic-quotient-and-two-sided-minima]]. Two characters of the parabolic Hecke algebra $H_J\subseteq H_v(n)$ are used. For $s\in J$ the quadratic relation makes $v^{-1}$ and $-v$ the two roots of $x^2-(v^{-1}-v)x-1=0$, so there are well-defined algebra homomorphisms $\varphi_{+},\varphi_{-}:H_J\to A$ with $\varphi_+(H_s)=v^{-1}$ and $\varphi_-(H_s)=-v$ for all $s\in J$ (they respect the braid relations because they are scalar on the generators). Viewing $A$ through $\varphi_+$ (resp. $\varphi_-$) as a right $H_J$-module gives the **spherical parabolic module** $M^J:=A\otimes_{H_J}H_v(n)$ and the **antispherical parabolic module** $N^J:=A\otimes_{H_J}H_v(n)$, right $H_v(n)$-modules under right multiplication on the second factor. Throughout, $\Phi^+$ is the positive system of $\Phi$ and $\Phi_J^+=\Phi_J\cap\Phi^+$, and $$^JW:=\{w\in S_n:\ell(sw)>\ell(w)\ \text{for all }s\in J\},\qquad W^J:=\{w\in S_n:\ell(ws)>\ell(w)\ \text{for all }s\in J\}$$ are the minimal left and right coset representatives; by [[thm-hh-parabolic-minimal-representatives-and-length-additivity]] and [[thm-cg-parabolic-intersections-and-coset-factorization]] every $w\in S_n$ factors uniquely as $w=l y$ with $l\in W_J$, $y\in{^JW}$ and $\ell(w)=\ell(l)+\ell(y)$, and inversion interchanges ${^JW}$ and $W^J$. The definitions of $\varphi_\pm$ use only the quadratic relation on generators; no further module-theoretic input enters.

items.title: The singular integral block and its dot stabilizer
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice, inherited from the published block theory. Work in category $\mathcal O$ of a finite-dimensional complex semisimple Lie algebra $\mathfrak g$ with Cartan $\mathfrak h$, positive system $\Phi^+$, simple roots $\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_r$, Weyl group $W$, Weyl vector $\rho$ and dot action $w\cdot\lambda=w(\lambda+\rho)-\rho$, as in [[def-bgg-category-o]] and [[def-dot-action-facets-and-single-wall-translation-data]]. A weight $\mu$ is **dot-antidominant** if $\langle\mu+\rho,\alpha^\vee\rangle\le0$ for every $\alpha\in\Phi^+$ and **integral** if $\langle\mu,\alpha_i^\vee\rangle\in\mathbb Z$ for all $i$ ([[def-integral-weyl-group-of-a-weight]], [[def-integral-dominant-and-strictly-dominant-weights]]). Fix such a weight $\mu$ and put $J=J(\mu):=\{i:\langle\mu+\rho,\alpha_i^\vee\rangle=0\}$ and $W_\mu:=W_J=\langle s_i:i\in J\rangle$; then the dot stabilizer $\{v\in W:v\cdot\mu=\mu\}$ equals $W_J$ (the inclusion $W_J\subseteq$ stabilizer holds because each $s_i$, $i\in J$, fixes $\mu+\rho$; equality follows since the stabilizer of an integral antidominant weight is generated by the reflections it contains and is a standard parabolic, [[lem-finite-weyl-closed-chambers-and-stabilizers]]). The **singular integral block** $\mathcal O_\mu$ is the block of [[thm-central-character-summands-split-into-linkage-blocks]] of the central character of $\mu$; its simple objects $L(w\cdot\mu)$, standard objects $\Delta(w\cdot\mu)=M(w\cdot\mu)$, costandard objects $\nabla(w\cdot\mu)$ and projective covers $P(w\cdot\mu)$ are indexed by $w\in W$ ([[def-standard-and-costandard-objects-in-category-o]], [[def-verma-module]]), and $w'\cdot\mu=w\cdot\mu$ if and only if $w'\in wW_J$. Hence the labels can be normalized by the minimal right coset representatives $w\in W^J=\{w:\ell(ws)>\ell(w)\ \forall s\in J\}$, and inversion carries $W^J$ onto ${^JW}$ of [[def-parabolic-hecke-module-and-antispherical-standard-basis]]. The block is a highest-weight category with the standard and simple classes as bases of its Grothendieck group ([[def-grothendieck-group-and-character-of-category-o]]), it satisfies BGG reciprocity $(P(w\cdot\mu):\Delta(y\cdot\mu))=[M(y\cdot\mu):L(w\cdot\mu)]$, and the multiplicity matrix is unitriangular for the refinement of the dominance order on the dot orbit ([[thm-bgg-reciprocity]], [[def-verma-flag-and-its-multiplicities]]). The block is **regular** when $J=\varnothing$ (no wall) and **singular** when $J\neq\varnothing$; the singular translation statements use this notation, and $J=\varnothing$ recovers the regular case. The genuine regular-parabolic multiplicity statements below have their separate explicit dominant regular base.

items.title: Standard parabolic and Levi subalgebras from a subset of simple roots
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice inherited from the published root-space/sl2 suppliers. Let g be finite-dimensional complex semisimple with Cartan h, roots Phi, positives Phi^+, simple roots alpha_i, and J a subset of the simple indices. Put Phi_J=Phi intersect span_R{alpha_j:j in J}, H_j=the coroot of alpha_j, h_J=span_C{H_j:j in J} and z_J={h:alpha_j(h)=0 for all j in J}. Define s_J=h_J plus the root spaces of Phi_J, l_J=h plus those root spaces, u_J=the sum of positive root spaces outside Phi_J, and p_J=l_J plus u_J. Then h=h_J direct-sum z_J, s_J is semisimple with roots Phi_J, and l_J=s_J direct-sum z_J is reductive with center z_J, Cartan h and Weyl group W_J. The sums l_J,u_J,p_J are Lie subalgebras, u_J is the nilradical of p_J, and p_J=l_J semidirect u_J is its reductive parabolic Levi decomposition. In the published radical-based sense of def-levi-subalgebra-and-levi-decomposition, rad(p_J)=z_J plus u_J and s_J is the SEMISIMPLE Levi factor complementing that radical; l_J need not be semisimple. The parabolic contains b and equals b plus the negative Phi_J root spaces. For J empty it is b; for J all it is g. There exists zeta in z_J with alpha_i(zeta)=1 outside J, giving u_J strictly positive integral degrees and v_J (the outside negative radical) strictly negative degrees, with l_J degree0. Both radicals have finite-dimensional fixed-degree PBW slices. The construction depends only on the positive system and J.

items.title: Standard bases, right actions and bar involutions on the parabolic Hecke modules
items.statement:
Retain the notation of [[def-parabolic-hecke-module-and-antispherical-standard-basis]] and put $m_x:=1\otimes H_x$, $n_x:=1\otimes H_x$ for $x\in{^JW}$, and $C_s:=\underline H_s=H_s+v$ for $s\in S$. (1) (Bases.) The sets $\{m_x:x\in{^JW}\}$ and $\{n_x:x\in{^JW}\}$ are $A$-bases of $M^J$ and $N^J$ respectively: indeed every $w\in S_n$ factors uniquely as $w=ly$ with $l\in W_J$, $y\in{^JW}$, length-additively, and $\varphi_\pm(H_l)=\varphi_\pm(H_s)^{\ell(l)}\in\{v^{-\ell(l)},\pm v^{\ell(l)}\}$ is a unit of $A$, so $1\otimes H_w=\varphi_\pm(H_l)\,(1\otimes H_y)$ in both modules. (2) (Right action.) For $s\in S$ and $x\in{^JW}$: $$m_x C_s= egin{cases}m_{xs}+v\,m_x,&xs\in{^JW},\ xs>x,\ m_{xs}+v^{-1}m_x,&xs\in{^JW},\ xs<x,\ (v+v^{-1})m_x,&xs
otin{^JW},\end{cases}\qquad n_xC_s= egin{cases}n_{xs}+v\,n_x,&xs\in{^JW},\ xs>x,\ n_{xs}+v^{-1}n_x,&xs\in{^JW},\ xs<x,\ 0,&xs
otin{^JW}.\end{cases}$$ (3) (Bar.) The assignment $a\otimes h\mapsto  ar a\otimes ar h$ (bar on $A$ and the bar involution of $H_v(n)$) descends to $A$-antilinear involutions of $M^J$ and $N^J$ that satisfy $\overline{X\cdot h}=\overline X\cdot ar h$ and $\overline{m_x}=m_x+\sum_{y<x}a_{y,x}m_y$, $\overline{n_x}=n_x+\sum_{y<x}b_{y,x}n_y$ with $a_{y,x},b_{y,x}\in A$ and $a_{x,x}=b_{x,x}=1$; the top coefficient is one. (4) (Parabolic property.) If $x\in{^JW}$ and $s\in S$ with $xs
otin{^JW}$ then $xs=rx$ for a unique simple $r\in J$ and $xs>x$.

items.title: The facet tensor-weight exclusion lemma
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\lambda$ be an integral dot-antidominant dot-regular weight and let $\mu$ be an integral dot-antidominant weight such that the facet $F_\mu$ lies in the closure of the chamber $F_\lambda$, i.e. $\langle\mu+\rho,\alpha^\vee\rangle=0$ for the positive roots $\alpha\in\Phi_J^+$ of the parabolic subsystem $\Phi_J$ of $J=J(\mu)$ defined in [[def-singular-integral-category-o-block-and-stabilizer]], and $\langle\mu+\rho,\alpha^\vee\rangle$ has the same sign as $\langle\lambda+\rho,\alpha^\vee\rangle$ for every remaining positive root. Let $\nu$ be the unique dominant weight of the linear orbit $W(\mu-\lambda)$ ([[lem-finite-weyl-closed-chambers-and-stabilizers]]) and let $E=L(\nu)$ ([[thm-finite-dimensional-simple-modules-are-classified-by-dominant-highest-weights]]). Then for all $w,w'\in W$ and every weight $\gamma$ of $E$: if $w'\cdot\mu=w\cdot\lambda+\gamma$, then $w'\cdot\mu=w\cdot\mu$ and $\gamma=w(\mu-\lambda)$. Consequently, for every $w$ the tensor $E\otimes\Delta(w\cdot\lambda)$ has exactly one Verma factor whose central character is that of $\mu$, namely $\Delta(w\cdot\mu)$, and its multiplicity in the Verma flag computed by [[lem-tensoring-with-a-finite-dimensional-module-preserves-verma-flags]] is one.

items.title: Parabolic category O for a standard parabolic
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice, inherited from the published category-O theory. Let $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak p_J=\mathfrak l_J\oplus\mathfrak u_J$ be the standard parabolic of [[def-standard-parabolic-and-levi-subalgebras-from-simple-roots]], with reductive parabolic Levi $\mathfrak l_J$ and nilradical $\mathfrak u_J$, and $W_J$ its Weyl group. A weight $\lambda$ is **$\mathfrak p$-dominant** if $\langle\lambda,\alpha^\vee\rangle\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}$ for all $\alpha\in\Phi_J^+$ (this is dominance for the Levi root system; in particular $\lambda$ is integral for $\Phi_J$). For such a $\lambda$ let $E(\lambda)$ be the finite-dimensional simple $\mathfrak p$-module obtained from the finite-dimensional simple $\mathfrak l_J$-module of highest weight $\lambda$ ([[thm-finite-dimensional-simple-modules-are-classified-by-dominant-highest-weights]]) by letting $\mathfrak u_J$ act by zero, and define the **generalized Verma module** $$M_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda):=U(\mathfrak g)\otimes_{U(\mathfrak p)}E(\lambda).$$ The **parabolic category** $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$ is the full subcategory of $\mathcal O$ whose objects are the finitely generated $\mathfrak h$-semisimple $\mathfrak g$-modules on which $U(\mathfrak p)$ acts locally finitely; its objects are exactly the modules $M\in\mathcal O$ such that every vector lies in a finite-dimensional $\mathfrak p$-submodule. For each $\mathfrak p$-dominant integral $\lambda$ the module $M_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda)$ lies in $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$, has highest weight $\lambda$, and $M(\lambda)\twoheadrightarrow M_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda)$ is the largest quotient of the Verma module $M(\lambda)$ that lies in $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$. The simple objects of $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$ are the simple highest-weight modules $L(\lambda)$ with $\lambda$ $\mathfrak p$-dominant integral, and $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$ is closed under subobjects, quotients and extensions in $\mathcal O$. The costandard objects are $\nabla_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda)=D M_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda)$, naturally submodules of the ordinary dual Vermas. They need not be quotients of ordinary dual Vermas.

items.title: Existence and uniqueness of the parabolic Kazhdan–Lusztig bases
items.statement: Retain the notation of [[def-parabolic-hecke-module-and-antispherical-standard-basis]] and [[lem-the-parabolic-hecke-modules-have-standard-bases-actions-and-compatible-bars]]. For every $x\in{^JW}$ there is a unique $C_x\in M^J$ and a unique $D_x\in N^J$ with (i) $\overline{C_x}=C_x$ and $\overline{D_x}=D_x$, and (ii) $C_x\in m_x+\sum_{y<x}v\mathbb Z[v]\,m_y$, $D_x\in n_x+\sum_{y<x}v\mathbb Z[v]\,n_y$, the sums over the lower Bruhat ideal of $x$ inside ${^JW}$. The sets $\{C_x\}_{x\in{^JW}}$ and $\{D_x\}_{x\in{^JW}}$ are $A$-bases of $M^J$ and $N^J$. No coefficientwise positivity is asserted.

items.title: Translation to the wall on Verma, simple and projective objects
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $(\lambda,\mu)$ be as in [[lem-facet-tensor-weight-exclusion]]: $\lambda$ integral dot-antidominant and dot-regular, $\mu$ integral dot-antidominant with $F_\mu$ in the closure of the chamber $F_\lambda$, $J=J(\mu)$, $W_\mu=W_J$. Let $
u$ be the unique dominant weight of $W(\mu-\lambda)$ and let $$T:=T_\lambda^\mu=\operatorname{pr}_{\chi_\mu}\circ(L(
u)\otimes-)\circ\operatorname{incl}_{\chi_\lambda}\colon\mathcal O_\lambda\longrightarrow\mathcal O_\mu,\qquad T':=T_\mu^\lambda,$$ be the translation functors of [[def-translation-functor-between-o-blocks]], which are exact and biadjoint ([[prop-translation-functors-are-exact-and-biadjoint-across-a-wall]]). Then: (1) $T\Delta(w\cdot\lambda)\cong\Delta(w\cdot\mu)$ and $T
abla(w\cdot\lambda)\cong
abla(w\cdot\mu)$ for every $w\in W$. (2) $TL(w\cdot\lambda)\cong L(w\cdot\mu)$ if $w\in W^J$, and $TL(w\cdot\lambda)=0$ otherwise; equivalently $TL(w\cdot\lambda)
eq0$ if and only if the facet $F_{w\cdot\mu}$ is contained in the upper closure $F^+_{w\cdot\lambda}$ of [[def-dot-action-facets-and-single-wall-translation-data]]. (3) (Big projective on the wall.) Let $\Xi_\mu:=T_{-ho}^{\mu}L(-ho)$ be the translate of the simple object of the most singular block. Then $\Xi_\mu$ is projective and injective in $\mathcal O_\mu$, it is the projective cover $P(1\cdot\mu)$ of $L(\mu)$, and $(\Xi_\mu:\Delta(w\cdot\mu))=1$ for every distinct orbit label (equivalently for its representatives $w\in W^J$); consequently $(P(\mu):\Delta(y\cdot\mu))=1$ for every distinct label $y\in W^J$ and $[\Delta(w\cdot\mu):L(\mu)]=1$ for all $w\in W$.

items.title: Parabolic category O is a highest weight category
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let
$\mathfrak p=\mathfrak l_J\oplus\mathfrak u_J$ and $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$
be as in [[def-parabolic-category-o-for-a-standard-parabolic]]. Then:

**(1) (Simples.)** Within an integral block, $L(\lambda)\in\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$
if and only if $\lambda$ is $\mathfrak p$-dominant integral; every simple
object of $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$ is of this form.

**(2) (Standards.)** For $\mathfrak p$-dominant integral $\lambda$ the
generalized Verma $M_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda)$ lies in $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$,
has finite length, has $L(\lambda)$ as its unique simple quotient (head), and
$[M_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda):L(\mu)]\neq0$ forces $\mu\le\lambda$ in the
dominance order; $M_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda)$ is the largest quotient of
$M(\lambda)$ lying in $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$.

**(3) (Enough projectives.)** The inclusion
$\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}\subseteq\mathcal O$ is exact and has a left adjoint
$L_{\mathfrak p}$ (the largest $\mathfrak p$-locally-finite quotient);
$L_{\mathfrak p}$ is right exact and sends projective objects of $\mathcal O$
to projective objects of $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$. Consequently, for every
$\mathfrak p$-dominant integral $\lambda$ the object
$P^{\mathfrak p}(\lambda):=L_{\mathfrak p}(P^{(\mathcal O)}(\lambda))$ is a
projective cover of $L(\lambda)$ in $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$, and
$\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$ has enough projectives and injectives.

**(4) (Generalized-standard flags, BGG reciprocity and duality.)** Every
projective in a fixed integral block has a finite generalized Verma flag. Its
projective cover surjects to its labelled generalized standard with a kernel
filtered by higher-labelled generalized standards. The simple and
generalized-standard classes form bases of the finite block Grothendieck
group, and characters are injective on this group. For $\mathfrak p$-dominant
integral $\lambda,\mu$,
$$(P^{\mathfrak p}(\lambda):M_{\mathfrak p}(\mu))=[M_{\mathfrak p}(\mu):L(\lambda)],$$
the multiplicities being finite; moreover restricted duality restricts to an
exact contravariant involution of $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$ exchanging
$M_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda)$ and $\nabla_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda)$, and
$\operatorname{Ext}^1_{\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}}(M_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda),\nabla_{\mathfrak p}(\mu))=0$
for all $\lambda,\mu$.

items.title: The parabolic Kazhdan–Lusztig bases and polynomials
items.statement: Retain the notation of the preceding items and write the parabolic Kazhdan-Lusztig bases of [[thm-existence-and-uniqueness-of-the-parabolic-kazhdan-lusztig-basis]] as $$C_x=\sum_{y\le x,\ y\in{^JW}}m_{y,x}\,m_y,\qquad D_x=\sum_{y\le x,\ y\in{^JW}}n_{y,x}\,n_y,\qquad x\in{^JW},$$ with coefficients $m_{y,x},n_{y,x}\in\mathbb Z[v]$ supported on the lower Bruhat ideal, $m_{x,x}=n_{x,x}=1$ and $m_{y,x},n_{y,x}\in v\mathbb Z[v]$ for $y<x$. The **spherical parabolic Kazhdan-Lusztig polynomials** are $M^J_{y,x}(q):=v^{-\ell(x)+\ell(y)}m_{y,x}$ with $q=v^{-2}$, and the **antispherical (sign) parabolic Kazhdan-Lusztig polynomials** are $N^J_{y,x}(q):=v^{-\ell(x)+\ell(y)}n_{y,x}$; the parity and degree bounds established in [[thm-parabolic-kazhdan-lusztig-polynomials-are-alternating-sums-of-ordinary-ones]] make these polynomials in $q$. Normalization dictionary (the exact Deodhar normalization): with $P^J_{y,x}(u)$ the parabolic polynomials of Deodhar (1987) attached to the subset $J$, one has $M^J_{y,x}=P^J_{y^{-1},x^{-1}}$ for $u=-1$ and $N^J_{y,x}=P^J_{y^{-1},x^{-1}}$ for $u=q$, in the index convention of Deodhar and of the anti-spherical category. Values at $v=1$ are written $m_{y,x}(1)$, $n_{y,x}(1)$. The spherical coefficients reduce to ordinary ones: if $W_J$ is finite with longest element $w_0^J$ then $m_{y,x}=p_{w_0^J y,\,w_0^J x}$ for all $y,x\in{^JW}$, where $p$ is the coefficient of the ordinary Kazhdan-Lusztig basis of [[def-kazhdan-lusztig-polynomials-in-the-classical-q-normalization]].

items.title: Parabolic Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomials are alternating sums of ordinary ones
items.statement: Retain the notation of [[def-parabolic-kazhdan-lusztig-basis-and-polynomials]]. (1) (Antispherical alternating sum.) For all $x,y\in{^JW}$, $$n_{y,x}=\sum_{z\in W_J}(-1)^{\ell(z)}\,v^{\ell(z)}\,p_{zy,\,x},$$ the sum over all $z\in W_J$ (the product $zy$ taken in $S_n$, and $p_{\cdot,x}$ the ordinary coefficient of the Kazhdan-Lusztig basis of [[thm-existence-and-uniqueness-of-the-kazhdan-lusztig-basis]], so the inner coefficients vanish unless $zy\le x$). (2) (Spherical reduction.) If $W_J$ is finite with longest element $w_0^J$ then for all $x,y\in{^JW}$ $$m_{y,x}=p_{w_0^J y,\ w_0^J x}.$$ In particular both families are computable from the ordinary Kazhdan-Lusztig coefficients of $S_n$, with no separate recursion.

items.title: Singular category O multiplicities are parabolic Kazhdan–Lusztig values
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) and work in the type-$A$
root datum $W=S_n$ of the page's Hecke module and ordinary multiplicity
theorem. Let $(\lambda,\mu)$ be as in [[lem-facet-tensor-weight-exclusion]]
with $J=J(\mu)$, so $\mathcal O_\mu$ is the singular integral block of
[[def-singular-integral-category-o-block-and-stabilizer]] with labels
normalized by the minimal right coset representatives $W^J$, and let $w_0$ be
the longest element of $W$. Then for all $y,w\in W^J$,
$$[M(y\cdot\mu):L(w\cdot\mu)]=(P(w\cdot\mu):\Delta(y\cdot\mu))=P_{yw_0,\,ww_0}(1),$$
the value at $q=1$ of the ordinary Kazhdan--Lusztig polynomial attached to the
pair $(yw_0,ww_0)$ in the classical normalization of
[[def-kazhdan-lusztig-polynomials-in-the-classical-q-normalization]].
Equivalently, put $k(w)=w_0^Jw^{-1}w_0\in{}^JW$. Then
$$[M(y\cdot\mu):L(w\cdot\mu)]=m_{k(y),k(w)}(1).$$
This is the spherical family. The antispherical family instead governs the
genuine regular parabolic locally finite category with dominant labels;
changing to an opposite positive system does not identify the two families.
In particular all singular multiplicities are computable from the ordinary
Kazhdan--Lusztig coefficients of $S_n$, and no individual polynomial
coefficients beyond the value at one occur.

items.title: Parabolic category O multiplicities are parabolic Kazhdan–Lusztig values
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Fix a dominant regular
integral weight $\lambda$ of the complex type-$A$ Lie algebra and the standard
parabolic $\mathfrak p_J$, with reductive Levi $\mathfrak l_J$ and longest
Levi Weyl element $w_J$
([[def-standard-parabolic-and-levi-subalgebras-from-simple-roots]]). The
$\mathfrak p_J$-dominant weights in this regular block are exactly
$y\cdot\lambda$ for $y\in{}^JW$. Write
$\Delta^J(y\cdot\lambda)=M_{\mathfrak p}(y\cdot\lambda)$,
$L(x\cdot\lambda)$ and $P^J(x\cdot\lambda)$ for its generalized standards,
simples and projective covers
([[def-parabolic-category-o-for-a-standard-parabolic]]). Then for
$x,y\in{}^JW$,
$$[\Delta^J(y\cdot\lambda):L(x\cdot\lambda)]=(P^J(x\cdot\lambda):\Delta^J(y\cdot\lambda))=\sum_{u\in W_J}(-1)^{\ell(u)}P_{uy,x}(1)=n_{y,x}(1).$$

These are the antispherical sign coefficients, with support $y\le x$ and
diagonal $1$. The precise character/Grothendieck identity supplying the
formula is
$$\operatorname{ch}\Delta^J(y\cdot\lambda)=\sum_{u\in W_J}(-1)^{\ell(u)}\operatorname{ch}\Delta(uy\cdot\lambda).$$

For the same highest weights in the antidominant base
$\lambda_{\mathrm{anti}}=w_0\cdot\lambda$, the actual longest-left label is
$z=yw_0$, since $y\cdot\lambda=z\cdot\lambda_{\mathrm{anti}}$.
Its shortest-left encoding is $a=\mathrm{lf}(y):=w_Jyw_0\in{}^JW$, so the
weight in that encoding is $(w_Ja)\cdot\lambda_{\mathrm{anti}}$, not
$a\cdot\lambda_{\mathrm{anti}}$. With $b=\mathrm{lf}(x)$, the reindexed matrix is
$$\widetilde N_{a,b}:=n_{\mathrm{lf}^{-1}(a),\mathrm{lf}^{-1}(b)}(1)=n_{w_Jaw_0,\,w_Jbw_0}(1).$$
It is the same multiplicity matrix with both indices permuted and has reversed
support in the transported order. It is not in general $n_{a,b}(1)$.
Every label retains its explicit dot-baseweight.
The highest-weight category theorem applies also to singular integral
parabolic blocks, but this ordinary regular KL matrix formula assumes the
ambient central character is regular. No singular/parabolic category
equivalence, grading or Koszul duality is asserted.

items.title: The parabolic Kazhdan–Lusztig character formula
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) and the dominant regular
integral conventions of
[[thm-parabolic-category-o-multiplicities-are-parabolic-kl-polynomials]]. Put
$N=(n_{y,x}(1))_{y,x\in{}^JW}$, with rows indexed by generalized standards and
columns by simples in a Bruhat-compatible order
([[def-parabolic-kazhdan-lusztig-basis-and-polynomials]]). Then $N$ is upper
unitriangular and, for each $x$,
$$\operatorname{ch}L(x\cdot\lambda)=\sum_{y\ge x}(N^{-1})_{x,y}\,\operatorname{ch}\Delta^J(y\cdot\lambda).$$
Its inverse entries are integers computed by the finite signed chain sum of
products of $n_{a,b}(1)$; they are weighted incidence inverses, not generally
ordinary Bruhat Mobius values. In the antidominant base $\lambda_{\mathrm{anti}}=w_0\cdot\lambda$, set
$a=\mathrm{lf}(y)=w_Jyw_0$ and encode the same weight as
$(w_Ja)\cdot\lambda_{\mathrm{anti}}$. The reindexed matrix is
$\widetilde N_{a,b}=N_{\mathrm{lf}^{-1}(a),\mathrm{lf}^{-1}(b)}$
and its inverse is reindexed by the same permutation; thus the same formula
has reversed support in the transported order. This does not replace the
entries by $n_{a,b}(1)$.
This is the ungraded
character formula for the regular parabolic block, and constructs no Koszul or
Ext grading.

decision.reason: The corrected restricted semi-regular constructions and ordinary column reading preserve the full independently proved finite tableau and Ringel scope

decline_pages.title: Parabolic Category O and Fock-Space Bases

items.title: Standard- and costandard-filtered objects and tilting objects
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) inherited from the category-$\mathcal O$ suppliers. Fix a finite genuine integral parabolic central summand $\mathcal C$ over $\mathbb C$, with its finite highest-weight structure from [[thm-parabolic-category-o-is-a-highest-weight-category]]. Connectedness is not required. Write $(\Lambda,\preceq)$ for its label poset, $L_\lambda$ for its simples, $\Delta_\lambda$ for its generalized standards, and $\nabla_\lambda=D\Delta_\lambda$ for its costandards. The duality $D$ is exact, contravariant and simple-preserving.

The projective cover $P_\lambda$ and injective envelope $I_\lambda=DP_\lambda$ have exact sequences
$$0\longrightarrow K_\lambda\longrightarrow P_\lambda\longrightarrow\Delta_\lambda\longrightarrow0,\qquad0\longrightarrow\nabla_\lambda\longrightarrow I_\lambda\longrightarrow C_\lambda\longrightarrow0,$$
where $K_\lambda$ has a finite standard flag with labels strictly greater than $\lambda$, and $C_\lambda=DK_\lambda$ has a finite costandard flag with such labels. Generally $I_\lambda$ is larger than $\nabla_\lambda$. Standards have simple heads, costandards simple socles, and their composition labels are $\preceq\lambda$. In this split setting,
$$\operatorname{Hom}(\Delta_\lambda,\nabla_\mu)=\delta_{\lambda\mu}\mathbb C,\qquad\operatorname{Ext}^j(\Delta_\lambda,\nabla_\mu)=0\quad(j>0),$$
and BGG reciprocity is $(P_\lambda:\Delta_\mu)=[\nabla_\mu:L_\lambda]=[\Delta_\mu:L_\lambda]$. Higher Ext vanishing is justified below from the standard-kernel sequences and the local Hom/$\operatorname{Ext}^1$ statement.

A **finite standard flag** of $N$ is a finite chain $0=N_0\subset N_1\subset\cdots\subset N_r=N$ with sections $\Delta_{\lambda_i}$; a **finite costandard flag** has sections $\nabla_{\lambda_i}$. The zero object has the empty flag. Write $\mathcal F(\Delta)$ and $\mathcal F(\nabla)$ for the corresponding full subcategories. They are exact categories with the short exact sequences inherited from $\mathcal C$, closed under finite sums, extensions and direct summands. Their flag multiplicities are independent of the chosen flag and satisfy
$$(N:\Delta_\lambda)=\dim\operatorname{Hom}(N,\nabla_\lambda),\qquad(M:\nabla_\lambda)=\dim\operatorname{Hom}(\Delta_\lambda,M).$$
For arbitrary objects of the fixed finite summand, the equivalent homological criteria are
$$\mathcal F(\Delta)=\{N:\operatorname{Ext}^1(N,\nabla_\lambda)=0\text{ for all }\lambda\}=\{N:\operatorname{Ext}^j(N,\nabla_\lambda)=0\text{ for all }\lambda,j>0\},$$
$$\mathcal F(\nabla)=\{M:\operatorname{Ext}^1(\Delta_\lambda,M)=0\text{ for all }\lambda\}=\{M:\operatorname{Ext}^j(\Delta_\lambda,M)=0\text{ for all }\lambda,j>0\}.$$
The duality exchanges the two flag categories. A **tilting object** belongs to their intersection.

An indecomposable tilting object is **normalized at** $\lambda$, and written $T_\lambda$, if it has an inclusion $\Delta_\lambda\hookrightarrow T_\lambda$ whose cokernel is standard-filtered by labels strictly smaller than $\lambda$. Its bottom standard occurs once and $\lambda$ is its unique maximal composition-support label. Such an object, when it exists, is unique up to isomorphism. Existence and classification are supplied later; they are not used to prove the criteria. For a lower ideal $\Gamma$ containing $\lambda$, this same object is normalized tilting in the corresponding Serre subcategory; it is unchanged by the truncation.

items.title: The Fock-space convention dictionary for finite type-A quantum modules
items.statement:
Throughout this pair the **source parameter** of the Fock-space literature is
written $s$ and the **library parameter** of the Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra
[[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]] is written $t$; the
dictionary below sets $t=s^{-1}$.

Let $I$ be a nonempty consecutive set of simple-root indices and put $I^+=I\cup(I+1)$, the coordinate alphabet. On a finite coordinate interval $J=[k,r]\subseteq I^+$ the roots have indices $[k,r-1]$, the coordinate weight lattice is $\bigoplus_{a=k}^r\mathbb Z\delta_a$, $\alpha_a=\delta_a-\delta_{a+1}$ and $h_a=e_a-e_{a+1}$. The full central coordinate is retained. The source algebra $U_s$ has toral generators $D_a^{\pm1}$ for $a\in J$ and root generators $E_a,F_a$ for $k\le a<r$, acting on natural vectors $v_b$, $b\in J$, by

$$D_av_b=s^{\delta_{ab}}v_b,\qquad E_av_b=\delta_{a+1,b}\,v_a,\qquad F_av_b=\delta_{a,b}\,v_{a+1},$$

$$\Delta E_a=1\otimes E_a+E_a\otimes D_aD_{a+1}^{-1},\qquad \Delta F_a=F_a\otimes1+D_a^{-1}D_{a+1}\otimes F_a .$$

The library parameter $t$ is identified with $s^{-1}$; the **semilinear Hopf
dictionary** is the coefficient map $t\mapsto s^{-1}$ together with the
generator assignment

$$E_a\longmapsto E_a,\qquad F_a\longmapsto F_a,\qquad K_h\longmapsto D_{-h},$$

where the $E_a,F_a$ on the source side are the *divided* generators of the
source normalization and on the library side those of
[[def-lusztig-divided-power-integral-form]] (the assignments agree on the
undivided generators $E_a=E_a^{(1)}$, $F_a=F_a^{(1)}$, and divided powers are
carried to divided powers because the quantum integers are invariant under
$q\mapsto q^{-1}$, [[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]).
Root-label weights are preserved, while toral numerical eigenvalues use the
reciprocal parameter: on a weight vector of weight $\mu$ the library generator
$K_h$ acts by $t^{\mu(h)}=s^{-\mu(h)}$, which is the action of $D_{-h}$ because
$(-h)(\mu)=-\mu(h)$.

The **bar involution** sends $s\mapsto s^{-1}$, fixes $E_a$ and $F_a$ and
inverts each $D_a$; the corresponding library operation is the involution with
$t\mapsto t^{-1}$, $E_a\mapsto E_a$, $F_a\mapsto F_a$ and
$K_h\mapsto K_h^{-1}$ of [[def-the-bar-lattice-and-integral-lattice-of-a-based-module]]
and [[def-lusztig-divided-power-integral-form]].

The **natural highest weight** attached to an interval $[k,r]$ is
$\delta_k=\varepsilon_k$ (equivalently the highest weight reached by the
leading coordinate vector $v_k$), its **dual highest weight** is
$-\delta_r$, and the **fundamental wedge weight** is
$\delta_k+\delta_{k+1}+\cdots+\delta_m$ for $k\le m\le r$. Every fundamental
factor carries its own highest-vector-normalized bar, integral lattice and
divided-string crystal charts ([[def-kashiwara-lattices-lambda-and-infinity]]);
its internal antisymmetrizer embedding is primitive and integral but is *not*
asserted to be based in the library's raw lower $q_0$ chart. Infinite intervals
are defined by the compatible system of their finite subintervals, and
[[def-quantum-weight-module-and-integrability]] with
[[thm-integrable-quantum-highest-weight-module-exists-and-is-unique]] supplies
the library integrable modules used on each finite interval.

The source Fock families $L,T,P$ and the library form-dual upper family
([[def-contravariant-form-on-an-integrable-quantum-highest-weight-module]]) will
be compared below through their actual forms; they are never identified by
their names.

items.title: The higher-level wedge-tensor Fock module
items.statement:
Work with the type-$A$ coordinate lattice and the dictionary of
[[def-the-fock-convention-dictionary-for-finite-type-a-quantum-modules]];
weights are written in the coordinates $\delta_a=\varepsilon_a$.

Fix a set $I$ of consecutive residues (for the finite box model
$I=\{k_0,\dots,k_0+N-2\}$ and $I^+=I\cup(I+1)=\{k_0,\dots,k_0+N-1\}$; $I$ may be
unbounded below or above), a positive **level** $l$, and
$$\Lambda=\Lambda_{m_1}+\cdots+\Lambda_{m_l}\in P^+,\qquad m_1\ge m_2\ge\cdots\ge m_l,$$
where $m_j\in I^+$ and, if $I$ has lower endpoint $k$, $\Lambda_m=\sum_{k\le a\le m}\delta_a$. When $I$ is unbounded below, $\Lambda_m$ is the ground semi-infinite fundamental weight with the finite-coordinate-difference interpretation below. For $I$ bounded below put
$n_j=m_j+1-\inf(I)$ boxes in column $j$ and $n=\sum_j n_j$; for $I$ unbounded
below use semi-infinite columns with a common finite tail below, as explained
after the weight definition.

The **higher-level wedge-tensor Fock module** is
$$F(\Lambda):=V(\Lambda_{m_1})\otimes V(\Lambda_{m_2})\otimes\cdots\otimes V(\Lambda_{m_l}),$$
the tensor product of the fundamental modules of the dictionary item. When $I$
is bounded below, $V(\Lambda_{m_j})$ is the fundamental integrable highest
weight module of highest weight $\Lambda_{m_j}$ in the library algebra. When
$I$ is unbounded below, $V(\Lambda_{m_j})$ is the semi-infinite wedge
$\Lambda^{m_j+\infty}V$ with $V$ the natural module for the locally finite
type-$A$ algebra on $I$; its basis is the set of normally ordered wedges
$v_{i_1}\wedge v_{i_2}\wedge\cdots$ with $i_1>i_2>\cdots$ and the tail
$i_k=m_j+1-k$ for all sufficiently large $k$.

A **$\Lambda$-tableau** $A$ fills the diagram of $\Lambda$ — the columns
$1,\dots,l$ of heights $n_j$, with rows indexed by $I^+$ — with entries in
$I^+$; it is **column-strict** if in each column the entries strictly increase
from bottom to top and all but finitely many entries of row $i$ equal $i$, and
**standard** if in addition the entries weakly increase from left to right in
each row. Write $\mathrm{Col}^\Lambda$, respectively $\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$,
for the sets of column-strict, respectively standard $\Lambda$-tableaux, and
$A_\Lambda$ for the **ground-state tableau** with row $i$ filled entirely
with $i$.

For $A\in\mathrm{Col}^\Lambda$ the **column monomial** is
$$M_A:=\left(v_{A(m_1,1)}\wedge v_{A(m_1-1,1)}\wedge\cdots\right)\otimes\cdots\otimes\left(v_{A(m_l,l)}\wedge v_{A(m_l-1,l)}\wedge\cdots\right),$$
with each wedge normally ordered (the entries strictly decrease from top to
bottom inside a column), and
$$\mathrm{wt}_j(A)=\sum_{m_j\ge i\in I^+}\delta_{A(i,j)},\qquad \mathrm{wt}(A)=\mathrm{wt}_1(A)+\cdots+\mathrm{wt}_l(A),\qquad \mathrm{Col}^\Lambda_\alpha=\{A:\mathrm{wt}(A)=\Lambda-\alpha\}$$
for $\alpha\in Q^+$. When a column is semi-infinite, the displayed sum means
its ground fundamental weight $\Lambda_{m_j}$ plus the finite sum of the
coordinate differences $\delta_{A(i,j)}-\delta_i$ over the finitely many
positions where $A$ differs from the ground state, evaluated on each
finite-support coroot or torus input; no divergent infinite coordinate sum is
asserted.

The **Bruhat order** on $\mathrm{Col}^\Lambda$ is defined by $A\le B$ iff
$\mathrm{wt}(A)=\mathrm{wt}(B)$ and
$\mathrm{wt}_1(A)+\cdots+\mathrm{wt}_j(A)\ge\mathrm{wt}_1(B)+\cdots+\mathrm{wt}_j(B)$
in the dominance order of [[def-dominance-order-on-partitions]] for every
$j<l$; then $A<B$ whenever $B$ is obtained from $A$ by swapping entries $a<b$
in columns $i<j$. The column reading of a tableau (list the columns from left
to right, each column read top to bottom) gives the passage to partitions and
to the Young-diagram conventions of
[[def-partition-young-diagram-and-conjugate-partition]] and
[[def-young-tableau-standard-tableau-and-shape]]; the removable- and
addable-node notation of [[def-removable-and-addable-nodes-of-a-partition]]
is used for the box moves of a tableau.

The vector $v_\Lambda:=M_{A_\Lambda}$ is called the **vacuum vector**. Weight
bookkeeping, the uniqueness of the monomial of weight $\Lambda$ and the
bijectivity of the column reading are verified below; the column-monomial theorem records the full integral tensor-basis statement. The well-definedness verification here constructs each fundamental factor explicitly without treating a citation to integrability as a wedge-basis theorem.

items.title: Parabolic semi-regular duality and the reverse-column label map
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $\mathfrak g=\mathfrak{gl}_n$, with its upper Borel and Cartan, and let $\mathfrak p$ be the standard parabolic of the tableau column sizes $n_1,\ldots,n_l$. Let $\bar{\mathfrak p}=\bar{\mathfrak l}\oplus\bar{\mathfrak u}$ be the standard parabolic with these block sizes reversed. Set $\alpha_i(\zeta)=0$ on the simple Levi roots and $\alpha_i(\zeta)=1$ on the remaining simple roots, and grade by $\operatorname{ad}\zeta$. Thus
$$\mathfrak g_0=\bar{\mathfrak l},\qquad \mathfrak g_{>0}=\bar{\mathfrak u},\qquad \mathfrak g_{<0}=\bar{\mathfrak u}^{-}.$$
Degrees greater than one are retained. Put $U=U(\mathfrak g)$, $B=U(\bar{\mathfrak p})$, $N=U(\bar{\mathfrak u}^{-})$, and $\gamma=2\rho_{\mathfrak g}-2\rho_{\bar{\mathfrak l}}$, a character of $\bar{\mathfrak l}$ extended by zero to $\bar{\mathfrak u}$. For a graded vector space $V$, write $V^{\#}=\bigoplus_d(V_{-d})^*$ and
$$\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(V,W)=\bigoplus_d\operatorname{Hom}^d(V,W).$$
Here $\operatorname{Hom}^d$ consists of maps homogeneous of degree $d$; the direct sum allows only finitely many degrees. These conventions are essential.

(1) The algebraic space $S=N^{\#}\otimes B$ has commuting left and right $U$-actions and identifications
$$S\cong N^{\#}\otimes_N U\cong U\otimes_N N^{\#}.$$
Its left action is obtained from the restricted coinduction model
$$S\cong\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_B(U,\mathbb C_\gamma\otimes B).$$
No completion of $S$ is taken. With $P$ and $Q$ the projections of $\mathfrak g$ to $\mathfrak g_{\ge0}$ and $\mathfrak g_{<0}$, respectively, the polarization trace governing normal ordering is
$$\omega(X,Y)=\operatorname{tr}_{\mathfrak g_{\ge0}}(P\operatorname{ad}XQ\operatorname{ad}YP-P\operatorname{ad}YQ\operatorname{ad}XP)=\gamma_0([X,Y]),$$
where $\gamma_0$ is zero outside degree zero. In particular, for $X\in\mathfrak g_1$ and $Y\in\mathfrak g_{-1}$ this is $\gamma([X,Y])=\operatorname{tr}_{\mathfrak g_0}(\operatorname{ad}X\operatorname{ad}Y)$, not the full adjoint-composition trace.

(2) On graded $U$-modules free over $N$ of finite graded rank, $T=S\otimes_U-$ is an exact equivalence onto the graded $U$-modules cofree over $N$ of finite graded rank. Its inverse is $H=\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_U(S,-)$; finite graded rank means a finite sum of grading shifts of $N$, respectively $N^{\#}$. In this restricted sense
$$\underline{\operatorname{End}}_N(N^{\#})\cong N^{\mathrm{op}}.$$
This equality is not an assertion about unrestricted endomorphisms: for $N=\mathbb C[x]$ with $\deg x=-1$, the unrestricted ring is $\mathbb C[\![x]\!]$.

(3) With the principal contragredient action $(Xf)(v)=-f(Xv)$ on the restricted dual, $\Phi(M)=(S\otimes_U M)^{\#}$ is an exact contravariant equivalence of the finite generalized-standard flag category for $\bar{\mathfrak p}$ with its own opposite. On a finite-dimensional simple $\bar{\mathfrak l}$-module $E$,
$$\Phi(\Delta^{\bar{\mathfrak p}}(E))\cong\Delta^{\bar{\mathfrak p}}(\mathbb C_{-\gamma}\otimes E^*).$$
The parabolic in this formula is unchanged.

(4) Let $c(X)=-w_0X^{\mathsf T}w_0$, which carries the upper Borel to itself and reverses the Levi blocks, and set $\Psi=c^*\Phi$. For a lower-bounded tableau shape set $n_j=m_j+1-\inf(I)$ and use the concatenated ordinary highest-weight reading $a_i$, with each column read from top to bottom in strictly decreasing order, and $\lambda_{A,i}=a_i+i-1$. The source reading is the reversed sequence of columns, without reversing positions within a column. Then
$$\Psi:\mathcal F(\bar\Delta)\longrightarrow\mathcal F(\Delta)^{\mathrm{op}},\qquad\Psi(\bar\Delta(A))\cong\Delta(A).$$
This is an exact contravariant equivalence. It preserves the tableau label and the corresponding central-character summands, including the scalar central coordinate, and the reverse-column label order is opposite to the target order. More explicitly its weight map is
$$\lambda\longmapsto w_0w_{\bar J}\lambda+2w_0\rho_{\bar{\mathfrak u}}.$$

(5) For restricted BGG transpose duality $D$, the composite $F=D\Psi$ is an exact covariant equivalence $\mathcal F(\bar\Delta)\simeq\mathcal F(\nabla)$ with $F(\bar\Delta(A))\cong\nabla(A)$.

For category-$\mathcal O$ modules these constructions use finite weight spaces and the finite direct sum of $\zeta$-eigenvalue cosets modulo $\mathbb Z$. Internal homogeneous Hom becomes the $\zeta$-locally finite part of Hom, and the dual is the weight-restricted dual. No equivalence on arbitrary category-$\mathcal O$ objects or unrestricted completed Hom spaces is asserted.

items.title: The column monomial basis of the higher-level Fock module
items.statement:
Work in the conventions of
[[def-higher-level-wedge-tensor-fock-module]] and
[[def-the-fock-convention-dictionary-for-finite-type-a-quantum-modules]] with
source parameter $s$.

(1) For a finite interval $[k,r]$, the normally ordered wedges
$v_{i_1}\wedge\cdots\wedge v_{i_d}$, $i_1>\cdots>i_d$, $i_a\in[k,r]$, form an
integral basis of the fundamental wedge $\Lambda^d V$, where the wedge is the
antisymmetrized tensor word with coefficients $(-s)^{\ell(w)}$ over the
symmetric group; the span is primitive over $\mathbb Z[s^{\pm1}]$. This does
not assert that the antisymmetrizer embedding into the raw tensor power is based
in the library's lower $q_0$ chart.

(2) The column monomials $M_A$, $A\in\mathrm{Col}^\Lambda$, form a basis of the
higher-level Fock module $F(\Lambda)$ on every finite cut, with the weights
$\mathrm{wt}(A)$ of the Definition.

(3) Let a finite interval $[k,r]\subseteq I^+$ be a **cut** containing all
entries of a given monomial (upper cut), and $k-1<k$ a further lower residue;
the **lower-cut embedding** $\iota_k$ appends the common bottom entry $k-1$ to
each of the $l$ columns, $\iota_k(M_A)=M_{A\sqcup(k-1)^l}$. The embeddings are
injective, compatible with the monomial action, and their compatible direct
limit over shrinking lower cuts and growing upper cuts is the full bounded or
semi-infinite Fock module of the Definition.

(4) Every generator acts by finitely many box moves and shifts weight spaces;
each fixed-weight space of $F(\Lambda)$ is finite dimensional. A merely
lower-bounded infinite interval need not give finite-dimensional fundamental
factors; all finite-Cartan statements are applied on finite cuts.

items.title: The tensor-product bar on the Fock module and its truncation compatibility
items.statement:
Assume inherited AC [[def-axiom-of-choice]] for the invoked based/global lattice suppliers.

Work in the conventions of
[[def-higher-level-wedge-tensor-fock-module]] and
[[def-the-fock-convention-dictionary-for-finite-type-a-quantum-modules]], with
source parameter $s$ and the ordered column-monomial basis
$\{M_A:A\in\mathrm{Col}^\Lambda\}$ of
[[thm-higher-level-wedge-tensor-fock-module-has-the-column-monomial-basis]].

(1) On every finite interval the Fock module carries an **ordinary compatible
bar** $\psi$, the tensor-product quasi-$R$ bar built from the factors' own
normalized bars on the finite-product based integrable modules of
[[thm-quasi-r-tensor-bars-on-finite-products-of-based-integrable-modules]].
It is involutive (semilinear with $s\mapsto s^{-1}$) and independent of the
parenthesization of the tensor factors.

(2) It is **triangular** on the monomial basis:
$$\psi M_A=M_A+\sum_{B<A}\mathbb Z[s^{\pm1}]\,M_B$$
in the Bruhat order of the Definition; it fixes each ordered fundamental wedge,
and it preserves the integral monomial lattice
$\bigoplus_A\mathbb Z[s^{\pm1}]M_A$.

(3) Both kinds of truncation commute with $\psi$ and preserve the actual
charts and bases: an upper-cut inclusion of the smaller coordinate alphabet (equivalently the inverse identification on the supported truncation),
and the common-bottom-tail embedding
$\iota_k(M_A)=M_{A\sqcup(k-1)^l}$, satisfy
$\psi\iota_k=\iota_k\psi$ and map bar-fixed/chart vectors to bar-fixed/chart
vectors. Hence $\psi$ induces a well-defined bar on the full direct limit of
[[thm-higher-level-wedge-tensor-fock-module-has-the-column-monomial-basis]],
including the semi-infinite columns.

Its finite products are used only on actual finite-Cartan based fundamental
factors; no universal two-sided-unbounded tensor theorem and no arbitrary
integral quasi-$R$ action claim is imported.

items.title: The dual-canonical, canonical and quasi-canonical Fock bases
items.statement:
Assume inherited AC [[def-axiom-of-choice]] for the invoked quantum based/global lattice and normalized quasi-$R$ suppliers.

Work in the conventions of
[[def-higher-level-wedge-tensor-fock-module]] and
[[def-the-fock-convention-dictionary-for-finite-type-a-quantum-modules]]: the
**source parameter** is $s$, the **library parameter** is $t=s^{-1}$, the
monomial basis of the Fock module is $\{M_A\}$, and $\psi$ is the ordinary
compatible bar of
[[thm-the-qg-tensor-product-bar-is-triangular-and-compatible-with-fock-truncations]],
which is triangular and integral on the monomial basis.

The **source dual-canonical family** $(L_A)$ is the unique $\psi$-fixed family
with
$$L_A=M_A+\sum_{B<A}s\,\mathbb Z[s]\,M_B,$$
and the **canonical family** $(T_A)$ is the unique $\psi$-fixed family with
$$T_A=M_A+\sum_{B<A}s^{-1}\mathbb Z[s^{-1}]\,M_B .$$

Let $d_{A,B}(s)$ and $p_{A,B}(-s)$ be the transition coefficients defined by
$$M_B=\sum_A d_{A,B}(s)\,L_A,\qquad L_B=\sum_A p_{A,B}(-s)\,M_A,$$
and define the **quasi-canonical family** by
$$P_A:=\sum_B d_{A,B}(s)\,M_B,\qquad\text{so that}\qquad M_A=\sum_B p_{A,B}(-s)\,P_B .$$
The families $L$ and $T$ are ordinary-bar fixed; $P$ generally is not.

The **reverse-factor monomials** $\widetilde M_A$ use the reverse-column
reading of the tableau $A$; the corresponding bar-fixed families
$\widetilde L_A,\widetilde T_A$ are defined by the same triangular conditions
with respect to $\widetilde M_A$, so that $\widetilde L_A$ is supported on
$B>A$. **Rectification** is the weight-preserving combinatorial identification
of the original lower ground component $\mathrm{Rev}^\Lambda$ with the
reverse-factor lower ground component $\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$, given by reading
down columns and reverse row insertion.

The **source sesquilinear form** is the $\mathbb C$-antilinear-in-the-first
argument pairing with
$$\langle M_A,\psi M_B\rangle=\delta_{AB},$$
and the **bilinear reverse-factor form** is
$$C(\widetilde M_A,\psi M_B)=\delta_{AB}.$$
Thus the labelled monomial Gram matrices of the two forms are the inverse
ordinary-bar matrix, not the identity. Transition duality gives
$$\langle P_A,L_B\rangle=\delta_{AB},\qquad C(\widetilde L_A,T_B)=\delta_{AB},\qquad C(\widetilde T_A,L_B)=\delta_{AB}.$$

All four families are Laurent-integral bases of the finite Fock cuts and
commute with the upper-cut and common-bottom-tail embeddings. On a highest
constituent, the source bilinear normalization $C_0$ and the library
polarization of [[def-upper-global-basis-by-the-contravariant-form]] differ by
an explicit weight power, proved in the global-basis comparison later in this
pair; no unqualified library-upper/ordinary-bar identification is asserted.

items.title: Type-A tableau central summands are single linkage blocks
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). For the Fock shape
$n_1\ge\cdots\ge n_l$ (the original nonincreasing-charge hypothesis) and any
admitted integral entry multiset, the genuine $\mathfrak{gl}_n$ parabolic
central summand labelled by its strict-column tableaux is a **single linkage
block**. The same holds for its reverse-column/reversed-Levi counterpart.
This includes repeated-entry singular ambient characters. The proof uses
actual indecomposable generalized standards and locally constructed tiltings:
adjacent-column positive exclusive-pair canonical coefficients specialize
to $1$, so those labels lie in a common actual linkage block, and these edges
connect the whole fixed-margin binary tableau fiber. No future
higher-Schur/cyclotomic-centre theorem is imported.

items.title: Standard tableau monomials form a basis of the highest weight Fock submodule
items.statement:
Assume inherited AC [[def-axiom-of-choice]] for the invoked based/global lattice suppliers.

Work in the conventions of
[[def-higher-level-wedge-tensor-fock-module]] and
[[def-dual-canonical-canonical-and-quasi-canonical-fock-bases]], with source
parameter $s$, monomial basis $M_A$, ordinary bar $\psi$, source
dual-canonical family $L_A$, canonical family $T_A$, and the source forms
$\langle-,-\rangle$, $C$.

The highest vector $M_{A_\Lambda}$ generates the multiplicity-one constituent
$V(\Lambda)\subseteq F(\Lambda)$, and there is its normalized module projection
$\pi:F(\Lambda)\to V(\Lambda)$.

(1) The vectors $S_A:=\pi M_A$, $A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$, form a basis of
$V(\Lambda)$, and $D_A:=\pi L_A$ for $A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$ form the
**source dual-canonical basis** of $V(\Lambda)$.

(2) What vanishes is $\pi L_A$ for $A$ not standard; $\pi M_A$ need not vanish
for nonstandard $A$. The integral kernel of $\pi$ is the saturated direct
summand with basis the $L_A$ with $A\notin\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$, and
$\pi(F_{\mathcal A})$ has the actual basis $D_A$ (also $S_A$ on
$\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$), the source upper/costandard lattice. For every $B$,
$$\pi M_B=\sum_{A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda}d_{A,B}(s)\,D_A,$$
which gives the explicit straightening of nonstandard projected monomials.

(3) All bases and maps commute with upper cuts and common-tail embeddings, so
the assertions hold in the full direct limit. The relation of the source
$D_A$ to the library form-dual upper family
([[def-upper-global-basis-by-the-contravariant-form]]) is the explicit weight
rescaling proved in the global-basis comparison, not an unqualified
identification.

items.title: The integral parabolic category-O blocks for higher-level Schur-Weyl duality
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) and that $I$ is bounded
below, so $n_j=m_j+1-\inf(I)$ and $n=\sum_jn_j$ are finite; the upper end of
$I$ may remain unbounded. Let $\mathfrak g=\mathfrak{gl}_n(\mathbb C)$ and let
the standard parabolic $\mathfrak p$ have Levi
$\mathfrak{gl}_{n_1}\oplus\cdots\oplus\mathfrak{gl}_{n_l}$
([[def-standard-parabolic-and-levi-subalgebras-from-simple-roots]]).
For a tableau $A$ let $a_1,\dots,a_n$ be its ordinary highest-weight
reading: read columns from left to right and each column from top to bottom,
so its entries are strictly decreasing. This is also the normally ordered column reading of
[[def-higher-level-wedge-tensor-fock-module]]. Put
$$\lambda_A=\sum_{j=1}^{n}(a_j+j-1)\,\varepsilon_j .$$
Strict columns make $\lambda_A$ Levi-dominant, so that the simple highest weight
module $L(A)$ of [[thm-simple-objects-of-category-o-are-highest-weight-modules]]
and the induced generalized standard
$M(A)=M_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda_A)$ of
[[def-parabolic-category-o-for-a-standard-parabolic]] belong to the genuine
parabolic category $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$ of
[[thm-parabolic-category-o-is-a-highest-weight-category]].

Use the published **half-sum convention**
$\rho_j=(n+1-2j)/2$; then
$$\lambda_{A,j}+\rho_j=a_j+\frac{n-1}{2},$$
so the $\mathfrak{gl}_n$ Harish-Chandra shifted-coordinate multiset of the
block is the tableau-entry multiset plus the common scalar $(n-1)/2$, and this
multiset together with the displayed scalar $\mathfrak{gl}_n$ centre labels the
central character ([[cor-central-characters-are-dot-weyl-orbits]]). The Fock
weight $\sum_j\delta_{a_j}=\Lambda-\alpha$ of the Fock item belongs to the
different $\mathfrak{gl}_{I^+}$ weight lattice and indexes that entry multiset;
it is **not** a literal $\mathfrak{gl}_n$ highest weight.

For an entry multiset $\alpha$ the corresponding **finite parabolic central
block** $\mathcal O^\Lambda_\alpha$ has labels
$\mathrm{Col}^\Lambda_\alpha$, generalized standards $M(A)$, simples $L(A)$,
projective covers $P(A)$ and costandards $\nabla(A)$, with the BGG reciprocity,
restricted duality and highest-weight structure inherited from
[[thm-parabolic-category-o-is-a-highest-weight-category]]; by
[[lem-type-a-tableau-central-summands-are-single-linkage-blocks]] it is a single
linkage block. Its simple and standard classes form bases of its Grothendieck
group, and its numerical multiplicities include repeated-entry singular central
characters. The direct sum over the admitted entry multisets is
$\mathcal O^\Lambda$. **Opposite blocks** use the reversed Levi order and the
reverse-column reading, with the correspondingly reversed label order
([[lem-the-parabolic-semi-regular-duality-and-reverse-column-label-map]]).

items.title: The residue translation functors on the sum of parabolic blocks
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) and work with the finite
classical $\mathfrak{gl}_n$ tableau blocks of
[[def-integral-parabolic-category-o-block-for-higher-level-schur-weyl-duality]],
and with the general translation machinery of
[[def-translation-functor-between-o-blocks]] and
[[prop-translation-functors-are-exact-and-biadjoint-across-a-wall]].

Let $V$ be the natural $\mathfrak{gl}_n$-module and $V^{*}$ its dual. For a
residue $i$ define the **residue translation functor** $f_i$ on
$\mathcal O^\Lambda$ by tensoring with $V$ and projecting onto the entry-multiset
central character in which exactly one entry $i$ is replaced by $i+1$; define
$e_i$ by tensoring with $V^{*}$ and the reverse character change ($i+1\mapsto i$,
with the signs of the natural form). Concretely, on a block
$\mathcal O^\Lambda_\alpha$ the functor is the exact block projection
$\operatorname{pr}_{\alpha-\alpha_i}(-\otimes V)$ for $f_i$ and
$\operatorname{pr}_{\alpha+\alpha_i}(-\otimes V^{*})$ for $e_i$, where
$\alpha_i$ is the Fock root label of the dictionary item
([[def-the-fock-convention-dictionary-for-finite-type-a-quantum-modules]]).

On the direct sum $\mathcal O^\Lambda$ of the blocks these functors are exact
and biadjoint, preserve projective and injective objects, and commute with the
restricted transpose duality
([[prop-restricted-duality-is-an-exact-involution-on-category-o]]).
Equivalently, $f_i$ is the generalized $i$-eigencomponent of the tensor
Casimir (including the place factors), and $e_i$ is the generalized
$-n-i$-eigencomponent on the dual tensor product.

The functors are **special residue translations**, not automatically ordinary
regular-wall translations; the Fock root label shifts by $\pm\alpha_i$, and
that label is not the classical $\mathfrak{gl}_n$ highest weight.

items.title: Parabolic Kazhdan-Lusztig polynomials give the dual-canonical transition matrix
items.statement:
For $I$ bounded below use the actual finite classical tableau-block dictionary (including repeated entries). Fix the right place action $(a w)_i=a_{w(i)}$. Let $w_A$ be shortest with $a(A)w_A$ weakly increasing, and let $K$ be the Young stabilizer of that sorted multiset. Then $w_A$ is shortest RIGHT modulo $K$, $d(A)=w_A^{-1}$ shortest LEFT, and
$$p_{A,B}(s)=s^{\ell(w_B)-\ell(w_A)}\sum_{z\in K}(-1)^{\ell(z)}P_{w_Az,w_B}(s^{-2}).$$
This is the ANTISPHERICAL/sign family for the ENTRY stabilizer, in the left convention after inversion, with Hecke variable $v=s$; the library QUANTUM parameter is instead $t=s^{-1}$. It has support $A\le B$ and diagonal1; $d$ is its inverse coefficient matrix through $p(-s)$. The COLUMN Levi subgroup $J$ is generally different from $K$. Assuming AC, the genuine parabolic block composition matrix is
$$[M(B):L(A)]=d_{A,B}(1)=\sum_{C\sim_{\rm col}B}(-1)^{\ell(B,C)}P_{d(C)w_0,d(A)w_0}(1).$$
This uses singular ordinary SPHERICAL coefficients for the entry stabilizer inside finite Levi cancellation, so covers mixed singular-ambient/parabolic-Levi blocks. It does not identify a singular category with genuine parabolic O or identify the two polynomial families by an opposite convention.

items.title: Residue Casimir operators and local affine-Hecke actions
items.statement: Assume AC and work with finite $n$ classical $gl_n$ category O, distinct from the Fock algebra $gl_{I^+}$. Tensor Casimir $x_j$ on the jth natural factor (including all preceding factors) and adjacent place swaps $T_j$ on $M\otimes V^{\otimes r}$ satisfy the degenerate affine-Hecke relations: commuting $x_j$, symmetric-group braid/quadratic relations, $T_jx_j-x_{j+1}T_j=-1$ and commuting distant generators. They restrict naturally to repeated residue functors $f_i^r$, where $x_j-i$ is locally nilpotent; dual actions are biadjoint mates on $e_i^r$. Finite Levi tensor decomposition and exact PBW induction give multiplicity-free generalized-standard flags for the entry moves $i\to i+1$ and $i+1\to i$. The standard-class map $[\Delta(A)]\mapsto M_A$ gives the full integral Fock K0 action, its Chevalley/Serre relations and local integrability; each root's biadjoint functors therefore give a positive, locally finite $sl_2$ action on the simple-class basis. The ground-state class generates the highest constituent, not generally the entire tensor Fock module.

items.title: The highest weight Fock submodule carries the quantum-group global bases
items.statement:
Assume inherited AC [[def-axiom-of-choice]] for the invoked based/global lattice suppliers.

Work in the conventions of
[[def-dual-canonical-canonical-and-quasi-canonical-fock-bases]] and
[[def-the-fock-convention-dictionary-for-finite-type-a-quantum-modules]]:
source parameter $s$, library parameter $t=s^{-1}$. On the highest constituent
$V(\Lambda)\subseteq F(\Lambda)$ put $a(\alpha)=(2\Lambda-\alpha,\alpha)/2$ at
weight $\Lambda-\alpha$.

(1) Under the proved convention and pairing dictionary, the library lower
global vector is
$$G_{\mathrm{low}}(A)=T_{A^{\uparrow}}=s^{-a(\alpha)}P_A\qquad(A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda),$$
whereas the actual library form-dual upper vector is
$$G_{\mathrm{up}}(A)=s^{a(\alpha)}D_A,\qquad D_A=\pi L_A .$$
Source $D_A$ is ordinary-bar fixed; its rescaled library upper vector is fixed
by the form-adjoint upper bar, with the genuine dual integral lattices and
charts of [[def-upper-global-basis-by-the-contravariant-form]].

(2) The source upper/costandard image lattice with basis $D_A$ is identified
with the library form-dual upper lattice by the weightwise units $s^{a(\alpha)}$.
Separately, the source quasi-canonical lattice with basis $P_A$ on the highest
constituent is identified with the library lower divided-power lattice by the
units $s^{-a(\alpha)}$. The embedded upper and lower lattices remain distinct;
no Laurent-unit Gram determinant or unit rescaling between those two embedded
lattices is asserted. All comparisons are integral and compatible with finite
cuts and their direct limits, and then with the supplier's permitted
specializations.

No ordinary-bar fixedness is asserted for the unqualified library upper family.

items.title: The local affine-Hecke socle argument for residue translations
items.statement: Assume AC and the preceding positive biadjoint residue $sl_2$/local degenerate affine-Hecke action. At a coincident eigenvalue the completed affine-Hecke algebra on r steps is $Mat_{r!}$ over the completed symmetric polynomial centre. The first-i image in its central fibre is $Mat_{i!}(Z_{i,r})$, where $Z_{i,r}=\mathbb C[c_1,\ldots,c_i]/(h_{r-i+1},\ldots,h_r)$ is a finite local complete-intersection Frobenius ring of dimension $\binom ri$ and one-dimensional socle. Divided residue functors and the complementary-idempotent restriction have the corresponding simple head/socle. Consequently $e_iL(A)$ and $f_iL(A)$ are either0 or self-dual indecomposables with simple isomorphic head and socle labelled $\tilde e_iA$ and $\tilde f_iA$, respectively. Vanishing is exactly absence of that crystal edge. This retains the complete residue-translation crystal claim, not only its K0 action.

items.title: The residue translation functors give the integrable Fock-space action
items.statement: Assume AC. The exact residue functors on genuine finite-n parabolic blocks have multiplicity-free generalized-standard flags given by valid single-entry moves $i\to i+1$ and $i+1\to i$. Their K0 operators are the full integrable $gl_{I^+}$ Fock Chevalley action, satisfying the integral Chevalley/Serre relations on the standard basis. For each simple, a residue translate vanishes exactly when its corresponding crystal edge is absent; otherwise it is a self-dual indecomposable with simple equal head/socle $L(\tilde f_iA)$ or $L(\tilde e_iA)$. The full tensor Fock module is represented by all standard classes; the ground-state class, with $M(A_\Lambda)=L(A_\Lambda)=P(A_\Lambda)$, generates only its multiplicity-one highest constituent. No action on labels alone proves the K0 relations or head/socle statement.

items.title: Indecomposable tilting objects exist and are classified in parabolic category O
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Every label $A$ in a
genuine tableau parabolic block of
[[def-integral-parabolic-category-o-block-for-higher-level-schur-weyl-duality]]
has a unique indecomposable tilting object $T(A)$ whose standard flag begins
with $M(A)$ once at the bottom and has all remaining labels $B<A$.
Equivalently, $T(A)$ has that maximal-label normalized standard flag and
$\operatorname{Ext}^1(M(B),T(A))=0$ for all $B$. Every tilting object is a finite
direct sum of these, and their classes form a unitriangular Grothendieck basis.
Restricted duality fixes $T(A)$. For a finite lower ideal $\Gamma$ containing
$A$ the corresponding partial tilting is the same ambient $T(A)$, since all
support labels are $\le A$; compatible ideal systems therefore stabilize in each
finite block, with flag-preserving inclusions. No uniqueness is claimed from a
bottom-standard occurrence alone without indecomposability and maximal support.
In the inline prinjectivity claim, $P(A)$ is projective-injective (equivalently
self-dual) exactly when $A$ is standard; in that case $P(A)=T(A^{\uparrow})$
with the proved rectification label.

items.title: The Ringel dual of a finite highest weight ideal
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). In a finite
highest-weight block or in a lower Serre ideal $\Gamma$ of
[[def-standard-costandard-filtered-and-tilting-objects-in-a-highest-weight-category]]
put
$$T_\Gamma=\bigoplus_{A\in\Gamma}T(A),\qquad R_\Gamma=\operatorname{End}(T_\Gamma)^{\mathrm{op}},$$
the **characteristic tilting generator** and its opposite endomorphism ring.
By the classification theorem
([[thm-indecomposable-tiltings-exist-and-are-classified-in-parabolic-category-o]])
$T_\Gamma$ is Ext-self-orthogonal and has finite projective dimension.

The **Ringel-dual category** of $\Gamma$ is the category of finite-dimensional
left $R_\Gamma$-modules, made a highest-weight category by the reversed poset
and the standards
$$\Delta_R(A)=\operatorname{Hom}(T_\Gamma,\nabla(A)),\qquad A\in\Gamma .$$
The functor $\operatorname{Hom}(T_\Gamma,-)$ is exact and fully faithful on
costandard-filtered objects and identifies them with standard-filtered
Ringel-dual objects; projectives of the dual category correspond to tilting
objects of the original. Its algebraic realization by the opposite-parabolic
highest-weight quotient is proved in the next theorem.

items.title: The parabolic category-O Grothendieck group is the integral Fock module
items.statement: Assume AC and $I$ bounded below. The standard-class map $[M(A)]\mapsto M_A$ identifies the direct-sum K0 of genuine tableau parabolic blocks with the full integral Fock module, with matching multiset degrees and residue Chevalley action of $gl_{I^+}$. For every projective $P$ and finite-length $N$, $\dim\operatorname{Hom}(P,N)=\langle[P],[N]\rangle$ at $s=1$. In particular $\langle P_A,L_B\rangle=\delta_{AB}$; no false standard/simple orthogonality $\langle M_A,L_B\rangle=\delta$ is asserted. The projective, simple and tilting basis identifications are proved separately below.

items.title: The Fock pairing matches the projective-simple and standard-costandard pairings
items.statement: Assume AC. At $s=1$ the SOURCE Fock pairing gives $\langle P_A,L_B\rangle=\delta_{AB}$ and $\langle[P],[N]\rangle=\dim\operatorname{Hom}(P,N)$ for projectives. Genuine generalized-standard/costandard Hom has its separate delta pairing $\operatorname{Hom}(M(A),\nabla(B))=\delta_{AB}\mathbb C$, transported by restricted duality and the typed opposite filtered equivalence. At general s the SOURCE forms are $\langle M_A,\psi M_B\rangle=\delta$ and $C(\widetilde M_A,\psi M_B)=\delta$; their labelled raw Gram is $B_\psi^{-1}$, notI. They satisfy $\langle P_A,L_B\rangle=\delta$, $C(\widetilde L_A,T_B)=\delta$ and the complementary duality. On the highest constituent let $C_0$ be the normalized EF-swap bilinear form; for weight $\Lambda-\alpha$, the actual library polarization is $s^{-a(\alpha)}C_0$, $a(\alpha)=(2\Lambda-\alpha,\alpha)/2$. Hence the library upper family uses its own form-adjoint bar and the rescaling below; these two source forms and the library form are not conflated.

items.title: Type-A parabolic category-O Ringel duality via the opposite parabolic
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) and the actual type-$A$
tableau parabolic data of
[[def-integral-parabolic-category-o-block-for-higher-level-schur-weyl-duality]].
Let $\bar{\mathfrak p}$ have the reversed Levi block order, conjugate to the
opposite parabolic, with reverse-column labels, and let
$F=D\Psi$ be the exact **covariant** equivalence constructed by
[[lem-the-parabolic-semi-regular-duality-and-reverse-column-label-map]].
Then
$$F:\mathcal F(\bar\Delta)\simeq\mathcal F(\nabla),\qquad F(\bar M(A))=\nabla(A),\qquad F(\bar P(A))=T(A),$$
and the explicit highest-weight shifts cancel to the original column reading, so
labels $A$ and the matching central-character blocks are preserved. Therefore the
full-block Ringel dual is the opposite-parabolic block, and
$$(T(A):M(B))=[\bar M(B):\bar L(A)] .$$
For a proper original lower ideal $\Gamma$, its Ringel dual is the matching
opposite **highest-weight Serre quotient** by the complementary labels (an upper
ideal in the opposite order), not the same Serre down-set subcategory. The
filtered equivalence and the projective/tilting corner construction give this
compatible finite-ideal transport. No unchanged underived full-longest Borel
twisting and no equivalence on arbitrary category-$\mathcal O$ objects is
asserted.

items.title: Simples, projectives and tiltings map to the three distinguished Fock bases
items.statement: Assume AC and the genuine tableau K0/Fock identification at $s=1$. For every label A, $[L(A)]=L_A$, $[P(A)]=P_A$ and $[T(A)]=T_A$. The projective coefficients are $d_{A,B}(1)$ by BGG; tilting coefficients are the OPPOSITE/reverse-column composition coefficients $\widetilde d_{A,B}(1)$, by the exact parabolic Ringel equivalence. They are not generally the inverse-transpose of the ORIGINAL composition matrix. Simples, projectives and tiltings therefore give the dual-canonical, quasi-canonical and canonical Fock families, respectively. These are ungraded specializations; no Koszul grading or an identification of library upper/lower families is asserted.

decline_pages.title: Parabolic Category O and Fock-Space Bases — Examples

items.title: The four Fock bases in a small two-factor tensor space
items.statement: Take $I=\{0\}$, $I^+=\{0,1\}$ and $\Lambda=2\Lambda_0$, so $F=V\otimes V$ has monomials $M_{00},M_{01},M_{10},M_{11}$. In the mixed order $(M_{01},M_{10})$, $B_\psi=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}1&s^{-1}-s\\0&1\end{smallmatrix}\right)$ and both SOURCE monomial Gram matrices are $S=B_\psi^{-1}$. All unchanged labels have $L=T=M$; $L_{10}=M_{10}-sM_{01}$, $T_{10}=M_{10}+s^{-1}M_{01}$, $P_{01}=M_{01}+sM_{10}$ and $P_{10}=M_{10}$. The reverse family has $\widetilde L_{01}=\widetilde M_{01}-s\widetilde M_{10}$. Give all transition/pairing entries and verify $\overline P^tSL=I$ and $\widetilde L^tST=I$; the four whole families are pairwise different. Both L and T are ordinary-bar fixed, unlike general P. This finite example also verifies the highest-module form rescaling $B_8(T_{10},T_{10})=1+t^2$, $D_{01}=T_{10}/(s+s^{-1})$ and $G_{\rm up}=sD_{01}$ at $t=s^{-1}$.

items.title: The canonical and quasi-canonical bases need not coincide
items.statement:
In the four-dimensional model of
[[ex-four-fock-bases-in-a-small-two-factor-tensor-space]] the canonical and
quasi-canonical Fock families coincide on every label.

items.title: Residue translation on small parabolic category-O standards
items.statement: Take $I=\{0\}$ and $\Lambda=2\Lambda_0$. There is only the residue0. On the four standard monomials, $f_0M_{00}=M_{01}+M_{10}$, $f_0M_{01}=f_0M_{10}=M_{11}$, $f_0M_{11}=0$, and $e_0M_{11}=M_{01}+M_{10}$, $e_0M_{01}=e_0M_{10}=M_{00}$, $e_0M_{00}=0$. Verify $[e_0,f_0]=\operatorname{diag}(2,0,0,-2)$. The source crystal has component $00\to01\to11$ and isolated10; categorical residue translates of the simples have the corresponding unique heads/socles. Outside the allowed alphabet the moves vanish. The calculation uses generalized standards and exact functors, not labels alone.

items.title: Opposite-parabolic Ringel duality on a finite ideal
items.statement: Use classical $gl_3$, Levi(2,1), $I=\{0,1\}$ and $\Lambda=\Lambda_1+\Lambda_0$; take the distinct-entry regular block. In target tableau order let $A_0=(1,0|2)$, $A_1=(2,0|1)$, $A_2=(2,1|0)$, with highest weights $(1,1,4),(2,1,3),(2,2,2)$. The target standard/simple matrix is $D=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}1&0&0\\1&1&0\\0&1&1\end{smallmatrix}\right)$. Reverse readings $(2|1,0),(1|2,0),(0|2,1)$ give opposite highest weights $(2,2,2),(1,3,2),(0,3,3)$ and opposite matrix $N=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}1&1&0\\0&1&1\\0&0&1\end{smallmatrix}\right)$. Verify the semiregular label shift, $F\bar M(A)=\nabla(A)$, $F\bar P(A)=T(A)$ and tilting-standard ROW matrix $N^t$, distinct from target projective-standard rows $D^t$. On the genuine target lower ideal $\Gamma=\{A_0,A_1\}$ the tilting rows are $\left(\begin{smallmatrix}1&0\\1&1\end{smallmatrix}\right)$; its Ringel dual is the opposite highest-weight SERRE QUOTIENT, with standard/simple rows $\left(\begin{smallmatrix}1&1\\0&1\end{smallmatrix}\right)$. Simples/canonical classes in the target ideal are unchanged ambient ones, whereas projective/quasi-canonical classes use the standard-flag truncation of the ambient projectives. This gives the actual three-basis finite-ideal dictionary without a false same-downset opposite restriction.

decision.reason: The approved mathematical scope is preserved by the actual reviewed final repairs and exact canonical metadata reconciliation

decline_pages.title: Arakawa–Suzuki Functors and Higher-Level Schur–Weyl Duality

items.title: The degenerate affine Hecke algebra
