decline_pages.title: Type-A Hecke Specht Modules and Cellular Bases

items.title: Cellular bases and cell modules
items.statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring with $1$ and $A$ a unital $R$-algebra ([[def-algebra-over-a-commutative-ring]]) which is free as an $R$-module on a finite set $C=\{c^{\lambda}_{st}:\lambda\in\Lambda,\ s,t\in T(\lambda)\}$, where $(\Lambda,\unrhd)$ is a finite poset ([[def-partial-order]]; its strict order is written $\rhd$) and each $T(\lambda)$ is a finite set. For $\lambda\in\Lambda$ let $A^{\rhd\lambda}$ be the $R$-submodule of $A$ spanned by all $c^{\mu}_{uv}$ with $\mu\rhd\lambda$. Then $(C,\Lambda)$ is a **cellular basis** of $A$, and $A$ is a **cellular algebra**, if: (i) the $R$-linear map $i:A\to A$ with $i(c^{\lambda}_{st})=c^{\lambda}_{ts}$ for all $\lambda,s,t$ is an algebra anti-automorphism of $A$, i.e. $i(ab)=i(b)i(a)$ and $i(1)=1$ (equivalently $i$ is an isomorphism of $A$ with the opposite algebra; the displayed formula forces $i^2=\mathrm{id}$); and (ii) for every $\lambda\in\Lambda$, every $t\in T(\lambda)$ and every $a\in A$ there exist $r_v\in R$ ($v\in T(\lambda)$) with $$c^{\lambda}_{st}\,a\equiv\sum_{v\in T(\lambda)}r_v\,c^{\lambda}_{sv}\pmod{A^{\rhd\lambda}}.$$

**Cell modules.** For $\lambda\in\Lambda$ let $C^{\lambda}$ be the free $R$-module with basis $\{c^{\lambda}_t:=c^{\lambda}_{tt}:t\in T(\lambda)\}$; condition (ii) makes $C^{\lambda}$ a right $A$-module by $c^{\lambda}_t a:=\sum_v r_vc^{\lambda}_v$ when $c^{\lambda}_{tt}a\equiv\sum_v r_vc^{\lambda}_{tv}\pmod{A^{\rhd\lambda}}$, and it makes $C^{\lambda}$ a left $A$-module via $i$. The module $C^{\lambda}$ is the **(right) cell module** of $\lambda$, and $A^{\unrhd\lambda}/A^{\rhd\lambda}\cong C^{\lambda}\otimes_R C^{\lambda}$ via $c^{\lambda}_{st}+A^{\rhd\lambda}\mapsto c^{\lambda}_s\otimes c^{\lambda}_t$. A cellular algebra may have several cellular bases.

items.title: e-regular and e-restricted partitions
items.statement: Let $e\in\{2,3,4,\dots\}\cup\{\infty\}$ and let $\lambda\vdash n$ be a partition with parts $\lambda_1\ge\lambda_2\ge\cdots$ and conjugate $\lambda'$ ([[def-partition-young-diagram-and-conjugate-partition]]). Then $\lambda$ is **$e$-regular** when every positive integer occurs as a part of $\lambda$ fewer than $e$ times, i.e. $z_j(\lambda)<e$ for every $j\ge1$, and **$e$-restricted** when $\lambda_i-\lambda_{i+1}<e$ for every $i\ge1$ (with $\lambda_i:=0$ for $i>\ell(\lambda)$). For finite $e$ these are exactly the $p$-regular and $p$-restricted notions of [[def-p-regular-and-p-restricted-partitions]] with $p=e$, and $\lambda$ is $e$-restricted if and only if its conjugate $\lambda'$ is $e$-regular. For $e=\infty$ both conditions are vacuous, so every partition is both $e$-regular and $e$-restricted.

items.title: The quantum characteristic of an invertible Hecke parameter
items.statement:
Let $F$ be a field and $q\in F^{	imes}$ an invertible element. The **quantum characteristic** $e=e(F,q)$ is the least integer $e\ge2$ such that $1+q+\cdots+q^{e-1}=0$ in $F$, and $e:=\infty$ when no such integer exists ([[def-q-integer-q-factorial-and-q-multinomial]], [[def-generic-type-a-hecke-algebra]]). Since $[1]_q=1
e0$, the least positive integer $e$ with $[e]_q=0$, when it exists, automatically satisfies $e\ge2$, so the two formulations coincide. Concretely: (i) if $q
e1$ then $[m]_q=(q^m-1)/(q-1)$ for all $m\ge0$, so a finite $e$ exists exactly when $q$ is a root of unity and then $e$ is the multiplicative order of $q$ in $F^{	imes}$; (ii) if $q=1$ then $[m]_1=m$, so $e=\operatorname{char}(F)$ when $\operatorname{char}(F)>0$ and $e=\infty$ when $\operatorname{char}(F)=0$ ([[prop-group-algebra-and-finite-field-specializations-of-the-generic-hecke-algebra]]). If $e<\infty$ then $q
e1$ implies $q^e=1$, and hence $[m+e]_q=[m]_q$ for every integer $m$; in particular the quantum characteristic, not merely the multiplicative order, is the parameter governing the modular representation theory of the Hecke algebra. No choice principle is used.

items.title: Decompositions of the identity into primitive central idempotents are unique
items.statement: Let $A$ be a unital ring, with centre $Z(A):=\{z\in A: za=az	ext{ for all }a\in A\}$. Suppose that $$1=e_1+\cdots+e_k=f_1+\cdots+f_\ell$$ where $\{e_1,\dots,e_k\}$ and $\{f_1,\dots,f_\ell\}$ are finite families of pairwise orthogonal central idempotents of $A$ that are primitive among central idempotents: each is nonzero and admits no decomposition as a sum of two nonzero orthogonal central idempotents (zero parts are omitted). Then $k=\ell$ and there is a bijection $\sigma$ of the index sets with $e_i=f_{\sigma(i)}$ for all $i$; in particular the decomposition of $1$ into primitive central idempotents is unique up to order. No choice principle is used, the families being finite.

items.title: The identity of a finite-dimensional algebra decomposes into primitive central idempotents
items.statement: Let $F$ be a field and $A$ a finite-dimensional unital $F$-algebra with centre $Z(A):=\{z\in A:za=az	ext{ for all }a\in A\}$ ([[def-algebra-over-a-commutative-ring]]). Then $Z(A)$ is a finite-dimensional commutative $F$-algebra, and the identity $1\in Z(A)$ admits a decomposition $$1=e_1+\cdots+e_k$$ into pairwise orthogonal primitive central idempotents of $A$: each $e_i$ is a nonzero idempotent of $Z(A)$ that is not the sum of two nonzero orthogonal idempotents of $Z(A)$. No semisimplicity of $A$ is assumed and no choice principle is used.

items.title: The star anti-automorphism of the type-A Hecke algebra
items.statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $q\in R^{\times}$, and let $H=H_{R,q}(S_n)$ be the specialized type-A Hecke algebra with generators $T_1,\dots,T_{n-1}$ and relations $T_i^2=(q-1)T_i+q$, the braid relations and the distant commutations ([[def-generic-type-a-hecke-algebra]], [[thm-standard-basis-of-the-generic-type-a-hecke-algebra]]). Then the assignment $T_i\mapsto T_i$ ($1\le i<n$) extends uniquely to an $R$-algebra anti-automorphism $*:H\to H$, i.e. an $R$-linear map with $(ab)^*=b^*a^*$ and $1^*=1$; it is an involution, $**=\mathrm{id}_H$, and on the standard basis $$T_w^{*}=T_{w^{-1}}\qquad(w\in S_n).$$ In particular $(T_wT_{w^{-1}})^*=T_wT_{w^{-1}}$ and, for the symmetrizers $m_\lambda=\sum_{w\in S_\lambda}T_w$, one has $m_\lambda^*=m_\lambda$.

items.title: Blocks of a finite-dimensional algebra via primitive central idempotents
items.statement: Let $F$ be a field and $A$ a finite-dimensional unital $F$-algebra with centre $Z(A):=\{z\in A:za=az	ext{ for all }a\in A\}$ ([[def-algebra-over-a-commutative-ring]]). A **central idempotent** of $A$ is an idempotent $e\in Z(A)$; it is **primitive** when $e\ne0$ and $e$ is not the sum of two nonzero orthogonal central idempotents. Then $Z(A)$ is a finite-dimensional commutative $F$-algebra, so $1\in Z(A)$ admits a decomposition $$1=e_1+\cdots+e_k$$ into pairwise orthogonal primitive central idempotents ([[lem-the-identity-of-a-finite-dimensional-algebra-decomposes-into-primitive-central-idempotents]]), and this decomposition is unique up to order ([[lem-central-idempotent-decompositions-of-one-are-unique]]). A **block** of $A$ is the two-sided ideal $B=eA=Ae$ cut out by a primitive central idempotent $e$. The blocks are pairwise orthogonal two-sided ideals, $A=B_1\oplus\cdots\oplus B_k$ as $F$-algebras with units $e_i$, each $B_i$ is an indecomposable two-sided ideal, and for every (not necessarily finite-dimensional) $A$-module $M$ one has $M=\bigoplus_{i=1}^ke_iM$ as $A$-modules; a simple $A$-module $S$ satisfies $e_iS\ne0$ for exactly one $i$ and then $S=e_iS$ lies in the corresponding block. Nothing here asserts that a block is semisimple or simple, and the construction is choice-free.

items.title: Hecke Jucys-Murphy elements and q-contents
items.statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $q\in R^{\times}$, and $H=H_{R,q}(S_n)$ ([[def-generic-type-a-hecke-algebra]]). For $1\le k\le n$ define $$L_1:=0,\qquad L_k:=q^{-1}T_{(k-1,k)}+q^{-2}T_{(k-2,k)}+\cdots+q^{1-k}T_{(1,k)}\in H\quad(k\ge2),$$ where $T_{(i,k)}$ is the standard basis element indexed by the transposition $(i\ k)$ ([[thm-standard-basis-of-the-generic-type-a-hecke-algebra]]). The $L_k$ are the **Hecke Jucys-Murphy elements**. They are fixed by the star anti-automorphism $T_w^*=T_{w^{-1}}$ ([[lem-the-star-antiautomorphism-of-the-type-a-hecke-algebra]]); they commute pairwise and every symmetric polynomial in $L_1,\dots,L_n$ with coefficients in $R$ is central in $H$ ([[thm-hecke-jucys-murphy-action-is-dominance-triangular]]).

**q-contents.** The quantum integers $[m]_q$ for $m\ge0$ are those of [[def-q-integer-q-factorial-and-q-multinomial]]; extend the definition to negative indices by $[-m]_q:=-q^{-m}[m]_q$ for $m>0$, so that $[m]_q=(q^m-1)/(q-1)$ for all $m\in\mathbb Z$ when $q\ne1$, and $[m]_1=m$ for all $m\in\mathbb Z$. For a standard $\lambda$-tableau $t$ and $1\le k\le n$ let $\operatorname{content}_t(k)=c-r$ be the content of the node carrying $k$ ([[def-content-vector-of-a-standard-tableau]]) and define the **q-content value** $[\operatorname{content}_t(k)]_q$. If $e=e(F,q)<\infty$ for a field $F$ then $[m+e]_q=[m]_q$ for every $m\in\mathbb Z$, so the q-content value depends only on the residue of the content modulo $e$. At $q=1$ the specialization $T_w\mapsto w$ of [[prop-group-algebra-and-finite-field-specializations-of-the-generic-hecke-algebra]] sends $L_k$ to the ordinary Jucys-Murphy element $X_k=\sum_{j<k}(j\ k)$ ([[def-jucys-murphy-elements-of-the-symmetric-group-algebra]]), and $[\operatorname{content}_t(k)]_1=\operatorname{content}_t(k)$.

items.title: Murphy elements and Murphy tableau elements
items.statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $q\in R^{\times}$, and $H=H_{R,q}(S_n)$ with standard basis $\{T_w\}$ and star anti-automorphism $*$ ([[def-generic-type-a-hecke-algebra]], [[thm-standard-basis-of-the-generic-type-a-hecke-algebra]], [[lem-the-star-antiautomorphism-of-the-type-a-hecke-algebra]]). For a composition (in particular a partition) $\mu$ of $n$ put $m_\mu:=\sum_{w\in S_\mu}T_w\in H$, the **row symmetrizer** of the standard Young subgroup $S_\mu$ ([[def-young-subgroup-tabloid-and-permutation-module]]); the sum has $|S_\mu|=\prod_i\mu_i!$ terms. For a row-standard $\mu$-tableau $s$ ([[def-young-tableau-standard-tableau-and-shape]]) let $d(s)\in S_n$ be the unique permutation of minimal length with $s=t^{\mu}d(s)$, where $t^{\mu}$ is the row-standard tableau obtained by entering $1,2,\dots,n$ in increasing order from left to right along the rows; $d(s)$ is the distinguished right-coset representative of $S_\mu$ in $S_n$ and $S_\mu$ is the stabiliser of $t^\mu$ ([[def-row-and-column-stabilizers-of-a-tableau]]). For row-standard $\mu$-tableaux $s,t$ define the **Murphy element** $$m_{st}:=T_{d(s)}^{*}\,m_{\mu}\,T_{d(t)}\in H,$$ and for a standard $\lambda$-tableau $t$ shorten $m_t:=m_{tt}=T_{d(t)}^{*}m_\lambda T_{d(t)}$. Then $m_{st}^{*}=m_{ts}$ for all row-standard $s,t$ of the same shape, and $m_\mu T_w=q^{\ell(w)}m_\mu$ for every $w\in S_\mu$.

items.title: The cell form is associative and its radical is a submodule
items.statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $A$ a cellular $R$-algebra with cellular basis $(C,\Lambda)$ and cell modules $C^{\lambda}$ ([[def-cellular-algebra-basis-and-cell-module]]). For each $\lambda\in\Lambda$ there is a unique $R$-bilinear form $$\langle\ ,\ \rangle_\lambda:C^{\lambda}\times C^{\lambda}\longrightarrow R$$ with $$c^{\lambda}_{us}c^{\lambda}_{tv}\equiv\langle c^{\lambda}_s,c^{\lambda}_t\rangle_\lambda\,c^{\lambda}_{uv}\pmod{A^{\rhd\lambda}}$$ for all $s,t,u,v\in T(\lambda)$; in particular the right hand side is independent of $u$ and $v$, and $\langle c^{\lambda}_s,c^{\lambda}_t\rangle_\lambda$ depends only on $s,t$. This form is (i) symmetric, $\langle x,y\rangle_\lambda=\langle y,x\rangle_\lambda$; (ii) associative, $\langle xa,y\rangle_\lambda=\langle x,\,i(a)y\rangle_\lambda$ for all $a\in A$ (and dually for the left action); (iii) characterised by $x\,c^{\lambda}_{uv}=\langle x,c^{\lambda}_u\rangle_\lambda\,c^{\lambda}_v$ for $x\in C^{\lambda}$; and (iv) its radical $\mathrm{rad}\,C^{\lambda}:=\{x\in C^{\lambda}:\langle x,y\rangle_\lambda=0\text{ for all }y\in C^{\lambda}\}$ is an $A$-submodule of $C^{\lambda}$, namely the kernel of $x\mapsto\langle x,-\rangle_\lambda$.

items.title: The type-A q-Schur algebra and its Weyl modules
items.statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $q\in R^{	imes}$, $d,n\ge0$, and $H=H_{R,q}(S_n)$ ([[def-generic-type-a-hecke-algebra]]). Let $\Lambda(d,n)$ be the set of compositions $\mu=(\mu_1,\dots,\mu_d)$ of $n$ (so $\mu_i\in\mathbb N$ and $\sum_i\mu_i=n$). For $\mu\in\Lambda(d,n)$ let $m_\mu=\sum_{w\in S_\mu}T_w$ ([[def-murphy-elements-and-murphy-tableau-elements]]) and let $M^{\mu}:=m_\mu H$ be the right ideal it generates, the **(Hecke) permutation module**; $M^{\mu}$ is free over $R$ with basis $\{m_\mu T_{d(t)}:t	ext{ row-standard }\mu	ext{-tableau}\}$ and is the Hecke analogue of the module induced from the trivial representation of the Young subgroup ([[def-young-subgroup-tabloid-and-permutation-module]]).

Here is the freeness statement in detail: the cosets $S_\mu d$ with $d\in D_\mu$ partition $S_n$, and $\ell(ud)=\ell(u)+\ell(d)$ for $u\in S_\mu$, $d\in D_\mu$ ([[def-murphy-elements-and-murphy-tableau-elements]]), so the standard basis theorem ([[thm-standard-basis-of-the-generic-type-a-hecke-algebra]]) gives $T_uT_{d(t)}=T_{ud(t)}$ and $m_\mu T_{d(t)}=\sum_{u\in S_\mu}T_{u\,d(t)}$; these are the standard basis elements indexed by the single coset $S_\mu d(t)$, and the cosets are disjoint, whence $M^\mu= igoplus_tR\,m_\mu T_{d(t)}$ is free with the displayed basis as $t$ runs over the row-standard $\mu$-tableaux.

Put $M:= igoplus_{\mu\in\Lambda(d,n)}M^{\mu}$ ([[def-direct-sum-of-a-family-of-modules]]) and define the **q-Schur algebra** $$S(d,n):=\mathrm{End}_H(M),$$ the $R$-algebra of right $H$-module endomorphisms of $M$ ([[def-left-and-right-modules]]).

**Cellular structure.** For all $\mu,
u\in\Lambda(d,n)$, $\mathrm{Hom}_H(M^{\mu},M^{
u})$ is free with a basis indexed by row-semistandard tableaux; for every partition $\lambda$ of $n$ with at most $d$ parts and all semistandard $\lambda$-tableaux $S,T$ there is an element $\varphi_{ST}\in S(d,n)$ ([[def-semistandard-tableau-and-kostka-number]]), and the family $$\{\varphi_{ST}:\lambda\in\Lambda^{+}(d,n),\ S,T\in T_0(\lambda)\},$$ where $\Lambda^{+}(d,n)$ is the set of partitions of $n$ with at most $d$ parts ordered by dominance $\unrhd$ ([[def-dominance-order-on-partitions]]), is an $R$-basis of $S(d,n)$; the map $\varphi_{ST}\mapsto\varphi_{TS}$ is an algebra anti-automorphism and the triangular axiom holds modulo the span of the $\varphi_{UV}$ with $\muhd\lambda$. Hence $(\varphi,\Lambda^{+}(d,n))$ is a dominance-cellular basis of $S(d,n)$ ([[def-cellular-algebra-basis-and-cell-module]]) and its cell modules are the **Weyl modules** $W^{\lambda}$, free over $R$ with basis $\{\varphi_T:T\in T_0(\lambda)\}$. Over a field $F$, $W^{\lambda}$ has nonzero simple head $L^{\lambda}$, the $L^{\lambda}$ for $\lambda\in\Lambda^{+}(d,n)$ form a complete set of pairwise non-isomorphic absolutely irreducible $S(d,n)$-modules, and the decomposition matrix satisfies $d_{\lambda\lambda}=1$ and $d_{\lambda\mu}
e0\Rightarrow\lambda\unrhd\mu$.

**Explicit normalization of the semistandard maps.** For a standard $\lambda$-tableau $s$, let $\mu(s)$ replace each entry by the row of that entry in the canonical $\mu$-tableau. For semistandard $S,T$ of respective types $\mu,
u$, put $$m_{ST}:=\sum_{\substack{s,t\in\operatorname{Std}(\lambda)\ \mu(s)=S,\ 
u(t)=T}}m_{st}.$$ The normalized basis map $\varphi_{ST}$ is zero on the other summands and sends $m_
u h\in M^
u$ to $m_{ST}h\in M^\mu$. The intersection $m_{ST}\in M^\mu\cap(M^
u)^*$ makes this well-defined: if $m_
u h=0$, write $m_{ST}=a m_
u$ and obtain $m_{ST}h=0$. The semistandard intersection-basis theorem gives exactly these maps as the Hom basis; their composition is ordinary composition of endomorphisms. For the regular type $\omega=(1^n)$ the fibers are singleton standard tableaux, so evaluation at $1$ identifies the corner map with $m_{st}$. This fixes the actual module-and-form normalization used by the corner and weight-Gram calculations (Mathas (4.13), with Corollary 4.12 and Theorem 4.14). No quantum factorial is inverted in this definition.

**Weight idempotents and weight spaces.** For each composition $
u\in\Lambda(d,n)$, let $1_
u\in\operatorname{End}_H(M)$ be the identity on the summand $M^
u$ and zero on every other summand. These weight projections satisfy $$1_
u^2=1_
u,\qquad 1_\mu1_
u=0\ (\mu
e
u),\qquad   \sum_
u1_
u=1.$$ They are not all of the diagonal cellular elements $\varphi_{TT}$: a general cellular diagonal is not asserted idempotent or orthogonal. For a partition $
u$ the canonical tableau $T^
u$ of shape and type $
u$ gives $1_
u=\varphi_{T^
u T^
u}$; for a general composition the projection is defined directly as above, without pretending that an arbitrary composition is a partition-shaped semistandard tableau. The basis map $\varphi_{ST}$ is supported between the summands indicated by the types of $S$ and $T$. Thus the fixed-first-index Weyl basis vector $\varphi_T$ survives right multiplication by $1_
u$ exactly when $T$ has type $
u$. Over any field, $$\dim_F(W^\lambda1_
u)=|T_0(\lambda,
u)|=K_{\lambda
u}.$$ This follows by applying the projection to the displayed free Weyl basis, not by assuming every diagonal cellular element is a projection ([[def-semistandard-tableau-and-kostka-number]]).

items.title: The Murphy tableau elements form a cellular basis
items.statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $q\in R^{\times}$, and $H=H_{R,q}(S_n)$
([[def-generic-type-a-hecke-algebra]]). Let $\Lambda$ be the set of partitions
of $n$ ordered by dominance $\unrhd$
([[def-dominance-order-on-partitions]]), and for $\lambda\in\Lambda$ let
$T(\lambda)=\mathrm{Std}(\lambda)$ be the set of standard $\lambda$-tableaux
([[def-young-tableau-standard-tableau-and-shape]]). Then the **Murphy basis
theorem** holds: the family
$$\mathcal M=\{m_{st}:\lambda\vdash n,\ s,t\in\mathrm{Std}(\lambda)\}$$
is an $R$-basis of $H$, and $(\mathcal M,\Lambda)$ is a cellular basis of $H$ in
the sense of [[def-cellular-algebra-basis-and-cell-module]]. Explicitly:
(i) $m_{st}^{*}=m_{ts}$ for all $\lambda$ and $s,t$; and (ii) for every
$\lambda$, every $t\in\mathrm{Std}(\lambda)$ and every $h\in H$ there exist
$r_v\in R$ with
$$m_{st}h\equiv\sum_{v\in\mathrm{Std}(\lambda)}r_v\,m_{sv}\pmod{H^{\rhd\lambda}},$$
where $H^{\rhd\lambda}$ is spanned by the $m_{uv}$ with $\mu\rhd\lambda$. The
theorem holds over every commutative coefficient ring with $q\in R^{\times}$
and assumes no semisimplicity; the total number of Murphy elements is
$\sum_{\lambda\vdash n}|\mathrm{Std}(\lambda)|^2=n!$
([[cor-sum-of-squares-of-standard-tableau-numbers]]), matching the rank of $H$.

items.title: The Schur idempotent and the Schur functor for type-A q-Schur algebras
items.statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring with $1$, let $q\in R^{\times}$, let $d,n\ge0$ with $d\ge n$, and let $H=H_{R,q}(S_n)$ ([[def-generic-type-a-hecke-algebra]]). Write $S:=S(d,n)=\mathrm{End}_H(M)$ for the type-A q-Schur algebra with $M=\bigoplus_{\mu\in\Lambda(d,n)}M^{\mu}$ the direct sum of the permutation modules ([[def-type-a-q-schur-algebra-and-weyl-modules]], [[def-direct-sum-of-a-family-of-modules]]) and let $\{\varphi_{ST}:\lambda\in\Lambda^{+}(d,n),\ S,T\in T_0(\lambda)\}$ be its cellular semistandard basis ([[def-murphy-elements-and-murphy-tableau-elements]] for the underlying Murphy elements and [[thm-standard-basis-of-the-generic-type-a-hecke-algebra]] for the standard basis along which this basis is defined). Put $\omega:=(1^n)\in\Lambda(d,n)$, the composition with $n$ parts equal to $1$ (legitimate because $d\ge n$), so that the Young subgroup $S_\omega$ is trivial and $m_\omega=1$; hence $$M^{\omega}=m_\omega H=H$$ is the regular right $H$-module. Let $t^{\omega}$ be the unique standard $\omega$-tableau, with entries $1,2,\dots,n$ down its single column; it is in particular the unique row-standard $\omega$-tableau whose entries increase down the column. Set $$e:=\varphi_{t^{\omega}t^{\omega}}\in S.$$

Then:

1. $e$ is the projection of $M$ onto the direct summand $M^{\omega}=H$ along the other summands $M^{\mu}$, $\mu\ne\omega$; in particular $e^2=e$ and $$eSe\cong\mathrm{End}_H(M^{\omega})=\mathrm{End}_H(H),$$ via the algebra isomorphism $$\rho:H\longrightarrow eSe,\qquad h\longmapsto\rho_h,\qquad \rho_h(x):=hx,$$ left multiplication by $h$ on $M^{\omega}=H$ being a right $H$-module endomorphism. Here the isomorphism $eSe\cong\mathrm{End}_H(M^{\omega})$ sends $efe$ to $f|_{M^{\omega}}$ and is inverted by extending an endomorphism of $M^{\omega}$ by zero on the other summands, and the identification $\mathrm{End}_H(H)\cong H$ sends an endomorphism to its value at $1$. By the construction of the semistandard basis elements $\varphi_{ST}$ (Mathas (4.13) with Corollaries 4.9 and 4.12; see the locator above), the diagonal element $\varphi_{t^{\omega}t^{\omega}}$ is exactly the endomorphism of $M$ that is the identity on $M^{\omega}$ and zero on all $M^{\mu}$ with $\mu\ne\omega$, which is the projection asserted above. 2. The **Schur functor** is $$F:\mathrm{mod}\text{-}S\longrightarrow\mathrm{mod}\text{-}H,\qquad F(X):=Xe=X\otimes_SSe,$$ with the right $H$-action transported along $\rho$, so that $(xe)\cdot h:=x\,\rho_h$ for $x\in X$, $h\in H$ ([[def-left-and-right-modules]]). It is exact and $R$-linear on morphisms: as a **left** $S$-module, $Se$ is the image of the left-$S$-linear projection $s\mapsto se$ on $S$, hence is a direct summand of the regular left module and is projective. Tensoring right $S$-modules with this left module is therefore exact. Equivalently, for a short exact sequence of right modules, an element $ye$ in the target lifts to $xe$ from any lift $x$ of $y$; kernels and injections are likewise preserved by the same idempotent projection. The bimodule corner action makes these maps right $H$-linear. The convention is fixed: the functor is $X\mapsto Xe$ on the right, and the left-module formula $X\mapsto eX$ is not used on this page.

items.title: Semistandard weight dimensions detect virtual Weyl classes
Nonzero cell heads classify the simple modules of a cellular algebra
Cellular decomposition matrices are unitriangular for the cell order
The type-A Hecke Specht module and its cell form
items.statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $q\in R^{\times}$. With the Murphy cellular
basis $(\mathcal M,\Lambda)$ of $H=H_{R,q}(S_n)$
([[thm-murphy-tableau-elements-form-a-cellular-basis]],
[[def-cellular-algebra-basis-and-cell-module]]) and the canonical tableau
$t^\lambda$ of shape $\lambda\vdash n$
([[def-murphy-elements-and-murphy-tableau-elements]]), the **Murphy cell
module** $S^{\lambda}_{\mathrm M}$ is the right cell module $C^{\lambda}$ of the
Murphy basis: it is the free $R$-module with basis
$\{m_t:=m_{t^\lambda t}:t\in\mathrm{Std}(\lambda)\}$ - the classes of the
Murphy elements whose *first* index is the canonical tableau - and $H$ acts by
$m_th=\sum_vr_vm_v$ whenever
$m_{t^\lambda t}h\equiv\sum_vr_vm_{t^\lambda v}\pmod{H^{\rhd\lambda}}$. (The
cellular action rule transforms the second index and fixes the first, so the
diagonal elements $m_{tt}$ alone do not span a submodule; the module basis is
the fixed-first-index family above.) Its **cell form** is the unique bilinear
form $\langle\ ,\ \rangle_\lambda:S^{\lambda}_{\mathrm M}\times
S^{\lambda}_{\mathrm M}\to R$ with
$$m_{us}m_{tv}\equiv\langle m_s,m_t\rangle_\lambda\,m_{uv}\pmod{H^{\rhd\lambda}}$$
for all $s,t,u,v\in\mathrm{Std}(\lambda)$; it is symmetric and associative and
$\mathrm{rad}\,S^{\lambda}_{\mathrm M}$ is a submodule, so
$D^{\lambda}_{\mathrm M}:=S^{\lambda}_{\mathrm M}/\mathrm{rad}\,S^{\lambda}_{\mathrm M}$
is a right $H$-module
([[lem-cell-form-is-associative-and-its-radical-is-a-submodule]]).

**Convention (Dipper-James signed cellular normalization).** Let $\theta:H\to H$
be the involutive algebra automorphism defined by
$\theta(T_i)=-qT_i^{-1}=(q-1)-T_i$
([[lem-dj-bridge-sign-automorphism-and-star-dual]]). For a right module $M$,
write $M^\theta$ for the same $R$-module with action $x\cdot h=x\theta(h)$. The
page's ordinary Specht normalization is the signed conjugate Murphy
construction
$$S^{\lambda}:=(S^{\lambda'}_{\mathrm M})^\theta,$$
where $\lambda'$ is the conjugate partition ([[def-partition-young-diagram-and-conjugate-partition]]). Its form is the form of
$S^{\lambda'}_{\mathrm M}$ on the same underlying module; because $\theta$
commutes with $*$ this is associative for the twisted action
([[lem-dj-bridge-sign-automorphism-and-star-dual]]). Over a field put
$$D^{\lambda}:=S^{\lambda}/\operatorname{rad}_{\rm form}S^{\lambda}=(D^{\lambda'}_{\mathrm M})^\theta.$$
Thus $S^{\lambda'}_{\mathrm M}=(S^{\lambda})^\theta$ and
$D^{\lambda'}_{\mathrm M}=(D^{\lambda})^\theta$; conjugation alone does not
identify these modules
([[thm-dj-bridge-murphy-cell-is-the-same-shape-specht-dual]],
[[thm-dj-bridge-ordinary-specht-is-the-signed-conjugate-murphy-cell]]). At
$q=1$, $\theta(\sigma)=\operatorname{sgn}(\sigma)\sigma$, so these identities
contain tensoring with sign; in characteristic $2$ the sign twist becomes
trivial at $q=1$
([[cor-dj-bridge-specialization-and-composition-multiplicity-dictionary]]).
The nonzero quotients in this signed normalization have $e$-regular labels
by [[thm-simple-type-a-hecke-modules-are-indexed-by-e-regular-partitions]]:
that theorem proves the nonzero Murphy quotient criterion in $e$-restricted
labels, and conjugation makes these precisely $e$-regular labels
([[def-e-regular-and-e-restricted-partitions]]). No generic root-of-unity
Hecke claim is inferred from the published prime-characteristic group-only sign
dictionary, and no semisimplicity or choice principle is assumed.

items.title: Virtual Weyl and Specht symbols attached to beta sequences
items.statement:
Fix a beta length $L\ge1$. For a partition $
u$ with at most $L$ columns (that is, $
u_1\le L$), put $$ eta_i(
u)=
u'_i+L-i\qquad(1\le i\le L).$$ Its beta numbers are strictly decreasing nonnegative integers. Conversely, from any strictly decreasing nonnegative sequence $b$ recover the unique partition with conjugate parts $
u'_i=b_i-L+i$, of degree $|
u|=\sum_i b_i-L(L-1)/2$ ([[def-partition-young-diagram-and-conjugate-partition]]).

For arbitrary $b\in\mathbb Z^L$, first set all its alternating symbols to zero if it has repeated entries or a negative entry. Otherwise there is a unique sorting permutation $w$ taking it to decreasing order; let $
u$ be the recovered partition and let $\epsilon(b)=(-1)^{\ell(w)}$. Uniqueness of the sorting permutation is claimed only in this distinct-entry case. In the fixed degree-$r$ Grothendieck groups define $$[W^b]_{d,r}:= egin{cases}\epsilon(b)[W^
u],&|
u|=r	ext{ and } \ell(
u)\le d,\0,&	ext{otherwise},\end{cases} \qquad [S^b]_r:= egin{cases}\epsilon(b)[S_{\mathrm M}^
u],&|
u|=r,\ 0,&	ext{otherwise}.\end{cases}$$ The notation $[\Delta^b]$ is synonymous with $[W^b]_{d,r}$ when $d,r$ are fixed. The ordinary Dipper-James translation conjugates every partition label and pulls every compared module back by the same $	heta$ ([[def-type-a-hecke-specht-module-and-cell-form]], [[def-type-a-q-schur-algebra-and-weyl-modules]]).

For a composition $\mu$ define the signed semistandard number directly by $$d_\mu(b):= egin{cases}\epsilon(b)|T_0(
u,\mu)|,&b	ext{ has distinct nonnegative entries and }|
u|=|\mu|,\0,&	ext{otherwise}. \end{cases}$$ Here the tableau alphabet is the length of $\mu$; a shape with too many rows automatically has no such tableau ([[def-semistandard-tableau-and-kostka-number]]). This function is alternating in the beta entries. It also obeys the branching identity $$d_\mu(b)=\sum_{\substack{C\subseteq\{1,\ldots,L\}\|C|=z}}  d_{ ar\mu}(b-\mathbf1_C),$$ where $z$ is the last nonzero part of $\mu$ and $ ar\mu$ deletes that part. The selected entries are **decreased by one**, not replaced by $-1$. For a decreasing beta sequence this is the deletion of the largest semistandard entries: they occupy a horizontal strip, at most one box in each selected column. Sorting extends the identity to distinct arbitrary sequences; if entries repeat, terms selecting just one of the equal entries cancel in pairs, while terms selecting both or neither vanish. Negative entries remain negative after decrementing. Thus the identity also holds in all zero-symbol cases. At $\mu=0$ its value is the sorting sign for a permutation of $(L-1,\ldots,0)$ and is zero otherwise, so the recursion terminates without another unproved extension rule.

In the formulas of this page take $L=r$ when $r>0$. A nonzero degree-$r$ partition has width at most $r$, so this length suffices; the Weyl cutoff $\ell(
u)\le d$ is retained even when $d<r$. A balanced displacement $+h\mathbf e_b-h\mathbf e_c$ preserves total degree. An unbalanced change is not silently treated as a class in the same fixed-degree group. The empty degree is handled by the empty beta sequence and unit symbol. No choice principle is used.

items.title: The Jantzen filtration of a lifted cell module
items.statement: Let $R$ be a principal ideal domain ([[def-principal-ideal-domain]]) with a chosen prime element $\pi$, let $F:=R/\pi R$ be the residue field, and let $M$ be a free $R$-module of finite rank ([[def-free-module-on-a-set-and-standard-basis]]) equipped with a symmetric $R$-bilinear form $\langle\ ,\ \rangle:M\times M\to R$ whose extension to the fraction field $K=\operatorname{Frac}(R)$ is non-degenerate (equivalently $\det G\ne0$ for a Gram matrix $G$ of the form). For $i\ge1$ put $$M(i):=\{x\in M:\langle x,y\rangle\in\pi^iR\ \text{for all }y\in M\},\qquad M_F(i):=(M(i)+\pi M)/\pi M\subseteq M_F:=M\otimes_RF.$$ Then $M(0)=M$, the $M(i)$ are $R$-submodules with $M(i+1)\subseteq M(i)$, the descending chain $$M_F=M_F(0)\supseteq M_F(1)\supseteq M_F(2)\supseteq\cdots$$ stabilises at $0$ (that is, $M_F(z)=0$ for all sufficiently large $z$, because $\det G\ne0$), and $M_F(1)=\mathrm{rad}\,M_F$, the radical of the reduced form. This finite descending filtration is the **Jantzen filtration** of $M$ with respect to $(R,\pi,\langle\ ,\ \rangle)$. The hypotheses are exactly: $R$ a PID, $\pi$ a prime element, the form non-degenerate over $\operatorname{Frac}(R)$; no valuation-ring or DVR hypothesis is substituted, and the prime element $\pi$, its ideal $\pi R$ and the fraction field $K$ are kept distinct.

items.title: The Hecke Jucys-Murphy action is dominance triangular
items.statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $q\in R^{\times}$, $H=H_{R,q}(S_n)$, and let
$L_1,\dots,L_n$ be the Hecke Jucys-Murphy elements
([[def-hecke-jucys-murphy-elements-and-q-contents]]). For every $\lambda\vdash n$,
every standard $\lambda$-tableau $t$ and every $1\le k\le n$ there exist
$a_v\in R$ with
$$m_tL_k=[\operatorname{content}_t(k)]_q\,m_t+\sum_{v\rhd t}a_v\,m_v,$$
where $(m_t)_{t\in\mathrm{Std}(\lambda)}$ is the Murphy basis of the Murphy cell
module $S^{\lambda}_{\mathrm M}$
([[def-type-a-hecke-specht-module-and-cell-form]]) and the sum is over standard
$\lambda$-tableaux $v$ strictly dominating $t$ in the dominance order on
tableaux ([[def-dominance-order-on-partitions]],
[[def-young-tableau-standard-tableau-and-shape]]). In particular $L_k$ acts on
the Murphy cell module $S^{\lambda}_{\mathrm M}$ with Murphy basis $(m_t)$ by a
triangular matrix whose diagonal entries are the q-content values.
Consequently the $L_k$ commute pairwise and every symmetric polynomial in
$L_1,\dots,L_n$ is central in $H$.

items.title: The simple type-A Hecke modules are indexed by e-regular partitions
items.statement:
Let $F$ be a field, $q\in F^{\times}$, let
$e=e(F,q)\in\{2,3,\dots\}\cup\{\infty\}$ be the quantum characteristic
([[def-quantum-characteristic-of-an-invertible-hecke-parameter]]) and let
$H=H_{F,q}(S_n)$ for $n\ge0$. For $\lambda\vdash n$ let $S^{\lambda}$ be the
Hecke Specht module and $D^{\lambda}=S^{\lambda}/\mathrm{rad}\,S^{\lambda}$ its
cell-form quotient ([[def-type-a-hecke-specht-module-and-cell-form]]). Then:

1. $D^{\lambda}\ne0$ if and only if $\lambda$ is $e$-regular
   ([[def-e-regular-and-e-restricted-partitions]]);
2. $\{D^{\lambda}:\lambda\vdash n\text{ is }e\text{-regular}\}$ is a complete
   set of pairwise non-isomorphic absolutely irreducible $H$-modules;
3. $H$ is split semisimple if and only if $e>n$ (including $e=\infty$); when
   $e\le n$ the algebra has nonzero radical.

This is the exact root-of-unity replacement for the ordinary Specht
classification. At $q=1$ in characteristic $p>0$ it specialises to the
classification of the simple $F[S_n]$-modules by $p$-regular partitions
([[thm-modular-simple-modules-of-sn-are-the-p-regular-specht-heads]]). No
semisimplicity is assumed and no choice principle is used.

items.title: The type-A Hecke decomposition matrix is dominance unitriangular
items.statement:
Let $F$ be a field, $q\in F^{\times}$, $e=e(F,q)$ and $H=H_{F,q}(S_n)$
([[def-quantum-characteristic-of-an-invertible-hecke-parameter]]). For
$\lambda\vdash n$ and $e$-regular $\mu\vdash n$ let
$$d_{\lambda\mu}:=[S^{\lambda}:D^{\mu}],$$
the multiplicity of $D^{\mu}$ in a composition series of the Specht module
$S^{\lambda}$ ([[def-type-a-hecke-specht-module-and-cell-form]],
[[thm-simple-type-a-hecke-modules-are-indexed-by-e-regular-partitions]]). Then
$$d_{\mu\mu}=1\qquad\text{and}\qquad d_{\lambda\mu}\ne0\ \Longrightarrow\ \mu\unrhd\lambda,$$
where $\unrhd$ is the dominance order on partitions
([[def-dominance-order-on-partitions]]): a simple factor $D^{\mu}$ of
$S^{\lambda}$ can occur only if the $e$-regular label $\mu$ dominates
$\lambda$. Equivalently the decomposition matrix $(d_{\lambda\mu})$ is
unitriangular along dominance. This constrains but does not compute the
entries: no off-diagonal decomposition number is determined by cellularity.

items.title: Jantzen layer dimensions sum to the Gram determinant valuation
items.statement:
In the setting of [[def-jantzen-filtration-of-a-lifted-cell-module]] ($R$ a PID, $\pi$ a prime element, $F=R/\pi R$, $M$ free of finite rank with a form whose extension to $K=\operatorname{Frac}(R)$ is non-degenerate), let $
u_\pi$ be the $\pi$-adic valuation normalised by $
u_\pi(\pi)=1$ and let $G\in R\setminus\{0\}$ be the Gram determinant of the form with respect to any $R$-basis of $M$. Then $$
u_\pi(G)=\sum_{i>0}\dim_FM_F(i),$$ where $M_F(i)$ are the Jantzen layers of [[def-jantzen-filtration-of-a-lifted-cell-module]]; in particular the sum is finite and independent of the chosen basis.

items.title: The Schur functor sends Weyl and simple modules to Specht and Hecke simple modules
items.statement:
Let $k$ be a field, $q\in k^	imes$, $d\ge n$, and let $\mathcal F(X)=Xe$ be the right-module Schur functor of [[def-schur-idempotent-and-schur-functor-for-type-a-q-schur-algebras]]. Set $e_q=e(k,q)$ ([[def-quantum-characteristic-of-an-invertible-hecke-parameter]]). For each $\lambda\in\Lambda^+(d,n)$ let $W^\lambda$ be the Weyl module with Schur cell form $B_\lambda$ and nonzero simple head $L^\lambda$ ([[def-type-a-q-schur-algebra-and-weyl-modules]]). Write $C_{\mathrm M}(\lambda)$ and $D_{\mathrm M}(\lambda)$ for the independent Murphy cell module and its cell-form quotient ([[lem-dj-bridge-murphy-cellular-basis-and-cell-form]]). Then:

1. $\mathcal F(W^\lambda)\cong C_{\mathrm M}(\lambda)$ as right $H$-modules, and this isomorphism identifies $B_\lambda|_{W^\lambda e}$ exactly with the Murphy cell form. 2. $\mathcal F(L^\lambda)\cong D_{\mathrm M}(\lambda)$, including the zero quotient; it is nonzero exactly when $\lambda$ is $e_q$-restricted. 3. For every $e_q$-restricted $
u\vdash n$, $$[W^\lambda:L^
u]=[C_{\mathrm M}(\lambda):D_{\mathrm M}(
u)].$$

In the page's ordinary Dipper–James normalization ([[def-type-a-hecke-specht-module-and-cell-form]], [[thm-dj-bridge-ordinary-specht-is-the-signed-conjugate-murphy-cell]]), these identities become $$\mathcal F(W^{\lambda'})\cong(S^\lambda)^	heta,\qquad \mathcal F(L^{\lambda'})\cong(D^\lambda)^	heta.$$ The latter module is nonzero exactly for $e_q$-regular $\lambda$ and is zero otherwise. For $e_q$-regular $
u$, $$[W^{\lambda'}:L^{
u'}]=[S^\lambda:D^
u].$$ The accepted ordinary polytabloid comparison identifies $S^\lambda$ with the historical DJ module $P(\lambda)$ and identifies their form radicals through an explicit unit factor. Thus the dictionary concerns the actual ordinary modules, not merely a renamed cell module. A zero Hecke cell-form quotient is not asserted to be its actual module head. No semisimplicity or choice principle is assumed, and $n=0$ is included.

items.title: Separated Hecke residues give seminormal idempotents and bases
items.statement:
Let $F$ be a field, $q\in F^{\times}$, let $e=e(F,q)$ and assume $e>n$ (with $e=\infty$ allowed); let $\lambda\vdash n$, $H=H_{F,q}(S_n)$, and let $S^{\lambda}_{\mathrm M}$ be the Murphy cell module with Murphy basis $(m_t)_{t\in\mathrm{Std}(\lambda)}$ ([[def-type-a-hecke-specht-module-and-cell-form]]).

1. (**Separation**) If $s,t$ are standard $\lambda$-tableaux with $[\operatorname{content}_s(k)]_q=[\operatorname{content}_t(k)]_q$ for all $1\le k\le n$ then $s=t$. More precisely, if the q-content values agree for all $k\notin\{i,i+1\}$ for some $i$, then $s=t$ or $t=s(i\ i+1)$. 2. (**Idempotents**) Let $\mathcal R_k$ be the set of distinct q-content values of the entry $k$ over standard tableaux of **all** partitions of $n$. For a standard $\lambda$-tableau $t$ define $$F_t:=\prod_{k=1}^{n}\ \prod_{\substack{c\in\mathcal R_k\\        c\ne[\operatorname{content}_t(k)]_q}}        \frac{L_k-c}{[\operatorname{content}_t(k)]_q-c}\in F[L_1,\ldots,L_n].$$ These are orthogonal idempotents of $H$; their actions on $S_{\mathrm M}^\lambda$ project onto the corresponding simultaneous eigenlines. Put $f_t=m_tF_t$. Then $f_tL_k=[\operatorname{content}_t(k)]_qf_t$ and $f_t=m_t+\sum_{s\rhd t}a_sm_s$. The global content sets are essential for the asserted idempotency in $H$, rather than only the induced same-shape endomorphisms. 3. (**Orthogonal seminormal basis**) $\{f_t:t\in\mathrm{Std}(\lambda)\}$ is a basis of $S^{\lambda}_{\mathrm M}$ satisfying $f_tF_s=\delta_{ts}f_t$ and $\langle f_s,f_t\rangle_\lambda=\delta_{st}\langle f_t,f_t\rangle_\lambda$; it is the **seminormal basis** of the Murphy cell module. 4. (**Generator action**) Let $s$ be a standard $\lambda$-tableau, $1\le i<n$ and $t:=s(i\ i+1)$, and put $\rho:=\operatorname{content}_s(i)-\operatorname{content}_s(i+1)\in\mathbb Z$. If $i$ and $i+1$ lie in the same row of $s$ then $f_sT_i=q\,f_s$; if they lie in the same column then $f_sT_i=-f_s$; otherwise $t$ is standard and $$f_sT_i=\alpha_i(s)\,f_t-\frac{1}{[\rho]_q}f_s,\qquad \alpha_i(s):=\begin{cases}1,&s\rhd t,\\[1mm]\dfrac{[1+\rho]_q[1-\rho]_q}{[\rho]_q[-\rho]_q},&t\rhd s,\end{cases}$$ where $[-\rho]_q$ is the extended quantum integer of [[def-hecke-jucys-murphy-elements-and-q-contents]] and for the swapped tableau $\operatorname{content}_t(i)-\operatorname{content}_t(i+1)=-\rho$. No semisimplicity of $H$ is assumed and no choice principle is used.

items.title: Hecke Specht theory specialises to group Specht theory at q = 1
items.statement:
Let $F$ be a field, $q=1\in F$, and let $H_{F,1}(S_n)$ be the specialization of
the generic type-A Hecke algebra at $v\mapsto1$, so that
$H_{F,1}(S_n)\cong F[S_n]$ with $T_w\mapsto w$
([[prop-group-algebra-and-finite-field-specializations-of-the-generic-hecke-algebra]]).
Then the Hecke theory of this page specializes as follows.

1. The Murphy elements $m_\mu=\sum_{w\in S_\mu}T_w$ specialize to the row
   symmetrizers $\sum_{w\in S_\mu}w$, and the Murphy basis $\{m_{st}\}$ of
   $H_{F,1}(S_n)$ specializes to the Murphy basis of the group algebra
   $F[S_n]$ (the base change $\mathbb Z[S_n]\to F[S_n]$ of the integral Murphy
   basis).
2. For every $\lambda\vdash n$ the specialization of the page's Hecke Specht
   module $S^{\lambda}$ ([[def-type-a-hecke-specht-module-and-cell-form]]) is
   the ordinary Specht module in the Dipper-James convention:
   $S^{\lambda}_{q=1}\cong S^{\lambda}_{\mathrm{DJ}}$ as $F[S_n]$-modules, with
   the standard polytabloid basis ([[thm-standard-polytabloid-basis]]); the
   specialized cell form is the standard bilinear form on $S^{\lambda}$ whose
   radical defines the James quotient $D^{\lambda}$
   ([[def-modular-specht-form-and-radical-quotient]]).
3. The quantum characteristic of $q=1$ is $e=\operatorname{char}(F)$ when
   $\operatorname{char}(F)>0$, and $e=\infty$ when
   $\operatorname{char}(F)=0$
   ([[def-quantum-characteristic-of-an-invertible-hecke-parameter]]); in
   characteristic $p>0$ a partition is $e$-regular exactly when it is
   $p$-regular. Hence $D^{\lambda}_{q=1}\ne0$ exactly for $p$-regular $\lambda$
   ([[thm-specht-radical-quotient-is-nonzero-exactly-for-p-regular-partitions]]),
   and for non-$p$-regular $\lambda$ one has
   $\mathrm{rad}\,S^{\lambda}=S^{\lambda}$. This matches the group-side
   classification
   [[thm-modular-simple-modules-of-sn-are-the-p-regular-specht-heads]] and the
   conjugate-sign dictionary
   [[prop-p-regular-and-p-restricted-simple-labels-are-related-by-conjugate-sign-duality]].
   In characteristic $0$ the specialization is split semisimple and all Specht
   modules are irreducible.

items.title: The q-Schur Weyl weight-space Gram determinant is a hook product
items.statement:
Let $R$ be an integral domain, $q\in R^\times$, $d,n\ge1$, and let $W^\lambda$ be the Weyl module of $S(d,n)$ for a partition $\lambda\vdash n$ with at most $d$ parts. For a composition $\mu$ of $n$ of length $d$, let $G^\lambda_\mu$ be the Gram determinant of its $\mu$-weight space in the semistandard basis ([[def-type-a-q-schur-algebra-and-weyl-modules]]). Put $\beta_j=\lambda'_j+n-j$ and $h_{ab}=\lambda_a-b+\lambda'_b-a+1$. Then $$G^\lambda_\mu=q^N\prod_{\substack{(a,b),(a,c)\in[\lambda]\\b<c}}  \left(\frac{[h_{ab}]_q}{[h_{ac}]_q}\right)^{  d_\mu(\beta+h_{ac}\mathbf e_b-h_{ac}\mathbf e_c)},$$ where $N=\sum_{T\in T_0(\lambda,\mu)}\ell(d(\operatorname{last}(T)))$. Here $\operatorname{last}(T)$ is the least-dominant standardization in the fiber of $T$, and $d_\mu$ is the exact alternating semistandard number of [[def-alternating-weyl-and-specht-symbols-from-beta-sequences]]. **Both beta shifts use the same removed hook length $h_{ac}$.**

The exponent is the sorting sign times $|T_0(\eta,\mu)|$ if that balanced beta sequence has distinct nonnegative entries and recovers $\eta$; it is zero otherwise. Equivalently, remove the rim strip $R_{ac}$ and rewrap its $h_{ac}$ boxes with lowest node in column $b$. The sign is the parity of the heights of the removed strip and the newly added strip, the latter measured in the new diagram $\eta$; it is not generally the sum of two old $\lambda$ hook legs ([[def-removable-border-strip-and-height]], [[lem-hooks-correspond-to-removable-border-strips]]).

Form the product first in the universal field $\mathbb Q(Q)$. It equals a Laurent polynomial in $\mathbb Z[Q,Q^{-1}]$, namely the universal integral Gram determinant divided by its displayed unit $Q^N$. Over $R$ the formula means the specialization of that Laurent polynomial. It does not require inverting a vanishing hook number or evaluating $0/0$. All weights and $d<n$ are retained; an empty weight space has determinant $1$.

items.title: The q-Schaper virtual radical-layer formula
items.statement:
Let $R$ be a principal ideal domain, $\pi$ a prime element, $F=R/\pi R$ the residue field, and let $\hat q\in R^{	imes}$ satisfy $[n]!_{\hat q}
e0$ in $R$; put $q:=\hat q+\pi R\in F^{	imes}$. Let $d\ge1$, let $\lambda$ be a partition of $n$ with at most $d$ parts, and let $W^{\lambda}_F$ be the Weyl module of the q-Schur algebra $S_F(d,n)=S(d,n)\otimes_RF$ with its Jantzen filtration $W^{\lambda}_F(i)$ with respect to $(R,\pi)$ ([[def-jantzen-filtration-of-a-lifted-cell-module]], [[def-type-a-q-schur-algebra-and-weyl-modules]]).

1. (**Jantzen sum formula**) In the Grothendieck group of finite-dimensional $S_F(d,n)$-modules, $$\sum_{i>0} igl[W^{\lambda}_F(i) igr]=\sum_{\substack{(a,b),(a,c)\in[\lambda]\ b<c}}\Bigl(
u_\pi igl([h^{\lambda}_{ab}]_{\hat q} igr)-
u_\pi igl([h^{\lambda}_{ac}]_{\hat q} igr)\Bigr)\Bigl[W_F^{( eta_1,\dots, eta_b+h^{\lambda}_{ac},\dots, eta_c-h^{\lambda}_{ac},\dots, eta_n)}\Bigr],$$ where $ eta= eta(\lambda)$ is the beta sequence of $\lambda$, $h^{\lambda}_{ab}$ are its hook lengths and the symbols are the virtual Weyl symbols of [[def-alternating-weyl-and-specht-symbols-from-beta-sequences]]. 2. (**q-Schaper, $d\ge n$**) If $d\ge n$ and $\Pi$ denotes the Schur functor of [[def-schur-idempotent-and-schur-functor-for-type-a-q-schur-algebras]], then applying $\Pi$ to (1) gives the corresponding identity for the Hecke Specht modules in the source's normalisation, that is, for the Murphy cell modules $\Pi(W^{\lambda}_F)=S^{\lambda}_{\mathrm M}$ of [[def-type-a-hecke-specht-module-and-cell-form]] (the Dipper-James form is obtained by conjugating partitions and applying the same $	heta$ pullback to every Hecke module), $$\sum_{i>0} igl[S^{\lambda}_F(i) igr]=\sum_{\substack{(a,b),(a,c)\in[\lambda]\ b<c}}\Bigl(
u_\pi igl([h^{\lambda}_{ab}]_{\hat q} igr)-
u_\pi igl([h^{\lambda}_{ac}]_{\hat q} igr)\Bigr)\Bigl[S_F^{( eta_1,\dots, eta_b+h^{\lambda}_{ac},\dots, eta_c-h^{\lambda}_{ac},\dots, eta_n)}\Bigr]$$ in the Grothendieck group of finite-dimensional $H_{F,q}(S_n)$-modules, with the virtual Specht symbols of [[def-alternating-weyl-and-specht-symbols-from-beta-sequences]]. The formula is a positive filtration-sum identity expressed in a signed Weyl/Specht basis. A single nonzero signed Weyl coefficient does not force the corresponding labelled simple factor: the entire right side must first be expanded and cancelled in simple classes. For a Weyl module and an off-head label $
u$, the resulting multiplicity of $L^
u$ is an upper bound for $[W^\lambda:L^
u]$, and is positive exactly when that factor occurs in the radical. This does not give a general closed algorithm for decomposition numbers.

items.title: General type-A decomposition numbers remain unsolved
items.statement:
The two preceding constraints on the decomposition matrix of $H_{F,q}(S_n)$ are real but limited, and neither solves the general problem.

(i) Dominance unitriangularity ([[cor-type-a-hecke-decomposition-matrix-is-dominance-unitriangular]]) determines only the diagonal entries $d_{\mu\mu}=1$ and the vanishing region $d_{\lambda\mu}\ne0\Rightarrow\mu\unrhd\lambda$; it gives no value for an off-diagonal entry.

(ii) The q-Schaper/Jantzen sum formula ([[thm-q-schaper-virtual-radical-layer-formula]]) is an identity for the sum of the positive Jantzen filtration submodules. Its individual signed hook terms are not multiplicity bounds. After the whole virtual sum is expanded in simple classes and all cancellations are performed, its nonnegative simple coefficients bound the corresponding radical composition multiplicities from above; it neither determines a general multiplicity nor produces a positive combinatorial rule.

Special coefficient regimes and low-rank calculations determine additional entries (canonically based, weight-one, and small-$n$ cases), but the classification of irreducible Specht modules in arbitrary positive characteristic is a known open problem, and no general closed formula for the decomposition numbers of $S_n$ in a fixed positive characteristic is claimed anywhere on this page. This remark records the boundary; it carries no proof obligation and no choice principle.

decline_pages.title: Type-A Hecke Specht Modules and Cellular Bases — Examples

items.title: Residue sequences need not separate when e is at most n
items.statement: The hypothesis $e>n$ in [[thm-separated-hecke-residues-give-seminormal-idempotents-and-bases]] cannot be dropped. Take $F=\mathbb C$, $q=-1$ (so $e=e(\mathbb C,-1)=2$, [[def-quantum-characteristic-of-an-invertible-hecke-parameter]]), $n=3$ and $\lambda=(2,1)$. The two distinct standard tableaux $s=\begin{smallmatrix}1&2\\3\end{smallmatrix}$ and $t=\begin{smallmatrix}1&3\\2\end{smallmatrix}$ have contents $\operatorname{content}_s(1),\operatorname{content}_s(2),\operatorname{content}_s(3)=0,1,-1$ and $\operatorname{content}_t(1),\operatorname{content}_t(2),\operatorname{content}_t(3)=0,-1,1$, and the extended quantum-integer identity gives $[1]_{-1}=1=[-1]_{-1}$, since $[-1]_{-1}=-(-1)^{-1}[1]_{-1}=1$. Hence $$([\operatorname{content}_s(k)]_q)_{k=1,2,3}=(0,1,1)=([\operatorname{content}_t(k)]_q)_{k=1,2,3}\quad(q=-1):$$ the q-content sequences collide although $s\ne t$, so the separation conclusion of the theorem fails. The difference of the two putative separating eigenvalues at $k=2$ is $[-1]_{-1}-[1]_{-1}=0$. Thus interpolation cannot distinguish the two tableaux: a formula that excludes equal values may still define a polynomial, but it is not a separating projector for these two labels. The attempted generator formula has axial distance $\rho=2$ and $[\rho]_{-1}=0$. In fact $L_2$ has a nontrivial Jordan block on this cell, so this cell has no simultaneous JM-eigenbasis. This explicit example shows that the uniform separation hypothesis $e>n$ cannot be dropped; it does not claim that every individual cell at every parameter with $e\le n$ lacks a seminormal basis.

items.title: The Hecke Jucys-Murphy elements through rank four
items.statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $q\in R^{\times}$. In $H=H_{R,q}(S_n)$ the Hecke Jucys-Murphy elements ([[def-hecke-jucys-murphy-elements-and-q-contents]]) for $n\ge4$ are $$L_1=0,\quad L_2=q^{-1}T_{(1,2)},\quad L_3=q^{-1}T_{(2,3)}+q^{-2}T_{(1,3)},\quad L_4=q^{-1}T_{(3,4)}+q^{-2}T_{(2,4)}+q^{-3}T_{(1,4)},$$ and in general $L_k=\sum_{j<k}q^{j-k}T_{(j,k)}$. For the standard tableau $t=\begin{smallmatrix}1&3&4\\2\end{smallmatrix}$ of shape $(3,1)$ the contents of the entries $k=1,2,3,4$ are $0,-1,1,2$ ([[def-content-vector-of-a-standard-tableau]]), so the diagonal eigenvalues of $L_1,\dots,L_4$ on the Murphy vector $m_t$ are $[0]_q=0$, $[-1]_q=-q^{-1}$, $[1]_q=1$ and $[2]_q=1+q$; the triangular correction terms $\sum_{v\rhd t}a_vm_v$ are present in general ([[thm-hecke-jucys-murphy-action-is-dominance-triangular]]) in the Murphy basis, even in the semisimple range. In the separated range, replacing $m_t$ by the seminormal vector $f_t$ removes these correction terms, as proved in [[thm-separated-hecke-residues-give-seminormal-idempotents-and-bases]]. At $q=1$ the four elements specialize to the ordinary Jucys-Murphy elements $X_1=0$, $X_2=(1\,2)$, $X_3=(1\,3)+(2\,3)$, $X_4=(1\,4)+(2\,4)+(3\,4)$ and the eigenvalues to $0,-1,1,2$, the standard contents of $t$.

items.title: The Murphy cellular basis of H(S_3)
items.statement: Work over any commutative ring $R$ with $q\in R^{\times}$ and let $H=H_{R,q}(S_3)$ with generators $T_1,T_2$, the braid relation $T_1T_2T_1=T_2T_1T_2$ and quadratics $T_i^2=(q-1)T_i+q$. The Murphy cellular basis ([[thm-murphy-tableau-elements-form-a-cellular-basis]]) is indexed by the partitions $(3),(2,1),(1^3)$ ordered by dominance. Explicitly, with $*$ the antiautomorphism $T_w^*=T_{w^{-1}}$ ([[def-murphy-elements-and-murphy-tableau-elements]]): (a) for $\lambda=(3)$, $\mathrm{Std}(3)=\{s\}$ and $m_{ss}=m_{(3)}=1+T_1+T_2+T_1T_2+T_2T_1+T_1T_2T_1$; (b) for $\lambda=(2,1)$, $\mathrm{Std}(2,1)=\{t,u\}$ with $t=\begin{smallmatrix}1&2\\3\end{smallmatrix}$, $u=\begin{smallmatrix}1&3\\2\end{smallmatrix}$, and $m_{(2,1)}=1+T_1$ (the row symmetrizer of $S_{(2,1)}=\langle(1\,2)\rangle$), so that $m_{tt}=1+T_1$, $m_{tu}=(1+T_1)T_2$, $m_{ut}=T_2(1+T_1)$ and $m_{uu}=T_2(1+T_1)T_2$; (c) for $\lambda=(1^3)$, $\mathrm{Std}(1^3)=\{v\}$ and $m_{vv}=m_{(1^3)}=1$. In total $1+4+1=6=3!=|S_3|$ elements; the middle cell carries $|\mathrm{Std}(2,1)|^2=4$ basis elements, its two off-diagonal elements satisfy $m_{tu}^*=m_{ut}$, and the largest cell is spanned by $m_{ss}$, illustrating the cellular anti-involution. At $q=1$ this is the Murphy basis of the group algebra $\mathbb Z[S_3]$ ([[prop-hecke-specht-theory-specializes-to-group-specht-theory-at-q-one]]).

items.title: The q-Schaper calculation for (3,2) at e = 2
items.statement:
Take $R=\mathbb C[\hat q]_{(1+\hat q)}$, the prime element $\pi=1+\hat q$ (so that $F=\mathbb C$ and $q:=\hat q+\pi R$ specialises to $-1$, giving $e=2$), and $\lambda=(3,2)$, $n=5$. Evaluating the q-Schaper virtual sums ([[thm-q-schaper-virtual-radical-layer-formula, thm-q-schur-weyl-weight-space-gram-determinant-hook-product, thm-schur-functor-sends-weyl-and-simple-modules-to-specht-and-hecke-simple-modules, lem-dj-bridge-murphy-cellular-basis-and-cell-form, lem-dj-bridge-integral-murphy-and-polytabloid-straightening, thm-nonzero-cell-heads-classify-the-simple-modules-of-a-cellular-algebra]]) with the hook valuations $
u_\pi([2]_{\hat q})=
u_\pi([4]_{\hat q})=1$, $
u_\pi([3]_{\hat q})=
u_\pi([1]_{\hat q})=0$ gives, in the source's normalisation, $$\sum_{i>0} igl[W^{(3,2)}_F(i) igr]= igl[W^{(3,1^2)}_F igr]+ igl[W^{(2^2,1)}_F igr]- igl[W^{(1^5)}_F igr],\qquad \sum_{i>0} igl[S^{(3,2)}_F(i) igr]=2 igl[D^{(2^2,1)}_{\mathrm{M}} igr].$$ Further Jantzen calculations give $W^{(1^5)}_F=L^{(1^5)}_F$, $W^{(2^2,1)}_F=L^{(2^2,1)}_F$ and $W^{(3,1^2)}_F\sim L^{(3,1^2)}_F+L^{(2^2,1)}_F+L^{(1^5)}_F$, so at the level of the sum formula alone one gets $d_{(3,2),(3,1^2)}=1$ and only the bound $d_{(3,2),(2^2,1)}\in\{1,2\}$. The extra dimension/filtration argument on the Specht side gives $S^{(3,2)}_{\mathrm{M}}\cong D^{(2^2,1)}_{\mathrm{M}}$ (both sides have dimension $5$), whence $d_{(3,2),(2^2,1)}=1$: the virtual sum alone did not determine the entry. Translated to the Dipper-James convention of this page by conjugating and applying the same $	heta$ pullback to both modules ([[def-type-a-hecke-specht-module-and-cell-form]]), this reads $S^{(2,2,1)}_{\mathrm{DJ}}\cong D^{(3,2)}_{\mathrm{DJ}}$, while the partition $(2,2,1)$ is not $2$-regular, so its own labelled cell-form quotient vanishes, $D^{(2,2,1)}_{\mathrm{DJ}}=0$. The computed entry is consistent with the dominance bound $d_{\lambda\mu}
e0\Rightarrow\mu\unrhd\lambda$ of [[cor-type-a-hecke-decomposition-matrix-is-dominance-unitriangular]].

items.title: Cellularity does not make every cell module simple
items.statement:
A cellular algebra need not be semisimple, its cell modules need not be simple, and a labelled cell-form quotient $D^{\lambda}$ may vanish although the cell module $C^{\lambda}$ is nonzero.

(a) Abstract degenerate instance: let $F$ be a field and $A=F[x]/(x^2)$, with $\Lambda=\{2\rhd1\}$ ordered so that $2\rhd1$, cellular basis $c_{11}:=1$ in cell $1$ and $c_{22}:=x$ in cell $2$ and $i=\mathrm{id}$ ([[def-cellular-algebra-basis-and-cell-module]]). For $a+bx\in A$ one has $1(a+bx)\equiv a\cdot1\pmod{(x)}$ and $x(a+bx)=ax$, so the triangular axiom holds, and $A^{\rhd1}=(x)$, $A^{\rhd2}=0$. The cell form on $C^{2}$ has $c_{22}c_{22}=x^2=0$, so it is identically zero, $\mathrm{rad}\,C^{2}=C^{2}$ and $D^{2}=0$, while both $C^{1}$ and $C^{2}$ are one-dimensional simple modules: on either, $a+bx$ acts as the scalar $a$. In particular the Jacobson radical of $C^{2}$ is zero and its actual head is $C^{2}$, even though its cell-form radical is all of $C^{2}$ and its cell-form quotient is zero: cellularity does not force $D^{\lambda}\ne0$, and the algebra is not semisimple since $\mathrm{rad}\,A=(x)$.

(b) Hecke instance: let $F$ be a field of characteristic $2$ and $q=1$, so $e=\operatorname{char}(F)=2$ ([[def-quantum-characteristic-of-an-invertible-hecke-parameter]]); for $n=3$ and $\lambda=(1,1,1)$ the partition $(1,1,1)$ is not $2$-regular ([[def-e-regular-and-e-restricted-partitions]]), so $D^{(1,1,1)}=0$ while the page's Specht module $S^{(1,1,1)}\cong D^{(3)}$ is the nonzero trivial module (in characteristic $2$ the sign module is trivial) ([[thm-simple-type-a-hecke-modules-are-indexed-by-e-regular-partitions]], [[def-type-a-hecke-specht-module-and-cell-form]]).

(c) Reducible cell module: in the $F=\mathbb C$, $q=-1$, $e=2$ specialization of the example the q-Schur cell module $W^{(3,2)}_F$ satisfies $\sum_{i>0}[W^{(3,2)}_F(i)]=[L^{(3,1^2)}_F]+2[L^{(2^2,1)}_F]\ne0$ ([[thm-q-schaper-virtual-radical-layer-formula]], the calculation of [[ex-q-schaper-for-shape-three-two-at-e-two]]), so its radical is nonzero and $W^{(3,2)}_F$ is reducible even though it has a simple head.

items.title: Beta-sets, the shift, and the e-runner abacus of a partition
items.statement: Let $\lambda\vdash n$ be a partition with $m=\ell(\lambda)$ parts and put $b_i(\lambda):=\lambda_i+m-i$ for $1\le i\le m$, so that $X_\lambda=\{b_1>\cdots>b_m\}$ is the set of first-column hook lengths of $\lambda$ ([[def-partition-young-diagram-and-conjugate-partition]], [[def-hook-arm-leg-and-hook-length]]). A **$\beta$-set** is any finite strictly decreasing subset $X=\{h_1>\cdots>h_m\}\subseteq\mathbb N_0$; its **$l$-shift** is $X+l=\{h+l:h\in X\}\cup\{l-1,l-2,\dots,1,0\}$ for $l\ge0$, and its partition is $P(X)=(h_1-(m-1),h_2-(m-2),\dots,h_m-0)$ with trailing zeros deleted. Then $P(X_\lambda)=\lambda$, and $X$ is a $\beta$-set *for* $\lambda$ (that is, $P(X)=\lambda$) if and only if $X=X_\lambda+l$ for some $l\in\mathbb N_0$. For $e\ge2$ the **$e$-abacus** has runners $0,1,\dots,e-1$ (left to right) with the position in row $a\ge0$ of runner $i$ labelled $ae+i$; the **configuration $A_X$** carries a bead in the positions of $X$, and $X\mapsto A_X$ is a bijection onto the finite bead configurations, with inverse $A\mapsto X_A$ and $P(A):=P(X_A)$. Shifting $l$ only changes the row labels of the beads, so every shifted $\beta$-set represents the same partition.

items.title: Hooks are bead-gap pairs on the abacus
items.statement: Let $e\ge2$, $\lambda\vdash n$ and let $X=\{h_1>\cdots>h_m\}$ be a $\beta$-set for $\lambda$ ([[def-beta-set-and-e-runner-abacus-of-a-partition]]). (i) For $h\ge0$ and $i\in[m]$, $h$ is a hook length in row $i$ of $\lambda$ if and only if $h\le h_i$ and $h_i-h\notin X$; equivalently the hooks of $\lambda$ correspond bijectively to the *bead-gap pairs* $(b,g)$ with $b\in X$, $g\notin X$ and $0\le g<b$, the hook $H_{i,j}(\lambda)$ corresponding to $(b,g)$ having length $b-g$ ([[def-hook-arm-leg-and-hook-length]]). (ii) Removing that hook replaces $X$ by $X'=(X\setminus\{b\})\cup\{g\}$, which is a $\beta$-set for $\lambda\setminus H_{i,j}$, and the hook $H_{i,j}$ is the removable border strip of the corresponding rim hook of $\lambda$ ([[def-removable-border-strip-and-height]], [[lem-hooks-correspond-to-removable-border-strips]]). (iii) Hence $e\mid|H_{i,j}|$ if and only if $b\equiv g\pmod e$, that is, if and only if the bead $b$ and the gap $g$ lie on the same runner of the $e$-abacus; and a hook of length $e$ in row $i$ exists if and only if some bead of $X$ has an empty position immediately below it on its own runner.

items.title: The e-core, the e-quotient, and the e-weight
items.statement: Let $e\ge2$ and $\lambda\vdash n$ with $\beta$-set $X$ ([[def-beta-set-and-e-runner-abacus-of-a-partition]], hooks as in [[lem-hooks-are-bead-gap-pairs-on-an-abacus]]). $\lambda$ is an **$e$-core** when $e\notin H(\lambda)$, that is, when $\lambda$ has no hook of length $e$. For a $\beta$-set $X$ let $X^{(e)}_i=\{a\in\mathbb N_0:ae+i\in X\}$ be the set of row labels of the beads on runner $i$; set $X^{(e)}=\bigcup_{i=0}^{e-1}\{ae+i:0\le a\le|X^{(e)}_i|-1\}$ (the *top-packed* $\beta$-set) and define the **$e$-core** $C_e(\lambda):=P(X^{(e)})$. Choose the $\beta$-set so that $|X|\equiv0\pmod e$, and define the **$e$-quotient** $Q_e(\lambda)=(\lambda^{(0)},\dots,\lambda^{(e-1)})$ by $\lambda^{(i)}=P(X^{(e)}_i)$ and the **$e$-weight** by $w_e(\lambda):=|Q_e(\lambda)|=\sum_i|\lambda^{(i)}|$. Every $e$-core is $e$-regular and $e$-restricted. The definitions are independent of the chosen $\beta$-set: shifting by $1$ permutes the runners and changes the quotient only by a cyclic shift of the components, which the normalisation $|X|\equiv0\pmod e$ removes (proved below in the core-independence theorem of this page).

items.title: Virtual Weyl combinations detect q-Schur block separation
items.statement: Let $F$ be a field, $q\in F^{\times}$, $d,n\ge1$, and let $S=S(d,n)$ be the $q$-Schur algebra with Weyl modules $W^{\lambda}$, $\lambda\in\Lambda^{+}(d,n)$ ([[def-type-a-q-schur-algebra-and-weyl-modules]]). Let $M$ be a finite-dimensional right $S$-module all of whose composition factors lie in a single block $B$ ([[def-blocks-of-a-finite-dimensional-algebra-by-primitive-central-idempotents]]), and let integers $a_\lambda$ satisfy $[M]=\sum_\lambda a_\lambda[W^{\lambda}]$ in $G_0(S\text{-mod})$ ([[def-grothendieck-group-of-an-essentially-small-abelian-category]]). Then $W^{\lambda}$ lies in $B$ whenever $a_\lambda\ne0$. In particular no nonzero virtual combination of Weyl classes all of whose terms lie outside $B$ can equal the class of a module in $B$.

items.title: The e-core is independent of the rim hook removal order
items.statement: Let $e\ge2$ and $\lambda\vdash n$. The top-packed $\beta$-set $X^{(e)}$ of [[def-e-core-e-quotient-and-e-weight]] does not depend on the chosen $\beta$-set of $\lambda$ up to a shift that leaves $P$ unchanged, so the $e$-core $C_e(\lambda)$ is a well-defined $e$-core partition; it is exactly the terminal partition reached by successively removing rim $e$-hooks (removable border strips of size $e$, [[def-removable-border-strip-and-height]], [[lem-hooks-correspond-to-removable-border-strips]]) until none is left. In particular every removal order gives the same terminal partition $C_e(\lambda)$, each removed strip has size exactly $e$, and the terminal partition contains no hook of length $e$.

items.title: The e-quotient controls the hooks of e-divisible length
items.statement: Let $e\ge2$ and $\lambda\vdash n$ with $e$-quotient $Q_e(\lambda)$ and $e$-core $C_e(\lambda)$ ([[def-e-core-e-quotient-and-e-weight]]). There is a bijection $f$ from the hooks of $\lambda$ of $e$-divisible length onto the hooks of the multipartition $Q_e(\lambda)$, that is, onto $\bigsqcup_{i=0}^{e-1}\{\text{hooks of }\lambda^{(i)}\}$, such that $|H|=e\,|f(H)|$ and $Q_e(\lambda\setminus H)=Q_e(\lambda)\setminus f(H)$, where the right-hand side means that the corresponding hook of the single component containing it is removed. On the abacus $f$ is the rescaling $b=b'e+i$, $g=g'e+i$ of a bead-gap pair lying on runner $i$ ([[lem-hooks-are-bead-gap-pairs-on-an-abacus]]).

items.title: The core-quotient size formula defines the weight
items.statement: Let $e\ge2$ and $\lambda\vdash n$ with $e$-core $C_e(\lambda)$ and $e$-weight $w_e(\lambda)=|Q_e(\lambda)|$ ([[def-e-core-e-quotient-and-e-weight]]). Then $n=|\lambda|=|C_e(\lambda)|+e\,w_e(\lambda)$, so $w_e(\lambda)=(n-|C_e(\lambda)|)/e\in\mathbb N_0$. Equivalently every sequence of rim $e$-hook removals from $\lambda$ down to its $e$-core ([[thm-e-core-is-independent-of-the-rim-hook-removal-order]]) has exactly $w_e(\lambda)$ steps, and $w_e(\lambda)=|Q_e(\lambda)|$ equals both the number of hooks of the multipartition $Q_e(\lambda)$ and, by the bijection of [[thm-e-quotient-controls-hooks-divisible-by-e]], the number of hooks of $\lambda$ of length divisible by $e$.

items.title: q-Schur Weyl modules are in the same block iff their labels have the same e-core
items.statement:
Let $F$ be a field and $q\in F^{\times}$ with quantum characteristic $e$ ([[def-quantum-characteristic-of-an-invertible-hecke-parameter]], [[def-q-integer-q-factorial-and-q-multinomial]]), let $d\ge n$, and let $W^{\lambda}_F$ be the Weyl modules of $S_F(d,n)$ ([[def-type-a-q-schur-algebra-and-weyl-modules]]). Then for partitions $\lambda,\mu\vdash n$ with at most $d$ parts, $W^{\lambda}_F$ and $W^{\mu}_F$ lie in the same block of $S_F(d,n)$ if and only if $\lambda$ and $\mu$ have the same $e$-core ([[def-e-core-e-quotient-and-e-weight]]). Consequently the blocks of $S_F(d,n)$ are indexed by the $e$-cores $\gamma$ with $|\gamma|\le n$ and $|\gamma|\equiv n\pmod e$, and the block of $W^{\lambda}_F$ is determined by $C_e(\lambda)$. (For $e=\infty$ every partition is its own core and every Weyl module is its own block, the algebra being semisimple.)

No choice principle is used.

items.title: The weight-one block decomposition pattern
items.statement:
Let $F$ be a field and $q\in F^{\times}$ with quantum characteristic $e\ge2$ ([[def-quantum-characteristic-of-an-invertible-hecke-parameter]]), let $\gamma$ be an $e$-core of $m$, and put $n=m+e$ ([[def-e-core-e-quotient-and-e-weight]]). There are exactly $e$ partitions $\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_e$ of $n$ with $e$-core $\gamma$; list them in dominance order, $\lambda_1\rhd\lambda_2\rhd\cdots\rhd\lambda_e$. In the source's (Murphy) normalisation the Weyl modules and simple modules of this weight-one class satisfy $W^{\lambda_e}=L^{\lambda_e}$ and $$[W^{\lambda_k}]=[L^{\lambda_k}]+[L^{\lambda_{k+1}}]\qquad(1\le k<e),$$ so the decomposition matrix of the class is the $e\times e$ bidiagonal matrix with rows and columns $\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_e$. Moreover exactly $\lambda_1$ is not $e$-restricted, while $\lambda_2,\dots,\lambda_e$ are. Under the Schur functor ([[thm-schur-functor-sends-weyl-and-simple-modules-to-specht-and-hecke-simple-modules]]) the corresponding Murphy Specht classes are $$[S^{\lambda_1}_{\mathrm M}]=[D^{\lambda_2}_{\mathrm M}],\qquad [S^{\lambda_k}_{\mathrm M}]=[D^{\lambda_k}_{\mathrm M}]+[D^{\lambda_{k+1}}_{\mathrm M}]\ (2\le k<e),\qquad [S^{\lambda_e}_{\mathrm M}]=[D^{\lambda_e}_{\mathrm M}],$$ with $D^{\lambda_1}_{\mathrm M}=0$; conjugating partitions and applying the same $\theta$ pullback to both modules ([[def-type-a-hecke-specht-module-and-cell-form]], [[thm-dj-bridge-ordinary-specht-is-the-signed-conjugate-murphy-cell]]) gives the corresponding decomposition matrix for the page's Dipper-James Specht modules in $e$-regular labels.

No choice principle is used.

items.title: Type-A Hecke Specht modules are in the same block iff their labels have the same e-core
items.statement:
Let $F$ be a field and $q\in F^{\times}$ with quantum characteristic $e$ ([[def-quantum-characteristic-of-an-invertible-hecke-parameter]]), and let $S^{\lambda}$ be the type-A Hecke Specht module of this page in the Dipper-James convention ([[def-type-a-hecke-specht-module-and-cell-form]]) for $\lambda\vdash n$. Then for all partitions $\lambda,\mu\vdash n$ the modules $S^{\lambda}$ and $S^{\mu}$ lie in the same block of $H_{F,q}(S_n)$ if and only if $\lambda$ and $\mu$ have the same $e$-core ([[def-e-core-e-quotient-and-e-weight]]). Equivalently the blocks of $H_{F,q}(S_n)$ are indexed by the $e$-cores $\gamma$ of size at most $n$ with $|\gamma|\equiv n\pmod e$, and the block of $S^{\lambda}$ is determined by $C_e(\lambda)$. (For $e=\infty$ the Hecke algebra is semisimple and each partition is its own core, so the statement is the trivial block decomposition.)

No choice principle is used.

items.title: Nakayama block classification for symmetric groups
items.statement:
Let $k$ be a splitting field of characteristic $p>0$ (equivalently the residue field of the fixed splitting $p$-modular system, [[def-splitting-p-modular-system-for-a-finite-group]], [[def-p-blocks-by-primitive-central-idempotents]]) and let $n\ge0$. Two Specht modules $S^{\lambda}_k,S^{\mu}_k$ of $k[S_n]$ lie in the same block of $k[S_n]$ if and only if $\lambda,\mu\vdash n$ have the same $p$-core ([[def-e-core-e-quotient-and-e-weight]]). Consequently the blocks of $k[S_n]$ are indexed by the pairs $(\gamma,w)$ with $\gamma$ a $p$-core, $w\in\mathbb N_0$ and $n=|\gamma|+pw$, and the block of $S^{\lambda}_k$ is the pair $(C_p(\lambda),w_p(\lambda))$ with $w_p(\lambda)=(n-|C_p(\lambda)|)/p$ ([[prop-core-quotient-size-and-weight-formula]]).

No choice principle is used.

items.title: Weight-zero symmetric-group blocks are defect zero
items.statement: Let $k$ be a splitting field of characteristic $p>0$ and $\lambda\vdash n$ a partition of $p$-weight $w_p(\lambda)=0$, that is, a $p$-core. Then the block $B$ of $k[S_n]$ containing $S^{\lambda}_k$ ([[thm-nakayama-block-classification-for-symmetric-groups]]) contains exactly one Specht label, namely $\lambda$; its decomposition matrix is the $1\times1$ matrix $(1)$, so $D^{\lambda}$ is both the unique simple and the unique projective indecomposable of $B$; its Cartan matrix is $(1)$; the block algebra is a full matrix algebra over $k$; and $B$ has trivial defect group, that is, defect zero in the fixed splitting modular system ([[def-defect-group-and-numerical-defect-of-a-block]]).

items.title: Block weight is not the same as numerical defect
items.statement: The $e$- or $p$-weight of a block records combinatorial data: the number of $e$-hooks removed from a label to reach its $e$-core, so that $n=|\gamma|+ew$ by [[prop-core-quotient-size-and-weight-formula]]. The numerical defect of a block is defined from its defect group and is a $p$-adic order invariant of the block algebra in the fixed modular system ([[def-defect-group-and-numerical-defect-of-a-block]]). The two invariants must not be identified without a theorem and an explicit range: only the weight-zero case is settled on this page, where Nakayama's classification forces the block to be simple and of defect zero ([[prop-weight-zero-symmetric-group-blocks-are-defect-zero]]). The general defect-group computation for weight-$w$ symmetric-group blocks, and the exact range in which the two invariants coincide, are not proved or claimed here; they require the block-theoretic defect computation of the modular representation theory of the symmetric groups, outside this page's proof route.
