items.title: Generalized Jucys-Murphy primary idempotents and the residue-summand functors $E_i$, $F_i$
items.statement:
Let $k$ be a field of characteristic $p>0$ and let $L_1,\dots,L_n\in kS_n$
be the Jucys-Murphy elements $L_r=\sum_{s<r}(s,r)$ of the symmetric group
algebra ([[def-jucys-murphy-elements-of-the-symmetric-group-algebra]]). Recall
that they commute pairwise
([[cor-jucys-murphy-elements-commute-pairwise]]), and for $r\le n$ the
element $L_r$ lies in the subalgebra $kS_r\subseteq kS_n$ and therefore
commutes with $S_{r-1}$.

**(i) Primary idempotents.** In the commutative subalgebra
$k[L_1,\dots,L_n]\subseteq kS_n$ the minimal polynomial of each $L_r$ on the
regular module splits into linear factors $X-a$ with $a$ in the prime field
$\mathbb F_p\subseteq k$, and the commuting family admits the following
simultaneous primary decomposition. There are pairwise orthogonal idempotents
$P_{r,a}\in k[L_r]\subseteq k[L_1,\dots,L_n]$, indexed by $r\in\{1,\dots,n\}$
and $a\in\mathbb F_p$, with
$$\sum_{a\in\mathbb F_p}P_{r,a}=1,\qquad P_{r,a}P_{r,b}=\delta_{a,b}P_{r,a},$$
such that for every finite-dimensional $kS_n$-module $M$ the action of
$P_{r,a}$ on $M$ is the projection onto the generalized eigenspace
$M_{r,a}=\{m\in M:(L_r-a)^Nm=0\text{ for }N\gg0\}$. The $P_{r,a}$ for
different $r$ commute, and for each sequence $\mathbf i=(i_1,\dots,i_n)$
with entries in $\mathbb F_p$ the products
$$e(\mathbf i):=\prod_{r=1}^nP_{r,i_r}\ \in\ k[L_1,\dots,L_n]$$
are pairwise orthogonal idempotents with $\sum_{\mathbf i}e(\mathbf i)=1$ and
$e(\mathbf i)M=M_{\mathbf i}$, the simultaneous generalized weight space
$M_{\mathbf i}=\{m:(L_r-i_r)^Nm=0\ \forall r,\ N\gg0\}$. Every $P_{r,a}$ and
every $e(\mathbf i)$ is fixed by the antipode $g\mapsto g^{-1}$ of $kS_n$.

**(ii) Content sums and blocks.** The symmetric group $S_n$ permutes the
coordinates of sequences, and two sequences are called *equivalent* when they
differ by a permutation, i.e. when they have the same content (the same
multiset of entries of $\mathbb F_p$). Write $\mathcal C_n=(\mathbb F_p)^n/S_n$ for the set of content classes
(equivalently, multisets of $n$ residues). For $\alpha\in\mathcal C_n$ let
$I_\alpha$ be the set of sequences representing $\alpha$, and put
$$e_\alpha:=\sum_{\mathbf i\in I_\alpha}e(\mathbf i)\ \in\ kS_n .$$
Each $e_\alpha$ is a central idempotent of $kS_n$, and distinct $e_\alpha$
are orthogonal; the nonzero $e_\alpha$ are exactly the primitive central
idempotents, that is the block idempotents of $kS_n$
([[def-p-blocks-by-primitive-central-idempotents]]), and every block
idempotent of $kS_n$ is of the form $e_\alpha$: this last identification of
the content sums with the blocks is the block theorem of Lyle-Mathas and
Brundan recorded as (2.41) in Kleshchev's survey (printed p. 11), with the
content of the block being the content of any of its partitions. The present
item proves the centrality, idempotency and orthogonality of the sums
$e_\alpha$ and then uses only those properties; primitivity and
exhaustiveness are recorded from the cited block theorem, not re-proved here.

**(iii) Residue-summand functors.** For a finite-dimensional $kS_n$-module
$M$, a residue $i\in\mathbb Z/p$ and a content class
$\alpha\in\mathcal C_{n-1}$, put
$$e_{\alpha,\alpha_i}:=\sum_{\mathbf j\in I_\alpha}e((\mathbf j,i)) \ =\ e_\alpha^{(n-1)}\,P_{n,i},$$
where $(\mathbf j,i)$ denotes concatenation, $e_\alpha^{(n-1)}=\sum_{\mathbf
j\in I_\alpha}e(\mathbf j)$ is the content sum computed in $kS_{n-1}$ and
regarded in $kS_n$ through the inclusion $kS_{n-1}\subseteq kS_n$, and
$P_{n,i}\in k[L_n]$. Each $e_{\alpha,\alpha_i}$ is an idempotent of $kS_n$
commuting with $kS_{n-1}$, the family
$\{e_{\alpha,\alpha_i}\}_{i\in\mathbb F_p,\alpha\in\mathcal C_{n-1}}$ is a family of pairwise orthogonal
idempotents with $\sum_{i,\alpha}e_{\alpha,\alpha_i}=1$, and
$$E_iM:=\sum_{\alpha\in\mathcal C_{n-1}}e_{\alpha,\alpha_i}M =\bigoplus_{\alpha}e_{\alpha,\alpha_i}M$$
is a $kS_{n-1}$-submodule of the restricted module with
$$\operatorname{Res}^{S_n}_{S_{n-1}}M=\bigoplus_{i\in\mathbb Z/p}E_iM .$$
Dually, for a finite-dimensional $kS_d$-module $M$ of content
$\alpha\in\mathcal C_d$, i.e. $M=e_\alpha^{(d)}M$, put
$$F_iM:=kS_{d+1}\,e_{\alpha,\alpha_i}\otimes_{kS_d}M \qquad(i\in\mathbb Z/p),$$
with $e_{\alpha,\alpha_i}=e_\alpha^{(d)}P_{d+1,i}\in kS_{d+1}$; for a
general finite-dimensional $M$, with the sum indexed by $\alpha\in\mathcal C_d$, put
$F_iM:=\bigoplus_\alpha kS_{d+1}e_{\alpha,\alpha_i}\otimes_{kS_d}e_\alpha M$.
Then $\operatorname{Ind}^{S_{d+1}}_{S_d}M=\bigoplus_{i\in\mathbb Z/p}F_iM$,
and all the functors $E_i,F_i$ are additive and exact, preserve
finite-dimensionality, and commute with contragredient duality, because the
projectors are fixed by the antipode. All statements hold at $p=2$; the
construction is choice-free.

items.title: Residue signatures, normal, good, conormal and cogood nodes
items.statement:
Let $p>0$ and let $\mu$ be a $p$-restricted partition, so that
$\mu_i-\mu_{i+1}<p$ for all $i\ge1$
([[def-p-regular-and-p-restricted-partitions]],
[[def-partition-young-diagram-and-conjugate-partition]]). A node $(r,c)$ of
the Young diagram $[\mu]$ is an **$i$-node** if its residue
$$\operatorname{res}(r,c):=c-r\bmod p$$
equals $i\in\mathbb Z/p$; the $i$-nodes of $\mu$ are its addable and removable
nodes of residue $i$
([[def-removable-and-addable-nodes-of-a-partition]]).

**The reduced $i$-signature.** Fix $i\in\mathbb Z/p$ and list the $i$-nodes
of $\mu$ as $A_1,\dots,A_n$ from top to bottom, that is, in increasing row
index and, for equal row index, in increasing column index. Form the word
$\sigma=(\sigma_1,\dots,\sigma_n)$ with $\sigma_m=+$ if $A_m$ is addable and
$\sigma_m=-$ if $A_m$ is removable. Whenever $r<s$, $\sigma_r=-$,
$\sigma_s=+$ and $\sigma_{r+1}=\dots=\sigma_{s-1}=0$, replace $\sigma_r$ and
$\sigma_s$ by $0$; repeat until no $-$ lies to the left of a $+$. The
resulting **reduced $i$-signature** has the form $+\cdots+- \cdots-$ with the
zeros deleted, and the nodes attached to its signs are:

- the **normal $i$-nodes** of $\mu$ are the removable nodes corresponding to
  the $-$ signs of the reduced signature;
- the **good $i$-node** is the topmost (first listed) of the normal $i$-nodes;
- the **conormal $i$-nodes** of $\mu$ are the addable nodes corresponding to
  the $+$ signs of the reduced signature;
- the **cogood $i$-node** is the bottommost (last listed) of the conormal
  $i$-nodes.

Write $\varepsilon_i(\mu)$ and $\varphi_i(\mu)$ for the numbers of normal and
of conormal $i$-nodes of $\mu$; the good $i$-node exists exactly when
$\varepsilon_i(\mu)>0$, and the cogood $i$-node exactly when
$\varphi_i(\mu)>0$. At most one good and at most one cogood $i$-node occur,
for each residue.

**Well-definedness.** Each reduction step deletes two nonzero entries, so any
sequence of steps terminates after at most $\lfloor n/2\rfloor$ steps, and in
the resulting word no $-$ lies to the left of a $+$: otherwise, take two
nonzero entries that are consecutive among the nonzero entries of the current
word and are ordered $-$, $+$; all entries strictly between them are $0$ by
the choice, so the pair would still be reducible. Hence, after deleting the zero entries, a terminal word is
$+^a-^b$ for some $a,b\ge0$; cancelled positions remain in their original
places and need not form a contiguous block. The terminal word does not depend on the
order in which reducible pairs are chosen: two reducible pairs cannot overlap
partially, because an endpoint of one pair lying strictly inside the other
would be a nonzero entry in a position that the other pair requires to be
$0$, and pairs sharing exactly one endpoint would similarly place a nonzero
entry strictly inside the other pair; so any two reducible pairs are either
disjoint (and the corresponding steps commute) or equal, there are no
critical pairs, and the rewriting relation is locally confluent. Uniqueness follows
by induction on the number of nonzero entries. A terminal word admits no
step. Otherwise, two distinct first steps commute and reach a common word
after one further step each. All these successor words have fewer nonzero
entries, so the induction hypothesis identifies their terminal words. Thus
any two reduction sequences have the same terminal word; in it the first surviving $-$ and the last surviving
$+$ are unique positions whenever they exist. Thus the reduced signature,
the sets of normal and conormal nodes, and the good and cogood nodes are well
defined. The empty partition has the unique addable node $(1,1)$, of residue $0$,
and no removable nodes. Its $0$-signature is $(+)$ and its other signatures
are empty. Thus $\varepsilon_i(\varnothing)=0$ for every $i$,
$\varphi_0(\varnothing)=1$, and $\varphi_i(\varnothing)=0$ for $i\ne0$.
It has no good node and its cogood $0$-node is $(1,1)$.

**Convention warning.** The residue $c-r$ used here is the negative of
Brundan's $\ell$-residue $r-c$, and a removable node of $\mu$ is normal here
exactly when its transposed node is normal in Brundan's sense for the
transpose partition $\mu'$; lists of addable and removable nodes, and the
signs of the residues, must never be silently mixed between the two
conventions
([[def-removable-and-addable-nodes-of-a-partition]],
[[def-partition-young-diagram-and-conjugate-partition]]).

items.title: Finite-group induction is coinduction, hence biadjoint to restriction
items.statement:
Let $H\le G$ be finite groups and let $k$ be any field. For every left
$kH$-module $M$ the map
$$\Phi_M:\ \operatorname{Ind}_H^G M=kG\otimes_{kH}M\longrightarrow\operatorname{Coind}_H^G M=\operatorname{Hom}_{kH}(kG,M),\qquad \Phi_M(g\otimes m)(x)=\begin{cases}(xg)m,&xg\in H,\\ 0,&xg\notin H,\end{cases}$$
is a natural isomorphism of $kG$-modules
([[def-restriction-induction-and-coinduction-for-group-modules]]). Consequently
$\operatorname{Ind}_H^G\cong\operatorname{Coind}_H^G$ naturally, so induction
is both a left and a right adjoint of restriction
([[thm-induction-is-left-adjoint-and-coinduction-right-adjoint-to-restriction]])
and is exact. No hypothesis on the characteristic of $k$, on splitting
fields, or on the prime $2$ is needed, and the argument is choice-free: it
uses only the finite selection of least representatives of the finitely many
left cosets.

items.title: The socle of an uncoloured modular restriction is the multiplicity-free sum over the good residues
items.statement:
Let $k$ be a field of characteristic $p>0$ and let $\mu$ be a $p$-restricted
partition of $d\ge1$; write $D(\mu)$ for the simple $kS_d$-module labelled by
$\mu$
([[thm-modular-simple-modules-of-sn-are-the-p-regular-specht-heads]],
[[prop-p-regular-and-p-restricted-simple-labels-are-related-by-conjugate-sign-duality]]).
Let $A_i$ denote the good $i$-node of $\mu$, for those
$i\in\mathbb Z/p$ with $\varepsilon_i(\mu)>0$
([[def-residue-signature-normal-good-conormal-and-cogood-nodes]]). Then
$$\operatorname{soc}_{S_{d-1}}\bigl(D(\mu){\downarrow}_{S_{d-1}}\bigr)=\bigoplus_{i:\,\varepsilon_i(\mu)>0}D(\mu\setminus A_i),$$
a multiplicity-free sum over distinct simple modules: distinct residues give
distinct summands. The sum runs over the residues $i$ with
$\varepsilon_i(\mu)>0$, one good node per such residue; the completely
reducible special case (the restriction is semisimple if and only if every
normal node is good, Kleshchev II Theorem 0.6) is a separate statement and is
not asserted here.

items.title: Good-node deletion and cogood-node addition operators
items.statement:
On the set of $p$-restricted partitions
([[def-p-regular-and-p-restricted-partitions]]) define partial operators
$\tilde e_i,\tilde f_i$ for $i\in\mathbb Z/p$ by
$$\tilde e_i\mu:=\mu\setminus A\quad\text{if }\varepsilon_i(\mu)>0,$$
where $A$ is the good $i$-node of $\mu$
([[def-residue-signature-normal-good-conormal-and-cogood-nodes]]), the
operator being undefined on $\mu$ when $\varepsilon_i(\mu)=0$; and
$$\tilde f_i\mu:=\mu\cup B\quad\text{if }\varphi_i(\mu)>0,$$
where $B$ is the cogood $i$-node of $\mu$, the operator being undefined on
$\mu$ when $\varphi_i(\mu)=0$. Then
$$\mu=\tilde f_i\nu\qquad\Longleftrightarrow\qquad\nu=\tilde e_i\mu$$
for all $p$-restricted $\mu,\nu$; in particular $\tilde e_i$ and $\tilde f_i$
are mutual inverses on their domains, each $\tilde e_i$ lowers the rank by one
and each $\tilde f_i$ raises the rank by one, and at most one good and at most
one cogood node exist in each residue. No module-theoretic statement is made
here: this item is pure combinatorics, and the identification of these
operators with the crystal operators of the level-one Fock space is a theorem
of the later Fock-space page, not an input here.

items.title: Every $p$-restricted partition is reached from the empty partition by cogood additions
items.statement:
Let $k$ be a field of characteristic $p>0$. Every $p$-restricted partition
$\mu$ of $d$ is obtained from the empty partition by $d$ successive cogood
additions: there are residues $i_1,\dots,i_d$ with
$$\mu=\tilde f_{i_d}\cdots\tilde f_{i_1}\varnothing;$$
equivalently, every $p$-restricted $\mu\ne\varnothing$ has at least one good
node, and successive good deletions carry $\mu$ to $\varnothing$
([[def-good-node-and-cogood-node-crystal-operators]],
[[def-residue-signature-normal-good-conormal-and-cogood-nodes]]). Hence, in
the graph whose vertices are the $p$-restricted partitions and whose edges
join $\nu$ to $\tilde f_i\nu$ for every $i$ for which the operator is
defined, the empty partition is the unique vertex of rank $0$ and every
vertex is reached from it; dually every vertex reaches the empty partition by
successive good deletions. The argument is choice-free.

items.title: The crystal identification does not elementarily identify the cellular simple labels
items.statement:
Two labellings of the simple modules of the group algebra $kS_d$ and of the
Hecke algebra $H_d$ are in play on this page and on the Fock-space page.

- The **cellular labels** $D(\mu)=\operatorname{hd}(S(\mu))$ are the heads of
  the Specht modules in the dual-Specht convention; they are the labels used
  by the modular classification
  ([[prop-p-regular-and-p-restricted-simple-labels-are-related-by-conjugate-sign-duality]]).
- The **inductive (crystal) labels** $\dot D(\mu)$ are defined recursively
  from the residue-summand functors $F_i$ of
  [[def-generalized-jm-primary-idempotents-and-residue-summand-functors]] by
  $\dot D(\varnothing)=k$ and, for $\mu\ne\varnothing$,
$$\dot D(\mu):=\operatorname{hd}\bigl(F_i\dot D(\tilde e_i\mu)\bigr) \quad\text{for any }i\text{ for which }\tilde e_i\mu\text{ is defined},$$ the
  operators $\tilde e_i,\tilde f_i$ being those of
  [[def-good-node-and-cogood-node-crystal-operators]] and the independence
  of the choice of $i$ a theorem of the crystal theory. The two labellings
  agree, $$\dot D(\mu)\cong D(\mu)\qquad(\mu\ \text{p-restricted}),$$ and this
  identification (11.1) of Kleshchev's survey is *not* elementary: it was
  first established by Ariki and later by graded arguments, both depending on
  the full theory of the cyclotomic Hecke/KLR categorification.

Consequently no proof on this page or on the later Fock-space page may use
Fock-space reachability to establish the cellular classification of simple
modules, or the cellular classification to establish the Fock-space
component; the two directions are separated by this reminder. In particular
the socle theorem
`cor-socle-of-uncoloured-modular-restriction-is-the-sum-over-good-residues`
and the branching theorems of this page are stated and used for the cellular
labels, while any statement about the crystal operators as operators on Fock
space is a separate obligation of the Fock-space page.

items.title: An integral essential-subset basis and count for type-A root intervals
items.statement:
Let $F$ have characteristic $p>0$, let $N\ge2$, and let $\mu=(\mu_1\ge\cdots\ge\mu_N\ge0)$ be a polynomial highest weight. Let $L_N(\mu)$ be the nonzero Schur Weyl-cell simple at $q=1$, regarded as a left module by star, with its canonical highest vector $v$. Put $a_i=\mu_i-\mu_{i+1}$. For every $1\le r\le s<N$, define $B(i,j)=j-i+\sum_{t=i}^j a_t$ and $C(i,j)=j-i+\sum_{t=i}^{j-1}a_t$, reduced modulo $p$ for zero tests. A matching is an injection $d$ with $x\le d(x)$; it need not preserve order between different sources. Call $J\subseteq(r,s]$ essential when no $t<u$ outside $J$ in $[r,s+1]$ admits a zero-$B$ matching $\{t\}\cup(J\cap(t,u))\to[t,u)$. Write $\varepsilon_a(r,s)$ for the number of essential sets.

The vectors $T_{r,s}(J)v$ constructed by the explicit integral coefficient recursion in the proof, indexed by essential $J$, form a basis of $L_N(\mu)_{\mu-\alpha_r-\cdots-\alpha_s}$. In particular this weight-space dimension is $\varepsilon_a(r,s)$, including dimension zero. The construction has integer-polynomial coefficients, and its positive-word pivots remain valid in every field of characteristic $p$.

Define a root $x$ to be normal in $[x,y]$ when $a_x\ne0$ and its demands $m>x$ with $B(x,m)=0$ admit an injection $z$ satisfying $x<z(m)\le m$ and $B(z(m),m)=0$. If $r$ is not normal set $\nu_a(r,s)=0$; otherwise let it be the number of $x\in[r,s]$ normal in $[x,s]$ with $C(r,x)=0$. Set $\varepsilon'_a(r,t)=\varepsilon_{a+\omega_t}(r,t)$, where only coordinate $t$ is increased by one. Then, as ordinary integers,
$$\varepsilon_a(r,s)=\nu_a(r,s)+\sum_{u=r+1}^s\varepsilon'_a(r,u-1)\nu_a(u,s).$$
No restrictedness condition is imposed on $\mu$ or on the shifted auxiliary highest weights.

items.title: Kleshchev's first-level branching multiplicity
items.statement:
Let $k$ be a field of characteristic $p>0$ (every field is splitting for
symmetric groups, so no algebraic closedness is needed) and let $\lambda$ be
a $p$-regular partition of $n$
([[def-p-regular-and-p-restricted-partitions]]), so that $D^\lambda$ is the
simple head of the Specht module $S^\lambda_k$
([[thm-modular-simple-modules-of-sn-are-the-p-regular-specht-heads]]). Let
$A=(j,\lambda_j)$ be a removable node of $\lambda$ whose removal
$\lambda(j)$ is again $p$-regular, and call $A$ **normal** for $\lambda$ when
the transposed node $(\lambda_j,j)$ of the $p$-restricted partition
$\lambda'$ is a normal node in the sense of
[[def-residue-signature-normal-good-conormal-and-cogood-nodes]] (this is
Kleshchev's normality; it is computed in the reduced signature of the correct
residue class of $\lambda'$). Then
$$[\,D^\lambda{\downarrow}_{S_{n-1}}:D^{\lambda(j)}\,]=0$$
if $A$ is not normal, and
$$[\,D^\lambda{\downarrow}_{S_{n-1}}:D^{\lambda(j)}\,]=1+\#\{B:\ B\ \text{is a normal removable node of }\lambda\text{ strictly above }A\text{ with }\operatorname{res}(B)=\operatorname{res}(A)\}$$
if $A$ is normal. Here $\operatorname{res}$ is the residue $c-r\bmod p$ and
"above" means strictly smaller row index. Equivalently, the multiplicity is the piecewise integer
$\gamma(A)=\mathbf1_{A\text{ normal}}\cdot\#\{B:B\text{ normal removable, weakly above }A,\ \operatorname{res}(B)=\operatorname{res}(A)\}$.
Thus $A$ is normal precisely when this piecewise multiplicity is nonzero.

items.title: Normal-node composition multiplicities under residue restriction
items.statement:
Let $k$ be a field of characteristic $p>0$, $\mu$ a $p$-restricted partition
of $d$ and $A$ a removable $i$-node of $\mu$ such that $\nu=\mu\setminus A$
is again $p$-restricted; let $D(\mu)$ be the simple $kS_d$-module labelled by
$\mu$ in the dual-Specht (cellular) convention, so that
$D(\mu)\cong D^{\mu'}\otimes\operatorname{sgn}$
([[prop-p-regular-and-p-restricted-simple-labels-are-related-by-conjugate-sign-duality]],
[[thm-modular-simple-modules-of-sn-are-the-p-regular-specht-heads]]), and let
$E_i$ be the residue-summand functor of
[[def-generalized-jm-primary-idempotents-and-residue-summand-functors]]. Then
$$[\,E_iD(\mu):D(\nu)\,]=0$$
if $A$ is not a normal $i$-node of $\mu$, and
$$[\,E_iD(\mu):D(\nu)\,]=\#\{B:\ B\ \text{normal }i\text{-node of }\mu\text{ weakly below }A\}$$
(counting $A$ itself) if $A$ is normal. The corresponding
Specht-to-restriction Hom criterion (Brundan 1998 Theorem 2.5, equivalently
Kleshchev II Theorem 0.4) is a distinct statement and is not asserted here.

items.title: Conormal-node composition multiplicities under residue induction
items.statement:
In the notation of
[[thm-normal-node-composition-multiplicities-under-residue-restriction]], let
$B$ be an addable $i$-node of the $p$-restricted partition $\mu$ such that
$\nu=\mu\cup B$ is again $p$-restricted, and let $F_i$ be the residue-summand
induction functor of
[[def-generalized-jm-primary-idempotents-and-residue-summand-functors]]. Then
$$[\,F_iD(\mu):D(\nu)\,]=0$$
if $B$ is not a conormal $i$-node of $\mu$, and
$$[\,F_iD(\mu):D(\nu)\,]=\#\{B':\ B'\ \text{conormal }i\text{-node of }\mu\text{ weakly above }B\}$$
(counting $B$ itself) if $B$ is conormal. The dual Specht-to-induction Hom
criterion (Kleshchev survey Theorem 11.7(i), Brundan 1998 Theorem 2.5 dual
form) is a distinct statement and is not asserted here.

items.title: The good node gives the simple socle and head of the residue restriction
items.statement:
Let $k$ be a field of characteristic $p>0$, $\mu$ a $p$-restricted partition
of $d$ and $i\in\mathbb Z/p$ with $\varepsilon_i(\mu)>0$; let $A$ be the good
$i$-node and $\nu=\mu\setminus A$
([[def-residue-signature-normal-good-conormal-and-cogood-nodes]]). For the
residue-summand functor $E_i$ of
[[def-generalized-jm-primary-idempotents-and-residue-summand-functors]] the
module $E_iD(\mu)$ has simple socle and simple head, both isomorphic to
$D(\nu)$, and the total (ungraded) multiplicity of $D(\nu)$ in $E_iD(\mu)$ is
$\varepsilon_i(\mu)$. Thus the Loewy endpoints are simple even though the
formal character of $E_iD(\mu)$ may contain the additional normal-node
factors of
[[thm-normal-node-composition-multiplicities-under-residue-restriction]].

items.title: The cogood node gives the simple socle and head of the residue induction
items.statement:
Let $k$ be a field of characteristic $p>0$, $\mu$ a $p$-restricted partition
of $d$ and $i\in\mathbb Z/p$ with $\varphi_i(\mu)>0$; let $B$ be the cogood
$i$-node and $\nu=\mu\cup B$
([[def-residue-signature-normal-good-conormal-and-cogood-nodes]]). Then
$F_iD(\mu)$ has simple socle and simple head, both isomorphic to $D(\nu)$,
and the total (ungraded) multiplicity of $D(\nu)$ in $F_iD(\mu)$ is
$\varphi_i(\mu)$
([[def-generalized-jm-primary-idempotents-and-residue-summand-functors]]).

items.title: The Schur functor compares first-level branching with Hecke restriction
items.statement:
Let $F$ be a field, $q\in F^\times$, $\ell=e(F,q)$, and $n\ge r\ge1$; at the empty lower-rank boundary put $S(0,0)=H(0)=F$ with its identity functor. Use the left-module version of the q-Schur algebra $S(n,r)$ and its exact Schur functor $f_{n,r}:V\mapsto eV$ with left adjoint $h_{n,r}:X\mapsto S(n,r)e\otimes_{eS(n,r)e}X$ ([[def-type-a-q-schur-algebra-and-weyl-modules]], [[def-schur-idempotent-and-schur-functor-for-type-a-q-schur-algebras]]). Right-module suppliers are converted to left modules through their star anti-involutions. All Specht and simple labels below are **Murphy labels**: $f(W^\mu)=S_{\mathrm M}^\mu$ and $f(L_n(\mu))=D_{\mathrm M}^\mu$, the latter nonzero exactly when $\mu$ is $\ell$-restricted ([[thm-schur-functor-sends-weyl-and-simple-modules-to-specht-and-hecke-simple-modules]]).

For a degree-$r$ polynomial module $V=\bigoplus_{|\alpha|=r}V_\alpha$, its **first level** is $$V^1:=\bigoplus_{\alpha_n=1}V_\alpha.$$ It is a module for the Levi polynomial algebra $S(n-1,r-1)$: the first $n-1$ coordinates sum to $r-1$. It is not the sum of the weights one simple root below the highest weight. For an $\ell$-restricted partition $\lambda\vdash r$, the following hold.

1. There is a natural $H(r-1)$-module isomorphism $$f_{n-1,r-1}(L_n(\lambda)^1)\cong      \operatorname{Res}_{H(r-1)}^{H(r)}f_{n,r}(L_n(\lambda)).$$ 2. For any $S(n,r)$-modules $W,V$ with $W^{(e)}=W$ and $V_{(e)}=0$, the Schur functor induces $$\operatorname{Hom}_{S(n,r)}(W,V)\cong      \operatorname{Hom}_{H(r)}(fW,fV).$$ Here $W^{(e)}=S(n,r)eW$ is the intersection of submodules whose quotient is killed by $e$, and $V_{(e)}$ is the sum of submodules killed by $e$. 3. The socle of $L_n(\lambda)^1$ as a Levi module has only $\ell$-restricted labels.

For every partition $\mu\vdash r-1$ with $\mu$ $\ell$-restricted, $$[L_n(\lambda)^1:L_{n-1}(\mu)]  =[\operatorname{Res}D_{\mathrm M}^{\lambda}:D_{\mathrm M}^{\mu}].$$ The exact functor transfers these surviving multiplicities; it may kill nonrestricted simple factors. At $q=1$ these statements hold over every field for the group algebras. In ordinary James labels the dictionary is $D_{\mathrm M}^{\lambda}\cong D^{\lambda'}\otimes\operatorname{sgn}$, not an untwisted identification with $D^\lambda$ ([[prop-hecke-specht-theory-specializes-to-group-specht-theory-at-q-one]]).

items.title: The symmetric-group level-one residue and partition-label convention
items.statement: Fix finite e≥2 and charge0. English nodes(r,c) have residue c−r mod e, with the full independent-root affine datum already fixed. An e-regular partition has every positive-part multiplicity<e; an e-restricted partition has lambda_a−lambda_(a+1)<e for every a. Thus lambda restricted iff lambda-prime regular. The MODULAR/restricted signature lists corners top-to-bottom, cancels −+, takes good removable FIRST surviving− and cogood addable LAST surviving+. Crystal labels of the basic module here are restricted shapes. To make the ambient module comparison exact, define the Q(q)-linear isomorphism J:F_sym→F_QG by J M_lambda=|lambda-prime>. Define E_i^sym=J^-1 E_-i^QG J,F_i^sym=J^-1 F_-i^QG J,K_h^sym=J^-1 K_(tau h)^QG J, and psi_sym=J^-1 psi_QG J; J does not invert q. The standard chart is ⊕ A0 M_lambda. Its full crystal has ALL partitions; its empty component restricted shapes. Weight is Lambda0−Σ_i m_i(lambda)alpha_i; J applies tau:i→−i to weight. The conjugation map exchanges addable/removable node TYPES with themselves and negates residue, and is a map BETWEEN models, not the same-model sign/Mullineux involution. In characteristic p>0 with e=p prime, simple labels satisfy D^mu=D(mu-prime)⊗sgn; for Hecke algebras finite e is the quantum characteristic, not necessarily prime. The source boundary e=0 means no positive e with 1+xi+...+xi^(e−1)=0; colors are Z and every level-one partition is a crystal label. No finite affine datum is claimed there.

items.title: Residue-node reading orders and the conjugation dictionary
items.statement: For distinct addable/removable corners of one residue i (finite e≥2), smaller row implies strictly larger column and strictly larger content. Hence top-to-bottom=DECREASING content=decreasing column; bottom-to-top=increasing content. A same-residue row or column cannot repeat. Conjugation sends a top-to-bottom i-corner list of lambda to the bottom-to-top (increasing content) −i-corner list of lambda-prime, preserving signs. Thus its modular −+ cancellations, FIRST− good deletion and LAST+ cogood addition agree exactly with the QG INCREASING-content −+ rule on lambda-prime. Equivalently reverse the latter list and use decreasing-content +− cancellation, LAST− deletion and FIRST+ addition. Both versions select the same actual nodes. They apply to all partitions as signatures; the basic graph restriction is imposed separately.

items.title: The QG Fock-crystal arrows are the modular good-node operators
items.statement: Conjugation C sends the restricted/modular crystal on restricted lambda onto the EMPTY COMPONENT of the QG full partition Fock crystal, with colors negated: C tilde-e_i lambda=tilde-e_-i^QG C lambda and C tilde-f_i lambda=tilde-f_-i^QG C lambda, including zero values. Epsilon_i/phi_i are the numbers of surviving−/+, and weight transforms by tau. With the explicitly transported full module F_sym the modular signatures give its Kashiwara operators on ALL partitions, whose restricted subset is its basic component. Good is removable (tilde-e), cogood addable (tilde-f) in BOTH conventions; there is no opposite naming-polarity dictionary. Ordinary Chevalley coefficients, especially negative powers, do not define these arrows.

items.title: The restricted-partition component is the basic crystal in the symmetric-group convention
items.statement: For finite e≥2 the empty component of F_sym is exactly the e-restricted partitions, with modular good deletions/cogood additions and wt(lambda)=Lambda0−Σ m_i alpha_i. It is B(Lambda0), every restricted shape is reached from empty, and epsilon/phi count normal/conormal nodes. The entire F_sym has ALL partitions and is reducible, with the transported full p(k) highest-module decomposition; its other vertices are the nonrestricted shapes. In the symmetric-group regime of algebraically closed characteristic p>0 and xi=1, e=p is PRIME: restricted labels lambda correspond to James simples D^(lambda-prime)=D(lambda)⊗sgn, and if epsilon_i(lambda)>0 then soc E_-i D^(lambda-prime)=D^((tilde-e_i lambda)-prime). The standard E_-i is the residue functor after sign twist. General finite-e Hecke crystal labels remain valid but are not called symmetric-group modules of 'characteristic e'. At quantum characteristic e=0 (colors Z), every level-one partition is in the empty sl_infinity crystal; there are no same-content corner cancellations, and no finite-affine assertion is made.

items.title: Level-one global-basis transition polynomials in the symmetric-group convention
items.statement:
Work in the linear symmetric-group model of
[[def-symmetric-group-level-one-residue-and-partition-label-convention]]: the
$\mathbb{Q}(q)$-linear isomorphism $J M_\mu = |\mu'\rangle$, the transported
action, bar and $A_0$ standard chart $(F_0)_{\mathrm{sym}}$, and the weight
$\operatorname{wt}(M_\mu) = \Lambda_0 - \sum_i m_i(\mu)\alpha_i$, with
$A = \mathbb{Z}[q,q^{-1}]$.

**The basic module and its lower basis.** Let
$M_{\mathrm{sym}} := J^{-1}V(\Lambda_0) = J^{-1}M_{\mathrm{QG}}$ be the
transported highest-weight module of the vacuum; by
[[thm-restricted-partition-component-is-the-basic-crystal-in-the-symmetric-group-convention]]
its crystal is the $e$-restricted component and its labels are the $e$-restricted
partitions. For an $e$-restricted $\lambda$ define
$$G_{\mathrm{sym}}(\lambda) := J^{-1}G_{\mathrm{QG}}(\lambda'),$$
where $G_{\mathrm{QG}}(\mu)$ is the lower global (canonical) basis element of
the Fock space at the standard vector $|\mu\rangle$
([[thm-the-basic-representation-global-basis-is-unitriangular-in-the-partition-basis]]).
Then $G_{\mathrm{sym}}(\lambda) \equiv M_\lambda \bmod q\,(F_0)_{\mathrm{sym}}$
and the family $\{G_{\mathrm{sym}}(\lambda)\}$ is the transported lower global
basis of $M_{\mathrm{sym}}$, indexed by the restricted labels. Define the
**level-one transition polynomials in the symmetric-group convention** by the
finite weightwise expansion
$$G_{\mathrm{sym}}(\lambda) = \sum_\mu d_{(\lambda,\mu)}(q)\, M_\mu ,$$
the sum being over the partitions $\mu$ of the weight of $\lambda$.

**Ambient polarization and ambient upper coordinates.** Define the ambient
polarization by $B(M_\mu,M_\nu) = \delta_{\mu\nu}$ on the standard basis, a
symmetric nondegenerate bilinear form on each finite weight space. Fix a weight
$w$ and let $V_w$ be the (finite-dimensional) weight space of
$F_{\mathrm{sym}}$; let $D_{\mathrm{rect}}$ be the matrix with columns the
coordinate vectors of $G_{\mathrm{sym}}(\lambda)$ for the finitely many
$e$-restricted $\lambda$ of weight $w$, and rows the **standard** shapes
$M_\mu$, $\mu$ of weight $w$; let
$$H := D_{\mathrm{rect}}^{\mathsf{t}}\, D_{\mathrm{rect}} , \qquad G_{\mathrm{sym}}^*(\lambda) := \sum_\mu \bigl(D_{\mathrm{rect}}H^{-1}\bigr)_{(\mu,\lambda)}\, M_\mu^* ,$$
where $M_\mu^*$ denotes the ambient orthonormal dual frame of the standard
basis. The $G_{\mathrm{sym}}^*(\lambda)$ are the **ambient upper coordinates**
of the basic module: they are the unique elements of the basic subspace
$(M_{\mathrm{sym}})_w\subseteq V_w$ characterized weightwise by $B(G_{\mathrm{sym}}^*(\lambda), G_{\mathrm{sym}}(\lambda')) = \delta_{\lambda\lambda'}$,
and are viewed in the ambient standard frame; adding a vector of the
$B$-orthogonal complement in $V_w$ gives other ambient representatives with
the same pairings. The coefficients
$e_{(\lambda,\mu)}(q) := (D_{\mathrm{rect}}H^{-1})_{(\mu,\lambda)}$ lie in
$\mathbb{Q}(q)$ but need not be Laurent integral or polynomial. They are
coordinates in the ambient space and not a "standard basis of the basic
module"; the exact integral upper basis is the transported upper global basis of
[[thm-upper-and-lower-global-bases-are-dual-and-crystal-compatible]], whose
restricted graded $A$-dual lattice is free weightwise and perfectly paired with
the basic lower $A$-span, while no lower-$A$ selfduality, no $A$-unit $H$ and no
full algebraic duality in infinite rank is implied. The restriction of $B$ to the basic module equals the normalized transported
contravariant form (proved in step 4.2), so these are the same upper vectors
viewed in the ambient standard frame and in their own integral dual lattice.
Upper bar is the adjoint bar
$\psi^\vee$ with its own dual infinity chart and weighted upper operators, not
the ordinary lower bar.

**The full ambient case.** On the whole Fock space the analogous matrix
$D_{\mathrm{full}}$, with columns the $G(\mu)$ over all partitions and rows the
standard shapes, is unitriangular (diagonal $1$, in $q\mathbb{Z}[q]$ below the
diagonal), and the dual matrix with respect to $B$ is
$$D_{\mathrm{full}}^{-\mathsf{t}},$$
which is Laurent integral because the inverse of a unitriangular matrix with
entries in $\mathbb{Z}[q]$ has entries in $\mathbb{Z}[q]$.

**A worked instance.** At $e = 2$ the restricted shape $\lambda = (1,1)$ has
$G_{\mathrm{sym}}(1,1) = M_{1,1} + q\,M_{2}$, so $D_{\mathrm{rect}}$ has the
single column $(q,1)^{\mathsf{t}}$, $H = 1 + q^2$, and
$$G_{\mathrm{sym}}^*(1,1) = \frac{M_{1,1}^* + q\,M_2^*}{1+q^2} = \frac{M_{1,1} + q\,M_2}{1+q^2},$$
an explicit ambient coordinate that is rational but not Laurent integral:
$1 + q^2$ is not a unit of $\mathbb{Z}[q,q^{-1}]$. No specialization of the $d$
to decomposition numbers of Hecke algebras is asserted here without the
separate correct Hecke parameter hypotheses.

decline_pages.title: Level-One Fock Space and Residue Crystals — Examples

items.title: The Fock E- and F-actions on the shape (2,1) at e = 3
items.statement: At e3 the QG standard vector |21> has F0=|22>,F1=q^-1|211>,F2=|31>; E0=0,E1=q^-1|11>,E2=|2>. The transported symmetric standard vector M21 has F0_sym=M22,F1_sym=M211,F2_sym=q^-1 M31; E0_sym=0,E1_sym=M11,E2_sym=q^-1 M2, since J transposes outputs AND reflects colors. The QG normalized crystal residue at21 has f0→22,f1→211,e1→11, and f2=e2=0. In the restricted symmetric model it instead has f0→22,f2→31,e2→2, and f1=e1=0. Raw21 IS a representative of its crystal residue in each model; an ordinary q^-1F coefficient does not refute that fact. Its Chevalley action is not its normalized Kashiwara action.

items.title: The charge-zero level-one crystal through rank four at e = 3
items.statement: At $e=3$, charge $\Lambda_0$, in the symmetric-group convention, the empty component through rank four has exactly the following vertices, one row per rank: rank $0$: $\varnothing$; rank $1$: $(1)$; rank $2$: $(2)$ and $(1,1)$; rank $3$: $(2,1)$ and $(1,1,1)$; rank $4$: $(3,1)$, $(2,2)$, $(2,1,1)$ and $(1,1,1,1)$. These are exactly the $3$-restricted partitions of each size ($1,1,2,2,4$ of them). The cogood-addition arrows staying within ranks0–4 are: $\varnothing\xrightarrow{\tilde f_0}(1)$; $(1)\xrightarrow{\tilde f_1}(2)$, $(1)\xrightarrow{\tilde f_2}(1,1)$; $(2)\xrightarrow{\tilde f_2}(2,1)$; $(1,1)\xrightarrow{\tilde f_1}(1,1,1)$; $(2,1)\xrightarrow{\tilde f_0}(2,2)$, $(2,1)\xrightarrow{\tilde f_2}(3,1)$; $(1,1,1)\xrightarrow{\tilde f_0}(1,1,1,1)$, $(1,1,1)\xrightarrow{\tilde f_1}(2,1,1)$; All other additions from ranks0–3 vanish; additions from rank4 leaving the displayed window are omitted, not declared zero. The good-deletion arrows into the listed ranks are: $(1)\xrightarrow{\tilde e_0}\varnothing$; $(2)\xrightarrow{\tilde e_1}(1)$, $(1,1)\xrightarrow{\tilde e_2}(1)$; $(2,1)\xrightarrow{\tilde e_2}(2)$, $(1,1,1)\xrightarrow{\tilde e_1}(1,1)$; $(2,2)\xrightarrow{\tilde e_0}(2,1)$, $(3,1)\xrightarrow{\tilde e_2}(2,1)$, $(2,1,1)\xrightarrow{\tilde e_1}(1,1,1)$, $(1,1,1,1)\xrightarrow{\tilde e_0}(1,1,1)$. In particular $(2,1)$ has no arrow of residue $1$ in either direction, and $(2,1)\xrightarrow{\tilde f_2}(3,1)$ is the arrow whose conjugate is the QG-6 Fock arrow $\tilde f_1$ from $(2,1)$ to $(2,1,1)$.

items.title: The full Fock space is not automatically the irreducible basic module
items.statement: At e3 the entire F_sym is strictly larger than its cyclic basic module. The shape4 is not3-restricted since4−0≥3; its conjugate is1111 (NOT111), which is not3-regular since part1 has multiplicity4≥3. Both raw M4 in F_sym and |1111> in F_QG are nonzero and are OUTSIDE their respective field basic modules, and their ambient lower global lifts are outside too. The full signature rule remains meaningful on these shapes in the full Fock crystal; for example restricted-model e0(4)=3 is an edge of another component, not a route into the empty component. Modular/basic signature statements restricted to restricted labels do not apply to4 as a basic label.

decline_pages.title: Cyclotomic Hecke and Quiver Hecke Algebras

items.title: Arbitrary-level cyclotomic Hecke, Murphy cell and multipartition Schur modules
items.statement:
Let R be a commutative ring, n≥0, ℓ≥1, and z,U_1,...,U_ℓ units of R. Define H_n by commuting invertible X_1,...,X_n, finite generators T_i satisfying (T_i−z)(T_i+1)=0, the type-A braid/distant relations, T_iX_iT_i=zX_(i+1), distant mixed commutation, and ∏_a(X_1−U_a)=0. For n=0 set H_0=R. The grading variable v is not z. An ℓ-multipartition λ of n is an ordered tuple of partitions; dominance compares every cumulative component/row sum. Fill tλ in component,row,column order. Put a_k=Σ_(b<k)|λ^(b)|, uλ=∏_k∏_(j≤a_k)(X_j−U_k), xλ=Σ_(w∈Sλ)T_w, mλ=xλuλ, Mλ=mλH_n. The row subgroup Sλ stabilizes the rows of tλ. The presentation involution * fixes all X_j,T_i and reverses products. For standard s,t of shapeλ put m_st=T_d(s)*mλT_d(t), where tλd(s)=s. Denote by H^{>λ} the span of higher Murphy shapes once their basis/cell law is established by [[thm-arbitrary-level-cyclotomic-hecke-murphy-basis-is-cellular]], and Sλ the right cell/Specht module with basis m_t and action from that cell law. Its cellular form defines Dλ=Sλ/radSλ; Dλ may vanish.

Types are EXACTLY all ℓ-multipartitions of n, including empty components, not all multicompositions. A semistandard tableau S has labels (row,component) ordered by component then row, weak rows, strict columns, and a label of component a can occur only in physical component b≤a; its type counts each label with the multiplicity of that multipartition row. For a standard s, µ(s) replaces each entry by its row/component in tµ. Set m_(S,t)=Σ_(s:µ(s)=S)m_st and m_(S,T)=Σ_(s,t:µ(s)=S,ν(t)=T)m_st. Define M=⊕_(λ multipartition of n)Mλ and C_n=End_(H_n)(M), with ordinary composition. For S,T of shapeλ and typesµ,ν, the map φ_ST, once justified by [[lem-cyclotomic-semistandard-sums-give-schur-endomorphism-basis]], sends mαh to δ_(α,ν)m_(S,T)h. Its right cell module ∆λ has basis v_T for semistandard T of multipartition types, contravariant cell form and quotient Lλ. Let Tλ be the unique tableau of shape/typeλ, and let eλ be the identity projection onto Mλ. Put ω=(∅,...,∅,(1^n)) and e=eω; mω=1, so Mω=H_n. In particular H_n is an actual direct summand of M. Weight projections for Jantzen theory are eν with ν multipartition. Define K_(λ,ν)=#SStdν(λ). All asserted module/form/map laws are discharged by the linked local theorem/lemma suppliers; the definition itself does not claim their proofs or the primitive residue-content classification.

items.title: Laurent binomial valuation at one over any field
items.statement: For nonzero A,B in F and integers u,v, the valuation of A t^u-B t^v is zero if A!=B. If A=B and N=u-v!=0, it is 1 in characteristic zero, and p^{v_p(|N|)} in characteristic p>0. If A=B and N=0 the polynomial is zero and does not have finite valuation.

items.title: Ultra-tight multisets admit integer column potentials
items.statement: Let $r\ge1$ and $L_r=\mathbb Z^r/\mathbb Z(1,\ldots,1)$. For a finite multiset $X$ in $L_r$, call $X$ tight if $(x_k-x_l)-(y_k-y_l)\le2$ for all occurrences $x,y$ and indices $k,l$. A zero exchange replaces $x,y$ by $x-e_k+e_l,y+e_k-e_l$ when that difference equals2; it is symmetric. Call $X$ ultra-tight if every finite zero-exchange sequence ends in a tight multiset. Then $X$ is ultra-tight iff some $s\in\mathbb Z^r$ satisfies $x_k-x_l\le s_k-s_l+1$ for every $x\in X,k,l$. This includes the empty multiset and $r=1$.

items.title: Affine type-A presentations and charged cyclotomic quotients
items.statement: Let A be a commutative base ring and z a unit. The nondegenerate AFFINE presentation has commuting units X_r and finite generators T_r with T_r²=(z−1)T_r+z, braid/distant relations, T_rX_rT_r=zX_(r+1) and T_rX_s=X_sT_r for s not r,r+1. The degenerate AFFINE presentation over A has commuting x_r and symmetric-group generators s_r, with s_r x_r=x_(r+1)s_r−1, s_r x_(r+1)=x_r s_r+1 and distant mixed commutation. Auxiliary cyclotomic quotients impose a monic polynomial f of degree ℓ only on the first polynomial generator, with unit constant term in NG. Rank zero is A; degree-zero f=1 at positive rank gives zero. For the charged CYCLIC specialization take A=F a field, z=q_H of finite quantum characteristic e>=2, I=Z/eZ an integer LABEL set, λ_i>=0 and ℓ=Σ_iλ_i (a dominant cyclic type-A weight). If q_H!=1 use NG and c_i=q_H^i; if q_H=1 (charF=e) use DG and c_i=i·1_F. Impose f(z_1)=∏_i(z_1−c_i)^{λ_i} to define H^Λ_d. This charged finite-e branch is the native24 scope; the arbitrary-base affine/monic definitions supply its necessary universal PBW/trace proof inputs. No basis, spectrum, primitive blocks or BK isomorphism is asserted by this pure definition. The grading variable v is independent of q_H.

items.title: DVR cellular Jantzen filtration and exact Gram valuation
items.statement: Let O be a DVR with uniformizer pi and residue field F. Let M be a finite free O-module with an O-valued bilinear pairing b whose scalar extension to Frac(O) is nondegenerate. Set M(s)={x:b(x,M) subset pi^s O} and M_F^s=(M(s)+pi M)/pi M. Then M_F^0=M/pi M, M_F^1=rad(b_F), the filtration terminates, and sum_{s>0}dim_F M_F^s=nu_pi(det G) for any Gram matrix G. If A acts on M with anti-involution * and b(ax,y)=b(x,a* y), all M(s), and hence M_F^s, are submodules. If M_F is a cellular standard module with nonzero cellular form, rad(b_F) is its unique maximal submodule and therefore its module radical.

items.title: Universal nondegenerate affine Hecke ordered monomials form a basis
items.statement: For the affine presentation associated to [[def-arbitrary-level-cyclotomic-hecke-murphy-cell-and-schur-modules]] over the universal Laurent parameter ring R, without imposing the first-variable cyclotomic relation, both families X^aT_w and T_wX^a, a∈Z^n,w∈S_n, are R-bases. Left multiplication by any nonzero Laurent polynomial is injective. Localizing at variable differences embeds this algebra into its rational crossed product; Φ_i=T_i−(z−1)X_(i+1)/(X_(i+1)−X_i) obeys Φ_i f=s_i(f)Φ_i. No cyclotomic basis, BK theorem, trace or primitive-content assertion is used.

items.title: Bounded ordered monomials span the cyclotomic Hecke quotients
items.statement:
Over any commutative base ring $A$ with invertible nondegenerate parameter,
use the defining relations of
[[def-type-a-affine-presentations-and-charged-cyclotomic-quotients]], writing
$q_H$ for the nondegenerate Hecke parameter. For a monic cyclotomic polynomial
$f$ of degree $\ell>0$, with unit constant term in the nondegenerate branch,
the quotient by $f(X_1)=0$ is spanned by
$$X_1^{a_1}\cdots X_d^{a_d}T_w,\qquad 0\le a_r<\ell,\ w\in S_d,$$
and the degenerate quotient by $f(x_1)=0$ is spanned by
$$x_1^{a_1}\cdots x_d^{a_d}w,\qquad 0\le a_r<\ell,\ w\in S_d .$$
In particular, over a field $F$ each quotient has dimension at most
$\ell^dd!$. This applies to $f(t)=\prod_{i\in I}(t-q_H^i)^{\lambda_i}$ and
$f(t)=\prod_{i\in I}(t-i)^{\lambda_i}$ in the two finite-quantum-characteristic
branches, with $\ell=\sum_i\lambda_i$. No independence and no separate relation
$f(X_r)=0$ or $f(x_r)=0$ for $r>1$ is asserted. If $\ell=0$ and $d>0$, the
imposed relation $1=0$ gives the zero algebra with empty spanning family; for
$d=0$ the algebra is $A$ with the singleton empty monomial.

items.title: Degenerate affine Hecke ordered monomials form a basis
items.statement: Let $F$ be any field and let $H_d^{\rm deg}$ be the algebra generated by commuting $x_1,\ldots,x_d$ and symmetric-group generators $s_1,\ldots,s_{d-1}$ with $s_rx_r=x_{r+1}s_r-1$, $s_rx_{r+1}=x_rs_r+1$, and $s_rx_j=x_js_r$ for $j\notin\{r,r+1\}$, together with the symmetric-group quadratic, braid and distant commutation relations. Then $\{x_1^{a_1}\cdots x_d^{a_d}w:a_j\ge0,\ w\in S_d\}$ is an $F$-basis. This uses only the degenerate presentation clause of [[def-type-a-affine-presentations-and-charged-cyclotomic-quotients]]; no cyclotomic basis or BK isomorphism is assumed. For $d=0$ the basis is the singleton empty monomial.

items.title: Nonzero-form cellular heads, cell purity and shared-factor linkage
items.statement: For a finite-dimensional cellular algebra over a field F, every nonzero cell-form quotient Dλ is an absolutely simple head, all simples occur exactly once this way, and [Cλ:Dµ]≠0 implies λ≥µ, with [Cµ:Dµ]=1 when Dµ≠0. Nonzero quotient means nonzero form, not necessarily nondegenerate form on Cλ. Every nonzero cell module, including zero-form labels, has all factors in one block. Two cell modules share a block exactly when they are linked by a finite chain of cell modules whose neighboring terms share a simple factor. For one primitive idempotent eµ per simple, dim eµAeν=Σλ[Cλ:Dµ][Cλ:Dν].

items.title: Selfadjoint weight Gram valuations detect Jantzen classes
items.statement:
In Leaf A suppose 1=sum_nu e_nu is a finite decomposition into pairwise orthogonal idempotents of A, with e_nu*=e_nu. Write M_nu=e_nu M and G_nu for the restricted Gram matrix. Then each M_nu is finite free, each restricted generic form is nondegenerate, and

$$\sum_{s>0}\dim_F e_\nu M_F^s=\nu_\pi(\det G_\nu).$$

For a split finite-dimensional highest-weight algebra S_F whose standard classes [Delta(mu)] form a Z-basis of K0, if the matrix K_{mu nu}=dim e_nu Delta(mu) has a square unitriangular submatrix indexed by partition weights, then the weight-character map ch:K0 -> Z^{weights}, [N] -> (dim e_nu N)_nu is injective. It follows that a class equality involving Jantzen pieces is equivalent to the corresponding equalities of weight Gram valuations.

items.title: Symmetric polynomial centers have primitive split content idempotents
items.statement: Let A be a finite-dimensional unital F-algebra, with commuting elements x_1,...,x_d and split joint regular-module generalized-eigenprojectors p_word∈A, pairwise orthogonal and summing to1, with (x_r−word_r)p_word nilpotent. For each finite multiset α of eigenvalues let eα be the sum over words of that multiset, and assume each eα is central. If Z(A) is the image of the symmetric polynomial ring in x_1,...,x_d, then each eα is zero or primitive central, and its nonzero terms are exactly all primitive central idempotents of A. No splitting-simple-module or algebraically closed field hypothesis is required. For d=0 the asserted symmetric-center hypothesis says Z(A)=F·1 and yields the same conclusion.

items.title: Polynomial spectra and central content sectors of finite cyclotomic Hecke algebras
items.statement: Use the charged finite-e FIELD specialization of [[def-type-a-affine-presentations-and-charged-cyclotomic-quotients]], over any field F. H^Λ_d is finite-dimensional before any basis independence argument. Every polynomial generator has a monic annihilator split over the residue values c_i: q_H^i in NG, i·1_F in DG. The canonical finite CRT projectors ε_r(i) and e(ν)=∏_r ε_r(ν_r) are orthogonal, sum to1, and project every finite H-module onto its joint generalized residue spaces. For each α=Σ_i n_i α_i of height d, e_α=Σ_(ν of contentα)e(ν) is central. H is the direct sum of its central ideals e_α H, possibly zero; no primitivity is asserted here. On e(ν), z_r−c_(ν_r) is nilpotent, so all invertible-constant local power series have finite evaluations.

items.title: Central content sectors of the cyclotomic Hecke algebra
items.statement: For the projectors supplied by [[lem-cyclotomic-hecke-polynomial-spectra-and-central-content-sectors]], denote e(ν) the joint residue projector and e_α their sum at contentα. Put H^Λ_α=e_α H^Λ_d=e_α H^Λ_d e_α, with unit e_α; this is a central content SECTOR, possibly zero. Do not assume it is a primitive block at this stage. On it set y_r=Σ_ν(x_r−ν_r)e(ν) in DG, and y_r=Σ_ν(1−q_H^(−ν_r)X_r)e(ν) in NG. These named elements are commuting nilpotents by the declared spectral supplier. Use α=0, e_empty=1, H^Λ_0=F at rankzero. Later primitivity can identify nonzero sectors with blocks without changing these objects.

items.title: Charged core height matrices: content-preserving descent and minimal switch connectivity
items.statement: Fix finite $e\ge2$, $\ell\ge1$ and charges $c_a\in\mathbb Z$. Give nodes of component $a$ residue $c_a+j-i\pmod e$. Write $C_i$ for residue counts and $\delta_i$ for removable minus addable $i$-nodes. Then $\delta_i=2C_i-C_{i-1}-C_{i+1}-m_i$, $m_i=\#\{a:c_a\equiv i\}$, with both neighboring terms retained at $e=2$. Equal hubs and equal size are equivalent to equal content. For componentwise $e$-cores, let $b_{ia}$ be the largest charged beta bead on runner $i$ and $t_{ia}=(b_{ia}-i)/e$. Cores of fixed hub/charges correspond exactly to integer matrices with fixed row sums and column sums $c_a-e$; for two such cores, their size difference is $\frac e2$ times the difference of $\sum t_{ia}^2$. Every nonminimum-size core admits a finite same-hub core-switch path that never increases size and ends at a smaller core. Every pair of minimum-size cores is connected by equal-size switches. A switch subtracts1 at $(i,a),(j,b)$ and adds1 at $(i,b),(j,a)$; each path switch can be oriented with $\gamma=t_{ia}-t_{ib}-t_{ja}+t_{jb}\ge2$, giving size change $-e(\gamma-2)$. Minimum cores exist for every nonempty fixed-hub class.

items.title: Cyclic type-A KLR regular Hom norm gives the total dimension
items.statement: Let $F$ be any field, $I=\mathbb Z/e\mathbb Z$ with finite $e\ge2$, and use the standard homogeneous cyclotomic KLR quotient at $\Lambda=\sum_i\lambda_i\Lambda_i$ for the cyclic affine type-A Cartan datum and admissible graded parameters. Put $\ell=\sum_i\lambda_i$ and $B_d=\bigoplus_{\operatorname{ht}\beta=d}R^\Lambda(\beta)$. Then $\dim_F B_d=\ell^d d!$ for $d>0$, and $B_0=F$ has dimension one. The proof uses the basic first induction-restriction adjunction and mixed relations on projective $K_0$ modulo $v-1$, where $v$ is the formal grading variable, independent of any Hecke parameter $q_H$. No Frobenius theorem, tensor-form perfectness, highest-weight/global-basis isometry or Hecke basis is required. If $\ell=0,d>0$, then $B_d=0$.

items.title: Type-A Hecke permutation modules: semistandard Murphy bases and Specht filtrations
items.statement: For every commutative ring R, invertible z, ordinary finite type-A Hecke algebra H_n and composition ρ of n, xρH_n has R-basis m_(S,t)=Σ_(s:ρ(s)=S)m_st for semistandard partition-shape S of typeρ and standard t of the same shape. It has a Specht filtration with multiplicity #SStdρ(λ) of the ordinary Specht Sλ. The row-double-coset membership uses each coset word once and no quantum-factorial division. Over the generic field this number equals the trivial-character multiplicity of the ρ-row parabolic in Sλ. The explicit ordinary Garnir row-coset identity, additive nonstandard-tableau factorization, and same-column generator refinement T_a m_st≡−m_st+Σ_(u⊲s)c_u m_ut modulo higher shapes hold; row-standard straightening has no smaller-shape terms and its same-shape terms increase tableau-prefix dominance. Shape support uses the already proved ordinary Murphy dominance ideals; the finite Garnir algorithm terminates in lexicographic shape/tableau order before that dominance refinement.

items.title: Cyclotomic Hecke algebras of level one are finite Hecke algebras
items.statement: Let $\Lambda=\Lambda_j$ be a level-one fundamental weight and keep the conventions of [[def-type-a-affine-presentations-and-charged-cyclotomic-quotients]]. Then the assignments $T_r\mapsto T_r$ ($1\le r<d$) in the nondegenerate case and $s_r\mapsto s_r$ in the degenerate case extend to $F$-algebra isomorphisms $H_{F,q}(S_d)\to H^\Lambda_d$ and $FS_d\to H^\Lambda_d$ respectively.

items.title: Affine and cyclotomic type-A Hecke algebras
items.statement:
Let $F$ be a field and $q\in F^{\times}$ with FINITE quantum characteristic $e=e(F,q)$, $2\le e<\infty$, residue set $I=\mathbb Z/e\mathbb Z$ with integer residue labels $0,1,\dots,e-1$; in the nondegenerate branch their distinct spectral values are $q^i$, while in the degenerate branch they are $i\cdot1_F$ (here $e=\operatorname{char}F$), and the cyclic affine type-A Cartan datum with dominant weights $P^+$ and pairing $(\Lambda,\alpha_i)$ ([[def-quantum-characteristic-of-an-invertible-hecke-parameter]], [[def-cyclic-affine-type-a-cartan-datum]]). Fix $\Lambda\in P^+$ of level $\ell=\sum_{i\in I}(\Lambda,\alpha_i)$ and put $\lambda_i:=(\Lambda,\alpha_i)$.

**(NG) Nondegenerate case $q\ne1$.** The affine Hecke algebra of type $A_{d-1}$ at parameter $q$ is the unital $F$-algebra $H_d$ with generators $X_1^{\pm1},\dots,X_d^{\pm1}$, $T_1,\dots,T_{d-1}$ and relations (4.2)-(4.5) of the source: $X_rX_s=X_sX_r$, $X_rX_r^{-1}=1$, $T_rX_rT_r=qX_{r+1}$, $T_rX_s=X_sT_r$ ($s\notin\{r,r+1\}$), $T_r^2=(q-1)T_r+q$, $T_rT_{r+1}T_r=T_{r+1}T_rT_{r+1}$, $T_rT_s=T_sT_r$ ($|r-s|>1$). The **cyclotomic Hecke algebra** is $H^\Lambda_d:=H_d/\langle\prod_{i\in I}(X_1-q^i)^{\lambda_i}\rangle$.

**(DG) Degenerate case $q=1$** (then necessarily $\operatorname{char}F=e>0$). The **degenerate affine Hecke algebra** $H_d$ is the unital $F$-algebra with generators $x_1,\dots,x_d,s_1,\dots,s_{d-1}$ and relations (3.2)-(3.5): $x_rx_s=x_sx_r$, $s_rx_{r+1}=x_rs_r+1$, $s_rx_s=x_ss_r$ ($s\notin\{r,r+1\}$), $s_r^2=1$, braid and distant commutation; its ordered monomials $x_1^{m_1}\cdots x_d^{m_d}w$ form an $F$-basis by [[lem-degenerate-affine-hecke-ordered-monomials-form-a-basis]]. The **degenerate cyclotomic Hecke algebra** is $H^\Lambda_d:=H_d/\langle\prod_{i\in I}(x_1-i)^{\lambda_i}\rangle$.

**Conventions.** $H^\Lambda_0=F$; the cyclotomic polynomial is imposed on the FIRST polynomial generator; $T_r$ acts on positions $r,r+1$. The Hecke parameter is the one of [[def-generic-type-a-hecke-algebra]] ($T_i^2=(q-1)T_i+q$). At level one $\Lambda=\Lambda_j$, $H^\Lambda_d$ is the finite type-A Hecke algebra $H_{F,q}(S_d)$ if $q\ne1$ and the group algebra $FS_d$ if $q=1$ ([[prop-cyclotomic-hecke-algebras-of-level-one-are-finite-hecke-algebras]]). Only finite $e$ is treated: the source's $e=0$ branches ($q$ not a root of unity, and the characteristic-zero degeneration, whose quiver is $A_\infty$) are outside this page's cyclic scope and are deferred in the batch notes. No choice principle is used.

items.title: The type-A cyclotomic specialization of the QG-KLR algebras
items.statement: Let $F,q,e,I,\Lambda,\lambda_i$ be as in [[def-affine-and-cyclotomic-type-a-hecke-algebras]]. On the cyclic affine type-A Cartan datum define the normalized symmetrizers d_i=1 and the type-A KLR datum $Q^{A}$ by $Q^{A}_{ii}=0$, $Q^{A}_{ij}=1$ if $a_{ij}=0$, $Q^{A}_{i,i+1}(u,v)=v-u$ and $Q^{A}_{i+1,i}(u,v)=u-v$ for the two edge orientations when $e\ge3$, and $Q^{A}_{01}(u,v)=Q^{A}_{10}(u,v)=-(u-v)^2$ when $e=2$. Then $Q^{A}$ satisfies (Q1)-(Q4) of [[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]]. Write $R_\alpha$ for the resulting generalised KLR algebra over $F$ and $R^\Lambda_\alpha$ for the STANDARD cyclotomic quotient of [[def-cyclotomic-klr-quotient-at-a-dominant-weight]] (monic first-strand relations $x_1^{\lambda_{i_1}}e(\nu)=0$). With $y_r:=x_r$ and $\psi_r:=-\tau_r$ the relations (1.6)-(1.15) of the source hold in $R^\Lambda_\alpha$, and conversely the quotient presented by those relations is the same algebra; in other words $R^\Lambda_\alpha$ is the sign-modified cyclotomic Khovanov-Lauda algebra of the source for the cyclic quiver of quantum characteristic $e$.

items.title: Cyclotomic Hecke intertwiners and local power series
items.statement: Let $H^\Lambda_\alpha$ be a central content sector (possibly zero) as in [[def-cyclotomic-hecke-central-content-sector-notation]]. (i) Set $y_r:=\sum_{i\in I_\alpha}(x_r-i_r)e(i)$ in the degenerate case and $y_r:=\sum_{i\in I_\alpha}(1-q^{-i_r}X_r)e(i)$ in the nondegenerate case ($1\le r\le d$). Then $y_1,\dots,y_d$ are commuting nilpotent elements of $H^\Lambda_\alpha$; consequently every rational expression displayed below, expanded as a power series in the nilpotent $y$'s, is a finite and well-defined element of $H^\Lambda_\alpha$. (ii) The power series $p_r(i):=1$ if $i_r=i_{r+1}$ and $p_r(i):=(i_r-i_{r+1}+y_r-y_{r+1})^{-1}$ otherwise (degenerate case), resp. $P_r(i):=1$ if $i_r=i_{r+1}$ and $P_r(i):=(1-q)(1-y_r(i)y_{r+1}(i)^{-1})^{-1}$ with $y_r(i):=q^{i_r}(1-y_r)$ otherwise (nondegenerate case), satisfy (3.23)-(3.25) resp. (4.24)-(4.26), (4.28)-(4.30) and (4.32); and the intertwining elements $\varphi_r:=\sum_i(s_r+p_r(i))e(i)$, resp. $\Phi_r:=\sum_i(T_r+P_r(i))e(i)$, satisfy all identities (3.14)-(3.20) of [BK Lemma 3.1], resp. (4.14)-(4.20) of [BK Lemma 4.1]. (iii) There exist invertible power series $q_r(i)\in F[[y_r,y_{r+1}]]$ (resp. $Q_r(i)$) satisfying (3.27)-(3.29), resp. (4.33)-(4.35); the explicit candidates (3.30) resp. (4.36) do, and for them the identity (3.43) resp. (4.44) holds.

items.title: The cyclotomic KLR block satisfies the Hecke relations
items.statement: In the specialized cyclotomic KLR content algebra $R^\Lambda_\alpha$ define $x_r:=\sum_{i\in I_\alpha}(y_r+i_r)e(i)$ and $s_r:=\sum_{i\in I_\alpha}(\psi_rq_r(i)-p_r(i))e(i)$ (degenerate case), resp. $X_r:=\sum_{i\in I_\alpha}q^{i_r}(1-y_r)e(i)$ and $T_r:=\sum_{i\in I_\alpha}(\psi_rQ_r(i)-P_r(i))e(i)$ (nondegenerate case), where $p,P,q,Q$ are the power series of [[lem-cyclotomic-hecke-intertwiners-and-local-power-series]] evaluated in $R^\Lambda_\alpha$ using the nilpotence of the $y$'s. Then these elements satisfy the defining relations (3.2)-(3.5), resp. (4.2)-(4.5), of the affine Hecke algebra and the cyclotomic relation $\prod_i(x_1-i)^{\lambda_i}=0$, resp. $\prod_i(X_1-q^i)^{\lambda_i}=0$; hence they define a unique $F$-algebra homomorphism $\sigma:H^\Lambda_d\to R^\Lambda_\alpha$. Moreover $\sigma$ kills $e_\beta$ and every corner component $e_\beta H^\Lambda_de_\gamma$ with $(\beta,\gamma)\ne(\alpha,\alpha)$, and restricts to a unital homomorphism $\sigma:H^\Lambda_\alpha\to R^\Lambda_\alpha$ with $\sigma(e(i))=e(i)$ for $i\in I_\alpha$ and $\sigma(e(i))=0$ otherwise.

items.title: Hecke intertwiners produce the local KLR generators
items.statement: Let $H^\Lambda_\alpha$ be a central content sector, possibly zero, as in [[def-cyclotomic-hecke-central-content-sector-notation]] and let $y_r$ be the elements of [[lem-cyclotomic-hecke-intertwiners-and-local-power-series]]. Put $\psi_r:=\sum_{i\in I_\alpha}\varphi_rq_r(i)^{-1}e(i)$ (degenerate case) resp. $\psi_r:=\sum_{i\in I_\alpha}\Phi_rQ_r(i)^{-1}e(i)$ (nondegenerate case). Then the elements $\{e(i):i\in I_\alpha\}\cup\{y_1,\dots,y_d\}\cup\{\psi_1,\dots,\psi_{d-1}\}$ of $H^\Lambda_\alpha$ satisfy the relations (1.6)-(1.15) of the sign-modified cyclotomic KLR presentation. Consequently there is a unique $F$-algebra homomorphism $\rho:R^\Lambda_\alpha\to H^\Lambda_\alpha$ with $e(i)\mapsto e(i)$, $y_r\mapsto y_r$ and $\psi_r\mapsto\psi_r$.

items.title: Cyclotomic Hecke central sectors are isomorphic to type-A cyclotomic KLR algebras
items.statement: Over any field F in the charged finite-e conventions, the explicit maps ρ:R^Λ_α→H^Λ_α and σ:H^Λ_α→R^Λ_α from the preceding forward and inverse relation lemmas are mutually inverse, for every content α, including zero sectors. Here H^Λ_α is only the central CRT content sector; no primitivity is assumed. Thus H^Λ_α=0 iff R^Λ_α=0, and summing over finite height-d contents gives H^Λ_d≅⊕_α R^Λ_α. On idempotents the maps are literal identity, and the dot image is x_r−i_r (DG) or 1−q_H^(−i_r)X_r (NG). This result precedes the late dimension/basis and primitive-block theorems. No algebraic closure hypothesis is required.

items.title: Basis and dimension of the cyclotomic Hecke algebra
items.statement: With the conventions of [[def-affine-and-cyclotomic-type-a-hecke-algebras]], the images of the ordered monomials $x_1^{m_1}\cdots x_d^{m_d}w$ with $0\le m_r<\ell$, $w\in S_d$ (degenerate case) respectively $X_1^{m_1}\cdots X_d^{m_d}T_w$ with $0\le m_r<\ell$, $w\in S_d$ (nondegenerate case) form an $F$-basis of $H^\Lambda_d$. In particular $\dim_F H^\Lambda_d=\ell^d d!$ and $H^\Lambda_d$ is finite dimensional. For d=0 the singleton empty word gives H^Λ_0=F and dimension one independently of ℓ. If ℓ=0 and d>0 the relation 1=0 gives the zero algebra and empty basis; no ambiguous 0^0 convention is used.

items.title: Universal cyclotomic Hecke ordered monomials form a basis
items.statement: For R=Z[z^(±1),U_1^(±1),...,U_ℓ^(±1)], ℓ>=1, the actual nondegenerate cyclotomic presentation at first polynomial ∏_a(X_1−U_a) is free with indexed R-basis X^a T_w, 0<=a_r<ℓ,w∈S_n. This basis specializes to every commutative R-algebra. Rankzero is R with singleton empty word. The separate levelzero positive-rank quotient is zero with empty family.

items.title: The degenerate cyclotomic Hecke center is the symmetric polynomial image
items.statement: Let $F$ be any field of characteristic $e>0$, with $e\ge2$, and let $H_d^\Lambda$ be the degenerate cyclotomic Hecke algebra with the FIRST relation $f(x_1)=\prod_{i\in\mathbb Z/e\mathbb Z}(x_1-i)^{\lambda_i}=0$, $\lambda_i\ge0$ and $\ell=\sum_i\lambda_i\ge1$. Then $Z(H_d^\Lambda)$ is exactly the image of $F[t_1,\ldots,t_d]^{S_d}$ under $t_r\mapsto x_r$. The proof is over the original F, for every d≥0 and level ℓ, and does not divide by ℓ or d!. The required degree filtration is proved from the independent late bounded field basis and the transported degree-decreasing cyclotomic relations.

items.title: The universal cyclotomic Hecke canonical trace is perfect and symmetric
items.statement: For the preceding universal cyclotomic presentation, extract coefficient of the zero-dot identity-permutation PBW word to define τ. Then τ(ab)=τ(ba) and (a,b)↦τ(ab) is a perfect R-bilinear associative pairing. Both properties hold after every commutative unit-parameter base change, including the LM DVR. Rankzero is R with τ(1)=1_R. For the separate levelzero positive-rank zero algebra the zero pairing is perfect; no nonzero trace1 assertion is made.

items.title: The arbitrary-level cyclotomic Hecke Murphy basis is cellular
items.statement: For H_n in [[def-arbitrary-level-cyclotomic-hecke-murphy-cell-and-schur-modules]] over the universal Laurent parameter ring, the m_st indexed by all ℓ-multipartitions of n and standard s,t are a basis and a dominance-cellular datum: m_st*=m_ts and m_sth≡Σ_v r_(t,v)(h)m_sv modulo higher shapes, with coefficients independent of s. The higher spans are actual two-sided ideals. Every commutative specialization with unit parameters inherits this cellular basis. In particular arbitrary-field finite-e charged specializations and the LM DVR retain the result. Its universal rank is supplied independently by [[lem-universal-cyclotomic-hecke-ordered-monomials-form-a-basis]], not by a primitive-block classification.

items.title: Arbitrary-level Murphy Jucys–Murphy action is content triangular
items.statement:
On the Specht module $S_\lambda$ of
[[def-arbitrary-level-cyclotomic-hecke-murphy-cell-and-schur-modules]], $X_r$
acts dominance-triangularly with diagonal $U_az^{j-i}$ at the node $(i,j,a)$
carrying $r$. Over a field with $z=q_H$ of finite order $e\ge2$ and
$U_a=q_H^{c_a}$, every simultaneous generalized eigenword of $S_\lambda$ is
among the standard-tableau residue words $c_a+j-i$ modulo $e$; every such word
has the fixed node-residue multiplicities of $\lambda$. The universal
triangularity also specializes to the LM deformation DVR and the generic
fibre, with no semisimplicity or affine-center premise.

items.title: Cyclotomic semistandard row-type sums give permutation-module bases
items.statement: For H_n in [[def-arbitrary-level-cyclotomic-hecke-murphy-cell-and-schur-modules]] and every multipartition typeµ, Mµ=mµH_n has basis m_(S,t), S semistandard of arbitrary multipartition shapeλ/typeµ and t standard of shapeλ. This holds over the universal Laurent parameter ring and every commutative specialization. Each sum has a disjoint coefficient1 Murphy pivot, so Mµ is an R-direct summand of H_n. In the affine algebra the proof explicitly constructs h with m_(S,t)=mµh, without quantum-factorial or parameter-difference division. Its Specht filtration is ordered by higher shapes and contains one copy of Sλ per semistandard S. No basis is inferred from generic flatness.

items.title: Cyclotomic semistandard sums give the actual Schur endomorphism basis
items.statement: For the actual multipartition-summand C_n in [[def-arbitrary-level-cyclotomic-hecke-murphy-cell-and-schur-modules]], evaluation identifies Hom_H(Mν,Mµ) with Mµ∩H mν, with basis m_(S,T). The maps φ_ST are actual well-defined endomorphisms and form a free dominance-cellular basis, φ_ST*=φ_TS and φ_STφ≡Σ_W r_(T,W)(φ)φ_SW modulo higher shapes independently of S. Formation of this basis and its constants specializes to every commutative unit-parameter base, including the LM DVR. The proof uses the perfect symmetric trace [[lem-universal-cyclotomic-hecke-canonical-trace-is-perfect-and-symmetric]] and the codomain direct-summand pivots [[lem-cyclotomic-semistandard-row-type-sums-give-permutation-module-bases]], with no field-only double-annihilator or nonsaturated-lattice argument.

items.title: Cyclotomic Schur standards and corner functor control block linkage
items.statement: For C_n=End_H(⊕_(λ multipartition)mλH) in [[def-arbitrary-level-cyclotomic-hecke-murphy-cell-and-schur-modules]], over every field F with unit parameters, its standards ∆λ have nonzero absolutely simple heads Lλ indexed by all multipartitions, [∆λ:Lλ]=1 and [∆λ:Lµ]≠0 only if λ≥µ; C_n is split quasihereditary. Its standard classes form a Z-basis of G_0 and weight dimensions dim ∆λeν=K_(λ,ν) give a unitriangular multipartition Kostka matrix. Over the universal ring/DVR the standards and forms are free and eν*=eν. The exact corner functor V↦Veω gives ∆λeω≅Sλ and Lλeω≅Dλ (possibly0), so [∆λ:Lµ]=[Sλ:Dµ] for Dµ≠0. The centers Z(C_n) and Z(H_n) are canonically isomorphic because Mω=H_n is a summand, and ∆λ,∆µ share a C_n-block iff Sλ,Sµ share an H_n-block. Standard/Specht linkage is exactly shared-simple-factor linkage. No equality-of-residue-contents ⇒ primitive-block assertion is included.

items.title: Generic cyclotomic Schur deformation standards have nondegenerate forms
items.statement: Over the fraction field of the universal Laurent parameter ring, all cyclotomic Specht modules are simple and H_n is split semisimple; all Schur standards ∆λ equal Lλ and have nondegenerate cellular forms. Also fix N≥1 and any field F with nonzero q_H,Q_a; for 0≤d≤N take O=F[t,t^(-1)]_(t−1), z=q_Ht, U_a=Q_at^(Na). Over F(t), all rank-d Specht/Schur standards are simple and their forms nondegenerate. This includes the charged finite-e specialization used by LM. It establishes generic nondegeneracy only, not any signed rim-hook weight-Gram determinant valuation formula.

items.title: Cyclotomic Schur weight Gram determinants are products of monic semistandard norms
items.statement: Use the actual arbitrary-level Murphy/Schur datum over the universal Laurent ring and generic field, or LM deformation z=q_Ht,U_a=Q_at^(na) over ANY field F. For every shape λ and ACTUAL multipartition Schur weight ν, det Gλν=∏_(T∈SStdν(λ))γ_tT/(C_tT u_T), empty determinant1. Here tT is the dominance-MINIMAL refinement, C_t=∏_(i<j in same type row)(z r_t(j)−r_t(i))/(r_t(j)−r_t(i)), and u_T=∏_x∏_(b>typecomponent_T(x))(r_x−U_b). The monic transition determinant is exactly1. The initialγ and adjacent standard-swap recurrence, and its equivalent explicit boundary/C/R node-pair norm product, are defined and proved in the strategy. All factors are nonzero in the stated generic fields; no quantum factorial is inverted in the O-lattice. Arbitrary-composition series are auxiliary only.

items.title: Cyclotomic Schur weight Gram valuations equal signed rim-hook Kostka sums
items.statement: For ANY field F, arbitrary level ℓ>=1, q_H∈F^× of finite order e≥2, charges Q_a=q_H^(c_a), fixed n≥0, O=F[t,t^−1]_(t−1), z=q_Ht,U_a=Q_at^(na), and every shape λ and ACTUAL multipartition Schur weight ν, V(det Gλν)=ΣµJλµKµν. Jλµ=0 unless λ strictly dominates µ; otherwise it is the sum over equal-length rim hooks removed from λ and µ to the SAME remainder, with sign (−1)^(leg λ+leg µ) and valuation V(res_O(foot λ)−res_O(foot µ)). Every difference is nonzero in F(t). The full signed marked-strip commutator and auxiliary coefficient identity are proved locally; arbitrary-composition coefficients are combinatorial only, not extra Schur modules.

items.title: Cyclotomic Schur Jantzen sum formula from rim-hook valuations
items.statement:
Let F be any field, q_H in F^× have finite multiplicative order e>=2, ell>=1 be arbitrary, and Q_a=q_H^(c_a), with charges c_a in Z. Fix n>=0 and let S_F be the cyclotomic q-Schur algebra with summands indexed by all ell-multipartitions of n. Put

$$O=F[t,t^{-1}]_{(t-1)},\quad \pi=t-1,\quad K=F(t),\quad z=q_Ht,\quad U_a=Q_at^{na}.$$

Let Delta_O(lambda) be its standard Weyl lattice with its actual cellular form. Define

$$\Delta_O(\lambda)(s)=\{v:\langle v,\Delta_O(\lambda)\rangle\subseteq\pi^sO\},\qquad\Delta_F(\lambda)^s=(\Delta_O(\lambda)(s)+\pi\Delta_O(\lambda))/\pi\Delta_O(\lambda).$$

Then this is a filtration by S_F-submodules, its first term is rad Delta_F(lambda), it terminates, and in the INTEGER Grothendieck group of finite-dimensional S_F-modules,

$$\sum_{s>0}[\Delta_F(\lambda)^s]=\sum_{\mu}J_{\lambda\mu}[\Delta_F(\mu)].$$

For a node x=(i,j,a), define the rim hook r_x^lambda and foot f_x^lambda=(lambda'_j,j,a) as in LM, leg(r_x^lambda)=lambda'_j-i, and res_O(i,j,a)=U_a z^(j-i). If lambda strictly dominates mu, set

$$J_{\lambda\mu}=\sum_{\substack{x\in[\lambda],\ y\in[\mu]\\[\lambda]\setminus r_x^\lambda=[\mu]\setminus r_y^\mu}}(-1)^{\operatorname{leg}(r_x^\lambda)+\operatorname{leg}(r_y^\mu)}\nu_\pi\big(\operatorname{res}_O(f_x^\lambda)-\operatorname{res}_O(f_y^\mu)\big);$$

otherwise set J_(lambda mu)=0. Equal remainder diagrams force equal hook lengths. Every displayed difference is nonzero in K, including samecomponent terms with distinct labels, by the local foot-exponent separation proof. No level-one or characteristic-zero restriction is present.

items.title: Cyclotomic Jantzen equivalence is Schur and Hecke block linkage
Multipartitions with fixed component cores are cyclotomic Jantzen-connected
items.statement:
Under the arbitrary-field finite-$e$ nondegenerate cyclotomic hypotheses of
[[lem-cyclotomic-jantzen-equivalence-is-schur-and-hecke-block-linkage]], any
two $\ell$-multipartitions of a common rank $n$ with equal componentwise
$e$-cores are $J$-equivalent, even if their component sizes differ. At fixed
component sizes, the full-level coefficient for a change in a single
component equals its level-one coefficient. The proof consumes the actual
same-$e$-core Hecke Specht block theorem for all ranks
([[cor-type-a-hecke-specht-modules-are-in-the-same-block-iff-their-labels-have-the-same-e-core]])
rather than a readiness receipt, and imports no Carter-partition
classification.

items.title: Cyclotomic multipartitions have equal residue content exactly when Jantzen-connected
items.statement: Let $F$ be any field, $q_H\in F^\times$ have finite order $e\ge2$ with $q_H\ne1$, let $\ell\ge1$ and $Q_a=q_H^{c_a}$. For all $\ell$-multipartitions $\lambda,\mu$ of rank $n\ge0$, the node-residue contents $C_i(\lambda)=\#\{(r,s,a)\in[\lambda]:c_a+s-r\equiv i\pmod e\}$ agree for every $i\in\mathbb Z/e\mathbb Z$ iff $\lambda\sim_J\mu$ for the exact integer Jantzen coefficients of [[thm-cyclotomic-schur-jantzen-sum-formula-from-rim-hook-valuations]]. This includes arbitrary levels and all field characteristics.

items.title: Central content sectors are zero or primitive cyclotomic Hecke blocks
items.statement: Let F be any field and q_H∈F× have finite quantum characteristic e≥2. Use the standard cyclotomic type-A Hecke presentation, level ℓ=Σ_iλ_i≥0, imposed on the FIRST polynomial variable, with λ_i≥0 and I=Z/eZ. For q_H≠1 the roots are q_H^i and q_H has order e; for q_H=1, char F=e>0 and the roots are the prime-field residues i. Use only the early central CRT notation of [[def-cyclotomic-hecke-central-content-sector-notation]] and [[lem-cyclotomic-hecke-polynomial-spectra-and-central-content-sectors]]. For every content α of rank d, eα=Σ_(word contentα)e(word) is either zero or a primitive central idempotent. The nonzero eα are exactly all primitive central idempotents, so H_d^Λ=⊕_α eαH_d^Λ is precisely the block decomposition. At d=0 the unique sector is F, regardless of level; at d>0,ℓ=0 the algebra is zero. This is an arbitrary-level result over the original field in both branches.

items.title: Residue-sequence idempotents and cyclotomic Hecke blocks
items.statement:
Use the charged finite-e field conventions of [[def-affine-and-cyclotomic-type-a-hecke-algebras]]. By [[lem-cyclotomic-hecke-polynomial-spectra-and-central-content-sectors]], H^Λ_d is finite-dimensional and each minimal polynomial of z_r=X_r (NG) or x_r (DG) splits over c_i=q_H^i or i·1_F. Let ε_r(i) be its canonical CRT primary idempotent (zero for an absent root), and e(ν)=∏_r ε_r(ν_r). On every finite H-module it projects onto the joint generalized residue space. These mutually orthogonal idempotents sum to1. At content α put e_α=Σ_(ν∈I_α)e(ν); it is central, and H^Λ_d is the direct sum of its central ideals H^Λ_α=e_αH^Λ_d=e_αH^Λ_de_α. By [[thm-cyclotomic-hecke-central-content-sectors-are-zero-or-primitive-blocks]], every nonzero e_α is primitive, so every nonzero H^Λ_α is an actual block. This rich block claim is proved, not retained as an unused citation.

At level one Λ=Λ_j, the polynomial generators correspond under the explicit finite-Hecke inverse to X_r=q_H^j(1+(q_H−1)L_r) in NG and x_r=j+L_r in DG, where L_r is the ordinary additive JM element. Thus on a standard tableau node of content m their eigenvalues are q_H^(j+m) and j+m; L_r itself has additive q-content [m]_(q_H). The nonzero joint projectors are precisely the residue words of standard tableaux, and grouping those words by content gives the block labels. At rankzero the empty projector is1 and the unique block is F; at levelzero positive rank all projectors and blocks are zero.

items.title: The Brundan–Kleshchev blockwise Hecke–KLR isomorphism
items.statement:
Let $F$ be any field, $q\in F^{	imes}$ with finite quantum characteristic $e=e(F,q)\ge2$, $\Lambda\in P^+$ dominant, and $\alpha\in Q_+$ of height $d$ with $e_\alpha
e0$ (the conventions of [[def-affine-and-cyclotomic-type-a-hecke-algebras]] and [[def-residue-sequence-idempotents-and-cyclotomic-hecke-blocks]]). Then the homomorphisms $ho:R^\Lambda_\alpha	o H^\Lambda_\alpha$ of [[lem-hecke-intertwiners-produce-local-klr-generators]] and $\sigma:H^\Lambda_\alpha	o R^\Lambda_\alpha$ of [[lem-cyclotomic-klr-block-satisfies-the-hecke-relations]] are mutually inverse $F$-algebra isomorphisms. Equivalently, $H^\Lambda_\alpha$ is generated by the Khovanov-Lauda generators $\{e(i)\}\cup\{y_r\}\cup\{\psi_r\}$ subject only to the relations (1.6)-(1.15), and the isomorphism is normalised by $ho(e(i))=e(i)$ and $ho(y_re(i))=(1-q^{-i_r}X_r)e(i)$ if $q
e1$, resp. $ho(y_re(i))=(x_r-i_r)e(i)$ if $q=1$. The degenerate ($q=1$, $\operatorname{char}F=e$) and nondegenerate ($q
e1$) cases are proved separately and both hold in finite quantum characteristic $e$.

items.title: Cyclotomic Hecke blocks inherit a nontrivial Z-grading
items.statement: In the situation of [[thm-brundan-kleshchev-blockwise-hecke-klr-isomorphism]], each fixed choice of admissible local normalising series transports the KLR homogeneous decomposition to a Z-grading on H^Λ_α. This is the unique grading for those fixed generator images with deg e(i)=0, deg y_r=2 and deg ψ_r e(i)=−a_(i_r,i_(r+1)). Different admissible series choices give graded-isomorphic transported algebras via ρ′∘ρ^(-1); their underlying identity map need not be graded. The grading can be nontrivial, but it may be trivial on an individual block, including the one-dimensional level-one rank-two e=3 blocks. The ordinary Hecke presentation always has the trivial assignment of degree zero to all its generators. The transported grading is generally expressed using the nilpotent dots and local crossings; ordinary Hecke generators can be sums of different homogeneous pieces, and may be homogeneous in special cases. No claim forbids the degree-zero assignment or asserts every block grading is nontrivial.
