items.title: Homogeneous degree check for the corrected KLR braid relation
items.statement: In the specialized cyclotomic KLR algebra of [[def-type-a-cyclotomic-specialization-of-the-qg-klr-algebras]] with the grading $\deg e(i)=0$, $\deg y_r=2$, $\deg\psi_re(i)=-a_{i_r,i_{r+1}}$, fix a triple $i=(i_r,i_{r+1},i_{r+2})$ and put $d(i):=-a_{i_ri_{r+1}}-a_{i_ri_{r+2}}-a_{i_{r+1}i_{r+2}}$ (the degree of both three-crossing words $\psi_r\psi_{r+1}\psi_re(i)$ and $\psi_{r+1}\psi_r\psi_{r+1}e(i)$, computed on the successive permuted colour pairs). Then both sides of (1.15) are homogeneous of degree $d(i)$ and the correction term has the same degree: it is $\pm1$ (degree $0$) when $i_{r+2}=i_r\to i_{r+1}$ or $i_{r+2}=i_r\leftarrow i_{r+1}$, it is $y_r+y_{r+2}-2y_{r+1}$ (degree $2$) when $i_{r+2}=i_r\rightleftarrows i_{r+1}$ (the $e=2$ double edge), and it is $0$ otherwise. In particular the single-edge corrected braid relations have degree $0$ and the $e=2$ double-edge corrected braid relation has degree $2$; both match the two sides.

items.title: The degenerate level-one Hecke–KLR map for S_3
items.statement: Work over $F=\mathbb F_3$ with $q=1$ (so $e=3$), $\Lambda=\Lambda_0$ (level one) and $d=3$: then $H^\Lambda_3\cong \mathbb F_3S_3$ and exactly one block is nonzero, namely $\alpha=\alpha_0+\alpha_1+\alpha_2$ with $e_\alpha=1$. The residue sequences realised by standard tableaux all have residue multiset $\{0,1,2\}$. The degenerate KLR generators are the elements $y_r=\sum_i(x_r-i_r)e(i)$ with $x_r$ the Jucys-Murphy elements of $\mathbb F_3S_3$ (so $x_1=0$, $x_2=(12)$, $x_3=(13)+(23)$), and $\psi_r=\sum_i\varphi_rq_r(i)^{-1}e(i)$ with $\varphi_r=s_r+p_r(i)$ and $p_r(i)=(i_r-i_{r+1}+y_r-y_{r+1})^{-1}$ on unequal components. In this block the mixed relations $\psi_1y_2e(i)=y_1\psi_1e(i)+e(i)$ for $i_1=i_2$ and $\psi_1y_2e(i)=y_1\psi_1e(i)$ for $i_1\ne i_2$, and the quadratic relation $\psi_1^2e(i)=(y_2-y_1)e(i)$ for $i_1\to i_2$, are explicit identities in the six-dimensional algebra $\mathbb F_3S_3$.

items.title: The level-one rank-two cyclotomic KLR algebra at e=3
items.statement:
Let $F$ be algebraically closed of characteristic $
e3$, let $q\in F^{	imes}$ be a primitive cube root of unity (so $e=3$), $\Lambda=\Lambda_0$ (level one) and $d=2$. Then: (i) for $i=(i_1,i_2)\in I^2$ the cyclotomic relation is $y_1^{\delta_{i_1,0}}e(i)=0$; thus $y_1e(i)=0$ for the three sequences with $i_1=0$, and $e(i)=0$ for all six sequences with $i_1
e0$, because their exponent is zero and $y_1^0e(i)=e(i)$; (ii) $\psi_1^2e(i)$ equals $0$ if $i_1=i_2$, equals $(y_2-y_1)e(i)$ if $i_2=i_1+1$ and equals $(y_1-y_2)e(i)$ if $i_2=i_1-1$; for $e=3$ these are all cases; (iii) the nonzero blocks of $H^\Lambda_2$ are exactly $H^\Lambda_{\alpha_0+\alpha_1}$ and $H^\Lambda_{\alpha_0+\alpha_2}$; both are one dimensional, with $e((0,1))
e0$ in the first (the block of the trivial module of $H_{F,q}(S_2)$) and $e((0,2))
e0$ in the second (the block of the sign module); the other four $\alpha$-blocks of height $2$ are zero.

items.title: The whole affine Hecke algebra is not one cyclotomic KLR block
items.statement: For a fixed content-block isomorphism, replacing one side by the whole affine algebra, or by the whole cyclotomic quotient in the example below, fails. This does not forbid summing all the central-sector isomorphisms on BOTH sides: (i) the affine Hecke algebra $H_1$ is $F[x_1^{\pm1}]$ resp. $F[x_1]$, hence infinite dimensional, while every cyclotomic block $H^\Lambda_\alpha$ is finite dimensional of dimension $\le\ell^dd!$; (ii) even after imposing the cyclotomic relation, a single residue-content idempotent $e_\alpha$ cuts out a proper factor: at level one with $d=2$, $e=3$ and $q$ a primitive cube root, $H^\Lambda_2\cong H_{F,q}(S_2)\cong F\times F$ has two nonzero blocks $H^\Lambda_{\alpha_0+\alpha_1}$ and $H^\Lambda_{\alpha_0+\alpha_2}$, so $H^\Lambda_2$ is not isomorphic to either one of them, and on the KLR side $R^\Lambda_2=R^\Lambda_{\alpha_0+\alpha_1}\oplus R^\Lambda_{\alpha_0+\alpha_2}$ is not isomorphic to a single block.

items.title: The domination order on tableaux, Garnir tableaux and bricks
items.statement:
Retain English Young diagrams, an $l$-multicomposition $\mu$ of $d$, its
diagram, and the row-reading initial standard tableau $t^\mu$, in which
$1,2,\dots,d$ appear in order along the successive rows from top to bottom
([[def-partition-young-diagram-and-conjugate-partition]]); for a single
component this is the standard tableau of
[[def-young-tableau-standard-tableau-and-shape]]. A $\mu$-tableau $T$ is a
placement of $1,\dots,d$ in the nodes of $\mu$. It is **row-strict** if its
entries increase from left to right in every row of every component, and
**standard** if it is row- and column-strict. The group $S_d$ acts on tableaux
by its action on entries, and for a $\mu$-tableau $T$ the permutation $w_T$ is
defined by $w_Tt^\mu=T$. The **strong Bruhat order** on tableaux is
$$S\le_BT\quad:\Longleftrightarrow\quad w_S\le w_T$$
in the Bruhat order of [[def-bruhat-order-on-the-symmetric-group]], identified
with its one-based realization as in
[[lem-bruhat-order-basic-properties-for-permutations]]. We write $S\unlhd T$
for $S\le_BT$ and $S\lhd T$ for strict order; the separately declared meaning
of $\unrhd$ on partitions ([[def-dominance-order-on-partitions]]) is not
reused for tableaux. On row-strict $S,T$ the order $\unlhd$ is equivalent to
the prefix-shape comparison
$$\operatorname{sh}(S^{\le a})\unrhd\operatorname{sh}(T^{\le a})\quad\text{for every }a,$$
where $T^{\le a}$ erases the nodes occupied by entries $>a$ and
$\operatorname{sh}$ records the resulting row lengths read in row-reading
order; this row-sequence dominance is distinct from the weak Bruhat order and
must not be reversed. The transposition criterion is
$$S=(a_1\,b_1)\cdots(a_m\,b_m)T$$
with $a_n<b_n$ and $b_n$ occupying an earlier row-reading node than $a_n$ in
$(a_{n+1}\,b_{n+1})\cdots(a_m\,b_m)T$ for each $n$.

For entries $r,s$ of one component define $r\to_Ts$ if they lie in the same row
and $s$ is strictly to the right of $r$; $r\downarrow_Ts$ if they lie in the
same column and $s$ is strictly below $r$; and $r\nearrow_Ts$ if $s$ is
strictly above and strictly right of $r$ (south-west is the reverse of
$\nearrow_T$). A **weak Bruhat graph edge** $T\xrightarrow{r}S$ requires both
tableaux standard, $S=s_rT$, and $r$ occupying an earlier row-reading node
than $r+1$. Equivalently $r+1\nearrow_Tr$, or $r$ lies in an earlier component
than $r+1$. In particular a same-row or same-column swap is NOT a standard
edge. A **terminal path** is a directed path in this graph, and $T$ is
$(r_1,\dots,r_m)$-**terminal** if there are standard tableaux
$S_1\xrightarrow{r_1}S_2\xrightarrow{r_2}\cdots\xrightarrow{r_m}T$.

The **Garnir belt** at a node $(a,b,n)$ with $(a+1,b,n)$ also a node of $\mu$
consists of the nodes $(a,c,n)$ for $b\le c\le\mu_a$ and the nodes
$(a+1,g,n)$ for $1\le g\le b$. The **Garnir tableau** of shape $\mu$ at
$(a,b,n)$ is the unique maximal standard $\mu$-tableau in the order $\unlhd$
among the standard $\mu$-tableaux agreeing with $t^\mu$ outside the
$(a,b,n)$-Garnir belt; it equals $t^\mu$ in the degenerate case
$b=1=\mu_a$. A **horizontal brick** is a string of consecutive entries along
same-row right arrows. For the vertical exceptional-prefix and terminal assertions assume that
$\mu$ is a multipartition; the rank, prefix-order and row-sorting assertions
allow multicompositions. The following source facts are retained with these
exact conventions and are proved below: the transposition criterion and the
prefix-shape criterion; the row-strictness of a vertical consecutive swap and
its exceptional-prefix comparison; agreement outside the Garnir belt for
tableaux below a Garnir tableau; and the four terminal alternatives for a
horizontal or vertical consecutive pair, the last alternative being $t^\mu$
for a horizontal pair and the corresponding Garnir tableau for a vertical
pair. No choice.

items.title: Generic nondegenerate local inverse tables on integer colors
items.statement:
Work over a field $k$ of characteristic zero, with $q\in k^\times$ of infinite multiplicative order, integer colors, and the arrows $a\to a+1$. On any finite permutation-stable set of color words, complete the dot ring at the zero dots. The completed local affine Hecke presentation at spectral words $(q^{i_1},\ldots,q^{i_d})$ and the completed type-$A_\infty$ KLR presentation have mutually inverse changes of generators below. This is a local statement; it does not assert cyclotomic support, a tower comparison, or a Specht dictionary.

Write $x=q^a(1-u)$, $z=q^b(1-v)$ and set
$$P_{ab}(u,v)=\begin{cases}1&a=b,\\(1-q)/(1-x/z)&a\ne b,\end{cases}$$
$$Q_{ab}(u,v)=\begin{cases}1-q+qv-u&a=b,\\-q^a/(x-z)&a=b+1,\\(x-qz)/(x-z)&a\ne b,\ a\ne b+1.\end{cases}$$
These are explicit, invertible, rank-independent power series over $k$; in particular the result applies over $\mathbb C$. Use $y_r=1-q^{-i_r}X_r$ on $e(i)$ and the source convention $\psi_r=-\tau_r$, where $\tau$ is the native crossing. The changes of generators are
$$\psi_re(i)=(T_r+P_{i_ri_{r+1}}(y_r,y_{r+1}))Q_{i_ri_{r+1}}(y_r,y_{r+1})^{-1}e(i),$$
$$X_re(i)=q^{i_r}(1-y_r)e(i),\qquad T_re(i)=(\psi_rQ_{i_ri_{r+1}}(y_r,y_{r+1})-P_{i_ri_{r+1}}(y_r,y_{r+1}))e(i).$$
The quadratic polynomial is $K_{aa}=0$, $K_{a,a+1}(u,v)=v-u$, $K_{a+1,a}(u,v)=u-v$, and $K_{ab}=1$ otherwise. The exact equal-color dot moves are $\psi_ru-v\psi_r=-1$ and $\psi_rv-u\psi_r=1$, the same convention as the degenerate dictionary. The braid order is $\psi_1\psi_2\psi_1-\psi_2\psi_1\psi_2$; on $(a,b,a)$ its value is $[K_{ab}(u,v)-K_{ab}(w,v)]/(w-u)$, hence respectively $+1,-1,0$ for forward, backward, nonadjacent colors.

items.title: An integer cyclic presentation descends the simple-head generator line
items.statement: Let $A_{\mathbb Z}$ be a finite free unital integer algebra with $A_{\mathbb Q}=\mathbb Q\otimes A_{\mathbb Z}$, and let $K$ be any characteristic-zero field. Suppose a finite-dimensional graded cyclic $A_K$-module $S_K$, with specified homogeneous generator $z_K$, is obtained from a homogeneous integer cyclic presentation $S_{\mathbb Z}=A_{\mathbb Z}/I_{\mathbb Z}$ by scalar extension, carrying $1+I_{\mathbb Z}$ to $z_K$. Suppose $S_K$ has a nonzero simple head $D_K$, with its specified grading normalization. Then the pair consisting of $D_K$ and the line spanned by the image $v$ of $z_K$ descends to $\mathbb Q$. More precisely there is a graded quotient $D_{\mathbb Q}$ of $S_{\mathbb Q}$ and $v_{\mathbb Q}\ne0$ such that $K\otimes D_{\mathbb Q}\cong D_K$ carries $1\otimes v_{\mathbb Q}$ to $v$. Consequently $A_{\mathbb Z}v$ is free of rank $\dim_KD_K$. If $D_K$ is absolutely simple, every nonzero quotient map from the specified $S_K$ to the fixed normalized $D_K$ has generator image on this same line, up to $K^\times$.

items.title: Generic cyclotomic type-A support is bounded by rank
items.statement:
Let $k$ have characteristic zero, let $\xi\in k^\times$ have infinite
multiplicative order, and fix a finite integral multicharge
$m_1,\ldots,m_\ell$. Write $S=\{m_j:1\le j\le\ell\}$.
Use the arbitrary-base presentations of
[[def-type-a-affine-presentations-and-charged-cyclotomic-quotients]] to define
$H_d^{\deg}$ by $\prod_j(x_1-m_j)=0$ and $H_d^{\xi}$ by
$\prod_j(X_1-\xi^{m_j})=0$.
For $d>0$, every nonzero joint generalized weight in the regular module has
labels $\nu\in\mathbb Z^d$, with eigenvalues $\nu_r$ respectively
$\xi^{\nu_r}$, and
$$\min_{s\in S}|\nu_r-s|\le d-1.$$
Thus both algebras have finite joint spectral decompositions defined over $k$.

Use the directed line $i\to i+1$ on $\mathbb Z$, with $d_i=1$,
$Q_{i,i+1}(u,v)=v-u$, $Q_{i+1,i}(u,v)=u-v$ and $Q_{ij}=1$ for
$|i-j|>1$. Define the rank-$d$ cyclotomic KLR algebra as the direct sum of its
finite-content presentations, with first-strand exponents
$\lambda_i=\#\{j:m_j=i\}$. Every nonzero word idempotent satisfies the same
bound, so this rank algebra is a finite sum of finite-dimensional graded
content algebras. Any interval containing
$[\min S-d+1,\max S+d-1]$ gives exactly the same rank-$d$ algebra;
enlarging it introduces only zero word idempotents. Rank zero is $k$.
At level zero every positive rank is zero. This lemma supplies support and
finite windows; it asserts no Hecke--KLR isomorphism or basis correspondence.

items.title: Extremal word characters detect normalized cyclotomic simple labels
items.statement: For a finite-dimensional standard homogeneous cyclotomic KLR module M over any field, choose a word by successive maximal last-color blocks i_1^{r_1}...i_s^{r_s}. There is exactly one normalized simple shift orbit S_c contributing to that word; its right crystal label is c=tilde f_{i_s}^{r_s}...tilde f_{i_1}^{r_1}u_Lambda. Its word graded dimension is product_a [r_a]_{i_a}!, and [M:S_c]_v equals gdim e(word)M divided by that product. All other simple orbits have zero word space. Consequently graded word characters are injective on G0. If two fields have modules with the same word character, their extremal words and detected canonical B(Lambda) labels coincide. No one-dimensional word-space assertion is made. Choice is inherited only through the existing abstract crystal identification.

items.title: Standard Fock vectors expand in the upper global basis
items.statement:
Use the symmetric model $M_\mu=|\mu'\rangle$ of
[[def-symmetric-group-level-one-residue-and-partition-label-convention]], the
basic field subspace $V$ of the vacuum Fock space spanned by the restricted
lower vectors $G(\lambda)=\sum_\mu d_{(\lambda,\mu)}(q)M_\mu$ of
[[def-level-one-global-basis-transition-polynomials-in-the-symmetric-group-convention]],
and the bilinear form $B(M_\mu,M_\nu)=\delta_{\mu,\nu}$. Define the **standard
coordinate functional** $\operatorname{Std}_\mu$ in the restricted integral
weight dual of the lower lattice by
$\operatorname{Std}_\mu(x)=B(x,M_\mu)$. The restriction of $B$ to $V$ is
nondegenerate; identify its field dual with $V$ via $B$ and denote by
$\pi(M_\mu)$ the vector representing $\operatorname{Std}_\mu$, equivalently the
$B$-orthogonal projection of $M_\mu$ onto $V$. This is the definition of $\pi$
used below, not an undeclared projection from a generic upper-basis definition.
If $G^*(\lambda)$ is the $B$-dual upper vector, then
$$\operatorname{Std}_\mu=\pi(M_\mu)=\sum_{\lambda\ \mathrm{restricted}} d_{(\lambda,\mu)}(q)\,G^*(\lambda).$$
At each content the restricted $\operatorname{Std}_\lambda$ form an $A$-basis of
the upper dual lattice, by the restricted dominance-unitriangular coefficient
minor. The full family of raw $M_\mu$ is the basis of the ambient standard
lattice; the full projected family $\operatorname{Std}_\mu$ is generally
redundant. The projection $\pi$ need not land in the lower integral lattice. In
$e=2$ one has $G_{11}=M_{11}+qM_2$ and
$G_{11}^*=(M_{11}+qM_2)/(1+q^2)$, exhibiting the possible field denominator.
The sums at fixed content are finite. Choice is inherited only from the
declared global-basis suppliers.

items.title: Graded module and projective Grothendieck groups of the KLR and Hecke towers
items.statement:
Let $k$ be a field and let $R=\bigoplus_{\alpha\in Q_+}R_\alpha$ be a tower of
finite-dimensional unital $\mathbb Z$-graded $k$-algebras with local units
$e(\alpha)$: every finite root-supported element has a unit given by the sum of its finitely many sector units, each
$R_\alpha$ a direct summand and $R_0=k$. Define
$$K_0^{\rm gr}(R):=\bigoplus_{\alpha\in Q_+}K_0^{\rm gr}(R_\alpha),\qquad G_0^{\rm gr}(R):=\bigoplus_{\alpha\in Q_+}G_0^{\rm gr}(R_\alpha),$$
the restricted direct sums of the blockwise Grothendieck groups of
[[def-graded-grothendieck-group-shift-module-and-cartan-map]]:
$K_0^{\rm gr}(R_\alpha)$ of finitely generated graded left
$R_\alpha$-projectives modulo split exact sequences
([[def-finitely-generated-graded-projective-module]]) and
$G_0^{\rm gr}(R_\alpha)$ of finite-dimensional graded left $R_\alpha$-modules
modulo short exact sequences. Both are modules over
$A:=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$ by $q[M]:=[M\{1\}]$
([[def-graded-ring-module-bimodule-and-internal-shift]]), and inside each
finite-dimensional block the shift-orbit bases of
[[thm-graded-projective-and-simple-classes-have-shift-orbit-bases]] hold. The
Cartan homomorphism $c:K_0^{\rm gr}(R)\to G_0^{\rm gr}(R)$, $[P]\mapsto[P]$, is
$A$-linear. The forgetful maps $\zeta$ to the ungraded groups $K_0(R)$,
$G_0(R)$ are additive and satisfy $\zeta(qm)=\zeta(m)$. The groups $K_0^{\rm gr}$ and
$G_0^{\rm gr}$ are DIFFERENT objects and are never identified.

**The two towers used below.** (i) For the standard homogeneous cyclotomic
quotient of [[def-cyclotomic-klr-quotient-at-a-dominant-weight]] at the
level-one weight $\Lambda_0$ of
[[def-type-a-cyclotomic-specialization-of-the-qg-klr-algebras]], put
$R^\Lambda_\alpha=R^\Lambda(\alpha)$; every block is finite dimensional and has
the homogeneous symmetrizing functional of
`thm-cyclotomic-klr-algebras-are-finite-dimensional-graded-symmetric`, with
grading shifts as in [[def-klr-grading-and-diagrammatic-composition]]. (ii) For
the cyclotomic Hecke tower $H^{\Lambda}:=\bigoplus_\alpha H^\Lambda_\alpha$ of
`def-affine-and-cyclotomic-type-a-hecke-algebras` with the block decomposition
of `def-residue-sequence-idempotents-and-cyclotomic-hecke-blocks`, fix an
admissible local normalising series and transport the homogeneous KLR
decomposition through the blockwise isomorphism of
`thm-brundan-kleshchev-blockwise-hecke-klr-isomorphism`, as in
`cor-cyclotomic-hecke-blocks-inherit-a-nontrivial-z-grading`; the induced
transport identifies $K_0^{\rm gr}(H^{\Lambda})\cong K_0^{\rm gr}(R^\Lambda)$
as $A$-modules and similarly for $G_0^{\rm gr}$, compatibly with $\zeta$ and
with the Cartan homomorphisms. Every class has finite root support, so the
direct sums are restricted.

No choice principle is used in this definition.

items.title: The nondegenerate root-of-unity level-one Hecke regime
items.statement:
**Parameters.** Let $F$ be a field and $\xi\in F^\times$ with finite quantum
characteristic $e=e(F,\xi)\in\{2,3,\dots\}$
([[def-quantum-characteristic-of-an-invertible-hecke-parameter]]). We work in
the NONDEGENERATE branch $\xi\ne1$; then $\xi$ is a primitive $e$-th root of
unity in $F$, and all statements on this page live in one of the two
sub-branches: (C0) $\operatorname{char}F=0$, or (CP)
$\operatorname{char}F=p>0$ with $p\nmid e$. The Hecke parameter is written
$\xi$ here; it is the letter $q$ of `def-affine-and-cyclotomic-type-a-hecke-algebras`.

**Hecke side.** Fix the level-one fundamental weight $\Lambda_0$ of the cyclic
affine type-$A$ datum with all $d_i=1$ and charge $0$
([[def-cyclic-affine-type-a-cartan-datum]]). With the conventions of
`def-affine-and-cyclotomic-type-a-hecke-algebras`, $H^\Lambda_d=H_{F,\xi}(S_d)$
is the finite type-$A$ Hecke algebra $T_r^2=(\xi-1)T_r+\xi$
(`prop-cyclotomic-hecke-algebras-of-level-one-are-finite-hecke-algebras`), and
$H^\Lambda_\alpha=e_\alpha H^\Lambda_d$ are its residue-content blocks
(`def-residue-sequence-idempotents-and-cyclotomic-hecke-blocks`).

**KLR side.** Use the type-$A$ specialization $Q^A$ of
`def-type-a-cyclotomic-specialization-of-the-qg-klr-algebras` with the same $e$
and the STANDARD homogeneous first-strand cyclotomic quotient
$R^\Lambda_\alpha$ of [[def-cyclotomic-klr-quotient-at-a-dominant-weight]]: the
cyclotomic relation is $y_1^{\delta_{i_1,0}}e(i)=0$, induction appends on the
right, and the grading is $\deg e(i)=0$, $\deg y_r=2$,
$\deg\psi_re(i)=-a_{i_ri_{r+1}}$
([[def-klr-grading-and-diagrammatic-composition]]). The transported grading on
$H^\Lambda_\alpha$ uses a FIXED admissible local normalising series
(`cor-cyclotomic-hecke-blocks-inherit-a-nontrivial-z-grading`); a different
series gives a graded-isomorphic transported algebra via $\rho'\rho^{-1}$, and
the graded multiplicities studied below do not depend on the choice.

**Grading and Fock variables.** All grading shifts and all global-basis
polynomials are in the variable $q$, $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$. Thus
$\xi\in F^\times$ (the Hecke parameter) and $q$ (the grading variable) are
INDEPENDENT data; the phrase "Ariki's normalization $\xi=q^2$" is retained only
as the source dictionary of [Ariki 1996], whose Hecke parameters are powers of
a square, and no numerical relation or specialization between $\xi$ and $q$ is
imposed.

**Fock side.** Use the level-one symmetric model of
[[def-symmetric-group-level-one-residue-and-partition-label-convention]]: charge
$0$, node residues $c-r$, standard vectors $M_\mu$ for ALL partitions $\mu$,
basic/restricted labels the $e$-restricted partitions
$RP_\alpha=\{\lambda:\lambda_a-\lambda_{a+1}<e,\ \operatorname{cont}(\lambda)=\alpha\}$,
empty component $B(\Lambda_0)$. For $\lambda\in RP$ the conjugate $\lambda'$ is
$e$-regular. Write $P(\nu)$ for the independently constructed ordinary
Dipper--James Specht module and $D_{\rm DJ}^{\nu}$ for its form quotient in
`thm-dj-bridge-ordinary-specht-is-the-signed-conjugate-murphy-cell`. Define
$\theta(T_r)=(\xi-1)-T_r=-\xi T_r^{-1}$, the involutive sign automorphism of
[[lem-dj-bridge-sign-automorphism-and-star-dual]]. After converting right
modules to left modules through the star anti-involution, the intrinsic
restricted Murphy simple with label $\lambda$ is the $\theta$-pullback of
$D_{\rm DJ}^{\lambda'}$, not the untwisted ordinary module. This is an ungraded
convention dictionary. The pullback can move blocks: on the multiplicative
Jucys--Murphy elements $\theta(X_j)=X_j^{-1}$, so charge-zero residue content
is sent from $\alpha$ to $-\alpha$. Thus the ordinary module before pullback has
the conjugate content; no claim identifies it untwisted inside the same block.
At $\xi=1$ the separate specialization theorem
`cor-dj-bridge-specialization-and-composition-multiplicity-dictionary`
identifies $\theta$ with sign tensoring over every field; $\xi=1$ remains
outside the present nondegenerate regime.

No choice principle is used.

items.title: The graded Cartan pairing between projective and module classes
items.statement:
In the situation and notation of [[def-graded-module-and-projective-grothendieck-groups-for-klr-towers]], for each root degree $\alpha$, finite-dimensional graded left $R^\Lambda_\alpha$-modules $M$ and finitely generated graded projective $P$ put $$h_\alpha(P,M):=\operatorname{gdim}\operatorname{HOM}_{R^\Lambda_\alpha}(P,M)=\sum_{d\in\mathbb Z}q^d\dim_k\operatorname{Hom}_{R^\Lambda_\alpha,d}(P,M)\in A .$$ By [[thm-projective-hom-pairing-is-additive-and-graded-sesquilinear]] (whose finite-dimensional hypotheses hold blockwise) this descends to an $A$-sesquilinear pairing $$h:K_0^{\rm gr}(R^\Lambda)\times G_0^{\rm gr}(R^\Lambda)\longrightarrow A,$$ with the twist $q\mapsto q^{-1}$: $h(q^r[P],q^s[M])=q^{s-r}h([P],[M])$. In particular $h^0(P,S):=\dim_k\operatorname{Hom}^0(P,S)$ is the degree-zero part. The pairing on the Hecke side is the transported pairing of [[def-graded-module-and-projective-grothendieck-groups-for-klr-towers]]. Also fix the two dualities used below: the descended anti-involution $\psi$ of [[def-cyclotomic-klr-diagram-duality-and-graded-module-duals]] with its finite-module duality $D_\psi$ and finite-projective duality $\#$, both shift-reversing and involutive on their domains; and the convention that a simple module or projective cover is called *normalized* when it is fixed (not merely fixed up to shift) by the relevant duality and, for a cover, when $\operatorname{Hom}^0(P,S)=k$.

No perfectness, nondegeneracy or $A$-self-duality is asserted in this definition; those are supplied by [[thm-cyclotomic-klr-module-g-zero-is-the-dual-integral-highest-weight-module]] and its transported form on the Hecke side.

items.title: The graded Specht module by homogeneous standard tableaux
items.statement:
Work in the regime of
[[def-nondegenerate-root-of-unity-level-one-hecke-regime]]. Fix a partition
$\mu$, put $d=|\mu|$, $\alpha=\operatorname{cont}(\mu)$, and let $K(\mu)$ be
the $F$-span of the Murphy elements $m_{S,T}$ of
[[def-arbitrary-level-cyclotomic-hecke-murphy-cell-and-schur-modules]] with
$S,T$ standard tableaux of a multipartition strictly dominating $\mu$; by
[[thm-arbitrary-level-cyclotomic-hecke-murphy-basis-is-cellular]] $K(\mu)$ is a
two-sided ideal of $H^\Lambda_d$ and $z_\mu:=m_{t^\mu t^\mu}+K(\mu)$ is
defined. Define the (level-one) **cell/Specht module**
$$S(\mu):=H^\Lambda_d\,z_\mu\subseteq H^\Lambda_d/K(\mu),$$
a LEFT $H^\Lambda_d$-module lying in the block $H^\Lambda_\alpha$.

For every standard $\mu$-tableau $T$
([[def-young-tableau-standard-tableau-and-shape]]) fix a reduced decomposition
$w_T=s_{r_1}\cdots s_{r_m}$ of the associated permutation and put
$z_T:=T_{w_T}z_\mu$, $v_T:=\psi_{w_T}z_\mu$ in the Khovanov--Lauda presentation
of `def-type-a-cyclotomic-specialization-of-the-qg-klr-algebras`. For a
removable $i$-node $A$ of a partition $\lambda$
([[def-removable-and-addable-nodes-of-a-partition]]) define
$$d_A(\lambda):=\#\{\text{addable }i\text{-nodes strictly below }A\}-\#\{\text{removable }i\text{-nodes strictly below }A\}$$
(equivalently in the level-one symmetric residue convention of the regime) and
define the **degree** of a standard tableau inductively by
$\deg(\varnothing):=0$ and, for $d>0$,
$\deg(T):=\deg(T_{\le d-1})+d_A(\mu)$ where $A$ is the node of $T$ containing
$d$.

The definition asserts, and
`thm-graded-specht-module-has-homogeneous-tableau-basis` on this page proves,
that $\{v_T:T\in\operatorname{Std}(\mu)\}$ is a homogeneous $F$-basis of
$S(\mu)$ making it a graded $R^\Lambda_\alpha$-module whose $q$-character is
$\operatorname{ch}_qS(\mu)=\sum_Tq^{\deg T}i_T$; forgetting the grading
recovers the ungraded cell module. **Convention.** This is the LEFT Murphy cell
module, obtained from the right cellular datum by $h\cdot m=m h^*$. Forgetting
its grading, `thm-dj-bridge-murphy-cell-is-the-same-shape-specht-dual`
identifies it with the star-contragredient dual of the same-shape
independently defined ordinary Dipper--James Specht module $P(\mu)$. Separately,
`thm-dj-bridge-ordinary-specht-is-the-signed-conjugate-murphy-cell` gives
$S(\mu)\cong P(\mu')^{\theta}$ after the same left-module conversion. These are
two proved module comparisons, not the identification of an untwisted conjugate
module. The sign pullback may change ordinary residue content from $-\alpha$ to
$\alpha$; these ungraded comparisons do not assert homogeneity of the ordinary
form or of a raw Hecke sign automorphism in the fixed transported grading. The
labelling of simples by $e$-restricted or $e$-regular partitions is NOT asserted
here; it is determined by the head-classification theorem later on this page.

No choice is used in the definition.

items.title: The integral form of the cyclotomic Hecke-KLR block
items.statement: Let $K$ be a characteristic-zero field in branch (C0) of [[def-nondegenerate-root-of-unity-level-one-hecke-regime]] and fix, for each residue content $\alpha$, the Khovanov-Lauda generators $\{e(i)\}$, $\{y_r\}$, $\{\psi_r\}$ of the block $H^\Lambda_\alpha(K)$ of [[def-affine-and-cyclotomic-type-a-hecke-algebras]], i.e. the $\rho_\alpha$-images of the KLR generators ([[thm-brundan-kleshchev-blockwise-hecke-klr-isomorphism]], [[def-type-a-cyclotomic-specialization-of-the-qg-klr-algebras]]), in a fixed admissible local normalising series. Define $$H^\Lambda_\alpha(\mathbb Z):=\bigl\langle e(i),\ y_r,\ \psi_r\ \bigr\rangle_{\mathbb Z}\subseteq H^\Lambda_\alpha(K)$$ to be the $\mathbb Z$-subring generated by them. It is the $\mathbb Z$-span of the same finite normal forms (in the Khovanov-Lauda generators) that span $H^\Lambda_\alpha(K)$ over $K$, hence a free $\mathbb Z$-module and a lattice; the generator degrees give it a grading, and the base-change maps $$K\otimes_{\mathbb Z}H^\Lambda_\alpha(\mathbb Z)\longrightarrow H^\Lambda_\alpha(K),\qquad F\otimes_{\mathbb Z}H^\Lambda_\alpha(\mathbb Z)\longrightarrow H^\Lambda_\alpha(F)$$ sending $1\otimes e(i)\mapsto e(i)$, $1\otimes y_r\mapsto y_r$, $1\otimes\psi_r\mapsto\psi_r$ are isomorphisms of graded algebras for every field $F$ of sub-branch (CP) with a primitive $e$-th root of unity, the second being the reduction modulo $p$. The direct sums over $\alpha$ give the integral form of the tower. No choice is used.

items.title: Degree and codegree of standard tableaux
items.statement:
In the situation of
[[def-graded-specht-module-by-homogeneous-standard-tableaux]], define
$d^A(\lambda)$ for an ADDABLE $i$-node $A$ to be the number of addable
$i$-nodes strictly ABOVE $A$ minus the number of removable $i$-nodes strictly
ABOVE $A$. Define the codegree of a standard tableau $T$ by
$\operatorname{codeg}(\varnothing):=0$ and
$\operatorname{codeg}(T):=d^A(\mu^A)+\operatorname{codeg}(T_{\le d-1})$, where
$A$ is the node containing $d$ and $\mu^A=\mu\setminus A$. Define the defect of
a residue content $\alpha\in Q_+$ by
$\operatorname{def}(\alpha):=(\Lambda_0,\alpha)-(\alpha,\alpha)/2$ (the
symmetric form of [[def-cyclic-affine-type-a-cartan-datum]]). Then for every
partition $\mu$ with content $\alpha$ and every standard $\mu$-tableau $T$:

1. $d_A(\mu)+d^A(\mu^A)=d_i(\mu)+1$ where $i$ is the residue of the removable
node $A$ and
$d_i(\mu)=\#\{\text{addable }i\text{-nodes of }\mu\}-\#\{\text{removable }i\text{-nodes of }\mu\}$;

2. $d_i(\mu)=(\Lambda_0-\alpha,\alpha_i)$;

3. $\operatorname{def}(\alpha)=\operatorname{def}(\alpha-\alpha_i)+d_i(\mu)+1$;

4. $\deg(T)+\operatorname{codeg}(T)=\operatorname{def}(\alpha)$;

5. removing a brick does not change the codegree: if
$m\to_Tm+1\to_T\cdots\to_Td$ and $S=T_{\le m-1}$, then
$\operatorname{codeg}(S)=\operatorname{codeg}(T)$ whenever (i) $m,\dots,d$
occupy nodes in the first row of the first component of $T$, or (ii)
$d-m+1=e$ (the quantum characteristic).

No choice is used.

items.title: A graded algebra isomorphism transports the graded module category, its Grothendieck groups and its dualities
items.statement:
Let $\rho:R\to H$ be an isomorphism of finite-dimensional unital
$\mathbb Z$-graded $k$-algebras. Restriction of scalars along $\rho$ is an
equivalence of graded left module categories which is exact, sends
finite-dimensional modules to finite-dimensional modules, sends a shift
$M\{r\}$ to $M\{r\}$, sends finitely generated graded projectives to finitely
generated graded projectives, preserves composition multiplicities of graded
simples (with shifts), and identifies the graded Hom pairings
$\operatorname{gdim}\operatorname{HOM}$ of
[[def-graded-cartan-pairing-between-projectives-and-modules]]. The inverse equivalence, restriction along $\rho^{-1}$, therefore
induces $A$-module isomorphisms $K_0^{\rm gr}(R)\to K_0^{\rm gr}(H)$ and
$G_0^{\rm gr}(R)\to G_0^{\rm gr}(H)$ intertwining the Cartan homomorphisms and
the forgetful maps $\zeta$.

If moreover $\rho$ intertwines fixed grading-preserving anti-involutions $\ast_R$ and $\ast_H$
(i.e. $\rho(x^{\ast_R})=\rho(x)^{\ast_H}$), then the transported functor
intertwines the two diagram dualities $D_\psi$ and the two projective
Hom-dualities $\#$ of `def-cyclotomic-klr-diagram-duality-and-graded-module-duals`,
and hence preserves normalized self-dual simples and normalized self-dual
indecomposable projectives.

**Application.** For each nonzero content sector choose the actual graded block
isomorphism $\rho_\alpha$. DEFINE the Hecke duality by
$\ast_H=\rho_\alpha\ast_R\rho_\alpha^{-1}$. This is a grading-preserving
anti-involution, fixing the NAMED images of $e(i),y_r,\psi_r$, and $\rho_\alpha$
intertwines it by definition. Thus the preceding duality conclusion applies
blockwise. This does not identify $\ast_H$ with the raw cellular
anti-involution that fixes affine Hecke generators, and does not infer that a
product is fixed merely because its factors are fixed.

items.title: The QG-8 categorification transports across the blockwise Hecke-KLR bridge
items.statement:
Assume inherited AC [[def-axiom-of-choice]] for the highest-weight, crystal and global-basis suppliers invoked below; the finite algebra transport introduces no additional choice.

In the regime of
[[def-nondegenerate-root-of-unity-level-one-hecke-regime]] (both branches (C0)
and (CP)), fixing an admissible normalising series, the blockwise graded
isomorphism $\rho_\alpha:R^\Lambda_\alpha\to H^\Lambda_\alpha$ of
`thm-brundan-kleshchev-blockwise-hecke-klr-isomorphism` with the grading of
`cor-cyclotomic-hecke-blocks-inherit-a-nontrivial-z-grading` transports the
standard homogeneous cyclotomic data to the Hecke side, block by block and then
by the restricted direct sums of
[[def-graded-module-and-projective-grothendieck-groups-for-klr-towers]]:

1. the unique $A$-module isomorphism
$\phi:K_0^{\rm gr}(R^\Lambda)\to V_A(\Lambda_0)$ of
`thm-cyclotomic-klr-projective-k-zero-is-the-integral-highest-weight-module`
(sending the vacuum class to $v_{\Lambda_0}$ and intertwining the normalized
divided powers $E_i,F_i,K_i$) becomes an $A$-module isomorphism
$\phi^{\rm Hecke}:K_0^{\rm gr}(H^{\Lambda})\to V_A(\Lambda_0)$ with the same
properties;

2. the canonical identification
$\Psi_{\rm can}:G_0^{\rm gr}(R^\Lambda)\to V_A(\Lambda_0)^\vee$ of
`thm-cyclotomic-klr-module-g-zero-is-the-dual-integral-highest-weight-module`
(restricted weight dual, canonical module action, normalized simple classes to
the form-dual projective basis) becomes an isomorphism
$\Psi_{\rm can}^{\rm Hecke}:G_0^{\rm gr}(H^{\Lambda})\to V_A(\Lambda_0)^\vee$
with the same properties;

3. the two identifications intertwine the transported $E_i,F_i,K_i$ of
`thm-cyclotomic-klr-functors-define-an-integrable-quantum-action-on-k-zero-and-g-zero`
with the Hecke-side functors induced by
[[def-cyclotomic-klr-induction-and-restriction-functors]], and the
FIRST-BAR-SEQUILINEAR Hom pairing $h$ of
[[def-graded-cartan-pairing-between-projectives-and-modules]] and, separately,
the $A$-BILINEAR tensor pairing $T$ defining $\Psi_{\rm can}$, with
$h(P,M)=T(P^{\#},M)$. Both are weightwise perfect on normalized cover/simple
bases, where $P^{\#}=P$; they are not identified on arbitrary shifted first
arguments;

4. in branch (C0), and with the additional hypotheses of
`thm-self-dual-indecomposable-cyclotomic-klr-projectives-give-the-lower-global-basis`
and `thm-self-dual-simple-cyclotomic-klr-modules-give-the-upper-global-basis`
(symmetric Cartan datum with $d_i=1$, characteristic zero, finite loopless
quiver with arbitrary edge multiplicities and
$Q_{ij}=(-1)^{h_{ij}}(u-v)^{h_{ij}+h_{ji}}$), which the type-$A$
specialization of the regime satisfies, the transported normalized
$\#$self-dual indecomposable projectives correspond bijectively to the lower
global basis and the transported normalized $D_\psi$-self-dual simples to the
upper global basis; the transported simple and projective crystals are the
$B(\Lambda_0)$-crystals of
`thm-simple-and-indecomposable-projective-crystals-agree-with-b-lambda`, so
each class carries its crystal label in $RP$.

In BOTH branches the normalized finite-module duality representatives and their
right crystal labels come from
`def-cyclotomic-klr-diagram-duality-and-graded-module-duals` and
`thm-simple-and-indecomposable-projective-crystals-agree-with-b-lambda`,
independently of clause (4)'s characteristic-zero global-basis conclusion.

No based-quotient, quantum-star or cyclotomic categorification statement is
asserted beyond these transported clauses. Choice is inherited through the cited highest-weight, crystal and global-basis suppliers.

items.title: Shifted degrees and Garnir exchanges for standard tableaux
items.statement:
In the situation of
[[def-graded-specht-module-by-homogeneous-standard-tableaux]]:

1. If $T\xrightarrow{\,r\,}S$ (i.e. both tableaux are standard, $S=s_rT$, and
$r$ occupies an earlier row-reading node than $r+1$, as in
[[def-tableau-domination-order-garnir-tableaux-and-bricks]]), then
$\deg(S)-\deg(T)=-a_{i_ri_{r+1}}$, where $i_T=(i_1,\dots,i_d)$ and $a$ is the
Cartan matrix of the regime.

2. More generally, if $w_T=s_{r_1}\cdots s_{r_m}$ is a reduced decomposition,
then $\deg(T)-\deg(t^\mu)=\deg\bigl(\psi_{r_1}\cdots\psi_{r_m}e(i_{t^\mu})\bigr)$
in the grading of [[def-klr-grading-and-diagrammatic-composition]].

3. If $T$ is the $(a,b)$-Garnir tableau with entry $r$ in the node $(a,b)$, and
$S$ is a standard $\mu$-tableau with $S\lhd T$ and $i_S=i_{s_rT}$, then
$\deg(S)-\deg(T)=-a_{i_ri_{r+1}}$ as well.

No choice is used.

items.title: The graded Specht module has a homogeneous tableau basis
items.statement:
Keep the notation of
[[def-graded-specht-module-by-homogeneous-standard-tableaux]]; the vectors
$v_T=\psi_{w_T}z_\mu$ may a priori depend on the chosen reduced decompositions
$w_T=s_{r_1}\cdots s_{r_m}$. Then:

1. For every $\mu$-tableau $T$ one has $v_T=\sum_{S\unlhd T}a_Sz_S$ with
$a_T\ne0$ when $T$ is standard; hence the standard vectors form a basis of
$S(\mu)$ triangular with respect to the standard basis $\{z_T\}$ of
[[def-graded-specht-module-by-homogeneous-standard-tableaux]].

2. If $w_T=s_{r_1}\cdots s_{r_m}=s_{t_1}\cdots s_{t_m}$ are two reduced
decompositions of the same $w_T$, then
$\psi_{r_1}\cdots\psi_{r_m}z_\mu-\psi_{t_1}\cdots\psi_{t_m}z_\mu=\sum_{S\lhd T,\ i_S=i_T,\ \deg S=\deg T}a_Sv_S$;
in particular the grading on $S(\mu)$ defined by $\deg(v_T):=\deg(T)$ is
independent of the choices.

3. For every $r$ the vectors $e(i)v_T$, $y_rv_T$ and $\psi_rv_T$ lie in
the prescribed homogeneous components; when nonzero their degrees satisfy
$$e(i)v_T=\delta_{i,i_T}v_T,\qquad \deg(y_rv_T)=\deg(y_r)+\deg(T),\qquad \deg(\psi_rv_T)=\deg(\psi_re(i_T))+\deg(T).$$
Hence $S(\mu)$ is a graded $R^\Lambda_\alpha$-module with homogeneous basis
$\{v_T\}$ and $q$-character
$\operatorname{ch}_qS(\mu)=\sum_{T\in\operatorname{Std}(\mu)}q^{\deg T}i_T$;
forgetting the grading recovers the ungraded cell module of
[[def-graded-specht-module-by-homogeneous-standard-tableaux]].

No choice beyond the finite selections of reduced decompositions is used; the
resulting graded isomorphism class is independent of them by (2).

items.title: Rational Garnir annihilator lines present the specified Specht generator
items.statement:
Fix the level-one type-A integer KLR presentation, charge $0$, and finite quantum characteristic $e\in\{2,3,\ldots\}$. Let $K$ be any characteristic-zero field in the specified Hecke regime, let $\lambda$ be the specified partition, and let $S_K(\lambda)$ be the LEFT graded Murphy cell Specht module with its specified initial cyclic generator $z_K$. Then there is a finite-dimensional graded module $S_{\mathbb Q}(\lambda)$ for the rational KLR algebra, with a specified homogeneous cyclic vector $z_{\mathbb Q}$, and a graded generator-preserving isomorphism $K\otimes_{\mathbb Q} S_{\mathbb Q}(\lambda)\cong S_K(\lambda)$. The rational module is explicitly presented by the initial weight, dot and horizontal crossing relations, together with one homogeneous rational relation for each Garnir belt. Each of these relations is the unique vector with Garnir coefficient $1$ in the kernel of a finite matrix with integer entries, obtained from crossing operators in the integer row permutation module. It therefore depends only on the integer presentation, not on a choice of $K$ or of a root of unity.

If the specified normalized simple head $D_K(\lambda)$ is nonzero and absolutely simple, this construction, combined with the local cyclic-head descent lemma, defines its initial-generator image line over $\mathbb Q$ up to scalar. The orbit of that image under the finite integer cyclotomic algebra is a lattice of rank $\dim_K D_K(\lambda)$.

items.title: Graded Specht restriction has the removable-node filtration
items.statement:
Keep the notation of
[[def-graded-specht-module-by-homogeneous-standard-tableaux]], let $\mu$ be a
partition of $d$, $\alpha=\operatorname{cont}(\mu)$, and let
$i\in I=\mathbb Z/e\mathbb Z$. Let $A_1,\dots,A_c$ be the removable $i$-nodes
of $\mu$ ordered from bottom to top, and let
$\mu^{A_m}=\mu\setminus A_m$. Write $E_i:=E_i^{\rm basic}$ for the restriction
functor $N\mapsto e(\alpha-\alpha_i,\alpha_i)N$ of
[[def-cyclotomic-klr-induction-and-restriction-functors]] (equivalently the
$i$-part of the tower restriction of
[[def-klr-induction-and-restriction-bimodules]]). Then $E_iS(\mu)$ has a
filtration
$$0=V_0\subset V_1\subset\cdots\subset V_c=E_iS(\mu)$$
of graded $R^\Lambda_{\alpha-\alpha_i}$-modules with
$V_m/V_{m-1}\cong S(\mu^{A_m})\{d_{A_m}(\mu)\}$ for $1\le m\le c$.

Equivalently, the restriction of $S(\mu)$ to the previous rank has the
removable-node filtration of [BKW, Theorem 4.11] over ALL removable nodes, and
$E_i$ selects the removable-$i$-node part. No choice is used.

items.title: Graded Specht classes realize the standard Fock vectors
items.statement:
In the regime of
[[def-nondegenerate-root-of-unity-level-one-hecke-regime]], let
$\Psi_{\rm can}^{\rm Hecke}:G_0^{\rm gr}(H^{\Lambda})\to V_A(\Lambda_0)^\vee$ be
the transported identification of
[[prop-qg8-categorification-transports-across-the-hecke-klr-bridge]], and let
$S_\mu:=\pi(M_\mu)$ be the standard monomial image of the standard Fock vector
$M_\mu$ of
[[def-symmetric-group-level-one-residue-and-partition-label-convention]] under
the projection to the basic module. Then for every partition $\mu$ with content
$\alpha$,
$$\Psi_{\rm can}^{\rm Hecke}\bigl([S(\mu)]\bigr)=S_\mu .$$
In other words, the class of the graded Specht module of
[[def-graded-specht-module-by-homogeneous-standard-tableaux]] is the standard
Fock vector in the fixed level-one convention. This holds in both branches (C0)
and (CP). No choice beyond the inherited suppliers is used.

items.title: The restricted graded Specht classes form a basis of the module Grothendieck group
items.statement: In the stated nondegenerate level-one regime and each residue content alpha, the classes [S(lambda)] indexed by RESTRICTED shapes lambda form an A-basis of G0^gr(H_alpha). Under Psi_can they correspond to the restricted standard coordinate functionals Std_lambda=pi(M_lambda), which form an A-basis of the UPPER integral dual lattice. Separately, all raw standard M_mu of that content form an A-basis of the ambient Fock standard lattice; their full projected family is generally redundant. No claim that Std_lambda is a basis of the lower lattice or that the field Gram denominator is an A-unit is made. Choice only as inherited.

items.title: Ariki's canonical basis theorem in characteristic zero
items.statement:
In branch (C0) of the regime of
[[def-nondegenerate-root-of-unity-level-one-hecke-regime]], with the normalized
self-dual simples $D(\lambda)$ and their normalized projective covers
$Y(\lambda)$ labelled by the crystal $B(\Lambda_0)=RP$ as in
[[prop-qg8-categorification-transports-across-the-hecke-klr-bridge]] (4):

1. the transported isomorphism
$\phi^{\rm Hecke}:K_0^{\rm gr}(H^{\Lambda})\to V_A(\Lambda_0)$ sends the class
of the normalized self-dual indecomposable projective $Y(\lambda)$ to the lower
global basis vector $G(\lambda)$ for every $\lambda\in RP$;

2. the transported identification
$\Psi_{\rm can}^{\rm Hecke}:G_0^{\rm gr}(H^{\Lambda})\to V_A(\Lambda_0)^\vee$
sends $[D(\lambda)]$ to the upper global basis vector $G^*(\lambda)$, form-dual
to $G(\lambda)$ under the highest-weight contravariant form;

3. equivalently the lower global basis is the canonical basis of the basic
module $V_A(\Lambda_0)$ and corresponds to projective indecomposables, while
the upper global basis is the dual-canonical basis and corresponds to simple
classes, and the labels are those of
[[prop-qg8-categorification-transports-across-the-hecke-klr-bridge]] (4): the
crystal $B(\Lambda_0)=RP$, with a simple and its projective cover carrying the
same label. The passage from these crystal labels to the
cellular/Dipper--James parametrization of the simple modules is not asserted
here; it is established with the head classification later on this page;

4. specializing the grading $q=1$ via the forgetful maps $\zeta$ of
[[def-graded-module-and-projective-grothendieck-groups-for-klr-towers]]
recovers Ariki's ungraded canonical-basis statement, and combined with the
graded decomposition theorem later on this page it gives his ungraded
decomposition-number theorem.

Choice is inherited only through the QG-8 global-basis suppliers; no choice is
introduced by the transport or by the label comparison.

items.title: Graded decomposition numbers equal canonical-basis coefficients in characteristic zero
items.statement:
In branch (C0) of the regime of
[[def-nondegenerate-root-of-unity-level-one-hecke-regime]], for every partition
$\mu$ with content $\alpha$ and every $\lambda\in RP_\alpha$, the graded
composition multiplicity satisfies
$$[S(\mu):D(\lambda)]_q=d_{\lambda,\mu}(q),$$
where $d_{\lambda,\mu}$ is the level-one global-basis transition polynomial of
[[def-level-one-global-basis-transition-polynomials-in-the-symmetric-group-convention]];
equivalently
$[S(\mu)]=\sum_{\lambda\in RP_\alpha}d_{\lambda,\mu}(q)[D(\lambda)]$ in
$G_0^{\rm gr}(H^\Lambda_\alpha)$, and $d_{\lambda,\mu}=0$ unless
$\lambda\unlhd\mu$. Specializing $q=1$ gives Ariki's ungraded
decomposition-number theorem
$[S(\mu):D(\lambda)]=d_{\lambda,\mu}(1)$. Choice is inherited only through the
QG-8 global-basis suppliers.

items.title: Graded Specht heads classify the graded simple modules
items.statement:
In the regime of
[[def-nondegenerate-root-of-unity-level-one-hecke-regime]], for
$\lambda\in RP_\alpha$ the graded Specht module $S(\lambda)$ of
[[def-graded-specht-module-by-homogeneous-standard-tableaux]] has irreducible
head, denoted $\dot D(\lambda)$, and
$\dot D(\lambda)^\circledast\cong\dot D(\lambda)$. Moreover:

1. the modules $\{\dot D(\lambda)\langle m\rangle:\lambda\in RP_\alpha,\ m\in\mathbb Z\}$
are a complete set of pairwise non-isomorphic graded simple
$R^\Lambda_\alpha$-modules (equivalently, of $H^\Lambda_\alpha$ with the
transported grading);

2. in $G_0^{\rm gr}(H^\Lambda_\alpha)$ one has
$[S(\lambda)]=[\dot D(\lambda)]+(\ast)$ if $\lambda$ is restricted and
$[S(\lambda)]=(\ast)$ otherwise, where $(\ast)$ is an $A$-linear combination of
$[\dot D(\mu)]$'s with $\mu\lhd\lambda$; consequently
$[S(\mu):\dot D(\lambda)]_q\ne0$ implies $\lambda\unlhd\mu$, and
$[S(\lambda):\dot D(\lambda)]_q=1$;

3. in branch (C0), $\dot D(\lambda)\cong D(\lambda)$, the normalized simple
with crystal label $\lambda$ of
[[prop-qg8-categorification-transports-across-the-hecke-klr-bridge]] (4);
separately, after forgetting the grading and converting the ordinary right
modules through star, $\dot D(\lambda)\cong(D_{\rm DJ}^{\lambda'})^{\theta}$ by
`thm-dj-bridge-ordinary-specht-is-the-signed-conjugate-murphy-cell`. Thus the
conjugate $e$-regular ordinary label occurs with the explicit
sign-automorphism pullback, which reflects residue content and is not an
untwisted same-block identification. The ordinary module dictionary and radical
comparison hold in both field branches; the crystal-label comparison in this
part is the stated (C0) assertion.

Parts (1) and (2) hold in both branches (C0) and (CP); part (3) is stated in
branch (C0), the branch of the decomposition theorem it consumes. The branch
(CP) analogue of (3) is the identification [BK 2009, Theorem 5.18] and is NOT
asserted here. Choice is inherited only through the cited transported
global-basis suppliers, as recorded in the contract.

items.title: Reduction of characteristic-zero simple modules modulo p
Positive-characteristic Specht head and cyclotomic crystal labels agree
items.statement: In the positive-characteristic nondegenerate level-one regime, the normalized cellular head dotD(lambda) for each restricted partition lambda is isomorphic, with shift zero, to the normalized simple of the same right crystal label lambda. The reduction J(lambda) of the characteristic-zero normalized simple contains that crystal-labelled simple once, and has no constituents with cellular labels not dominated by lambda. Its G0 class is invariant under finite-module diagram duality. This proves the CP label comparison needed for the crystal-labelled adjustment matrix; it is not a positive-characteristic global-basis identification.

items.title: The graded adjustment polynomials in positive characteristic
items.statement:
In branch (CP) of the regime of [[def-nondegenerate-root-of-unity-level-one-hecke-regime]], with the reduced modules $J(
u)$ of [[lem-reduction-of-characteristic-zero-simple-modules-modulo-p]] and the normalized simples $D(\lambda)$ with crystal label $\lambda\in RP_\alpha$ of the general-field normalization/crystal clauses of [[prop-qg8-categorification-transports-across-the-hecke-klr-bridge]] and [[lem-positive-characteristic-specht-head-and-cyclotomic-crystal-labels-agree]] (in branch (C0) these are the heads of the graded Specht modules by [[thm-graded-specht-heads-classify-the-graded-simple-modules]] (3)), define the **graded adjustment polynomials** $a_{\lambda,
u}(q)\in\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$ for $\lambda,
u\in RP_\alpha$ by $$[J(
u)]=\sum_{\lambda\in RP_\alpha}a_{\lambda,
u}(q)[D(\lambda)]\qquad\Longleftrightarrow\qquad a_{\lambda,
u}(q)=[J(
u):D(\lambda)]_q .$$ Then the matrix $(a_{\lambda,
u})$ is the graded adjustment matrix; its entries are bar-invariant, have nonnegative integer coefficients, satisfy $a_{
u,
u}(q)=1$ and vanish unless $\lambda\unlhd
u$ (dominance); equivalently $a_{\lambda,
u}$ is the coefficient of $[D(\lambda)]$ in $(\Psi_{m can}^{m Hecke})^{-1}(D_
u)$.

**Source comparison (recorded, not used).** For level one and $\xi=1$ the source states that this adjustment matrix specializes at $q=1$ to the adjustment matrix of James; that degenerate comparison lies outside the nondegenerate branch of this page and is deferred (see the batch coverage record). No choice is used in the definition.

items.title: Positive-characteristic decomposition polynomials factor through adjustment
Canonical bases do not solve arbitrary positive-characteristic decomposition numbers
items.statement: The characteristic-zero theorems of this page ([[thm-ariki-canonical-basis-theorem-in-characteristic-zero]], [[thm-graded-decomposition-numbers-equal-canonical-basis-coefficients-in-characteristic-zero]]) compute graded decomposition numbers of graded Specht modules as global-basis coefficients. In characteristic $p>0$ the factorization [[thm-positive-characteristic-decomposition-polynomials-factor-through-adjustment]] reduces the graded decomposition matrix to a product of the adjustment matrix and the SAME global-basis coefficients, but the adjustment matrix is generally nontrivial: the theorem computes no adjustment entry and asserts no identity adjustment matrix in general. Consequently the characteristic-zero canonical-basis theory does not by itself solve the decomposition-number problem in arbitrary positive characteristic; the general problem retains the boundary recorded in [[rem-general-modular-decomposition-numbers-are-not-determined-by-triangularity]] and [[rem-general-type-a-decomposition-numbers-remain-unsolved]]. This remark records the boundary; it carries no proof obligation and no choice principle.

decline_pages.title: Kronecker Coefficients and Internal Products

items.title: Kronecker coefficients and the internal tensor product
items.statement: Fix n >= 0 and work over C. For partitions lambda, mu, nu of n the diagonal tensor product S^lambda (x) S^mu is a finite-dimensional complex S_n-module; by Maschke's theorem it is completely reducible, and by the classification of complex irreducibles of S_n the Specht modules S^nu (nu |- n) are a complete set of pairwise inequivalent irreducibles. Let (S^lambda (x) S^mu)_{(S^nu)} be the isotypic component of type S^nu and put g(lambda,mu,nu) := dim (S^lambda (x) S^mu)_{(S^nu)} / dim S^nu; equivalently g(lambda,mu,nu) is the multiplicity of S^nu in S^lambda (x) S^mu. Call (lambda,mu) -> S^lambda (x) S^mu the internal (Kronecker) product of S_n-representations. Unlike the outer induction product this operation keeps the rank: both inputs and the output are S_n-modules of the same degree n, and it is never the same operation as Ind_{S_a x S_b}^{S_{a+b}}.

items.title: Complex Specht modules are self-dual with real-valued characters
items.statement: For every lambda |- n the complex Specht module S^lambda carries a nondegenerate symmetric S_n-invariant bilinear form b(x,y) = sum_T x_T y_T (coefficientwise product in the tabloid basis), so v -> b(v,-) is an isomorphism of C S_n-modules S^lambda -> (S^lambda)^*; equivalently S^lambda is self-dual. Consequently chi^lambda(g^{-1}) = chi^lambda(g), i.e. every irreducible character of S_n is real-valued.

items.title: The Kronecker coefficient is a three-character inner product
items.statement: For all lambda,mu,nu |- n, g(lambda,mu,nu) = <chi^lambda chi^mu, chi^nu> = (1/n!) sum_{sigma in S_n} chi^lambda(sigma) chi^mu(sigma) chi^nu(sigma), where the sum uses the real-valuedness of the irreducible characters (no conjugation on the third factor).

items.title: Kronecker coefficients are nonnegative integers with full S_3 and conjugation symmetries
items.statement: For all lambda,mu,nu |- n: (a) g(lambda,mu,nu) is a nonnegative integer; (b) g(lambda,mu,nu) is invariant under every permutation of lambda,mu,nu; (c) conjugating exactly two of the three partitions preserves the coefficient: g(lambda,mu,nu) = g(lambda',mu',nu) = g(lambda',mu,nu') = g(lambda,mu',nu'). No positive combinatorial rule is asserted.

items.title: The internal (Kronecker) product on symmetric functions
items.statement: Let ch: R_S -> Lambda be the Frobenius characteristic, a degree-preserving ring isomorphism from the graded character ring of the symmetric groups onto the stable symmetric-function ring. For f in Lambda^m and g in Lambda^n define f * g := ch( ch^{-1}(f) . ch^{-1}(g) ) if m = n, where the dot is the pointwise (internal tensor) product of class functions, and f * g := 0 if m != n; extend bilinearly. Then * is a degree-preserving, commutative, associative, bilinear product on Lambda with degreewise unit h_n = s_(n) = ch(trivial character of S_n) on Lambda^n (h_0 = 1); the direct sum Lambda has no global unit for *, and for partitions lambda,mu of n, s_lambda * s_mu = sum_nu g(lambda,mu,nu) s_nu.

items.title: Power sums diagonalize the internal product
items.statement: For partitions rho,sigma of n one has p_rho * p_sigma = delta_{rho,sigma} z_rho p_rho, where z_rho = prod_i i^{m_i(rho)} m_i(rho)!; consequently s_lambda * s_mu = sum_{nu |- n} g(lambda,mu,nu) s_nu. The internal product of symmetric functions is therefore diagonal in the power-sum basis and has integer structure constants (the Kronecker coefficients) in the Schur basis.

items.title: First-row padding of a partition
items.statement: For a partition alpha and an integer n, define alpha[n] := (n - |alpha|, alpha_1, alpha_2, ...) whenever n >= |alpha| + alpha_1; the displayed sequence is then a partition of n, and below the threshold it is not a partition (the first part is smaller than the second, or negative). The threshold |alpha| + alpha_1 is exact. This notation is neutral: it records no constancy and is shared with the FI-module and representation-stability developments.

items.title: Padded Kronecker coefficient sequences
items.statement: Let alpha,beta,gamma be partitions and let n_0 := max{|alpha|+alpha_1, |beta|+beta_1, |gamma|+gamma_1}. For integers n >= n_0 all three padded sequences alpha[n], beta[n], gamma[n] are partitions of n, and one defines g_n(alpha,beta,gamma) := g(alpha[n], beta[n], gamma[n]). Below n_0 the notation is undefined because at least one padded sequence is not a partition. This definition asserts no eventual constancy; Murnaghan stability is a theorem about this sequence proved elsewhere.

items.title: Littlewood's identity - the internal product against an outer product
items.statement: For partitions lambda |- n, tau |- r and theta |- n - r, Littlewood's identity holds in Lambda^n: s_lambda * (s_tau s_theta) = sum_{alpha |- r, beta |- n-r} c^lambda_{alpha,beta} (s_alpha * s_tau)(s_beta * s_theta), with c^lambda_{alpha,beta} the Littlewood-Richardson coefficient. Both sides have degree n and the sum is finite.

items.title: The Kronecker reduction lemma of Pak and Panova
items.statement:
Let $n\ge0$ and $\ell\ge0$, and let $\lambda,\mu,\nu\vdash n$ have lengths at most $\ell$. Read missing parts as zero and put $s:=n-\nu_1$, with $\nu_1=0$ for the empty partition.

**(i)** If $|\lambda_i-\mu_i|>s$ for some $i\le\ell$, then $g(\lambda,\mu,\nu)=0$.

**(ii)** Otherwise put $\rho:=\lambda\cap\mu$, $\omega:=\lambda\cup\mu$, $\omega_{\ell+1}:=0$, and define
$$\delta_i:=\max\{0,\rho_i-\omega_{i+1}-2s\},\qquad D_j:=\sum_{i=j}^{\ell}\delta_i,\qquad \varphi(\theta)_j:=\theta_j-D_j\quad(1\le j\le\ell).$$
For every partition $\theta$ with at most $\ell$ parts satisfying $\rho_j-s\le\theta_j\le\omega_j$ for each $j$, the image $\varphi(\theta)$ is a partition after deletion of zero parts. In particular $\varphi(\lambda)$ and $\varphi(\mu)$ have a common size $r$, and $\varphi(\nu):=(r-s,\nu_2,\nu_3,\ldots)$ is a partition of $r$. Then
$$g(\lambda,\mu,\nu)=g(\varphi(\lambda),\varphi(\mu),\varphi(\nu)),\qquad r\le2s\ell^2.$$

This is a corrected reduction map for the bounded-reduction conclusion of Pak–Panova. It retains their Littlewood–Richardson/Jacobi–Trudi proof route and the same size bound; the map is not the block formula printed in their papers.

items.title: Row-gap reduction and conditional k-stability of Kronecker coefficients
items.statement:
Fix $\lambda,\mu,\nu\vdash n$ and an integer $k\ge1$. Write $(t^k)$ for $k$ parts equal to $t$ and $(tk)$ for the one-part partition of size $tk$, and read missing parts as zero. Put $s:=n-\nu_1$, with $\nu_1=0$ if $n=0$.

**(i)** Suppose $\lambda_1\le\mu_1\le\nu_1$ and
$$\min\{\lambda_k,\mu_k\}\ge\max\{\lambda_{k+1},\mu_{k+1}\}+s.$$
Then for every integer $t\ge0$,
$$g(\lambda+(t^k),\mu+(t^k),\nu+(tk))=g(\lambda,\mu,\nu).$$
All shifted arguments are partitions of $n+tk$. For $k=1$, this is the first-row padding of the three tails to size $n+t$ ([[def-first-row-padding-of-a-partition]]).

**(ii)** For arbitrary $\lambda,\mu,\nu\vdash n$ and $k\ge1$, the sequence $G_k(t):=g(\lambda+(t^k),\mu+(t^k),\nu+(tk))$ is eventually constant. More precisely, it is constant for every integer $t\ge t_0$, where
$$t_0:=\max\{0,\ s+\max\{\lambda_{k+1},\mu_{k+1}\}-\min\{\lambda_k,\mu_k\}\}.$$
The proof of the row-gap identity does not require first-part ordering, so the threshold also covers $k=1$ when $\nu_1<\max\{\lambda_1,\mu_1\}$. No monotonicity is asserted.

items.title: No general positive combinatorial rule for Kronecker coefficients is known
items.statement: The character formula, the reduction lemma and k-stability of this page do not supply a general positive combinatorial rule: it remains a well-known open problem to give a combinatorial interpretation of, or a positive formula for, all Kronecker coefficients g(lambda,mu,nu). In particular this page claims no such rule, no polynomial-time algorithm and no general positivity criterion. Provenance: literature-derived statement, no proof section.

decline_pages.title: Kronecker Coefficients and Internal Products — Examples

items.title: The complete internal product table for S_3
items.statement: For S_3 the three irreducibles are S^(3) (trivial), S^(2,1) (standard, dim 2) and S^(1,1,1) (sign). The character values on cycle types (1^3),(2,1),(3) are (1,1,1), (2,0,-1), (1,-1,1) respectively; consequently the complete internal product table is: S^(3) (x) X = X for every irreducible X; S^(2,1) (x) S^(2,1) = S^(3) + S^(2,1) + S^(1,1,1); S^(2,1) (x) S^(1,1,1) = S^(2,1); S^(1,1,1) (x) S^(1,1,1) = S^(3). Equivalently all Kronecker coefficients g(lambda,mu,nu) for n=3 are 0 or 1 and the table is invariant under all permutations of the three arguments.

items.title: First-row padding below the threshold is undefined
items.statement: For alpha = (2,1) the padded sequence alpha[n] = (n-3,2,1) is a partition exactly when n >= 5. In particular alpha[3] = (0,2,1) and alpha[4] = (1,2,1) are not partitions, so the padded family and the padded Kronecker coefficient g_n(alpha,beta,gamma) are undefined below the stated threshold; the stable family for this shape begins only at n = 5.

items.title: Row padding need not preserve a Kronecker coefficient before stability
items.statement: With lambda = mu = (2,2) and nu = (3,1) (n = 4, k = 1) one has g((2,2),(2,2),(3,1)) = 0, whereas g((2+t,2),(2+t,2),(3+t,1)) = 1 for every t >= 1. Thus adding (t^k) does not preserve the coefficient from t = 0 on: the separation hypothesis of the row-gap theorem fails at t = 0, since min{lambda_1,mu_1} = 2 < max{lambda_2,mu_2} + (n - nu_1) = 2 + 1 = 3. Eventual constancy is not immediacy.

decline_pages.title: Character Polynomials, FI-Modules, and Representation Stability

items.title: The category FI and FI-modules over a commutative ring
items.statement: Let $FI$ be the category whose objects are the finite sets and whose morphisms are the injections ([[def-category]]); it is equivalent to the full subcategory on the objects $[n]=\{1,\dots,n\}$, $n\ge0$, so that $\operatorname{End}_{FI}([n])\cong S_n$ ([[def-finite-symmetric-group-and-permutation-notation]]). An **FI-module over a commutative ring $k$** ([[def-commutative-ring]]) is a covariant functor $V\colon FI\to k\text{-Mod}$ ([[def-functor-and-contravariant-functor]], [[def-left-and-right-modules]]); write $V_S=V(S)$, $V_n=V([n])$ and $f_*=V(f)$ for a morphism $f$. Since $\operatorname{End}_{FI}([n])=S_n$, the maps $V_n\to V_n$ induced by permutations make $V_n$ a left $kS_n$-module ([[def-group-ring]]), and each $f_*\colon V_m\to V_n$ is equivariant for the conjugation homomorphism $S_m\to S_n$ determined by $f$. A **sub-FI-module** of $V$ is a subfunctor of $V$ ([[def-submodule]]), a **map of FI-modules** is a natural transformation, and kernels, images and cokernels are computed pointwise, so the FI-modules over $k$ inherit an abelian-category structure from $k\text{-Mod}$ ([[def-quotient-module]]). An **FB-module** over $k$ is a functor from the groupoid $FB$ of finite sets and bijections to $k\text{-Mod}$; an FB-module is determined up to isomorphism by the $kS_n$-modules $W_n$ and carries no transition maps.

items.title: Span, finite generation and generation degree of an FI-module
items.statement: Let $V$ be an FI-module over $k$ and let $\Sigma\subseteq\bigsqcup_S V_S$ be a set of elements. The **sub-FI-module generated by $\Sigma$**, written $\operatorname{span}_V(\Sigma)$, is the intersection of all sub-FI-modules of $V$ containing $\Sigma$; it is the smallest such sub-FI-module and consists of all finite $k$-linear combinations of elements $f_*(v)$ with $v\in\Sigma$ and $f$ a morphism of $FI$. Call $V$ **finitely generated** when $\operatorname{span}_V(\Sigma)=V$ for some finite $\Sigma$, and **generated in degree $\le d$** when $\operatorname{span}_V(V_{\le d})=V$, where $V_{\le d}=\bigsqcup_{|S|\le d}V_S$; the **generation degree** is the least such $d$, and $\infty$ when no such $d$ exists ([[def-generated-cyclic-finitely-generated-and-free-modules]]). Finite generation of $V$ and pointwise finite generation of the $k$-modules $V_S$ are different conditions: the latter is implied by the former ([[lem-generated-in-degree-d-is-a-quotient-of-free-fi-modules]]) but does not imply it, and no pointwise finite-dimensionality is built into either notion ([[def-submodule]] for the span).

items.title: The coinvariant functors $\Phi_a$ and the transition maps $T$
items.statement: A **graded $k[T]$-module** consists of $k$-modules $U_n$, $n\ge0$, together with $k$-linear maps $T\colon U_n\to U_{n+1}$ for all $n$. Fix $a\ge0$, a set $\mathbf a$ of cardinality $a$ and a functorial disjoint union. For an FI-module $V$ over $k$ and $n\ge0$ put $$\Phi_a(V)_n:=(V_{\mathbf a\sqcup n})_{S_n},$$ the coinvariants of the $kS_n$-module $V_{\mathbf a\sqcup n}$ ([[def-coinvariants-functor-of-a-group-module]], [[def-quotient-module]]). Any injection $f\colon n\to n+1$ gives an injection $\mathrm{id}_{\mathbf a}\sqcup f\colon\mathbf a\sqcup n\to\mathbf a\sqcup n+1$ and an induced map $\Phi_a(V)_n\to\Phi_a(V)_{n+1}$; postcomposition by $S_{n+1}$ shows that this map depends only on $f$ and $\mathrm{id}_{\mathbf a}$, because any two injections $n\to n+1$ differ by an element of $S_{n+1}$. Writing $T$ for it, $(\Phi_a(V),T)$ is a graded $k[T]$-module, and $\Phi_a$ is a functor from FI-modules to graded $k[T]$-modules. Each $\Phi_a$ is right exact in every degree, and is exact when $k$ contains $\mathbb Q$, since averaging over the finite groups $S_n$ splits the coinvariant quotient; in that case $\Phi_a(W)\subseteq\Phi_a(V)$ for every sub-FI-module $W\subseteq V$.

items.title: Injectivity, surjectivity and stability degree
items.statement: Let $V$ be an FI-module over $k$. The **injectivity degree** $\operatorname{inj-deg}(V)$ (respectively the **surjectivity degree** $\operatorname{surj-deg}(V)$) is the least $s\ge0$ such that for every $a\ge0$ the transition map $T\colon\Phi_a(V)_n\to\Phi_a(V)_{n+1}$ is injective (respectively surjective) for all $n\ge s$; the **stability degree** is $$\operatorname{stab-deg}(V):=\max\bigl(\operatorname{inj-deg}(V),\operatorname{surj-deg}(V)\bigr).$$ Each of the three is $+\infty$ when no such $s$ exists. Equivalently, $T\colon\Phi_a(V)_n\to\Phi_a(V)_{n+1}$ is an isomorphism for all $a\ge0$ and all $n\ge\operatorname{stab-deg}(V)$. The three bounds are kept distinct: stability degree is the max, and injectivity and surjectivity degree need not agree in examples.

items.title: Specht modules classify the irreducibles over every field of characteristic zero
items.statement: Let $F$ be a field of characteristic $0$ and $n\ge0$. The field-valued Specht modules $S^\lambda_F$, $\lambda\vdash n$, of [[def-polytabloid-specht-module-over-an-arbitrary-field]] are nonzero, irreducible and pairwise non-isomorphic, and every irreducible $F S_n$-module is isomorphic to exactly one of them; consequently, by Maschke, every finite-dimensional $F S_n$-module is a direct sum of copies of the $S^\lambda_F$, so the irreducible $F S_n$-modules are indexed by the partitions of $n$ and the $S^\lambda_F$ form a complete irredundant list. This is the constituent convention used throughout the pair: over $F=\mathbb C$ it specialises to the published complex classification, and over a general characteristic-zero field F it is proved using rational Specht models and extension Q -> F, not a scalar extension from C to F.

items.title: Weight of an FI-module over a field of characteristic zero
items.statement: Let $k$ be a field of characteristic $0$ and let $V$ be an FI-module over $k$ ([[def-fi-category-and-fi-module]]). For a partition $\lambda$ and $n\ge|\lambda|+\lambda_1$ put $\lambda[n]:=(n-|\lambda|,\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\dots)$, the first-row padding ([[def-first-row-padding-of-a-partition]]), and let $V(\lambda)_n$ denote the irreducible $kS_n$-module indexed by the partition $\lambda[n]$, i.e. $k\otimes_{\mathbb Q}S^{\lambda[n]}_{\mathbb Q}$, the scalar extension of its rational Specht model ([[thm-complex-specht-modules-are-irreducible]], [[lem-specht-modules-classify-irreducibles-over-characteristic-zero-fields]]). The **weight** of $V$ is $$\operatorname{weight}(V):=\sup\{|\lambda|:V(\lambda)_n\text{ occurs as a constituent of }V_n\text{ for some }n\ge|\lambda|+\lambda_1\},$$ the supremum over all pairs $(\lambda,n)$ as displayed; it is $0$ for $V=0$ and $+\infty$ when the set is unbounded. If $W$ is a subquotient of $V$ then $\operatorname{weight}(W)\le\operatorname{weight}(V)$.

items.title: The free FI-module $M(W)$ generated by an $S_m$-module
items.statement: Let $W$ be an FB-module over $k$, i.e. a family of $kS_m$-modules $W_m$ ([[def-fi-category-and-fi-module]]). The **free FI-module** $M(W)$ is the FI-module with $$M(W)_S:=\bigoplus_{T\subseteq S}W_T,$$ where $W_T$ denotes $W_{|T|}$ transported along a bijection $T\to[|T|]$ (well defined up to canonical isomorphism), and on an injection $f\colon S\to S'$ the map $M(W)_S\to M(W)_{S'}$ is the sum of the maps $W_T\to W_{f(T)}$ induced by $f|_T$ ([[def-direct-sum-of-a-family-of-modules]]). $M(-)$ is the left adjoint of the forgetful functor from FI-modules to FB-modules, so $$\operatorname{Hom}_{FI\text{-}Mod}(M(W),V)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{FB\text{-}Mod}(W,\pi V)$$ naturally in $V$; the unit sends $W_S$ to the summand $W_S$ of $M(W)_S$. As an $S_n$-module, $$M(W)_n\cong\bigoplus_{a=0}^{n}\operatorname{Ind}_{S_a\times S_{n-a}}^{S_n}\bigl(W_a\boxtimes k\bigr),$$ with $\boxtimes$ the external tensor product of modules for the direct factors and $\operatorname{Ind}$ the induced module built from $H$-covariant functions ([[def-induced-r-linear-g-module-by-h-covariant-functions]], [[def-outer-induction-product-for-symmetric-group-characters]], [[lem-character-ring-of-a-direct-product-is-the-tensor-product]], [[def-tensor-product-of-modules-by-generators-and-relations]]). For $m\ge0$, $M(m):=M(k[S_m])$ has as a $k$-basis the injections $m\to S$; for a partition $\lambda$ and a field $k$ of characteristic $0$, $M(\lambda):=M(S^\lambda_k)$.

items.title: Generation in bounded degree presents an FI-module as a quotient of free FI-modules
items.statement: Let $V$ be an FI-module over $k$. (a) For $v\in V_m$ the FI-module map $M(m)\to V$ sending the basis element $\mathrm{id}_m\in M(m)_m$ to $v$ has image $\operatorname{span}_V(v)$; more generally, for any $\Sigma\subseteq\bigsqcup_S V_S$ the canonical map $\bigoplus_{s\in\Sigma}M(|S_s|)\to V$ has image $\operatorname{span}_V(\Sigma)$. (b) $V$ is finitely generated if and only if there is a finite family $m_1,\dots,m_k\ge0$ with a surjection $M(m_1)\oplus\cdots\oplus M(m_k)\twoheadrightarrow V$; $V$ is generated in degree $\le d$ if and only if there is a surjection $\bigoplus_{i\in I}M(m_i)\twoheadrightarrow V$ with $m_i\le d$ for all $i$. In particular, if $V$ is generated in degree $\le d$ then the evaluation map $\bigoplus_{m\le d}M(V_m)\to V$ is surjective, where $V_m$ is regarded as an FB-module. (c) If $V$ is finitely generated, then $V_S$ is a finitely generated $k$-module for every finite set $S$.

items.title: Branching rule for Specht modules: adding or removing boxes in distinct columns
items.statement:
Let $F$ be a field of characteristic $0$, let $\lambda\vdash n$ and let $S^\lambda_F$ be the corresponding Specht module. (i) For every $k\ge0$ there is an isomorphism of $F S_{n+k}$-modules $$\operatorname{Ind}_{S_n	imes S_k}^{S_{n+k}} igl(S^\lambda_F oxtimes F igr)\cong igoplus_{\mu}S^\mu_F,$$ summed over the partitions $\mu\vdash n+k$ obtained from $\lambda$ by adding one box to each of $k$ different columns. (ii) For every $k\le n$ there is an isomorphism of $F S_{n-k}$-modules $$ igl(\operatorname{Res}^{S_n}_{S_{n-k}	imes S_k}S^\lambda_F igr)_{S_k}\cong igoplus_{
u}S^
u_F,$$ summed over the partitions $
u\vdash n-k$ obtained from $\lambda$ by removing one box from each of $k$ different columns. All multiplicities are $0$ or $1$.

items.title: Free FI-modules have computable stability degree and weight
items.statement: Let $W$ be an FB-module over $k$. Then $\operatorname{inj-deg}(M(W))=0$, and if $W_i=0$ for $i>m$ then $\operatorname{surj-deg}(M(W))\le m$; in particular $M(m)=M(k[S_m])$ has $\operatorname{inj-deg}(M(m))=0$ and $\operatorname{stab-deg}(M(m))=m$. If moreover $k$ is a field of characteristic $0$ and $\lambda$ is a partition, then $\operatorname{weight}(M(\lambda))=|\lambda|$ and $\operatorname{stab-deg}(M(\lambda))=\lambda_1$.

items.title: Bounded generation degree bounds surjectivity degree and weight
items.statement: Let $V$ be an FI-module over $k$. (a) Every quotient $V\twoheadrightarrow W$ satisfies $\operatorname{surj-deg}(W)\le\operatorname{surj-deg}(V)$. (b) If $V$ is generated in degree $\le d$, then $\operatorname{surj-deg}(V)\le d$. (c) If moreover $k$ is a field of characteristic $0$ and $V$ is generated in degree $\le d$, then $\operatorname{weight}(V)\le d$.

items.title: Tensor products of finitely generated FI-modules are finitely generated
items.statement: Let $V$ and $W$ be finitely generated FI-modules over $k$, with pointwise tensor product $(V\otimes W)_S=V_S\otimes_k W_S$. Then $V\otimes W$ is finitely generated. More precisely, if $V$ is generated in degree $\le m_1$ and $W$ in degree $\le m_2$, then $V\otimes W$ is generated in degree $\le m_1+m_2$.

items.title: Coinvariants detect vanishing of subquotients of bounded weight, and padded irreducibles stabilise
items.statement: Let $k$ be a field of characteristic $0$, let $\mu\vdash n$ and write $\mu=\lambda[n]$ as in the padding definition. (i) For $a\le n$, with $k_0:=n-a$, the $S_a$-representation $(V_\mu)_{S_{k_0}}$ is zero if and only if $n-a>\mu_1$, equivalently $(V(\lambda)_n)_{S_{n-a}}=0$ if and only if $a<|\lambda|$. (ii) If $n-a=\mu_1$ (that is, $a=|\lambda|$), then $(V(\lambda)_n)_{S_{n-a}}\cong V_\lambda$ as $S_{|\lambda|}$-modules. (iii) For fixed $\lambda$ and $a\ge|\lambda|$, the $S_a$-module $(V(\lambda)_n)_{S_{n-a}}$ is independent of $n$ once $n\ge a+\lambda_1$; in fact $(V(\lambda)_n)_{S_{n-a}}\cong\operatorname{Ind}_{S_{|\lambda|}\times S_{a-|\lambda|}}^{S_a}(V_\lambda\boxtimes k)$ throughout that range. (iv) If $V$ is an FI-module over $k$ with $\operatorname{weight}(V)\le a$, then every subquotient $W_n$ of the $S_n$-module $V_n$ satisfies $W_n=0\iff(W_n)_{S_{n-a}}=0$.

items.title: A stability degree bounds the first row of every padding tail
items.statement: Let $V$ be an FI-module over a field $k$ of characteristic $0$, with $s:=\operatorname{stab-deg}(V)<\infty$. Then for every $n\ge0$ every irreducible constituent $V(\lambda)_n$ of the $S_n$-module $V_n$ satisfies $\lambda_1\le s$; equivalently, the second row of the full Specht diagram has length at most s, since the first row of the padding tail is the second row of the full diagram.

items.title: FI-modules over a Noetherian $\mathbb Q$-algebra form a Noetherian category
items.statement: Let $k$ be a commutative Noetherian ring containing $\mathbb Q$ ([[def-noetherian-ring]]), and let $V$ be a finitely generated FI-module over $k$ ([[def-finite-generation-and-generation-degree-of-an-fi-module]]). Then every sub-FI-module $W\subseteq V$ is finitely generated; that is, the category of FI-modules over $k$ is Noetherian. The hypothesis that $k$ contains $\mathbb Q$ is used only through the exactness of the functors $\Phi_a$ and through restriction of scalars to $\mathbb Q$.

items.title: Uniform representation stability for consistent sequences of $S_n$-modules
items.statement: Let $k$ be a field of characteristic $0$. A **consistent sequence** is a sequence $(V_n,\varphi_n)_{n\ge0}$ in which $V_n$ is a finite-dimensional $kS_n$-module and $\varphi_n\colon V_n\to V_{n+1}$ is $S_n$-equivariant, $V_{n+1}$ being regarded as an $S_n$-module by restriction along the standard inclusion $S_n\hookrightarrow S_{n+1}$; an FI-module $V$ with finite-dimensional values determines the consistent sequence $(V_n,f_*)$ for the standard inclusions. The sequence is **uniformly representation stable with stable range $n\ge N$** when (I) $\varphi_n$ is injective for all $n\ge N$; (II) the $S_{n+1}$-span of $\varphi_n(V_n)$ is all of $V_{n+1}$ for all $n\ge N$; and (III) writing $V_n\cong\bigoplus_{\lambda}c_{\lambda,n}V(\lambda)_n$ with padded irreducibles $V(\lambda)_n$ ([[def-first-row-padding-of-a-partition]]), the multiplicity $c_{\lambda,n}$ is independent of $n$ for every fixed $\lambda$ and all $n\ge N$. The sequence is uniformly representation stable when it is so for some $N$. All three conditions are part of the definition; (II) is not implied by (I) and (III).

items.title: Weight and stability degree give a uniform representation-stability range
items.statement: Let $k$ be a field of characteristic $0$ and let $V$ be an FI-module over $k$ with finite-dimensional values, weight $d=\operatorname{weight}(V)$ and stability degree $s=\operatorname{stab-deg}(V)$. Then the consistent sequence $(V_n,\varphi_n)$ is uniformly representation stable with stable range $n\ge d+s$.

items.title: Finite generation is equivalent to uniform representation stability
items.statement: Let $k$ be a field of characteristic $0$ and let $V$ be an FI-module over $k$ with finite-dimensional values. Then $V$ is finitely generated if and only if the consistent sequence $(V_n,\varphi_n)$ is uniformly representation stable.

items.title: Character polynomials in the cycle counts $X_i$
items.statement: For $i\ge1$ and $n\ge0$ let $X_i\colon S_n\to\mathbb N$ be the class function sending a permutation to the number of its $i$-cycles ([[def-permutation-support-disjoint-cycles-and-cycle-type]]); thus $X_1(\sigma)$ is the number of fixed points. A **character polynomial** is a polynomial $P\in\mathbb Q[X_1,X_2,\dots]$ in finitely many of the variables $X_i$, its **weighted degree** being defined by $\deg X_i:=i$ ([[def-polynomial-ring-over-a-commutative-ring]]). Since the class functions on $S_n$ form a $\mathbb Q$-algebra under pointwise multiplication ([[def-class-function-and-the-space-of-complex-class-functions]]), every character polynomial $P$ defines a class function $P\colon S_n\to\mathbb Q$ for every $n\ge0$. The expression is not unique on a single $S_n$, since $X_i$ vanishes identically for $i>n$; it is unique in the limit: if $P$ and $Q$ agree as functions on $S_n$ for infinitely many $n$, then $P=Q$. A sequence $(\chi_n)$ of class functions with $\chi_n$ a class function on $S_n$ is **eventually polynomial** when there are $N$ and a character polynomial $P$ with $\chi_n(\sigma)=P(\sigma)$ for all $n\ge N$ and all $\sigma\in S_n$.

items.title: Padded irreducible characters are eventually given by character polynomials
items.statement: For every partition $\lambda$ there is a character polynomial $P_\lambda\in\mathbb Q[X_1,X_2,\dots]$ of weighted degree at most $|\lambda|$ such that for every $n\ge|\lambda|+\lambda_1$ and every $\sigma\in S_n$ $$\chi^{\lambda[n]}(\sigma)=P_\lambda(X_1(\sigma),X_2(\sigma),\dots),$$ where $\chi^{\lambda[n]}$ is the character of the irreducible Specht module $S^{\lambda[n]}$.

items.title: Finitely generated FI-modules have eventual character polynomials
items.statement: Let $k$ be a field of characteristic $0$ and let $V$ be a finitely generated FI-module over $k$ with finite-dimensional values, weight $d=\operatorname{weight}(V)$ and stability degree $s=\operatorname{stab-deg}(V)$. Then there is a unique character polynomial $P_V\in\mathbb Q[X_1,X_2,\dots]$ of weighted degree at most $d$ such that $$\chi_{V_n}(\sigma)=P_V(X_1(\sigma),X_2(\sigma),\dots)$$ for every $n\ge s+d$ and every $\sigma\in S_n$; here $\chi_{V_n}$ is the character of the $kS_n$-module $V_n$, and $\mathbb Q\subseteq k$ is the prime field.

items.title: Each padded irreducible family is realised by a finitely generated FI-module
items.statement: Let $k$ be a field of characteristic $0$ and let $\lambda$ be a partition with $|\lambda|=m$. There is an FI-module $V(\lambda)$ over $k$ with $$V(\lambda)_n\cong\begin{cases}V_{\lambda[n]},&n\ge m+\lambda_1,\ \varnothing,&n<m+\lambda_1.\end{cases}$$ It is finitely generated in degree $m+\lambda_1$, has $\operatorname{weight}(V(\lambda))=m$ and $\operatorname{stab-deg}(V(\lambda))=\lambda_1$.

items.title: Dimensions of finitely generated FI-modules are eventually polynomial
items.statement: Let $k$ be a field of characteristic $0$ and let $V$ be a finitely generated FI-module over $k$ with finite-dimensional values, weight $d$ and stability degree $s$, with character polynomial $P_V$ as above. Then $$\dim_kV_n=P_V(n,0,0,\dots)$$ for every $n\ge s+d$; in particular $\dim_kV_n$ is given by a polynomial in $n$ of degree at most $d$ for all sufficiently large $n$.
