items.title: Specializations of symmetric functions and the series $\sigma$
items.statement: Work in the algebra of symmetric functions over Q in an alphabet X, in which the power sums p_1,p_2,... are algebraically independent generators. A specialization is an algebra homomorphism f |-> f[A] to a commutative Q-algebra; it is determined by the sequence (p_k[A])_{k>=1}, and conversely every sequence of values gives one. For specializations A,B define p_k[A+B]:=p_k[A]+p_k[B], p_k[-A]:=-p_k[A] and p_k[AB]:=p_k[A]p_k[B]. For a coefficient multiplicity c write c dot A with p_k[c dot A]:=c p_k[A]. Distinguish this from a one-letter alphabet t, for which p_k[t]:=t^k and therefore p_k[tA]=t^k p_k[A]; all occurrences of tX, t^{-1} and sigma[t] below use this one-letter convention. The symbol 1 is the one-letter alphabet with p_k[1]=1, and -1 is its plethystic negative, with p_k[-1]=-1 (not the ordinary one-letter alphabet whose letter is minus one). Write f[A+B], f[-A], f[AB] and f[c dot A] for the corresponding specializations. Define X^perp to be the specialization with f[X^perp]:=f^perp for all f, where f^perp denotes the adjoint of multiplication by f with respect to the Hall inner product. Define the series sigma[X]:=sum_{n>=0} h_n[X]. Sigma is interpreted in the graded completion, or with a formal degree variable; every use of Hall pairing with a polynomial means its finite degree truncation. No convergence of a scalar infinite sum is asserted.

items.title: Threefold Schur coefficients $c^\delta_{a,b,c}$
items.statement: For partitions delta,a,b,c with |delta|=|a|+|b|+|c| define the threefold Schur coefficient c^delta_{a,b,c}:=[s_delta] s_a s_b s_c, the coefficient of s_delta in the ordinary product of the three Schur functions. These are nonnegative integers, they are symmetric in a,b,c, and they satisfy the iterated Littlewood-Richardson identity c^delta_{a,b,c}=sum_phi c^phi_{a,b} c^delta_{phi,c}=sum_psi c^psi_{a,c}c^delta_{psi,b}, the sums over partitions phi (respectively psi) of |a|+|b| (respectively |a|+|c|). Equivalently c^delta_{a,b,c}=<s_a s_b s_c | s_delta>.

items.title: The Jacobi–Trudi completion $s_\mu$, the operators $U_n$ and $V$, and $\operatorname{stab}(\alpha,\beta)$
items.statement: Let alpha=(alpha_1,...,alpha_k) be a partition and n>=0; the padded sequence is alpha[n]:=(n-|alpha|,alpha_1,...,alpha_k). For an arbitrary finite sequence of integers mu=(mu_1,...,mu_m) define s_mu by the Jacobi-Trudi determinant det(h_{mu_j+i-j})_{1<=i,j<=m} with h_k=0 for k<0, as in the source; every such determinant is either 0 or +-1 times a Schur function. Define Z-linear endomorphisms of the ring of symmetric functions by U_n(s_lambda):=s_{lambda[n]} and V(s_lambda):=s_{lambda+(1)} on the Schur basis, extended linearly. Finally, for partitions alpha,beta define stab(alpha,beta) to be the least n_0>=0 such that s_{alpha[n_0+k]}*s_{beta[n_0+k]}=V^k(s_{alpha[n_0]}*s_{beta[n_0]}) as elements of the symmetric function ring for all k>0, where * is the internal product; stab(alpha,beta) is not shown to exist by this definition alone (its existence and value are the sharp global threshold theorem).

items.title: Schur functions on sums and products of alphabets
items.statement: For all partitions lambda,mu,nu and all specializations A,B: (a) s_lambda[A+B] = sum_{mu,nu} c^lambda_{mu,nu} s_mu[A] s_nu[B], the sum over pairs with |mu|+|nu|=|lambda|; (b) s_lambda[AB] = sum_{mu,nu} g^lambda_{mu,nu} s_mu[A] s_nu[B], the sum over pairs with |mu|=|nu|=|lambda|, where g^lambda_{mu,nu} is the ordinary Kronecker coefficient. Both sums are finite.

items.title: The series $\sigma$: product formula, Cauchy identity, adjunction and reproducing kernel
items.statement: Let sigma[X]=sum_{n>=0}h_n[X]. (1) sigma[X]=prod_{x in X}(1-x)^{-1} and sigma[-X]=prod_{x in X}(1-x); in particular sigma[t]=(1-t)^{-1} and sigma[-t]=1-t for a scalar t. (2) sigma[A+B]=sigma[A]sigma[B] and, for the one-letter alphabet t, sigma[tA]=sum_{n>=0}t^n h_n[A]. (3) Cauchy identity: sigma[XY]=sum_lambda s_lambda[X]s_lambda[Y]. (4) For every specialization A the operator sigma[AX^perp] is the adjoint of multiplication by sigma[AX]: sigma[AX^perp]f[X]=f[X+A] for all f. (5) Reproducing kernel: <sigma[AX] | f[X]>_X = f[A] for all f.

items.title: Vertex-operator generating series for the padded Schur functions
items.statement: Let alpha be a partition and t a formal variable. With the Jacobi-Trudi convention of the first definition item for the integer sequences alpha[n]=(n-|alpha|,alpha_1,alpha_2,...), one has the identity of formal Laurent series with coefficients in the symmetric function ring: sum_{n in Z} s_{alpha[n]}[X] t^n = sigma[tX] . s_alpha[tX - 1] = t^{|alpha|} . sigma[tX] . s_alpha[X - t^{-1}], where s_alpha[tX-1] is evaluated through the specialization p_k |-> t^k p_k[X] - 1 and s_alpha[X-t^{-1}] through p_k |-> p_k[X]-t^{-k}. Equivalently, sum_{n in Z} s_{alpha[n]}[X]t^n = sigma[tX] sum_{mu: alpha/mu a vertical strip} (-1)^{|alpha|-|mu|} t^{|mu|} s_mu[X]. (This is the growth paper's identity (6) p. 7, displayed there as t^{|alpha|}Gamma(t|X)s_alpha[X] = sigma[tX]s_alpha[tX-1].)

items.title: The Jacobi–Trudi completion is compatible with the internal product
items.statement: For partitions alpha,beta with a=|alpha|, b=|beta|, define R_{alpha,beta}[Z]=<s_alpha[A]s_beta[B] | sigma[ZAB+ZA+ZB+AB]>_{A,B}. This is a finite symmetric-function polynomial of Z-degree at most a+b. For every n>=0, (U_n s_alpha)*(U_n s_beta)=U_n R_{alpha,beta}, where U_n uses Jacobi-Trudi completion, including when the padded sequences are not partitions. Equivalently sum_{n>=0}(U_n s_alpha)*(U_n s_beta)t^n=sigma[tX]R_{alpha,beta}[tX-1], with t a one-letter formal alphabet. The same polynomial is the finite Littlewood expression R=sum_{delta,epsilon,tau} ((s_delta s_tau)^perp s_alpha) ((s_epsilon s_tau)^perp s_beta) (s_delta*s_epsilon), all factors evaluated in Z.

items.title: Murnaghan stability for Kronecker coefficients
items.statement: Fix partitions alpha, beta, gamma. Put m(gamma):=max{|alpha|+alpha_1, |beta|+beta_1, |gamma|+gamma_1} and, for n >= m(gamma), let g_n(alpha,beta,gamma):=g^{gamma[n]}_{alpha[n],beta[n]} be the multiplicity of the Specht module V_{gamma[n]} in V_{alpha[n]} (x) V_{beta[n]}; set g_n(alpha,beta,gamma):=0 for n<m(gamma). Then the sequence n |-> g_n(alpha,beta,gamma) is eventually constant. More precisely there is a finite set S(alpha,beta) of partitions and nonnegative integers bar-g^gamma_{alpha,beta} for gamma in S(alpha,beta), with bar-g^gamma_{alpha,beta}:=0 for gamma not in S(alpha,beta), such that g_n(alpha,beta,gamma)=bar-g^gamma_{alpha,beta} for all sufficiently large n and every partition gamma. No explicit bound on the stable rank is asserted here (the sharp global bound is a separate claim).

items.title: The reduced (stable) Kronecker coefficient $\bar g^\gamma_{\alpha,\beta}$
items.statement: For partitions alpha, beta, gamma define the reduced (stable) Kronecker coefficient bar-g^gamma_{alpha,beta} to be the eventual value of the padded sequence n |-> g_n(alpha,beta,gamma) furnished by the Murnaghan stability theorem; equivalently bar-g^gamma_{alpha,beta} := lim_{n to infinity} g^{gamma[n]}_{alpha[n],beta[n]}, where the sequence is defined for n>=max{|alpha|+alpha_1,|beta|+beta_1,|gamma|+gamma_1} and set to 0 below. Well-definedness is exactly the Murnaghan stability theorem. Two immediate conventions: bar-g^gamma_{alpha,beta}=bar-g^gamma_{beta,alpha} (commutativity of the tensor product), and for fixed alpha,beta only finitely many gamma have bar-g^gamma_{alpha,beta} nonzero. Values used later and verified in the source's introduction for alpha=beta=(2): bar-g^{(2)}_{(2),(2)}=2 and bar-g^{(4)}_{(2),(2)}=1.

items.title: Brion's formula for the reduced Kronecker coefficients
items.statement: For all partitions alpha,beta,gamma: bar-g^gamma_{alpha,beta} = < s_alpha[X] s_beta[Y] | sigma[XY] s_gamma[XY+X+Y] >_{X,Y}, the inner product being the extension of the Hall inner product to symmetric functions in two alphabets X,Y. Equivalently, introducing a third alphabet Z, sum_{alpha,beta,gamma} bar-g^gamma_{alpha,beta} s_alpha[X]s_beta[Y]s_gamma[Z] = sigma[XYZ+XY+XZ+YZ], the symmetric Cauchy-type identity of the source.

items.title: The nonnegative expansion of a reduced Kronecker coefficient
items.statement: For all partitions alpha,beta,gamma one has the finite nonnegative expansion bar-g^gamma_{alpha,beta} = sum_{mu,lambda,eta,rho,theta,pi} c^gamma_{mu,theta,pi} c^alpha_{rho,lambda,theta} c^beta_{rho,eta,pi} g^mu_{lambda,eta}, the sum over all six-tuples of partitions (only finitely many summands are nonzero), where the c's are threefold Schur coefficients and the g's are ordinary Kronecker coefficients. Consequences: (i) bar-g^gamma_{alpha,beta}>0 if and only if there exist partitions mu,lambda,eta,rho,theta,pi with c^gamma_{mu,theta,pi}, c^alpha_{rho,lambda,theta}, c^beta_{rho,eta,pi} and g^mu_{lambda,eta} all positive; (ii) for every nonzero summand the degree equations |alpha|=|rho|+|lambda|+|theta|, |beta|=|rho|+|eta|+|pi|, |gamma|=|mu|+|theta|+|pi| and |mu|=|lambda|=|eta| hold; (iii) for fixed alpha,beta the index set is finite because rho,lambda,theta are contained in alpha, rho,eta,pi in beta, and |mu|=|lambda|. All summands are nonnegative integers, so no cancellation occurs.

items.title: The Murnaghan expansion at every admissible rank
items.statement: For all partitions alpha,beta and every n >= max{|alpha|+alpha_1, |beta|+beta_1}: s_{alpha[n]} * s_{beta[n]} = sum_gamma bar-g^gamma_{alpha,beta} s_{gamma[n]}, an identity in the symmetric function ring, where s_{gamma[n]} is the Jacobi-Trudi determinant attached to the integer sequence gamma[n] (zero or +-1 times a Schur function). For an ordinary partition delta of n, the coefficient is g^{delta}_{alpha[n],beta[n]}=sum_gamma bar-g^gamma_{alpha,beta}<s_{gamma[n]},s_delta>, where each Hall factor is zero or a sign from Jacobi-Trudi straightening. At small admissible ranks the signed terms can cancel or coalesce; individual coefficients need not yet equal their reduced values. The range displayed is precisely the set of n for which alpha[n] and beta[n] are partitions.

items.title: Murnaghan–Littlewood: top-degree reduced coefficients are Littlewood–Richardson coefficients
items.statement: Let alpha,beta,gamma be partitions with |gamma|=|alpha|+|beta|. Then bar-g^gamma_{alpha,beta}=c^gamma_{alpha,beta}, the Littlewood-Richardson coefficient. In particular bar-g^{alpha+beta}_{alpha,beta}=c^{alpha+beta}_{alpha,beta}=1.

items.title: The support of the reduced Kronecker coefficients satisfies the size triangle inequalities
items.statement: If bar-g^gamma_{alpha,beta}>0 then |alpha| <= |beta|+|gamma|, |beta| <= |alpha|+|gamma| and |gamma| <= |alpha|+|beta| (Murnaghan's inequalities). Hence the support Supp(alpha,beta) of the nonzero reduced coefficients with fixed alpha,beta lies in the triangle region of the weight lattice.

items.title: The exact global stabilization threshold for a fixed Kronecker product
items.statement: For all partitions alpha,beta, with missing parts zero: stab(alpha,beta)=N:=|alpha|+|beta|+alpha_1+beta_1. At every n>=N all support labels gamma[n] are ordinary partitions, and the full product has the fixed nonnegative Schur expansion sum_gamma bar-g^gamma_{alpha,beta}s_{gamma[n]}; the family is V-stable from N onward. If both alpha and beta are nonempty, N-1 is admissible and the product at N is not V of the product at N-1: the coefficient of s_{(alpha+beta)[N]} is 1, its first two parts are equal, and no such Schur basis vector lies in the image of V. If exactly one input is empty, N is already the least ordinary input rank; the same image obstruction at N excludes any earlier stabilization index in the Jacobi-Trudi convention of the Definition. If both inputs are empty, N=0, s_(n)*s_(n)=s_(n) (including s_(0)=1) and V^n(1)=s_(n), so stabilization begins at zero and no negative-rank product is invoked. No sharpness for an individual coefficient is claimed.

decline_pages.title: Murnaghan Stability via FI-Modules — Examples

items.title: Murnaghan stability for $\alpha=\beta=(2)$, ranks 4 to 9
items.statement: For alpha=beta=(2) the source's introduction displays s_{2,2}*s_{2,2}=s_4+s_{1,1,1,1}+s_{2,2}; s_{3,2}*s_{3,2}=s_5+s_{2,1,1,1}+s_{3,2}+s_{4,1}+s_{3,1,1}+s_{2,2,1}; s_{4,2}*s_{4,2}=s_6+s_{3,1,1,1}+2s_{4,2}+s_{5,1}+s_{4,1,1}+2s_{3,2,1}+s_{2,2,2}; s_{5,2}*s_{5,2}=s_7+s_{4,1,1,1}+2s_{5,2}+s_{6,1}+s_{5,1,1}+2s_{4,2,1}+s_{3,2,2}+s_{4,3}+s_{3,3,1}; s_{6,2}*s_{6,2}=s_8+s_{5,1,1,1}+2s_{6,2}+s_{7,1}+s_{6,1,1}+2s_{5,2,1}+s_{4,2,2}+s_{5,3}+s_{4,3,1}+s_{4,4}; s_{7,2}*s_{7,2}=s_9+s_{6,1,1,1}+2s_{7,2}+s_{8,1}+s_{7,1,1}+2s_{6,2,1}+s_{5,2,2}+s_{6,3}+s_{5,3,1}+s_{5,4}; and the stable row s_{bullet,2}*s_{bullet,2}=s_bullet+s_{bullet,1,1,1}+2s_{bullet,2}+s_{bullet,1}+s_{bullet,1,1}+2s_{bullet,2,1}+s_{bullet,2,2}+s_{bullet,3}+s_{bullet,3,1}+s_{bullet,4}. Consequently the reduced coefficients for the pair ((2),(2)) are bar-g^gamma_{(2),(2)} = 1,1,2,1,1,2,1,1,1,1 for gamma = empty, (1,1,1), (2), (1), (1,1), (2,1), (2,2), (3), (3,1), (4) respectively, and bar-g^gamma=0 for all other gamma; in particular bar-g^{(2)}_{(2),(2)}=2 and bar-g^{(4)}_{(2),(2)}=1. The displayed data also verify directly, for this pair, that the whole product is V-stable at rank 8 and not at rank 7: applying V (adding a box to the first row of every Schur function) to the rank-8 expansion s_{6,2}*s_{6,2} reproduces the rank-9 expansion s_{7,2}*s_{7,2} term by term, whereas applying V to the rank-7 expansion s_{5,2}*s_{5,2} misses the single term s_{4,4} of s_{6,2}*s_{6,2}, the other nine terms matching term by term (the rank-7 product does contain s_{4,3} and s_{3,3,1}, whose V-images s_{5,3} and s_{4,3,1} are present at rank 8). The proved threshold theorem establishes V-stability for every rank from 8 onward, with exact least global index 8=|(2)|+|(2)|+2+2; the displayed finite data independently verify the six listed products and the failure of the preceding step.

items.title: A global product threshold is not a per-coefficient sharpness claim
items.statement: For alpha=beta=(2) the individual coefficient bar-g^{(2)}_{(2),(2)}=2 is already attained at rank 6: the rank-6 product s_{4,2}*s_{4,2} contains 2s_{4,2}, i.e. g^{(4,2)}_{(4,2),(4,2)}=2, which is the stable value bar-g^{(2)}_{(2),(2)}=2 read off from the stable row. Thus this single coefficient stops growing strictly before the whole product stabilizes: the rank-7 and rank-8 products still contain 2s_{5,2} and 2s_{6,2} respectively, matching the stable value, while the whole product is not even V-stable at rank 7 (applying V to s_{5,2}*s_{5,2} misses the term s_{4,4} occurring in s_{6,2}*s_{6,2}) and only becomes V-stable at rank 8. Therefore the exact global product threshold (the least rank from which the whole product is V-stable) is not a per-coefficient sharpness statement: single coefficients may stabilize earlier, and no claim that a coefficient first becomes stable at the global threshold is valid.

decline_pages.title: Relative Smooth Triangulation And Bundle Fitting

items.title: Relative smooth triangulations, strong approximation and bundle fitting
items.statement: A finite geometric simplicial complex $K$ is considered with its Euclidean realization and induced metric; subcomplex, closure, star and link terminology follows [[def-simplicial-subcomplex-star-closure-and-link]]. For $b\in|K|$ the **tangent star** is the union of the tangent cones at $b$ of all simplices containing $b$, that is, the rays locally contained in the closed star. A map $f:|K|\to M$ is **piecewise smooth** when every restriction $f|\sigma$ to a closed simplex extends smoothly to a neighbourhood in its affine hull and the extensions agree on common faces; in a target coordinate chart the differential $df_b$ is then the well-defined continuous piecewise linear map on the tangent star that equals $D(f|\sigma)(b)$ on the cone of each simplex $\sigma$ containing $b$. A **smooth immersion of a complex** requires $df_b$ injective on the entire tangent star at every point, not merely on each simplex tangent space; a **smooth embedding** requires in addition that $f$ be a homeomorphism onto its image, and a **finite smooth triangulation** of $M$ is such an embedding onto $M$. A corner-adapted triangulation must be face compatible: every local corner face is the image of a subcomplex, and the differential fan maps the source tangent star homeomorphically onto the appropriate tangent orthant, or its specified face sector. After an ambient Euclidean realization of the target, or in a fixed finite family of compact target chart patches, $g:K'\to M$ on a finite subdivision $K'$ of $K$ is a **strong $C^1$ $\delta$-approximation** to $f$ if $\sup_b|g(b)-f(b)|<\delta$ and $|dg_b(v)-df_b(v)|<\delta|v|$ for all $b$ and all tangent-star vectors $v$. A relative approximation **fixed on $L$** means $g|_{|L|}=f|_{|L|}$, subdivision of $L$ permitted unless explicitly prohibited. **Shape control** means a positive lower bound on $r(\sigma)/\operatorname{diam}\sigma$ for every positive-dimensional simplex, where $r(\sigma)$ is the distance from the barycentre to the relative boundary; it is not asserted for arbitrary iterated barycentric subdivisions. Two embeddings $f_i:K_i\to M$ **fit in a subcomplex** if the inverse images of $f_1(|K_1|)\cap f_2(|K_2|)$ are subcomplexes $L_i$ and $f_2^{-1}f_1:L_1\to L_2$ is a simplexwise affine isomorphism; the fit is **full** if every simplex all of whose vertices belong to $L_i$ belongs to $L_i$. Gluing along that isomorphism defines the union realization and union map. For a smooth bundle $\pi:E\to B$ and a supplied base triangulation $h:D\to B$, a **projection-preserving diagram** consists of $F:K\to E$ and a map $r:K\to D$ that is affine on each simplex into a simplex of the original $D$ and satisfies $\pi F=hr$; the affine/PL requirement does not require domain vertices to map to vertices of the original fixed base complex. Fitting preserves the projection when all modified maps satisfy the same equality with the original $h$ and the original affine $r$ restricted to their subdivisions; a fixed relative bundle piece must already carry such a diagram. No generic smooth map is called a bundle merely because it is proper. For relative extension on a compact manifold with corners, supplied boundary data are admissible only when they are compatible on all corner-face intersections and satisfy the tangent-orthant condition above; the extension keeps their pointwise parametrization, with compatible subdivisions permitted, and no extension of arbitrary incompatible boundary data is asserted.

items.title: Whole-star smooth embeddings are stable under strong piecewise $C^1$ approximation
items.statement: Let $K$ be finite and $f:K\to\mathbb R^q$ a whole-star smooth immersion in the sense of [[def-relative-smooth-triangulation-and-projection-preserving-fitting]]. There is $\delta>0$ such that every strong piecewise $C^1$ $\delta$-approximation $g:K'\to\mathbb R^q$, on any finite subdivision $K'$, is a whole-star immersion. If $f$ is also an embedding, $\delta$ may be chosen so that $g$ is an embedding. The subdivision need not have a mesh or shape bound.

items.title: Shape-controlled secants and relative piecewise smooth extension
items.statement:
Let $K$ be a finite geometric complex and $f:K\to\mathbb R^q$ piecewise smooth in the sense of [[def-relative-smooth-triangulation-and-projection-preserving-fitting]]. There are subdivisions $K_m$ agreeing on every original face, with mesh tending to zero and a single lower thickness bound $\theta>0$ for every positive-dimensional simplex, whose secant maps $S_m$, defined by affine interpolation of the values of $f$ at vertices, converge strongly in piecewise $C^1$ to $f$.

If $L\subset K$ is a subcomplex and $U$ an open neighbourhood of $|L|$, the approximation can instead be chosen pointwise equal to $f$ on a neighbourhood of $|L|$ and equal to a secant map outside $U$, on shape-controlled subdivisions; subdivision of $L$ is permitted and does not alter $f$ there, and every affine target-plane constraint already satisfied by $f$ on original simplices is preserved.

There is also a local extension statement: given a finite subcomplex $A\subset K$, a sufficiently small strong approximation $g$ to $f|_A$ on any subdivision extends to a prescribed small strong approximation $G$ to $f$ on a subdivision of $K$, with $G=f$ and with the original simplices unchanged outside the closed star of $A$. The permitted error of $g$ depends on the requested error and the finite original simplices, not on the shape of the subdivision of $A$. If the correction $g-f$ has zero component under an affine linear target map $p$ on $A$, then the extended correction has zero $p$ component everywhere. This last extension does not assert a shape bound on its coned simplices.

items.title: Corner-adapted strong approximations preserve orthant sides
items.statement:
Let $F:K\to[0,\infty)^c\times\mathbb R^{n-c}$ be a finite whole-star smooth embedding, and write $\rho_iF$ for its first $c$ coordinate functions. Assume for each original simplex $\sigma$ and each $i$ that $Z_{i,\sigma}=\{x\in\sigma:\rho_iF(x)=0\}$ is a union of faces and that, at every $b\in Z_{i,\sigma}$, the linear form $d(\rho_iF)_b$ on the tangent cone of $\sigma$ is nonnegative with zero set precisely the tangent cone of $Z_{i,\sigma}$. These are the adapted face/tangent conditions, not merely simplex rank conditions.

There is $\delta>0$ such that every strong $\delta$-approximation $G$ preserving each of these coordinate planes on the specified zero subcomplexes maps all of $K$ into the same closed orthant and has exactly the same coordinate zero sets. It is an embedding for this choice of $\delta$. Thus plane-preserving fitting and extension can be used in corner charts when the initial pieces satisfy these adapted face conditions.

items.title: Finite smooth fitting with exact bundle projection and protected regions
items.statement:
Let $F:K\to M$ and $G:L\to M$ be whole-star smooth embeddings of finite complexes into a smooth manifold without boundary. Given any positive strong $C^1$ tolerance, there are approximations on finite subdivisions fitting in a full subcomplex whose union is a whole-star smooth embedding.

The same conclusion holds for bundle diagrams $\pi F=hr_K$, $\pi G=hr_L$ over a fixed whole-star smooth base embedding $h:D\to B$, when all relevant images are in a smooth bundle with product trivializations. The final approximations satisfy these same diagrams with $h$ and $r_K,r_L$ unchanged as point maps, so the bundle projection is preserved exactly. The union map has the induced affine map to $D$.

The construction may be supported in a prescribed open neighbourhood $V$ of the new piece being fitted, including only the old pieces whose images meet that neighbourhood. In particular it fixes a closed protected region $R$ pointwise whenever all newly processed pieces and their required closed stars have images in $V$, with $\overline V\cap R=\varnothing$, and the maps already fit on the pieces outside this support. This is the fixed-collar relative interface: it does not assert arbitrary pointwise fixed-side fitting without the neighbourhood/separation hypotheses. Additional local affine plane constraints are preserved if the chosen charts make them coordinate planes and the already supplied diagrams respect them. For corner targets the same construction applies when all pieces satisfy the adapted face/tangent hypotheses of [[lem-corner-adapted-strong-approximations-remain-in-the-same-orthant]] in these charts; that lemma proves every altered piece remains in its original orthant.

items.title: Finite smooth triangulation of compact corners, relative to admissible boundary data
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice as an ambient hypothesis; the finite construction and the ODE interfaces below use no additional choice, so this hypothesis is dispensable. A smooth manifold with corners here is Hausdorff and second countable, with charts in relatively open subsets of $[0,\infty)^c\times\mathbb R^{n-c}$ and transition maps smoothly extendible with invertible derivative at corner points; transitions preserve the local depth and its face germs. Let $M$ be compact. Then $M$ has a finite corner-adapted whole-star smooth triangulation. Every local corner face, and any specified finite union of such closed faces, is a subpolyhedron.

If the total boundary already has a finite piecewise smooth triangulation $f:L\to\partial M$ compatible on all local face intersections, with its differential fan giving a homeomorphism onto the union of boundary faces of the tangent orthant at each point, the triangulation extends to $M$, pointwise preserving $f$ with compatible subdivisions allowed. In the resulting finite union construction all intersections may be made full subcomplexes. The same relative conclusion applies to a fixed triangulated closed neighbourhood piece whose smaller protected subcomplex lies in its relative interior: fitting is performed away from that protected subcomplex. No extension of arbitrary incompatible boundary data is asserted.

items.title: Finite smooth bundle triangulation over a fixed base, relative to a supplied collar diagram
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\pi:E\to B$ be a smooth bundle with compact total space, compact smooth base and compact smooth fibre, permitting corners. A bundle here comes with finite smooth local product trivializations, whose transition maps preserve all local source/target corner faces; a boundary face in a product chart is either a base face or a fibre face. Let $h:D\to B$ be a supplied finite corner-adapted whole-star smooth triangulation.

Then there is a finite corner-adapted whole-star smooth triangulation $F:K\to E$ and a piecewise affine map $r:K\to D$ with $\pi F=hr$. Thus the actual bundle projection is PL over the fixed base parametrization. Refining base pieces for local construction does not change $h$ or the original complex $D$ in the final diagram: $r$ on a domain simplex is affine into a simplex of the original $D$.

The construction is relative to any supplied finite diagram $C:J\to E$, $\pi C=hr_J$, embedding onto a closed neighbourhood of a protected subpolyhedron $R$ contained in its relative interior, provided the fitting supports of the remaining pieces can be chosen disjoint from $R$. In particular this applies when $C$ is an already triangulated collar neighbourhood of the entire boundary and $R$ is a smaller collar: the original boundary and all its corner-face intersections are kept pointwise, with compatible subdivisions allowed. All union intersections are full subcomplexes.

This relative contract requires the collar diagram, not just an arbitrary triangulation of the boundary without any projection-preserving neighbourhood extension. Nor does proper smoothness of $\pi$ alone replace the supplied bundle trivializations.

decline_pages.title: Sequences and Limits

items.title: Sequences of reals: bounded, eventually, frequently, tails, subsequences
Convergence depends only on the tail
A sequence has at most one limit
Every convergent sequence is bounded
Every convergent sequence is Cauchy
A null sequence times a bounded sequence is null
Algebra of limits: sums, scalar multiples, products and quotients
Limits preserve non-strict inequalities
The squeeze theorem
The absolute value is compatible with limits
Divergence to $+\infty$ and to $-\infty$
For positive terms, null and divergence to $+\infty$ are reciprocal
A strictly increasing index map satisfies $n_k \ge k$
Subsequences inherit the limit
FALSE: every bounded sequence converges
FALSE: limits preserve strict inequalities
FALSE: a convergent subsequence forces the sequence to converge
Conventions for sequences: indexing, eventually, $\lim$, and rational $\varepsilon$

decline_pages.title: Sequences and Limits: Examples and Counterexamples

items.title: The sequence $1/(k+1)$ converges to $0$
items.statement: The sequence of reals $x_k := (k+1)^{-1}$, with $k+1 = \sigma(k)$ the successor of $k$ read in $\mathbb{R}$ through the canonical-natural embedding ([[lem-of-naturals-positive]]), converges to $0$ ([[def-real-limit]], [[def-sequence]]). Every term is defined and positive. This is the real-sequence counterpart of the rational null sequence $1/n$ of the construction page, and it is the reference null sequence of this page: the later examples and counterexamples compute with it. The argument spends only density of $\mathbb{Q}$ ([[lem-rat-embeds-dense]]), the Archimedean property of $\mathbb{Q}$ ([[lem-rat-archimedean]]) and reciprocal reversal ([[lem-of-inverse-positive]]); no completeness beyond the Archimedean property and no choice principle is used.

items.title: A rational expression in $k$: $(2(k+1)+3)/(5(k+1)+1) \to 2/5$
items.statement: The sequence $x_k := \dfrac{2(k+1)+3}{5(k+1)+1}$ converges to $2/5$ ([[def-real-limit]]). The point is method: an explicit rational expression of $k$ is evaluated from the algebra of limits ([[thm-algebra-of-limits]]) once a single null sequence is known, without an $\varepsilon$-estimate fitted to the expression. Dividing numerator and denominator by the positive factor $k+1$ turns the expression into a quotient of two affine expressions in the null sequence $(k+1)^{-1}$ of [[ex-the-reciprocal-of-k-plus-one-is-null]].

items.title: The alternating sequence $(-1)^k/(k+1)$ converges to $0$
items.statement: Let $(s_k)$ be the sequence with $s_0 = 1$ and $s_{\sigma(k)} = -s_k$ — the sequence usually written $(-1)^k$, introduced and proved non-convergent as a bounded sequence in [[fs-bounded-implies-convergent]]. The sequence $y_k := s_k (k+1)^{-1}$ converges to $0$ ([[def-real-limit]]): a null sequence may oscillate in sign at every term. The proof is the null-times-bounded lemma ([[lem-null-times-bounded]]) applied to the null sequence of [[ex-the-reciprocal-of-k-plus-one-is-null]] and the bounded sequence $(s_k)$, so no estimate depending on the sign pattern is needed.

items.title: The square roots $\sqrt{k}$ diverge to $+\infty$
items.statement: Let $\sqrt{k}$ denote the unique nonnegative square root of the canonical natural $k \in \mathbb{R}$ ([[thm-of-square-roots]]). Then $(\sqrt{k})_{k \in \mathbb{N}}$ diverges to $+\infty$ ([[def-divergence-to-infinity]]): it is unbounded, hence not convergent ([[lem-convergent-implies-bounded]]). The proof is the Archimedean comparison $k > M^2 \Rightarrow \sqrt{k} > M$; it uses only that $\mathbb{R}$ is Archimedean ([[thm-of-archimedean]]) and that squaring is monotone on the nonnegatives ([[lem-of-square-monotone]]).

items.title: The successive differences $\sqrt{k+1} - \sqrt{k}$ converge to $0$
items.statement: The sequence $z_k := \sqrt{k+1} - \sqrt{k}$ converges to $0$ ([[def-real-limit]]). Since $(\sqrt{k+1} - \sqrt{k})(\sqrt{k+1} + \sqrt{k}) = 1$, the differences are the reciprocals of the sequence $w_k := \sqrt{k+1} + \sqrt{k}$, which diverges to $+\infty$ because $w_k \ge \sqrt{k}$ and $(\sqrt{k})$ does ([[ex-square-roots-diverge-to-infinity]]); the converse direction of [[lem-reciprocal-of-null-diverges]] then gives $z_k \to 0$. Thus a difference of two sequences that both diverge can converge, so the algebra of limits has no difference rule for divergent sequences.

items.title: Changing the first hundred terms leaves convergence to $0$ and boundedness intact
items.statement: Let $u_k := (k+1)^{-1}$ and let $(x_k)$ be $u$ modified in its first hundred terms: $x_k := k+1$ for $k < 100$ and $x_k := (k+1)^{-1}$ for $k \ge 100$. Then $x_k \to 0$ and $(x_k)$ is bounded, indeed $|x_k| \le 100$ for every $k$ ([[def-sequence]], [[def-real-limit]]). The initial block is arbitrary prescribed data: convergence depends only on the tail ([[lem-limit-of-tail]]), while the bound is read off the finite block and the tail separately. This is the worked form of the tail theorem.

items.title: Two squeeze computations: $1/((k+1)\sqrt{k+1}) \to 0$ and $(k+(-1)^k)/(k+1) \to 1$
items.statement: (i) The sequence $a_k := \big((k+1)\sqrt{k+1}\big)^{-1}$ converges to $0$, squeezed between the constant sequence $0$ and $(k+1)^{-1}$. (ii) With $(s_k)$ the alternating sequence of [[fs-bounded-implies-convergent]], the sequence $b_k := (k + s_k)/(k+1)$ converges to $1$, squeezed between $1 - 2(k+1)^{-1}$ and the constant $1$. Both use [[thm-squeeze]]; in (ii) the middle sequence is not presented as a sum of two sequences whose limits are known in advance, which is what the squeeze theorem is for.

items.title: Even and odd subsequences of $1/(k+1)$ converge to $0$
items.statement: Let $(x_k)$ be the null sequence of [[ex-the-reciprocal-of-k-plus-one-is-null]], and let $n, m : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ be the strictly increasing index maps constructed in [[fs-bounded-implies-convergent]] (the even and the odd index map). Then the subsequences $x_{n_j}$ and $x_{m_j}$ both converge to $0$ ([[lem-subsequence-inherits-limit]]): removing infinitely many indices from this already convergent sequence, even all odd ones, preserves its inherited limit. A convergent subsequence of a divergent sequence can exist, so no converse is asserted, and by [[lem-index-map-grows]] the index maps satisfy $n_j \ge j$ and $m_j \ge j$, so the subsequences are genuine thinnings of the sequence.

items.title: The absolute value of the limit, and the limit of the absolute value
items.statement: Let $x_k := (k+1)^{-1} - 1$. Then $x_k \to -1$, and $|x_k| \to 1 = |-1|$ ([[lem-limit-abs]], [[def-real-limit]]). Since $|x_k| = 1 - (k+1)^{-1}$ converges to $1$ while $x_k$ converges to $-1 \ne 1$, this separates the two halves of [[lem-limit-abs]]: the absolute value of the limit is recovered from the absolute values, but the limit itself is not, and the reversal of the implication fails for a nonzero limit exactly as it does for the boundedness direction discussed in the remarks of that item.

items.title: The sum of two divergent sequences can converge: $k + (-k)$
items.statement: **Refuted claim:** if the sum $(x_k + y_k)$ of two sequences of reals converges, then $(x_k)$ and $(y_k)$ both converge. The witnesses are $x_k := k$ and $y_k := -k$, where $k$ denotes the canonical natural of $\mathbb{R}$ ([[lem-of-naturals-positive]]): $(x_k)$ diverges to $+\infty$ and $(y_k)$ to $-\infty$, while the sum is the constant sequence $0$, which converges to $0$ ([[def-sequence]], [[def-real-limit]]). This is the caution noted immediately after the algebra of limits: the clauses of [[thm-algebra-of-limits]] may not be read backwards.

items.title: A null sequence times an unbounded sequence need not be null: $(k+1)^{-1}\cdot(k+1) = 1$
items.statement: **Refuted claim:** if $(x_k)$ converges to $0$, then $x_k y_k$ converges to $0$ for every sequence $(y_k)$. The witnesses are $x_k := (k+1)^{-1}$ and $y_k := k+1$: $(x_k)$ is null ([[ex-the-reciprocal-of-k-plus-one-is-null]]) and $(y_k)$ diverges to $+\infty$, but $x_k y_k = 1$ for every $k$, so the product converges to $1 \ne 0$. The boundedness hypothesis of [[lem-null-times-bounded]] therefore cannot be dropped, and it is the only hypothesis that the null-times-bounded lemma uses beyond convergence of the null factor.

items.title: The quotient rule needs a nonzero limit in the denominator: $1\big/(k+1)^{-1} = k+1$
items.statement: **Refuted claim:** if $x_k \to x$ and $y_k \to y$ and $x_k \ne 0$ for every $k$, then $y_k/x_k$ converges. The witnesses are $x_k := (k+1)^{-1}$ and $y_k := 1$: both converge — to $0$ and to $1$ — and every $x_k$ is nonzero, but $y_k/x_k = k+1$ diverges to $+\infty$. The quotient clause of [[thm-algebra-of-limits]] requires the limit of the denominator to be nonzero, and the example is the extremal failure of exactly that hypothesis. It also instantiates the reciprocal bridge of [[lem-reciprocal-of-null-diverges]].

items.title: The squeeze theorem needs the two bounds to share their limit
items.statement: **Refuted claim:** if $a_k \le x_k \le b_k$ eventually and $(a_k)$ and $(b_k)$ both converge, then $(x_k)$ converges. The witnesses are the constant sequences $a_k := -1$, $b_k := 1$ and the alternating sequence $x_k := s_k$ of [[fs-bounded-implies-convergent]]; the inequalities hold at every index, the two bounds converge to $-1$ and $1$ respectively, and $(s_k)$ does not converge. So [[thm-squeeze]] genuinely needs the two limit values to coincide, not merely the two bounds to exist.

items.title: Geometric sequences: the complete classification for every real ratio
items.statement: For every real $r$, let $a_k=r^k$ for natural $k\ge0$, using the integer powers of [[def-integer-power]], so $a_0=1$ even when $r=0$, and $a_{k+1}=a_k r$. This notation is valid for negative real ratios and is not rational exponentiation of a negative base. The complete classification is: if $|r|<1$, then $r^k\to0$; if $r=1$, the sequence is constantly $1$ and converges to $1$; if $r=-1$, its even and odd subsequences are constantly $1$ and $-1$, so it is bounded but divergent; if $r>1$, then $r^k\to+\infty$; if $r<-1$, then $|r^k|\to+\infty$, while the even subsequence diverges to $+\infty$ and the odd subsequence to $-\infty$, and the whole sequence neither converges nor diverges to either signed infinity. Consequently $(r^k)$ converges exactly when $-1<r\le1$. Here signed-infinity assertions mean [[def-divergence-to-infinity]], not a finite limit value. Quantitative checks: if $0<|r|<1$ and $h=|r|^{-1}-1>0$, then $|r^k|\le(1+kh)^{-1}$ for every natural $k$, and for $k\ge1$ one has $|r^k|<(kh)^{-1}$; if $|r|>1$ and $d=|r|-1>0$, then $|r^k|\ge1+kd$. The weak Bernoulli estimates have equality for $k=0,1$ and are strict for $k\ge2$. Thus $(1/2)^k$ and $(-1/2)^k$ are both null, $2^k$ diverges positively, and $(-2)^k$ grows in absolute value while alternating sign.

items.title: Analytic topology and finite smooth algebraic stratifications of complex varieties
items.statement:
Let $X$ be a classical algebraic variety over $\mathbb C$ in the sense of [[def-classical-algebraic-prevariety-regular-maps-and-varieties]]: a separated quasi-compact locally ringed space over $\mathbb C$ with a finite cover by affine models $Z\subseteq\mathbb C^n$, the morphisms being the regular maps, i.e. the morphisms of locally ringed spaces over $\mathbb C$ ([[def-morphism-locally-ringed-spaces]]).

(a) **Analytic topology.** An affine model $Z\subseteq\mathbb C^n$ carries the subspace topology of the Euclidean topology of $\mathbb C^n$ ([[lem-metrics-on-rn]], [[def-complex-numbers-and-arithmetic]]). If $Z_1,Z_2\subseteq X$ are affine models and $\varphi:Z_1\to Z_2$ is the structure-sheaf isomorphism, then on $Z_1\cap Z_2$ the maps $\varphi$ and $\varphi^{-1}$ are given locally by polynomial quotient functions and are therefore continuous for the Euclidean topologies. Hence the topologies transported from the two affine models agree on the overlap, so the affine-model topologies glue to a unique topology on the underlying set of $X$ ([[def-topological-space]], [[def-subspace-topology-top]]): the **analytic topology** of $X$. Every regular map of complex classical varieties is continuous for the analytic topologies, and the analytic topology refines the Zariski topology because polynomial zero sets are Euclidean closed. Whenever a complex algebraic variety is used as a topological space below it carries the analytic topology, and each subvariety carries the subspace topology.

(b) **Smooth points.** Let $S$ be a classical variety over $\mathbb C$ and $x\in S$. The point $x$ is a **smooth point of $S$** if its algebraic local ring $\mathcal O_{S,x}$ is a regular local ring: a nonzero Noetherian local ring whose maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_x$ satisfies $\dim_{\mathbb C}(\mathfrak m_x/\mathfrak m_x^2)=\dim\mathcal O_{S,x}$ ([[def-embedding-dimension-and-regular-local-ring]]). The residue field at a classical complex point is $\mathbb C$. The variety $S$ is **smooth** if every point is smooth. This intrinsic algebraic condition does not require a Zariski neighbourhood to be algebraically isomorphic to an open subset of affine space.

(c) **Finite smooth algebraic stratifications.** A **finite smooth algebraic stratification with the frontier condition** of $X$ is a finite decomposition $X=\coprod_{\alpha\in A}S_\alpha$ into pairwise disjoint nonempty connected locally closed subsets $S_\alpha\subseteq X$ - the **strata** - such that each $S_\alpha$, with its reduced induced algebraic structure (locally the polynomial-quotient function sheaf on the locally closed algebraic set), is a smooth algebraic subvariety of $X$, and such that for every $\alpha$ the closure $\overline{S_\alpha}$ of $S_\alpha$ in $X$ is a union of strata. The latter is the **frontier condition**: the frontier $\overline{S_\alpha}\setminus S_\alpha$ of every stratum is a union of strata. An open subset of an affine model is a union of principal open subsets, and each principal open subset is again an affine model, so every locally closed subvariety of $X$ is a classical variety for the induced structure sheaf.

items.title: Locally constant sheaves of finite rank
items.statement:
Let $S$ be a topological space ([[def-topological-space]]), let $k$ be a field and let $\mathcal F$ be a sheaf of $k$-vector spaces on $S$ ([[def-sheaf-on-topological-space]], [[def-presheaf-of-groups-rings-modules]]). Then $\mathcal F$ is **locally constant of finite rank** if every point $x\in S$ has an open neighbourhood $U\subseteq S$ for which there are an integer $n\ge0$ and an isomorphism of sheaves on $U$
$$\mathcal F|_U\;\cong\;k_U^{\,n},$$
where $k_U$ is the constant sheaf on $U$ with value $k$ and $\mathcal F|_U$ is the restriction of $\mathcal F$ to the open subspace $U$ ([[def-restriction-sheaf-open-subspace]], [[def-morphism-of-presheaves]], [[lem-constant-sheaf-is-the-sheaf-of-locally-constant-functions]]). A sheaf with this property is also called a **finite-rank local system of $k$-vector spaces** on $S$. This is a property of the sheaf on the space; no identification of such sheaves with functors on the fundamental groupoid is part of the definition.

items.title: Algebraically constructible complexes of analytic field sheaves
items.statement:
Let $X$ be a separated finite-type complex algebraic variety, i.e. a classical algebraic variety over $\mathbb C$ ([[def-classical-algebraic-prevariety-regular-maps-and-varieties]]), regarded as a topological space with its analytic topology ([[def-analytic-topology-and-finite-smooth-algebraic-stratifications]]), and let $k$ be a field. Write $\operatorname{Sh}_k(X)$ for the category of sheaves of $k$-vector spaces and $k$-linear morphisms ([[def-sheaf-on-topological-space]], [[def-presheaf-of-groups-rings-modules]], [[def-module-on-ringed-space]]); it is an abelian category ([[thm-abelian-sheaves-form-abelian-category]]), so its bounded derived category $D^b(\operatorname{Sh}_k(X))$ is defined with the conventions of [[def-derived-category-of-an-abelian-category]], under the standing smallness hypothesis recorded there.

The category $D_c^b(X;k)$ is the full subcategory of $D^b(\operatorname{Sh}_k(X))$ consisting of the complexes $A$ satisfying:

1. $A$ is **cohomologically bounded**: $H^j(A)=0$ for $|j|$ sufficiently large; and
2. $A$ is **algebraically constructible**: there exists a finite smooth algebraic stratification with the frontier condition $\mathfrak S$ of $X$ ([[def-analytic-topology-and-finite-smooth-algebraic-stratifications]]) such that for every stratum $S\in\mathfrak S$ and every integer $j$ the restriction $H^j(A)|_S$ is locally constant of finite rank ([[def-locally-constant-sheaf-of-finite-rank]]).

These are topological constructible sheaves, not coherent or quasi-coherent sheaves. We use the shift convention of [[def-derived-category-of-an-abelian-category]]: $H^j(A[m])=H^{j+m}(A)$. A groupoid local system is identified with a locally constant sheaf only through an explicit local comparison, which is not made here.

items.title: Analytic field sheaves have injective derived models
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $X$ be a topological space and let $k$ be a field. The category $\operatorname{Sh}_k(X)$ of sheaves of $k$-vector spaces is the category of modules over the ringed space $(X,k_X)$ with constant structure sheaf $k_X$ ([[def-locally-ringed-space]], [[def-module-on-ringed-space]]); it is a locally small Grothendieck category and carries a functorial injective embedding, and iterating that embedding on cokernels yields for every $k$-sheaf one specific injective resolution ([[lem-ringed-space-module-sheaves-enough-injectives]]). These resolutions are bounded-below injective replacements, so with the dependent choice supplied by AC ([[thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice]]) the bounded-below injective complexes model the bounded derived category: $K^+(\operatorname{Inj}\operatorname{Sh}_k(X))\to D^+(\operatorname{Sh}_k(X))$ is an equivalence, and morphisms of the bounded derived category are computed by these replacements ([[thm-injective-complexes-model-the-bounded-below-derived-category]]).

Now let $X$ be a separated finite-type complex algebraic variety and let $\mathfrak S$ be a finite smooth algebraic stratification with the frontier condition of $X$ ([[def-analytic-topology-and-finite-smooth-algebraic-stratifications]]). Let $D^b_{\mathfrak S}(X;k)$ be the full subcategory of $D^b(\operatorname{Sh}_k(X))$ of complexes whose cohomology sheaves are bounded and constructible with respect to $\mathfrak S$ ([[def-algebraically-constructible-complex-of-analytic-field-sheaves]]). Then $D^b_{\mathfrak S}(X;k)$ is a triangulated subcategory: it is closed under shifts, isomorphisms and mapping cones. More generally, if two bounded algebraically constructible complexes are constructible with respect to one common finite smooth algebraic frontier stratification, then their cone is bounded and constructible with respect to that stratification.

items.title: Finite poset diagrams have bounded finite bar models
items.statement: Let $P$ be a finite nonempty poset, regarded as a category with one arrow $p\to q$ exactly when $p\le q$, and let $h$ be the largest number of strict inequalities in a chain of $P$. Let $\operatorname{Diag}_k(P)$ be the abelian category of covariant diagrams of $k$-vector spaces on $P$, i.e. the functor category of $k$-vector spaces indexed by $P$, with its cochain complexes as in [[def-cochain-complex-in-an-abelian-category]]. If $M$ is a bounded complex of diagrams in $\operatorname{Diag}_k(P)$ whose vector spaces are finite-dimensional and vanish outside internal degrees $[a,b]$, then the derived inverse limit $\mathbf R\lim M:=\mathbf R\operatorname{Hom}(\underline k,M)$ ([[def-derived-hom-in-the-bounded-setting]]) has a finite-dimensional cochain model concentrated in $[a,b+h]$. If $A,B$ are such complexes, concentrated in $[a,b]$ and $[c,d]$ respectively, then their derived Hom has a finite-dimensional cochain model concentrated in $[c-b,d-a+h]$. These models commute with every field extension. For the empty poset, the diagram sections and the derived Hom model are zero by convention.

items.title: Locally contractible metric spaces have singular constant sheaf cohomology
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $X$ be a metric space ([[def-metric-space]]) having a neighbourhood basis of contractible open sets at every point, and let $k$ be a field. Write $k_X$ for its constant sheaf. There are natural isomorphisms
$$H^q(X,k_X)\cong H^q_{\operatorname{sing}}(X;k)$$
in every degree, where the left side is derived cohomology in the category of sheaves of $k$-vector spaces (computed with the functorial $k$-linear injective resolutions supplied by [[lem-ringed-space-module-sheaves-enough-injectives]]; compare [[def-sheaf-cohomology-derived-global-sections]]). The same assertion holds on every open subset of $X$. In particular a nonempty contractible space with this local property has constant-sheaf cohomology $k$ in degree zero and zero otherwise. This applies to every finite-polyhedral open star and to its nonempty intersection with a closed simplex.

items.title: Point operations and the open closed constructible line
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) and let $k$ be a field. (1) The constructible category of a point is the bounded derived category of finite-dimensional $k$-vector spaces, $D_c^b(\operatorname{pt};k)\simeq D^b(k\text{-}\mathbf{Vect}^{\mathrm{fd}})$ ([[def-algebraically-constructible-complex-of-analytic-field-sheaves]]). For the identity map of the point, all four pullback/pushforward operations $f^*,f_*,f_!,f^!$ are the identity functors of that category, the tensor product and internal Hom are the usual finite cochain constructions, and the dualizing object is $k$ concentrated in degree $0$ ([[lem-bounded-analytic-field-sheaves-have-derived-tensor-hom-and-pullback-pushforward-adjunctions]], [[def-derived-operations-on-analytic-sheaves-over-locally-compact-spaces]]). (2) On the complex line with the open inclusion $j:\mathbb C^*\hookrightarrow\mathbb C$ and the closed inclusion $i:\{0\}\hookrightarrow\mathbb C$, there is a $k$-linear short exact sequence of sheaves
$$0\to j_!k_{\mathbb C^*}\to k_{\mathbb C}\to i_*k\to0,$$
and its associated exact triangle is the ordinary localization triangle of the constructible derived category.

items.title: Second-order Laplace-type operators on metric vector bundles
items.statement:
Let $M$ be a Hausdorff second-countable smooth manifold without boundary of dimension $n\ge2$ ([[def-smooth-manifold]]), let $\mu$ be a smooth positive density on $M$ ([[def-density-bundle-and-smooth-density]]), and let $E\to M$ be a finite-rank smooth vector bundle ([[def-smooth-vector-bundle-rank-fibre-and-trivial-bundle]]) over $\mathbb K=\mathbb R$ or $\mathbb C$ carrying a smooth bundle metric $\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle$ ([[def-smooth-bundle-metric]]), Euclidean in the real case and Hermitian, linear in the first variable, in the complex case; in the complex case the fibres are complex vector spaces through a smooth complex structure on $E$ ([[def-complex-linear-and-compatible-bundle-connections]]). Write $\Gamma(E)$ for the smooth sections ([[def-smooth-section-local-section-and-support]]).

A $\mathbb K$-linear map $P:\Gamma(E)\to\Gamma(E)$ is a **linear differential operator of order at most two** on $E$ when, on every chart domain $\Omega$ of $M$ with coordinates $x=(x^1,\ldots,x^n)$ and in every local frame of $E$ over $\Omega$ in which a section is written $s\leftrightarrow u=(u^1,\ldots,u^r)$ and its image as $Ps\leftrightarrow((Ps)_1,\ldots,(Ps)_r)$,
$$(Ps)_\lambda=-\sum_{i,j=1}^na^{ij}_{\lambda\mu}(x)\,\partial_i\partial_ju^\mu(x)+\sum_{j=1}^nb^j_{\lambda\mu}(x)\,\partial_ju^\mu(x)+c_{\lambda\mu}(x)u^\mu(x),\qquad1\le\lambda\le r,$$
with smooth coefficient functions on $\Omega$ and summation over repeated indices $\mu$ (and over $i,j$); by the strategy below, verifying this on the members of one atlas of charts and frames already forces it everywhere. Such an operator is **Laplace type** when in addition, in every such chart and frame, its second-order coefficients are scalar multiples of the identity, $a^{ij}_{\lambda\mu}=a^{ij}\delta_{\lambda\mu}$, with $a^{ij}$ smooth real functions for which $(a^{ij}(x))$ is symmetric and positive definite at every $x\in\Omega$. Its **principal symbol** is the smooth section $\sigma_2(P)$ of $\mathrm{Sym}^2T^*M$ ([[def-smooth-tensor-field]]) given on such a chart by $\sigma_2(P)(x,\xi)=a^{ij}(x)\xi_i\xi_j$ for $\xi\in T_x^*M$; equivalently $\sigma_2(P)(x,\xi)=a_x(\xi,\xi)\,\mathrm{id}_{E_x}$ for a smooth field of positive-definite quadratic forms $a_x$ on $T_x^*M$, so that $\sigma_2(P)(x,\xi)>0$ whenever $\xi\ne0$.

$P$ is **formally symmetric** for $(\mu,\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle)$ when
$$\int_M\langle Ps,t\rangle\,d\mu=\int_M\langle s,Pt\rangle\,d\mu$$
for all compactly supported smooth sections $s,t\in\Gamma_c(E)$ ([[def-integral-of-a-compactly-supported-smooth-density]]).

items.title: Formal adjoints of differential operators on metric vector bundles
items.statement:
Let $M$ be a Hausdorff second-countable smooth manifold without boundary, $\mu$ a smooth positive density on $M$, and $E,F\to M$ finite-rank smooth vector bundles over $\mathbb K=\mathbb R$ or $\mathbb C$ with smooth bundle metrics, Hermitian (first-variable-linear) in the complex case, with the conventions of [[def-second-order-laplace-type-operators-on-vector-bundles]]. Let $P:\Gamma(E)\to\Gamma(F)$ be a linear differential operator of order at most two (the target-$F$ version of the local description in [[def-second-order-laplace-type-operators-on-vector-bundles]]).

Then there is a unique linear differential operator $P^\star:\Gamma(F)\to\Gamma(E)$ of order at most two such that
$$\int_M\langle Pu,v\rangle_F\,d\mu=\int_M\langle u,P^\star v\rangle_E\,d\mu$$
for all compactly supported smooth sections $u\in\Gamma_c(E)$ and $v\in\Gamma_c(F)$; it is the **formal adjoint** of $P$. It is given locally as follows: in a chart with coordinates $x$, with density coefficient $\gamma>0$ defined by $\mu=\gamma\,|dx^1\cdots dx^n|$ ([[def-density-bundle-and-smooth-density]]), with orthonormal frames of $E$ and $F$, and with local coefficients $Pu=\sum_{|\alpha|\le2}a_\alpha D^\alpha u$,
$$P^\star v=\sum_{|\alpha|\le2}(-1)^{|\alpha|}\gamma^{-1}D^\alpha\bigl(\gamma\,a_\alpha^*v\bigr),$$
where $a_\alpha^*$ is the fibre adjoint. Consequently:
1. if $P$ has order $\delta\in\{0,1,2\}$, with principal symbol defined on a chart by $\sigma_\delta(P)(x,\xi)=\sum_{|\alpha|=\delta}a_\alpha(x)\xi^\alpha$, then $\sigma_\delta(P^\star)=(-1)^\delta\sigma_\delta(P)^*$; thus a Laplace-type operator has a Laplace-type formal adjoint with the same principal form;
2. $(P^\star)^\star=P$;
3. if $E=F$, then $P$ is formally symmetric in the sense of [[def-second-order-laplace-type-operators-on-vector-bundles]] exactly when $P=P^\star$.

items.title: Complex manifolds, holomorphic vector bundles and Hermitian metrics
items.statement:
Let $m\ge1$. A **chart** on a topological space $X$ is a homeomorphism $\varphi:U\to\varphi(U)$ from an open set $U\subseteq X$ onto an open subset of $\mathbb C^m$ with its usual topology ([[def-homeomorphism-and-open-maps]]); two charts $\varphi,\psi$ are **holomorphically compatible** when the transition maps $\psi\circ\varphi^{-1}$ and $\varphi\circ\psi^{-1}$ are holomorphic on the open sets where they are defined ([[def-holomorphic-function-in-several-complex-variables]]). A **holomorphic atlas** is a family of pairwise compatible charts whose domains cover $X$. A **complex manifold of dimension $m$** is a nonempty Hausdorff ([[def-hausdorff-space]]) second-countable ([[def-second-countable-space]]) topological space carrying a holomorphic atlas; exactly as for [[def-riemann-surface-and-holomorphic-atlas]] one passes to the maximal atlas and calls its members holomorphic charts, and for connected $X$ the case $m=1$ recovers Riemann surfaces ([[def-topological-manifold-without-boundary]]).

A **holomorphic map** $f:X\to Y$ between complex manifolds is a continuous map whose expression in every pair of holomorphic charts is holomorphic ([[def-holomorphic-map-and-complex-jacobian]]); equivalently, composition with $f$ preserves holomorphic functions.

**Induced smooth structure and complex structure.** Holomorphic functions on open subsets of $\mathbb C^m$ are smooth ([[cor-holomorphic-functions-in-several-variables-are-smooth]]), so every holomorphic atlas is a smooth atlas ([[def-smooth-atlas]]) and $X$ is a smooth manifold of real dimension $2m$ ([[def-smooth-manifold]]) whose smooth charts include the holomorphic ones. In holomorphic coordinates $z_k=x_k+iy_k$ the **complex structure** is the endomorphism field $J$ of the tangent bundle determined by $J\partial_{x_k}=\partial_{y_k}$ and $J\partial_{y_k}=-\partial_{x_k}$; it satisfies $J^2=-\mathrm{id}$ and is independent of the holomorphic chart because holomorphic transition maps have complex-linear differentials ([[thm-chain-rule-for-holomorphic-maps-in-several-variables]], [[def-holomorphic-map-and-complex-jacobian]]). A **Hermitian metric** on $X$ is a Riemannian metric $g$ ([[def-riemannian-metric-and-riemannian-manifold]]) satisfying $g(Jv,Jw)=g(v,w)$ for all tangent vectors; its Riemannian volume density is written $\mu_g$ ([[def-riemannian-volume-density]]).

**Holomorphic vector bundles and Hermitian bundle metrics.** A **holomorphic vector bundle of rank $r$** on $X$ is a smooth complex vector bundle $\pi:E\to X$ of rank $r$ ([[def-smooth-vector-bundle-rank-fibre-and-trivial-bundle]], [[def-complex-linear-and-compatible-bundle-connections]]) together with an open cover $(V_\alpha)$ of $X$ and smooth local trivializations $\theta_\alpha:E|_{V_\alpha}\to V_\alpha\times\mathbb C^r$ whose transition matrices $g_{\alpha\beta}:V_\alpha\cap V_\beta\to\mathrm{GL}_r(\mathbb C)$, defined by $\theta_\alpha\theta_\beta^{-1}(p,v)=(p,g_{\alpha\beta}(p)v)$, are holomorphic. A **holomorphic frame** over an open set $V$ is such a trivialization. A **Hermitian metric** $h$ on $E$ is a smooth bundle metric ([[def-smooth-bundle-metric]]) whose fibre pairings are positive definite Hermitian forms, linear in the first variable and conjugate-linear in the second.

items.title: E-valued Dolbeault operators and their L2 structure
items.statement:
Let $X$ be a complex manifold of dimension $m\ge1$ ([[def-complex-manifolds-and-holomorphic-vector-bundles]]) with a Hermitian metric $g$, and let $E\to X$ be a holomorphic vector bundle of rank $r$ with a Hermitian metric $h$ ([[def-complex-manifolds-and-holomorphic-vector-bundles]]). Fix integers $p,q\ge0$. In a holomorphic chart with coordinates $z=(z_1,\ldots,z_m)$ and a holomorphic frame of $E$, an **$E$-valued $(p,q)$-form** is an expression
$$s=\sum_{|I|=p}\sum_{|J|=q}s_{IJ}\otimes dz^I\wedge d\bar z^J,$$
with $s_{IJ}$ smooth local sections of $E$ and increasing multi-indices $I,J$ ([[def-bigraded-complex-differential-forms]]); such expressions agree on overlaps because holomorphic changes of coordinates preserve bidegree and holomorphic frame changes are complex-linear. The resulting smooth global sections of the bundle $\Lambda^{p,q}T^*X\otimes E$ are denoted $\mathcal A^{p,q}(X,E)$.

The **Dolbeault operator** is the first-order operator
$$\bar\partial_E:\mathcal A^{p,q}(X,E)\to\mathcal A^{p,q+1}(X,E),\qquad \bar\partial_E s=\sum_{I,J}\sum_{k=1}^m \bar\partial_{z_k}s_{IJ}\otimes d\bar z_k\wedge dz^I\wedge d\bar z^J,$$
with the Wirtinger operators $\bar\partial_{z_k}$ ([[def-wirtinger-operators-in-several-complex-variables]], [[def-bigraded-complex-differential-forms]]) acting componentwise on the local sections $s_{IJ}$. It is independent of the holomorphic chart and frame, and $\bar\partial_E^2=0$ ([[thm-d-dbar-decomposition-and-identities]]).

Equip $\Lambda^{p,q}T^*X\otimes E$ with the Hermitian metric induced by $g$ and $h$ ([[prop-riemannian-metrics-induce-metrics-on-dual-tensor-and-exterior-bundles]] and [[def-complex-manifolds-and-holomorphic-vector-bundles]]). For compactly supported smooth $s,t\in\mathcal A^{p,q}(X,E)$ the **$L^2$ pairing**
$$\langle s,t\rangle_{L^2}=\int_X\langle s,t\rangle\,d\mu_g$$
uses the Riemannian volume density $\mu_g$ ([[def-riemannian-volume-density]], [[def-integral-of-a-compactly-supported-smooth-density]]) and is a complex inner product in the first-variable-linear convention ([[def-complex-l-two-inner-product]]); its completion $L^2(X,\Lambda^{p,q}T^*X\otimes E)$ is a complex Hilbert space ([[lem-l-two-with-the-integral-pairing-is-a-hilbert-space]], [[thm-complex-holder-minkowski-and-the-quotient-norm]]). By [[lem-formal-adjoints-of-differential-operators-exist-and-are-unique]] the operator $\bar\partial_E$ has a **formal adjoint** $\bar\partial_E^*:\mathcal A^{p,q+1}(X,E)\to\mathcal A^{p,q}(X,E)$, the unique smooth first-order operator with
$$\langle\bar\partial_Es,t\rangle_{L^2}=\langle s,\bar\partial_E^*t\rangle_{L^2}$$
for all compactly supported smooth forms.

The **Dolbeault Laplacian** $\Delta_{\bar\partial_E}=\bar\partial_E\bar\partial_E^*+\bar\partial_E^*\bar\partial_E$ is a formally symmetric Laplace-type second-order operator ([[def-second-order-laplace-type-operators-on-vector-bundles]]) preserving each bidegree $(p,q)$, with
$$\langle\Delta_{\bar\partial_E}s,s\rangle_{L^2}=\|\bar\partial_Es\|_2^2+\|\bar\partial_E^*s\|_2^2\ge0$$
for compactly supported smooth $s$. Its principal symbol is $\sigma_2(\Delta_{\bar\partial_E})(x,\xi)=|\xi^{0,1}|_g^2\,\mathrm{id}$, where $\xi^{0,1}$ is the $(0,1)$-part of $\xi\in T_x^*X$; in particular the principal form is smooth, and it is positive definite on nonzero real covectors.

items.title: Compact Laplace-type bundle operators: regularity and shifted parametrices
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $M$ be a compact smooth manifold without boundary of real dimension $n\ge2$, equipped with a smooth positive density, and $E\to M$ a finite-rank real Euclidean or complex Hermitian smooth vector bundle. Let $P$ be a Laplace-type second-order differential operator on $E$ in the sense of [[def-second-order-laplace-type-operators-on-vector-bundles]] — smooth coefficients, formally symmetric for the density and metric, whose positive-frequency principal symbol is
$$\sigma_2(P)(x,\xi)=a_x(\xi,\xi)\,\mathrm{id}_{E_x},$$
where $a$ is a smooth positive-definite real quadratic form on cotangent vectors; thus in any local frame $P=-a^{ij}\partial_i\partial_j+B^j\partial_j+C$, with scalar real positive-definite $a^{ij}$ and matrix-valued lower coefficients. Nonnegativity of $P$ is not needed here.

For nonnegative integers $k$, define $H^k(M,E)$ by requiring the coefficients of each member of a finite smooth partition of unity times the section, in precompact bundle charts and extended by zero, to lie in $H^k(\mathbb R^n)$ ([[def-hk-and-hk-zero-notation]], [[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]]); the norm is the square root of the sum of these component Sobolev norms squared. Different such choices give equivalent norms. The following hold.

1. These are Hilbert spaces, smooth sections are dense, $H^0=L^2$ with equivalent norms, $H^{k+1}\hookrightarrow H^k$ is compact, and $H^k\hookrightarrow C^r$ continuously whenever $k>r+n/2$.
2. If $u\in H^1$ and $Pu=f\in H^k$ distributionally, then $u\in H^{k+2}$ and
$$\|u\|_{H^{k+2}}\le C_k(\|f\|_{H^k}+\|u\|_{L^2}).$$
In particular smooth data give smooth weak solutions. The same estimate holds for all $u\in H^{k+2}$.
3. For sufficiently large real $\lambda>0$, $P+\lambda:H^2\to L^2$ is a bounded bijection with bounded inverse $B:L^2\to H^2$. As an operator on $L^2$, $B$ is compact, injective and selfadjoint, has dense range $H^2$, and the unbounded operator $P$ with domain exactly $H^2$ is selfadjoint. The map $B:H^k\to H^{k+2}$ is bounded for every nonnegative integer $k$ and preserves smooth sections.
4. It supplies two-sided parametrices **modulo compact operators**:
$$PB=I-\lambda B\quad\hbox{on }L^2,\qquad BP=I-\lambda B\quad\hbox{on }H^2.$$
Here on the second space $B$ denotes its restriction after inclusion $H^2\hookrightarrow L^2$; it is compact on $H^2$. No assertion concerning arbitrary-order elliptic operators, or pseudodifferential symbol classes, is part of this theorem.

items.title: Compact Laplace-type operators: smooth kernel, closed range and Green inverse
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $M,E,P$ have exactly the compact, boundaryless, scalar-positive-symbol and formal symmetry hypotheses of [[thm-elliptic-differential-operators-on-compact-vector-bundles-have-parametrices-and-regularity]], with $\operatorname{dom}P=H^2(M,E)$. Write $\mathcal H=\ker P$.

Then $\mathcal H$ is finite dimensional and consists of smooth sections, $\operatorname{ran}P=\mathcal H^\perp$ is closed in $L^2$, and
$$L^2(M,E)=\mathcal H\mathbin{\oplus^\perp}\operatorname{ran}P.$$
Let $\Pi$ be the orthogonal projection onto $\mathcal H$ ([[def-hilbert-orthogonal-projection]]). There is a unique linear operator $G:L^2\to H^2\cap\mathcal H^\perp$ with
$$PG=I-\Pi\quad\hbox{on }L^2,\qquad GP=I-\Pi\quad\hbox{on }H^2,\qquad G\Pi=\Pi G=0.$$
It is bounded from $H^k$ to $H^{k+2}$ for every integer $k\ge0$, compact and selfadjoint on $L^2$, and preserves smooth sections. For all such $k$,
$$H^k=\mathcal H\oplus P(H^{k+2}),\qquad C^\infty(M,E)=\mathcal H\oplus P(C^\infty(M,E)),$$
where the second summands are the corresponding intersections with $\mathcal H^\perp$, and the decompositions are topological. The projection is smoothing: for every integer $r\ge0$, $\|\Pi f\|_{C^r}\le C_r\|f\|_2$. Consequently $G$ is a two-sided parametrix with finite-rank smoothing remainders. If additionally $(Pu,u)_2\ge0$ for smooth $u$, then $P$ and $G$ are nonnegative on their respective domains.

items.title: Harmonic representatives for compact de Rham and Dolbeault complexes
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $M$ be a compact smooth Riemannian manifold without boundary, of real dimension at least two ([[def-smooth-manifold]], [[def-riemannian-metric-and-riemannian-manifold]]). Its metric defines the $L^2$ pairing on forms by the Riemannian density ([[prop-riemannian-metrics-induce-metrics-on-dual-tensor-and-exterior-bundles]], [[def-riemannian-volume-density]], [[def-integral-of-a-compactly-supported-smooth-density]]); orientation is unnecessary. Let $d^*$ denote the formal adjoint of $d$ ([[lem-formal-adjoints-of-differential-operators-exist-and-are-unique]]), and $\Delta=dd^*+d^*d$ on total real forms, or on their complexification. With domain $H^2$ the operator is nonnegative and selfadjoint. Its degreewise smooth kernels $\mathcal H^k$ are finite dimensional, and there is an orthogonal smooth decomposition
$$\Omega^k(M)=\mathcal H^k\mathbin{\oplus^\perp}d\Omega^{k-1}(M)\mathbin{\oplus^\perp}d^*\Omega^{k+1}(M).$$
The map $h\mapsto[h]$ is an isomorphism $\mathcal H^k\to H^k_{\mathrm{dR}}(M)$ ([[def-de-rham-cohomology]]), over $\mathbb R$ or $\mathbb C$ as appropriate.

More generally let $X$ be a compact complex manifold of complex dimension $m\ge1$ with a smooth Hermitian metric ([[def-complex-manifolds-and-holomorphic-vector-bundles]]). Let $E$ be a holomorphic bundle of finite rank with a smooth Hermitian metric ([[def-complex-manifolds-and-holomorphic-vector-bundles]]). On $E$-valued $(p,q)$ forms let $\bar\partial_E$ be the Dolbeault operator of [[def-e-valued-dolbeault-operators-and-ltwo-structure]] and let $\bar\partial_E^*$ be its formal adjoint; for each fixed $p$, $\Delta_{\bar\partial_E}=\bar\partial_E\bar\partial_E^*+\bar\partial_E^*\bar\partial_E$ on the sum over $q$ is nonnegative and selfadjoint on $H^2$; its smooth harmonic spaces $\mathcal H_E^{p,q}$ are finite dimensional and
$$\Omega^{p,q}(X,E)=\mathcal H_E^{p,q}\mathbin{\oplus^\perp}\bar\partial_E\Omega^{p,q-1}(X,E)\mathbin{\oplus^\perp}\bar\partial_E^*\Omega^{p,q+1}(X,E).$$
In particular harmonic forms represent the smooth Dolbeault quotient
$$H_{\bar\partial}^{p,q}(X,E):=\ker\bar\partial_E/\operatorname{im}\bar\partial_E$$
uniquely. Terms outside the degree range are zero. This asserts smooth Dolbeault cohomology; an identification with sheaf cohomology requires a separate Dolbeault-resolution comparison theorem.

For either complex write $D=d$ or $D=\bar\partial_E$, $P=DD^*+D^*D$, and let $\Pi,G$ be the preceding Green projection and inverse. They preserve degree, $G$ preserves smooth forms, and on smooth forms
$$DG=GD,\qquad D^*G=GD^*,\qquad D\Pi=\Pi D=D^*\Pi=\Pi D^*=0.$$
Every closed smooth $u$ satisfies $u=\Pi u+D(D^*Gu)$.

decline_pages.title: Compact Support Sheaf Calculus

items.title: Support of a section of a sheaf
items.statement: Let $X$ be a topological space, let $\mathcal F$ be a presheaf of $k$-vector spaces (or of abelian groups) on $X$, let $U\subseteq X$ be open and let $s\in\mathcal F(U)$. The support of $s$ is $$\operatorname{Supp}(s):=\{\,x\in U: s_x\neq 0\,\}\subseteq U,$$ where $s_x$ denotes the germ of $s$ at $x$ in the stalk $\mathcal F_x$. A section $s\in\mathcal F(X)$ is compactly supported when its support is a compact subspace of $X$. For a subspace $Z\subseteq X$ and a presheaf $\mathcal G$ on $Z$, the support of $t\in\mathcal G(Z)$ is defined by the same condition using the stalks of $\mathcal G$. When $\mathcal F$ is a sheaf of $k$-vector spaces the following hold: (1) $\operatorname{Supp}(s)$ is closed in $U$; (2) $\operatorname{Supp}(s)=\varnothing$ if and only if $s=0$; (3) $\operatorname{Supp}(s|_V)=\operatorname{Supp}(s)\cap V$ for every open $V\subseteq U$. The support is not assumed closed in $X$ nor compact.

items.title: Sections on a compact set extend to a neighbourhood
items.statement: Let $K\subseteq X$ be a compact subset of a locally compact Hausdorff space, let $\mathcal F$ be a sheaf of $k$-vector spaces on $X$ and let $i:K\hookrightarrow X$ be the inclusion. Then the canonical map $$\varinjlim_{U\supseteq K,\ U\ \text{open}}\mathcal F(U)\longrightarrow\Gamma(K,i^{-1}\mathcal F)=(i^{-1}\mathcal F)(K)$$ is an isomorphism. Moreover, for pairwise disjoint compact subsets $K_1,\dots,K_m\subseteq X$ and sections $s_j$ of $\mathcal F$ over open neighbourhoods $U_j$ of the respective $K_j$, there is a single section $s$ of $\mathcal F$ over a neighbourhood of $K_1\cup\dots\cup K_m$ which restricts to $s_j$ near $K_j$ for every $j$; in particular the zero section can be prescribed on any compact set disjoint from $K$.

items.title: c-soft sheaves
items.statement: Let $X$ be a locally compact Hausdorff space and let $\mathcal F$ be a sheaf of $k$-vector spaces on $X$. Then $\mathcal F$ is c-soft (soft for compact supports) if for every compact subset $K\subseteq X$ the restriction map $$\Gamma(X,\mathcal F)\longrightarrow\Gamma(K,i^{-1}\mathcal F),\qquad s\longmapsto s|_K,$$ is surjective, that is: every section of $\mathcal F$ over a compact subset extends to a global section. By lem-sections-near-a-compact-set-are-sections-on-that-set, this is equivalent to requiring that every section of $\mathcal F$ over an open neighbourhood of a compact set $K$ agrees near $K$ with a global section. C-softness is a property of the pair $(X,\mathcal F)$; a flasque sheaf on a locally compact Hausdorff space is c-soft.

items.title: Compactly supported global sections and their right derived functors
items.statement: Assume AC. Let $X$ be a locally compact Hausdorff space and let $\mathcal F$ be a sheaf of $k$-vector spaces on $X$. The compactly supported global sections of $\mathcal F$ are $$\Gamma_c(X,\mathcal F):=\{\,s\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal F):\operatorname{Supp}(s)\ \text{is compact}\,\}\subseteq\Gamma(X,\mathcal F).$$ A morphism $\varphi:\mathcal F\to\mathcal G$ induces $\Gamma_c(X,\varphi)$ by restriction of $\Gamma(X,\varphi)$, so $\Gamma_c(X,-)$ is an additive functor with values in $k$-vector spaces, and it is left exact: for every short exact sequence $0\to\mathcal F'\to\mathcal F\to\mathcal F''\to0$ the sequence $0\to\Gamma_c(X,\mathcal F')\to\Gamma_c(X,\mathcal F)\to\Gamma_c(X,\mathcal F'')$ is exact. Fix the supplied functorial injective resolution datum $\mathcal F\mapsto I^\bullet(\mathcal F)$ on the abelian category of sheaves of $k$-vector spaces and define $$H^q_c(X,\mathcal F):=R^q\Gamma_c(X,\mathcal F):=H^q\bigl(\Gamma_c(X,I^\bullet(\mathcal F)_{\mathrm{del}})\bigr)\quad(q\ge0),\qquad H^q_c(X,\mathcal F):=0\ (q<0).$$ These groups are independent of the supplied resolution datum up to canonical natural isomorphism, and they are the right derived functors of $\Gamma_c(X,-)$, which therefore form a cohomological delta functor with connecting maps and long exact sequences. When $X$ is compact, $\Gamma_c(X,-)=\Gamma(X,-)$ and $H^q_c(X,\mathcal F)=H^q(X,\mathcal F)$.

items.title: Compact-support acyclicity of c-soft sheaves
items.statement: Assume AC. Let $X$ be a locally compact Hausdorff space and let $\mathcal F$ be a sheaf of $k$-vector spaces on $X$. Then: (1) if $\mathcal F$ is c-soft, every section of $\mathcal F$ over a compact subset $K\subseteq X$ extends to a compactly supported global section whose support is contained in any prescribed open neighbourhood of $K$; (2) every injective sheaf of $k$-vector spaces on $X$ is c-soft; (3) if $\mathcal F$ is c-soft, then $H^q_c(X,\mathcal F)=0$ for every $q>0$ (when $X$ is compact this is vanishing of ordinary sheaf cohomology); (4) c-softness is preserved by restriction to open subsets, by restriction to closed subsets, by extension by zero along an open inclusion, by arbitrary direct sums, and by tensor product with a constant $k$-vector space; (5) if $0\to\mathcal F'\to\mathcal F\to\mathcal F''\to0$ is a short exact sequence of sheaves of $k$-vector spaces and $\mathcal F'$ is c-soft, then every section of $\mathcal F''$ over a compact subset lifts to a section of $\mathcal F$ over an open neighbourhood of it, and the induced sequence $0\to\Gamma_c(X,\mathcal F')\to\Gamma_c(X,\mathcal F)\to\Gamma_c(X,\mathcal F'')\to0$ is exact whenever $\mathcal F$ is also c-soft; if $\mathcal F'$ and $\mathcal F$ are c-soft then $\mathcal F''$ is c-soft.

items.title: Compact-support calculus along open and closed embeddings
items.statement: Assume AC. Let $X$ be a locally compact Hausdorff space, let $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ be the inclusion of an open subspace with closed complement $Z=X\setminus U$, and let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be the closed inclusion. (1) For every sheaf $\mathcal A$ of $k$-vector spaces on $U$ the canonical map $\Gamma_c(X,j_!\mathcal A)\to\Gamma_c(U,\mathcal A)$ is an isomorphism, natural in $\mathcal A$, and $j_!$ carries c-soft sheaves on $U$ to c-soft sheaves on $X$; consequently there are natural isomorphisms $R^q\Gamma_c(X,j_!\mathcal A)\cong R^q\Gamma_c(U,\mathcal A)$ for all $q\ge0$. (2) For every sheaf $\mathcal B$ of $k$-vector spaces on $Z$ the canonical map $\Gamma_c(X,i_*\mathcal B)\to\Gamma_c(Z,\mathcal B)$ is an isomorphism, natural in $\mathcal B$, $i_*$ carries c-soft sheaves on $Z$ to c-soft sheaves on $X$, and there are natural isomorphisms $R^q\Gamma_c(X,i_*\mathcal B)\cong R^q\Gamma_c(Z,\mathcal B)$ for all $q\ge0$. (3) If $Z$ is compact, then $\Gamma_c(X,i_*\mathcal B)\cong\Gamma(Z,\mathcal B)$ and $R^q\Gamma_c(X,i_*\mathcal B)\cong H^q(Z,\mathcal B)$ for all $q$.

items.title: Vanishing compactly supported first cohomology on opens characterises c-softness
items.statement: Assume AC. Let $X$ be a locally compact Hausdorff space and let $\mathcal E$ be a sheaf of $k$-vector spaces on $X$ satisfying $H^1_c(V,\mathcal E|_V)=0$ for every open subspace $V\subseteq X$. Then $\mathcal E$ is c-soft; more precisely, every section of $\mathcal E$ over a compact subset $K\subseteq X$ extends to a compactly supported global section of $\mathcal E$. Conversely, if $\mathcal E$ is c-soft then $H^q_c(V,\mathcal E|_V)=0$ for every $q>0$ and every open $V\subseteq X$, so c-softness of $\mathcal E$ is equivalent to $R\Gamma_c(V,\mathcal E|_V)$ being concentrated in degree $0$ for every open $V\subseteq X$.

items.title: A refinement compatible with tuple-indexed coverings
items.statement: Let $X$ be a compact Hausdorff space, let $I$ be a finite set, and let $(U_i)_{i\in I}$ be an open cover of $X$. Fix an integer $p\ge0$ and suppose that for every $(p+1)$-tuple $(i_0,\dots,i_p)$ of elements of $I$ a family $(W_{i_0\dots i_p,k})_k$ of open subsets of $U_{i_0}\cap\dots\cap U_{i_p}$ is given which covers it. Then there are a finite set $J$, a map $\alpha:J\to I$ and an open cover $(V_j)_{j\in J}$ of $X$ with $V_j\subseteq U_{\alpha(j)}$ for all $j$, such that every $V_{j_0}\cap\dots\cap V_{j_p}$ is contained in some $W_{\alpha(j_0)\dots\alpha(j_p),k}$. No choice principle is used.

items.title: Refinement-limit Cech cohomology computes sheaf cohomology on compact Hausdorff spaces
items.statement: Assume AC. Let $X$ be a compact Hausdorff space. For every sheaf of abelian groups $\mathcal F$ on $X$ and every $p\ge0$, the canonical comparison map $$\varphi^p_X:\check H^p(X,\mathcal F)\longrightarrow H^p(X,\mathcal F)$$ from the refinement-limit Cech cohomology of $X$ (taken over all open covers, equivalently over finite open covers because $X$ is compact) to sheaf cohomology is an isomorphism, natural in $\mathcal F$; these isomorphisms form an isomorphism of cohomological delta functors extending the identity in degree $0$ and hence commute with the connecting homomorphisms of short exact sequences. Consequently, if a cofinal family of open covers of $X$ has $\check H^p(\mathcal U,\mathcal F)=0$ for every $p>d$, then $H^p(X,\mathcal F)=0$ for every $p>d$.

items.title: A polyhedral dimension bound for every sheaf
items.statement: Assume AC. Let $P=|K|$ be the realization of a finite abstract simplicial complex $K$ of dimension $d$ (a finite compact polyhedron of dimension $d$), and let $\mathcal F$ be a sheaf of abelian groups on $P$. Then: (1) $H^q(P,\mathcal F)=0$ for every $q>d$; (2) for every open subspace $U\subseteq P$ and every sheaf $\mathcal E$ of abelian groups on $U$, $H^q_c(U,\mathcal E)=0$ for every $q>d$; (3) more generally, the same conclusions hold for every compact topological space in which every open cover admits a finite open refinement of order at most $d+1$, and for every open subspace of such a space. These bounds concern arbitrary sheaves, not merely cellular, constructible or coherent ones. If $L\subseteq K$ is a subcomplex, then $|L|$ is closed in $P$, the complement $P\setminus|L|$ is open, and every open subspace of $P\setminus|L|$ is an open subspace of $P$; this is the fibre model on which the bound is applied.

items.title: Bounded fibrewise-soft resolutions from a uniform all-sheaf dimension bound
items.statement: Assume AC. Let $f:X\to Y$ be a continuous map between locally compact Hausdorff spaces and let $d\ge0$ be an integer such that $$H^q_c(V,\mathcal F)=0\qquad(q>d)$$ for every open subspace $V$ of every fibre of $f$ and every sheaf $\mathcal F$ of $k$-vector spaces on $V$. Then every sheaf of $k$-vector spaces on $X$ has a bounded resolution whose terms are c-soft on every fibre: for every sheaf $\mathcal A$ on $X$ there is an exact sequence $$0\longrightarrow\mathcal A\longrightarrow\mathcal K^0\longrightarrow\cdots\longrightarrow\mathcal K^d\longrightarrow0$$ in which each $\mathcal K^j$ restricts to a c-soft sheaf on every fibre $f^{-1}(y)$; for $d=0$ this says that $\mathcal A$ is already c-soft on every fibre. Every bounded complex of sheaves of $k$-vector spaces on $X$ admits a bounded resolution by complexes whose terms are fibrewise c-soft, obtained by totalising these termwise resolutions over the bounded index range. In particular the constant sheaf $k_X$ has such a resolution. The hypothesis is the uniform fibrewise form of finite all-sheaf compact-support dimension; in the geometric applications it is supplied by finite triangulations of fibre compactifications of dimension at most $d$.
