items.title: Truncation functors, t-cohomology, amplitude and bounded t-structures
items.statement:
Let $(\mathcal T^{\le0},\mathcal T^{\ge0})$ be a t-structure on a triangulated category $\mathcal T$ with translation $[1]$ ([[def-canonical-t-structure-on-a-derived-category]], [[def-triangulated-category]]), and set $\mathcal T^{\le n}:=\mathcal T^{\le0}[-n]$ and $\mathcal T^{\ge n}:=\mathcal T^{\ge0}[-n]$ for $n\in\mathbb Z$; thus $X\in\mathcal T^{\le n}$ exactly when $X[n]\in\mathcal T^{\le0}$, and $X\in\mathcal T^{\ge n}$ exactly when $X[n]\in\mathcal T^{\ge0}$.

For $X\in\mathcal T$ and $n\in\mathbb Z$, the t-structure axiom applied to the translate $X[n]$ and then shifted by $[-n]$ produces a distinguished triangle
$$\tau_{\le n}X\longrightarrow X\longrightarrow\tau_{\ge n+1}X\longrightarrow\tau_{\le n}X[1]$$
with $\tau_{\le n}X\in\mathcal T^{\le n}$ and $\tau_{\ge n+1}X\in\mathcal T^{\ge n+1}$; such a triangle is a **truncation triangle** of $X$ at $n$. Truncation triangles of the same $X$ at the same $n$ are canonically isomorphic over $X$, so the objects and maps occurring in them are determined up to unique compatible isomorphism ([[lem-truncation-triangles-are-essentially-unique-and-functorial]]); one writes $\tau_{\le n}$ and $\tau_{\ge n}$ for the resulting **truncation functors**.

The **t-cohomology** of $X$ is
$$H^n_t(X):=(\tau_{\le n}\tau_{\ge n}X)[n],$$
an object of the heart $\mathcal C=\mathcal T^{\le0}\cap\mathcal T^{\ge0}$ ([[lem-t-cohomology-is-additive-shift-compatible-and-detects-amplitude]]). The **amplitude** of $X$ is the set of $n$ with $H^n_t(X)\not\cong0$; it is *contained in* an interval $[a,b]$ when $H^n_t(X)=0$ for every $n\notin[a,b]$. The t-structure is **bounded** when every object of $\mathcal T$ lies in $\mathcal T^{\le n}\cap\mathcal T^{\ge -n}$ for some integer $n$ depending on the object.

This item fixes notation and conventions only; existence, essential uniqueness and all algebraic properties of $\tau_{\le n}$, $\tau_{\ge n}$ and $H^n_t$ are proved in the two immediately following lemmas.

items.title: Truncation triangles are essentially unique and give adjoint truncation functors
items.statement:
Let $(\mathcal T^{\le0},\mathcal T^{\ge0})$ be a t-structure on a triangulated category $\mathcal T$, with truncations as in [[def-truncation-functors-and-cohomology-of-a-t-structure]].

(i) *Essential uniqueness.* For every $X$ and $n$, every distinguished triangle $A\to X\to B\to A[1]$ with $A\in\mathcal T^{\le n}$ and $B\in\mathcal T^{\ge n+1}$ is isomorphic to the truncation triangle $\tau_{\le n}X\to X\to\tau_{\ge n+1}X\to\tau_{\le n}X[1]$ by an isomorphism of triangles whose middle component is the identity of $X$; this isomorphism is unique.

(ii) *Adjunction and orthogonality.* The assignment $X\mapsto\tau_{\le n}X$ is a functor and for $T\in\mathcal T^{\le n}$ the map $\operatorname{Hom}(T,\tau_{\le n}X)\to\operatorname{Hom}(T,X)$, $f\mapsto(\tau_{\le n}X\to X)\circ f$, is a bijection natural in $X$; dually $\operatorname{Hom}(\tau_{\ge n}X,T)\to\operatorname{Hom}(X,T)$ is a bijection for $T\in\mathcal T^{\ge n}$. Moreover $\operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal T^{\le n},\mathcal T^{\ge n+1})=0$ for every $n$.

(iii) *Aisle criteria.* $X\in\mathcal T^{\le n}$ if and only if $\tau_{\le n}X\to X$ is an isomorphism, if and only if $\tau_{\ge n+1}X=0$, if and only if $\operatorname{Hom}(X,\mathcal T^{\ge n+1})=0$; dually $X\in\mathcal T^{\ge n}$ if and only if $X\to\tau_{\ge n}X$ is an isomorphism, if and only if $\tau_{\le n-1}X=0$, if and only if $\operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal T^{\le n-1},X)=0$.

(iv) *Extensions, direct sums and iteration.* If in a distinguished triangle two of the three vertices lie in $\mathcal T^{\le n}$ (respectively $\mathcal T^{\ge n}$), then so does the third; a finite direct sum lies in $\mathcal T^{\le n}$ (respectively $\mathcal T^{\ge n}$) if and only if each summand does. For $m\le n$ there are canonical isomorphisms $\tau_{\le m}\tau_{\le n}\cong\tau_{\le m}$, $\tau_{\le n}\tau_{\le m}\cong\tau_{\le m}$, $\tau_{\ge n}\tau_{\ge m}\cong\tau_{\ge n}$ and $\tau_{\ge m}\tau_{\ge n}\cong\tau_{\ge n}$ compatible with the truncation maps, and $\tau_{\le m}\tau_{\ge n}=0$ when $m<n$.

items.title: t-cohomology is functorial, additive, shift-compatible and detects amplitude
items.statement:
Let $(\mathcal T^{\le0},\mathcal T^{\ge0})$ be a t-structure on a triangulated category $\mathcal T$, with truncations and t-cohomology as in [[def-truncation-functors-and-cohomology-of-a-t-structure]] and [[lem-truncation-triangles-are-essentially-unique-and-functorial]], and let $\mathcal C=\mathcal T^{\le0}\cap\mathcal T^{\ge0}$ be the heart.

(i) Each $H^n_t$ is a functor from $\mathcal T$ to $\mathcal C$: for every morphism $f:X\to Y$ the induced map $H^n_t(f)$ is the unique map compatible with $f$ under the truncations, and values lie in the heart.

(ii) *Shifts.* $H^n_t(X[m])\cong H^{n+m}_t(X)$ for all $m,n\in\mathbb Z$, naturally in $X$.

(iii) *Additivity.* For a finite biproduct $X\oplus Y$ with injections $i_X,i_Y$ and projections $p_X,p_Y$, the maps $(H^n_t(i_X),H^n_t(i_Y)):H^n_t(X)\oplus H^n_t(Y)\to H^n_t(X\oplus Y)$ and $(H^n_t(p_X),H^n_t(p_Y)):H^n_t(X\oplus Y)\to H^n_t(X)\oplus H^n_t(Y)$ are mutually inverse isomorphisms; in particular $H^n_t(X\oplus Y)\cong H^n_t(X)\oplus H^n_t(Y)$ naturally.

(iv) *Amplitude detection.* If $X\in\mathcal T^{\le m}$ then $H^n_t(X)=0$ for every $n>m$, and if $X\in\mathcal T^{\ge m}$ then $H^n_t(X)=0$ for every $n<m$. If the t-structure is bounded ([[def-truncation-functors-and-cohomology-of-a-t-structure]]), the converses hold: $H^n_t(X)=0$ for all $n>m$ implies $X\in\mathcal T^{\le m}$, and $H^n_t(X)=0$ for all $n<m$ implies $X\in\mathcal T^{\ge m}$.

(v) *Concentration and its consequences.* If $X\in\mathcal T^{\le m}$ then $\tau_{\ge m}X\cong H^m_t(X)[-m]$, and if $X\in\mathcal T^{\ge m}$ then $\tau_{\le m}X\cong H^m_t(X)[-m]$; if $X$ lies in both aisles then the canonical map gives $X\cong H^m_t(X)[-m]$. If $X$ and $Y$ both have $H^n_t=0$ for every $n\ne m$, then $\operatorname{Hom}(X,Y)\to\operatorname{Hom}(H^m_t(X),H^m_t(Y))$, $f\mapsto H^m_t(f)$, is a bijection under these canonical identifications.

items.title: Hard Lefschetz splits a bounded t-structure complex
items.statement:
Let $\mathcal T$ be a triangulated category with a bounded t-structure, with truncation functors and t-cohomology as in [[def-truncation-functors-and-cohomology-of-a-t-structure]] and [[lem-t-cohomology-is-additive-shift-compatible-and-detects-amplitude]]. Let $K\in\mathcal T$ and let $L:K\to K[2]$ be a morphism such that for every integer $j\ge0$ the map
$$H^{-j}_t(L^j):H^{-j}_t(K)\longrightarrow H^{-j}_t(K[2j])\cong H^j_t(K)$$
is an isomorphism, where the identification is the shift isomorphism $H^{j}_t(K)\cong H^{-j}_t(K[2j])$ of that lemma. Then there is an isomorphism
$$K\cong\bigoplus_j H^j_t(K)[-j]$$
in $\mathcal T$; the sum is finite because the t-structure is bounded. The isomorphism is not asserted to be canonical, and no compatibility with primitive lifts is claimed: this is the abstract splitting criterion, not the stronger primitive-compatible decomposition used in the Hodge theory of projective maps. The degenerate case in which $H^{-n}_t(K)$ and $H^n_t(K)$ are both zero (they vanish together because $H^{-n}_t(L^n)$ is an isomorphism) is covered by the same formulas, all of which are then the zero maps between zero objects.

items.title: Graded hard Lefschetz has a canonical primitive decomposition
items.statement:
Let $H^j$ be objects of an abelian category, zero for all but finitely many integers $j$, and let $L:H^j\to H^{j+2}$ be morphisms whose iterates give isomorphisms $L^r:H^{-r}\to H^r$ for every $r\ge0$. Put $P^{-r}:=\ker\bigl(L^{r+1}:H^{-r}\to H^{r+2}\bigr)$ for $r\ge0$, and $P^{-r}=0$ for $r<0$. Then for every $r\ge0$ the powers of $L$ induce finite direct sum decompositions
$$H^{-r}=\bigoplus_{j\ge0}L^jP^{-r-2j},\qquad H^{r}=\bigoplus_{j\ge0}L^{r+j}P^{-r-2j},$$
each displayed power $L^j$ or $L^{r+j}$ restricts to a monomorphism on its primitive source, and both decompositions are natural for morphisms commuting with $L$. This is a decomposition statement for graded objects in an abelian category; it does not identify primitive objects with classes annihilated by an untruncated map on a derived splitting of a complex.

items.title: The nilpotent Lefschetz filtration is canonical and self-dual
items.statement:
Let $N$ be a nilpotent endomorphism of a finite-dimensional vector space $H$ over a field. There is a unique increasing finite filtration $W$ of $H$ such that $NW_i\subset W_{i-2}$ for all $i$ and $N^r:\operatorname{Gr}^W_rH\to\operatorname{Gr}^W_{-r}H$ is an isomorphism for every $r\ge0$. It is given intrinsically by
$$W_i=\sum_{a,b\ge0,\ a-b=i}\ker N^{a+1}\cap\operatorname{im}N^b.$$
If in addition $S$ is a nondegenerate bilinear form on $H$ with $S(Nv,w)+S(v,Nw)=0$ for all $v,w$, then $(W_i)^\perp=W_{-i-1}$ for every $i$, and consequently $S$ induces a perfect pairing between $\operatorname{Gr}^W_iH$ and $\operatorname{Gr}^W_{-i}H$; moreover for $i\ge0$ the form $S_i([v],[w]):=S(v,N^iw)$ on $\operatorname{Gr}^W_iH$ is well defined and nondegenerate.

decline_pages.title: Mixed Hodge Structures And Strictness

items.title: Rational mixed Hodge structures
items.statement: A rational mixed Hodge structure is a finite-dimensional rational vector space $H$ together with a finite increasing filtration $W$ of $H$, the weight filtration, and a finite decreasing filtration $F$ of $H_{\mathbb C}=H\otimes_{\mathbb Q}\mathbb C$, the Hodge filtration, such that for every integer $n$ the filtrations induced by $F$ and by its complex conjugate $\bar F$ on the graded piece $\operatorname{Gr}^W_nH_{\mathbb C}$ are $n$-opposed: writing $F^p\operatorname{Gr}^W_n$ for the image of $F^p\cap W_n$ in $\operatorname{Gr}^W_n$ and $H^{p,q}_n:=F^p\operatorname{Gr}^W_n\cap\bar F^q\operatorname{Gr}^W_n$, one has $$\operatorname{Gr}^W_nH_{\mathbb C}=\bigoplus_{p+q=n}H^{p,q}_n,\qquad \overline{H^{p,q}_n}=H^{q,p}_n.$$ A morphism of rational mixed Hodge structures is a $\mathbb Q$-linear map $f\colon H\to K$ with $f(W_nH)\subseteq W_nK$ and $f_{\mathbb C}(F^pH_{\mathbb C})\subseteq F^pK_{\mathbb C}$ for all $n,p$. A pure structure of weight $n$ is the special case $W_{n-1}H=0$, $W_nH=H$. A substructure or quotient carries the induced or quotient filtrations; that the kernel, image and cokernel of a morphism do carry such structures is proved in the strictness lemma below and is not part of the definition. The Tate structure $\mathbb Q(r)$ is the pure structure of weight $-2r$ with $\mathbb Q(r)_{\mathbb C}=\mathbb C$ concentrated in type $(-r,-r)$. The tensor conventions are $W_n(H\otimes K)=\sum_{a+b=n}W_aH\otimes W_bK$ and $F^p(H\otimes K)_{\mathbb C}=\sum_{a+b=p}F^aH_{\mathbb C}\otimes F^bK_{\mathbb C}$, and the dual conventions are $W_n(H^*)=\{u:u(W_{-n-1}H)=0\}$ and $F^p(H^*_{\mathbb C})=\{u:u(F^{1-p}H_{\mathbb C})=0\}$. A pure rational Hodge structure is polarizable if it carries a rational bilinear form of the parity of its weight that pairs only complementary Hodge types and whose Weil-operator Hermitian form is positive definite. No mixed structure is assumed to split over $\mathbb R$ or $\mathbb Q$.

items.title: The Deligne splitting of a mixed Hodge structure
items.statement:
Let $(H,W,F)$ be a rational mixed Hodge structure
([[def-rational-mixed-hodge-structure]]) with complex conjugation $\sigma$ on
$H_{\mathbb C}=H\otimes_{\mathbb Q}\mathbb C$, and write
$\bar F^a=\sigma(F^a)$ for the conjugate Hodge filtration; all weight spaces
below are the complexifications $W_aH_{\mathbb C}$. For integers $p,q$ put
$m=p+q$ and
$$I^{p,q}=\bigl(F^p\cap W_m\bigr)\cap\Bigl(\bigl(\bar F^q\cap W_m\bigr)+\sum_{j\ge1}\bigl(\bar F^{q-j}\cap W_{m-j-1}\bigr)\Bigr),$$
the intersections and the sum taken in $H_{\mathbb C}$. Then:

(a) $I^{p,q}\subseteq W_m\cap F^p$, the intersection $I^{p,q}\cap W_{m-1}$ is
zero, and the projection $W_m\to\operatorname{Gr}^W_mH_{\mathbb C}$ maps
$I^{p,q}$ isomorphically onto the summand $H^{p,q}_m$ of the mixed Hodge
definition;

(b) $W_mH_{\mathbb C}=\bigoplus_{p+q\le m}I^{p,q}$,
$F^aH_{\mathbb C}=\bigoplus_{p\ge a}I^{p,q}$ for all integers $a,m$; in
particular $H_{\mathbb C}=\bigoplus_{p,q}I^{p,q}$;

(c) every morphism $f\colon H\to K$ of rational mixed Hodge structures
satisfies $f_{\mathbb C}(I^{p,q}(H))\subseteq I^{p,q}(K)$.

The construction satisfies
$I^{p,q}+W_{m-2}=\sigma(I^{q,p})+W_{m-2}$ inside $W_m$.
It need not satisfy $\sigma(I^{p,q})=I^{q,p}$, and the same splitting need
not split $\bar F$: its conjugate gives
$\bar F^bH_{\mathbb C}=\bigoplus_{q\ge b}\sigma(I^{q,p})$. The splitting is
the one pinned down in the sources by the displayed formula, not an arbitrary
direct-sum decomposition.

items.title: Strictness of mixed Hodge morphisms
items.statement: Every morphism $f\colon H\to K$ of rational mixed Hodge structures is strict for $W$ and for $F$: $$f(W_nH)=f(H)\cap W_nK,\qquad f(F^pH_{\mathbb C})=f(H_{\mathbb C})\cap F^pK_{\mathbb C}$$ for all $n,p$. Its kernel, image and cokernel, with the induced or quotient filtrations, are mixed Hodge structures; the functor $\operatorname{Gr}^W_n$ is exact; and a morphism from a structure of weights at least $n$ (that is $W_{n-1}H=0$) to a structure of weights at most $n$ (that is $W_nK=K$) has pure image of weight $n$.

items.title: Cohomological mixed Hodge complexes
items.statement: A rational cohomological mixed Hodge complex consists of: (a) a bounded-below cochain complex $K_{\mathbb Q}$ of $\mathbb Q$-vector spaces with a finite increasing filtration $W$ by subcomplexes, finite on each cochain group; (b) a cochain complex $K_{\mathbb C}$ of $\mathbb C$-vector spaces with a finite increasing filtration $W$ by subcomplexes and a finite decreasing filtration $F$ by subcomplexes, again finite on each cochain group; (c) a filtered comparison morphism $K_{\mathbb Q}\otimes_{\mathbb Q}\mathbb C\to K_{\mathbb C}$ which is a quasi-isomorphism; subject to the axiom: for every integer $w$ the weight-graded complex $\operatorname{Gr}^W_wK$ has finite-dimensional cohomology, its induced differential is strict for the induced filtration $F$, and for every $r$ the induced filtration $F$ on $H^r(\operatorname{Gr}^W_wK_{\mathbb C})$, together with the induced rational comparison, is a pure Hodge structure of weight $r+w$. The weight filtration on $H^n(K)$ is the shifted filtration $W_mH^n(K)=\operatorname{im}\bigl(H^n(W_{m-n}K)\to H^n(K)\bigr)$; this shift is essential and pole-count weight on a logarithmic complex is not the weight on its cohomology. The same definitions apply to bounded-below complexes of sheaves on a space when the complexes are replaced by derived global sections and the required resolutions preserve the graded pieces; the existence of such resolutions for the concrete complexes used later is proved where those complexes are constructed, not here.

items.title: Mixed Hodge complex cohomology and simplicial weights
items.statement: (i) Let $K$ be a rational cohomological mixed Hodge complex. Then for every $n$ the vector space $H^n(K_{\mathbb Q})$ carries a mixed Hodge structure whose weight filtration is the shifted image filtration $W_mH^n(K)=\operatorname{im}(H^n(W_{m-n}K)\to H^n(K))$ and whose Hodge filtration is the image filtration $F^pH^n(K_{\mathbb C})=\operatorname{im}(H^n(F^pK_{\mathbb C})\to H^n(K_{\mathbb C}))$. In the weight spectral sequence $E_1^{p,q}=H^{p+q}(\operatorname{Gr}^W_{-p}K)$ one has $E_1^{p,q}$ pure of weight $q$, the sequence degenerates at $E_2$, and $\operatorname{Gr}^W_mH^n(K)\cong E_2^{n-m,m}$ compatibly with the Hodge filtrations. A morphism of cohomological mixed Hodge complexes induces, on every $H^n$, a morphism of the resulting mixed Hodge structures. (ii) Let $K^\bullet$ be a cosimplicial system of weight-zero rational Hodge complexes concentrated in nonnegative cohomological degrees, i.e. cochain complexes $K^{p,q}$ with coface maps and an internal differential satisfying the cosimplicial identities, with $K^{p,q}=0$ unless $p,q\ge0$, and with $H^q(K^p)$ a pure Hodge structure of weight $q$ for all $p,q$. Form its simple complex $sK$ with the standard total differential and the increasing filtration $L$ by cosimplicial degree, $L_{-p}sK^n=\bigoplus_{i\ge p}K^{i,n-i}$. Then $sK$ is a rational cohomological mixed Hodge complex for the filtration $L$ and the Hodge filtrations of the $K^p$, the cosimplicial spectral sequence $E_1^{p,q}=H^q(K^p)\Rightarrow H^{p+q}(sK)$ degenerates at $E_2$, and $\operatorname{Gr}^W_qH^n(sK)\cong E_2^{n-q,q}$; consequently all weights of $H^n(sK)$ are at most $n$.

decline_pages.title: Compact Kahler Hodge Foundations

items.title: Compact Kähler and rational Hodge polarization conventions
items.statement:
Assume AC, the standing convention of this page: the analytic and cohomological suppliers invoked below assume full AC. A **Kähler manifold** is a complex manifold $X$ of complex dimension $n\ge1$ ([[def-complex-manifolds-and-holomorphic-vector-bundles]]) with a Hermitian metric $g$ whose real fundamental form $\omega(v,w)=g(Jv,w)$ is closed, $d\omega=0$, and positive, $\omega(v,Jv)>0$ for $v\ne0$; it is **compact Kähler** when $X$ is compact. The complex structure orients $X$, $(e_1,Je_1,\dots,e_n,Je_n)$ being positive for every complex frame. Normalize the metric so that in an oriented orthonormal real coframe $(e_1,f_1,\dots,e_n,f_n)$ one has $\omega=\sum_{j=1}^n e_j\wedge f_j$ and $dV=\omega^n/n!$. For $n=0$, $X$ is a finite set of points with its unique complex structure, all operators below are zero, and $dV$ is the counting measure.

Complex-valued differential forms use the complex-linear extension of the Hodge star of [[def-riemannian-hodge-star]] and the integral inner product $\langle\alpha,\beta\rangle=\int_X\alpha\wedge*\bar\beta$, complex-linear in the first variable. In holomorphic charts the complex-valued $k$-forms split as $\Omega^k(X;\mathbb C)=\bigoplus_{p+q=k}\Omega^{p,q}(X)$ and $d=\partial+\bar\partial$ with $\partial,\bar\partial$ of bidegree $(1,0)$ and $(0,1)$. Put $L=\omega\wedge$, let $\Lambda,\partial^*,\bar\partial^*,d^*$ be the formal adjoints of $L,\partial,\bar\partial,d$ ([[lem-formal-adjoints-of-differential-operators-exist-and-are-unique]]), and $\Delta_d=dd^*+d^*d$, $\Delta_\partial=\partial\partial^*+\partial^*\partial$, $\Delta_{\bar\partial}=\bar\partial\bar\partial^*+\bar\partial^*\bar\partial$; write $\epsilon(k)=(-1)^{k(k-1)/2}$.

A **rational pure Hodge structure of weight $k$** is a finite-dimensional $\mathbb Q$-vector space $V$ with $V_{\mathbb C}=\bigoplus_{p+q=k}V^{p,q}$ and $\overline{V^{p,q}}=V^{q,p}$. Its **Weil operator** $C$ acts as $i^{p-q}$ on $V^{p,q}$. A **polarization** is a rational nondegenerate bilinear form $Q$ with $Q(y,x)=(-1)^kQ(x,y)$, with $Q(V^{p,q},V^{a,b})=0$ unless $(a,b)=(q,p)$, and with $h(x,y)=Q(Cx,\bar y)$ positive definite Hermitian. A **rational sub-Hodge structure** is a rational subspace $U$ with $U_{\mathbb C}=\bigoplus_{p+q=k}(U_{\mathbb C}\cap V^{p,q})$, and the **Tate shift** $V(-r)$ keeps the underlying rational space with bidegrees $(p+r,q+r)$ and weight $k+2r$.

items.title: Rational cohomology scalar comparison on compact smooth manifolds
items.statement: Assume AC. For a compact smooth manifold $X$, the natural coefficient maps induce isomorphisms $H^k(X;\mathbb Q)\otimes_{\mathbb Q}F\cong H^k(X;F)$ for every characteristic-zero field $F$, finite-dimensional in each degree. For $F=\mathbb R,\mathbb C$ these identify singular cohomology with the real or complex de Rham cohomology. They preserve cup products and are natural for maps between such manifolds. No ordered-field or positivity structure is asserted for a general $F$.

items.title: Top de Rham integration equals fundamental-class evaluation
items.statement: Assume AC. For a compact oriented smooth boundaryless $m$-manifold $M$ and a smooth real or complex top form $\alpha$, the natural de Rham comparison satisfies $\langle J_M[\alpha],[M]\rangle=\int_M\alpha$. Thus rational cup products that become top de Rham forms integrate to their rational fundamental-class evaluation.

items.title: Hermitian exterior Lefschetz decomposition and Weil star identity
items.statement: Let $V$ be a real vector space of dimension $2n$ with a positive-definite inner product $g$, a compatible complex structure $J$ ($g(Jv,Jw)=g(v,w)$, $J^2=-1$), fundamental form $\omega(v,w)=g(Jv,w)$ and the orientation in which $(e_1,Je_1,\dots,e_n,Je_n)$ is positive, with the conventions of [[def-compact-kahler-manifold-and-hodge-polarization-conventions]]. On the complexified exterior algebra $\Lambda^\bullet V_{\mathbb C}$ the operators $L=\omega\wedge$, $\Lambda=L^*$ and $H=[L,\Lambda]$ satisfy $[L,\Lambda]=H$, $H|_{\Lambda^k}=(k-n)I$, $[H,L]=2L$ and $[H,\Lambda]=-2\Lambda$. Every degree-$k$ element has a unique decomposition $\sum_{r\ge\max(0,k-n)}L^ru_r$ with $\Lambda u_r=0$ and $\deg u_r=k-2r$. For primitive $u$ of degree $t$, $L^{n-t+1}u=0$ and $$\Lambda^sL^ru=\frac{r!}{(r-s)!}\frac{(n-t-r+s)!}{(n-t-r)!}L^{r-s}u\qquad(0\le s\le r\le n-t);$$ no nonzero primitive element has $t>n$. Hence $L^{n-k}:\Lambda^k\to\Lambda^{2n-k}$ is an isomorphism for $k\le n$, and primitive degree $k$ is equivalently $L^{n-k+1}u=0$. With $J=i^{p-q}$ on type $(p,q)$ and $W=\exp L\exp(-\Lambda)\exp L$ one has $W|_{\Lambda^k}=\epsilon(k)J*$; in particular, if $u$ is primitive of type $(p,q)$ and $k=p+q$, then $$*u=\frac{\epsilon(k)i^{q-p}}{(n-k)!}L^{n-k}u.$$ All decomposition projections are rational polynomials in $L,\Lambda$ on each fixed degree.

items.title: Kähler commutators and preservation of harmonic types
items.statement: Assume AC. On a Kähler manifold, with the conventions of [[def-compact-kahler-manifold-and-hodge-polarization-conventions]], the formal adjoints satisfy $$[\Lambda,\partial]=i\bar\partial^*,\qquad[\Lambda,\bar\partial]=-i\partial^*,\qquad[\bar\partial^*,L]=i\partial,\qquad[\partial^*,L]=-i\bar\partial.$$ One has $\Delta_d=2\Delta_\partial=2\Delta_{\bar\partial}$, the mixed anticommutators $\partial\bar\partial^*+\bar\partial^*\partial$ and $\bar\partial\partial^*+\partial^*\bar\partial$ vanish, and $\Delta_d$ commutes with $L,\Lambda,\partial,\bar\partial,*$ and preserves each $(p,q)$ type.

items.title: Compact Kähler Hodge decomposition from elliptic harmonic forms
items.statement: Assume AC. For a compact Kähler manifold $X$ in the sense of [[def-compact-kahler-manifold-and-hodge-polarization-conventions]], every de Rham class has a unique smooth harmonic representative and $$H^k(X;\mathbb C)=\bigoplus_{p+q=k}H^{p,q}(X),\qquad \overline{H^{p,q}(X)}=H^{q,p}(X).$$ Here $H^{p,q}(X)$ is precisely the set of classes with a $d$-closed smooth representative of type $(p,q)$, so the decomposition is independent of the Kähler metric. Writing $\Omega_X^p$ for the sheaf of holomorphic $p$-forms (the kernel of $\bar\partial$ on the sheaf $\mathcal A^{p,0}$ of smooth $(p,0)$-forms), $H^{p,q}(X)$ is isomorphic to $H^q(X,\Omega_X^p)$, the sheaf cohomology of [[def-sheaf-cohomology-derived-global-sections]]. The Hodge filtration $F^a=\bigoplus_{p\ge a}H^{p,k-p}$ of $H^k(X;\mathbb C)$ equals the filtration induced by the holomorphic-degree filtration of the de Rham complex, whose spectral sequence has $E_1^{p,q}=H^q(X,\Omega_X^p)$ and degenerates at $E_1$. Pullback by holomorphic maps of compact Kähler manifolds and cup product preserve Hodge type, so $H^k(X;\mathbb Q)$ is a functorial rational pure Hodge structure.

decline_pages.title: Constructible Incidence And Cochain Models

items.title: Finite simplicial constructible sheaves have an actual derived incidence model
items.statement: Assume AC. Let $K$ be a finite simplicial complex, $D$ a subcomplex and $X=|K|\setminus|D|$. Let $P$ be the face poset of the open simplices of $K$ not in $D$, ordered by inclusion of faces. The exact realization of finite-dimensional covariant $k$-diagrams on $P$ induces a fully faithful functor into $D^b(\operatorname{Sh}_k(X))$, with essential image the complexes having bounded finite-rank locally constant cohomology on each open simplex. Ordinary and compact-support cohomology, ordinary Hom and internal derived Hom have bounded finite cochain models and commute with every coefficient field extension. For a local product projection $\operatorname{pr}:V\times F\to V$ with supplied finite deleted-boundary models, there is a natural local comparison $R\operatorname{pr}_*\operatorname{pr}^*B\simeq B\otimes_k C^*(F;k)$, taking the unit to $B\otimes(k\to C^*(F;k))$. This does not assert that an arbitrary algebraic map is simplicial.

items.title: Locally split Cech nerves give actual derived Cartesian sheaf descent
items.statement: Assume AC. For a strict augmented simplicial space $Z_\bullet\to S$, its category of simplicial analytic $k$-sheaves has explicit coinduced injective resolutions. The derived augmentation is computed by the normalized double complex with first page $R^j q_{p*}F_p$ and alternating face differential. A common internal lower bound makes every total-degree diagonal finite. The same construction works for strict bisimplicial diagrams and is compatible with composition of derived right adjoints to exact inverse image. If $Z_\bullet$ is the Čech nerve of a map $P\to S$ admitting local sections, inverse image gives an equivalence from $D^b(\operatorname{Sh}_k(S))$ to the full derived subcategory with Cartesian cohomology. For algebraic principal $\mathrm{GL}$ bundles this restricts to the algebraically constructible subcategories.

decline_pages.title: Constructible Incidence And Cochain Models Examples

items.title: Incidence cochains of a closed interval
items.statement:
Assume AC ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Stratify the closed interval by its endpoints and open edge. A finite constructible sheaf has vector spaces $V_0,V_1,V_e$ with generization maps $u_0:V_0\to V_e$ and $u_1:V_1\to V_e$. Its actual derived global sections are computed by
$$[V_0\oplus V_1\xrightarrow{u_0-u_1}V_e],$$
in degrees zero and one. Thus a constant sheaf $k$ has cohomology $k$ in degree zero and zero otherwise. Extension by zero of $k$ on the open edge has one copy of $k$ in degree one and zero otherwise.

decline_pages.title: Complex Algebraic Stratified Topology

items.title: Finite complex algebraic Whitney stratification and control data
items.statement:
Let $X$ be a reduced quasi-projective complex algebraic variety, regarded as a classical variety over $\mathbb C$ ([[def-classical-algebraic-prevariety-regular-maps-and-varieties]]) with its analytic topology, its smooth points (regular local rings) and its finite smooth algebraic frontier stratifications ([[def-analytic-topology-and-finite-smooth-algebraic-stratifications]]).

(a) **Whitney conditions.** Let $X=\coprod_{\alpha\in A}S_\alpha$ be a finite smooth algebraic frontier stratification whose strata are pure-dimensional, and let $R\subseteq\overline S\setminus S$ be incident strata. In local analytic charts of an ambient smooth manifold, the pair $(S,R)$ satisfies **Whitney (a)** at $y\in R$ if for every sequence $x_n\in S$ with $x_n\to y$ whose tangent planes $T_{x_n}S$ converge to a plane $T$, one has $T_yR\subseteq T$; it satisfies **Whitney (b)** at $y$ if additionally, whenever $y_n\in R$ with $y_n\to y$ and the real secant lines through $x_n,y_n$ converge to a line $\ell$, one has $\ell\subseteq T$. A **finite complex algebraic Whitney stratification** of $X$ is a finite smooth algebraic frontier stratification satisfying (a) and (b) at every point of every incident pair. Coordinate independence of the limits and the implication (b)$\Rightarrow$(a), commonly used in the literature, are not assumed as proved here; requiring both conditions makes the intended interface explicit.

(b) **Tube control data.** A system of **tube control data** on the analytic stratified space $X$ consists of an open neighbourhood $T_R$ of each stratum $R$, a continuous retraction $\pi_R:T_R\to R$ and a continuous radius $\rho_R:T_R\to[0,\infty)$ such that $\rho_R^{-1}(0)=R$, both maps are smooth on each stratum, and for every incident upper stratum $S$ the pair $(\pi_R,\rho_R)$ restricts to a submersion $S\cap T_R\to R\times(0,\infty)$. On the overlap neighbourhoods where the compositions are defined one requires $\pi_R\pi_S=\pi_R$ and $\rho_R\pi_S=\rho_R$ for $R<S$; every compatibility assertion must name the common domain on which the composition is defined. Tubes may be shrunk. For local conical constructions one requires local properness over compact base slices: sufficiently small closed radius ranges over a compact neighbourhood in $R$ have compact inverse image inside the tube.

(c) **$f$-compatible tubes and controlled lifts.** Let $f:W\to B$ be a stratified submersion onto a smooth manifold. A tube system is **$f$-compatible** if $f\pi_R=f$ on the tubes used. A **controlled lift** of a smooth base field $v$ on $B$ is a field $V$ that is smooth on each stratum and satisfies $df(V)=v\circ f$, $d\pi_R(V)=V|_R\circ\pi_R$ and $d\rho_R(V)=0$ on specified controlled tube neighbourhoods. **Locally bounded** means the ambient norm is bounded on a neighbourhood of every point; this is an additional hypothesis, not a consequence of the definition. **Radial controlled lifts** instead satisfy $d\rho_R(V)=\rho_R$ with fixed $\pi_R$ together with the appropriate annular overlap controls.

(d) **Conical product neighbourhoods.** A **conical product neighbourhood along $R$** is a stratum-preserving homeomorphism from a neighbourhood of a point of $R$ to $B^{2\dim_{\mathbb C}R}\times c(L)$ carrying $R$ to the ball times the cone apex, with compact finitely Whitney-stratified $L$. The radial and tangential transports must be compatible with the actual coefficient data when cohomological local systems are deduced; topological existence alone does not supply canonical derived-sheaf transport.

(e) **Finite triangulation of a noncompact space.** In the compactification convention used here, a **finite triangulation** of a noncompact space $X$ consists of finite simplicial complexes $D\subseteq K$ together with a homeomorphism $|K|\setminus|D|\to X$; compatibility with prescribed subsets means they are unions of interiors of retained simplices. This does not assert that algebraic morphisms become simplicial, and real simplicial dimensions do not replace the complex dimensions of the algebraic strata.

items.title: Complex algebraic boundary points admit normalized curve arcs
items.statement: Assume AC. Let $V$ be an irreducible complex algebraic variety of positive dimension, let $O\subseteq V$ be a nonempty Zariski open subset and let $z\in V$. There is an irreducible algebraic curve $C\subseteq V$ through $z$ not contained in $V\setminus O$. There is also a holomorphic map $\gamma:\Delta\to V$ from a sufficiently small complex disk with $\gamma(0)=z$ and $\gamma(s)\in O$ for all $s\ne0$. The arc can be obtained by analytically parametrizing a point over $z$ in the finite normalization of $C$.

items.title: Generic complex algebraic Whitney regularity
items.statement: Assume AC. Let $S,Y\subseteq\mathbb C^n$ be disjoint irreducible smooth locally closed complex algebraic varieties with $Y\subseteq\overline S$ and $\dim Y<\dim S$. There is a proper closed algebraic subset $E\subsetneq Y$ such that $(S,Y)$ satisfies Whitney (a) and (b) at every point of $Y\setminus E$. Finitely many prescribed incident upper strata can be treated with one common exceptional subset by taking a finite union. The same result holds in the affine charts of a quasi-projective algebraic ambient manifold.

items.title: Complex algebraic morphisms admit compatible finite smooth stratifications
items.statement: Assume AC. Let $f:X\to Y$ be one morphism of reduced separated complex algebraic varieties of finite type, and prescribe finitely many closed algebraic subsets of each. There are finite partitions of $X$ and $Y$ into irreducible smooth locally closed algebraic strata such that every prescribed subset is a union of strata, every stratum closure is a union of strata of no larger dimension with boundary of strictly smaller dimension, and each source stratum maps surjectively and smoothly onto one target stratum. On analytic spaces each such restriction is a submersion. The source may be empty. No Whitney condition, conical control or topological triviality is asserted.

items.title: Complex algebraic varieties and maps admit compatible finite stratifications
items.statement: Assume AC. Let $f:X\to Y$ be one morphism of reduced quasi-projective complex algebraic varieties, and prescribe finitely many closed or locally closed algebraic subsets in source and target. There exist finite smooth complex algebraic Whitney (a),(b) stratifications with frontier on $X$ and $Y$ respecting all prescribed subsets, such that each source stratum maps surjectively and smoothly onto one target stratum. A further finite algebraic stratification may be prescribed and refined. The analytic strata are smooth complex manifolds and the restrictions are smooth submersions. If $f$ is proper in the analytic topology, in particular if it is a projective algebraic morphism, the whole restriction $f^{-1}(T)\to T$ over any target stratum is proper; no restriction of $f$ to a nonclosed individual source stratum is asserted proper.

items.title: Whitney normal tubes have submersive radius and bounded stratumwise lifts
items.statement: Assume AC. Let a finite smooth Whitney (a),(b) stratification be embedded in $\mathbb R^N$, let $R$ be one stratum, and choose its ordinary Euclidean normal tube with projection $\pi$ and distance $r(x)=\|x-\pi(x)\|$. Near every point of $R$, after shrinking the tube, the pair $(\pi,r)$ is a submersion on each incident upper stratum. There are smooth stratumwise right inverses for its differential whose norms are locally uniformly bounded near $R$. Consequently a smooth bounded field $w$ on $R$ has smooth locally bounded lifts on each incident stratum with $d\pi(V)=w\circ\pi$ and $dr(V)=0$; there are also radial lifts with $d\pi(V_{\mathrm{rad}})=0$, $dr(V_{\mathrm{rad}})=r$ and $\|V_{\mathrm{rad}}\|\le Cr$. These are lifts relative to this one lower stratum only; no simultaneous Mather control identities or continuous stratified flow is claimed.

items.title: Relative tubular neighborhoods preserve a chain of submersions
items.statement: Assume AC. Let $S\subseteq\mathbb R^N$ be an embedded smooth manifold and let $F_i:U_i\to B_i$ be a finite family of smooth submersions such that $F_i|_{S\cap U_i}$ is a submersion. Prescribe closed subsets $C_i\subseteq S\cap U_i$, closed relative to $S$. Suppose the maps relevant at each $s\in S$ form a chain: on a neighbourhood of $s$, every $F_i$ with $s\in C_i$ factors smoothly through a single maximal such map $F_j$. Then a tubular retraction $\pi:T\to S$ can be chosen so that $F_i(x)=F_i(\pi(x))$ whenever $\pi(x)\in C_i$ and $x$ lies sufficiently close to its zero-section point in the chosen tube. Its tube map is a smooth embedding from a variable-radius neighbourhood of the normal quotient bundle. Additional prescribed positive pointwise size bounds can be imposed on its displacement and fibre radius. No convex average of manifold-valued retractions is used.

items.title: Whitney stratifications admit compatible control data
items.statement: Assume AC. Let $W\subseteq\mathbb R^N$ have a finite smooth Whitney (a),(b) frontier stratification by locally closed embedded strata. There are tube control data $(T_S,\pi_S,\rho_S)$, with $\rho_S$ a squared bundle radius, such that incident overlap compositions are defined and satisfy $\pi_R\pi_S=\pi_R$, $\rho_R\pi_S=\rho_R$ for $R<S$. Incomparable strata have disjoint tubes, $(\pi_R,\rho_R)$ is a submersion on incident upper strata, and the tube data have local properness over compact lower-stratum slices. If a smooth ambient map $f$ is a submersion on every stratum, the tubes can additionally satisfy $f\pi_S=f$. The statement is about compatible data; continuous controlled flows are a separate construction.

items.title: Controlled stratified submersions have continuous local trivializations
items.statement: Assume AC. Let $W$ be a locally closed finite Whitney-stratified subset of a smooth ambient manifold, and let $f:W\to B$ be the restriction of a smooth ambient map that is a submersion on every stratum. Every smooth base field admits, after tube shrinking, a stratumwise smooth locally bounded controlled lift. Its stratumwise ODE solutions form a jointly continuous stratum-preserving local flow with jointly continuous inverse. Each source point has a stratum-preserving product neighbourhood over a small coordinate box in $B$. If $f$ is proper, every base point has a whole-fibre stratum-preserving bundle trivialization. No global simplicial model of $f$ is asserted.

items.title: Algebraic Whitney strata have controlled local conical neighborhoods
items.statement:
Assume AC. Let $X$ be a reduced quasi-projective complex algebraic variety with a finite smooth complex algebraic Whitney stratification. Its analytic stratified space admits compatible tube control data. At every point $y$ of a stratum $R$ there is a stratum-preserving neighbourhood homeomorphism
$$U_y\cong B^{2\dim_{\mathbb C}R}\times c_{<1}(L_y),$$
where $L_y$ is a compact finitely Whitney-stratified real semialgebraic normal link. The ball times cone apex is $R\cap U_y$, and upper strata correspond to their link strata times positive radius and the ball. The local construction can preserve a chosen ordinary normal projection and radius at $R$. Links are locally constant in stratified homeomorphism type along $R$. Proper stratified algebraic submersions, with their actual analytic properness, have whole-fibre local stratified bundle trivializations; local submersions have source-neighbourhood products. No compatible triangulation or finite sheaf-cochain model is assumed or asserted here.

items.title: Compact controlled Whitney spaces admit commuting radial collars
items.statement:
Assume AC. Let $W$ be a compact finite smooth Whitney-stratified subset of a smooth Euclidean ambient space, with the frontier condition. After shrinking compatible tube data and smoothly rescaling their squared radii by positive functions of their base projections, there are normalized tubes $T_X=\{\rho_X<1\}$ and stratum-preserving radial projections $R_X(s):T_X\setminus X\to\{\rho_X=s\}$ for $0<s<1$. On every incident overlap $Y<X$ they satisfy
$$R_X(s)R_Y(t)=R_Y(t)R_X(s),\qquad \rho_YR_X(s)=\rho_Y,\qquad \rho_XR_Y(t)=\rho_X,$$
whenever the source and target points lie in the indicated retained tubes. They also satisfy $\pi_XR_X(s)=\pi_X$, $R_X(s)R_X(t)=R_X(s)$, and $\pi_ZR_X(s)=R_X(s)|_Z\pi_Z$ for $X<Z$ on overlaps. They are continuous on their stratified domains and smooth on individual strata. For a fixed reference $a\in(0,1)$, $(R_X(a),\rho_X)$ identifies the punctured tube with $S_X(a)\times(0,1)$, where $S_X(a)=W\cap\{\rho_X=a\}$; adjoining $X$ identifies it with the corresponding open mapping cylinder of $\pi_X:S_X(a)\to X$. This is a controlled topological collar; no semialgebraicity of the resulting flows is asserted.

items.title: Finite simplicial maps have explicit compatible triangulated mapping cylinders
items.statement:
Let $f:K\to L$ be a simplicial map of finite complexes; vertex identifications are allowed. Its topological mapping cylinder
$$M_f=(|K|\times[0,1]\sqcup|L|)/((x,0)\sim f(x))$$
has a finite triangulation of dimension at most $\max(\dim K+1,\dim L)$ and a homeomorphism $H$ to $M_f$ fixing both boundary copies. The triangulated cylinder retraction to $|L|$ is piecewise linear. Before triangulating, its cells and $H$ have explicit formulas. For every finite collection of pairs of subcomplexes $(K_j,L_j)$ with $f(K_j)\subseteq L_j$, the corresponding cylinders are subpolyhedra; one simultaneous subdivision makes them subcomplexes. The construction also retains the top subpolyhedron $f^{-1}(|L_j|)$ for each $L_j$. On each cell away from the collapsed end, $H$ is smooth in affine coordinates; no immersion or smooth tangent-star claim is made at a collapsed end. All boundaries may be subdivided: the lemma does not promise an extension of an arbitrarily fixed boundary triangulation without subdivision.

items.title: Compact controlled Whitney spaces admit compatible finite triangulations
items.statement: Assume AC. A compact finite controlled Whitney-stratified subset of a smooth ambient space admits a finite triangulation of dimension at most the largest real stratum dimension, compatible with every stratum closure and any prescribed union of strata. Each open stratum is a union of open simplices. The homeomorphism is smooth on the pieces within each stratum. The construction may make the finitely many normal link-bundle projections between triangulated compact stratum cores piecewise linear. It does not make an arbitrary algebraic map globally simplicial. In particular it applies individually to compactifications of quasi-projective complex varieties and to their compact controlled links, once the stated Whitney/control hypotheses have been supplied.

items.title: Finite simplicial open stars have explicit conical product charts
items.statement:
Let $K$ be a finite simplicial complex and let $\sigma$ be a nonempty simplex. Let $\operatorname{lk}_K\sigma$ be the subcomplex of simplices $\tau$ disjoint from $\sigma$ such that $\sigma\cup\tau\in K$. Define the open star to consist of points whose coordinates at every vertex of $\sigma$ are positive. Then
$$\operatorname{st}_K(\sigma)\cong\operatorname{relint}|\sigma|\times c_{<1}(|\operatorname{lk}_K\sigma|),$$
where $c_{<1}(L)=(L\times[0,1))/(L\times\{0\})$ with the quotient topology, and the cone on the empty space means a single apex. The homeomorphism takes each simplex interior containing $\sigma$ to the product with the corresponding link-simplex interior and positive radial coordinate; the simplex $\sigma$ itself maps to the apex. The link is compact and has finitely many simplices. If $D\subseteq K$ is a subcomplex and $\sigma\notin D$, this star lies in $|K|\setminus|D|$.

items.title: Finite cell local system cohomology is finite and commutes with field extension
items.statement:
Assume AC. Let $(X,A)$ be a finite CW pair of dimension $d$, let $k$ be a field and let $L$ be a $k$-vector-space local system with finite-dimensional fibres. Then $H^q(X,A;L)$ is finite-dimensional, vanishes for $q<0$ and $q>d$, and for every field extension $k\subseteq k'$ the natural map is an isomorphism:
$$H^q(X,A;L)\otimes_k k'\cong H^q(X,A;L\otimes_k k').$$
The assertion holds separately on every component, including the empty pair.

items.title: Algebraically constructible sheaves have finite compatible stratified and local cochain models
items.statement:
Assume AC. Let $X$ be a quasi-projective complex algebraic variety, $k$ a
field, and $F$ a bounded complex of analytic $k$-sheaves whose cohomology is
locally constant of finite rank on a finite complex algebraic stratification.
Fix finitely many algebraic supports and locally closed inclusions to be
respected. There is a finite compatible smooth complex algebraic Whitney
refinement, a projective compactification with its algebraic boundary
respected, and a finite pair of simplicial complexes $(K,D)$ such that
$X^{\mathrm{an}}\cong|K|\setminus|D|$, every open simplex lies in one complex
stratum, and the marked supports are unions of simplices. One can take
$\dim K\le2\dim_{\mathbb C}X$; in particular constant-sheaf cohomology vanishes
above that real dimension. The same construction applies individually to the
compact controlled links supplied by the conical-neighborhood theorem.

On these models, actual ordinary and compact-support cohomology, ordinary
derived Hom, internal derived Hom and local cohomology with a prescribed
algebraic support have bounded finite-dimensional cochain models. Internal Hom
is constructible on a finite complex Whitney refinement. The local link and
support models vary locally constantly along the corresponding complex strata;
thus their cohomology has finite rank there. Every such model commutes with
extension of the coefficient field. Inclusions and supports are chosen in
finite collections for a given construction; no compatible triangulation of
arbitrary algebraic maps or cyclic diagrams is asserted. Perverse dimensions
remain the dimensions of the complex strata, independent of the auxiliary real
simplices.

items.title: Complex algebraic constructible complexes have finite conical cochain models
items.statement: Assume AC ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). For quasi-projective complex varieties and finitely many algebraic operations/support collections, the geometric suppliers give individually chosen compatible smooth Whitney strata, conical local products and finite deleted-boundary triangulation models for each operation. No simultaneous stratification of an arbitrary cyclic diagram respecting all marked supports is asserted. On any separated finite-type complex variety, bounded algebraically constructible objects have bounded finite ordinary and compact-support cohomology, ordinary derived Hom and bounded constructible internal Hom, with coefficient-extension compatibility, by these models locally and finite affine-open descent globally. A noncompact variety is not asserted to be a finite compact realization.

decline_pages.title: Complex Algebraic Stratified Topology Examples

items.title: A noncompact algebraic line needs a deleted boundary triangulation
items.statement: The analytic complex affine line $\mathbb A^1(\mathbb C)=\mathbb C$ cannot be homeomorphic to the realization of a finite simplicial complex. It is homeomorphic to a finite triangulated compactification with one boundary vertex deleted. Thus "finite triangulation" for noncompact varieties must allow a deleted subcomplex or another equivalent noncompact finite-cell convention.

decline_pages.title: Logarithmic Hodge Complexes And Smooth Open Weights

items.title: SNC projective compactifications of smooth quasiprojective varieties
items.statement: Assume AC. Every smooth quasiprojective complex variety $U$ admits a smooth projective compactification $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ with reduced boundary a simple normal crossings divisor $D$. Given finitely many such compactifications, there is another dominating all of them and restricting to the identity on $U$. A morphism of smooth quasiprojective varieties extends to a morphism of such compactifications after modifying the source compactification outside its open variety.

items.title: Modification preserves open cohomology images
items.statement: Assume AC. Let $p:X'\to X$ be a proper morphism between smooth projective complex varieties of equal pure dimension, restricting to the identity on a common open variety $U$. Then $H^n(X,\mathbb Q)$ and $H^n(X',\mathbb Q)$ have the same image in $H^n(U,\mathbb Q)$ for every $n$. Consequently the compactification-image formula of logarithmic weights extends from an SNC compactification to every smooth projective compactification.

items.title: Logarithmic construction of smooth-open mixed Hodge structures
items.statement:
Assume AC. Let $U$ be smooth quasiprojective over $\mathbb C$, and choose an SNC smooth projective compactification $j:U\hookrightarrow X$, boundary $D$. The logarithmic de Rham complex with Hodge filtration by degree and pole-count weight filtration constructs a functorial rational mixed Hodge structure on $H^n(U,\mathbb Q)$, independent of the compactification. Its weights are at least $n$, and
$$W_nH^n(U,\mathbb Q)=\operatorname{im}(H^n(X,\mathbb Q)\longrightarrow H^n(U,\mathbb Q)).$$

decline_pages.title: Projective Hodge Polarization Foundations

items.title: Smooth projective analytifications have rational Kähler forms
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]), inherited from the Jacobian-criterion, embedding and Chern-form suppliers below. Let $X$ be a smooth projective complex scheme of pure dimension $n$. Then the closed points of $X$ carry a structure of **compact Hausdorff second-countable smooth complex manifold** $X^{\mathrm{an}}$ of complex dimension $n$, its analytification, such that: every standard smooth algebraic chart of $X$ becomes a holomorphic chart of $X^{\mathrm{an}}$, and every morphism of smooth complex schemes $X\to Y$ induces a holomorphic map $X^{\mathrm{an}}\to Y^{\mathrm{an}}$. Moreover, for every ample invertible sheaf $A$ on $X$ there is a smooth positive closed real $(1,1)$-form $\eta_A$ on $X^{\mathrm{an}}$ whose de Rham class is the real image of the topological first Chern class $c_1(A):=c_1(A^{\mathrm{an}})\in H^2(X^{\mathrm{an}};\mathbb Z)$: $$J_{X^{\mathrm{an}}}[\eta_A]=\rho_{X^{\mathrm{an}}}\bigl(c_1(A)\bigr),$$ where $J$ is the de Rham comparison and $\rho$ the change of coefficients $\mathbb Z\to\mathbb R$.

items.title: Kähler identities give Lefschetz sl-two and hard Lefschetz
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]), inherited from the analytic suppliers below. Let $X$ be a compact Kähler $n$-fold with Kähler form $\omega$, in the conventions of [[def-compact-kahler-manifold-and-hodge-polarization-conventions]], and put $L=[\omega]\smile(-)$ on cohomology. Then $L^{n-k}:H^k(X;\mathbb R)\to H^{2n-k}(X;\mathbb R)$ is an isomorphism for $0\le k\le n$. Harmonic representatives transport $(L,\Lambda,H)$ to an $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ action: here $\Lambda$ on cohomology means applying $\Lambda$ to the harmonic representative, not to an arbitrary closed form, and $H$ acts by $\deg-n$. Primitive cohomology is $P^k=\ker L^{n-k+1}$, and $$H^k(X;\mathbb R)=\bigoplus_{r\ge\max(0,k-n)}L^rP^{k-2r},$$ with the type decomposition inherited from forms: a class of type $(p,q)$ has primitive components of type $(p-r,q-r)$. If $[\omega]$ is the real image of a rational class $\ell$, all these decompositions and $L$-isomorphisms are rational, and they remain isomorphisms after extension to every characteristic-zero field.

items.title: Morphisms, polarizability and simplicity of rational Hodge structures
items.statement: With the conventions of [[def-compact-kahler-manifold-and-hodge-polarization-conventions]], all structures in this item are rational pure Hodge structures of a fixed weight $k$. A **morphism of Hodge structures** $f:(V,\{V^{p,q}\})\to(W,\{W^{p,q}\})$ is a $\mathbb Q$-linear map $f:V\to W$ whose $\mathbb C$-linear extension satisfies $f_{\mathbb C}(V^{p,q})\subseteq W^{p,q}$ for all $p+q=k$. **Kernels and images** are again rational sub-Hodge structures: a bidegree-preserving map sends the bidegree components of a vector into the matching components, so $\ker(f_{\mathbb C})=\bigoplus_{p+q=k}\bigl(\ker(f_{\mathbb C})\cap V^{p,q}\bigr)$ and $\operatorname{im}(f_{\mathbb C})=\bigoplus_{p+q=k}\bigl(\operatorname{im}(f_{\mathbb C})\cap W^{p,q}\bigr)$, the second sum being direct because the target bidegrees $W^{p,q}$ are distinct. The **direct sum** is $(V\oplus W)^{p,q}=V^{p,q}\oplus W^{p,q}$, with the inclusions and projections as morphisms. A **short exact sequence** $0\to U\xrightarrow{i}V\xrightarrow{\pi}W\to 0$ of weight-$k$ Hodge structures consists of morphisms that are exact as a sequence of $\mathbb Q$-vector spaces; it **splits** in the category of Hodge structures if $\pi$ admits a morphism $s:W\to V$ with $\pi\circ s=\operatorname{id}_W$. A Hodge structure is **polarizable** if it admits a polarization, and **simple** if it has no nonzero proper rational sub-Hodge structure.

items.title: Polarized rational Hodge structures split orthogonally
items.statement: Let $(V,Q)$ be a polarized rational pure Hodge structure and $U\subseteq V$ a rational sub-Hodge structure, with the notions of [[def-compact-kahler-manifold-and-hodge-polarization-conventions]] and [[def-morphisms-and-polarizability-of-rational-hodge-structures]]. Then $Q|_U$ is a polarization of $U$, and $V=U\oplus U^{\perp_Q}$ is an orthogonal direct sum of rational Hodge structures in which the complement is polarized. Every short exact sequence of polarizable rational pure Hodge structures of a fixed weight splits in the category of Hodge structures, and every polarizable rational pure Hodge structure is a finite direct sum of simple Hodge structures. These are claims about rational Hodge substructures; they do not assert a splitting for an arbitrary local system. Every rational splitting persists after extension of scalars to any characteristic-zero field; no positivity or ordered-field structure on that field is asserted, and a subobject over an extension field need not be defined over $\mathbb Q$.

items.title: Hodge–Riemann bilinear relations for smooth projective varieties
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]), inherited from the analytic suppliers below. Let $X$ be a compact Kähler $n$-fold in the conventions of [[def-compact-kahler-manifold-and-hodge-polarization-conventions]] and let $0\le k\le n$. On the primitive space $P^k$ put $$Q_k(a,b)=\epsilon(k)\int_Xa\wedge b\wedge\omega^{n-k}.$$ This form is $(-1)^k$-symmetric, pairs $P^{p,q}$ only with $P^{q,p}$, and for nonzero $a\in P^{p,q}$ satisfies $$i^{p-q}Q_k(a,\bar a)=(n-k)!\,\|a_{\mathrm{harm}}\|_{L^2}^2>0.$$ If $[\omega]=\ell\in H^2(X;\mathbb Q)$, then $Q_k$ is a rational polarization of $P^k$. Full $H^k$ is polarized by the orthogonal direct sum form that on $L^rP^{k-2r}$ is $(-1)^rQ_k$; degrees $k>n$ are polarized by transporting the polarization of $H^{2n-k}$ along $L^{k-n}$, with Tate shift. In particular this applies to smooth closed complex projective submanifolds of projective space with a hyperplane polarization, hence to smooth projective complex varieties through their smooth projective analytifications; more generally it applies to every real Kähler class, including $\ell+\epsilon\eta$ when represented by a positive closed form. For any continuous family of Kähler classes the primitive kernels (of every fixed degree $0\le k\le n$) vary continuously as subspaces; rational primitive spaces are asserted only at rational classes.

items.title: Polarized Hodge and hard Lefschetz package for smooth projective varieties
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]), inherited from the suppliers below. For a smooth projective complex variety $X$ of pure dimension $n$ with a chosen ample line class $\ell\in H^2(X;\mathbb Q)$, its rational cohomology is finite-dimensional pure Hodge in each degree, functorial for pullback along holomorphic maps of the analytifications. Cup product has Hodge type $(0,0)$ and $\ell$ has type $(1,1)$. For $0\le k\le n$ the hard-Lefschetz maps $\ell^{n-k}:H^k\to H^{2n-k}$ are rational isomorphisms, and for $k>n$ so are their inverses $\ell^{k-n}:H^{2n-k}\to H^k$; the rational primitive summands satisfy the Hodge-Riemann positivity of [[thm-hodge-riemann-bilinear-relations-for-smooth-projective-varieties]], and the sign-adjusted full cohomology pairing is a rational polarization. Rational Hodge substructures split orthogonally. The same absolute positivity and hard-Lefschetz statements hold for real Kähler classes, and primitive kernels vary continuously along Kähler families. Rational splittings and isomorphisms persist after extension to any characteristic-zero field. This package does not supply weak hyperplane Lefschetz, relative hard Lefschetz, singular intersection-cohomology purity, or semisimplicity of arbitrary local systems.

decline_pages.title: Analytic Derived Six Operations And Duality

items.title: Proper continuous maps of topological spaces
items.statement: Let $X$ and $Y$ be topological spaces ([[def-topological-space]]) and let $f:X\to Y$ be continuous ([[def-continuous-map-top]]). Then $f$ is **proper** when for every compact subset $K\subseteq Y$ ([[def-compact-space]]) its preimage $f^{-1}(K)$ is a compact subset of $X$. Compactness of subsets is the intrinsic condition of [[def-compact-space]], namely compactness of the subspace $f^{-1}(K)$ with the subspace topology ([[def-subspace-topology-top]]); by [[lem-compactness-of-a-subspace-is-ambient]] it is equivalent to the ambient reading, so a subset is compact exactly when every cover by open subsets of the ambient space has a finite subcover, and the two readings are used interchangeably below without further comment. This is the notion of properness used throughout the analytic six-operation development on this page, where the spaces involved are locally compact Hausdorff ([[def-locally-compact-space]], [[def-hausdorff-space]]). The stability properties consumed by the later items — closed inclusions are proper, composites of proper maps are proper, properness is preserved by base change along a continuous map into a Hausdorff space, and fibres and closed subspaces of a proper map inherit properness — are proved in the lemma `lem-proper-continuous-map-stability` on this page. The definition involves no choice principle: it quantifies over compact subsets and preimages only.

items.title: Basic stability of proper continuous maps
items.statement: Let $X$, $Y$ and $Z$ be topological spaces ([[def-topological-space]]), with properness as in [[def-proper-continuous-map]]. 1. If $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ is the inclusion of a closed subset, then $i$ is proper. 2. If $f:X\to Y$ and $g:Y\to Z$ are proper continuous maps, then the composite $gf:X\to Z$ is proper. 3. If $f:X\to Y$ is proper, $Y$ is Hausdorff ([[def-hausdorff-space]]) and $u:Y'\to Y$ is continuous, then the pullback $$f':X\times_YY'\longrightarrow Y',\qquad X\times_YY'=\{(x,y')\in X\times Y': f(x)=u(y')\},$$ the subset carrying the subspace topology of the product ([[def-product-topology]], [[def-subspace-topology-top]]), is proper. 4. If $f:X\to Y$ is proper, then every fibre $f^{-1}(y)$ is a compact subset of $X$. 5. If $f:X\to Y$ is proper and $S\subseteq X$ is closed, then the restriction $f|_S:S\to Y$ is proper. 6. If $f:X\to Y$ is proper and $Y$ is locally compact Hausdorff ([[def-locally-compact-space]]), then $f$ is a closed map: the image of every closed subset of $X$ is closed in $Y$. These are the stability properties consumed by the closed-support functor $f_!$ on this page; no choice principle is used in any of them.

items.title: Derived tensor–Hom and inverse/direct image for field sheaves
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $f:X\to Y$ be a continuous map of topological spaces and let $k$ be a field. Inverse image of sheaves of $k$-vector spaces ([[def-sheaf-on-topological-space]], [[def-inverse-image-presheaf-and-sheaf]]) is exact and $f^*\dashv Rf_*$, where $Rf_*$ is computed on bounded-below $k$-linear injective replacements ([[lem-bounded-below-complexes-admit-injective-replacements]], [[thm-injective-complexes-model-the-bounded-below-derived-category]]). For bounded complexes $A,B$ ([[def-bounded-bounded-below-and-bounded-above-complex]]) the derived tensor over $k$ is their signed total tensor ([[def-sheaf-tensor-product]]), and for bounded $A$ and bounded-below $B$ the derived internal Hom $R\mathcal Hom(A,B)$ is computed by $\mathcal Hom^\bullet(A,I_B)$ in a $k$-linear bounded-below injective model $B\to I_B$ ([[def-sheaf-hom]], [[def-derived-hom-in-the-bounded-setting]]). Flasque $k$-sheaves ([[def-flasque-sheaf]]) are acyclic for sections on every open set ([[def-sheaf-cohomology-derived-global-sections]]). The tensor-Hom adjunction and the dg associativity, evaluation and symmetry identities are natural. No bounded-constructibility claim for the internal Hom is made here; that requires the local geometric supplier of the later constructible items.

items.title: Derived operations on analytic field sheaves
items.statement: Let $k$ be a field and let $X,Y$ be locally compact Hausdorff spaces ([[def-locally-compact-space]], [[def-hausdorff-space]]). Write $\operatorname{Sh}_k(X)$ for the category of sheaves of $k$-vector spaces ([[def-sheaf-on-topological-space]], [[def-sheaf-cohomology-derived-global-sections]]) viewed as modules over the constant ring sheaf $k_X$, and form derived categories in those sheaves ([[def-derived-category-of-an-abelian-category]]). For a continuous map $f:X\to Y$, set $f^*=f^{-1}$ ([[def-inverse-image-presheaf-and-sheaf]]) and define $f_!F$ on an open $V\subseteq Y$ to consist of the sections of $F$ on $f^{-1}(V)$ whose closed support ([[def-support-of-a-sheaf-section]], [[def-compactly-supported-global-sections]]) maps properly to $V$, properness being that of [[def-proper-continuous-map]] together with its stability lemma [[lem-proper-continuous-map-stability]]. Under AC ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]), $Rf_*$ and $Rf_!$ are computed on bounded-below $k$-linear injective replacements. Tensor means the signed total tensor over $k$ ([[def-sheaf-tensor-product]]) and internal derived Hom is the injective construction of [[lem-bounded-analytic-field-sheaves-have-derived-tensor-hom-and-pullback-pushforward-adjunctions]] ([[def-sheaf-hom]]). Suppose the uniform all-fibre-open cohomological dimension bound of [[lem-finite-fibre-dimension-gives-bounded-fibrewise-soft-resolutions]] holds, and choose its finite resolution $k_X\to K$; for an open $U\subseteq X$ put $K_U=j_{U!}j_U^*K$ ([[def-extension-by-zero-abelian-sheaf]], [[def-c-soft-sheaf]]). For a bounded-below injective complex $I$ on $Y$, define the exceptional inverse-image candidate to be the sheaf complex with open sections $\operatorname{Hom}_Y^\bullet(f_!K_U,I)$. [[thm-compactly-supported-derived-pushforward-has-exceptional-inverse-image-adjoint]] proves that this candidate is a sheaf complex and is independent of the chosen resolution. Set $\omega_X=a_X^!k$ and $D_XA=R\mathcal Hom(A,\omega_X)$ when the terminal map satisfies the same finite-dimensional hypotheses. Constructible restriction is a separate geometric theorem; none of these definitions asserts a generic six-functor axiom. The prescriptions are those of Verdier's exposé: $f^*$ is the exact inverse image, $f_!$ is the sheaf of sections whose closed support is proper over the base — a presheaf by the local nature of properness, whose sheaf property on bounded-below injective inputs is proved by the exceptional-adjoint theorem recorded in `justified_by` — $Rf_*$ is derived from the direct image [[def-direct-image-sheaf]] on bounded-below injective replacements, and the terms of the chosen finite resolution are $c$-soft and hence acyclic for compact support ([[lem-c-soft-field-sheaves-are-compact-support-acyclic]]). The ordinary-operations lemma also supplies the flasque acyclicity ([[def-flasque-sheaf]]) used to compare resolutions. AC is used only for injective replacements; the proper-support sections, extension by zero and the exceptional candidate itself are choice-free constructions. Cohomological shifts obey $H^i(A[r])=H^{i+r}(A)$ in the convention of [[def-derived-category-of-an-abelian-category]].

items.title: Exceptional inverse image as the adjoint of derived proper-support image
items.statement: Assume AC ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) and the uniform all-fibre-open dimension bound $d$ of [[lem-finite-fibre-dimension-gives-bounded-fibrewise-soft-resolutions]]. For a continuous map $f:X\to Y$ of locally compact Hausdorff spaces, the proper-support functor $f_!$ of [[def-derived-operations-on-analytic-sheaves-over-locally-compact-spaces]] is left exact, satisfies $(Rf_!A)_y\simeq R\Gamma_c(X_y,A|_{X_y})$ on every fibre, and maps bounded derived categories into bounded derived categories. Its exceptional inverse-image candidate $f^!$ represents the natural Hom transposition $$\operatorname{Hom}(Rf_!A,B)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}(A,f^!B)$$ for bounded source objects $A$ and bounded-below target objects $B$, and has lower cohomological bound $\inf(B)-d$. When the later geometric theorem proves that $f^!$ preserves the bounded constructible subcategory, this becomes the right adjunction $Rf_!\dashv f^!$ there; on that bounded constructible specialization the adjunction unit, counit and resolution comparisons satisfy the triangle, identity and cocycle laws. The proper-support evaluation constructs the counit directly. The proof constructs this adjoint from a finite fibrewise-soft resolution and generator complexes, independently of Verdier biduality; it does not infer an unrestricted $D^+$-source adjunction from the bounded-source generator argument.

items.title: Support localization, base change, projection and trace calculus
items.statement: Under the preceding locally compact and finite-dimensional hypotheses, $u^*Rf_!\simeq Rf'_!v^*$ for Cartesian squares; proper maps have $Rf_!=Rf_*$, giving proper ordinary base change. Bounded tensor factors satisfy the projection formula. Proper-support direct images compose canonically. On the bounded constructible specialization proved by the subsequent local duality construction, exceptional adjoints also compose canonically; their units, counits and traces respect composition and Cartesian pasting. For a closed inclusion $i:Z\to X$ with complement $j$, $i^!$ is the derived functor of $i^{-1}\Gamma_Z$, and both localization triangles hold. Locally, $R\mathcal Hom(i_*k_Z,A)$ is $R\Gamma_ZA$. This lemma does not assume or claim extraordinary dual base change before constructible biduality.

items.title: Constructible Verdier duality and complex orientation
items.statement: Assume AC and the actual finite conical/triangulation and derived-incidence-model suppliers listed below. On the analytic space $X$ of a separated finite-type complex algebraic variety, constructible complexes admit the fixed-space finite models required by those suppliers. Then $\omega_X=a_X^!k$ and $D_X=R\mathcal Hom(-,\omega_X)$ preserve bounded constructible objects and the natural evaluation $A\to D_XD_XA$ is an isomorphism. On a smooth complex $d$-variety, the complex orientation normalizes $\omega_X\simeq k_X[2d]$. For constructible maps for which the geometric supplier proves the stated bounded outputs, $Rf_*D_X\simeq D_YRf_!$, $D_YRf_*\simeq Rf_!D_X$, and $f^!\simeq D_Xf^*D_Y$. Proper base change has the coherent extraordinary dual exchange $u^!Rf_*\simeq Rf'_*v^!$. The fixed-space triangulation is not an assumed globally simplicial model of $f$.

items.title: Coherent six operations on analytic constructible field sheaves
items.statement: Assume AC and the actual geometric and derived-incidence suppliers of the Verdier theorem. For analytic algebraic maps on its proved constructible subcategory, the six operations $f^*,Rf_*,Rf_!,f^!,\otimes_k^L,R\mathcal Hom$ have their three adjunctions, composition and identity comparisons, ordinary proper and extraordinary proper base change, projection formula, support localization, dualizing transitivity and trace. The comparisons commute with Cartesian pasting, composition of maps, evaluation and trace, giving a coherent pull-push product calculus. For a locally trivial product projection with finite-type smooth fibre $F$, the actual finite product cochain model gives $R\mathrm{pr}_*\mathrm{pr}^*B\simeq B\otimes_k C^*(F;k)$, with its ordinary unit. Smooth base change for $Rf_*$ holds whenever a supplied factorization $f=p\circ j$ has $p$ proper and $j$ an open inclusion with the conical local models below; proper maps already satisfy it. Their finite constructible models commute with extension of coefficient fields. Geometric output preservation is the exact geometric supplier, not an additional axiom.

items.title: Actual analytic constructible sheaves admit coherent six operations
items.statement: Assume AC ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) and let $k$ be an arbitrary field. On separated finite-type complex varieties, the ordinary analytic sheaf operations restrict to bounded algebraically constructible complexes $D_c^b(-;k)$ ([[def-algebraically-constructible-complex-of-analytic-field-sheaves]]): $f^*\dashv Rf_*$, $Rf_!\dashv f^!$, the tensor/internal-Hom adjunction, coherent composition, support localization, ordinary and extraordinary proper base change, the projection formula and trace. Proper $f$ satisfies $Rf_!=Rf_*$. Verdier duality is involutive there and exchanges these adjoints. On a smooth complex $d$-fold $\omega_X=k_X[2d]$, and for a smooth map of relative dimension $d$, $f^!=f^*[2d]$. Coefficient extensions commute with these operations on bounded constructible inputs. The bounded constructibility and finite coefficient models are those of [[lem-complex-algebraic-stratifications-have-finite-conical-cochain-models]] and [[lem-finite-simplicial-constructible-sheaves-have-a-derived-incidence-model]].

items.title: Ordinary middle perverse t structure, recollement and intersection complexes
items.statement: Assume AC ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) and let $k$ be any field. On $D_c^b(X;k)$ for a separated finite-type complex variety $X$, middle perversity is given on smooth complex strata $S$ by the two inequalities $H^q(i_S^*A)=0$ for $q>-\dim_{\mathbb C}S$ and $H^q(i_S^!A)=0$ for $q<-\dim_{\mathbb C}S$. These inequalities define a bounded t structure ([[def-canonical-t-structure-on-a-derived-category]]) on $D_c^b(X;k)$, independent of compatible refinement and gluing across algebraic open/closed decompositions. Verdier duality exchanges its two aisles. The heart is abelian and of finite length, and its simple objects are the intersection complexes $j_{!*}L[\dim_{\mathbb C}Z]$ of simple finite-rank local systems $L$ ([[def-locally-constant-sheaf-of-finite-rank]]) on dense smooth opens of irreducible supports $Z$. Open restriction is perverse exact. Heart objects have no negative Hom, and the endomorphism ring of a simple object is a division $k$-algebra. This is the ORDINARY category: no equivariant category, no normalization, no semisimplicity and no noncharacteristic theorem is used or asserted.

items.title: Smooth complex pullback is exact for the middle perverse t structure
items.statement: Assume AC ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) and let $a:X\to Y$ be a smooth algebraic map of pure relative complex dimension $d$ between separated finite-type complex varieties, over an arbitrary coefficient field $k$. Then $a^*[d]$ is exact for the ordinary middle-perverse t structures of [[thm-ordinary-middle-perverse-t-structure-glues-and-has-simple-intersection-complexes]] on $D_c^b(-;k)$, and it commutes with their truncation and cohomology functors. Complex orientation gives $a^!=a^*[2d]$. If $a$ is surjective, its normalized pullback is conservative and reflects the perverse support and cosupport inequalities. The compatible finite stratifications used are those of [[thm-complex-algebraic-varieties-and-maps-admit-compatible-finite-stratifications]].
