decline_pages.title: Equivariant Constructible Perverse Foundations

items.title: Equivariant constructible derived category of complex varieties
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) and let $k$ be a characteristic-zero field. Let $X$ be a separated finite-type complex algebraic variety ([[def-classical-algebraic-prevariety-regular-maps-and-varieties]]) carrying an algebraic action of a product $G=\prod_i\operatorname{GL}_{n_i}(\mathbb C)$ of complex general linear groups ([[def-invertible-matrix-and-general-linear-group]]). Form the analytic action nerve $G^p\times X$: the simplicial space whose $p$-th space is $G^p\times X$ with the usual face and degeneracy structure maps. In the abelian category of all simplicial sheaves of $k$-vector spaces on this nerve ([[def-sheaf-on-topological-space]], [[def-module-on-ringed-space]]), take its bounded derived category ([[def-derived-category-of-an-abelian-category]]). The full subcategory $D^b_{G,c}(X;k)$ consists of the complexes whose cohomology sheaves are Cartesian under every nerve structure map and whose restrictions to the degree-zero space $X$ are algebraically constructible with finite-dimensional stalks ([[def-algebraically-constructible-complex-of-analytic-field-sheaves]]). Boundedness means uniform cohomological boundedness in the simplicial sheaf category. Morphisms are morphisms in that ambient derived category, not morphisms in the derived category of naive equivariant sheaves. Set $\operatorname{Ext}_G^m(A,B)=\operatorname{Hom}(A,B[m])$ with the ordinary cochain shift. Restriction to $X$ is the forgetful functor. The ambient category and its explicit coinduced injective resolutions are supplied by [[lem-locally-split-cech-nerves-give-derived-cartesian-sheaf-descent]]; triangulatedness, local smallness, conservative restriction and the finite GL Stiefel resolution comparisons are established by [[lem-cartesian-simplicial-sheaves-model-equivariant-constructible-derived-hom]], recorded as this definition's well-definedness discharge.

items.title: Acyclic product fibers stabilize bounded constructible pullback Hom
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $f:Y\to S$ be a locally trivial bundle in the finite constructible local-product setting of [[lem-finite-simplicial-constructible-sheaves-have-a-derived-incidence-model]] and [[lem-complex-algebraic-stratifications-have-finite-conical-cochain-models]], with nonempty connected finite-type smooth fiber $F$. Suppose the constant-sheaf cohomology of the fiber is $k$ in degree zero and vanishes in degrees $1,\dots,r$. For $B\in D_c^{\ge b}(S;k)$ the cone of the unit $B\to Rf_*f^*B$ belongs to $D^{\ge b+r+1}$. For $A\in D_c^{\le a}$, pullback gives an isomorphism $\operatorname{Hom}(A,B[m])\cong\operatorname{Hom}(f^*A,f^*B[m])$ whenever $m\le b+r-a$. It is fully faithful on $D_c^{[b,a]}$ when $r\ge a-b$, and its image is characterized by the counit $f^*\tau^{\le a}Rf_*C\to C$ being an isomorphism and is closed under direct summands. Extension closure is asserted only for the stronger bound $r\ge a-b+1$; at $r=a-b$ only the degree-zero Hom comparison and retract closure are claimed. No global tensor splitting $Rf_*f^*B\simeq B\otimes R\Gamma(F;k)$ is asserted.

items.title: General linear frame spaces have the Stiefel cohomology gap
items.statement: Assume AC. For $n_i\ge1$, $N_i\ge n_i+1$ and a field $k$, put $U_N=\prod_i\operatorname{Inj}(\mathbb C^{n_i},\mathbb C^{N_i})$ and $r_N=2\min_i(N_i-n_i)$. Each $\operatorname{Inj}(\mathbb C^n,\mathbb C^N)$ is homotopy equivalent to the Stiefel space $V_n(\mathbb C^N)$; each $V_n(\mathbb C^N)$ is a compact path-connected smooth manifold homeomorphic to a finite CW complex, and the forgetting map $V_n(\mathbb C^N)\to V_{n-1}(\mathbb C^N)$ is a numerable locally trivial bundle with fiber $S^{2(N-n)+1}$, hence a Serre fibration. Consequently $H^0(U_N;k)\cong k$ and $H^j(U_N;k)=0$ for $1\le j\le r_N$.

items.title: General linear Stiefel approximations stabilize bounded constructible Hom
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let
$G=\prod_i\operatorname{GL}_{n_i}(\mathbb C)$ be a finite product of complex
general linear groups with $n_i\ge1$
([[def-invertible-matrix-and-general-linear-group]]), acting algebraically on a
separated finite-type complex algebraic variety $X$
([[def-classical-algebraic-prevariety-regular-maps-and-varieties]],
[[def-algebraic-group-action-and-scheme-theoretic-stabilizer]]). For integers
$N_i\ge n_i+1$ put
$$U_N=\prod_i\operatorname{Inj}(\mathbb C^{n_i},\mathbb C^{N_i}),\qquad B_N=\prod_i\operatorname{Gr}(n_i,N_i),\qquad X_N=(U_N\times X)/G,$$
where $G$ acts on $U_N$ by precomposition of frames and on $U_N\times X$
diagonally, and set $r_N=2\min_i(N_i-n_i)$. Let
$p_N:G^\bullet\times P_N\to G^\bullet\times X$, with
$P_N=U_N\times X$ and $p_N=(\mathrm{id},\operatorname{pr}_X)$, be the
simplicial map of the two action nerves
([[def-equivariant-constructible-derived-category-for-complex-algebraic-varieties]]),
and let $Q_N:D^b_{G,c}(X;k)\to D_c^b(X_N;k)$ be the composite of $p_N^*$ with
the locally split Čech descent equivalence for the principal bundle
$P_N\to X_N$
([[lem-locally-split-cech-nerves-give-derived-cartesian-sheaf-descent]]).
Then, for bounded algebraically constructible $A,B$ in $D^b_{G,c}(X;k)$:

1. **Hom comparison.** If $A\in D_c^{\le a}$ and $B\in D_c^{\ge b}$, then
   pullback induces an isomorphism
   $\operatorname{Hom}_G(A,B[m])\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{X_N}(Q_N(A),Q_N(B)[m])$
   whenever $m\le b+r_N-a$;
2. **full faithfulness.** On an ordinary cohomological interval
   $D_c^{[b,a]}$ of width $a-b\le r_N$, the functor $Q_N$ is fully faithful;
3. **image.** On such an interval the image of $Q_N$ consists exactly of the
   objects $H$ whose principal-bundle pullback $q_N^*H$ lies in the image of
   $\operatorname{pr}_X^*:D_c^{[b,a]}(X;k)\to D_c^{[b,a]}(P_N;k)$, i.e. of
   the resolution triples whose frame-bundle pullback comes from $X$; the
   image is closed under retracts, and under extensions when
   $r_N\ge a-b+1$;
4. **coherence.** For two resolutions $N,M$, use the common product resolution
   $U_N\times U_M$ and its associated quotient
   $X_{N,M}=(U_N\times U_M\times X)/G$ with projections
   $\pi_N:X_{N,M}\to X_N$ and $\pi_M:X_{N,M}\to X_M$.
   The pullbacks $\pi_N^*Q_N(A)$ and $\pi_M^*Q_M(A)$ are canonically
   identified on intervals of width at most $\min(r_N,r_M)$, and their
   Hom comparisons commute with natural transformations and satisfy the
   cocycle identity after pullback to a triple product resolution.
   No identification of $U_N\times U_M$ with $U_{N+M}$ or direct
   isomorphism of functors with different target categories is asserted;
5. **trivial group.** If $G$ is trivial then $U_N$, $B_N$ and $X_N$ are $X$
   or a point, $r_N=\infty$, and $Q_N$ is the identity of $D_c^b(X;k)$.

No global tensor splitting
$Ra_{N*}a_N^*B\simeq B\otimes_kR\Gamma(U_N;k)$ is asserted for the
frame-bundle projection $a_N:P_N\to B_N$; the comparison is used only on the
nerve and through the finite local models.

items.title: Cartesian simplicial sheaves model actual equivariant derived Hom
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). The definition [[def-equivariant-constructible-derived-category-for-complex-algebraic-varieties]] gives a locally small triangulated category with conservative restriction to $X$ and the stated ordinary shift. Coinduced simplicial injectives compute its derived morphisms. Locally split free-action descent identifies its finite GL Stiefel resolution with the full bounded resolution-triple subcategory on $X_N$. The bounded Hom and image comparisons of [[lem-product-general-linear-stiefel-approximations-stabilize-bounded-constructible-hom]] hold, including the degree-zero ring comparison and retract closure. The category is idempotent complete. No derived full faithfulness of restriction to $X$ is asserted.

items.title: Constructible six functors, proper base change and normalized equivariant duality
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]), that $k$ has characteristic zero, and that a product $G$ of complex general linear groups acts algebraically on separated finite-type complex varieties. The coherent ordinary six-operation contract holds in the equivariant bounded constructible category $D^b_{G,c}$ of [[def-equivariant-constructible-derived-category-for-complex-algebraic-varieties]] for equivariant algebraic maps: $f^*\dashv Rf_*$, $Rf_!\dashv f^!$, $\otimes_k^L\dashv R\mathcal Hom$, composition and identity comparisons, support localization, the projection formula and trace. For a Cartesian square with $f:X\to Y$, $u:Y'\to Y$, $v:X'\to X$ and $f':X'\to Y'$, the actual exchange $u^*Rf_!\simeq Rf'_!v^*$ and its dual mate $u^!Rf_*\simeq Rf'_*v^!$ obey Cartesian pasting. Proper $f$ satisfies $Rf_!=Rf_*$. The normalized dualizing object restricts to the ordinary $\omega_X$; a smooth complex $d$-dimensional $X$ has $\omega_X^G=k_X[2d]$. This is not the unnormalized quotient-stack dualizing shift.

items.title: General linear Stiefel perverse normalization is exact and conservative
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) and the finite GL Stiefel resolution $P_N=U_N\times X\to X_N=P_N/G$ of [[lem-cartesian-simplicial-sheaves-model-equivariant-constructible-derived-hom]] for $G=\prod_i\operatorname{GL}_{n_i}(\mathbb C)$. Put $s_N=\dim_{\mathbb C}B_N$. The middle-perverse structure on the actual $D^b_{G,c}(X;k)$ of [[def-equivariant-constructible-derived-category-for-complex-algebraic-varieties]] is detected by restriction to $X$, and the functor $A\mapsto Q_N(A)[s_N]$ is perverse exact and conservative. Perverse truncations lift through sufficiently large bounded finite-resolution image comparisons. At the actual degree-zero Hom stabilization bound, lifted finite projectors preserve and reflect perverse concentration and simplicity after correcting the common shift $s_N$.

items.title: Middle perverse t structure glues and has simple intersection complexes
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) and let $k$ be a characteristic-zero field. On the equivariant constructible derived category $D^b_{G,c}(X;k)$ of [[def-equivariant-constructible-derived-category-for-complex-algebraic-varieties]], middle perversity is defined on smooth complex strata $S$ by $H^q(i_S^*A)=0$ for $q>-\dim_{\mathbb C}S$ and $H^q(i_S^!A)=0$ for $q<-\dim_{\mathbb C}S$; these inequalities give a bounded t-structure independent of compatible refinement and gluing across algebraic open/closed decompositions, and the equivariant structure is detected by restriction to $X$. Its heart is abelian of finite length, and its simple objects are the intermediate extensions $\operatorname{IC}_Z(L)=j_{!*}L[\dim_{\mathbb C}Z]$ of simple finite-rank local systems on dense smooth opens of irreducible supports, with equivariant data in the equivariant category. If $A,B$ lie in the heart, then $\operatorname{Hom}(A,B[m])=0$ for $m<0$. A simple object's endomorphism ring is a division $k$-algebra, not asserted to equal $k$.

items.title: Equivariant constructible Ext is degreewise finite and compatible with characteristic zero scalars
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $G$ be a product of complex general linear groups acting algebraically on a separated finite-type complex algebraic variety $X$, and let $k$ have characteristic zero. For bounded algebraically constructible $A,B$ in the actual $D^b_{G,c}(X;k)$ of [[def-equivariant-constructible-derived-category-for-complex-algebraic-varieties]], every $\operatorname{Ext}_G^m(A,B)$ is finite-dimensional and vanishes for sufficiently negative $m$. For every characteristic-zero field extension $k\to K$, the canonical map $\operatorname{Ext}_G^m(A,B)\otimes_kK\to\operatorname{Ext}_G^m(A_K,B_K)$ is an isomorphism, natural in $A$ and $B$ and compatible with shifts and Yoneda composition. Extension commutes with the coherent six operations, normalized Verdier duality, perverse truncation and intermediate extension on these bounded constructible objects. The total Ext space need not be finite-dimensional, and simplicity is not asserted to be preserved under extension.

decline_pages.title: Geometric Fixed Parts And Gauss Manin Semisimplicity

items.title: Geometric polarizable Hodge variations on algebraic bases
items.statement: Let $S$ be a connected smooth quasiprojective complex variety. A geometric polarizable rational Hodge variation on $S$ consists of a finite-rank rational local system $H$ ([[def-local-system-of-r-modules-and-its-pullback]]), a continuous pure Hodge decomposition of its fibers, or a finite direct sum of pure weights, in the sense of [[def-rational-mixed-hodge-structure]], and an algebraic realization on a nonempty Zariski open $U\subseteq S$: there are smooth projective morphisms $f_i:X_i\to U$, degrees $m_i$ and integers $r_i$ such that $H|_U$ is a Hodge direct summand of $$\bigoplus_iR^{m_i}(f_i)_*\mathbb Q(r_i),$$ where $\mathbb Q(r)$ is the Tate structure of [[def-rational-mixed-hodge-structure]]. A Hodge direct summand means the image of a flat rational idempotent that is a Hodge morphism at every point. A morphism of variations is a flat rational map that is a Hodge morphism at every point. A polarization of a pure object is a flat rational bilinear form with the Hodge positivity property on every fiber; it is not postulated for arbitrary local subsystems: a geometric realization carries one by relative ampleness, and Hodge direct summands inherit it. The closures recorded here under finite sums, tensor products, Hodge direct summands and Tate twists, the exterior-power realizability, the duals via the polarization, and the full monodromy-stable integral lattices are proved by the family construction later on this page; that forward mention is explanatory and is not a prerequisite of the definition.

items.title: Algebraic open inclusions surject on fundamental groups
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). If $U$ is a nonempty Zariski open subset of a connected smooth complex algebraic variety $S$, then $U$ is path connected and $\pi_1(U,s)\to\pi_1(S,s)$ is surjective for every $s\in U$ ([[def-fundamental-groupoid-of-a-space]]).

items.title: Geometric Gauss-Manin Hodge variations and integral lattices
items.statement: Assume AC ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). For a smooth projective morphism $f:X\to S$ of smooth quasiprojective complex varieties, $R^mf_*\mathbb Q$ is a finite-rank local system ([[def-local-system-of-r-modules-and-its-pullback]]), with full monodromy-stable integral lattice obtained from $R^mf_*\mathbb Z$ modulo torsion, and with a continuous pure Hodge decomposition of weight $m$ ([[def-geometric-polarizable-hodge-variation]]). A relatively ample line bundle supplies flat Lefschetz operators and a flat rational polarization of this variation. Products, sums, Tate twists, exterior powers and Hodge direct summands have the corresponding geometric realizations and full integral lattices. Pullbacks of algebraic maps between smooth projective fibers preserve rational Hodge structures.

items.title: Rational descent of a complex monodromy socle
items.statement: Let $A\subseteq\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb Q}(V)$ be a finite-dimensional rational algebra. The socle ([[def-socle-of-a-module]]) of the $A_{\mathbb C}$-module $V_{\mathbb C}$ is defined over $\mathbb Q$: it is $W\otimes\mathbb C$ for a rational $A$-submodule $W\subseteq V$. If $V\ne0$, then $W\ne0$.

items.title: Characteristic-zero scalar extension of geometric semisimplicity
items.statement: Let $S$ be connected and let $\mathcal V_{\mathbb Q}$ be a finite-rank rational local system ([[def-local-system-of-r-modules-and-its-pullback]]). If $\mathcal V_{\mathbb Q}\otimes\mathbb C$ is semisimple, then $\mathcal V_{\mathbb Q}\otimes k$ is semisimple for every characteristic-zero field $k$ ([[def-semisimple-module]]). In particular this applies to rational Gauss-Manin local systems after complex geometric semisimplicity has been proved. The field $k$ need not embed in $\mathbb C$. Semisimplicity means that every monodromy-invariant subspace has an invariant complement, equivalently that the monodromy module is a finite direct sum of simple modules.

items.title: The fixed part of a geometric Hodge variation
items.statement: Assume AC ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $H$ be a geometric polarizable rational Hodge variation ([[def-geometric-polarizable-hodge-variation]]) on a connected smooth quasiprojective complex variety $S$. For each base point $s$, the monodromy-invariant space $H_s^{\pi_1(S,s)}$ ([[def-local-system-of-r-modules-and-its-pullback]]) is a Hodge substructure of $H_s$ ([[def-rational-mixed-hodge-structure]]), and parallel transport identifies these spaces as one constant Hodge structure. Equivalently, the Hodge components of every global flat section are global flat sections. For $H=R^mf_*\mathbb Q$ with $f:X\to S$ smooth projective and an SNC smooth projective compactification $\overline X$ of $X$, the image of $H^m(\overline X,\mathbb Q)\to H^m(X_s,\mathbb Q)$ is exactly the invariant space.

items.title: Semisimplicity of geometric Gauss-Manin local systems
items.statement: Assume AC ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). If $f:X\to S$ is smooth projective with $S$ a connected smooth quasiprojective complex variety, then every local system $R^mf_*\mathbb Q$ ([[def-local-system-of-r-modules-and-its-pullback]]) is semisimple over $\mathbb Q$ ([[def-semisimple-module]]) and remains semisimple after scalar extension to every characteristic-zero field. More generally the complex local system of every geometric polarizable rational Hodge variation is semisimple. The algebraic realization and geometric integral lattice are essential hypotheses; no claim is made for every polarized analytic variation on a punctured disk.

decline_pages.title: Affine Perverse Vanishing And Universal Hyperplanes

items.title: Affine algebraic Whitney strata admit distance exhaustions with finitely many stratified Morse points
items.statement: Assume AC. Let $Z\subset\mathbb C^N$ be closed algebraic and let $\mathcal S$ be a finite Whitney stratification by smooth locally closed complex algebraic strata. In every prescribed nonempty real open subset of the parameter space $\mathbb C^N$, there exists $a$ such that $\phi_a(z)=\|z-a\|^2$ is a proper strongly plurisubharmonic exhaustion of $Z$, its restriction to each stratum has only nondegenerate critical points, there are finitely many such points in total, and at every critical point $p\in S$ its ambient differential is nonzero on every limiting tangent space of another stratum approaching $p$. Multiple critical points may have equal critical values; the Statement makes no unsupported distinct-value assertion. The same conclusion applies on any closed affine complex algebraic embedding of $Z$.

items.title: Complex stratified Morse data, constructible transport and complex links
items.statement:
Assume AC. Let $Z$ be a complex algebraic variety with a finite smooth complex algebraic Whitney stratification, and let $A$ be a bounded algebraically constructible complex of finite-rank sheaves over any field $k$, locally constant on these strata. At a nondegenerate stratified critical point $p$ of a smooth real function $f$, on a stratum $S$ of complex dimension $s$, require that its tangent Hessian is invertible and $df_p$ kills no limiting tangent plane of an incident upper stratum. Let $\lambda$ be its real tangent Morse index. There are sufficiently small adapted compact critical-band neighborhoods whose local relative cochain complex is the normal relative complex shifted by $-\lambda$. The normal relative complex is canonically the restriction cone

$$\operatorname{Cone}\bigl(A_p\longrightarrow R\Gamma(\mathcal L,A|_{\mathcal L})\bigr)[-1],$$

where $\mathcal L$ is a collared complex link obtained by intersecting a transverse complex affine normal plane with a nonzero nearby generic complex linear level and a small closed ball. An empty link has zero cochains. The identifications transport the actual relative restriction maps and hold for the stated constructible coefficients, not just constant coefficients.

For a proper strongly plurisubharmonic stratified Morse exhaustion with finitely many critical points, the relative cochains across each critical value are the finite direct sum of these local complexes. Regular bands, including the ray above the last critical value, preserve actual constructible cohomology. Such an affine exhaustion is supplied by the stated distance-exhaustion lemma. If $d$ is any upper complex dimension for $Z$, the complex link at an $s$-dimensional stratum has dimension at most $d-s-1$. Unrefined link strata have the original codimensions relative to these upper dimensions; further compatible refinement only weakens a stalk-degree bound expressed using codimension.

For these algebraic ball-cut links, one can refine globally on the closed affine complex section, choose a nearby radius and generic distance center preserving its collar, and identify closed-link cohomology with the open ball cut. On that open cut $-\log(R^2-\phi_a)$ is a proper strongly plurisubharmonic exhaustion with finitely many nondegenerate stratified critical points and the same indices as $\phi_a$. The link itself is not asserted to be a closed affine variety. All product identifications are conditional only on the named topology, incidence and sheaf suppliers; no decomposition theorem, arithmetic purity or affine paving is assumed.

items.title: Smooth and noncharacteristic complex pullbacks are perverse-exact
items.statement: Assume the inherited Axiom of Choice. Let $P$ be a bounded algebraically constructible complex on a complex variety $Y$ with a finite complex algebraic Whitney stratification. If $a:X\to Y$ is smooth of pure relative complex dimension $d$, then $a^*[d]$ is perverse-exact and $a^!=a^*[2d]$ in complex orientation. If $i:Z\hookrightarrow Y$ is the restriction of a smooth complex closed embedding of codimension $c$ transverse to every stratum, then $i^*[-c]$ is perverse-exact and $i^!P\cong i^*P[-2c]$. The latter comparison is for complexes constructible for that transverse stratification; no assertion is made for arbitrary closed embeddings.

items.title: Artin vanishing on complex affine varieties
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice as inherited from the constructible derived-category construction. If $Z$ is a complex affine algebraic variety of complex dimension $d$ and $F$ is an algebraically constructible sheaf of finite-dimensional $k$-vector spaces, then $H^q(Z,F)=0$ for $q>d$. More precisely the bound is the dimension of the closure of its support. If $P\in{}^pD^{\le0}_c(Z;k)$, then $H^q(Z,P)=0$ for $q>0$. If $P\in{}^pD^{\ge0}_c(Z;k)$, then $H_c^q(Z,P)=0$ for $q<0$. The empty variety and zero coefficients give zero groups.

items.title: Affine morphisms have one-sided perverse exactness
items.statement: Assume the inherited Axiom of Choice. For an affine morphism $u:X\to Y$ of complex algebraic varieties and finite-dimensional field coefficients, $Ru_*$ sends ${}^pD^{\le0}_c(X)$ into ${}^pD^{\le0}_c(Y)$ and $Ru_!$ sends ${}^pD^{\ge0}_c(X)$ into ${}^pD^{\ge0}_c(Y)$. More precisely a bounded constructible $K$ belongs to ${}^pD^{\le0}_c(Y)$ if and only if $H^q(V,K)=0$ for every affine Zariski open $V\subset Y$ and every $q>0$.

items.title: General projective hyperplanes decrease the defect of semismallness
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice as inherited from the algebraic dimension and Bertini suppliers. Let $f:X\to Y$ be a projective morphism of complex projective varieties with $X$ smooth, nonempty and irreducible of dimension $n$. Fix a projective embedding $X\hookrightarrow\mathbb P^d$ with $d\ge1$ and let $Y_i=\{y:\dim f^{-1}(y)=i\}$. Put $r(f)=\max_{Y_i\ne\varnothing}(2i+\dim Y_i-n)$. For the universal hyperplane incidence $g:\mathcal X\to Y\times(\mathbb P^d)^\vee$ one has $r(g)\le r(f)-1$ if $r(f)>0$. If $r(f)=0$, $g$ is small: it has defect zero and every positive-fiber-dimensional stratum gives a strictly negative defect contribution.

There is a nonempty Zariski open subset of the hyperplane parameter space such that every hyperplane $H$ in it has smooth $X_H=X\cap H$ and satisfies the same conclusions for $f_H:X_H\to Y$: its defect is at most $r(f)-1$ if $r(f)>0$, and it is small if $r(f)=0$. Empty hyperplane sections are omitted from the defect computation and have zero pushforward. Successive general sections therefore lower a positive defect at every nonempty step. A finite prescribed algebraic Whitney stratification can also be met transversally by shrinking this open subset when the separately supplied stratified transversality theorem is applicable.

items.title: Universal hyperplanes give relative weak Lefschetz and maximal pullback subobjects
items.statement: Assume the inherited Axiom of Choice. Let $f:X\to Y$ be a projective map of complex varieties, with a fixed closed embedding $X\hookrightarrow\mathbb P^d$ and $d\ge1$. Set $Y'=Y\times(\mathbb P^d)^\vee$, $p:Y'\to Y$, $X'=X\times(\mathbb P^d)^\vee$, $p':X'\to X$, and let $i:\mathcal X\hookrightarrow X'$ be the universal hyperplane incidence. Write $g=(f\times1)i$, and for $K\in\operatorname{Perv}(X;k)$ put $M=i^*p'^*K[d-1]$. Then $M$ is perverse and the restriction/Gysin maps give isomorphisms $p^*{}^pH^l(Rf_*K)[d]\to{}^pH^{l+1}(Rg_*M)$ for $l\le-2$ and monomorphisms for $l=-1$, with dual isomorphisms for $l\ge2$ and epimorphisms for $l=1$. In particular $p^*{}^pH^{-1}(Rf_*K)[d]$ identifies with the largest perverse subobject of ${}^pH^0(Rg_*M)$ belonging to the essential image of $p^*[d]$, and $p^*{}^pH^1(Rf_*K)[d]$ with the largest such quotient.

items.title: Universal hyperplanes lower the defect for projective space to a point
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice as inherited from the cited geometry suppliers. For $f:\mathbb P^n\to\mathrm{pt}$ with $n\ge1$, the defect is $r(f)=n$. The universal hyperplane family maps to the dual space $(\mathbb P^n)^\vee$ with fibers $\mathbb P^{n-1}$ and has defect $n-1$.

items.title: Complex-oriented diagonal Thom classes realize exceptional exchange on supports
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) as inherited from the analytic six-functor and equivariant constructible suppliers below. In the analytic constructible six-functor setting, let $M$ be a smooth complex manifold of pure dimension $d$, and let $A\to M$, $B\to M$ be algebraic maps whose fiber product is $T$. Assume the supplied duality construction has localization, tensor-Hom adjunction, coherent exchange maps, and the smooth orientation normalized by the positive compactly supported generator on a complex coordinate ball ([[thm-analytic-sheaf-six-operations-have-coherent-base-change-projection-and-trace]]), with its equivariant constructible form supplied by [[thm-constructible-six-functors-proper-base-change-and-verdier-duality]]. The refined pullback of dualizing classes on the support $A\times B$ by the ambient middle diagonal $M\to M\times M$ is the operation induced by the mate $a^*q^!\to b^!u^*$ of $b_!a^*\to u^*q_!$, after tensor evaluation and dualizing transitivity. It equals cap product with the positive middle-diagonal Thom class and lowers Borel-Moore degree by $2d$, even for singular, nontransverse supports. Ordered iterated diagonals are compatible with composed refined operations. For a complex vector bundle, zero-section self-intersection is cap product with its oriented Euler class.

items.title: Equivariant Borel–Moore homology and oriented correspondence convolution
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) as inherited from the equivariant
constructible and Borel-stabilization suppliers. Let $G=\prod_v\mathrm{GL}_{n_v}(\mathbb C)$,
let $k$ be a characteristic-zero field, and use bounded algebraically constructible complexes of
$k$-sheaves in the analytic topology, in the equivariant derived category
$D^b_{G,c}(-;k)$ of [[def-equivariant-constructible-derived-category-for-complex-algebraic-varieties]].
All functors are derived.

**Dualizing normalization and Borel–Moore homology.** The equivariant dualizing object is
normalized by $\omega_X^G|_X=\omega_X$, rather than by the dimension of the quotient stack; here
$\omega_X=a_X^!k$ is the ordinary constructible dualizing object and
$\omega_X^G\simeq k_X[2d]$ for a smooth complex $d$-dimensional $X$
([[thm-constructible-six-functors-proper-base-change-and-verdier-duality]]). Define
$$H_j^{\mathrm{BM},G}(X;k)=H_G^{-j}(X,\omega_X^G)=\operatorname{Hom}_{D^b_{G,c}(X;k)}(k_X,\omega_X^G[-j]).$$
Equivalently, for a free smooth approximation: a $G$-invariant open subset $U$ of a
finite-dimensional complex $G$-representation on which $G$ acts freely, and
$b=\dim_{\mathbb C}U-\dim_{\mathbb C}G$, the group is the eventual stable value
$H_{j+2b}^{\mathrm{BM}}(X\times_GU;k)$; existence of the stable value and its independence of the
approximation are supplied by
[[lem-cartesian-simplicial-sheaves-model-equivariant-constructible-derived-hom]]. Ordinary
Borel–Moore homology is the case $G=1$ in the same formula, i.e.
$H_j^{\mathrm{BM}}(X;k)=\operatorname{Hom}(k_X,\omega_X[-j])$, and the smooth complex orientation
gives $\omega_X=k_X[2d]$ for $X$ smooth of pure complex dimension $d$.

**Correspondences.** Let $f_i:X_i\to E$ be finitely many proper $G$-equivariant algebraic maps
with $X_i$ smooth of pure complex dimension $d_i$. Put $Z_{ij}=X_i\times_EX_j$ (reduced
analytically), $T_{ijk}=X_i\times_EX_j\times_EX_k$, and let $h:T_{ijk}\to Z_{ik}$ forget the
middle point; it is proper, being the base change of $f_j$. The first coordinate is the source.
For $a\in H_p^{\mathrm{BM},G}(Z_{ij})$, $b\in H_q^{\mathrm{BM},G}(Z_{jk})$, define
$$a*b=h_*\Delta_{X_j}^{!}(a\boxtimes b)\in H_{p+q-2d_j}^{\mathrm{BM},G}(Z_{ik}).$$
Here $\Delta_{X_j}^{!}$ is the refined oriented middle-diagonal operation on supports of
[[lem-complex-oriented-diagonal-thom-class-realizes-the-six-functor-exchange-on-supports]]: it
restricts the external class to $T_{ijk}$ by the Thom class of the complex normal bundle $TX_j$
of $X_j\hookrightarrow X_j\times X_j$. It is defined on arbitrary closed supports; no
transversality of $Z_{ij}$ and $Z_{jk}$ is assumed. Proper pushforward is the dualizing trace.
The ordered coordinates are $(i,j,j,k)$, and the two middle factors are contracted without a
permutation. If intermediate indices differ, the product is set to zero. Put degree $d_i+d_j-p$
on the $(i,j)$ corner. The normalized diagonal class $[\Delta_{X_i}]$ has corner degree zero.

**Sheaf model.** The sheaf model of the refined Thom operation uses the exchange morphism
$u^*v^!\to v'^!u'^*$ for the middle Cartesian square: with $u:Z_{ij}\to X_j$,
$v:Z_{jk}\to X_j$, $T=Z_{ij}\times_{X_j}Z_{jk}$ and projections $v':T\to Z_{ij}$,
$u':T\to Z_{jk}$, the morphism is obtained as the adjunction mate of proper base change
$u'_!v'^*\cong v^*u_!$. It is a morphism, not an asserted isomorphism for arbitrary supports.
Its orientation is fixed by the Thom class restricting to $+1$ on every positively
complex-oriented normal fiber. Agreement of this model with the stated refined geometric
operation, and compatibility with composition, are proved in
[[thm-verdier-duality-identification-intertwines-yoneda-product-and-convolution]] after the
foundational six-functor inputs are available.

**Well-formedness.** The definition is independent of the chosen free smooth approximation
because the stable Borel value exists and stabilizes by
[[lem-cartesian-simplicial-sheaves-model-equivariant-constructible-derived-hom]]; the product is
defined because the refined middle-diagonal operation of
[[lem-complex-oriented-diagonal-thom-class-realizes-the-six-functor-exchange-on-supports]] is
defined on arbitrary closed supports and $h$ is proper, so its dualizing trace is available; the
degree bookkeeping is fixed by the pure complex dimension $d_j$ of the middle factor. The claim
that the sheaf model and the geometric operation agree, and that the product is compatible with
composition and units, is not assumed here: it is the content of
[[thm-verdier-duality-identification-intertwines-yoneda-product-and-convolution]], which is
recorded in `justified_by` rather than in `deps` because that theorem depends on this
definition. The Axiom of Choice is consumed exactly through the three cited suppliers, whose
constructions (equivariant descent, injective replacements, Borel stabilization) declare it;
the definition itself introduces no further choice principle.

items.title: Proper-pushforward Ext is equivariant Borel–Moore homology of the fiber product
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) as inherited from the constructible six-functor and Borel-stabilization suppliers. Use the constructible equivariant setting $D^b_{G,c}(E;k)$ of [[def-equivariant-constructible-derived-category-for-complex-algebraic-varieties]] and proper $G$-equivariant algebraic maps $f_i:X_i\to E$ with smooth sources $X_i$ of pure complex dimension $d_i$, as in [[def-equivariant-borel-moore-homology-and-correspondence-convolution]]. Put $L_i=f_{i!}k_{X_i}[d_i]$. For every integer $r$ and every pair $(i,j)$ there is a natural isomorphism
$$\Phi_{ij}^r:\operatorname{Hom}_{D^b_{G,c}(E;k)}(L_i,L_j[r])\xrightarrow{\sim}H_{d_i+d_j-r}^{\mathrm{BM},G}(Z_{ij};k).$$
All groups are degreewise finite-dimensional for these finite-type algebraic varieties and $G$; no finite-dimensionality of their direct sum over all degrees is asserted. The isomorphism is equivariant-cohomology linear, commutes with enlargement of the Borel approximation, and is natural in constructible coefficient morphisms before smooth orientation is applied. No semismallness, decomposition theorem, purity, or smoothness of $E$ or $Z_{ij}$ is required.

items.title: Verdier-duality identification intertwines Yoneda product and oriented convolution
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) as inherited from the constructible six-functor and Borel-stabilization suppliers. For the data and cornerwise maps $\Phi$ of [[thm-proper-pushforward-ext-is-equivariant-borel-moore-homology-of-the-fiber-product]], let $\alpha:L_i\to L_j[r]$, $\beta:L_j\to L_k[s]$. With multiplication $\alpha*\beta=\beta[r]\circ\alpha$ one has
$$\Phi_{ik}^{r+s}(\beta[r]\circ\alpha)=\Phi_{ij}^r(\alpha)*\Phi_{jk}^s(\beta).$$
Here the right product is the external-product, refined middle-diagonal Thom intersection, proper-pushforward convolution of [[def-equivariant-borel-moore-homology-and-correspondence-convolution]], not a product transported by definition from Ext. The map sends $\operatorname{id}_{L_i}$ to $[\Delta_{X_i}]$. Consequently the direct sum of all corners is an isomorphism of unital graded algebras with this opposite-composition convention; nonmatching corners multiply to zero.

items.title: Unequal-dimensional proper pushforwards carry the summed-dimension Ext/Borel–Moore degree
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice as inherited from the cited constructible and cellular suppliers. For trivial $G$, $E=\mathrm{pt}$, $X_1=\mathrm{pt}$ and $X_2=\mathbb P^1$ with $d_1=0$, $d_2=1$, put $L_1=k$ and $L_2=R\Gamma(\mathbb P^1,k)[1]$ in the setting of [[def-equivariant-borel-moore-homology-and-correspondence-convolution]]. Then $\operatorname{Ext}^r(L_1,L_2)$ is $k$ for $r=-1,1$ and zero otherwise, and the corresponding summed-dimension Borel-Moore degrees $d_1+d_2-r$ are $2$ and $0$; the reverse corner $\operatorname{Ext}^r(L_2,L_1)$ has the same two nonzero degrees. The unaugmented shifts $2\dim_{\mathbb C}X_1-r= -r$ and $2\dim_{\mathbb C}X_2-r=2-r$ give the wrong degrees in at least one corner, so the summed $d_1+d_2$ normalization of [[thm-proper-pushforward-ext-is-equivariant-borel-moore-homology-of-the-fiber-product]] is the one compatible with the two unequal source dimensions.

items.title: A point and projective-line check of source-first convolution and opposite composition
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice as inherited from the cited constructible and cellular suppliers. In the point/projective-line geometry of [[ex-unequal-dimensional-proper-pushforwards-have-the-summed-dimension-ext-bm-shift]], let $\alpha\in\operatorname{Ext}^{-1}(L_1,L_2)$ be the unit $k\to R\Gamma(\mathbb P^1,k)$ and let $\beta\in\operatorname{Ext}^{1}(L_2,L_1)$ be point evaluation $R\Gamma(\mathbb P^1,k)[1]\to k[1]$, that is, evaluation $H^0(\mathbb P^1,k)\to k$ shifted by $1$ and extended by zero on $H^2$. Then $\alpha*\beta=\beta[-1]\circ\alpha=\operatorname{id}_k$ in the source-first convention of [[def-equivariant-borel-moore-homology-and-correspondence-convolution]], and under the correspondence isomorphism of [[thm-proper-pushforward-ext-is-equivariant-borel-moore-homology-of-the-fiber-product]] one has $[\mathbb P^1]*[\mathrm{pt}]=[\mathrm{pt}]$: the refined diagonal intersection of the fundamental class of $\mathbb P^1$ with the point class is the point class, and proper pushforward to the point corner gives its generator.

items.title: Bicosimplicial total complexes agree with diagonal totalization
items.statement: For a bicosimplicial complex $K^{p,r,q}$ of modules over a commutative ring, with $p,r\geq0$ and one fixed lower bound $q\geq a$, the alternating-face total complex and the diagonal alternating-face total complex are naturally chain-homotopy equivalent: $$\operatorname{Tot}_{p,r,q}K^{p,r,q}\simeq\operatorname{Tot}_{n,q}K^{n,n,q}.$$ On the left total degree is $p+r+q$ and differential is $\delta_h+(-1)^p\delta_v+(-1)^{p+r}d$; on the right total degree is $n+q$ and differential is $\delta_{\mathrm{diag}}+(-1)^nd$. These comparisons preserve augmentation and apply to coherent derived diagrams after a supplied functorial strict resolution. They require no dimensional finiteness of the coefficient modules and no choice principle. Normalization can be applied on either side without changing the conclusion.

items.title: Proper surjections have cohomological descent for constructible field sheaves
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice inherited from the supplied injective-resolution six-functor construction. Let $f:Y\to X$ be a proper surjective morphism of finite-type complex algebraic varieties, and let $F\in D^b_c(X;k)$ for a field $k$. Write $Y_p=Y\times_X\cdots\times_XY$ with $p+1$ factors, $f_p:Y_p\to X$, and $F_p=f_p^*F$. In the analytic topology of [[def-analytic-topology-and-finite-smooth-algebraic-stratifications]] the natural augmented derived Cech map is a quasi-isomorphism: $$F\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Tot}_{p\geq0}Rf_{p*}F_p.$$ Here totalization is the normalized or unnormalized alternating-face total supplied by the simplicial-derived construction. There is one fixed lower cochain bound; consequently its diagonals are finite in every degree. The claim commutes with arbitrary algebraic base change and coefficient morphisms. In particular $R\Gamma(X,F)\simeq\operatorname{Tot}_pR\Gamma(Y_p,F_p)$. Individual fibers of $f$ need not be cohomologically acyclic, connected, or smooth.

items.title: Proper hypercovers compute constructible derived cohomology
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice as inherited from the supplied six-functor resolutions. Let $X_\bullet\to X$ be an augmented simplicial finite-type complex algebraic variety ([[def-simplicial-object-and-simplicial-commutative-ring]], [[def-analytic-topology-and-finite-smooth-algebraic-stratifications]]). Assume $X_0\to X$ is proper surjective and, for each $p>0$, $X_p\to(\operatorname{cosk}_{p-1}\operatorname{sk}_{p-1}X_\bullet)_p$ is proper surjective over $X$, where skeleton and coskeleton are the standard finite-limit constructions of the simplicial category and the target is the matching object. Such an object is a proper hypercover; no smoothness or fiber acyclicity is assumed. For $F\in D^b_c(X;k)$ over a field, and $a_p:X_p\to X$, the augmentation gives $$F\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Tot}_{p\geq0}Ra_{p*}a_p^*F,\qquad R\Gamma(X,F)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Tot}_{p\geq0}R\Gamma(X_p,a_p^*F).$$ There is a natural strongly convergent spectral sequence $E_1^{p,q}=H^q(X_p,a_p^*F)\Rightarrow H^{p+q}(X,F)$. If $F$ has cochain lower bound $a$, every diagonal $p+q=m$ is finite; degree $m$ and its differential are determined by levels through $p=m-a+1$. All proper-hypercover refinements induce the same comparison via the base object; any two such hypercovers have a proper common refinement. For $F=k_X$, $a=0$, this is the first-quadrant spectral sequence required for smooth-projective hyperresolutions.

decline_pages.title: Proper Cohomological Descent And Constructible Hypercovers Examples

items.title: Proper Cech descent does not require acyclic fibers
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice; it is inherited from the descent lemma and from the field-dual corollary. Let $k$ be a field and let $S=\mathbb P^1(\mathbb C)$ be the complex projective line, realized as the classical complex algebraic variety obtained by gluing two affine lines along their punctured overlaps by $z=1/w$, with its analytic topology (equivalently, the Riemann sphere $\widehat{\mathbb C}=\mathbb C\cup\{\infty\}$). Then the unique morphism $f:S\to\mathrm{pt}$ is proper surjective, the single fiber $S$ satisfies $H^2(S;k)\cong k\neq0$ and is therefore not cohomologically acyclic, and yet the augmented Cech complex computes the constant sheaf: the unaugmented product total $\operatorname{Tot}_{p\geq0}R\Gamma(S^{p+1},k)$ has cohomology $k$ in degree $0$ and zero in all other degrees. In every internal degree $q$ the augmented row $H^q(k)\to H^q(S,k)\to H^q(S^2,k)\to\cdots$ is contracted by inserting one chosen point as first coordinate, even though the $q=2$ row contains the nonzero group $H^2(S;k)$ at $p=0$.

items.title: Hypercover total degree uses only a finite matching truncation
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice as inherited from the proper-hypercover theorem. Let $X_\bullet\to X$ be a proper hypercover and let $F$ be a coefficient complex in $D^b_c(X;k)$ with cochain lower bound $a$ ([[def-simplicial-object-and-simplicial-commutative-ring]]). Then the cohomology of the total complex in degree $m$, and its differential, are determined by the simplicial levels $p\leq m-a+1$ only; every hypercover truncation $\operatorname{cosk}_N\operatorname{sk}_NX_\bullet$ with $N\geq m-a+1$ computes the same $H^m(X,F)$. In particular for the constant sheaf $F=k_X$, where $a=0$, degree $n$ uses only levels through $n+1$. Keeping only the cochain terms through level $n$ and omitting the outgoing differential does not suffice in general: the differential out of the term $(p,q)=(n,0)$ of the Cech complex lands in the level $n+1$ term $(n+1,0)$.

items.title: Split augmented simplicial schemes and matching objects
items.statement: Fix a base scheme $S$ and work in the category of $S$-schemes, in which finite limits and coproducts exist. An augmented simplicial $S$-scheme is a simplicial object in this category augmented over $S$, with face and degeneracy maps over $S$; its matching object $M_p(X_\bullet)=(\operatorname{cosk}_{p-1}\operatorname{sk}_{p-1}X_\bullet)_p$ is the limit of the boundary diagram of structure maps out of degrees below $p$, with $M_0(X_\bullet)=S$ and canonical boundary maps $X_p\to M_p(X_\bullet)$. Its $N$-construction adjoins to $X_p$ one copy of $X_q$ for each order-preserving surjection $[p]\twoheadrightarrow[q]$ with $q<p$, with multiplication given by the identity on $X_p$ and the degeneracies on the copies; the object is split when this multiplication is an isomorphism in every degree. An augmented simplicial object is a proper hypercover of $S$ when the augmentation $X_0\to S$ and all canonical boundary maps are proper and surjective. Neither smoothness nor properness of the individual terms is part of the definition.

items.title: Blowups of projective schemes are projective
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $X$ be an integral projective complex scheme of finite type, with structure morphism $X\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbb C$ ([[def-projective-morphism-pre-proj]]), and let $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ be a nonzero finite-type quasi-coherent ideal sheaf ([[def-quasi-coherent-ideal-sheaf]]). Then the blowup $\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I}X$ of [[def-blowup-scheme-along-ideal]] is projective over $\mathbb C$: for some $M\ge0$ its structure morphism factors as a closed immersion $\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I}X\hookrightarrow\mathbb P^M_{\mathbb C}$ followed by the projection. Consequently every composition of blowups of an integral projective complex scheme along nonzero finite-type ideal sheaves remains integral and projective over $\mathbb C$.

items.title: Smooth projective proper hyperresolutions
items.statement: Assume AC. Every proper complex algebraic variety $Y$ admits a split simplicial proper hypercover $a:Y_\bullet\to Y$ with every $Y_p$ smooth projective. Here proper hypercover means that $Y_0\to Y$ and each map $Y_p\to(\operatorname{cosk}_{p-1}Y_\bullet)_p$ is proper and surjective. Two such systems admit a third smooth projective proper hypercover mapping to both over $Y$. Every morphism between proper varieties can be lifted to a morphism between such hypercovers after refining the source. Degree-$n$ cohomology uses only the finite skeleton through degree $n+1$.

items.title: Borel-Moore homology by locally finite chains
items.statement: Let $X$ be a locally compact Hausdorff space and $R$ a commutative ring. A formal sum of continuous $k$-simplices is locally finite when every point of $X$ has a neighbourhood meeting only finitely many of the images of the simplices with nonzero coefficient; these sums form the locally finite chain complex, coefficientwise boundary included, and its homology is the Borel-Moore homology $H_k^{\mathrm{BM}}(X;R)$. Ordinary singular chains are the sums with finite support, and only proper continuous maps induce pushforwards on locally finite chains.

items.title: Borel-Moore and ordinary homology agree for compact spaces
items.statement: For a compact Hausdorff space $X$ and a commutative ring $R$, the inclusion of the ordinary singular chain complex into the locally finite chain complex of [[def-borel-moore-homology]] is an isomorphism, so $H_k^{\mathrm{BM}}(X;R)\cong H_k^{\mathrm{sing}}(X;R)$ in every degree, naturally for continuous maps of compact Hausdorff spaces; in particular the class map of a proper complex algebraic variety may be computed in ordinary singular homology.

items.title: Proper cohomology and functorial mixed Hodge weights
items.statement: Assume AC. The rational cohomology $H^n(Y,\mathbb Q)$ of every proper complex algebraic variety has a functorial mixed Hodge structure with weights at most $n$. For a morphism $g:Y\to U$ with $Y$ proper and $U$ smooth quasiprojective, its pullback $H^n(U)\to H^n(Y)$ is a mixed Hodge morphism for the logarithmic structure on $U$. If $Y\to X$ is proper with $X$ smooth projective of dimension $d$, the proper homological class map $$H_i^{\mathrm{BM}}(Y,\mathbb Q)=H_i(Y,\mathbb Q)\longrightarrow H^{2d-i}(X,\mathbb Q)(d)$$ is a mixed Hodge morphism after the indicated Tate twist. Its image, and consequently the untwisted image in $H^{2d-i}(X)$, is a pure Hodge substructure. No smoothness of $Y$ is assumed.

items.title: Weights control restriction images into proper varieties
items.statement: Assume AC. Let $U$ be smooth quasiprojective over $\mathbb C$, let $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ be any smooth projective compactification, and let $g:Y\to U$ be a morphism with $Y$ proper (possibly singular and reducible). Then, in every degree $n$, $$\operatorname{im}(H^n(X,\mathbb Q)\xrightarrow{(jg)^*}H^n(Y,\mathbb Q))=\operatorname{im}(H^n(U,\mathbb Q)\xrightarrow{g^*}H^n(Y,\mathbb Q)).$$ Both images are pure Hodge substructures of weight $n$. This includes the restriction of a smooth projective total space to a proper singular fibre through an open subvariety, which is the exact use in de Cataldo-Migliorini Proposition 8.3.2.

items.title: A proper singular curve with weight-zero cohomology
items.statement:
Assume AC ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). A rational projective curve with one ordinary node has one-dimensional
$H^1(C,\mathbb Q)$ of weight $0$, illustrating that proper singular cohomology
need not be pure of its degree.

items.title: Closed-support splitting of a perverse sheaf is detected by its costalk-to-stalk map
items.statement:
Assume AC as inherited from the ordinary constructible suppliers, and let $i:Z\hookrightarrow Y$ be a closed complex algebraic inclusion with complementary open inclusion $j:U\hookrightarrow Y$. Let $P$ be an ordinary constructible perverse sheaf over a characteristic-zero field. Set $A={}^pH^0i^!P$ and $B={}^pH^0i^*P$. The adjunction maps define a natural morphism $\alpha:A\to B$. It is an isomorphism if and only if
$$P\simeq i_*A\oplus j_{!*}j^*P.$$
More precisely, $i_*A$ is the largest subobject of $P$ supported on $Z$, $i_*B$ is its largest quotient supported there, and their composite equals $i_*\alpha$. If $\alpha$ is invertible, these canonical maps give the displayed splitting. For $Z=\{y\}$, $A=H^0(i_y^!P)$ and $B=H^0(i_y^*P)$ are finite vector spaces, so the criterion is exactly invertibility of the degree-zero costalk-to-stalk map. This criterion does not assert that that map is invertible for projective direct images.

items.title: The middle primitive polarization follows from the nonmiddle forms and a Kähler limit
items.statement:
Assume AC, let $X$ be smooth projective of complex dimension $n$, and write $H^m=H^m(X;\mathbb R)$. Let $\eta$ be a Kähler class, and let $L$ be a real $(1,1)$ class such that $L+\epsilon\eta$ is Kähler for every $\epsilon>0$. Use the centered nilpotent filtration $W$ of cup product by $L$ on total cohomology, with $L:W_a\to W_{a-2}$ and $L^a:\operatorname{Gr}^W_a\to\operatorname{Gr}^W_{-a}$ an isomorphism. Assume the following three precise hypotheses, to be furnished by the preceding stages of a projective induction:

(a) $W$ is a Hodge filtration by subspaces stable under $\eta$, and $\eta:\operatorname{Gr}^W_aH^{n-2}\to\operatorname{Gr}^W_aH^n$ is injective for every $a\le0$.

(b) For every $i\ge0$, the form
$$q_i(x,y)=\int_X\eta^{i+2}L^i x\wedge y$$
on $\operatorname{Gr}^W_iH^{n-2-2i}$ restricts nondegenerately to the kernel of $L^{i+1}$ there. This includes well-definedness of that induced form; it concerns only nonmiddle graded primitive forms.

(c) Poincaré pairing between complementary ordinary degrees annihilates $W_a\times W_b$ when $a+b<0$.

Set $D=\ker(L:H^n\to H^{n+2})$, $R=D\cap W_{-1}H^n$, and $M=\eta\ker(L:H^{n-2}\to H^n)$. Then the limit $\Lambda=\lim_{\epsilon\downarrow0}\ker(L+\epsilon\eta:H^n\to H^{n+2})$ exists as a Hodge subspace, and
$$\Lambda=D\cap\bigcap_{j\ge1}\bigl(\eta^j\ker(L^j:H^{n-2j}\to H^n)\bigr)^\perp,\qquad D=\Lambda\mathbin{\perp\oplus}M.$$
The radical of the Poincaré form on $D$ is exactly $R$. Its restriction, with the classical degree-$n$ Hodge sign, polarizes $\Lambda/(\Lambda\cap R)$. Consequently it polarizes every Hodge subspace of $D/R$ orthogonal to the image of $M$. In particular this applies to the middle double primitive subspace once that subspace's graded primitive condition identifies it with such a Hodge subspace. No polarization or semisimplicity in the middle is assumed in (a)–(c).

items.title: Simultaneous projective Lefschetz, Hodge and perverse induction step
items.statement:
Assume AC. Let $f:X\to Y$ be a projective morphism of complex projective varieties, with $X$ smooth connected of dimension $n$, let $\eta$ be a very ample source class, and put $L=f^*c_1(B)$ for a very ample target line $B$. Write $K=Rf_*\mathbb Q_X[n]$, $P_b={}^pH^bK$, $F_bH^q(X)=\operatorname{im}(H^{q-n}(Y,{}^p\tau_{\le b}K)\to H^q(X))$, $H_b^q=F_bH^q/F_{b-1}H^q$, $m=\dim f(X)$ and

$$r(f)=\max_i\bigl(2i+\dim\{y:\dim f^{-1}(y)=i\}-n\bigr).$$

Consider the following package: relative $\eta$ hard Lefschetz $\eta^i:P_{-i}\simeq P_i$; a finite normalized splitting $K\simeq\bigoplus_bP_b[-b]$; semisimplicity of every $P_b$ with semisimple complexifications of its IC local systems; target graded hard Lefschetz $L^j:H_b^{n+b-j}\simeq H_b^{n+b+j}$; pure Hodge structures of their ordinary degree on the canonical graded groups; and polarized orthogonal double primitive decomposition. The double primitive space is

$$\mathcal P_{-i}^{-j}=\ker\eta^{i+1}\cap\ker L^{j+1}\subset H_{-i}^{n-i-j},\qquad i,j\ge0,$$

with polarization $Q_t(u,v)=(-1)^{t(t-1)/2}\int_X\eta^iL^ju\wedge v$, $t=n-i-j$, and positivity $Q_t(Cu,\bar u)>0$ for nonzero $u$, where $C$ acts on type $(p,q)$ by $i^{p-q}$. Filtration and primitive forms are the canonical graded ones; no primitive-compatible lift to ordinary global cohomology is assumed.

If this package holds for all smooth connected projective-source maps of lexicographically smaller pair $(r,m)$, with $r$ primary, then it holds for $f$. The image-dimension-zero base is supplied by absolute polarized Hodge theory and finite linear algebra. Finite disconnected smooth sources are handled componentwise. The statement preserves arbitrary projective fibres and requires neither semismallness nor affine paving.

items.title: Relative hard Lefschetz and perverse splitting for compact projective algebraic maps
items.statement: Assume the inherited Axiom of Choice. Let $f:X\to Y$ be a projective morphism of complex projective varieties, with $X$ smooth of pure complex dimension $n$, and let $\eta$ be the first Chern class of an ample line bundle on $X$. For $K=Rf_*\mathbb Q_X[n]$, the maps $\eta^i:{}^pH^{-i}K\to{}^pH^iK$ are isomorphisms for all $i\ge0$, and $K\cong\bigoplus_i{}^pH^iK[-i]$ is a finite perverse splitting. Every ${}^pH^iK$ is a finite direct sum of intersection complexes of simple rational local systems on smooth dense opens of irreducible supports. The complexifications of those local systems are semisimple. This compact-source theorem will be used on explicit quiver-incidence projective compactifications; it does not assert a general nonprojective-source reduction.

items.title: Compact smooth projective pushforwards have semisimple perverse cohomology in characteristic zero
items.statement: Assume the inherited Axiom of Choice. Let $f:X\to Y$ be a projective morphism of complex projective varieties, $X$ smooth of pure complex dimension $n$, and let $k$ be any characteristic-zero coefficient field. Then $Rf_*k_X[n]$ is a finite direct sum of shifts of simple perverse sheaves on $Y$; equivalently all its perverse cohomology objects are semisimple and it splits into their shifted sum. This holds without any assumption that $k$ embeds in $\mathbb C$.

items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice as inherited from the cited geometry suppliers. Let $f:\mathbb P^n\to\mathrm{pt}$. The published triangular decomposition gives uniqueness of these two toral coefficients; moving E_i through generator words gives existence on the actual Serre quotient. The maps are Q(q)-linear, vanish on1, and send F_j to δ_ij. For actual weight wt(F_j)=-alpha_j, e_i'(xy)=e_i'(x)y+q_i^{<wt(x),h_i>}x e_i'(y) and e_i''(xy)=e_i''(x)y+q_i^{-<wt(x),h_i>}x e_i''(y). Thus e_i'F_j=q_i^{-a_ij}F_je_i'+δ_ij and e_i''F_j=q_i^{a_ij}F_je_i''+δ_ij. Writing the negative component as U_q^-[-nu] for nu∈Q_+, these maps take it to U_q^-[-(nu-alpha_i)] (zero when nu-alpha_i is not positive). They remove one letter, increase actual weight by alpha_i and decrease positive height by one, hence are locally nilpotent. They obey e_i''=psi e_i' psi under the bar. These are equivalently the corresponding primitive-leading-term coefficient maps of the braided half coproduct, with the same twists; the commutator construction fixes which coefficient is e_i' rather than e_i''. No imaginary-root convention is used.

items.title: The Lusztig divided-power integral form $U_A$
items.statement:
Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a symmetrizable Cartan datum for a quantum group with no imaginary simple roots, so $a_{ii}=2$ for all $i$ ([[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]), let $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ be its Drinfeld-Jimbo algebra ([[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]]) with $q_i=q^{d_i}$ and $K_i=K_{d_ih_i}$, and put $A:=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]\subseteq\mathbb Q(q)$ ([[def-the-laurent-polynomial-ring]]).

For $i\in I$, $c\in\mathbb Z$ and $t\ge0$ define the **toral quantum binomial**
$$T_{i,c,t}:=\begin{bmatrix}K_i;c\\ t\end{bmatrix}:=\prod_{s=1}^{t}\frac{K_iq_i^{\,c-s+1}-K_i^{-1}q_i^{\,-c+s-1}}{q_i^{s}-q_i^{-s}}\in U_q(\mathfrak g),$$
the empty product being $T_{i,c,0}=1$. Each factor is defined in $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ because $q_i^{s}-q_i^{-s}\ne0$ for $s\ge1$ ([[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]), so $T_{i,c,t}$ is a polynomial in $K_i^{\pm1}$ with coefficients in $\mathbb Q(q)$; in particular all $T_{i,c,t}$ commute with the $K_h$ and with one another.

The **Lusztig divided-power integral form** is the $A$-subalgebra
$$U_A:=\langle E_i^{(r)},\ F_i^{(r)},\ K_h^{\pm1},\ T_{i,c,t}\ \colon\ i\in I,\ r,t\ge0,\ c\in\mathbb Z,\ h\in P^{\vee}\rangle\subseteq U_q(\mathfrak g),$$
where $x^{(r)}=x^r/[r]_i!$ are the divided powers of [[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]. Write $U_A^\pm$ for the $A$-subalgebras generated by the $E_i^{(r)}$ and the $F_i^{(r)}$, and $U_A^0$ for the one generated by the $K_h^{\pm1}$ and the $T_{i,c,t}$.

Then $U_A$ contains $E_i=E_i^{(1)}$, $F_i=F_i^{(1)}$ and all $K_h$, it is a root-graded $A$-subalgebra of the root-graded $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ ([[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]]), and $U_A\otimes_A\mathbb Q(q)=U_q(\mathfrak g)$. The shifted binomials $T_{i,c,t}$ with $c\ne0$ are included because the divided-power reordering identity of [[lem-divided-power-and-toral-quantum-binomial-reordering-identities]] has coefficients $T_{i,2t-a-b,t}$ with a nonconstant index; the specializations at $q=1$ of these elements are computed in [[lem-q-one-toral-specialization-identifies-the-classical-cartan-generators]], and the integral triangular decomposition and the specialization are treated only after this definition. No freeness, integrality of choices or triangularity is asserted here.

items.title: Quantum weight modules, weights in $P$, and integrability
items.statement: For the published Cartan datum with possibly nonperfect pairing, a P-graded type-one quantum weight module is a module equipped with a direct sum M=⊕_{mu∈P}M_mu such that K_h acts on M_mu by q^{<mu,h>}, E_iM_mu⊂M_{mu+alpha_i}, and F_iM_mu⊂M_{mu-alpha_i}. These are chosen label-weight spaces. If the pairing separates P, they equal the simultaneous toral eigenspaces; without separation distinct labels may have the same toral character, so a spectral eigenspace must not be equated with a single label space. Morphisms and the weight submodules/quotients considered on this page preserve this grading. Integrable means E_i and F_i are locally nilpotent on each vector. Finite dimensions and bounded support are additional hypotheses, not part of integrability. The zero module has the empty grading. Ordinary type-one modules for a separating datum recover the usual definition. Regularization of finite-cone support and all highest-weight comparisons are proved by the local realization supplier, not assumed by writing P=Hom(Pvee,Z).

items.title: The contravariant form on an integrable highest weight module
items.statement: Fix the Q(q)-linear anti-involution sigma with sigma(K_h)=K_h, sigma(E_i)=q_iF_iK_i^-1 and sigma(F_i)=q_i^-1K_iE_i (JKK(2.2)); it fixes q and is different from the semilinear contravariant tau. For lambda dominant and L(lambda) the normalized simple highest module, a contravariant form is a homogeneous symmetric bilinear form with B(v_lambda,v_lambda)=1 and B(xu,v)=B(u,sigma(x)v). Such a form exists uniquely, is nondegenerate on every finite label-weight space, and different label-weight spaces are orthogonal. Its existence, exact Verma radical and descent are supplied by the local Cartan-projection lemma. The sigma formulas imply B(E_i u,v)=B(u,q_iF_iK_i^-1v) and B(F_i u,v)=B(u,q_i^-1K_iE_i v); sigma fixes, rather than inverts, the torus.

items.title: Quantum Verma modules $M(\lambda)$, highest weight vectors, and the simple highest weight quotient $L(\lambda)$
items.statement: For lambda∈P, put M(lambda)=U_q⊗_{U_q^{≥0}}Q(q)_lambda, with E_i acting as0 and K_h asq^{<lambda,h>} on the inducing line. Give it the canonical P-label grading: via triangular decomposition, M(lambda)_{lambda-nu}=U_q^-[-nu]v_lambda. Its highest line is Q(q)v_lambda and every component is finite dimensional (there are finitely many words of a given height). A specified highest vector in a P-graded module gives the unique degree-preserving map from this Verma module; it is surjective for a cyclic highest module. The sum N(lambda) of all proper graded submodules is proper because each has zero top component; thus L(lambda)=M(lambda)/N(lambda) is the unique simple graded quotient. For separating torus data this is the usual simple weight-module quotient. The contravariant Cartan-projection lemma identifies N(lambda) exactly as a form radical and gives the canonical normalized form on L(lambda). Under dominance, the integrable theorem proves the ordinary simple and universal integrable conclusions. No arbitrary maximal submodule is selected.

items.title: The Lusztig-Kashiwara bilinear form on the negative half: the recursion
items.statement: The normalized Lusztig-Kashiwara form is a homogeneous Q(q)-bilinear form B on U_q^- with B(1,1)=1, B(U_q^-[-nu],U_q^-[-mu])=0 for nu≠mu, and B(F_iP,Q)=B(P,e_i'Q). Equivalently the degree-zero normalization is B(1,Q)=epsilon(Q) together with the recursion. Homogeneity/counit normalization is essential: recursion and B(1,1)=1 alone do not force symmetry or uniqueness. The normalized form is unique by peeling first letters in the first argument. Its existence, symmetry and nondegeneracy are proved by the separation/form suppliers; the divided-power integrality normalization is specified in the form theorem, not assumed in this Definition.

items.title: Divided-power multiplication, toral binomials and the $E_i^{(a)}F_i^{(b)}$ reordering identity
items.statement:
Let $i\in I$, put $q=q_i$ and let $T_{i,c,t}$ be the toral binomials of [[def-lusztig-divided-power-integral-form]]. Write $E=E_i$, $F=F_i$, $E^{(a)}=E_i^{(a)}$, $F^{(b)}=F_i^{(b)}$.

(i) **Divided-power multiplication.** For all $a,b\ge0$, $E^{(a)}E^{(b)}=\binom{a+b}{a}_iE^{(a+b)}$ and $F^{(a)}F^{(b)}=\binom{a+b}{a}_iF^{(a+b)}$ ([[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]).

(ii) **Toral recursion and commutation.** $T_{i,c,t}=\frac{K_iq_i^{\,c-t+1}-K_i^{-1}q_i^{\,-c+t-1}}{q_i^{t}-q_i^{-t}}T_{i,c,t-1}$ for $t\ge1$; the $T_{i,c,t}$ are Laurent polynomials in $K_i^{\pm1}$ and commute with each other and with all $K_h$; and $E_iT_{i,c,t}$, $F_iT_{i,c,t}$, $T_{i,c,t}E_i$, $T_{i,c,t}F_i$ lie in $U_A^0E_i$, $U_A^0F_i$, $E_iU_A^0$, $F_iU_A^0$ respectively, i.e. the toral factor can always be moved to the middle at the cost of a scalar $q$-power and a shift of the binomial index.

(iii) **Reordering identity.** For all $a,b\ge0$ and $\min(a,b)\ge t\ge0$,
$$E_i^{(a)}F_i^{(b)}=\sum_{t=0}^{\min(a,b)}F_i^{(b-t)}\,T_{i,\,2t-a-b,\,t}\,E_i^{(a-t)},$$
with all coefficients equal to toral quantum binomials of $U_A^0$; in particular $E_iF_i-F_iE_i=T_{i,0,1}$ and $E_i^{(a)}F_i^{(a)}=\sum_{t=0}^{a}F_i^{(a-t)}T_{i,2t-2a,t}E_i^{(a-t)}$. For $i\ne j$ the divided powers $E_i^{(a)}$ and $F_j^{(b)}$ commute with one another, The same-half divided powers commute when a_ij=0; for a_ij≠0 they satisfy quantum Serre relations and are not asserted to commute.

(iv) **Triangular spanning.** Every element of $U_A$ is an $A$-linear combination of products $b_-\,u\,b_+$ with $b_-\in U_A^-$, $u\in U_A^0$ and $b_+\in U_A^+$; equivalently $U_A=U_A^-U_A^0U_A^+$ as an $A$-module (no independence is asserted here).

items.title: Integral skew-string coefficients on the divided-power negative half
items.statement: Let A=Z[q,q^-1] and U_A^- be the divided-power half. Each e_i' preserves U_A^-. Define the finite-on-each-vector operator P_i=Σ_{n≥0}(-1)^n q_i^{-n(n-1)/2}F_i^(n)(e_i')^n, with ordinary, not divided, powers of the derivation. It projects onto ker e_i' along F_iU_q^-. Every x∈U_A^- has a unique finite expansion x=Σ_n F_i^(n)x_n, e_i'x_n=0, and x_n=q_i^{n(n-1)/2}P_i(e_i')^n x belongs to U_A^-. Thus the corresponding string raising/lowering operators preserve U_A^-. No global A-basis or global freeness is assumed.

items.title: Finite-support regularization of quantum label-weight modules
items.statement: Let a P-graded module have support in a finite union of cones lambda_j-Q_+. Choose a finite-rank direct coordinate summand X_f of the free group P containing all lambda_j and alpha_i. Set Y_aux=(⊕_i Z H_i)⊕Hom(X_f,Z), X_aux=Hom(Y_aux,Z), j(x)(H_i)=<x,h_i> and j(x)(f)=f(x), and alpha_i_aux=j(alpha_i). This is a finite-rank perfect-pairing root datum with independent simple roots and primitive independent simple coroots H_i, the original Cartan matrix and original symmetrizer d_i. In particular its fundamental weights exist. The original finite-support P-graded module extends uniquely on its labels to an auxiliary type-one module with support j(X_f): K_(Σ n_iH_i,f) acts on degree x by q^{Σ n_i<x,h_i>+f(x)}. Its E_i,F_i and simple K_i=K_{d_iH_i} actions are unchanged. Conversely all original K_h actions are reconstructed from the original label x as q^{<x,h>}; this gives an equivalence between the specified support-graded categories. It is not an embedding of the old torus algebra and is not asserted outside this finite-support category. The construction applies simultaneously to Verma/highest modules and finite tensor products by choosing X_f to contain the participating upper weights and all roots. The auxiliary rational Cartan space decomposes H_min⊕Z, with H_min a finite minimal realization and Z central (all alpha_i vanish on it).

items.title: The bar involution and the contravariant anti-involution preserve $U_A$
items.statement:
Let $\psi$ (the bar involution) and $\tau$ (the contravariant anti-involution) be the semilinear maps of [[lem-quantum-serre-relations-are-stable-under-the-chevalley-involutions]], so that $\psi(q)=q^{-1}$, $\psi(E_i)=E_i$, $\psi(F_i)=F_i$, $\psi(K_h)=K_h^{-1}$ and $\tau(q)=q^{-1}$, $\tau(E_i)=F_i$, $\tau(F_i)=E_i$, $\tau(K_h)=K_h^{-1}$, with $\tau$ anti-multiplicative. Then $\psi(U_A)=U_A$ and $\tau(U_A)=U_A$. On the generators of [[def-lusztig-divided-power-integral-form]],
$$\psi(E_i^{(r)})=E_i^{(r)},\quad \psi(F_i^{(r)})=F_i^{(r)},\quad \psi(K_h)=K_h^{-1},\quad \psi(T_{i,c,t})=T_{i,c,t},$$
$$\tau(E_i^{(r)})=F_i^{(r)},\quad \tau(F_i^{(r)})=E_i^{(r)},\quad \tau(K_h)=K_h^{-1},\quad \tau(T_{i,c,t})=T_{i,c,t}.$$
In particular both maps restrict to bijections of $U_A$, $\psi$ restricts to a semilinear algebra involution of $U_A$ and $\tau$ to a semilinear anti-involution of $U_A$, and $q^{\pm1}\in A$ keeps all coefficients in $A$. These are the two involutions under which the bar lattice and the contravariant duality of the later crystal and form constructions are taken; the formula is not the Chevalley involution $\omega$ (which changes signs and exchanges the halves and is treated in [[lem-quantum-serre-relations-are-stable-under-the-chevalley-involutions]]).

items.title: Cartan projection constructs the Verma contravariant form and identifies its radical
items.statement: For any lambda∈P the canonically graded Verma module admits a unique homogeneous sigma-contravariant symmetric form normalized on its top vector. If pr:U_q→U_q^0 is the toral projection of triangular decomposition and chi_lambda(K_h)=q^{<lambda,h>}, the form is B(a v_lambda,b v_lambda)=chi_lambda(pr(sigma(a)b)) for a,b∈U_q^-. Its radical equals the sum of all proper graded Verma submodules, so it descends to a nondegenerate normalized form on the actual simple graded quotient L(lambda). For dominant lambda it kills each F_i^(lambda(h_i)+1)v_lambda and therefore factors through the integrable Serre quotient. On the rank-one string, B(F_i^(r)v_lambda,F_i^(r)v_lambda)=q_i^{r(m_i-r)} binom(m_i,r)_i for 0≤r≤m_i. For an integrable cyclic graded quotient with this nondegenerate form and support lambda-Q_+, the module is also simple as an ordinary module: a maximum-height component can be raised to the top while all lesser-height components vanish. For integral lambda and the highest lattice V_A=U_Av_lambda=U_A^-v_lambda in L(lambda), B(V_A,V_A)⊂A. This does not assert perfectness over A or A-valuedness of the different negative-half Kashiwara form.

items.title: The dominant quantum Serre quotient is nonzero and integrable
items.statement: For lambda∈P^+ put m_i=<lambda,h_i>. In M(lambda), each s_i=F_i^(m_i+1)v_lambda is a singular vector. The graded submodule generated by all s_i is proper; its quotient tilde L(lambda) is nonzero, finite dimensional in each label-weight space, and integrable. Every integrable cyclic highest module of weight lambda is a quotient of tilde L(lambda). No commutation of distinct adjacent-root negative generators is assumed.

items.title: Separation of the negative half by iterated skew derivations
items.statement:
Let $e_i'$ be the skew derivations of [[def-kashiwara-skew-derivations-on-the-negative-quantum-half]] on the negative half $U_q^-$ of a symmetrizable Cartan datum with $a_{ii}=2$ for all $i$.

(i) **One step.** If $x\in U_q^-[-
u]$ with $
u
eq0$ satisfies $e_i'(x)=0$ for all $i\in I$, then $x=0$.

(ii) **Iterated separation.** For every $0
eq x\in U_q^-[-
u]$ there is a sequence $i_1,\dots,i_k\in I$ with $
u=\alpha_{i_1}+\cdots+\alpha_{i_k}$ (the multiset is uniquely determined by $
u$, because the simple roots are linearly independent, and $k=\mathrm{ht}(
u)$) such that $e_{i_1}'\cdots e_{i_k}'(x)
eq0$; equivalently, the common kernel of all composites $e_{i_1}'\cdots e_{i_k}'$ on $U_q^-[-
u]$, over all such sequences, is zero.

The statement is the quantum analogue of the classical fact that a nonzero element of $U(\mathfrak n^-)$ has a nonzero image under some iterated adjoint action; it is the nondegeneracy joint used both in the crystal development and in the categorification pairing. (The same statement holds with $e_i''$ in place of $e_i'$.)

items.title: The unmodified integral torus has a quantum-binomial basis
items.statement: Let A=Z[q,q^-1], L=Σ_i Z(d_i h_i)⊂Pvee and choose explicit representatives c of Pvee/L. The unmodified toral integral form U_A^0 has the A-basis K_c∏_i K_i^{delta_i}T_{i,0,t_i}, delta_i∈{0,1}, t_i≥0. In one simple torus put z=q_i,K=K_i,T_t=T_{i,0,t}; then T_rT_s=Σ_{j=0}^{min(r,s)}z^{rs}K^{-j}binom(r+s-j,r)_z binom(r,j)_z T_{r+s-j}, and T_{c+1,t}=z^tT_{c,t}+K^-1z^{-c+t-1}T_{c,t-1}. These are integral product/shift formulas. No integral PBW/canonical basis, non-PID freeness inference, or modified dot-U result is used.

items.title: Local q=1 deformation proves integrable highest weight universality
items.statement: For lambda∈P^+, every nonzero graded quotient V of tilde L(lambda) generated by its surviving highest line has the same weight character as the classical simple integrable highest module of the regularized minimal realization. Consequently tilde L(lambda)=L(lambda). Its R=Q[q]_(q-1) lattice V_R=Σ_w R F_w v is stable under every generator of U_A, finite free on each label weight, and its q=1 fibre is the classical simple integrable highest module. This proves field/local character deformation and the universal simple integrable quotient without assuming global Z[q±]-freeness. The weight comparison transports back to the original label lattice by the regularization supplier.

items.title: Rational-local quantum halves and torus specialize at q=1
items.statement: Put R=Q[q]_(q-1)⊂Q(q). It is a DVR with uniformizer q-1. Base change U_A⊗_A R is its actual image U_R in U_q because R is a localization of A. Each U_R^±[±nu] is finite free over R, and its q=1 fibre is U(n^±)_Q[±nu]. The toral algebra U_R^0 has an R-basis K_c∏_i K_i^{delta_i}H_i^{t_i}, where H_i=T_{i,0,1}, delta_i=0 or1, t_i≥0 and c runs through explicit representatives of Pvee/Σ_i Z(d_i h_i). Multiplication U_R^-⊗_R U_R^0⊗_R U_R^+→U_R is an isomorphism. For any characteristic-zero field k, the positive toral quotient U_A^0⊗_A k/(K_h-1: h∈Pvee) is k[H_i:i∈I], and Tbar_{i,c,t}=binom(H_i+c,t). The positive full quotient U_A⊗_A k/(K_h-1) is U(g_der)_k, where g_der is the classical Serre Lie algebra with Cartan span of the independent simple coroots. This is not an assertion that K_h=1 in the unquotiented specialization. AC is used only for the supplied generic/classical rank comparison.

items.title: The negative-half bilinear form is symmetric, nondegenerate and integral
items.statement:
Let $(\ ,\ )$ be the Lusztig-Kashiwara form on the negative half $U_q^-$ of [[def-the-lusztig-kashiwara-bilinear-form-on-the-negative-quantum-half]], with skew derivations $e_i',e_i''$ ([[def-kashiwara-skew-derivations-on-the-negative-quantum-half]]).

(i) **Existence and symmetry.** A bilinear form with $(1,1)=1$ and $(F_iP,Q)=(P,e_i'(Q))$ exists on $U_q^-$, and every normalized homogeneous form satisfying these conditions is symmetric; by the uniqueness in [[def-the-lusztig-kashiwara-bilinear-form-on-the-negative-quantum-half]] there is exactly one such form. (No separate right-adjunction formula for $(P,QF_i)$ is asserted: the symmetry is the source's statement, and in the rank-one subalgebra a formula $(P,QF_i)=c\,(e_i''P,Q)$ with constant $c$ is false, as the explicit values in (iv) show.)

(ii) **Orthogonality.** $(U_q^-[\nu],U_q^-[\mu])=0$ whenever $\nu\neq\mu$.

(iii) **Nondegeneracy.** For every $0\neq x\in U_q^-$ there is $y\in U_q^-$ with $(x,y)\neq0$; equivalently, the restriction of the form to each finite-dimensional graded piece $U_q^-[\nu]$ is nondegenerate.

(iv) **Integrality on the word lattice.** Let $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$ and let $W\subseteq U_A^-$ be the $A$-span of the monomials $F_{i_1}\cdots F_{i_k}$ ($k\ge0$). Then $W\subseteq U_A^-$ (because $F_i^k=[k]_i!F_i^{(k)}$ and $[k]_i!\in A$), and $(W,W)\subseteq A$. On the larger divided-power lattice $U_A^-$ the form is *not* $A$-valued: in the rank-one subalgebra generated by a single $F_i$ one has, for all $a,b\ge0$,
$$(F_i^{(a)},F_i^{(b)})=\delta_{ab}\,\frac{q_i^{-a(a-1)/2}}{[a]_i!}=\delta_{ab}\,\frac{1}{[a]_{q_i^2}!},$$
in particular $(F_i^{(2)},F_i^{(2)})=1/(1+q_i^2)\notin A$; here $[a]_{q_i^2}!=\prod_{m=1}^a(1+q_i^2+\cdots+q_i^{2(m-1)})$. Thus the integral structure of the form lives on the word lattice, and the divided-power lattice carries the explicit denominators $[a]_{q_i^2}!$. The form is nondegenerate on $W\otimes_A\mathbb Q(q)=U_q^-$ but is not $A$-valued on $U_A^-$ in this normalization. Globally, let A_loc=A[[r]_i!^{-1}:i∈I,r≥1], equivalently invert the Gaussian factorials [r]_{q_i^2}!, since their ratio is a Laurent unit. Then B(U_A^-,U_A^-)⊂A_loc: divided-power words are word vectors divided by finite products of these factorials. This is an exact denominator bound, not a false A-integrality assertion.

items.title: The q=1 toral specialization identifies the classical Cartan generators
items.statement: For any characteristic-zero field k and q↦1, the positive toral quotient U_A^0⊗_A k/(K_h-1) is the polynomial algebra k[H_i], H_i=Tbar_{i,0,1}, with Tbar_{i,c,t}=binom(H_i+c,t). No residual K_h ambiguity remains AFTER this stated quotient; K_h need not equal1 in the unquotiented specialization. On any U_A-stable label-graded weight lattice M_A=⊕_mu(M_A∩M_mu), K_h specializes to the identity and T_{i,c,t} acts by binom(<mu,h_i>+c,t), even over Z for these scalar operators. The E/F/H_i operators satisfy the classical Cartan commutators. The lattice must actually have this grading; it is not inferred merely because it spans a weight module.

items.title: The integrable quantum highest weight module exists and is unique
items.statement: For every dominant label weight lambda, the nonzero quantum Verma quotient by Σ_iU_qF_i^(<lambda,h_i>+1)v_lambda is integrable and equals the canonical simple highest module L(lambda). It is universal among integrable cyclic highest modules of that weight: each such module receives the unique map sending the highest vector to its specified highest vector, and every nonzero such cyclic module is isomorphic to L(lambda). The module has finite-dimensional label weights and lambda-Q_+ support and is also simple as an ordinary quantum module. Its character equals the classical integrable highest character of the explicitly regularized realization. No global Z-integral freeness or crystal/global-basis existence is used in this proof.

items.title: Integrable bounded-above quantum modules are direct sums of simple highest weight modules
items.statement:
Assume AC. Let $M$ be a $U_q(\mathfrak g)$-module such that (a) $M$ is a weight module with $\dim_{\mathbb Q(q)}M_\mu<\infty$ for every $\mu\in P$ ([[def-quantum-weight-module-and-integrability]]); (b) the weight set $\mathrm{wt}(M)$ is bounded above: it is contained in a finite union $\bigcup_{j=1}^s(\lambda_j-Q_+)$; and (c) $M$ is integrable, i.e. $E_i$ and $F_i$ act locally nilpotently for every $i$.

Then $M$ is isomorphic to an algebraic direct sum of simple integrable highest weight modules $L(\lambda)$, $\lambda\in P^+$; concretely, every nonzero submodule of $M$ contains a maximal vector $v$ whose cyclic submodule $U_q(\mathfrak g)v$ is isomorphic to $L(\lambda)$ for some $\lambda\in P^+$, and $M$ is the direct sum of the submodules generated by the vectors of any maximal independent family of simple submodules. AC is used exactly to select bases of the set-indexed family of finite-dimensional maximal-vector spaces simultaneously; restricted to any module generated by one finite-dimensional U^{≥0}-submodule, the decomposition is obtained by a finite induction and is choice-free. The finite-cone modules use explicit label grading and the regularization supplier when the original pairing is not separating.

items.title: Specialization at q=1 recovers the classical enveloping relations
items.statement: For any characteristic-zero field k and q↦1, U_A^±⊗_A k is isomorphic to U(n^±)_k by F_i↦f_i and E_i↦e_i. The positive full quotient (U_A⊗_A k)/(K_h-1:h∈Pvee) is isomorphic to U(g_der)_k, where g_der has the same classical Serre generators and independent simple-coroot Cartan span. In this quotient H_i=Tbar_{i,0,1} is the classical coroot generator and Tbar_{i,c,t}=binom(H_i+c,t); the positive toral quotient is k[H_i] with the exact kernel specified by the toral lemma. On label-graded U_A-stable lattices this quotient action is automatic, and all Cartan/Serre operator relations hold. The unquotiented specialization can retain K_h ambiguities (already K=-1 in sl2), so it is not identified with the positive quotient. Extra Cartan directions of a regular realization act diagonally on label-graded modules; they are not fabricated as generators of this particular toral integral form. These algebra comparisons use the proved rational-local theorem and generic/classical rank supplier, with its declared AC use. Direct q=1 substitution in vanishing rational denominators is never used.
