items.title: The Lusztig–Kashiwara form, parameter and coproduct dictionary
items.statement:
Set Lusztig's parameter v=q^-1, so v_i=q_i^-1. The presentation map E_i^L↦E_i,F_i^L↦F_i,K_h^L↦K_(-h) is an algebra isomorphism after parameter transport, preserves the divided-power A-forms and intertwines bar. It carries the Lusztig coproduct to the OPPOSITE of the fixed library coproduct ΔE_i=E_i⊗K_i^-1+1⊗E_i, ΔF_i=F_i⊗1+K_i⊗F_i. Therefore swapping tensor factors carries the Lusztig quasi-R convention to a bar-coproduct intertwiner in U^+⊗U^- for this Δ.
On the abstract half f, θ_i maps to F_i and θ_i^(n) to F_i^(n), and the twisted coproduct multiplication becomes (x1⊗x2)(y1⊗y2)=q^(−(deg x2,deg y1))x1y1⊗x2y2. Lusztig's form B_L on degree nu=Σ_i nu_i alpha_i is B_L=C_nu B_K, C_nu=∏_i(1−q_i²)^−nu_i, where B_K is the normalized Kashiwara half form. This is a color-degree scaling, a unit≡1 atq=0, not a single scalar or equality of forms on all degrees. In rank one B_L(F_i^(n),F_i^(n))=∏_(r=1)^n(1−q_i^(2r))^-1. The corresponding normalized Drinfeld pairing D on U^+_nu×U^-_(−nu) is D(x,y)=d_nu^-1 B_K(ιx,y), d_nu=∏_i(q_i−q_i^-1)^nu_i and ι(E_i)=F_i. Thus D(E_i,F_j)=delta_ij/(q_i−q_i^-1). Its coevaluation is exactly the transported/flipped Lusztig quasi-R component; the n1 coefficient is q_i−q_i^-1.

items.title: The bar lattice and the divided-power integral lattice of a based module
items.statement:
Fix $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]\subseteq\mathbb Q(q)$ and the crystal limiting ring $A_0\subseteq\mathbb Q(q)$ of [[def-the-local-ring-at-q-zero]], and put $A_\infty:=\psi(A_0)$, the image of $A_0$ under the semilinear involution $\psi(q)=q^{-1}$, i.e. the ring of rational functions regular at $q=\infty$; $A_0$ and $A_\infty$ are the rational local rings at0 and infinity; the integral affine chart coordinate rings are Z[q] and Z[q^-1].

Let $M$ be one of $U_q^-$ or $V(\lambda)=L(\lambda)$ ($\lambda\in P^+$). Equip $M$ with the bar involution $\psi$ of [[lem-the-lusztig-integral-form-is-stable-under-bar-and-contravariant-duality]]: on $U_q^-$ the semilinear algebra involution $\psi(q)=q^{-1}$, $\psi(E_i)=E_i$, $\psi(F_i)=F_i$, $\psi(K_h)=K_h^{-1}$; on $V(\lambda)$ the induced semilinear involution determined by $Pv_\lambda\mapsto\psi(P)v_\lambda$ (well defined because the highest vector is fixed). Let $M_A\subseteq M$ be the divided-power integral form: $M_A=U_A^-$ for $M=U_q^-$, and $M_A=V_A(\lambda):=U_A^-v_\lambda$ for $M=V(\lambda)$ ([[def-lusztig-divided-power-integral-form]]; $U_A^-$ and $V_A(\lambda)$ are $\psi$-stable). Let $L$ be the Kashiwara crystal lattice of $M$ over $A_0$: $L=L(\infty)$ for $U_q^-$ and $L=L(\lambda)$ for $V(\lambda)$ ([[def-kashiwara-lattices-lambda-and-infinity]], [[thm-grand-loop-existence-of-highest-weight-crystal-bases]]).

Define the **bar lattice** $L^-:=\psi(L)$, an $A_\infty$-submodule of $M$, and the **balanced part** $E:=M_A\cap L\cap L^-$. The definition keeps three structures on the same $\mathbb Q(q)$-vector space strictly separate: the $A$-module $M_A$, which is not assumed free and not claimed to be contained in $L$; the free $A_0$-module $L$; and the free $A_\infty$-module $L^-$. No equality $L^-=L$, no inclusion $M_A\subseteq L$, no freeness of $M_A$ and no identification $E=M_A$ are asserted; freeness is a conclusion of the balanced-triple construction, whereas E is a Z-module of global lifts and is not equal to the Laurent lattice M_A. The bar lattice is not the form-dual (upper) lattice, which is defined later on this page. Intersections M_A∩L and M_A∩L^- are respectively Z[q]- and Z[q^-1]-modules, generally not A-modules. The balanced part E is a Z-module; its Laurent extension A⊗_Z E is the full integral module once globalization is proved. More generally a based integrable module (M,B) here means exactly: B is a homogeneous field basis; M_A=⊕_b A b is U_A-stable; the semilinear involution fixing B is U/bar compatible; and L0=⊕_b A0 b with residue B is a crystal local basis at0. These are Lusztig27.1.2(a)–(d) after v=q^-1 and the integrable Bao–Wang extension. Such data do not automatically imply integral Θ action on an arbitrary based pair. A based subobject is a U-submodule spanned by a subset of B; a based quotient is its quotient with the complementary basis images. Based morphisms send B to the target basis or0 and have kernels spanned by the killed basis subset. These exact integral/bar-compatible maps, not arbitrary field summands, are used in tensor inheritance.

items.title: Balanced triples over the two charts of $\mathbb P^1$ and the globalization map
items.statement:
Let V be finite dimensional over Q(q), M⊂V an A=Z[q,q^-1]-submodule spanning V, and L0,L∞ free full rational chart lattices over A0,A∞. Put L_Z=M∩L0, L_Z^-=M∩L∞, E_Z=M∩L0∩L∞. The integral triple is balanced if the canonical Z-linear map E_Z→L_Z/qL_Z=(M∩L0)/(M∩qL0) is an isomorphism. Its inverse is the integral globalization map on the integral residue subgroup. Rational balancedness is the corresponding isomorphism Q⊗_Z E_Z→L0/qL0, after extending the integral subgroup by Q. In applications the integral subgroup is ZB, and its globalization gives the lower lifts G(b).
The two-chart lemma proves M≅A⊗_Z E_Z, L_Z≅Z[q]⊗_Z E_Z and L_Z^-≅Z[q^-1]⊗_Z E_Z. If E_Z has a finite Z-basis B_E whose rational residue classes are a basis of L0/qL0, these lifts give bases of M,L0,L∞ over A,A0,A∞. Thus actual A-freeness follows from integral balancedness PLUS the proved free integral residue basis; it is not automatic for an arbitrary non-finitely-generated Z-submodule. All definitions apply componentwise to the finite root/label spaces.

items.title: The integral residue lattices $L_A(\infty)$ and $L_A(\lambda)$
items.statement:
Let A=Z[q,q^-1], with rational DVRs A0 atq=0 and A∞ atq=∞. Put M_A=U_A^- or V_A(lambda)=U_A^-v_lambda, L=L∞ or Llambda, and L^-=bar L. The integral residue lattice is L_Z=M_A∩L, a Z[q]-module, and its bar lattice is L_Z^-=M_A∩L^-, a Z[q^-1]-module. Its balanced intersection E_Z=M_A∩L∩L^- is a Z-module. Since q^-1M_A=M_A, M_A∩qL=qL_Z; consequently the residue map L_Z/qL_Z→L/qL is injective and is Z-linear. Its image is an integral subgroup of the rational crystal space, not the entire Q-space. No Laurent-A-linearity is asserted on the residue lattice or map.
The field projection pi_lambda restricts to an A-linear surjection U_A^-→V_A(lambda) and sends L_Z(infinity) into L_Z(lambda), by the already proved grand-loop lattice projection. The module V_A is U_A-stable: reordering reduces actions on v_lambda to negative divided powers and toral Gaussian scalars in A, with all positive generators killing the top except the unit. No global freeness, residue spanning or balancedness is assumed here. The integral residue subgroup for the negative half is proved below to be ZB∞; the module subgroup ZBλ is a consequence of globalization.

items.title: The root-height completion for weightwise quasi-$R$ intertwiners
items.statement:
For the fixed library coproduct use the diagonal root-height completion C_hat=∏_(nu∈Q+)U^+[nu]⊗U^-[-nu], with multiplication (AB)_nu=Σ_(beta+gamma=nu)A_beta B_gamma. Each component sum is finite because I is finite and root coefficients are nonnegative integers. For intertwining with ΔU, use the ambient completed tensor square obtained from Lusztig4.1.1 by the actual v=q^-1, K_h↦K_-h presentation map and tensor flip; equivalently all generator identities are read coefficientwise in the root grading. The tensor orientation is POSITIVE first, NEGATIVE second.
A family acts on m_mu⊗n_eta by its finite sum whenever U^+_nu m_mu⊗U^-_-nu n_eta vanishes for all sufficiently high nu. This holds if the first factor has finite-union bounded-above support, or if the second factor is a lowest module with bounded-below support. For both factors in finite-weight-space O_int the relevant fixed total-weight subspace is finite dimensional, and every tail beyond a finite degree acts0 there. An infinite series is not evaluated on a two-sided-unbounded pair without this explicit finiteness condition. This completion and Θ_0=1 are field-level data; no universal-R, braiding or integral coefficient property is asserted here.

items.title: The Drinfeld pairing between the positive and negative quantum halves
items.statement: Let B_K be the normalized Kashiwara half form and let ι:U^+→U^- send E_i↦F_i (equivalently use the library's signed Chevalley involution with the compensating degree sign). For x of positive degree nu and y of negative degree−nu define D(x,y)=d_nu^-1 B_K(ιx,y), d_nu=∏_i(q_i−q_i^-1)^nu_i, and set different-degree pairings0. Then D(E_i,F_j)=delta_ij/(q_i−q_i^-1), and D(E_i^(n),F_i^(n))=q_i^(−n(n−1)/2)/([n]_i!(q_i−q_i^-1)^n). The pairing with generator value1 is B_K transport, not this quasi-R/Drinfeld normalization. The completed normalized tensor uses the D-dual basis. On the simple-root Borel extensions its toral normalization is D(K_nu,K_mu)=q^((nu,mu)), with mixed toral/root generator pairings0 and counit normalization; the Hopf adjunction identities use Δ on the negative Borel and Δ^op on the positive Borel. No unchosen pairing on arbitrary extra toral directions of Pvee is asserted.

items.title: The balanced-triple linear algebra over $\mathbb P^1$
items.statement:
For finite-dimensional V over Q(q), let M⊂V be an A=Z[q,q^-1]-submodule spanning V and L0,L∞ full free A0,A∞ lattices. Write E=M∩L0∩L∞. (1) If E→(M∩L0)/(M∩qL0) is a Z-isomorphism, then M∩L0≅Z[q]⊗_Z E, M∩L∞≅Z[q^-1]⊗_Z E and M≅A⊗_Z E; the infinity residue map is also an isomorphism. Rational chart extension gives A0⊗_Z E≅L0 and A∞⊗_Z E≅L∞. If E has a finite Z-basis, these are actual free bases. No containment M⊂L0∩L∞ or freeness of M/E is assumed.
(2) If a Z-module F maps into M∩L0∩L∞, generates M over A, and maps injectively into both rational residues L0/qL0 and L∞/q^-1L∞, then F≅E≅(M∩L0)/(M∩qL0).
(3) More generally let N⊂M be an A-submodule with integral balanced intersection E_N=N∩L0∩L∞. If a Z-module F maps to M∩(L0+N)∩(L∞+N), generates M modulo N over A, and maps injectively into (L0+Q N)/(qL0+Q N) and (L∞+Q N)/(q^-1L∞+Q N), then M is balanced. The sequence 0→(N∩L0)/(N∩qL0)→(M∩L0)/(M∩qL0)→(L0+Q N)/(qL0+Q N) is exact, and the last image is the image of F. If F and E_N are finite free Z-modules, so is E_M, and M is free over A. These are Kashiwara91 Lemmas7.1.1–7.1.2, in integral notation; their rational base extension gives the usual Q[q±] criterion.

items.title: Integral residues of the negative half: freeness, the crystal basis and the form characterization
items.statement: For L_Z(infinity)=U_A^-∩L(infinity), its canonical injection L_Z/qL_Z→L/qL has image exactly ⊕_(b∈B∞)Z b. It is a free Z-module with basis B∞ and becomes the full rational crystal space after tensoring with Q. The normalized Kashiwara half form takes values on U_A^- in K_Z=Z[q,q^-1,(1−q^(2n))^-1:n≥1], and on L_Z in A_Z=Z[q,(1−q^(2n))^-1:n≥1]. Thus its residue pairing is Z-valued. Its coefficients in B∞ are the integer pairings with b, and its norm1 elements are B∞∪(−B∞). The operators ẽ_i,f̃_i preserve L_Z and its integral residue subgroup. No A-module structure on L_Z, no equality with the rational residue as a Z-module, and no unsigned norm1 characterization is asserted. The module integral residue basis is established in globalization.

items.title: Reversal preserves the negative-half integral and crystal lattices
items.statement: The Q(q)-linear anti-involution star fixing each F_i reverses negative words, preserves U_A^-, commutes with bar, preserves the normalized half form, and preserves L∞ and L_Z∞ as well as their bar lattices. On the integral crystal residue it permutes B∞∪(−B∞). Only this signed lattice preservation, not an unproved unsigned star-crystal theorem, is required for gluing the string-ideal global lifts.

items.title: Integrality of the string decomposition and the divided-power string ideals
items.statement:
For the negative-half decomposition u=Σ_l F_i^(l)u_l, ker e_i'∋u_l, all u_l are in U_A^- if u∈U_A^-. The integral projector is P_i=Σ_l(−1)^l q_i^(−l(l−1)/2) F_i^(l)(e_i')^l and u_l=q_i^(l(l−1)/2)P_i(e_i')^l u. All derivation powers here are ORDINARY, not divided by [l]_i!.
Define I_(i,n)^A=U_A^-∩F_i^n U_q^-=⊕_(l≥n)F_i^(l)(ker e_i'∩U_A^-)=Σ_(l≥n)F_i^(l)U_A^- and J_(i,n)^A=pi_lambda(I_(i,n)^A)=Σ_(l≥n)F_i^(l)V_A(lambda). The latter is an A-submodule inside the field string-image subspace F_i^n V(lambda), not a U_q-submodule or U_A-stable lattice in general. Its equality with V_A∩F_i^n V is proved after the adapted global basis construction, not presumed before it.
The integral residue of I_(i,n)^A∩L∞ is the free Z-span of B∞∩f̃_i^n B∞, and the corresponding rational residue of F_i^nU^-∩L∞ is its Q-span. Integral balancedness of the zero/infinity triple is proved by the subsequent string-ideal induction. On every U_A-stable integrable module lattice M_A, if a label mu has <h_i,mu>=−n≤−1, then each u∈(M_A)_mu satisfies the finite identity u=Σ_(k≥n)(−1)^(k−n)[k−1 choose k−n]_i F_i^(k)E_i^(k)u. Thus (M_A)_mu=Σ_(k≥n)F_i^(k)(M_A)_(mu+k alpha_i). This is the exact boundary-generation supplier used in the string-ideal induction.

items.title: The Drinfeld pairing is nondegenerate in each root degree and matches the shuffle pairing
items.statement: The normalized D pairing is homogeneous, descends to the actual Serre halves and is nondegenerate/perfect over Q(q) in every finite root degree. Its rank-one values are those of the preceding Definition, with the factor(q_i−q_i^-1)^−n. It equals the formal generic Hopf pairing on the simple-root Borels with that exact generator and toral normalization. Thus D(xx′,y)=ΣD(x,y_(1))D(x′,y_(2)) and D(x,yy′)=ΣD(x_(1),y)D(x_(2),y′), with Δy on the negative Borel and Δ^opx on the positive Borel, including their toral factors. These are field identities; divided-power integral perfectness or A-valuedness is not asserted.

items.title: Homogeneous dual-basis sums: basis independence and weightwise finiteness
items.statement: For a field basis u_a of U^+_nu and its D-dual basis v_a of U^-_-nu, the tensor Θ_nu=Σ_a u_a⊗v_a is independent of the chosen basis and Θ_0=1. It has finite-dimensional components and defines a vectorwise finite action under the exact root-height finiteness hypotheses of the completion Definition. Its degree-nu action shifts the label pair (mu,eta) to(mu+nu,eta−nu), preserving total weight. On finite-weight O_int pairs each fixed total-weight space has a uniform finite tail bound. No integral algebra coefficients are asserted; the positive-height components have no same-weight-pair diagonal term.

items.title: The string-ideal triples are balanced: the induction step (Kashiwara 7.4.1 / JKK 10.4)
items.statement: Fix a root degree alpha of height r. Assume integral balanced/global lifts in every degree of height<r for both the negative half and all dominant highest modules, including based-quotient compatibility there and the negative-half string-ideal membership of each lower lift G∞(b) whenever b∈f̃_i^nB∞. Then for every i,n≥1 the image string-ideal J_(i,n)^A in each highest module, with its rational zero/infinity chart intersections, is integrally balanced in degree lambda−alpha. Its balanced Z-intersection maps isomorphically to the Z-span of Bλ∩f̃_i^n Bλ in that degree. Similarly the half ideal I_(i,n)^A is integrally balanced in degree−alpha, with residue Z-span B∞∩f̃_i^n B∞. Their Laurent extensions are free A-modules with these adapted global lifts. Freeness, chart intersection and the eventual module saturation J_(i,n)^A=V_A∩F_i^n V are conclusions, not hypotheses.

items.title: The highest weight and negative half integral crystal triples are balanced
items.statement:
For every symmetrizable datum in the explicitly chosen label-weight category, the triples (U_A^-,L∞,bar L∞) and (V_A(lambda),Llambda,bar Llambda) are integrally balanced componentwise. Their balanced Z-intersections map isomorphically to ZB∞ and ZBλ, respectively; after rational extension these maps identify with the full Q crystal spaces. The inverse lifts G∞(b),Gλ(b) are bar invariant. They form actual A=Z[q,q^-1] bases of the divided-power modules U_A^- and V_A(lambda), with finite free root/label components of ranks equal to their field dimensions (the half ranks are the classical PBW ranks).
For every i,n≥1, I_(i,n)^A=⊕_(b∈B∞∩f̃_i^nB∞)A G∞(b), and J_(i,n)^A=⊕_(b∈Bλ∩f̃_i^nBλ)A Gλ(b). In particular the module image ideal equals V_A∩F_i^n V; this saturation follows from the adapted global basis and is not an initial hypothesis. Under pi_lambda, G∞(b) maps to0 exactly when its crystal image is0 and otherwise to Gλ(pi(b)). All assertions are integral, general symmetrizable and proved without an integral-freeness premise. If ẽ_i b=0 and n≥1, then G∞(f̃_i^n b)−F_i^(n)G∞(b) lies in I_(i,n+1)^A. This is the exact normalized top-string transition modulo the higher string ideal, not merely a modulo-q congruence.

items.title: Existence and uniqueness of the weightwise quasi-$R$ intertwiner
items.statement:
The D-coevaluation family Θ=Σ_nu Θ_nu∈∏U^+_nu⊗U^-_-nu is the unique normalized bar-coproduct intertwiner for the fixed Δ: Δ(u)Θ=Θ barΔ(u) for all u, where barΔ(u)=(psi⊗psi)Δ(psi(u)). It has Θ_0=1. Its generator recursions are
[1⊗E_i,Θ_nu]=Θ_(nu−alpha_i)(E_i⊗K_i)−(E_i⊗K_i^-1)Θ_(nu−alpha_i),
[F_i⊗1,Θ_nu]=Θ_(nu−alpha_i)(K_i^-1⊗F_i)−(K_i⊗F_i)Θ_(nu−alpha_i),
with negative-degree components0 and toral weight-zero commutation. In rank one Θ_n= (q_i−q_i^-1)^n[n]_(q_i²)! E_i^(n)⊗F_i^(n), so Θ_alpha_i=(q_i−q_i^-1)E_i⊗F_i. The family evaluates precisely under the completion's explicit finite-support hypotheses. This is not the native unscaled doubled-torus ΨΔ^op relation and no integral algebra coefficient claim is made.

items.title: The lower global basis of $U_q^-$ and of a highest weight module
items.statement: For M=U^- or V(lambda), the integral balanced theorem identifies E_Z=M_A∩L∩bar L with the free Z residue subgroup ZB. Define the lower global lift G(b) to be the unique element of E_Z with residue b. The family G(B) is the lower global basis; its A-span is M_A, its A0-span is L and its A∞-span is bar L, whereas its Z-span is E_Z. Each G(b) is bar fixed. No equality of E_Z with the Laurent module is implied. Definitions apply in every finite root/label component and hence their direct sum.

items.title: The quasi-$R$ intertwiner determines its inverse and the coproduct factorizations
items.statement:
In the same positive-first/negative-second completion, Θ^-1=barΘ=(psi⊗psi)(Θ). For every nu the exact threefold identities are
(Δ⊗id)Θ_nu=Σ_(gamma+eta=nu)(Θ_gamma)_23(1⊗K_-eta⊗1)(Θ_eta)_13,
(id⊗Δ)Θ_nu=Σ_(gamma+eta=nu)(Θ_gamma)_12(1⊗K_eta⊗1)(Θ_eta)_13.
The two normalized tensor-bar compositions satisfy the field cocycle identity ((Δ⊗id)Θ)Θ_12=((id⊗Δ)Θ)Θ_23, coefficientwise in the transported source completion and on every vector for which the iterated actions are finite. The inverse does not switch positive/negative tensor order. Removing Θ_0=1 permits scalar multiples of the same linear intertwiner equation, so normalization is essential. No integrality or uncontrolled infinite evaluation is asserted. The bar-coproduct counterpart needed for the cocycle is (id⊗barΔ)Θ_nu=Σ_(gamma+eta=nu)(Θ_gamma)_13(1⊗K_-gamma⊗1)(Θ_eta)_12.

items.title: Bar invariance, congruence and uniqueness of the lower global basis
items.statement: For U^- and every dominant V(lambda), there exists a unique lower global family G(b)⊂M_A∩L∩bar L with residue b. It is bar invariant, a genuine A=Z[q,q^-1] basis of M_A and a basis of both rational chart lattices over A0,A∞. Its Z-span is the simultaneous balanced intersection; its field span is the whole module. It is adapted to every divided string-image ideal, in the exact sense of the integral balanced theorem. No word family is assumed to be a basis and no lower lattice self-duality is asserted.

items.title: The upper (form-dual) global basis and the required perfectness of the integral pairing
items.statement:
Let M=⊕_mu M_mu be U^- or V(lambda), with finite root/label components, lower global A-lattice M_A=⊕_b A G(b), rational lower charts L0 and L∞=bar L0, and the normalized homogeneous Kashiwara half or highest-module polarization B. Define its RESTRICTED graded integral form-dual by M_A^vee=⊕_mu{x∈M_mu:B(x,(M_A)_mu)⊂A}. Define dual rational charts L0^vee={x:B(x,L0)⊂A0} and L∞^vee={x:B(x,L∞)⊂A∞}, also as restricted direct sums. The upper global family is the unique homogeneous field family G^up(b) with B(G(b′),G^up(b))=delta_(b,b′). Its existence and actual dual-lattice bases/perfection are proved by the next theorem.
The upper bar is the B-adjoint semilinear involution psi^vee determined by B(psi u,psi^vee v)=overline{B(u,v)}. Upper Kashiwara operators are ẽ_i^up=(f̃_i^low)^adj and f̃_i^up=(ẽ_i^low)^adj, defined componentwise by the nondegenerate finite-dimensional form. They are distinct from the lower operators in general. The upper zero chart is the dual chart L0^vee; post-grand-loop perfection identifies it with L0, but the upper infinity chart L∞^vee is not automatically the lower bar chart L∞. The exact assertions of the following theorem are weightwise perfect A-duality, dual globalization in these genuine dual charts, and crystal compatibility for the respective adjoint operators. No full product Hom_A(M_A,A) identification, lower A-self-duality, ordinary-bar fixedness or unqualified upper/lower operator equality is asserted.

items.title: The based quotient: projection of the lower global basis to a highest weight module
items.statement: The projection pi_lambda:U_A^-→V_A(lambda) is a based quotient over Z[q,q^-1]: G∞(b) maps to0 if its crystal image is0 and to Gλ(pi(b)) otherwise. Thus its kernel is the A-span of exactly the killed global basis elements, and the surviving global basis elements map bijectively onto the integral highest-module basis. The module weight components are finite free over A, and the compatible zero/infinity chart and residue projections have the already proved crystal compatibility. This holds for every symmetrizable datum with the explicit label/auxiliary-realization convention. More precisely its integral kernel is Σ_iΣ_(s>lambda(h_i)) U_A^-F_i^(s). Thus the integral highest-module presentation uses ALL divided right powers beyond each highest limit, not just an ordinary power with a nonunit factorial.

items.title: Integral triangular decomposition and freeness of the Lusztig form
items.statement: Assume AC only for the generic/classical PBW rank supplier. Over A=Z[q,q^-1], multiplication U_A^-⊗_A U_A^0⊗_A U_A^+→U_A is an isomorphism. The two divided-power halves are free A-modules with finite free root components of the classical PBW ranks. The unmodified torus has an A-basis K_c∏K_i^{delta_i}T_{i,0,t_i}, with delta_i=0 or1 and c representing Pvee/Σ Z(d_i h_i). Hence U_A is free, and the degree-beta component is ⊕_{alpha,gamma∈Q_+, alpha-gamma=beta} U_A^-[-gamma]⊗U_A^0⊗U_A^+[alpha]. Unique coefficients refer to products of chosen basis elements, not to arbitrary sums of simple tensors.

items.title: Specialization of the global bases and the root-of-unity boundary
items.statement:
For every dominant lambda, the integral highest lattice V_A(lambda) has its genuine lower global A-basis. Hence for ANY unital base change A→S, including nonflat q=ζ specializations with ζ invertible, its tensor fibre has the corresponding S-basis and identical finite weight ranks. At characteristic-zero q=1 the positive toral quotient and local comparison identify it with the classical simple integrable highest module and its Weyl–Kac character.
The zero/infinity CHART lattices are obtained separately from Z[q]- and Z[q^-1]-spans of the global vectors, then rational DVR extension; there is no map A→A0 sending the unit q to0. At roots of unity the free integral fibre basis still survives, but this does not assert simplicity or semisimplicity, or equality with a naive ordinary-generator specialization. If the order of ζ_i² is greater than1, its Gaussian factorial vanishes once the index reaches that order; at ζ_i²=1 in characteristic0 it has value r! and that particular vanishing argument does not apply. Thus the algebra/module root-of-unity boundary is distinguished from the unconditional free-basis base-change fact.

items.title: Lusztig's canonical basis and Kashiwara's lower global basis agree in symmetric type
items.statement: In symmetric finite ADE type (all d_i=1), transport Lusztig's parameter by v=q^-1, the abstract half generators θ_i^(n)↦F_i^(n), and full torus K_h^L↦K_(-h). Divided-power integral forms and bar agree under this transport; the half forms agree by B_L=C_nu B_K, not by an unqualified identity. Under this exact dictionary Lusztig's canonical LOWER basis equals the Kashiwara lower global basis of U^-, and its canonical highest-module quotient bases equal the corresponding lower global bases for every dominant label lambda (using the explicit regular realization). The signed canonical set equals ±G∞; the positive canonical choice is matched by its actual Ti,n top-string recursion. No equality of upper and lower bases, or unproved 'unitriangular word-basis' characterization, is asserted.

items.title: Finitely generated free integral weight lattices and deformation of the classical weight character
items.statement: For every dominant label weight lambda, let V_A=U_Av_lambda=U_A^-v_lambda inside the simple integrable L(lambda). Over A=Z[q,q^-1], each label-weight component of V_A is finite FREE of rank dim_Q(q)L(lambda)_mu, not merely torsionfree. It spans the field module. For every characteristic-zero q=1 specialization k, the fibre has the same weight dimensions and is the classical simple integrable highest module of the explicitly regularized realization, transported to the original label lattice. Thus its character is the Weyl-Kac character (the finite Weyl character in finite type). The integral Serre quotient equals L(lambda) in every symmetrizable type, as already proved by the early local comparison.

items.title: Upper and lower global bases are dual and crystal compatible
items.statement:
For every finite root/label component of M=U^- or V(lambda), the restricted integral dual M_A^vee has the actual A-basis {G^up(b)} dual to {G(b)}, and B:(M_A^vee)_mu×(M_A)_mu→A is perfect. Globally these bases form direct sums; this means restricted graded perfectness, not identification with the full product Hom_A(M_A,A).
The dual charts are L0^vee=⊕A0G^up(b) and L∞^vee=⊕A∞G^up(b), and their balanced Z-intersection is ⊕ZG^up(b). Thus the dual triple is integrally balanced. At0, L0^vee=L0 and G^up(b) has residue b; at infinity its residue is the dual of the lower infinity-chart class in the dual infinity chart. The upper bar psi^vee fixes each G^up(b). The upper operators satisfy EXACT mixed adjunction B(f̃^low u,v)=B(u,ẽ^up v), B(ẽ^low u,v)=B(u,f̃^up v). Their reductions at0 equal the lower crystal operators and give the same crystal set B.
For a divided module string F_i^(n)v of top rank-one weight a, put d_(a,n)=q_i^(n(a−n))[a choose n]_i. Then ẽ_i^up at position n≥1 multiplies the preceding divided position by d_(a,n)/d_(a,n−1)=q_i^(a−2n+1)[a−n+1]_i/[n]_i, and f̃_i^up at position n<a multiplies the next by its reciprocal d_(a,n)/d_(a,n+1). For a half string with e_i′v=0, put d_n=q_i^(−n(n−1)/2)/[n]_i!=1/[n]_(q_i²)!; the corresponding ratios are d_n/d_(n−1)=1/[n]_(q_i²) and d_n/d_(n+1)=[n+1]_(q_i²). All admissible ratios are units≡1 in A0. Consequently unweighted lower adjunction holds modulo q, but generally not exactly over Q(q). No equality of upper and lower integral bases, even in symmetric type, is implied.

items.title: Divided-power integrality of the quasi-$R$ action on based lattices
items.statement:
For the actual Θ∈U^+⊗U^- and the exact four-axiom based modules, integral ACTION is proved in these cases: (a) V(lambda)⊗N for any based N (highest FIRST); (b) M⊗ωV(lambda) for any based M (lowest SECOND), with vectorwise finite action; (c) arbitrary U_A-stable based pairs in FINITE Cartan type; (d) a first factor in C_high with arbitrary based second, or an arbitrary based first with second in C_low, under vectorwise finite action. Here C_high consists of exact based subquotients of weight-admissible direct sums of finite highest tensor constructions; C_low is its lowest/unsigned-Chevalley counterpart. Based subobjects are saturated basis subsets and quotient maps are integral/bar compatible. These classes are closed under their normalized finite tensor construction. In particular all finite highest products and ordered highest-prefix/arbitrary-based-middle/lowest-suffix products have the integral tensor action and construction. Upper-cone/finite-component conditions are imposed on direct sums; in the lowest case use its explicit lower-cone action bound. No arbitrary based-O_int pair is covered in general type.
In these cases Θ preserves the actual integral tensor lattice and has A-valued ACTION coefficients in its tensor bases. Its degree0 component is identity; every positive root component shifts the first label up and second down, so the bar is locally weight-transfer triangular with diagonal1. In finite Cartan type the stronger algebra coefficients Θ_nu∈U_A^+_nu⊗U_A^-_-nu are also proved. That stronger universal coefficient claim is false in general affine type. A normalized triangular bar-correction constructs the genuine tensor global basis; raw tensor products of lower basis vectors need not themselves be bar fixed. The class in(d) means based subquotients of weight-admissible direct sums of finite highest tensors with the constructed tensor basis, not arbitrary integral lattices in semisimple field modules. The affine construction in the proof explicitly disproves unqualified arbitrary-based action integrality while retaining these full general symmetrizable cases.

items.title: Tensor bars on finite products of based integrable modules
items.statement:
For ANY finite sequence of based integrable modules in finite-weight-space O_int, the field tensor bar Ψ=Θ(composite factor bars) is well defined, semilinear, U/bar compatible, involutive and independent of all parenthesizations. All root-height sums are vectorwise finite. This field assertion is preserved for arbitrary based pairs; it does not imply integral action.
Its integral/based assertion holds for the actual admissible cases proved by the integral-action supplier: highest-first or first C_high with arbitrary based second; arbitrary based first with lowest/C_low second under finite action; all finite highest products and exact based subquotients/direct sums of their tensor constructions; ordered highest-prefix/based-middle/lowest-suffix products with explicit local support bounds; and arbitrary based pairs/products in finite Cartan type (including the finite-degree polynomial type-A modules). For any other pair the same conclusion is conditional on an independently PROVED integral Θ action, not field semisimplicity or lattice freeness.
In these cases Ψ preserves the divided-power integral tensor lattice. Its action on raw tensor lower basis vectors is locally weight-transfer triangular with diagonal1; the actual tensor global vectors are its uniquely corrected bar-fixed lifts congruent to those raw tensor vectors moduloq, with corrections in qZ[q]. They form a genuine A-basis and give the integral balanced tensor triple. The q0 tensor lattice and crystal basis are supplied separately by the completed crystal tensor rule. Its infinity chart is Ψ(L0_tensor), not an asserted bar containment in L0; semilinearity sends q toq^-1. The raw tensor lower vectors are generally not bar fixed. The exact based integral/bar-compatible subquotient maps preserve the corrected global bases by balanced uniqueness. No assertion covers arbitrary two-sided-unbounded evaluation, semi-infinite limits, a universal-R braiding, or general arbitrary-based integral action (the affine boundary in the supplier disproves the latter).

items.title: The cyclic affine type A Cartan datum and its residues
items.statement: Fix e≥2, I=Z/eZ and A with a_ii=2, a_(i,i±1)=−1 for e≥3 and the single double-edge a_01=a_10=−2 for e=2; all d_i=1 and q_i=q. Choose the explicit free lattices P=⊕_i Z Lambda_i⊕Z delta and Pvee=⊕_i Z h_i⊕Z d, with <Lambda_j,h_i>=delta_ij, <delta,h_i>=0, <Lambda_j,d>=0, <delta,d>=1. Define alpha_i=Σ_j a_ji Lambda_j+delta_(i,0) delta. Then the simple roots are independent, Σ_i alpha_i=delta, <h_i,alpha_j>=a_ij, and <d,alpha_i>=delta_(i,0). The central c=Σ_i h_i has <c,alpha_i>=0. Level means <c,weight>; Lambda_i has level1. The symmetric root form has (alpha_i,alpha_j)=a_ij; this is distinct from the lattice pairing. Put P_cl=P/Z delta. The diagram reflection tau fixes Lambda0,delta,d and sends Lambda_i,alpha_i,h_i to the indices−i. The finite vector representation below has level0; its perfect crystal has level1. Choose the normalized symmetric rational form on P_Q=Q_Q direct-sum Q Lambda0 with (Lambda0,alpha_i)=delta_i0 and (Lambda0,Lambda0)=0. It satisfies (lambda,alpha_i)=<lambda,h_i> and (lambda,delta)=level(lambda), and is tau- and W-invariant. The root form remains integral; the full weight form is rational-valued. The level-one subset of P_cl is an infinite affine hyperplane, distinct from the finite level-zero vector weights.

items.title: The level-one vector representation, its affinization and the energy function
items.statement:
Fix $e\ge2$ and let $(I,A,D,P,P^\vee,\alpha_i,h_i,\delta,d,c,q)$ be the cyclic
affine type $A$ Cartan datum of
[[def-cyclic-affine-type-a-cartan-datum]], so $I=\mathbb Z/e\mathbb Z$ and
$q_i=q$ for all $i$. Choose once and for all the representatives
$j\in\{1,\dots,e\}$ of the residues of $I$, so that $j=e$ represents the residue
$0$; all indices $j-1$, $j+1$ below are read in this representative range.

**The derived vector module.** Put $P^\vee_{\mathrm{cl}}:=\bigoplus_{i\in I}\mathbb Z h_i$, and let $U_q'(\mathfrak g)$ denote the subalgebra of $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ generated by $E_i,F_i,K_h$ with $h\in P^\vee_{\mathrm{cl}}$. Let $V:=\bigoplus_{j=1}^{e}\mathbb Q(q)v_j$ and
define $\mathbb Q(q)$-linear operators $K_h$ ($h\in P^\vee_{\mathrm{cl}}$), $E_i$, $F_i$
($i\in I$) on $V$ by

$$K_hv_j:=q^{\langle\Lambda_j-\Lambda_{j-1},h\rangle}v_j,\qquad E_iv_j:=\delta_{j\equiv i+1}\,v_{j-1},\qquad F_iv_j:=\delta_{j\equiv i}\,v_{j+1},$$

where $v_0:=v_e$ and $v_{e+1}:=v_1$ are read cyclically, and $\equiv$ refers to
the residues of $I$. The vector $v_j$ has **classical weight**
$\lambda_j^{\mathrm{cl}}\in P_{\mathrm{cl}}$, where $\lambda_j:=\Lambda_j-\Lambda_{j-1}\in P$ is the fixed representative used in the affinization, and **residue** $j\in I$. These operators give the derived $U_q'(\mathfrak g)$-action; no degree operator $K_d$ is part of this finite action.

**Affinization.** The **affinization** $V_{\mathrm{aff}}$ is the
$\mathbb Q(q)$-vector space with basis $\{u_m\}_{m\in\mathbb Z}$, identified
with $V\otimes\mathbb Q[z,z^{-1}]$ by $u_m:=z^av_j$ whenever
$m=j-ae$ with $j\in\{1,\dots,e\}$ and $a\in\mathbb Z$; this representation of
$m$ is unique. On this space the full affine operators $K_h$ ($h\in P^\vee$), $E_i,F_i$ are

$$K_hu_m:=q^{\langle\lambda_j+a\delta,h\rangle}u_m,\qquad E_iu_m:=\delta_{m\equiv i+1}\,u_{m-1},\qquad F_iu_m:=\delta_{m\equiv i}\,u_{m+1},$$

so that in the $z$-picture
$E_i(z^av_j)=\delta_{j\equiv i+1}z^{a+\delta_{i0}}v_{j-1}$ and
$F_i(z^av_j)=\delta_{j\equiv i}z^{a-\delta_{i0}}v_{j+1}$. We write
$\mathrm{wt}(u_m):=\lambda_j+a\delta\in P$ and $l(u_m):=ae-j=-m$; the
**ordinary order** is $u_m>u_n\iff m>n$.

**Crystal data.** Put $B:=\{b_1,\dots,b_e\}$, $B_{\mathrm{aff}}:=\{u_m\}_{m\in\mathbb Z}$,
and define partial operators $f_i,e_i$ on $B_{\mathrm{aff}}$ by
$f_iu_m:=u_{m+1}$ if $m\equiv i$ and $f_iu_m:=0$ otherwise, and
$e_iu_m:=u_{m-1}$ if $m\equiv i+1$ and $e_iu_m:=0$ otherwise. Let

$$\varepsilon_i(u_m):=\delta_{m\equiv i+1},\qquad \varphi_i(u_m):=\delta_{m\equiv i},\qquad \varepsilon(u_m):=\sum_i\varepsilon_i(u_m)\Lambda_i^{\mathrm{cl}},\qquad \varphi(u_m):=\sum_i\varphi_i(u_m)\Lambda_i^{\mathrm{cl}},$$

in $P_{\mathrm{cl}}$. On the finite set $B$ the same formulas apply through
$b_j\leftrightarrow v_j$, so that $f_ib_j=b_{j+1}$ if $j\equiv i$ and $0$
otherwise, and $e_ib_j=b_{j-1}$ if $j\equiv i+1$ and $0$ otherwise.

**The opposite channel and its energy.** On $B_{\mathrm{aff}}\otimes B_{\mathrm{aff}}$
use the tensor rule $\otimes_+$

$$f_i(x\otimes y):=\begin{cases}f_ix\otimes y,&\varepsilon_i(x)\ge\varphi_i(y),\\x\otimes f_iy,&\varepsilon_i(x)<\varphi_i(y),\end{cases}\qquad e_i(x\otimes y):=\begin{cases}e_ix\otimes y,&\varepsilon_i(x)>\varphi_i(y),\\x\otimes e_iy,&\varepsilon_i(x)\le\varphi_i(y),\end{cases}$$

and the **energy function**

$$H_{\mathrm{op}}(z^ab_j\otimes z^bb_k):=\chi(j>k)+b-a,\qquad \chi(j>k):=\begin{cases}1,&j>k,\\0,&j\le k,\end{cases}$$

for $a,b\in\mathbb Z$ and $j,k\in\{1,\dots,e\}$. For a fixed **charge**
$M\in\mathbb Z$ the **ground sequence** is $b^\circ_s:=u_{M-s}$ ($s\ge0$).

items.title: The affine Hecke algebra and its commuting action on tensor powers of the vector representation
items.statement:
Fix $e\ge2$ and keep all conventions of
[[def-the-level-one-vector-representation-its-affinization-and-energy-function]]:
the Cartan datum, the space $V_{\mathrm{aff}}=\bigoplus_{m\in\mathbb Z}\mathbb Q(q)u_m$
with $u_m=z^av_j$ ($m=j-ae$, $j\in\{1,\dots,e\}$), the operators
$K_h,E_i,F_i$, the classical weights $\lambda_j=\Lambda_j-\Lambda_{j-1}$, and the
fixed coproduct $\Delta(K_h)=K_h\otimes K_h$,
$\Delta(E_i)=E_i\otimes K_i^{-1}+1\otimes E_i$,
$\Delta(F_i)=F_i\otimes1+K_i\otimes F_i$ of
[[thm-the-drinfeld-jimbo-formulas-define-a-hopf-algebra]].
Put $Q:=q^2$ and $c:=Q-1$, and let $Y_j$ denote the operator "multiply the $j$-th
tensor factor by $z$", so that $Y_j$ is invertible with
$Y_ju_m=u_{m-e}$ in the $j$-th slot and different $Y_j$ commute.

**The affine Hecke algebra $\tilde H_N$.** For $N\ge1$, $\tilde H_N$ is the
unital $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra with generators $S_1,\dots,S_{N-1}$ and invertible
$Y_1^{\pm1},\dots,Y_N^{\pm1}$ subject to

$$S_i^2=(Q-1)S_i+Q,\qquad S_iS_{i+1}S_i=S_{i+1}S_iS_{i+1},\qquad S_iS_j=S_jS_i\quad(|i-j|\ge2),$$

$$Y_iY_j=Y_jY_i,\qquad S_iY_j=Y_jS_i\quad(j\notin\{i,i+1\}),\qquad S_iY_iS_i=QY_{i+1}.$$

The element $t_i:=-q^{-1}S_i$ then satisfies $(t_i-q^{-1})(t_i+q)=0$; for a
reduced word $w=s_{i_1}\cdots s_{i_k}\in S_N$ put $S_w:=S_{i_1}\cdots S_{i_k}$
and $A_N:=\sum_{w\in S_N}S_w$ (well defined by the braid relations).

**The two-vector operator and its extension.** On residue tensors
$v_j\otimes v_k$ ($j,k\in\{1,\dots,e\}$) set

$$S(v_j\otimes v_k)=\begin{cases}-q\,v_k\otimes v_j,&j<k,\\ -\,v_j\otimes v_j,&j=k,\\ -q\,v_k\otimes v_j+(Q-1)v_j\otimes v_k,&j>k.\end{cases}$$

For a Laurent monomial $f=Y_1^pY_2^q$ define, with $s(f):=Y_2^pY_1^q$ the
swap of the two loop variables,

$$S(f\,w):=s(f)\,S(w)+(1-Q)\,Y_2\,\frac{f-s(f)}{Y_1-Y_2}\,w\qquad(w\in V\otimes V),$$

and extend linearly; the quotient $(f-s(f))/(Y_1-Y_2)$ is a Laurent polynomial,
so $S$ is a well-defined linear endomorphism of $V_{\mathrm{aff}}\otimes V_{\mathrm{aff}}$.
On $V_{\mathrm{aff}}^{\otimes N}$ the generator $S_i$ acts by this operator on
the tensor factors $i,i+1$ and $Y_j$ acts on the $j$-th factor as above; this
defines the **affine Hecke action**. The whole action commutes with the derived quantum group $U_q'(\mathfrak g)$ (the generators $E_i,F_i$ and $K_h$ with $h$ in the span of the simple coroots). Each $S_i$, and therefore $A_N$, also preserves total loop degree and commutes with the full affine quantum-group action. The individual loops instead satisfy $K_dY_jK_d^{-1}=qY_j$. Products are composed as left operators; right-action notation reverses their order using the anti-involution fixing the generators.

items.title: Integrable rank-one actions force the quantum Serre sums
items.statement: Over Q(q), with q_i=q^(d_i) generic, suppose chosen type-one Cartan/E/F operators satisfy all toral and mixed [E_i,F_j] relations, with each single-color action integrable. Then BOTH quantum Serre sums of order n=1−a_ij hold, including cubic affine e2. This theorem uses no already-imposed Serre relation.

items.title: The q-antisymmetrizer splits the tensor power and its kernel is the sum of the Hecke kernels
items.statement:
Let $k=\mathbb Q(q)$, $Q=q^2$, and let $M_N=V_{\mathrm{aff}}^{\otimes N}$ carry the action of
[[def-the-affine-hecke-algebra-action-on-finite-tensor-powers-of-the-vector-representation]].
Put $A_N=\sum_{w\in S_N}S_w$ and
$C_N=\sum_{w\in S_N}Q^{l(w)}=\prod_{r=1}^N(1+Q+\cdots+Q^{r-1})\ne0$.
Then:

(i) $A_NS_i=S_iA_N=QA_N$ and $A_N^2=C_NA_N$. The operator
$P_N=C_N^{-1}A_N$ is a $k$-linear idempotent commuting with the quantum-group action.

(ii) $\ker A_N=\sum_{i=1}^{N-1}\ker(S_i+1)$, a sum of $k$-subspaces, and
$M_N=\ker A_N\oplus\operatorname{im}A_N$. The map $[x]\mapsto A_Nx$ identifies
$M_N/\ker A_N$ with $\operatorname{im}A_N$ as quantum-group modules;
$A_N$ acts there by $C_N$, and every $S_i$ acts there by $Q$.

(iii) On two factors put $x=Y_1$, $y=Y_2$, $R=k[x^{\pm1},y^{\pm1}]$ and
$B=k[x+y,(xy)^{\pm1}]$, the symmetric Laurent subring. The complete partial
q-symmetric kernel on the original Laurent-loop vector space is
$$\ker(S+1)=\bigoplus_j B(v_j\otimes v_j)\ \oplus\!\bigoplus_{j<k}\left(Bh_{jk}+Bh'_{jk}\right),$$
where, writing $a_{jk}=v_j\otimes v_k$ and $b_{jk}=v_k\otimes v_j$,
$$h_{jk}=a_{jk}+q^{-1}b_{jk},\qquad h'_{jk}=x b_{jk}+q^{-1}y a_{jk}.$$
Equivalently, it is the $k$-span of $(S-Q)(u_l\otimes u_m)$ for all integers
$l,m$. This kernel is stable under the quantum-group action and symmetric
Laurent multiplication; arbitrary Laurent multiplication need not preserve it.
Its quotient satisfies the full local straightening relations: repeated entries
vanish, and for $l<m$, writing $m-l=ae+b$ with $a\ge0$ and $0\le b<e$,
$$u_l\wedge u_m=\begin{cases}-u_m\wedge u_l,&b=0,\\-q^{-1}u_m\wedge u_l,&a=0,\ b>0,\\-q^{-1}u_m\wedge u_l-u_{l+ae}\wedge u_{m-ae}-q^{-1}u_{m-ae}\wedge u_{l+ae},&a>0,\ b>0.\end{cases}$$
The remaining unordered pair in the third case has strictly smaller gap, so
repetition terminates. At $q=1$, $S_i$ specializes to the negative flip,
$A_N$ to $\sum_w(-1)^{l(w)}w$, and $C_N$ to $N!$; the kernel and quotient
are the ordinary local symmetric relations and exterior power.

items.title: The vector representation is a perfect crystal of level one and carries a lower global basis
items.statement:
Keep the conventions of
[[def-the-level-one-vector-representation-its-affinization-and-energy-function]].
Then:

(i) The derived level-$0$ module $V$ has **level-one perfect crystal**
$B=\{b_1,\dots,b_e\}$ in the sense of axioms (P1)-(P3): the weights of $V$ are
the finite Weyl orbit of $\lambda^\circ=\Lambda_1-\Lambda_0$ in $P_{\mathrm{cl}}$
with one-dimensional weight spaces, $B\otimes B$ is connected,
$\varepsilon(b)\in P_{\mathrm{cl}}^+$ and $\varphi(b)\in P_{\mathrm{cl}}^+$ have
level one for every $b$, the maps $\varepsilon,\varphi:B\to(P_{\mathrm{cl}}^+)_1$
are bijections onto the level-one dominant weights, and
$B_{\min}:=\{b:\langle c,\varepsilon(b)\rangle=1\}$ equals $B$.

(ii) The basis $G(b_j):=v_j$ is a **lower global basis** of $V$ for the ordinary
semilinear bar involution with coefficient bar $q\mapsto q^{-1}$ and
$\overline{v_j}=v_j$: the local $A_0$-lattice $V_0=\bigoplus_j A_0v_j$ is
bar-stable up to $q\mapsto q^{-1}$, the images $b_j=G(b_j)+qV_0$ are the
crystal elements, $\bar{E_iv}=E_i\bar v$ and $\bar{F_iv}=F_i\bar v$ for all
$v\in V$, all nontrivial rank-one strings have exactly two vertices with $E$- and
$F$-coefficients $1$, and all remaining color strings are frozen singletons, and the divided powers
$E_i^{(m)},F_i^{(m)}$ vanish for $m\ge2$. Here
$A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$ and $A_0=\mathbb Q[q]_{(q)}$ are kept distinct, with the separate positive integral chart $\bigoplus_j\mathbb Z[q]v_j$. The Laurent, zero and infinity charts have balanced intersection $\bigoplus_j\mathbb Z v_j$, so this is the actual integral/bar-compatible lower basis.

(iii) The same statements hold on the affinization with
$G(z^ab_j)=z^av_j$, the loop variable fixed by the bar involution, and the full
$P$-weight $\Lambda_j-\Lambda_{j-1}+a\delta$; the finite $V$ is a
$U_q'(\mathfrak g)$-module with $P_{\mathrm{cl}}$-weights and is not a
level-one $P$-graded highest weight module.

items.title: The finite q-wedge space and the normal-ordering relations
items.statement:
For $N\ge1$ let $V_{\mathrm{aff}}^{\otimes N}$ carry the affine Hecke action and put
$W_N:=V_{\mathrm{aff}}^{\otimes N}\big/\ker A_N$, where $A_N=\sum_{w\in S_N}S_w$;
write $u_{m_1}\wedge\cdots\wedge u_{m_N}$ for the image of the pure tensor, and let
$\wedge$ denote this product. Call an index tuple **normal** (or normally
ordered) if $m_1>m_2>\cdots>m_N$, and set $W_A:=\sum_{\text{normal }I}\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]\,u_I$,
$W_0:=\bigoplus_{\text{normal }I}\mathbb Z[q]\,u_I$, where $u_I$ is the image of
the corresponding ordered wedge.

For $l<m$ write $m-l=ae+b$ with $a\ge0$, $0\le b<e$ (so $a=\lfloor(m-l)/e\rfloor$
and $b$ is the residue difference). The **normal-ordering relations** are:

$$u_l\wedge u_l=0;\qquad u_l\wedge u_m=-u_m\wedge u_l\quad(b=0);\qquad u_l\wedge u_m=-q^{-1}u_m\wedge u_l\quad(a=0,\ b>0);$$

$$u_l\wedge u_m=-q^{-1}u_m\wedge u_l-u_{l+ae}\wedge u_{m-ae}-q^{-1}u_{m-ae}\wedge u_{l+ae}\quad(a>0,\ b>0),$$

where the last line is to be read as a relation in $W_N$ and is applied
recursively to its two remaining unordered pairs; each recursion step strictly
decreases the gap of the unordered pair it rewrites and keeps every index
between $l$ and $m$, so the procedure terminates. The energy normal order is
the equivalent formulation through the opposite-channel energy:
$u_{m_1}\wedge u_{m_2}$ is rewritten toward decreasing indices by
$H_{\mathrm{op}}(u_{m_1}\otimes u_{m_2})>0\iff m_1>m_2$ of
[[def-the-level-one-vector-representation-its-affinization-and-energy-function]].

items.title: The q-wedge relations coincide with the type-A energy braiding kernel
items.statement:
On $V_{\mathrm{aff}}\otimes V_{\mathrm{aff}}$ put $a=Y_1/Y_2$ and let $P$ be the
flip of the two tensor factors including their loop variables. Define the
completed normalized left operator

$$R_{\mathrm{fix}}:=(q^2-a)^{-1}\bigl[(a-1)S+q^2-1\bigr],\qquad \psi_{\mathrm{fix}}:=1-q^2a^{-1},$$

where $S$ is the two-factor Hecke operator of
[[def-the-affine-hecke-algebra-action-on-finite-tensor-powers-of-the-vector-representation]]
and $(q^2-a)^{-1}$ is expanded $q$-adically as
$-a^{-1}\sum_{r\ge0}(q^2/a)^r$, so $\psi_{\mathrm{fix}}=1-q^2/a$ has constant term $1$. Then:

(i) $R_{\mathrm{fix}}$ swaps the two loop variables, fixes every extremal
pure tensor $u\otimes u$, and commutes with the fixed $U_q'(\mathfrak g)$-action;
the cleared identity
$\psi_{\mathrm{fix}}(R_{\mathrm{fix}}-1)=(a^{-1}-1)(S+1)$ holds in the Laurent
domain, and since multiplication by $a^{-1}-1$ is injective on the original
Laurent-loop module one has $\ker(R_{\mathrm{fix}}-1)=\ker(S+1)$ there, before
any localization.

(ii) $R_{\mathrm{fix}}$ satisfies the normalized Yang-Baxter equation
$R_{12}R_{23}R_{12}=R_{23}R_{12}R_{23}$ on the three-factor completed module.

(iii) The flipped operator $R_{\mathrm{op}}:=PR_{\mathrm{fix}}P$ with
$\psi_{\mathrm{op}}=1-q^2a$ is the opposite-channel ($\otimes_+$) normalized
braiding of
[[def-the-level-one-vector-representation-its-affinization-and-energy-function]]:
its $q^0$-leading term is
$z^{H_{\mathrm{op}}}b_1\otimes z^{-H_{\mathrm{op}}}b_2$ with the energy
$H_{\mathrm{op}}(z^ab_j\otimes z^bb_k)=\chi(j>k)+b-a$, and its kernel is
$N_{\mathrm{op}}=P\ker(S+1)$, the $U_q'(\mathfrak g)$- and symmetric-loop orbit of the extremal
diagonal generated by
$C_{j,k}=v_j\otimes z^{-\chi(j>k)}v_k+q\,z^{-\chi(j>k)}v_k\otimes v_j$ $(j\ne k)$
and $C_{j,j}=v_j\otimes v_j$. Flipping back gives the fixed-channel quotient
and the normal-ordering relations of
[[def-finite-q-wedge-space-and-normal-ordering-relations]].

items.title: Normally ordered q-wedges form a basis for every finite wedge length
items.statement:
For every $N\ge1$ the normally ordered wedges
$\{u_{m_1}\wedge\cdots\wedge u_{m_N}:m_1>m_2>\cdots>m_N\}$ of
[[def-finite-q-wedge-space-and-normal-ordering-relations]] form a
$\mathbb Q(q)$-basis of $W_N$ and an $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$-basis of the
Laurent lattice $W_A$. The straightening algorithm terminates with a
well-founded profile: the total index sum and the ambient index interval are
preserved, secondary pairs become strictly more balanced in the sorted
dominance profile, and a leading adjacent swap decreases the inversion count;
in particular no bound by the initial inversion count alone is used. The
local $A_0$-chart $L_0:=A_0W_0$, where $A_0=\mathbb Q[q]_{(q)}$ and $W_0$
is the separate $\mathbb Z[q]$-span of the normal wedges, is a crystal basis: for each color $i$, on the occupied set of a normal tuple
the disjoint pairs $(u_{i+ke},u_{i+ke+1})$ behave as two-vertex highest-weight
$1$ strings, empty and doubly occupied pairs are frozen, and a shift of an
index by one either stays ordered or collides to zero; hence the residues of
the ordered wedges are stable under the normalized string operators and give a
crystal of the integrable affine wedge module. The image of the full
$\mathbb Z[q]$-tensor lattice need not equal $W_0$, and negative powers of $q$
in the straightening are not asserted to be triangular at $q=0$.

items.title: The semi-infinite q-wedge Fock space and its q-adic topology
items.statement:
Fix a **charge** $M\in\mathbb Z$ and let $W_N$ be the finite q-wedge spaces of
[[def-finite-q-wedge-space-and-normal-ordering-relations]]. For $r\le s$ define
the connecting map
$\varphi_{r,s}(u_{i_1}\wedge\cdots\wedge u_{i_r})
=u_{i_1}\wedge\cdots\wedge u_{i_r}\wedge u_{M-r}\wedge u_{M-r-1}\wedge\cdots\wedge u_{M-s+1}$,
so that new entries are the consecutive ground tail
$u_{M-N},u_{M-N-1},\dots$ appended to a prefix of length $N$. The **charge-$M$
Fock space** is the algebraic direct limit $F^{(M)}:=\varinjlim_{N}W_N$ of the
finite wedge spaces along these maps; equivalently it is the quotient of the
eventually-vacuum tensor space by the local wedge kernels. Write
$|\lambda;M\rangle$ for the image of the normally ordered semi-infinite word
with entries $i_k=M+\lambda_k-k+1$ indexed by the positive parts of the
partition $\lambda$, so that the vacuum $\varnothing$ corresponds to
$u_M\wedge u_{M-1}\wedge u_{M-2}\wedge\cdots$.

The **Laurent, positive and integral charts** of $F^{(M)}$ are

$$F_A:=\bigoplus_{\lambda}A\,|\lambda;M\rangle,\qquad F_0:=\bigoplus_{\lambda}A_0\,|\lambda;M\rangle,\qquad F_{\mathbb Z0}:=\bigoplus_{\lambda}\mathbb Z[q]\,|\lambda;M\rangle,\qquad A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}],\ A_0=\mathbb Q[q]_{(q)}.$$

The **separated q-adic topology** on the full field space is the one induced by
the filtration $q^nF_0$, never by $q^nF_A=F_A$; a finite $A_0$-label component
completes to a $\mathbb Q[\![q]\!]$-lattice, and the full-field component completes
to $\mathbb Q((q))\otimes_{\mathbb Q(q)}F^{(M)}_\mu$ for the label-weight
pieces. Separately, the integral $\mathbb Z[q]$-chart completes to a
$\mathbb Z[\![q]\!]$-lattice; this completion is not identified with
$\mathbb Q((q))$ and is not asserted to carry a $\mathbb Q$-vector-space
topology.

**Vacuum weights.** For $M=j-ae$ with $j\in\{1,\dots,e\}$ and $a\in\mathbb Z$
the vacuum $P$-weight $\Omega_M$ is normalised by $\Omega_0=\Lambda_0$ and
$\Omega_M-\Omega_{M-1}=\mathrm{wt}(u_M)$; explicitly, if $M=te+r$ with
$0\le r<e$, then

$$\Omega_M=\Lambda_r-\Bigl(\frac{e\,t(t-1)}{2}+tr\Bigr)\delta.$$

The weight of the partition $\lambda$ is
$\Omega_M-\sum_{\text{cells}}\alpha_{c-r+M}$, its size $|\lambda|$ is a separate
grading, and the $d$-eigenvalue is $\Omega_M(d)$ minus the number of residue-$0$
cells; no periodicity $\Omega_M=\Omega_{M-e}+\delta$ is asserted.

items.title: Tail estimates: q-adic vanishing against the vacuum and finiteness of the weight strings
items.statement:
Let $F^{(M)}$ be the charge-$M$ Fock space with ground sequence
$b^\circ_s=u_{M-s}$ and let $H_{\mathrm{op}}$ be the opposite-channel energy.
Then:

(i) **Vanishing against the right tail.** For a fixed type-A ground sequence,
the condition $H_{\mathrm{op}}(b\otimes b^\circ_s)\le0$ means that the added
integer index lies inside or below the filled right tail
$\{M-s,M-s-1,\dots\}$; then $b\wedge b^\circ_s\wedge b^\circ_{s+1}\wedge\cdots=0$,
a sufficiently long finite prefix of this entire filled-tail wedge is already $0$, and hence the element lies in $q^nW_0$ for
every $n$.

(ii) **Dual left tail.** The mirrored condition with the left tail gives the
same exact finite vanishing, with the roles of left and right exchanged.

(iii) **Endomorphisms commuting with the loop.** A nonzero-weight endomorphism
$C$ of $V_{\mathrm{aff}}$ commuting with $z$ has only finitely many
loop-shift/color terms on each fundamental vector; inserting $C$ deep inside a
ground tail is eventually $0$, so it converges $q$-adically to $0$ on every
vector.

(iv) **The period operator.** For the explicit period operator
$T$ on $F^{(M)}$ that prepends $e$ vacuum entries and shifts every old index
down by $e$: $T$ preserves each label-weight/size component, and on the
positive-size-$n$ part its $k$-th power is $0$ as soon as $ke>n$.
Consequently $(1-T)^{-1}=1+T+T^2+\cdots$ is a finite geometric sum on every
nonvacuum weight, and each label weight has only finitely many partition
vectors.

items.title: Semi-infinite wedges are indexed by partitions and the action gives the node formulas
items.statement:
Keep the conventions of the charge-$M$ Fock space
[[def-semi-infinite-q-wedge-fock-space-and-q-adic-topology]]. Normal wedges are
bijective with partitions through $i_k=M+\lambda_k-k+1$; in charge $0$ the
vacuum is the empty partition. The stable finite-prefix action defines linear
endomorphisms $F_i,E_i,K_i,K_d$ of $F^{(0)}$ by

$$F_i|\lambda\rangle=\sum_{\text{addable }\gamma\text{ of residue }i}q^{A_i^r-R_i^r}\,|\lambda+\gamma\rangle,\qquad E_i|\mu\rangle=\sum_{\text{removable }\gamma\text{ of residue }i}q^{-(A_i^l-R_i^l)}\,|\mu-\gamma\rangle,$$

where for $F_i$ the counts are taken in the smaller diagram $\lambda$ and count
addable/removable $i$-nodes strictly to the right of the added node (higher
content), and for $E_i$ the counts are taken in the smaller diagram $\mu-\gamma$
and count nodes strictly to the left of the removed node (lower content), with
the removed node excluded; all sums are finite. The toral operators act by
$K_i|\lambda\rangle=q^{N_i(\lambda)}|\lambda\rangle$ with $N_i$ the
addable-minus-removable count, and $K_d|\lambda\rangle=q^{-m_0(\lambda)}|\lambda\rangle$;
the size $|\lambda|$ is a separate grading. Charge $M$ replaces the residues by
content $+M$ and $K_d$ by $\Omega_M(d)-m_0$.

items.title: The level-one partition Fock space and node residues
items.statement: Let F=⊕_(partitions lambda) Q(q)|lambda> with its chosen charge0 weight Lambda0−Σ m_i(lambda)alpha_i and size grading. Node(r,c) has residue c−r mod e. The vacuum is empty; F_i adds and E_i removes with the preceding explicit finite node formulas. K_i eigenvalues are proved by the node-count lemma; K_d acts by q^−m0. These are declared linear operators until the affine-relation theorem proves the module structure. A partition is e-regular iff each positive part has multiplicity<e; it is e-restricted iff lambda_r−lambda_(r+1)<e for every r, equivalently its CONJUGATE has part multiplicities<e. A column of height e is allowed in an e-restricted partition. Full Fock/crystal vertices are ALL partitions; the empty component will be the e-regular subset.

items.title: The addable-minus-removable node count is the level-one Cartan pairing
items.statement: For every partition lambda and every i in I, with N_i(lambda)=I_i(lambda)-R_i(lambda) the number of addable i-nodes minus the number of removable i-nodes of lambda, one has N_i(lambda)=delta_{i,0}-sum_j a_ij m_j(lambda). Consequently sum_i N_i(lambda)=1, the toral operator K_i acts on |lambda> by q^{<h_i,wt(|lambda>)>}=q^{N_i(lambda)}, and the central element K_0K_1...K_{e-1} acts by q, so wt(|lambda>)=Lambda_0-sum_j m_j alpha_j has level 1 and the toral action is the one required for F to be a U_q-module. In particular N_i(empty)=delta_{i,0}, and adding a node of residue k changes N_i by -a_ik, hence changes wt by -alpha_k.

items.title: The node order and the signed exponents $N_i^l$ and $N_i^r$
items.statement: For fixed residue list the addable/removable nodes by INCREASING content; larger content is further right/higher. N_i^r and N_i^l count addable minus removable nodes strictly larger/smaller than gamma, in the SMALLER diagram lambda when mu=lambda+gamma. Then N_i^r+N_i^l=N_i(lambda)−1. F coefficient isq^N_i^r and E coefficientq^−N_i^l. The finite signature selection is defined separately: a Chevalley coefficient minimizer is not in general a Kashiwara arrow, and even a nonzero single Chevalley term can have zero crystal arrow.

items.title: Fixed-residue node cubes realize the actual Fock strings
items.statement: For the declared charge0 node operators, fix i and one partition. The orbit obtained by toggling its addable/removable i-cells is a FINITE BOOLEAN cube: availability of one such cell is unchanged by every other i-toggle, including e2. Put the slots in DECREASING content order, state+=addable/top and state−=removable/bottom. The node operators on this cube are exactly V(1)^tensor k for the FIXED rank-one coproduct, with K=q^(#plus−#minus). Its raw A0 partition span is therefore stable under the actual normalized string operators. In that order cancel +−, take f FIRST surviving+, e LAST surviving−; equivalently in the fixed increasing-content order cancel−+, take f LAST+, e FIRST−. Residue labels are all cube vertices, both endpoints are included, and epsilon/phi are the surviving minus/plus counts. The standard partition-orthonormal form is the normalized rank-one polarization, and all divided E/F powers have Laurent-integral matrices. No Chevalley minimum argument is used.

items.title: Good and cogood nodes by residue-signature reduction
items.statement: For an i-node word in the fixed INCREASING-content order write+=(addable),−=(removable), cancel adjacent−+ until no such pair remains. Surviving minuses are normal REMOVABLE nodes and the FIRST surviving minus is the good node for e_i; surviving pluses are conormal ADDABLE nodes and the LAST surviving plus is the cogood node for f_i. Missing chosen sign means the operator is0. Equivalently read DECREASING content/columns (top-to-bottom), cancel+−, take good=LAST− and cogood=FIRST+. These name conventions match the usual Fayers good deletion/cogood addition. They are combinatorial string data, not a selection by minimum ordinary Chevalley exponent.

items.title: The Fock space node formulas satisfy the quantum affine relations
items.statement: The constructed node operators on ALL partition vectors give a chosen P-graded integrable U_q(affine sl_e)-module for the fixed coproduct/Cartan datum. All K/E/F commutators and BOTH Serre sums hold; e2 has a_01=a_10=−2 and the cubic coefficient[3]=q²+1+q^-2. Each color acts on finite bit cubes. K_0…K_(e−1)=q, K_d=q^-m0 and F_i/E_i change the P-weight by∓alpha_i. Ordinary standard coefficients may have q^-1 poles; normalized Kashiwara lattice stability is separate.

items.title: The empty partition generates an integrable highest weight submodule of highest weight $\Lambda_0$
items.statement:
In the charge-$0$ partition Fock space the vacuum $\varnothing$ has
$E_i\varnothing=0$, $K_i\varnothing=q^{\delta_{i0}}\varnothing$ and
$K_d\varnothing=\varnothing$, so its weight is $\Lambda_0$. The nonzero cyclic
submodule $M:=U_q(\mathfrak g)|\varnothing\rangle$ is the simple integrable
highest weight module $V(\Lambda_0)$; its integral lattice is
$U_A^-|\varnothing\rangle$ for $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$, and its crystal is the
empty graph component, identified in
[[thm-the-crystal-of-level-one-fock-space-is-the-good-node-partition-graph]]
rather than equated with the module.

items.title: The crystal of the level-one Fock space is the good-node partition graph
items.statement: The WHOLE level-one Fock module has the crystal basis(F0,B_F), F0=⊕_(ALL partitions)A0|lambda>, B_F={|lambda>+qF0}. The actual normalized Kashiwara operators REMOVE the good normal i-node and ADD the cogood conormal i-node of the corrected signature; epsilon/phi are survivor counts. This is a graph on ALL partitions, not only regular ones. Its empty connected component is precisely the e-regular partitions; e-restricted labels belong to the transposed model. A pole or a unique Chevalley term does not determine the crystal arrow.

items.title: The semi-infinite action on the Fock space is well defined and the Fock space is an integrable $U_q(\widehat{\mathfrak{sl}}_e)$-module
items.statement:
The stable prefix operators on the charge-$M$ algebraic wedge direct limit give
a well-defined integrable action of the affine quantum algebra, proved from the
node formulas and all defining relations of
[[thm-the-fock-space-node-formulas-satisfy-the-quantum-affine-relations]].
Infinite coproduct expressions converge $q$-adically and in this type-A model
have finite stabilised outputs; no two-sided-unbounded evaluation statement is
imported. On the vacuum $E_i\varnothing=0$, $F_i$ creates the single node of
residue $M$ and $K_i$ acts by $q^{\delta_{i\equiv M}}$. The wedge product of a
finite prefix with its correctly charged tail is $U_q$-linear with the fixed
formulas

$$E(v\wedge u)=Ev\wedge K_i^{-1}u+v\wedge Eu,\qquad F(v\wedge u)=Fv\wedge u+K_iv\wedge Fu .$$

With the declared use of the Axiom of Choice only in the general integrable
decomposition, the finite-weight upper cone of $F$ is a locally weight-finite
direct sum of simple integrable highest weight modules; completeness does not
mean finitely many constituents.

items.title: The empty component is the highest weight crystal $B(\Lambda_0)$
items.statement: With the declared AC for the general integrable-module decomposition, the empty component of the full partition crystal is the canonical B(Lambda0), with exactly the e-regular labels. Its module is M=U_q|empty> and its lower A0 lattice is M∩F0. It occurs once. More precisely F=⊕_(k≥0)V(Lambda0−k delta)^⊕p(k), a LOCALLY WEIGHT-FINITE indexed direct sum, where p(k) counts ordinary partitions of k. Hence chF=chV(Lambda0)Π_(r≥1)(1−exp(−r delta))^-1. A highest CRYSTAL label need not be a highest FIELD standard vector; the ambient canonical basis need not split these summands.

items.title: The regular-partition label convention and the Mullineux crystal involution
items.statement:
A partition is **regular** if each positive part occurs with multiplicity $<e$,
and **restricted** if $\lambda_r-\lambda_{r+1}<e$ for every $r$. Conjugation
$C:\lambda\mapsto\lambda'$ is the comparison map between the regular and the
restricted models; it sends the residue $i$ to $-i$. It is **not** the
same-model sign involution.

On the regular basic crystal of
[[thm-the-empty-component-is-the-highest-weight-crystal-b-lambda-zero]] define
$M$ by negating all colors of a lowering path from the empty partition:
$M(f_ib)=f_{-i}M(b)$ for every edge, $M(\varnothing)=\varnothing$. The
restricted sign involution is the conjugate $CMC^{-1}$.

items.title: The basic representation global basis is unitriangular in the partition basis
items.statement:
There is an explicit semi-infinite wedge bar $\psi$ with the vacuum fixed,
coefficient bar $q\mapsto q^{-1}$ and $U_q$/bar compatibility, whose restriction
to $M=V(\Lambda_0)$ is the normalized highest module bar. On **all** partitions
its integral triangular correction is

$$G(\lambda)=|\lambda\rangle+\sum_{\mu\ \text{strictly dominated by}\ \lambda}d_{\mu,\lambda}(q)|\mu\rangle, \qquad d_{\mu,\lambda}\in q\mathbb Z[q],$$

with diagonal $1$ and same $e$-core support; the family $\{G(\lambda)\}$ is an
$A$-basis of $F_A$ and an $A_0$-basis of $F_0$, with the actual infinity chart
and balanced $\mathbb Z$-intersection. Exactly the $e$-regular $G(\lambda)$ form
the lower global basis of $M$, identified by the two lower-global-basis
suppliers. The ambient basis is not automatically compatible with the other
field irreducible summands. The transpose equality
$d_{\lambda,\mu}=d_{\mu',\lambda'}$ is **false** in general; the source symmetry
concerns the bar matrix, not $D$. Ambient natural-form dual coefficients use
$(D^{-1})^{\mathsf T}$, and basic upper coefficients require the restricted Gram
inverse and need not be Laurent polynomials.

decline_pages.title: Quantum Affine Type A and Level-One Fock Space — Examples

items.title: Node actions for partitions of size at most three
items.statement:
For charge0 the following tables give ALL E_i,F_i actions on all standard partition vectors of size≤3, including outputs of size4, and all Cartan exponents N_i=#addable i−#removable i. A shape in a table denotes its standard vector; omitted terms have coefficient0.

e=2 (entries ordered i=0,...,e-1):
empty: N=(1, 0); F=('(1)', '0'); E=('0', '0')
(1): N=(-1, 2); F=('0', '(2)+q (1,1)'); E=('empty', '0')
(2): N=(1, 0); F=('(3)', 'q^-1 (2,1)'); E=('0', 'q^-1 (1)')
(1,1): N=(1, 0); F=('(1,1,1)', '(2,1)'); E=('0', '(1)')
(3): N=(-1, 2); F=('0', '(4)+q (3,1)'); E=('(2)', '0')
(2,1): N=(3, -2); F=('(3,1)+q (2,2)+q^2 (2,1,1)', '0'); E=('0', 'q (1,1)+(2)')
(1,1,1): N=(-1, 2); F=('0', '(2,1,1)+q (1,1,1,1)'); E=('(1,1)', '0')

e=3 (entries ordered i=0,...,e-1):
empty: N=(1, 0, 0); F=('(1)', '0', '0'); E=('0', '0', '0')
(1): N=(-1, 1, 1); F=('0', '(2)', '(1,1)'); E=('empty', '0', '0')
(2): N=(0, -1, 2); F=('0', '0', '(3)+q (2,1)'); E=('0', '(1)', '0')
(1,1): N=(0, 2, -1); F=('0', '(2,1)+q (1,1,1)', '0'); E=('0', '0', '(1)')
(3): N=(1, 0, 0); F=('(4)', '0', 'q^-1 (3,1)'); E=('0', '0', 'q^-1 (2)')
(2,1): N=(1, 0, 0); F=('(2,2)', 'q^-1 (2,1,1)', '(3,1)'); E=('0', 'q^-1 (1,1)', '(2)')
(1,1,1): N=(1, 0, 0); F=('(1,1,1,1)', '(2,1,1)', '0'); E=('0', '(1,1)', '0')

In both tables Σ_i N_i=1 and K_i acts by q^N_i, so the central product acts by q. The normalized crystal arrows on these same residues are computed separately by signature reduction; a minimal exponent of ordinary F is not their definition. The source calibration is Leclerc Exercise15 at e=2: F0|(3,1)>=q^-1|(3,2)>+|(3,1,1)> and E0|(3,1)>=q^-2|(2,1)>.

items.title: The double-edge Serre cancellation in affine $A_1$ on partitions
items.statement: At e=2, [3]=q²+1+q^-2 and S_X=X0³X1−[3]X0²X1X0+[3]X0X1X0²−X1X0³=0, for X=E,F. Products act right-to-left. The four E compositions all vanish on empty,1,2,11 (size<4); this is a trivial boundary check, not a cancellation proof. The four F compositions all vanish on empty,1,3,111. On2 the ordered four outputs are ([3]A,A,0,0), where A=(q^-2+1)|321>; on11 they are ([3]B,B,0,0), B=(q^-1+q)|321>, giving nontrivial cancellation. On21 they are (0,C,D,[3](D−C)), where C=[2](|52>+q|511>+q²|421>+q|3211>+q²|31111>+q³|22111>), and D−C=[2](|421>+q|331>+q³|3211>+q²|322>). All are explicit ordinary-generator compositions, not divided powers. A nontrivial E check on321 has four outputs (0,0,Z,[3]Z), where Z=(1+q²)|11>+(q^-1+q)|2>. Hence all displayed Serre sums vanish, whereas F0F1|1>=|3>+q|111> and F1F0|1>=0 show noncommutation. Both color orders obey the full cubic identity from the local rank-one Serre theorem.

items.title: The good-node crystal component of the empty partition for $e=3$
items.statement: At e=3, charge0, the QG empty component through size3 consists of ranks empty;1;2,11;3,21. Its arrows within this range are empty --f0-->1; 1--f1-->2 and 1--f2-->11; 2--f2-->3 and 11--f1-->21. Raising arrows are their inverses. All other additions from ranks≤2 vanish; additions from rank3 leaving the displayed range are omitted. The shapes are exactly the3-regular shapes at these sizes. The shape111 is outside this component and is a highest CRYSTAL vertex of weight Lambda0−delta; this does not say E_i|111>=0 as a field vector. Every shape has the exact weight Lambda0−Σ_i m_i alpha_i, not an unspecified delta correction. Good means removable, cogood means addable.

items.title: The whole partition Fock space is not the basic representation
items.statement:
The assertion that the entire partition Fock module $F$ is the basic
representation, i.e. that $F=M=U_q(\mathfrak g)|\varnothing\rangle\cong
V(\Lambda_0)$ for every finite $e\ge2$, is false. For every finite $e\ge2$ the
Fock module is strictly larger than $M$: the raw basis vector $|1^e\rangle$ is
not in $M$, and its ambient lower lift $G(1^e)$ is also not in $M$. The full
field decomposition is
$F=\bigoplus_{k\ge0}V(\Lambda_0-k\delta)^{\oplus p(k)}$, the $\Lambda_0$
multiplicity is $1$, and the higher constituents are nonzero; consequently the
full crystal has all partitions as vertices while its empty component is exactly
the $e$-regular partitions.

items.title: Unitriangular global basis elements at small rank
items.statement:
At $e=2$ the ambient lower basis in degrees $\le3$ is
$\varnothing\mapsto|\varnothing\rangle$, $1\mapsto|1\rangle$,
$11\mapsto|11\rangle$, $2\mapsto|2\rangle+q|11\rangle$,
$111\mapsto|111\rangle$, $3\mapsto|3\rangle+q|111\rangle$,
$21\mapsto|21\rangle$. The basic labels in these degrees are
$\varnothing,1,2,3,21$ (not $11$ or $111$). In degree $4$, rows and columns
ordered $4,31,22,211,1111$, the full lower transition matrix
$D$ (column $=G$-label, row $=$ standard shape) is

$$\begin{pmatrix}1&0&0&0&0\\q&1&0&0&0\\0&q&1&0&0\\q&q^2&q&1&0\\q^2&0&0&q&1\end{pmatrix}.$$

Its basic columns are $4$ and $31$. All entries lie in $\mathbb Z[q]$, the
diagonal is $1$, and off-diagonal entries lie in $q\mathbb Z[q]$, with the
proved dominance and core bounds. The apparent transpose-conjugation identity
holds accidentally for the displayed degrees $\le3$ but is **false** generally:
$d_{(211),(4)}=q$ whereas $d_{(1111),(31)}=0$. The source symmetry concerns the
bar transition matrix, not $D$. The ambient bar-fixed $G(111)$ lies outside the
basic module; no arbitrary bar-fixed combination need lie in one isotypic
summand.
